### Sūkta 5, The Tenth Mantra

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> मा नो॒ मर्ता॑ अ॒भि द्रु॑हन्तनू॒ना॑मिंद्र गिर्वणः ।
> ईशा॑नो यवया व॒धं ॥१०॥
>
> *mā no mártā abhí druhantanūnāmiṃdra girvaṇaḥ |*
> *ī́śāno yavayā vadháṃ ||10||*

*(Reading note: the Saṃhitā is printed "druhantanūnām" as one run, and is given so; the Pada text below shows "druhan | tanūnām.")*

### Page 198 — Rik 5.10: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 5." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; re-read from the better scan.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> मा । नः । मर्ताः । अभि । द्रुहन् । तनूनाम् । इन्द्र । गिर्वणः ।
> ईशानः । यवय । वधम् ॥१०॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे गिर्वण इन्द्र मर्ता विरोधिनो मनुष्या नोऽस्मदीयानां तनूनां शरीराणां माभि द्रुहन् । अभितो द्रोहं मा कुर्युः । ईशानः समर्थस्त्वं वधं वैरिभिः संपाद्यमानं यवय । अस्मत्तः पृथक्कुरु । मनुष्या इत्यादिषु पञ्चविंशतिसंख्याकेषु मनुष्यनामसु मर्ता व्राता इति पठितम् ॥
> *he girvaṇa indra martā virodhino manuṣyā no 'smadīyānāṃ tanūnāṃ śarīrāṇāṃ mābhi druhan | abhito droham mā kuryuḥ | īśānaḥ samarthas tvaṃ vadhaṃ vairibhiḥ sampādyamānaṃ yavaya | asmattaḥ pṛthak kuru | manuṣyā ity ādiṣu pañcaviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu manuṣya-nāmasu martā vrātā iti paṭhitam ||*
> *(Reading note, re-checked against the better scan: "martā virodhino" is the sandhi of "martāḥ"; in the list of names the print has "martā vrātā iti.")*

**Translation:** "O 'girvaṇaḥ' Indra! Let not 'martāḥ' — hostile men — 'abhi druhan' — do harm ('droha') on every side to 'naḥ tanūnām' — to our bodies. 'Īśānaḥ' — you, who are able — 'vadham' — the slaughter that is being worked by enemies — 'yavaya' — keep away; separate (it) from us. Among the twenty-five names of men beginning with 'manuṣyāḥ,' 'martāḥ' and 'vrātāḥ' are read."

**Grammar (re-read from the better scan; sūtras kept):** "Martāḥ" — the Uṇādi **असिहसिमृग्रिण्वामिदमिलूपूधुर्विभ्यस्तन्** (उ. सू. ३-८६) the affix "tan"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Abhi" — **एवमादीनामन्तः** (फि. सू. ४-१४), end-acute. "Druhan" — "druha jighāṃsāyām": **लिङर्थे लेट्** (पा. ३-४-७) in the sense of prayer (**प्रार्थनायाम्**, पा. ३-३-१६१); its "jhi" (**तिप्तस्झि…**, पा. ३-४-७८); **झोऽन्तः** (पा. ७-१-३); **इतश्च लोपः परस्मैपदेषु** (पा. ३-४-९७) elides the "i"; "śap" by "luk"; by **सार्वधातुकमपित्** (पा. १-२-४) the tiṅ is "ṅit," so no guṇa of the light penultimate (**क्ङिति च**, पा. १-१-५). "Tanūnām" — for lack of syntactic connection there is no "parāṅgavadbhāva." "Indra girvaṇaḥ" — vocatives, unaccented ("gatam," as said before). "Īśānaḥ" — the root being anudātta-it, the "śap" being elided by "luk" and the lasārvadhātuka unaccented, the root accent alone remains. "Yavaya" — after "yu" with "ṇic," vṛddhi is not done by the statement **संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः** (a rule introduced by a technical name is not binding); or "yavaḥ" from "yauti" by "ac" (**पचाद्यच्**, पा. ३-१-१३४), and "yavaṃ karoti" — **तत्करोति तदाचष्टे** (पा. ३-१-२६, 5-6 [as printed]) gives "ṇic"; by "iṣṭhavadbhāva" the "ṭi" is elided (पा. ६-४-१५५-१); as that elision is sthānivat (पा. १-१-५६), there is no vṛddhi. "Vadham" — **हनश्च वधः** (पा. ३-३-७६) the affix "ap" in the sense of state, with "vadha" for "han"; as "vadha" is taught together with the affix, it is end-acute by sthānivadbhāva; with the acute removed, the affix "ap" takes the acute. ॥१०॥

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**गिर्वणः (girvaṇaḥ)** — O one who is praised by words | **(हे) इन्द्र (he indra)** — O Indra | **मर्ताः (martāḥ)** — (our enemies) men | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **तनूनाम् (tanūnām)** — to bodies | **मा अभि द्रुहन् (mā abhi druhan)** — may they not do harm | **ईशानः (īśānaḥ)** — you, who are all-powerful (or, master) | **वधम् (vadham)** — (the harm that may come to us from enemies) hindrance | **यवय (yavaya)** — ward off.

### Page 199 — Rik 5.10: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 10 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." English as printed. References re-read from the better scan; the gloss is mine, tentative.)*

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

O Indra, who are praised by us in words! Let not the men who are hostile to us do harm to our bodies, that is, let them not injure us. Since you, being our master, are all-powerful, ward off from our bodies the harm that may come from enemies.

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"O Indra, adorable by praises, let not mortals do injury to our persons; you are powerful, keep away our destruction (by enemies)."

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**मर्ताः (martāḥ)** — Among the twenty-five words that signify human beings, beginning with "manuṣyāḥ," the word "martāḥ" is read (Ni. 2-3). Here, since it is desired that men who might do harm to our bodies not do so, "martāḥ" is to be understood as "men who are hostile to us." Although no word indicating "hostile" is found in the Ṛk in hand, because the word "druhan" ("may they injure") is used, it is fitting that the Bhāṣyakāra explained "martāḥ" as "hostile men."

**यवय (yavaya)** — in the saṃhitā-text it is "yavayā," with the final syllable lengthened to suit the metre.

**वधम् (vadham)** — death, destruction, harm. The commentators on the meaning of the Veda explain "vadha" as Indra's "vajra" (thunderbolt-weapon); the Bhāṣyakāra also does so, in the Ṛk —

> आर्चन्नत्र मरुतः सस्मिन्नाजौ विश्वे देवासो अमदन्ननु त्वा ।
> वृत्रस्य यद्भृष्टिमता वधेन नि त्वमिन्द्र प्रत्यानं जघन्थ ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-५२-१५)
> *ārcann atra marutaḥ sasminn ājau viśve devāso amadann anu tvā |*
> *vṛtrasya yad bhṛṣṭimatā vadhena ni tvam indra pratyānaṃ jaghantha || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-52-15)*
> Gloss (mine; tentative): "Here the Maruts sang in this contest, and all the gods rejoiced after you, when you, O Indra, struck down the face-to-face (opponent) of Vṛtra with the pointed (barbed) weapon."

in which "vadhena" is explained as "by the vajra, the weapon which is the means of killing"; in this context it is to be understood as "do not use your thunderbolt-weapon against us."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept)* **"Martāḥ"** — **असिहसिमृग्रिण्वामिदमिलूपूधुर्विभ्यस्तन्** (उ. सू. ३-३६६ [as printed]; "3-86" on p. 198) — the affix "tan" after the roots "asu" … "hase hasane" (to laugh), "mṛṅ prāṇatyāge" (to die), "gṝ nigaraṇe" (to swallow), "iṇ gatau" (to go), "vāg-ati-gandhanayoḥ," "ama-gaty-ādiṣu," "damu upaśame" (to be calm), "lūñ chedane" (to cut), "pūñ pavane" (to purify), "dhurvī hiṃsāyām" (to injure) — the affix "tan" comes after "mṛṅ"; by **सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः** (पा. ७-३-८४) guṇa → "mar-tan" → "martā"; "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute.

### Page 200 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 5.10 (characterized)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 5." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, restating the Sanskrit of p. 198, **characterized in outline**; sūtras kept; numbers as read.)*

*(Concluding "martāḥ":)* by **सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः** (पा. ७-३-८४) guṇa → "marta"; the affix being "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. **"Abhi"** — by **एवादीनामन्तः** (फि. सू. ८२ [?]; "4-14" on p. 198) it is end-acute. **"Druhan"** — "druha jighāṃsāyām"; **लिङर्थे लेट्** (पा. ३-४-७) and, with the sense of prayer, **प्रार्थनायां** (पा. ३-३-१६१); in the Veda "leṭ" comes after a root in the senses of the vidhi-liṅ and the like (and also in cause-and-effect and desire senses); the third-person plural "jhi"; **झोऽन्तः** (पा. ७-१-३) "ant"; **इतश्च लोपः परस्मैपदेषु** (पा. ३-४-९७) — the "i" of the tiṅ replacing "leṭ" is elided optionally; **बहुलं छन्दसि** (पा. २-४-७३) the "śap" is elided; **सार्वधातुकमपित्** (पा. १-२-४) makes the sārvadhātuka "ṅit," so "ant" is "ṅit" and by **क्ङिति च** (पा. १-१-५) guṇa is barred; so no guṇa arises even though **पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च** (पा. ७-३-८६) would give it. **"Tanūnām"** — "indra" (the vocative) stands after it and is "āmantrita"; **सुबामन्त्रिते पराङ्गवत्स्वरे** (पा. २-१-२) would make the preceding word part of the following one, but since this is a rule about word-formation (**समर्थः पदविधिः**, पा. २-१-१) it applies only where there is mutual syntactic connection, and "tanūnām" has none with "indra," so "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not occur. **"Indra"** — explained at Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-4; **"girvaṇaḥ"** — explained at the seventh mantra of this same sūkta. **"Īśānaḥ"** — "īśa aiśvarye" (to rule); the "laṭ" and "śānac"; **बहुलं छन्दसि** (पा. २-४-७३) elides the "śap"; the root is unaccented in its upadeśa, so **तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित्** (पा. ६-१-१८६) makes "śānac" unaccented; the "ī" retains the root's acute. **"Yavaya"** — "yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ" (to mix and to separate) with "ṇic" (**हेतुमति च**); **अचो ञ्णिति** (पा. ७-२-११५) would give vṛddhi to the penultimate of the root, but the vṛddhi laid down by **वृद्धिरादैच्** (पा. १-१-१) is a "saṃjñā-pūrvaka vidhi" (an operation that depends on a technical name), which is "anitya" (not constant); therefore vṛddhi is not done; the guṇa and "av" substitutions give "yavay-" and, in the imperative second-person singular, "yavaya." … *(continued on p. 201)*.

### Page 201 — Rik 5.10 grammar concluded; end of Sūkta 5 and of the Tenth Varga

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 10 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.)*

**"Yavaya"** *(concluding)* — because the vṛddhi is not done, one gets guṇa and "av" substitutions, and in the imperative second-person singular "yavaya." *Alternatively,* "yauti iti yavaḥ" (he who mixes — "yava," barley) from "yu" with **नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः** (पा. ३-१-१३४) "ac"; "yavaṃ karoti" — **तत्करोति तदाचष्टे** (पा. ३-१-२६, ५-६) "ṇic" in the sense of "he makes barley"; with it following, **णाविष्ठवत्प्रातिपदिकस्य** (पा. ६-४-१५५-१) gives the "iṣṭhavat" treatment and **टेः** (पा. ६-४-१५५) elides the "ṭi" — the "a" after "v." Since the elided "a" is treated as present by **अचः परस्मिन्पूर्वविधौ** (पा. १-१-५७; sthānivadbhāva), the vṛddhi that would be caused by the affix "ṇic" does not occur; "yavaya." In the saṃhitā the last vowel is lengthened.

**"Vadham"** — **हनश्च वधः** (पा. ३-३-७६) — after the root "han," when no prefix precedes it, the affix "ap" comes, and "vadha" is the substitute for "han" (with "ap"): "han + ap" → "vadha." The affix is "p"-marked and so unaccented (**अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ**, पा. ३-१-४). Since the sūtra reads "vadhaḥ" as an end-acute substitute, some say "vadha" is end-acute; the root "han" is end-acute by **धातोः** (पा. ६-१-१६२), and the substitute "vadha" in its place is, by sthānivadbhāva, end-acute — this is the view of Mādhavācārya. In either case, the final "a" of "vadha" is acute, and there is no difference of opinion on that. By **अतो लोपः** (पा. ६-४-४८) the "a" of the stem is elided before the case-ending; then by **अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः** (पा. ६-१-१६१) — in the place where an acute is elided, the unaccented vowel that follows takes the acute — the accent of the elided "a" passes to the affix's "a." ॥१०॥

**ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಪ್ರಥಮಮಂಡಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಐದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವು** — *illige prathama-maṇḍaladalli aidaneya sūktavu samāptavu* — "Here the **fifth sūkta** in the first Maṇḍala is complete."

**ಒಂದನೆಯ ಅಧ್ಯಾಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಹತ್ತನೆಯ ವರ್ಗವು ಸಮಾಪ್ತವು** — *ondaneya adhyāyadalli hattaneya vargavu samāptavu* — "In the first Adhyāya, the **tenth varga** is complete."

*(Note on the varga numbers: this closing note, plain in the print, confirms that the tenth varga ends here, with p. 201. Re-checked against the better scan: the headers read "Varga 7" on pp. 89–109, "Varga 8" on pp. 111–143 and "Varga 9" from p. 145; the seventh varga closes on p. 111 and the eighth on p. 135.)*

## Sūkta 6 — "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam"

### Pages 202–203 — Sūkta 6: heading; Sāyaṇa's introduction; the Anuvāda; Rik 6.1 (Saṃhitā, Pada, Bhāṣya opening)

*(Page headers: p. 202 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6"; p. 203 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; read from enlarged slices; [?] where unclear. Printed title: "ಆರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು" ("the sixth sūkta"). Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(p. 202)*

> सुरूपेत्यादिषु षट्सूक्तेषु तृतीयस्य युञ्जन्तीति सूक्तस्य मन्त्रसंख्याऋषिच्छन्दोदैवतानि विनियोगाश्चेत्येते पूर्ववदवगन्तव्याः । दशर्चे तस्मिन्सूक्त आद्यास्तिस्रोऽन्तिमा चेत्येताश्चतस्र ऐन्द्र्यः । आ दह स्वधामनु इत्येतां चतुर्थीमारभ्य षडृचो मारुत्यः । तासु मध्ये वीळु चिदिन्द्रेणेत्येते द्वे ऋचौ मारुत्यौ सत्यावैन्द्र्यावपि भवतः । तदेतत्सर्वमनुक्रमणिकायामुक्तम् । सुरूपकृत्नुं दश्यैन्द्रमा तु युञ्जन्त्यादहेत्येताः षण्मारुत्यो वीळु चिदिन्द्रेणेत्यैन्द्र्यौ चेति ॥ एतस्मिन्सूक्ते युञ्जन्तीत्यसौ तृचस्तृतीये रात्रिपर्याये ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनोऽनुरूपः । तथा चातिरात्रे पर्यायाणामिति खण्डे योगे योगे तवस्तरं युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषम् । आ. ६-४ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥
> *surūpety ādiṣu ṣaṭsūkteṣu tṛtīyasya yuñjantīti sūktasya mantra-saṃkhyā-ṛṣi-cchando-devatā-viniyogāś cety ete pūrvavad avagantavyāḥ | daśarce tasmin sūkta ādyās tisro 'ntimā cety etāś catasra aindryaḥ | ā daha svadhām anu ity etāṃ caturthīm ārabhya ṣaḍṛco mārutyaḥ | tāsu madhye vīḷu cid indreṇety ete dve ṛcau mārutyau satyāv aindryāv api bhavataḥ | tad etat sarvam anukramaṇikāyām uktam | surūpakṛtnuṃ daśy aindramā tu yuñjanty ādaha ity etāḥ ṣaṇ mārutyo vīḷu cid indreṇety aindryau ceti || etasmin sūkte yuñjantīty asau tṛcas tṛtīye rātri-paryāye brāhmaṇācchaṃsino 'nurūpaḥ | tathā cātirātre paryāyāṇām iti khaṇḍe yoge yoge tavastaraṃ yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam | ā. 6-4 | iti sūtritam ||*
> *(Reading notes: (i) "satyāv aindryāv api" is clear in the better scan; its sense — "these two Ṛks, being Marut Ṛks, are also Aindra" — is the one the Kannada commentary gives below; (ii) the Anukramaṇī quotation is as printed, with its abbreviated "daśy aindramā tu" run together; I give it without correcting; (iii) the sūtra-quotation reads "bradhnam" in the Rik but I read "ब्रध्नमरुषम्" here as printed.)*

**Translation:** "Of the six sūktas beginning with 'surūpa…', as for the third, 'yuñjanti…': its number of Ṛks, ṛṣi, metre, deity and applications are to be understood as before. In this ten-Ṛk sūkta, the first three and the last — these four — are Aindrī (addressed to Indra). Beginning with the fourth, 'ā daha svadhām anu,' six Ṛks are Mārutī (addressed to the Maruts). Among them, the two Ṛks 'vīḷu cid indreṇa' (the fifth) and the seventh are Mārutī and also Aindrī. All this is stated in the Anukramaṇī: '*surūpakṛtnuṃ … aindramā tu yuñjanti ādaha — these six are Mārutī; the two beginning 'vīḷu cid indreṇa' are Aindrī.*' In this sūkta the tṛca 'yuñjanti…' is the anurūpa (the 'corresponding' verse) of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin in the third night-round (paryāya); and in the Sūtra (Āśvalāyana 6-4), in the section 'atirātre paryāyāṇām,' it is laid down: '*yoge yoge tavastaraṃ … yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam.*'"

**॥ Anuvādaḥ ॥** *(Kannada commentary, translated; p. 202)*

In the sacrifice called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, at the time of the morning pressing, the application of the six sūktas beginning "surūpakṛtnum ūtaye," which the priest of the Hotṛ group called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite for the stoma-vṛddhi and āvāpa, has been given earlier (p. 87). The present sūkta "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam," which comes in that context, is the third among those six sūktas; so the application of those six applies to it too. There are ten Ṛks in this sūkta. Of them, the first three and the last one — four Ṛks — are addressed to Indra. Six Ṛks, from the fourth, "ā daha svadhām anu," to the ninth, are addressed to the Maruts. Among these six, the fifth, "vīḷu cid ārujatnubhiḥ," and the seventh, "indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase," are addressed to both Indra and the Maruts. This matter is stated in the Sarvānukramaṇī: "*surūpakṛtnuṃ … ṣaṇ mārutyo, vīḷu cid indreṇety aindryau ceti*" — that is, the ten Ṛks of the sūkta "surūpakṛtnum," the ten of "ā tvetā," and the first three and the last Ṛk of "yuñjanti bradhnam" are all addressed to the deity Indra; the six Ṛks from "ā daha svadhām anu" to "ata parī[?] gahi"-ending are addressed to the Maruts; but of these six, the two Ṛks "vīḷu cid ārujatnubhiḥ" and "indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase" are addressed to the two deities, Indra and the Maruts. The first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited, in the third night-round (paryāya) of the Atirātra, by the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. In this context the Āśvalāyana sūtra says: "*tathā cātirātre paryāyāṇām iti khaṇḍe yoge yoge tavastaraṃ yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam*" (Āśv. Sū. 6-4 [?]).

*(Reading note: the Kannada names the Mārut group by its first and last Ṛks — "ā daha svadhām anu" (the fourth) "to" "ataḥ pari jmann ā gahi" (the ninth), as printed. The Ṛk-numbering of the deities I take from the Sanskrit above and from the Kannada's own count: Aindrī — 1, 2, 3, 10; Mārutī — 4, 6, 8, 9; both — 5, 7.)*

**Heading (p. 203):**

**सूक्त—६** *(Sūkta 6)*
॥ मण्डल—१ ॥ अनुवाक—२ ॥ सूक्त—६ ॥
॥ अष्टक—१ ॥ अध्याय—१ ॥ वर्ग—११–१२ ॥
॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्ये १–१० ॥ *(Ṛks of the sūkta: 1–10)*
**ऋषिः** — मधुच्छन्दा वैश्वामित्रः (*ṛṣiḥ — madhucchandā vaiśvāmitraḥ*)
**देवता** — १–३ इन्द्रः । ४, ६, ८, ९ मरुतः । ५, ७ मरुत इन्द्रश्च । १० इन्द्रः (*devatā — 1–3 indraḥ; 4, 6, 8, 9 marutaḥ; 5, 7 maruta indraś ca; 10 indraḥ*) *(numerals as printed)*
**छन्दः** — गायत्री (*chandaḥ — gāyatrī*)

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> युं॒जंति॑ ब्र॒ध्नम॑रु॒षं चरं॑तं॒ परि॑ त॒स्थुषः॑ ।
> रोचं॑ते रोच॒ना दि॒वि ॥१॥
>
> *yuṃjáṃti bradhnámaruṣáṃ cáraṃtaṃ pári tasthúṣaḥ |*
> *rócaṃte rocanā́ diví ||1||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> युञ्जन्ति । ब्रध्नम् । अरुषम् । चरन्तम् । परि । तस्थुषः ।
> रोचन्ते । रोचना । दिवि ॥१॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(Rik 6.1; opening, p. 203)*

> इन्द्रो हि परमैश्वर्ययुक्तः । परमैश्वर्यं चाग्निवाय्वादित्यनक्षत्ररूपेणावस्थानमुपपद्यते । ब्रध्नमादित्यरूपेणावस्थितम् अरुषं हिंसकरहिताग्निरूपेणावस्थितं चरन्तं वायुरूपेण सर्वतः प्रसरन्तमिन्द्रं परि तस्थुषः परितोऽवस्थिता लोकत्रयवर्तिनः प्राणिनो युञ्जन्ति । स्वकीये कर्मणि देवताभावेन संबद्धं कुर्वन्ति । तस्यैवेन्द्रस्य मूर्तिविशेषभूतानि रोचना रोचनानि नक्षत्राणि दिवि द्युलोके रोचन्ते । प्रकाशन्ते । अस्य मन्त्रस्योक्तार्थपरत्वं ब्राह्मणान्तरे व्याख्यातम् । युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रध्नः । आदित्यमेवास्मै युनक्ति । अरुषमित्याह । अग्निर्वा अरुषः । अग्निमेवास्मै युनक्ति । चरन्तमित्याह । वायुर्वै चरन् । वायुमेवास्मै युनक्ति । परि तस्थुष इत्याह । इमे वै लोकाः परि तस्थुषः । इमानेवास्मै लोकान्युनक्ति । रोचन्ते रोचना दिवीत्याह ।
> *indro hi paramaiśvarya-yuktaḥ | paramaiśvaryaṃ cāgni-vāyv-āditya-nakṣatra-rūpeṇāvasthānam upapadyate | bradhnam āditya-rūpeṇāvasthitam aruṣaṃ hiṃsakara-hitāgni-rūpeṇāvasthitaṃ carantaṃ vāyu-rūpeṇa sarvataḥ prasarantam indraṃ pari tasthuṣaḥ parito 'vasthitā loka-traya-vartinaḥ prāṇino yuñjanti | svakīye karmaṇi devatā-bhāvena sambaddhaṃ kurvanti | tasyaiv endrasya mūrti-viśeṣa-bhūtāni rocanā rocanāni nakṣatrāṇi divi dyuloke rocante | prakāśante | asya mantrasyoktārtha-paratvaṃ brāhmaṇāntare vyākhyātam | yuñjanti bradhnam ity āha | asau vā ādityo bradhnaḥ | ādityam evāsmai yunakti | aruṣam ity āha | agnir vā aruṣaḥ | agnim evāsmai yunakti | carantam ity āha | vāyur vai caran | vāyum evāsmai yunakti | pari tasthuṣa ity āha | ime vai lokāḥ pari tasthuṣaḥ | imān evāsmai lokān yunakti | rocante rocanā divīty āha |*
> *(Reading notes: "hiṃsakara-hitā" is printed so, and I read "hiṃsaka-rahitā" ("free of the destructive") with that spelling noted; the sentence ends at the foot of p. 203 with "rocante rocanā divīty āha," and continues on p. 204.)*

**Translation:** "Indra is indeed endowed with supreme lordship, and his supreme lordship consists in his abiding in the forms of Agni, Vāyu, Āditya and the stars. 'Bradhnam' — abiding as the Sun; 'aruṣam' — abiding as the harmless (non-destroying) Agni; 'carantam' — spreading in all directions as Vāyu — Indra: 'pari tasthuṣaḥ' — the beings of the three worlds, standing round about, 'yuñjanti' — yoke (join) him: they make him connected, as a deity, with their own work. 'Rocanā' — the stars, the shining bodies that are particular forms of that same Indra, 'rocante' — shine, 'divi' — in the heavenly world. That this mantra has the sense stated is explained in another Brāhmaṇa: '*"yuñjanti bradhnam," it says: yonder Sun is "bradhna"; he yokes the Sun to him. "Aruṣam," it says: Agni is "aruṣa"; he yokes Agni to him. "Carantam," it says: Vāyu is "carat"; he yokes Vāyu to him. "Pari tasthuṣaḥ," it says: these worlds are "pari tasthuṣaḥ"; he yokes these worlds to him. "Rocante rocanā divi," it says: …'" *(continues on the next page)*.

### Page 204 — Rik 6.1: Bhāṣya concluded; grammar (characterized); Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script; read from an enlarged slice. References re-read from the better scan. English as printed.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(concluding p. 203's Brāhmaṇa quotation)*

> नक्षत्राणि वै रोचना दिवि । नक्षत्राण्येवास्मै रोचयति । (तै. ब्रा. ३-९-४-१) इति । पञ्चविंशतिसंख्याकेषु महन्नामसु महो ब्रध्न इति पठितम् । आदित्यस्यापि महत्त्वादेव ब्रध्नत्वम् ॥
> *nakṣatrāṇi vai rocanā divi | nakṣatrāṇy evāsmai rocayati | (tai. brā. 3-9-4-1) iti | pañcaviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu mahan-nāmasu maho bradhna iti paṭhitam | ādityasyāpi mahattvād eva bradhnatvam ||*

**Translation:** "'*The stars indeed are "rocanā" in the sky; he makes the stars shine for him.*' (Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa 3-9-4-1). Among the twenty-five names of 'the great,' 'mahaḥ' and 'bradhnaḥ' are read; the Sun, too, is 'bradhna' for the very reason that he is great."

**Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept; read from the slice):** "Yuñjanti" — the end-acute follows the affix's accent. "Bradhnam" — a stem (prātipadika) end-acute. "Aruṣam" — from "ṛṣ/ruṣa/riṣa" (roots in the sense of injuring; "ruṣā" = the injurers); **इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः** (पा. ३-१-१३५) the affix "ka"; the affix's accent acute; "na santi ruṣā yasya" — a bahuvrīhi after "nañ"; by **नञ्सुभ्याम्** (पा. ६-२-१७२) the second member is end-acute; **अमि पूर्वः** (पा. ६-१-१०७) the pūrvarūpa, then **एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः** (पा. ८-२-५). "Carantam" — "śap" is "p"-marked, hence unaccented; and the "śatṛ" being a "lasārvadhātuka," its own accent is lost, leaving the root's accent. "Tasthuṣaḥ" — after "tiṣṭhati," "kvasu" for "liṭ" (पा. ३-२-१०७); "iṭ" by **वस्वेकाजाद्घसाम्** (पा. ७-२-६७) would be internal (antaraṅga), but is set aside by the maxim **संप्रसारणं संप्रसारणाश्रयं च बलीयः** (म. ६-१-१७-२; confirmed on p. 213): before "śas," as the stem is "bha" (**यचि भम्**, पा. १-४-१८), **वसोः संप्रसारणम्** (पा. ६-४-१३१) and pūrvarūpa; **शासिवसिघसीनां च** (पा. ८-३-६०) "ṣ" for "s"; end-acute by the affix accent. "Rocante" — the "tiṅ" and "lasārvadhātuka" unaccented; **शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम्**; the root's accent alone remains. "Rocanā" — **अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः** (पा. ३-२-१४९) the affix "yuc"; **युवोरनाकौ** (पा. ७-१-१) puts "ana" for "yu"; end-acute by "c" (**चितः**). "Divi" — the case-ending is acute after "ūḍh-idam…" (**ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः**, पा. ६-१-१७१).

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**परि (pari)** — all around, in every direction | **तस्थुषः (tasthuṣaḥ)** — (in the three worlds) beings who stand | **ब्रध्नम् (bradhnam)** — (one who has) the form of the Sun | **अरुषम् (aruṣam)** — (one who has) the form of Agni, who does not injure | **चरन्तम् (carantam)** — (Indra) who moves everywhere in the form of Vāyu | **युञ्जन्ति (yuñjanti)** — they connect (to their own works, like a chief deity — that is, they join him in their own actions) | **रोचना (rocanā)** — the stars (that are special forms of that Indra) | **दिवि (divi)** — in the heavenly world (in the sky) | **रोचन्ते (rocante)** — shine.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

Indra is full of supreme lordship; supreme lordship means the power to shine in the forms of Agni, Vāyu, Āditya and the stars. Therefore Indra shines in the form of the Sun, in the form of fire, in the form of the ever-moving Vāyu, and in the form of the stars in the sky. All beings of the three worlds regard such an Indra as the chief god in their own worship and the like and establish with him a relation of greatness and honour.

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"Those who are standing around (i.e. living beings inhabiting the three worlds) associate with (Indra) the mighty (in the form of the sun) the non-injuring (in the form of fire) the moving (in the form of wind) the lights (or stars special incarnations of that same Indra) shine in the sky."

### Page 205 — Special topics on Rik 6.1: the classification of mantras by sense (Nirukta 7-1–3)

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." The Nirukta passage is printed in Kannada script; read from an enlarged slice and given in three layers. Its reference ("Nirukta, Daivata-kāṇḍa, adhyāya 7, khaṇḍa 1–3") is confirmed from the better scan. English words in the Kannada are as printed.)*

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The Pada-meanings, the Bhāvārtha and the English rendering of this Ṛk follow Sāyaṇa's Bhāṣya. Sāyaṇa's Bhāṣya follows the exposition given in the **Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa** (of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda). Since the Brāhmaṇa is counted as a part of the Veda, and since it contains very ancient exposition, it must be believed to be the chief authority in the investigation of Vedic meaning. The sage **Yāska**, the author of the Nirukta, says as follows in regard to explaining Vedic mantras:

> तद्यानि नामानि प्राधान्यस्तुतीनां देवतानां तद्दैवतमित्याचक्षते ॥ यत्काम ऋषिर्यस्यां देवतायामार्थपत्यमिच्छन्स्तुतिं प्रयुङ्क्ते तद्दैवतः स मन्त्रो भवति ॥ ताः त्रिविधा ऋचः परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृता आध्यात्मिकाश्च । तत्र परोक्षकृताः सर्वाभिर्नामविभक्तिभिर्युज्यन्ते प्रथमपुरुषैश्चाख्यातस्य ॥ अथ प्रत्यक्षकृता मध्यमपुरुषयोगास्त्वमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना ॥ अथाध्यात्मिकाः उत्तमपुरुषयोगा अहमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना ॥ परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृताश्च मन्त्रा भूयिष्ठा अल्पश आध्यात्मिकाः ॥ (निरुक्त—दैवतकाण्ड. अध्याय ७-खण्ड १–३)
> *tad yāni nāmāni prādhānya-stutīnāṃ devatānāṃ tad daivatam ity ācakṣate || yat-kāma ṛṣir yasyāṃ devatāyām ārthapatyam icchan stutiṃ prayuṅkte tad-daivataḥ sa mantro bhavati || tās trividhā ṛcaḥ parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtā ādhyātmikāś ca | tatra parokṣakṛtāḥ sarvābhir nāma-vibhaktibhir yujyante prathama-puruṣaiś cākhyātasya || atha pratyakṣakṛtā madhyama-puruṣa-yogās tvam iti caitena sarvanāmnā || athādhyātmikāḥ uttama-puruṣa-yogā aham iti caitena sarvanāmnā || parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtāś ca mantrā bhūyiṣṭhā alpaśa ādhyātmikāḥ || (nirukta — daivata-kāṇḍa, adhyāya 7, khaṇḍa 1–3)*
> *(Reading note: the opening clause is printed "tad yāni nāmāni prādhānya-stutīnāṃ devatānāṃ" and I give it so; the "yat-kāma ṛṣir yasyāṃ devatāyām ārthapatyam icchan" clause is as printed. The adverb "alpaśaḥ" is printed "alpaśa.")*

**Translation (mine, following the Kannada account below):** "'Those names of the deities who are praised chiefly (as the subject of a hymn) — of that (hymn) they say "its deity is so-and-so." Whatever the desire with which a seer, wishing for lordship (of that thing), addresses praise to a deity — that mantra has that deity. Those Ṛks are of three kinds: parokṣa-kṛta (made in the indirect form), pratyakṣa-kṛta (made in the direct form), and ādhyātmika (made in the personal form). Of these, the parokṣa-kṛta are joined with all the case-forms of the noun and with the third person of the verb. Then the pratyakṣa-kṛta are joined with the second person, and with the pronoun "tvam" (thou). Then the ādhyātmika are joined with the first person, and with the pronoun "aham" (I). The parokṣa-kṛta and the pratyakṣa-kṛta mantras are the most numerous; the ādhyātmika are few.'"

That is: among mantras there are many kinds — **daivata-mantra, stuti-mantra, āśīr-mantra, śapatha, abhiśāpa, kaścid-bhāva, paridevanā, nindā, praśaṃsā**, and so on. A "daivata-mantra" is a mantra that describes the greatness of the gods; "stuti" is a mantra that contains stotra and entreaties; "āśīḥ" is a mantra that gives a blessing — one that wishes the good of another; "śapatha" is a vow, a promise; "abhiśāpa" is a curse — wishing another harm; "kaścid-bhāva" is the description of a certain matter or of a truth; "paridevanā" is lamentation, distress; "nindā" is blame; "praśaṃsā" is praise; "dānastuti" is the praise of gifts; and so on.

Of the many kinds of mantras mentioned above, the Ṛks called "daivata" are of three kinds: **parokṣa-kṛta, pratyakṣa-kṛta** and **ādhyātmika**. A "parokṣa-kṛta" mantra is one in which the deity who is praised is not present before one — so that the praise is made in the form in which the third-person nouns and the third-person verbs are used with reference to that deity ("third person both in subject and predicate" — English as printed). A "pratyakṣa-kṛta" mantra is one in which the deity is imagined as standing visibly before one, and is praised by addressing him, using the second-person words "you," "your" and so on ("second person" — English as printed). An "ādhyātmika" mantra is one in which praise is made by using the first person ("first person" — English as printed). Of these three kinds of mantras, the two — parokṣa-kṛta and pratyakṣa-kṛta — are more numerous; the ādhyātmika mantras are only few.

### Page 206 — The Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa exposition of Rik 6.1; Skandasvāmī's commentary (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] where unclear. The Brāhmaṇa reference re-read from the better scan.)*

The Ṛk "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam," which is relevant here, ought by the above (classification) to belong to the group "parokṣa-kṛta" among daivata mantras. But since the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa explains this Ṛk with an adhyātmika meaning, the Bhāṣyakāra has explained it in accordance with that. In that Brāhmaṇa, in giving the exposition of this Ṛk, it is said:

> युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रध्नः । आदित्यमेवास्मै युनक्ति । अरुषमित्याह । अग्निर्वा अरुषः । अग्निमेवास्मै युनक्ति । चरन्तमित्याह । वायुर्वै चरन् । वायुमेवास्मै युनक्ति । परि तस्थुष इत्याह । इमे वै लोकाः परि तस्थुषः । इमानेवास्मै लोकान् युनक्ति । रोचन्ते रोचना दिवीत्याह । नक्षत्राणि वै रोचना दिवि । नक्षत्राण्येवास्मै रोचयति ॥ (तै. ब्रा. ३-९-४)
> *yuñjanti bradhnam ity āha | asau vā ādityo bradhnaḥ | ādityam evāsmai yunakti | aruṣam ity āha | agnir vā aruṣaḥ | agnim evāsmai yunakti | carantam ity āha | vāyur vai caran | vāyum evāsmai yunakti | pari tasthuṣa ity āha | ime vai lokāḥ pari tasthuṣaḥ | imān evāsmai lokān yunakti | rocante rocanā divīty āha | nakṣatrāṇi vai rocanā divi | nakṣatrāṇy evāsmai rocayati || (tai. brā. 3-9-4)*
> **Translation:** "'*Yuñjanti bradhnam,' he says: yonder Sun is 'bradhna'; he yokes the Sun to him. 'Aruṣam,' he says: Agni is 'aruṣa'; he yokes Agni to him. 'Carantam,' he says: Vāyu is the 'moving'; he yokes Vāyu to him. 'Pari tasthuṣaḥ,' he says: these worlds are 'pari tasthuṣaḥ'; he yokes these worlds to him. 'Rocante rocanā divi,' he says: the stars are the 'rocanā' in the sky; he makes the stars shine for him.*" *(This is the same passage that Sāyaṇa abridged on pp. 203–204.)*

That is, in this the sense is given, in an adhyātmika connection, that "bradhna" = the Sun, "aruṣa" = Agni, "carat" = Vāyu, "pari tasthuṣaḥ" = the three worlds, "rocanā" = the stars. Although we need not accept this meaning as authoritative, there is no refutation here of the meanings that other commentators give for this Ṛk. Since **Skandasvāmī** has explained this Ṛk in a different way, we give it here.

**Skandasvāmī's commentary** *(Sanskrit, printed in Kannada script; first part, p. 206):*

> योगः संबन्धः । युञ्जन्ति संबन्धयन्ति । केन, सामर्थ्यात् स्तुतिभिर्हविर्भिश्च । के, सामर्थ्यात् स्तोतारो यष्टारश्च । ब्रध्नं महन्नामैतत् । महान्तमिन्द्रम् । अरुषं रुशतिर्दीप्त्यर्थः । रुशद्वत्सारुशतीति प्रदर्शनात् । तस्य वा रोचतेर्वा दीप्तिकर्मण आज्पूर्वस्येदं रूपम् । आजश्च ह्रस्वत्वम् । अरुशं आरोचमानं वा दीप्तमित्यर्थः । आरुषत्यायतीति गतिकर्मसु पाठादृषतेर्गत्यर्थस्यारुषशब्दो गन्तृवचनः । शत्रून् यज्ञान् वा प्रतिगन्तारम् । चरन्तं परि सर्वतो गच्छन्तम् । यत्र यत्रेन्द्रो गच्छति तत्र तत्रैनं स्तोतारो यष्टारश्च स्तुवन्ति चेत्यर्थः । अथवा, युञ्जन्तीति युजिः शुद्धोऽपि सामर्थ्यात् सोपसर्गार्थे द्रष्टव्यः । स्वार्थसिद्धौ स्तोतारो यष्टारश्चैनं नियुञ्जते । महान्तं दीप्तं चेन्द्रं सर्वतो गच्छन्तं, यत्र यत्र गच्छति तत्र तत्रैनं मनुष्या इदमिदं च नः कुर्विन्त्यर्थं याचन्त इत्यर्थः । रथोऽत्र सामर्थ्यात् युज्यमानः नेन्द्रं युञ्जन्ति । इन्द्रस्य रथं ब्रध्नमरुषं
> *yogaḥ sambandhaḥ | yuñjanti sambandhayanti | kena, sāmarthyāt stutibhir havirbhiś ca | ke, sāmarthyāt stotāro yaṣṭāraś ca | bradhnaṃ mahan-nāmaitat | mahāntam indram | aruṣaṃ ruśatir dīptyarthaḥ | ruśadvatsāruśatīti pradarśanāt | tasya vā rocater vā dīpti-karmaṇa āj-pūrvasyedaṃ rūpam | ājaś ca hrasvatvam | aruśaṃ ārocamānaṃ vā dīptam ity arthaḥ | āruṣatyāyatīti gati-karmasu pāṭhād aruṣater gatyarthasyāruṣa-śabdo gantṛ-vacanaḥ | śatrūn yajñān vā pratigantāram | carantaṃ pari sarvato gacchantam | yatra yatrendro gacchati tatra tatrainaṃ stotāro yaṣṭāraś ca stuvanti cety arthaḥ | athavā, yuñjantīti yujiḥ śuddho 'pi sāmarthyāt sopasargārthe draṣṭavyaḥ | svārtha-siddhau stotāro yaṣṭāraś cainaṃ niyuñjate | mahāntaṃ dīptaṃ cendraṃ sarvato gacchantaṃ, yatra yatra gacchati tatra tatrainaṃ manuṣyā idam idaṃ ca naḥ kurv ity arthaṃ yācanta ity arthaḥ | ratho 'tra sāmarthyāt yujyamānaḥ nendraṃ yuñjanti | indrasya rathaṃ bradhnam aruṣaṃ …*
> *(Reading notes: (i) this stretch is dense and several of its words are crowded in the print — re-read from the better scan ("aruśam," "aruṣater," "draṣṭavyaḥ," "tatra tatrainaṃ" corrected); "ruśadvatsāruśatīti pradarśanāt" and "nendraṃ yuñjanti" are as printed; (ii) the sentence ends at the foot of the page and continues on p. 207.)*
> **Translation, in outline (what I can support):** "'Yoga' is connection. 'Yuñjanti' — they connect; by what? — by capacity, with praises and with oblations; who? — by capacity, the praisers and the sacrificers. 'Bradhna' is a name of the 'great' — the great Indra. 'Aruṣam' — the root 'ruś' is in the sense of shining; … [the grammatical explanation of 'aruṣa' as 'shining,' or as 'one who goes' from the root 'ṛṣ' in the list of roots of motion — hence 'aruṣa' is 'one who goes' — 'one who goes against enemies or to sacrifices']. 'Carantam' — going all around, in every direction: wherever Indra goes, there the praisers and the sacrificers praise him. Or: 'yuñjanti,' though the plain root 'yuj,' is by capacity to be understood in the sense of a prefixed verb ('niyuñjate'): the praisers and sacrificers 'engage' him for the accomplishing of their own aims; Indra, great and shining and going in all directions — wherever he goes, there men beg of him, 'do this and that for us.' … [the remainder — on the chariot — is garbled in the print and I do not translate it]."

### Page 207 — Skandasvāmī's commentary (concluded)

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] marks every place where letters are crowded or doubtful. The Brāhmaṇa-style argument at the foot of the page is very compressed; I give the Sanskrit as read and a translation in outline, saying where the sense is uncertain.)*

> …च सर्वतो गच्छन्तम् । के, सामर्थ्यात् सारथयो मातलिप्रभृतयः । अन्येऽस्य रथं युञ्जन्ति । स नः स्वयं युनक्ति ब्रध्नादिगुणः युञ्जन्ति न किंचिदिति । एवं गुणकीर्तनादिन्द्रस्यैयं स्तुतिः । किंच तस्थुषः रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि । तस्थुष इति षष्ठीनिर्देशात् प्रभावेनेति वाक्यशेषः । स्थितस्य व्याप्रियमाणेन्द्रस्य प्रभावेन रोचन्ते दीप्यन्ते । रोचना दीप्तिस्वभावकानि नक्षत्राणि दिवि द्युलोके । कथंपुनरिन्द्रप्रभावेन नक्षत्राणि दीप्यन्ते । उच्यते । वक्ष्यते — "इन्द्रो दीर्घाय चक्षस आ सूर्यं रोहयद्दिवि" इति । सूर्यस्य प्रभावश्च सुषुम्नो नाम रश्मिः तत्संबन्धाच्चन्द्रमा नक्षत्राणि च दीप्यन्ते । अथवा युजिरुत्पूर्वार्थे । अन्तर्णीतण्यर्थश्च द्रष्टव्यः । उद्योजयन्त्युत्साहयन्ति वृष्टिकर्माणि ब्रध्नमरुषं चेन्द्रम् । किं कुर्वन्तम् । उच्यते । चरन्तं परि तस्थुषः । परिशब्दो लक्षणे कर्मप्रवचनीयः तस्थुष इत्यनेन च संबध्यते । तस्थिवःशब्दः स्थावरवचनः । गच्छन्तं स्थावराणि प्रति । स्थावरग्रहणं चात्र जङ्गमस्यापि प्रदर्शनार्थम् । सोमपानायासुरयुद्धलोलुपतया जङ्गमस्थावरात्मकं कृत्स्नं (जनम्, जगत्) परिभ्रमन्तमित्यर्थः । के उद्योजयन्ति । उच्यते । रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि । एकवाक्यताप्रसिद्ध्यर्थं यत्तच्छब्दावध्याहार्यौ । आदित्यरश्मयो रोचन्ते रोचना दिवि ते आदित्यरश्मयो हि प्रावृडारम्भे रसादातारः । ते रसानर्पयन्तः उद्योजयन्तीन्द्रं वृष्टिकर्मणि । एतस्मिन्नर्थे रश्मिविषयत्वात् रोचनेत्येतत् पदमूष्मान्तन्यायं दृश्यते न स्वरान्तमन्तो नैष पदकाराभिप्रायः । ज्योतिष्पेक्षं वा रश्मीनां नपुंसकत्वम् । अध्वर्युवस्त्वादित्यदेवताम्ऋचं मन्यन्ते । कथम् । एतेषां हि विनियोजनेऽपि युक्तश्चाश्वोऽनयादित्यरूपेणोच्यते । कथमवगम्यते । श्रुतेः । एवं हि श्रुतिर्भवति — युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषमित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रध्नः । अरुषोऽमुमेवास्मादादित्यं युनक्ति । सुवर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै इति । तस्मादादित्यदेवत्येयमिति । तन्न । तत्रापि विनियोगवशान्नियुज्यमानोऽश्वो ब्रध्नोऽरुषश्चोच्यते । भक्तिमात्रं तु श्रुतिः । अपि च यदि श्रुतिबलात् तत्रादित्यो देवता, तथा नाम इह त्वैन्द्रप्रकरणे समाना ब्रध्नारुषयोश्चेन्द्रेऽपि संभवात् । परस्यां च ऋच्यस्य शब्देनानुवादात् । तेनेहादिष्टस्य ब्रध्नस्यान्वादेशात् तस्याश्च ऋचो हरिसंबन्धाद्यैन्द्रतायाः असंदिग्धत्वाद् ऐन्द्रत्वमेवास्या ऋच इति ॥

karmapravacanīyaḥ tasthuṣa ityanena ca saṃbadhyate | tasthivaḥśabdaḥ sthāvaravacanaḥ | gacchantaṃ sthāvarāṇi prati | sthāvaragrahaṇaṃ cātra jaṅgamasyāpi pradarśanārtham | somapānāyāsurayuddhalolupatayā jaṅgamasthāvarātmakaṃ kṛtsnaṃ (janam, jagat) paribhramantamityarthaḥ | ke udyojayanti | ucyate | rocante rocanā divi | ekavākyatāprasiddhyarthaṃ yattacchabdāvadhyāhāryau | ādityaraśmayo rocante rocanā divi te ādityaraśmayo hi prāvṛḍārambhe rasādātāraḥ | te rasānarpayantaḥ udyojayantīndraṃ vṛṣṭikarmaṇi | etasminnarthe raśmiviṣayatvāt rocanetyetat padamūṣmāntanyāyaṃ dṛśyate na svarāntamanto naiṣa padakārābhiprāyaḥ | jyotiṣpekṣaṃ vā raśmīnāṃ napuṃsakatvam | adhvaryuvastvādityadevatāmṛcaṃ manyante | katham | eteṣāṃ hi viniyojane 'pi yuktaścāśvo 'nayādityarūpeṇocyate | kathamavagamyate | śruteḥ | evaṃ hi śrutirbhavati — yuñjanti bradhnamaruṣamityāha | asau vā ādityo bradhnaḥ | aruṣo 'mumevāsmādādityaṃ yunakti | suvargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai iti | tasmādādityadevatyeyamiti | tanna | tatrāpi viniyogavaśānniyujyamāno 'śvo bradhno 'ruṣaścocyate | bhaktimātraṃ tu śrutiḥ | api ca yadi śrutibalāt tatrādityo devatā, tathā nāma iha tvaindraprakaraṇe samānā bradhnāruṣayoścendre 'pi saṃbhavāt | parasyāṃ ca ṛcyasya śabdenānuvādāt | tenehādiṣṭasya bradhnasyānvādeśāt tasyāśca ṛco harisaṃbandhādyaindratāyāḥ asaṃdigdhatvād aindratvamevāsyā ṛca iti ‖*
> *(Reading notes: (i) the first words "ca sarvato gacchantam" continue the sentence broken at the foot of p. 206; (ii) re-read from the better scan: "viniyojane 'pi yuktaś cāśvo 'nayādityarūpeṇocyate | katham avagamyate," "aśvo," "tathā nāma," "ṛcy asya śabdenānuvādāt," "ādiṣṭasya … anvādeśāt," "yat-tac-chabdau," "asura-yuddha-lolupatayā," "utsāhayanti"; (iii) translated in outline.)*
> **Translation, in outline:** "…and going in every direction. Who (engages him)? By capacity, charioteers such as Mātali; others yoke his chariot; 'he himself yokes us' — one endowed with 'bradhna' and other qualities; they yoke nothing (else) (?). Thus this is praise of Indra by the proclaiming of his qualities. Further: 'tasthuṣaḥ rocante rocanā divi' — by the genitive 'tasthuṣaḥ' the supplied word is 'by the power': by the power of Indra, who is stationed and active, 'rocante' — shine; 'rocanā' — the stars, whose nature is shining, 'divi' — in heaven. How, then, do the stars shine by Indra's power? It will be said: '*Indra made the Sun rise in heaven for long sight*' (a quotation, as printed). The Sun's power is the ray called Suṣumna, and by connection with it the Moon and stars shine. Or else the root 'yuj' has the sense 'ut-' ('up'): it must be understood with the causal sense included — 'they urge up, they stir up Indra, great and ruddy, to the rain-work.' Doing what? 'Carantam pari tasthuṣaḥ' — 'pari' is a karmapravacanīya in the sense of 'around' and is connected with 'tasthuṣaḥ' — the word means 'the stationary': going toward the stationary; the mention of the stationary here is also to show the moving ones: moving around the whole world of moving and stationary beings, out of eagerness for the battle with the Asuras, for the Soma-drinking. Who stir him up? — 'rocante rocanā divi': for the unity of the sentence 'yat' and 'tat' must be supplied: the Sun's rays shine in heaven; those rays, at the beginning of the rainy season, take up the juices; offering those juices, they stir Indra to the rain-work. (Grammatical remarks on the neuter 'rocanā' follow.) … But the Adhvaryus regard the Ṛk as having the Sun for its deity. How? 'For in the application of these (mantras) the yoked horse is spoken of in the form of the Sun.' How is that known? From Śruti: '*"Yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam," it says: yonder Sun is "bradhna"; he yokes that very Sun for him, for the sake of the whole of the world of heaven (suvarga)*'; therefore this Ṛk has the Sun as its deity. — [Reply:] No. There too, by force of the application, the horse that is being yoked is called 'bradhna' and 'aruṣa'; the Śruti is only a figurative statement (bhakti-mātra). Moreover, even if the Sun were the deity by force of Śruti, here, in the context of Indra, 'bradhna' and 'aruṣa' are equally possible of Indra, and the next Ṛk repeats the sense; therefore, by the use of 'bradhna' and 'aruṇa' as designations of the horses and by the connection of this Ṛk with 'hari' (the two bay horses), its being Aindrī is unquestioned: this Ṛk is addressed to Indra alone."

*(Source note on this long argument: Skandasvāmī's chief point is that Rik 6.1 has Indra, not the Sun, as its deity; his chief ground is the connection of "bradhna" and "aruṣa" with Indra's horses and with the "harī" of the next Ṛk. The details of the Mīmāṃsā-style reasoning are given above only in outline; the Sanskrit is preserved in full for checking.)*

### Page 208 — Anuvāda of Skandasvāmī's commentary; Western and other views (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose, translated in full; the Sanskrit citations in it are given in three layers. References re-read from the better scan; the Ṛg-vedic quotation was read from an enlarged slice; the gloss is mine, tentative.)*

**Anuvāda** *(of Skandasvāmī's commentary, in Kannada)*: "Yoga" means connection. So the sense is that it supplies a connection for the verb "yuñjanti." How is there a connection between Indra and the people? One must understand that, because the people satisfy Indra with stotras and oblations, there is a relation between Indra and the people who praise him, or who worship him in sacrifices and the like. For the word "bradhna" — "mahat," great — "bradhna" is read among the twenty-five words "mahat" and the rest (Ni. 3-13-5). So if "bradhnam" is taken as a qualifier of Indra, "bradhnam indram" means "the great Indra, endowed with great capacity." "**Aruṣam**" is also a qualifier of Indra. The root "ruś" has the sense of shining, of lustre; so "aruṣam" means "one who shines." In the Ṛk

> रुशद्वत्सा रुशती श्वेत्यागादारैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-११३-२)
> *ruśadvatsā ruśatī śvety āgād āraigu kṛṣṇā sadanāny asyāḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-113-2)*
> *(Reading note: "āraigu" is as printed, clear in the better scan.)*
> Gloss (mine; tentative): "The bright one, with her calf, the shining white one, has come; the dark one has left her abodes." — and the Kannada notes: here the word "ruśat" is plainly said to mean shining, lustre. *(Sāyaṇa too gives this meaning for "ruśat" in this Ṛk.)*

Besides, according to the statement "*āruṣatyāyatīti gati-karmasu pāṭhād aruṣater gatyarthasyāruṣa-śabdo gantṛ-vacanaḥ*" (आरुषत्यायतीति गतिकर्मसु पाठादरुषतेर्गत्यर्थस्यारुषशब्दो गन्तृवचनः — "because 'āruṣati' is read among the verbs of motion, the word 'āruṣa,' from the root 'aruṣ' in the sense of going, means 'one who goes'"), from the root "āruṣati," which has the sense of going, "aruṣam" means "gantāram" — one who goes (whether to war with enemies, or to receive the oblations in sacrifices). "**Carantam**" — one who goes to all regions. The sense: wherever Indra goes, there those who praise him go and worship him. Or: "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣaṃ carantam" — wherever the powerful and shining Indra goes, there men pray to him with stotras that their own desired aims be fulfilled.

*Or:* the words "bradhnam aruṣaṃ carantam" need not be used as qualifiers of Indra. These words may be taken, with the senses "large, shining, moving everywhere," as qualifiers of the chariot. Since "yuñjanti" is said here, one may say that Indra's charioteers, such as Mātali, "yuñjanti" — "harness" (the horses to) — such a chariot. Therefore the whole discussion in this connection takes the form of praise of Indra. Since the genitive "tasthuṣaḥ" is used, one must supply after it the word "prabhāvena" ("by the power"). Having supplied it, "pari tasthuṣaḥ prabhāveṇa rocante rocanā divi" means: the rays of the Sun, shining in the sky, carrying drops of water in the rainy season, urge Indra, so that rain is produced on earth — that is, they stir him to action. That is: "the stars that shine by the power of Indra, who pervades all regions — 'rocanā,' the stars, in 'divi,' the sky — 'rocante' — shine," is the sense. How the stars shine by Indra's power is confirmed by the mantra "*indro dīrghāya cakṣase ā sūryaṃ rohayad divi*" (इन्द्रो दीर्घाय चक्षस आ सूर्यं रोहयद्दिवि — *indro dīrghāya cakṣasa ā sūryaṃ rohayad divi*; ṛ. saṃ. 1-7-3), "Indra caused the Sun to rise in the sky for far-seeing." That is: Indra placed the Sun in the heavenly region (the sky) so that the world might be lit at all times. By connection with the ray named Suṣumna, which is a power of the Sun, the Moon and the stars also …

### Page 209 — Anuvāda concluded: Skandasvāmī vs. the Brāhmaṇa; Veṅkaṭamādhava's view; where the Ṛk occurs; the question of the sūkta's deity

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose, translated; references re-read from the better scan. Veṅkaṭamādhava's Sanskrit is read from an enlarged slice and flagged.)*

*(Continuing from p. 208:)* …the stars also shine, or these rays "yuñjanti" Indra in the rain-work — that is, they stimulate him. How? The word "tasthuṣaḥ" in "carantaṃ pari tasthuṣaḥ" indicates the fixed beings, and also the moving beings; so the sense is that Indra moves among the whole world, fixed and moving, for the drinking of Soma or for fighting.

In the sacrifice, the Adhvaryu and some other priests who carry the chief role regard this Ṛk as addressed to the Sun, for the following reasons. In regard to the application of this Ṛk, the Śruti sentence (of the Brāhmaṇa) — "*yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam ity āha | asau vā ādityo bradhnaḥ | aruṣo 'mum evāsmād ādityaṃ yunakti suvargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai*" (युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नमरुषमित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रध्नः । अरुषोऽमुमेवास्मादादित्यं युनक्ति सुवर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै — "'*yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam,' he says: yonder Sun is 'bradhna'; …* [he yokes the Sun to him] for the totality of the heavenly world") — says it. Since "bradhna" is plainly said here to mean the Sun, and since the word "Indra" is not found in this Ṛk, a doubt arises, quite naturally, in the question whether this Ṛk is addressed to the Sun. But that is not right. Because "bradhna" also means "horse" (Ni. 2-27 [?]). Hence for the sentence "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣaṃ carantam" the sense "they harness the shining, swiftly moving horses (to the chariot)" fits equally of the Sun and of Indra; it does not follow that it is spoken of the Sun alone. Besides, in the next Ṛk of this sūkta the word "harī," the name of Indra's horses, is plainly given, and in the fifth Ṛk the word "Indra" is read; so this mantra must be understood as addressed to Indra.

Further, in **Veṅkaṭamādhava**'s commentary there is not much that is special; he says only:

> युञ्जन्ति ब्रध्नम् । युञ्जन्ति महान्तमरोचमानं दिवि चरन्तं तस्थिवांसो देवा वा लोका वा । रोचनानि नक्षत्राणि इन्द्रतेजसा संधुक्षितान्यहत्वेऽपि प्रसारणमन्यत्रापि दृष्टम् ॥
> *yuñjanti bradhnam | yuñjanti mahāntam arocamānaṃ divi carantaṃ tasthivāṃso devā vā lokā vā | rocanāni nakṣatrāṇi indra-tejasā sandhukṣitāny ahatve 'pi prasāraṇam anyatrāpi dṛṣṭam ||*
> *(Reading note: re-read from the better scan; the clause "ahatve 'pi prasāraṇam anyatrāpi dṛṣṭam" is as printed.)*
> **Translation (mine, following the Kannada account):** "'Yuñjanti bradhnam': the gods — or the worlds — standing about 'join' the great, (shining), moving in the sky; the 'rocanāni' are the stars, kindled by Indra's lustre. (The lengthening ['prasāraṇa'] in the word 'tasthivāṃsaḥ' is seen elsewhere also.)"

That is: **Veṅkaṭamādhava** has only repeated Skandasvāmī's meaning. "Tasthivāṃsaḥ" means the gods or the worlds, and "rocanā" the stars. Besides, he says: "Not only that the daytime is lit by Indra's lustre, but that lustre (or capacity, power) is spread everywhere."

**Where the Ṛk occurs.** The Ṛk "yuñjanti bradhnam aruṣam" is found not only in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā but also in: Sāmaveda Saṃhitā 1468; Atharvaveda Saṃhitā 20-26-4, 20-47-10, 20-69-9; Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) 23-5; Taittirīya-saṃhitā (Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda) 7-4-20-1; Maitrāyaṇīya-saṃhitā 3-16-3; Kauṣītaki-āraṇyaka 4-9 — and in Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa 3-9-4 there is an exposition of the meaning of this mantra and of the two mantras that follow it.

**The question of the sūkta's deity.** There is a dispute as to the deity of this sūkta. For it is more favourable to firm interpretation if one says that the sūkta was spoken in view of one such deity … *(continues on the next page)*

### Page 210 — The deity of Sūkta 6 debated (Oldenburg); Dr. Sitanath Pradhan's and Max Müller's renderings; Pada-meanings

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose translated; the English passages are printed in English in the source and reproduced as printed. Ṛk numbers re-read from the better scan.)*

*(Continuing the question of the sūkta's deity:)* In the Anukramaṇī it is said that the first three Ṛks and the tenth Ṛk of this sūkta are addressed to the deity Indra; that the 4th, 6th, 8th and 9th are addressed to the Maruts; and that the 5th and 7th Ṛks are addressed to both deities, Indra and the Maruts. But the scholar **Oldenberg** (so printed, in Latin type) holds that when one considers the matters presented in the sūkta, it is not the Maruts but the **Aṅgirases** who are presented in place of the Maruts; and since "Aṅgiras" is also a name of Indra, there is no subject of the Maruts in this sūkta. Moreover, there is room for the statement that a large part of this sūkta is in praise of the Sun. Even among the ancient scholars there were different views about the deities presented in this sūkta.

Since this sūkta does not present any definite sacrifice or rite, **Dr. Sitanath Pradhan** states the chief intention shown in this sūkta in this way *(English as printed in the source):*

> "It is the twilight of the early dawn; the stars are still shining. The singers yoke the sun-horse and at the same time Indra's two horses; It is the same sun who was born (at the time after the bursting open of the rock with the dawns. The patriarchs, Angirases have since regularised the sun-rise and sun-set; they who had then found out the concealed cows with the help of Indra and had then invoked Indra may the sun now appear with Indra! Indra joins in the song of the host of the devout singers. Thence come hither o wanderer; or from the bright realm of heaven. For him do our eulogies combinedly strive. We pray to Indra, for reward from here or from heaven, from the earthy or from the aerial region."

**Max Müller** explains the meaning of this Ṛk as follows *(English as printed):*

> "Those who stand around him while he moves on, harness the bright red (steed); the lights in heaven shine forth."

The Kannada adds that this rendering follows the original without the slightest departure.

According to this, we explain the Pada-meaning and the Bhāvārtha in Kannada:

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**परि तस्थुषः (pari tasthuṣaḥ)** — the people who stand all around | **अरुषम् (aruṣam)** — shining (English as printed: "spirited") | **चरन्तम् (carantam)** — one with swift movement | **ब्रध्नम् (bradhnam)** — a horse | **युञ्जन्ति (yuñjanti)** — they harness (to the chariot) | **(तस्मिन् काले) रोचना (rocanā)** — the stars, or the rays of the Sun | **दिवि (divi)** — in the sky | **रोचन्ते (rocante)** — shine.

### Page 211 — Bhāvārtha; the chariot of the Sun or of Indra; the deities of the Ṛks; Aṅgiras and Paṇi

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose translated; the verse below is read from an enlarged slice; references re-read from the better scan; the gloss is mine, tentative.)*

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

Since the Sun has just risen, his rays spread through the whole sky and shine. At this time the people who stand all around harness to the chariot the shining, strong, swift-moving horse. Since the light has just begun, the stars are still shining.

Here the doubt arises whether "ratha" (chariot) means the Sun's chariot or Indra's. Indra's chariot must have two horses. The Sun's chariot must have seven horses. But since it is said "*eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā*" (एको अश्वो वहति सप्तनामा — *eko aśvo vahati saptanāmā*; ṛ. saṃ. 1-164-2) — "one horse, of seven names, carries" — it is right to say even one horse. And the second Ṛk plainly gives the name "harī," that of Indra's two horses. For these reasons we must believe what is said in the Anukramaṇī to be authoritative.

Now we shall consider the matter that sets forth the deities of the Ṛks 4, 6, 8 and 9: In the fifth Ṛk — "*vīḷu cid ārujatnubhir guhā cid indra vahnibhiḥ | avinda usriyā anu*" — it is said that the demons called **Paṇi** carried off the cows from the world of the gods and hid them in a cave that no one could know; and that Indra, with the help of those capable of destroying the stronghold (the Maruts or the Aṅgirases), searched for them and brought them back. Here "those who are capable" — the ancient commentators such as **Sāyaṇa, Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava** say, are the "Maruts." But modern Western scholars such as **Max Müller** and **Macdonell** hold that the word "ārujatnubhiḥ" refers to the **Aṅgirases**; because —

> वीळु चिद्दृळ्हा पितरो न उक्थैरद्रिं रुजन्नङ्गिरसो रवेण ।
> चक्रुर्दिवो बृहतो गातुमस्मे अहः स्वर्विविदुः केतुमुस्राः ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-७१-२)
> *vīḷu cid dṛḷhā pitaro na ukthair adriṃ rujann aṅgiraso raveṇa |*
> *cakrur divo bṛhato gātum asme ahaḥ svar vividuḥ ketum usrāḥ || (ṛ. saṃ. 1-71-2)*
> Gloss (mine; tentative): "Our fathers, by their hymns, the Aṅgirases, breaking the firm, the rock, with their cry — they made for us a path of the great heaven; they found the day, the light, the banner, the cows."

in this Ṛk and in some other places it is said that the Aṅgirases helped Indra in seizing the demon called Paṇi; so they think that the Ṛks of this sūkta have been spoken in view of the Aṅgirases. Moreover, the German scholar **Oldenberg** is of the opinion that in all the Ṛks of this sūkta that are connected with the Maruts the meaning concerning the Aṅgirases is quite natural. Thus this matter, too, is one that has to be called disputed.

### Pages 212–213 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.1 (Kannada) — characterized; Sūkta 6, Second Mantra: Saṃhitā

*(Page headers: p. 212 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6"; p. 213 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." These two pages are **pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose** for "yuñjanti," "bradhnam," "aruṣam," "carantam," "tasthuṣaḥ," "rocante," "rocanā" and "divi"; they do not bear on the sense of Rik 6.1 (pp. 203–204 and the commentary after them). **Characterized in outline**; sūtras kept; re-read from the better scan. Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**p. 212.** **"Yuñjanti"** — the root "yujir yoge" (to join): the third-person plural "laṭ," "jhi" → "ant"; because it is a "rudhādi" root (**रुधादिभ्यः श्नम्**, पा. ३-१-७८) the vikaraṇa "śnam" comes in place of "śap"; the "m" of "śnam" is an "it" and, as an "mit" augment, it is placed after the last vowel of the stem (**मिदचोऽन्त्यात्परः**, पा. १-१-४७) — so "yu-na-j"; **झोऽन्तः** (पा. ७-१-३) and **श्नसोरल्लोपः** (पा. ६-४-१११) elide the "a" of "śnam" before a "ñit/ṅit" sārvadhātuka; **नश्चापदान्तस्य झलि** (पा. ८-३-२४) puts anusvāra for "n" before a "jhal" letter; **अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः** (पा. ८-४-५८) the "parasavarṇa" nasal: "yuñjanti." The elision of "a" by "śnasor allopaḥ" is not treated as present for anusvāra and parasavarṇa, since **न पदान्तद्विर्वचनवरेयलोपस्वरसवर्णानुस्वारदीर्घजश्चर्विधिषु** (पा. १-१-५८) bars the sthānivadbhāva of **अचः परस्मिन्पूर्वविधौ** (पा. १-१-५७) there. The "anti" of "yuñjanti" is first-syllable acute (**आद्युदात्तश्च**, पा. ३-१-३). **"Bradhnam"** — end-acute by the accent of the bare stem (prātipadika). **"Aruṣam"** — "ṛṣ/ruṣa/riṣa" (roots of injuring): "ruṣā" are the destroyers; the affix "ka" (**इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः**, पा. ३-१-१३५); the affix's acute; "na santi ruṣā yasya saḥ" — a bahuvrīhi; **नञ्सुभ्याम्** (पा. ६-२-१७२) end-acute; the second-case "am" with **अमि पूर्वः** (पा. ६-१-१०७) the pūrvarūpa, and **एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः** (पा. ८-२-५).

**p. 213.** **"Carantam"** — "śap" unaccented as "p"-marked; the "śatṛ" affix is unaccented by **तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिददुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकमनुदात्तमहन्वनोर्ङित्** (पा. ६-१-१८६); the root's accent alone remains. **"Tasthuṣaḥ"** — the root "ṣṭhā gati-nivṛttau": in "liṭ," the substitute "kvasu" (**क्वसुश्च**, पा. ३-२-१०७); the "kvasu" being "iṭ"-less here; the doubling (**लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य**, पा. ६-१-८); **शर्पूर्वाः खयः** (पा. ७-४-६१) — in the reduplicative syllable, the "kh/ay" letters that follow "ś/ṣ/s" remain; **ह्रस्वः** (पा. ७-४-५९); **अभ्यासे चर्च** (पा. ८-४-५४): "tasthā + vas"; **वस्वेकाजाद्घसाम्** (पा. ७-२-६७) — "iṭ" for "vas" after a monosyllabic root with doubling; "sthā," ending in "ā," is a root for which "iṭ" is prescribed; the print argues that, since the "iṭ" is "antaraṅga," it should come first; but by **संप्रसारणं तदाश्रयं च कार्यं बलवत्** (पा. म. ६-१-१७-२) — samprasāraṇa and what depends on it are stronger — **वसोः संप्रसारणम्** (पा. ६-४-१३१) and **संप्रसारणाच्च** (पा. ६-१-१०८) apply first, and "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" gives "ṣ," with "ru" and visarga: "tasthuṣaḥ." The affix "vasu" gives the acute. **"Rocante"** — the "tiṅ" unaccented; "śap" "p"-marked; the root-accent alone. **"Rocanā"** — **अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः** (पा. ३-२-१४९) "yuc" after a root with an unaccented marker and a consonant initial; **युवोरनाकौ** (पा. ७-१-१) "ana"; the light penultimate takes guṇa; the affix is "c"-marked, so it is end-acute (**चितः**, पा. ६-१-१६३). **"Divi"** — the case-ending is acute by **ऊडिदम्पदाद्यप्पुम्रैद्युभ्यः** (पा. ६-१-१७१). ॥१॥

### Sūkta 6, The Second Mantra

*(Accent-marks are printed on the next page; not reproduced here.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> युं॒जंत्य॑स्य॒ काम्या॒ ह॒री विप॑क्षसा॒ रथे॑ ।
> शोणा॑ धृष्णू नृ॒वाह॑सा ॥२॥
>
> *yuṃjáṃtyasya kā́myā harī́ vípakṣasā ráthe |*
> *śóṇā dhṛṣṇū nṛvā́hasā ||2||*

### Page 214 — Rik 6.2: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, re-read from the better scan.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> युञ्जन्ति । अस्य । काम्या । हरी इति । विपक्षसा । रथे ।
> शोणा । धृष्णू इति । नृवाहसा ॥२॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> अस्य ब्रध्नादिशब्दप्रतिपाद्यस्यादित्यादिमूर्तिभिस्तत्र तत्रावस्थितस्येन्द्रस्य रथे हरी एतन्नामानौ द्वावश्वौ सारथयो युञ्जन्ति । इन्द्रसंबन्धिनोरश्वयोर्हरिनामत्वं हरी इन्द्रस्य रोहितोऽग्नेः । नै. १-१५ । इति पठितत्वात् । कीदृशौ हरी । काम्या कामयितव्यौ विपक्षसा । विविधे पक्षसी रथस्य पार्श्वे ययोरश्वयोस्तौ विपक्षसौ । रथस्य द्वयोः पार्श्वयोर्योजितावित्यर्थः । शोणा रक्तवर्णौ धृष्णू प्रगल्भौ नृवाहसा नृणां पुरुषाणामिन्द्रतत्सारथिप्रमुखानां वोढारौ ॥
> *asya bradhnādiśabdapratipādyasyādityādimūrtibhistatra tatrāvasthitasyendrasya rathe harī etannāmānau dvāvaśvau sārathayo yuñjanti | indrasaṃbandhinoraśvayorharināmatvaṃ harī indrasya rohito 'gneḥ | nai. 1-15 | iti paṭhitatvāt | kīdṛśau harī | kāmyā kāmayitavyau vipakṣasā | vividhe pakṣasī rathasya pārśve yayoraśvayostau vipakṣasau | rathasya dvayoḥ pārśvayoryojitāvityarthaḥ | śoṇā raktavarṇau dhṛṣṇū pragalbhau nṛvāhasā nṛṇāṃ puruṣāṇāmindratatsārathipramukhānāṃ voḍhārau ‖*
> *(Reading note: re-read from the better scan: "harī etan-nāmānau," "ādityādi-mūrtibhiḥ," "yayor aśvayoḥ"; the Nighaṇṭu reference "nai. 1-15" is clear.)*

**Translation:** "Of this (Indra) — who is conveyed by the words 'bradhna' and the rest, abiding here and there in the forms of Āditya and the rest — in his chariot the two horses named Hari — 'sārathayaḥ' — the charioteers 'yuñjanti' — yoke. That the two horses connected with Indra bear the name 'harī' is because it is read (in the Nighaṇṭu list of horse-names): '*harī indrasya, rohito 'gneḥ*' (Naighaṇṭuka 1-15). What kind of 'harī'? 'Kāmyā' — to be desired, desirable. 'Vipakṣasā' — those two (horses) which are yoked on the two various sides ('pakṣasī') of the chariot — yoked on both flanks of the chariot, the sense. 'Śoṇā' — red-coloured; 'dhṛṣṇū' — bold; 'nṛvāhasā' — the two bearers of men: Indra, his charioteer and the chief among them."

**Grammar within the Bhāṣya (re-read from the better scan; sūtras kept):** "Asya" — as it refers back to what was called "bradhna," **इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ** (पा. २-४-३२) gives "aś"; being "ś"-marked it replaces the whole (पा. १-१-५५) and is unaccented; the case-ending is unaccented too, so the word is wholly unaccented. "Kāmyā" — "kamu kāntau," **कमेर्णिङ्** (पा. ३-१-३०); then **अचो यत्** (पा. ३-१-९७); by **यतोऽनावः** (पा. ६-१-२१३), an exception to the "tit-svarita," first-syllable acute; the dual ending replaced by "ḍā" (**सुपां सुलुक्…**). "Harī" — "harato ratham": the Uṇādi **हृपिषि…** (उ. सू. ४-११८) the affix "in"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Vipakṣasā" — **पचिवचिभ्यां सुट् च** (उ. सू. ४-२१९): "asun" after "pac" with the augment "suṭ"; "vibhinne pakṣasī pārśve yayoḥ tau" — the bahuvrīhi; "vi" being a particle is acute, and the first member's accent is kept; "ḍā" for the dual. "Rathe" — "ramante 'sminn iti rathaḥ": **हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन्** (उ. सू. २-२) "kthan"; as it is "k"-marked, **अनुदात्तोपदेश…** (पा. ६-४-३७) elides the "m"; first-syllable acute by the "n"-mark. "Śoṇā" — "śoṇṛ varṇa-gatyoḥ": as the means of going, "ghañ" in the instrumental sense; "ñ"-marked, first-syllable acute; "ḍā" for the dual. "Dhṛṣṇū" — "ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye": **त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः** (पा. ३-२-१४०); "k"-marked, so no guṇa; the affix accent. "Nṛvāhasā" — "nṝn vahata iti": **वहिहाधाञ्भ्यश्छन्दसि** (उ. सू. ४-२२०) "asun"; with "ṇit" continued, vṛddhi; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute; by the accent of the kṛt-final second member this remains. ॥२॥

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated; continued on the next page)*

(The charioteers and others) **अस्य (asya)** — (as said before, the one who is conveyed by the words "Āditya" and the rest) of this Indra | **रथे (rathe)** — in the chariot (to the chariot) | **काम्या (kāmyā)** — (to Indra) beloved, or dear | **शोणा (śoṇā)** — …

### Page 215 — Rik 6.2: Pada-meanings concluded; Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose translated; English as printed; references re-read from the better scan.)*

*(Continuing the Pada-meanings from p. 214:)* **शोणा (śoṇā)** — red-coloured | **धृष्णू (dhṛṣṇū)** — full of enthusiasm | **नृवाहसा (nṛvāhasā)** — those who carry Indra and the charioteer (who have taken the form of men) | **विपक्षसा (vipakṣasā)** — yoked to the left and right flanks of the chariot | **हरी (harī)** — the two horses | **युञ्जन्ति (yuñjanti)** — they yoke (they harness).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

The charioteer and others yoke Indra's two favourite horses, on the two flanks, left and right, to Indra's chariot. Those horses, though red in colour, are full of enthusiasm and have the capacity to carry men — that is, their master Indra, the charioteer and others. Such excellent horses they yoke to Indra's chariot.

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"They are harnessing to his (Indra's) chariot, one on each side, his favourite pair of bay coloured horses, high-spirited and able to carry their brave lord."

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The pāda "yuñjanty asya kāmyā" is quoted in the **Āpastamba-śrauta-sūtra** (20-16-2) and the **Maitrāyaṇīya-saṃhitā** (9-2-3 [as printed]). In the **Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa** (3-9-4) there is an exposition of this Ṛk. There it says "*śoṇā dhṛṣṇū nṛvāhasety āha | aho rātre vai nṛvāhasā*" (शोणा धृष्णू नृवाहसेत्याह । अहो रात्रे वै नृवाहसा — "'*śoṇā dhṛṣṇū nṛvāhasā,' he says: day and night, indeed, are the 'nṛvāhasā'*") — that is, for the word "nṛvāhasā" an adhyātmika meaning, "day and night," is given; nothing further of special note.

**काम्या (kāmyā)** — wished-for, dear; favourite. **हरी (harī)** — Indra's two horses have the name "harī." **विपक्षसा (vipakṣasā)** — the separate flanks, that is, the left and right flanks. **रथे (rathe)** — "ramante 'smin iti rathaḥ" (रमन्तेऽस्मिन्निति रथः — "that in which they delight is the 'ratha'") — "ramu krīḍāyām" (to play): because one sits in it and moves, it is called "ratha." **शोणा (śoṇā)** — *(English as printed)* "crimson, bright, bay or chestnut." **धृष्णू (dhṛṣṇū)** — full of enthusiasm; *(English)* "fiery, high-spirited." **नृवाहसा (nṛvāhasā)** — those who have the capacity to carry (or to draw) men. The words "kāmyā, harī, vipakṣasā, śoṇā, dhṛṣṇū, nṛvāhasā" are all second-case dual words, and are qualifiers of the word "harī."

### Page 216 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.2 (Kannada) — characterized

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, restating the Sanskrit of p. 214; **characterized in outline**, re-read from the better scan; sūtras kept.)*

**"Asya"** — as Indra, conveyed in the previous mantra by "bradhna" and the rest, is referred back to by "asya," this "idam" is in a back-reference (anvādeśa); so **इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ** (पा. २-४-३२) gives the unaccented substitute "aś"; being "ś"-marked, by **अनेकाल्शित्सर्वस्य** (पा. १-१-५५) it replaces the whole of "idam"; the case-ending is unaccented too, so "asya" is wholly unaccented. **"Kāmyā"** — "kamu kāntau": **कमेर्णिङ्** (पा. ३-१-३०); **अत उपधायाः** (पा. ७-२-११६) → "kāmi"; **सनाद्यन्ता धातवः** (पा. ३-१-३२); **अचो यत्** (पा. ३-१-९७); **णेरनिटि** (पा. ६-४-५१) → "kāmya"; the svarita of **तित्स्वरितम्** (पा. ६-१-१८५) is set aside by **यतोऽनावः** (पा. ६-१-२१३), first-syllable acute; the second-case dual "au" → "ḍā" (**सुपां सुलुक्**, पा. ७-१-३९). **"Harī"** — "harataḥ ratham": the Uṇādi **हृपिषि…** (उ. सू. ४-५५८ [as printed]; "4-118" on p. 214) the affix "in"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. **"Vipakṣasā"** — **पचिवचिभ्यां सुट् च** (उ. सू. ८-३-४१ [as printed]): after "ḍupacaṣ pāke" and "vaca paribhāṣaṇe" "asun" with the augment "suṭ"; "pac + s + as" → **चोः कुः** (पा. ८-२-३०) "k"; **आदेशप्रत्यययोः** (पा. ८-३-५९) "ṣ" → "pakṣas"; "vibhinne pakṣasī pārśve yayoḥ tau vipakṣasau" — a bahuvrīhi; "vi" a particle, first-syllable acute; **बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम्** (पा. ६-२-१) retains it; the dual → "ḍā" (पा. ७-१-३९). **"Rathe"** — "ramante 'sminn iti rathaḥ": the Uṇādi **हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन्** (उ. सू. २-१४९ [as printed]; "2-2" on p. 214); "k"-marked, so **अनुदात्तोपदेश…** (पा. ६-४-३७) elides the "m"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute.

### Page 217 — Rik 6.2 grammar concluded; Sūkta 6, Third Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Sanskrit printed in Kannada script. Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.)*

**"Śoṇā"** *(concluding the grammar of Rik 6.2)* — "śoṇṛ varṇa-gatyoḥ" (colour, going); the affix "ghañ" in the instrument sense (the horses are the means of going); "ñit," so first-syllable acute; the dual "au" is replaced by "ā" (**सुपां सुलुक्…**, पा. ७-१-३९). **"Dhṛṣṇū"** — "ñidhṛṣā prāgalbhye" (to be bold) — the affix "knu" (**त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः**, पा. ३-२-१४०); "kit," so no guṇa for the light penultimate (**क्ङिति च**, पा. १-१-५); the affix's accent. **"Nṛvāhasā"** — "nṝn vahataḥ" — an etymological analysis ("those who carry men"); the Uṇādi **वहिहाधाञ्भ्यश्छन्दसि** (उ. सू. ४-६६० [as printed]) "asun" after these roots in the Veda; "ṇit" by continuation (**णिदित्यनुवृत्तेः**), vṛddhi of "vah" → "vāh-as" (**अत उपधायाः**, पा. ७-२-११६); the dual "ā" (**सुपां सुलुक्**); the whole is first-syllable acute as "n"-marked; **गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्** (पा. ६-२-१३९; printed "6-2-149") — the kṛt-final member's accent retained, so the first-syllable acute stands. ॥२॥
