### Sūkta 6, The Third Mantra

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> के॒तुं कृण्वन्न॑के॒तवे॒ पेशो॑ मर्या अपे॒शसे॑ ।
> समु॒षद्भि॑रजायथाः ॥३॥
>
> *ketúṃ kṛṇvánnaketáve péśo maryā apeśáse |*
> *samuṣádbhirajāyathāḥ ||3||*
>
> *(Accent note: the mark over "dbhi" is printed as a "T"-shaped sign, a stroke with a cross-bar; given here as svarita.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> केतुम् । कृण्वन् । अकेतवे । पेशः । मर्याः । अपेशसे ।
> सम् । उषत्ऽभिः । अजायथाः ॥३॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(opening, p. 217)*

> हे मर्या मनुष्या इदमाश्चर्यं पश्यतेत्यध्याहारः । किमाश्चर्यमिति तदुच्यते । आदित्यरूपोऽयमिन्द्र उषद्भिर्दाहकै रश्मिभिः प्रतिदिनमुषःकाले वा संभूयाजायथाः । उदपद्यत । अथवा सूर्यस्यैवास्तमये मरणमुपचर्य । व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं कृत्वा संबोधनं क्रियते । हे मर्य प्रतिदिनं त्वमजायथा इति योज्यं किं कुर्वन् । अकेतवे रात्रौ निद्राभिभूतत्वेन प्रज्ञानरहिताय
> *he maryā manuṣyā idamāścaryaṃ paśyatetyadhyāhāraḥ | kimāścaryamiti taducyate | ādityarūpo 'yamindra uṣadbhirdāhakai raśmibhiḥ pratidinamuṣaḥkāle vā saṃbhūyājāyathāḥ | udapadyata | athavā sūryasyaivāstamaye maraṇamupacarya | vyatyayena bahuvacanaṃ kṛtvā saṃbodhanaṃ kriyate | he marya pratidinaṃ tvamajāyathā iti yojyaṃ kiṃ kurvan | aketave rātrau nidrābhibhūtatvena prajñānarahitāya*
> *(Reading notes: the page ends at "prajñāna-rahitāya" and the sentence continues on the next page; "maryā" is the sandhi form of "maryāḥ"; re-read from the better scan ("dāhakai raśmibhiḥ," "sambhūyājāyathāḥ").)*

**Translation (of the part on this page):** "'O "maryāḥ" — O men! — behold this wonder': this is the supplied sense. What is the wonder? It is said: this Indra, who is of the form of the Sun, is born every day, becoming one with the burning rays, at dawn — he arises. Or: since the very setting of the Sun is a figurative 'death,' the vocative plural is used by a change of number — 'O mortal! you are born every day' (the sentence is to be construed so). Doing what? 'Aketave' — for the one (in the night) without understanding, overcome by sleep …" *(continues on the next page)*.

### Page 218 — Rik 6.3: Bhāṣya concluded; grammar (characterized); Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, read from enlarged slices; [?] where unclear. References re-read from the better scan.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(concluding)*

> प्राणिने केतुं कृण्वन् । प्रातः प्रज्ञानं कुर्वन् । अपेशसे रात्र्यान्धकारावृतत्वेनानभिव्यक्तत्वाद्रूपरहिताय पदार्थाय प्रातरन्धकारनिवारणेन पेशो रूपमभिव्यज्यमानं कुर्वन् । पेश इति रूपनामानि पिंशतेः । नि. ८-११ [as printed] । इति यास्कः । अकेतवेऽपेशस इति चतुर्थी षष्ठ्यर्थे द्रष्टव्या ॥
> *prāṇine ketuṃ kṛṇvan | prātaḥ prajñānaṃ kurvan | apeśase rātry-āndhakārāvṛtatvenānabhivyaktatvād rūpa-rahitāya padārthāya prātar-andhakāra-nivāraṇena peśo rūpam abhivyajyamānaṃ kurvan | peśa iti rūpa-nāmāni piṃśateḥ | ni. 8-11 [as printed] | iti yāskaḥ | aketave 'peśasa iti caturthī ṣaṣṭhy-arthe draṣṭavyā ||*

**Translation:** "Giving 'ketu' (awareness) to the living being: making knowledge (prajñāna) in the morning; 'apeśase' — to an object that, being covered by the darkness of night, is unmanifest and so is without form — making 'peśaḥ,' form, to be manifested by the removal of the morning-darkness. 'Peśaḥ' is a name for form, from 'piṃś' (to adorn) — thus Yāska (Nirukta "8-11" as printed). 'Aketave' and 'apeśase' are datives to be understood in the sense of the genitive."

**Grammar within the Bhāṣya (characterized, sūtras kept, re-read from the better scan):** "Ketum" — a bare stem, acute by its own accent (prātipadika-svara). "Kṛṇvan" — "kṛvi hiṃsā-karaṇayoś ca" (to injure, to do): the substitute "śatṛ" for "laṭ"; **इदितो नुम् धातोः** (पा. ७-१-५८) the augment "num"; "śap" might arise but **धिन्विकृण्व्योर च** (पा. ३-१-८०) — the affix "u" after "dhinv" and "kṛṇv," and "a" for the final "v" — "kṛṇv" + "u"; **अतो लोपः** (पा. ६-४-४८) elides the "a"; since that elision is treated as present (sthānivadbhāva), the guṇa of the light penultimate by **पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च** (पा. ७-३-८६; printed "7-4-86") does not occur; the accent is the affix's. "Aketave" — a bahuvrīhi with "nañ"; **नञ्सुभ्याम्** (पा. ६-२-१७२) makes the second member end-acute. "Peśaḥ" — a "sab-viṣaya"-class neuter stem, first-syllable acute (**नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य**, फि. सू. २-३). "Maryāḥ" — in the Veda "mṛ" with "kyap" (**छन्दसि निष्टर्क्यदेवहूयप्रणीयोन्नीयोच्छिष्यमर्यस्तर्यध्वर्यखन्यखान्यदेवयज्याऽऽपृच्छ्यप्रतिषीव्यब्रह्मवाद्यभाव्यस्ताव्योपचाय्यपृड्यानि**, पा. ३-१-१२३; the print quotes it as "chandasi niṣṭarkyety ādau") — "mṛ + kyap" — "marya"; the vocative loses its accent (**आमन्त्रितस्य च**, पा. ८-१-१९; printed "8-1-18" [?]); since there is no mutual connection of sense with the preceding word, "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not occur. "Apeśase" — **नञ्सुभ्याम्** — end-acute. "Sam" — a particle, first-syllable acute. "Uṣadbhiḥ" — "uṣa plusa dāhe" (to burn): "laṭ" and its substitute "śatṛ"; "śap" would arise, but by vyatyaya "śa" (the tudādi vikaraṇa); the sārvadhātuka is not "p"-marked (**सार्वधातुकमपित्**, पा. १-२-४), so no guṇa for the light penultimate; "śa" gives the accent by the affix's acute; and since "śatṛ" is unaccented (the root's upadeśa-based), the "lasārvadhātuka" is unaccented; the single substitute is acute (**एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः**). "Ajāyathāḥ" — in the sense "ajāyata" the second-person verb stands for the third (by vyatyaya), and by **पुरुषव्यत्ययो निघातः** — by the change of person, no nighāta.

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**(हे) मर्याः (he maryāḥ)** — O men (look at this wonder) | **आदित्यरूपनादे (ādityarūpanāde)** — (Indra) who has the form of the Sun | **उषद्भिः (uṣadbhiḥ)** — daily at dawn, with the rays | **अकेतवे (aketave)** — to those who, because of sleep at night, are without understanding | **केतुम् (ketum)** — (at dawn, awakening) understanding | **अपेशसे (apeśase)** — (at night) to things that, covered by darkness, cannot be seen as having any form, giving light | **पेशः (peśaḥ)** — (of things) each of their forms (the power to see them) | **कृण्वन् (kṛṇvan)** — making | **सं अजायथाः (saṃ ajāyathāḥ)** — he is born (appears).

*Or:* **मर्याः (maryāḥ)** — O man (the plural used for the singular) | **(त्वम्) (tvam)** — you | **उषद्भिः (uṣadbhiḥ)** … **समजायथाः (samajāyathāḥ)** — every day, at the time of sunset, like one who dies, you become without understanding, and at morning you are born with consciousness; so we say: "be aware."

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated; opening)*

O Indra! You, in the form of the Sun, rise every day at dawn, and set at sunset; when you set, creatures are overcome by sleep …

### Page 219 — Rik 6.3: Bhāvārtha concluded; English rendering; Special topics

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose translated; English as printed; references re-read from the better scan.)*

*(Concluding the Bhāvārtha from p. 218:)* …creatures are overcome by sleep, and are without consciousness, and from the darkness of night are unable to see the forms of anything. When you rise at dawn, creatures awake and, with consciousness or understanding, are able to see the forms of all things in the light. Therefore, to the creatures who are overcome by sleep, you give — every day — consciousness, and the power to see the forms of all things.

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"O mortals, (look at this wonder). Indra (in the form of Aditya) rises every day at dawn giving sense to the senseless (while in sleep) and form to the formless.
or  O mortal, having been dead (asleep) at the setting of the sun you are born ever with morning rays."

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The meaning of this Ṛk is not plain. For the word "ketu," the Nirukta (Ni. 3-9) says "prajñā" (understanding). In the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa (3-9-4) it is said that "ketu" means "dhvaja" (banner): "*ketuṃ kṛṇvann aketave iti dhvajaṃ pratimuñcati*" (केतुं कृण्वन्नकेतव इति ध्वजं प्रतिमुञ्चति — "'*ketuṃ kṛṇvann aketave,' with this he fastens the banner*"); when setting up a banner they recite this mantra. Though "ketu" has the sense of "banner," that sense does not fit here. Those who follow the method laid down in the Gṛhyasūtras recite this mantra in order to invoke the "ketu-graha" (the planet Ketu) when they perform the worship of the nine planets (navagraha); but in this mantra there is no subject concerning the planet Ketu. Since the word "ketu" alone is common to both, this is likely to be a customary (rūḍha) use; likewise the use of mantras that contain the names of other planets in the worship and invocation of those planets is probably a conventional one. For in the Ṛgveda there is no consideration of the nine planets. Only the two names, Sūrya and Candra, are found there. The names of the stars are not there either. Only in the Yajurveda are the names of the stars, and the descriptions of the full-moon and new-moon days, explained. The names of the nine planets are not there either. Therefore it may be said without doubt that the worship of the planets (graha-yajña) was not in use in the time of the Vedas and came into custom later.

**पेशः (peśaḥ)** — "*peśa iti rūpa-nāma piṃśate*" (पेश इति रूपनाम पिंशते — "'peśa' is a name of form, from 'piṃś'," Ni. 8-11 [as printed]); "peśa" means form. **अपेशसे (apeśase)** — to one without form.

**मर्याः (maryāḥ)** — men. This word is the first-case plural. In this Ṛk the verb "ajāyathāḥ" is in the second person, singular … *(continues on the next page)*

### Page 220 — Special topics on Rik 6.3 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose translated; grammar characterized, sūtras kept; re-read from the better scan.)*

*(Continuing "maryāḥ" from p. 219:)* …the verb "ajāyathāḥ" is in the second-person singular; if "maryāḥ" were taken as the agent (kartṛ), then, since the verb is singular, the two do not agree. For the convenience of the metre the singular "marya" is used in the long form "maryā," say some; but in such cases there is no cause for such a metrical advantage or disadvantage here; for after the word "maryā" comes "apeśase," and the final long "ā" of "maryā" should have combined with the first "a" of the following word (by savarṇa-dīrgha), which has not happened here. Besides, in the Pada-text the plural word with the visarga, "maryāḥ," is plainly given. Therefore, as Sāyaṇa has said at the beginning of his Bhāṣya, this word should be said to be used merely for addressing ordinary people (the public). Western scholars hold the same view. In the view that uses the singular "marya," the agent-word "tvam" must be supplied here.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept)*

**"Ketum"** — **फिषः** (फि. सू. १) — by the bare-stem accent, "ketu" is end-acute. **"Kṛṇvan"** — "kṛvi hiṃsā-karaṇayoś ca" (to injure; to do): after "laṭ," the substitute "śatṛ" (**लटः शतृशानचावप्रथमासमानाधिकरणे**, पा. ३-२-१२४); the root is "i"-marked (**इदितो नुम् धातोः**, पा. ७-१-५८), so "num" is added; by the paribhāṣā **मिदचोऽन्त्यात्परः** (पा. १-१-४७) the "num" is placed after the last vowel: "kṛṇv"; the agent-affix "śap" would come by **कर्तरि शप्** (पा. ३-१-६८), but, as it would be unsuitable, by **धिन्विकृण्व्योर च** (पा. ३-१-८०) — after "dhinv" and "kṛṇv," the final "v" is replaced by "a," and in place of the "śap" vikaraṇa the affix "u" comes — "kṛṇ + u + at"; **अतो लोपः** (पा. ६-४-४८; printed "3-1-80") — an "a" before an ārdhadhātuka that begins with a vowel is elided — the "a" before "u" is elided; then **पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च** (पा. ७-३-८६) would give guṇa to the light penultimate before a sārvadhātuka or ārdhadhātuka affix, but the "a"-elision is treated as present, **अचः परस्मिन्पूर्वविधौ** (पा. १-१-५७) — so the guṇa does not occur. *(The page ends in the middle of an argument about whether a single intervening letter blocks the operation — "vyavadhāna" — concluding that a mere letter-interposition does not prevent the rule when a rule's own wording requires it ("vacana-prāmāṇyāt"); it continues on the next page.)*

### Pages 221–222 — Rik 6.3 grammar concluded (characterized); Sūkta 6, Fourth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

*(Page headers: p. 221 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā"; p. 222 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." The grammar on p. 221 and the top of p. 222 is **pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose**, restating the Sanskrit of p. 218; **characterized in outline**, sūtras kept; re-read from the better scan. Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Sanskrit printed in Kannada script.)*

**p. 221 — "kṛṇvan" (concluded) and the other words of Rik 6.3.** *(Continuing p. 220:)* …even with many interposed letters the rule does not apply; but here, through sthānivadbhāva, the "n" and "a" interpose and so no guṇa comes: "kṛṇ + u + at." Taking the "śatṛ" as the ground, **सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः** (पा. ७-३-८४) would give guṇa, but it is barred by **क्ङिति च** (पा. १-१-५); **इकोयणचि** (पा. ६-१-७७) gives the "y/v" substitute → "kṛṇv-at"; since "śatṛ" is not at the beginning of the (substituted) stem, **तास्यनुदात्तेन्ङिद…** does not give it the unaccented; the affix-accent holds: "śatṛ" is acute on its "a." **ऋवर्णान्नस्य णत्वं वाच्यम्** (पा. ८-४-११ [as printed]) — "ṇ" for "n" after "ṛ," so "kṛṇv"; then "su" … **उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः** (पा. ७-१-७०) the "num" augment; **हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल्** (पा. ६-१-६८) elides "su"; **संयोगान्तस्य लोपः** (पा. ८-२-२३) elides the "t"; the elision being "asiddha," the "n" is not elided: **"kṛṇvan."** **"Aketave"** — a "nañ" bahuvrīhi (**नञ्सुभ्याम्**, पा. ६-२-१७२), second member end-acute. **"Peśaḥ"** — first-syllable acute (**नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य**, फि. सू. २६ [printed "Gā. sū. 26"]). **"Maryāḥ"** — **छन्दसि निष्टर्क्य…मर्यस्तर्यध्वर्य…** (पा. ३-१-१२३): in the Veda these forms are given as nipātanas, and "yat" after "mṛṅ" is so given; since "marya" is among the nipātanas, being a vocative it is unaccented (**आमन्त्रितस्य च**, पा. ८-१-१९); "peśaḥ" and "maryāḥ" have no mutual connection, so "parāṅgavad-bhāva" does not occur (**सुबामन्त्रिते पराङ्गवत्स्वरे**, पा. २-१-२). **"Apeśase"** — **नञ्सुभ्याम्**, end-acute. **"Sam"** — a particle, first-syllable acute. **"Uṣadbhiḥ"** — "uṣa dāhe" (to burn): "laṭ" and "śatṛ"; in place of "śap," by vyatyaya, the vikaraṇa "śa"; the sārvadhātuka is not "p"-marked, so no guṇa for the light penultimate (**क्ङिति च**); "śa" is acute by the affix accent; but the following "śatṛ," being a lasārvadhātuka after an anudātta-upadeśa root, is unaccented …

**p. 222 — "uṣadbhiḥ" and "ajāyathāḥ" concluded.** *(Continuing:)* …the "a" of "śa" and the "a" of "śatṛ" — since both are "a" — combine as pararūpa (**अतो गुणे**, पा. ६-१-९४), and the single substitute from the acute and unaccented is acute (**एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः**, पा. ८-२-५). **"Ajāyathāḥ"** — a second-person form standing, by vyatyaya, for the third-person "ajāyata"; it is unaccented by **तिङ्ङतिङः** (पा. ८-१-२८). ॥३॥

### Sūkta 6, The Fourth Mantra

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आदह॑ स्व॒धामनु॒ पुन॑र्गर्भ॒त्वमे॑रि॒रे ।
> दधा॑ना॒ नाम॑ य॒ज्ञि॑यं ॥४॥
>
> *ādáha svadhā́manu púnargarbhatvámeriré |*
> *dádhānā nā́ma yajñiyaṃ ||4||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आत् । अह । स्वधाम् । अनु । पुनः । गर्भत्वम् । आ । ईरिरे ।
> दधानाः । नाम । यज्ञियम् ॥४॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(opening)*

> अत्रास्ति विशेषविनियोगः । चतुर्विंशेऽहनि प्रातःसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्र आदह स्वधामन्निति द्वे ऋचौ । इन्द्रेण सं हि दृक्षस इत्येका । अयं तृचः षळहस्तोत्रियसंज्ञकः । तथा च सूत्रितं चतुर्विंशे होताजनिष्वेति खण्डे । इन्द्रेण सं हि दृक्षस आदह स्वधामन्नित्येका द्वे च । आ. ७-२ । इति । यद्यप्येतदैन्द्रं सूक्तं तथाप्यादहेत्यादिषु षट्सु मारुतो वर्ण्यन्ते । प्रायेणैन्द्रे मारुत इत्यनुक्रमणिकायामुक्तत्वात् । अनु. २-२२ ॥ आदित्ययमानन्तर्यार्थो निपातः । अहेत्यवधारणार्थः । आदह वर्षतोरनन्तरमेव । स्वधामनु । इतः परं जनिष्यमाणमन्नमुदकं वानुलक्ष्य मरुतो देवा गर्भत्वमेरिरे । मेघमध्ये जलस्य गर्भाकारं प्रेरितवन्तः । जलस्य कर्तारं पर्जन्यं प्रेरितवन्तः । प्रतिसंवत्सरमेवं कुर्वन्तीति दर्शयितुं पुनःशब्दः प्रयुक्तः । कीदृशा मरुतः । यज्ञियं यज्ञार्हं नाम दधानाः धारयन्तः । सप्तसु गणेषु मरुतामावृज्ञान्यावृज्ञेत्यादीनि यज्ञयोग्यानि नामान्यन्यत्राम्नातानि । अन्ध इत्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेष्वन्ननामसूर्क्र रसः …
> *atrāsti viśeṣaviniyogaḥ | caturviṃśe 'hani prātaḥsavane brāhmaṇācchaṃsiśastra ādaha svadhāmanniti dve ṛcau | indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣasa ityekā | ayaṃ tṛcaḥ ṣaḷahastotriyasaṃjñakaḥ | tathā ca sūtritaṃ caturviṃśe hotājaniṣveti khaṇḍe | indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣasa ādaha svadhāmannityekā dve ca | ā. 7-2 | iti | yadyapyetadaindraṃ sūktaṃ tathāpyādahetyādiṣu ṣaṭsu māruto varṇyante | prāyeṇaindre māruta ityanukramaṇikāyāmuktatvāt | anu. 2-22 ‖ ādityayamānantaryārtho nipātaḥ | ahetyavadhāraṇārthaḥ | ādaha varṣatoranantarameva | svadhāmanu | itaḥ paraṃ janiṣyamāṇamannamudakaṃ vānulakṣya maruto devā garbhatvamerire | meghamadhye jalasya garbhākāraṃ preritavantaḥ | jalasya kartāraṃ parjanyaṃ preritavantaḥ | pratisaṃvatsaramevaṃ kurvantīti darśayituṃ punaḥśabdaḥ prayuktaḥ | kīdṛśā marutaḥ | yajñiyaṃ yajñārhaṃ nāma dadhānāḥ dhārayantaḥ | saptasu gaṇeṣu marutāmāvṛjñānyāvṛjñetyādīni yajñayogyāni nāmānyanyatrāmnātāni | andha ityādiṣvaṣṭāviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣvannanāmasūrkra rasaḥ …*
> *(Reading notes: (i) re-read from the better scan: "ā. 7-2," "anu. 2-22," "ād ity ayam ānantaryārtho nipātaḥ | aheti…"; (ii) "āvṛjñān yāvṛjñety" is crowded and given as read — the Marut names listed elsewhere; (iii) the last line ends mid-list at the foot of the page and continues on p. 223.)*

**Translation (of the part on this page):** "Here is a special application: on the twenty-fourth day, at the morning pressing, in the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's śastra, the two Ṛks beginning 'ād aha svadhām anu' and the one 'indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase' are used. This tṛca is called the 'ṣaḷaha-stotriya.' So it is laid down in the Sūtra, in the section 'caturviṃśe hotājaniṣva': '*indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣasa — one; ād aha svadhām anu — and two*' (Āśv. 7-2). Although this sūkta is addressed to Indra, in the six Ṛks beginning 'ādaha' the Maruts are described; because the Anukramaṇī says 'mostly in an Indra (sūkta), the Maruts' (Anu. 2-22). 'Āt' is a particle in the sense of 'immediately after'; 'aha' is in the sense of emphasis: 'ād aha' — immediately after the raining. 'Svadhām anu' — looking to the coming food, or to the water, the Maruts, the gods, 'garbhatvam erire' — drove (set in motion) the form of a germ of water in the midst of the cloud: they impelled Parjanya, the maker of water. The word 'punaḥ' is used to show that they do this every year. What kind of Maruts? 'Yajñiyam nāma dadhānāḥ' — bearing a name fit for sacrifice. In the seven groups of the Maruts, names fit for sacrifice are recited elsewhere. Among the twenty-eight names of food beginning with 'andha,' 'ūrk' and 'rasaḥ' …" *(continues on the next page)*.

> *(Reading notes: (i) the first line carries on the Nighaṇṭu sentence from p. 222 ("…rasaḥ svadheti paṭhitam"); I give it as read; (ii) "svadheti paṭhitam" — "svadhā is read" among the food-names, and among the names of water; (iii) re-read from the better scan ("arṇa," "svadhākṣaram," "nipātāv," "āṅā saha," 8-1-39).)*

**Translation (sense in full; grammar in outline):** "'…svadhā' is read (among the food-names); among the hundred-and-one names of water beginning with 'arṇa,' 'tejaḥ,' 'svadhā' and 'akṣaram' are read. 'Ād aha' — a particle, first-syllable acute. 'Svadhām' — 'svaṃ lokaṃ dadhāti puṣṇātīti' — 'it supports, nourishes its own world': 'svadhā'; (affix) 'ka' (Pāṇini 3-2-3) after a root ending in ā when no prefix; the kṛt-final member's accent is retained. 'Anu' and 'punaḥ' are both particles, first-syllable acute. 'Garbhatvam' — 'garbhasya bhāvo garbhatvam' — the state of a germ; accent of the affix. 'Erire' — from 'īr gatau' (to go, to move), with the causal sense included; the substitute 'irec' for 'jha' of the 'liṭ' after a root with an unaccented marker (Pāṇini 3-4-81); end-acute by the 'c'-mark. 'Saha supā' (Pāṇini 2-1-4) — here, by dividing the sūtra at 'supā,' the compound of 'ā' (prefix) with the verb takes (in a compound) the accent of the whole compound, end-acute (Pāṇini 6-1-223); 'ām' does not come, since this is a mantra. By connection with the word 'aha' there is no nighāta (Pāṇini 8-1-39, 'tupaśyapaśyatāhaiḥ pūjāyām' — the prohibition). 'Dadhānāḥ' — where 'śānac' being 'c'-marked would be end-acute, **अभ्यस्तानामादिः** (पा. ६-१-१८९) gives first-syllable acute. 'Yajñiyam' — 'yajñam arhatīti yajñiyam': by 'yajña-ṛtvigbhyāṃ ghakhañau' (Pāṇini 5-1-71) the affix 'gha,' replaced by 'iya' (Pāṇini 7-1-2); the 'i' is acute by the affix's accent."

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**आत् अह (āt aha)** — immediately after (the end of the rainy season) | **यज्ञियम् (yajñiyam)** — worthy of sacrifice | **नाम (nāma)** — name | **दधानाः (dadhānāḥ)** — bearing (the Maruts, that is, the Marut-deities) | **स्वधाम् अनु (svadhām anu)** — (to produce) food in the form of grain (that must grow later) and water | **पुनः (punaḥ)** — again (now too, as in the previous rainy season) | **गर्भत्वम् (garbhatvam)** — (the water that gathers together in the cloud, as a germ) the water gathering in the cloud | **एरिरे (erire)** — impelled (that is, impelled Parjanya, who produces the rain).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

After the rainy season has passed, the Marut-deities, who are famous by names honoured in sacrifices and the like, in order to give people grain in the form of food and water, again, as before, now also, as a part of the work of rain, impelled Parjanya, so that, like a germ, the water gathers together in the midst of the clouds.

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"Thereafter (the Maruts) who bear the names invoked in sacrificial rites, having seen the rain about to be engendered instigated him to resume his embryo condition (in the clouds)."

### Page 224 — Special topics on Rik 6.4: the application; the Maruts and the rains; "svadhā" and "anu"

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose translated; English as printed; printed p. 224 is missing from the better scan; this page is checked against the older scan `Rig_Vol2.pdf` (its PDF 239).)*

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The Bhāṣyakāra has said that there is a special application for this Ṛk. On the twenty-fourth day, at the morning pressing, the priest Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite, as the śastra-mantra, the two Ṛks beginning "ād aha svadhām anu" (that is, the 4th and 5th Ṛks of this sūkta [as printed]) and the one Ṛk "indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase" (the 7th of this sūkta) — a tṛca of these three Ṛks together; that tṛca bears the name "ṣaḷaha-stotriya." On this matter **Āśvalāyana** says in his Śrauta-sūtra, in the section "hotājaniṣva": "*indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase ādaha svadhām anv ity ekā dve ca*" (Āśv. Sū. 7-2). Though this sūkta has Indra as its deity, the Maruts are described in the six Ṛks of this sūkta beginning with "ādaha." For this very reason, the Anukramaṇī says "aindre maruta" (Anu. 2-22) — that in this Indra-sūkta there is a Marut-subject.

The meaning of this Ṛk is not plain either. The names of the Maruts are not in these Ṛks; but the Bhāṣyakāra, following the Anukramaṇī, interprets it as concerning the Maruts. In the rainy season the large, huge clouds that gather together are here described as the "garbha" (germ) in which water gathers; and since, from such a cloud-germ, rain-water and food in the form of grain are obtained by men, the sense is that the Marut-deities impel it.

**आत् (āt)** — "anantara," that is, after the rainy season has passed. **अह (aha)** — "eva," emphasis; or it may be thought of as a word that gives the sense of "wonder."

**स्वधाम् (svadhām)** — Among the twenty-eight words that signify food, beginning with "andha," the words "ūrk," "rasaḥ" and "svadhā" are read (Ni. 2-7), and among the 101 words that signify water beginning with "arṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ" the word "svadhā" is also read (Ni. 1-12). On the question of the meaning of the word "svadhā," there is much speculation among the learned. **"Svaṃ lokaṃ dadhāti puṣṇātīti svadhā"** — "svadhā" because it supports and nourishes its own world — (the food): thus the Bhāṣyakāra has explained the sense of the parts of this word. Western scholars say that this word has various senses *(English as printed)*: "sva + dhā = svadhā: one's own place; svadhā: to offer the oblation to the Pitṛs (fathers) in the fire; self position; self power; inherent power; accustomed place; comfort; joy," etc. In this question of the meaning of the word, Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava have the same view as Sāyaṇa.

**अनु (anu)** — "paścāt," afterwards, after the rainy season has ended. **Skandasvāmī** explains it as: after the rainy season (the four months) has ended, and before the rainy season begins again, the eight months that are between …

### Page 225 — Special topics on Rik 6.4 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (characterized)

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Printed p. 225 is missing from the better scan; checked against the older scan `Rig_Vol2.pdf` (its PDF 240). Kannada prose translated; the Sanskrit quotation was read from an enlarged slice and is given in three layers, flagged where unclear. Grammar characterized, sūtras kept.)*

*(Continuing "anu" from p. 224:)* …that between the end of one rainy season and the beginning of the next lie the eight months — so Skandasvāmī says. In support of this he has quoted, as authority, the sentence:

> वार्षिकांश्चतुरो मासान् वर्षित्वा तदनन्तरमष्टौ मासांस्तदुदकं रश्मिभिः प्रत्याहृत्य तदागामिसंवत्सरे वर्षितुं पुनर्गर्भमापादयन्ति मरुतः
> *vārṣikāṃś caturo māsān varṣitvā tad-anantaram aṣṭau māsāṃs tad udakaṃ raśmibhiḥ pratyāhṛtya tad-āgāmi-saṃvatsare varṣituṃ punar garbham āpādayanti marutaḥ*
> *(Reading note: checked against the older scan: the print reads "pratyāhṛtya" (once) and "āpādayanti"; the rest as given.)*
> **Translation:** "Having rained the four months of the rains, then for eight months the Maruts, drawing back that water with the rays (of the Sun), bring about a germ (garbha) again, so as to rain in the coming year."

**पुनः (punaḥ)** — This word indicates that, as in the rainy season that has gone by, so there will come another rainy season in the future. **गर्भत्वम् (garbhatvam)** — here "garbha" must be understood as the mass of water that has gathered in a heap in the cloud-circle (of the cloud). **दधानाः (dadhānāḥ)** — Sāyaṇa explains this word, joined with "yajñiyaṃ nāma" — "bearing a name worthy of sacrifice" — as "bearing." Skandasvāmī explains "nāma" as water, "dadhānā" as "bearing"; and, joined with "svadhām" (food in the form of grain), "dadhānāḥ" as "giving" (the root "dadhāti" in the sense of giving). **नाम (nāma)** — name. Skandasvāmī says that "nāma" here also has the sense of water; among the 101 names of water beginning with "arṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ," the word "nāma" is read (Ni. 1-12); besides this, he says the word "nāma" is a word that gives the sense of "saṃjñā" (name). **यज्ञियम् (yajñiyam)** — connected with sacrifice; that is, fit to be worshipped in a sacrifice by invocation and the like.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(Kannada; characterized)* **"Āt," "aha"** — particles, first-syllable acute. **"Svadhām"** — "svaṃ lokaṃ dadhāti puṣṇātīti" (that which nourishes its own world). **"Svadhā"** — **आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः** (पा. ३-२-३) — when a subanta that is not a prefix is the upapada, "ka" comes after a root ending in "ā"; **आतो लोप इटि च** (पा. ६-४-६४) elides the "ā"; **अजाद्यतष्टाप्** (पा. ४-१-४) the feminine "ṭāp"; "ṭāp" is unaccented; "ka" gives the affix-accent; **गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्** (पा. ६-२-१३९) retains the kṛt-final member's accent; then the "ā" of the "ṭāp" merges in the savarṇa-dīrgha; the single substitute is acute (**एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः**, पा. ८-२-५); so "svadhā" is end-acute. **"Anu," "punaḥ"** — particles, first-syllable acute. **"Garbhatvam"** — "tasya bhāvas tvatalau" (**तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ**, पा. ५-१-११९): after a sixth-case-ending word, in the sense of state, the affixes "tva" and "tal"; "tal" gives the feminine; "garbhasya bhāvaḥ" with "tva" gives "garbhatva"; "tva" is acute by its affix accent.

### Page 226 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.4 concluded; Sūkta 6, Fifth Mantra: Saṃhitā

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Grammar characterized, sūtras kept; re-read from the better scan (PDF 238, the first page after the gap). Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**"Erire"** — the root "īr gatau" (to go), with the causal sense included, and it is "anudātteṭ" (unaccented in its upadeśa); "liṭ" is added, and in the third-person plural the "jha" is replaced by **इरेच्** — **लिटस्तझयोरेशिरेच्** (पा. ३-४-८१) — "e" for "ta" and "irec" for "jha" in the "liṭ" — "īr + irec"; because of the "c"-mark it is end-acute (**चितः**, पा. ६-१-१६३). **"Saha supā"** — **सह सुपा** (पा. २-१-४), which the print takes as two sūtras ("saha" and "supā," divided by the "yoga-vibhāga" principle): "saha" (a compound of a subanta with a tiṅanta in the "supā" sense); here "ā" (a prefix in the sense of a particle) combines with "erire" by that part of the sūtra, and the compound takes the accent of the whole compound, the end-acute (**समासस्य**, पा. ६-१-२२३). **"Ām"** — for a verb in "liṭ" with a heavy first syllable beginning with a vowel, **इजादेश्च गुरुमतोऽनृच्छः** (पा. ३-१-३६) would bring the augment "ām" (affix "ām") — the print says: but, as this is a mantra, by the rule **कास्प्रत्ययादाममन्त्रे लिटि** (पा. ३-१-३५) "ām" is added in "liṭ" only outside mantras, so "ām" does not come here. **"Aha" and nighāta** — by **तुपश्यपश्यताहैः पूजायाम्** (पा. ८-१-३९) there is a prohibition of nighāta on a verb joined with "tupaśya," "paśya," "tā" and "ahai" in the sense of praise; because of the word "aha" the verb "erire" is not made unaccented. **"Dadhānāḥ"** — "śānac" after "dhā"; "śānac" being "c"-marked would be end-acute (**चितः**), but **अभ्यस्तानामादिः** (पा. ६-१-१८९) gives it first-syllable acute; "dhā" is a "juhotyādi" root, so "śap" is replaced by "ślu" (**जुहोत्यादिभ्यः श्लुः**, पा. २-४-७५), and the doubling (**श्लौ**, पा. ६-१-१०): "dadhā," which by "ubhe abhyastam" is called "abhyasta." **"Yajñiyam"** — **यज्ञर्त्विग्भ्यां घखञौ** (पा. ५-१-७१): after "yajña" and "ṛtvij," in the sense "he deserves," the affixes "gha" and "khañ" (here "gha"); **आयनेयीनीयियः फढखछघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्** (पा. ७-१-२): the initial "ph, ḍh, kh, chh, gh" of an affix are replaced by "āyan, eya, īn, īy, iy" in order; "gh" → "iy" → "yajña + iya" → "yajñiya." The "i" is acute by the affix's accent. ॥४॥

### Sūkta 6, The Fifth Mantra

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> वी॒ळु चि॑दारुज॒त्नुभि॒र्गुहा॑ चिदिंद्र॒ वह्नि॑भिः ।
> अविं॑द उ॒स्रिया॒ अनु॑ ॥५॥
>
> *vīḷú cidārujatnúbhirgúhā cidiṃdra váhnibhiḥ |*
> *áviṃda usríyā ánu ||5||*

### Page 227 — Rik 6.5: Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (the Paṇi legend), grammar (characterized), Pada-meanings

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, re-read from the better scan. Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> वीळु । चित् । आरुजत्नुऽभिः । गुहा । चित् । इन्द्र । वह्निऽभिः ।
> अविन्दः । उस्रियाः । अनु ॥५॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> अस्ति किंचिदुपाख्यानम् । पणिभिर्देवलोकाद्गावोऽपहृता अन्धकारे प्रक्षिप्ताः ताश्चेन्द्रो मरुद्भिः सहाजयदिति । एतच्चानुक्रमणिकायां सूचितम् । पणिभिरसुरैर्निगूळ्हा गा अन्वेष्टुं सरमां देवशुनीमिन्द्रेण प्रहितामयुग्भिः पणयो मित्रीयन्तः प्रोचुः । अनु. ऋग्वे. १०-१०८ । इति । मन्त्रान्तरे च दृष्टान्ततया सूचितम् । निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः । ऋग्वे. १-३२-११ । इति । तदेतदुपाख्यानमभिप्रेत्योच्यते ॥ हे इन्द्र वीळु चिद्दृढमपि दुर्गमस्थानमारुजत्नुभिर्भञ्जद्भिर्वह्निभिर्वोढृभिरन्यत्र नेतुं समर्थैर्मरुद्भिः सहितस्त्वं गुहा चित् गुहायामपि स्थापिता उस्रिया गा अन्वविन्दः । अन्विष्य लब्धवानसि । ओजः पाज इत्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु बलनामसु दक्षो वीळु च्यौत्नमिति पठितम् । नवसंख्याकेषु गोनामस्वघ्न्योस्रोस्रियेति पठितम् ॥ वीळु । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । चित् । चादिरनुदात्तः । आरुजत्नुभिः । रुजो भङ्ग इत्यौणादिकः कत्नुच्प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । गुहा । सप्तम्या डादेशः । ग्रामादीनां च । फि. २-१५ । इत्याद्युदात्तः । वह्निभिः । वहिश्रिश्रुयुद्रुग्लाहात्वरिभ्यो नित् । उ. ४-५१ । इति वहेर्निप्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अविन्दः । शे मुचादीनाम् । पा. ७-१-५९ । इति नुमागमः । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः । पा. ६-४-७१ । वसन्तीत्युस्रियाः । वसेः कर्तरि रियक्प्रत्ययः । षत्वाभावश्च बाहुलकादूहनीयः । उक्तं हि । यन्न पदार्थविशेषसमुत्थं प्रत्ययतः प्रकृतेश्च तदूह्यमिति । इकारः प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः ॥५॥
> *asti kiṃcidupākhyānam | paṇibhirdevalokādgāvo 'pahṛtā andhakāre prakṣiptāḥ tāścendro marudbhiḥ sahājayaditi | etaccānukramaṇikāyāṃ sūcitam | paṇibhirasurairnigūḷhā gā anveṣṭuṃ saramāṃ devaśunīmindreṇa prahitāmayugbhiḥ paṇayo mitrīyantaḥ procuḥ | anu. ṛgve. 10-108 | iti | mantrāntare ca dṛṣṭāntatayā sūcitam | niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ | ṛgve. 1-32-11 | iti | tadetadupākhyānamabhipretyocyate ‖ he indra vīḷu ciddṛḍhamapi durgamasthānamārujatnubhirbhañjadbhirvahnibhirvoḍhṛbhiranyatra netuṃ samarthairmarudbhiḥ sahitastvaṃ guhā cit guhāyāmapi sthāpitā usriyā gā anvavindaḥ | anviṣya labdhavānasi | ojaḥ pāja ityādiṣvaṣṭāviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu balanāmasu dakṣo vīḷu cyautnamiti paṭhitam | navasaṃkhyākeṣu gonāmasvaghnyosrosriyeti paṭhitam ‖ vīḷu | prātipadikasvaraḥ | cit | cādiranudāttaḥ | ārujatnubhiḥ | rujo bhaṅga ityauṇādikaḥ katnucpratyayaḥ | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | cittvādantodāttatvam | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | guhā | saptamyā ḍādeśaḥ | grāmādīnāṃ ca | phi. 2-15 | ityādyudāttaḥ | vahnibhiḥ | vahiśriśruyudruglāhātvaribhyo nit | u. 4-51 | iti vahernipratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | avindaḥ | śe mucādīnām | pā. 7-1-59 | iti numāgamaḥ | luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣvaḍudāttaḥ | pā. 6-4-71 | vasantītyusriyāḥ | vaseḥ kartari riyakpratyayaḥ | ṣatvābhāvaśca bāhulakādūhanīyaḥ | uktaṃ hi | yanna padārthaviśeṣasamutthaṃ pratyayataḥ prakṛteśca tadūhyamiti | ikāraḥ pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ ‖5‖*
> *(Re-read in full from the better scan (no line is cut off there); the grammatical tail is transcribed.)*

**Translation:** "There is a certain legend. The Paṇis stole cows from the world of the gods and hurled them into darkness; (those) Indra, with the Maruts, won (back). This is indicated in the Anukramaṇī: '*To Saramā, the divine bitch sent by Indra to search out the cows hidden by the Paṇis, the Asuras, the Paṇis, seeking her friendship, spoke in alternate verses*' (Anukramaṇī on Ṛg. 10-108). And it is indicated in another mantra as an illustration: '*the waters were shut up, like the cows by the Paṇi*' (Ṛg. 1-32-11). With that legend in view it is said: O Indra! 'Vīḷu cit' — even what is firm, a place hard to reach — 'ārujatnubhiḥ' — by the breakers, 'vahnibhiḥ' — the bearers, the Maruts, who are able to carry (it) elsewhere — accompanied by them, you 'guhā cit' — even in the cave where they had been placed — 'usriyā gāḥ' — the cows — 'anvindaḥ' — you searched out and found. Among the twenty-eight names of strength beginning with 'ojaḥ, pājaḥ,' 'dakṣaḥ,' 'vīḷu' and 'cyautnam' are read; among the nine names of cow, 'aghnyā,' 'usrā' and 'usriyā' are read."

**Grammar within the Bhāṣya (in outline):** "Vīḷu" — the stem accent. "Cit" — a "cādi" particle, unaccented. "Ārujatnubhiḥ" — "rujo bhaṅge" with the Uṇādi affix "katnuc"; "k"-marked, so no guṇa; "c"-marked, end-acute; in the compound the kṛt-final member's accent stays. "Guhā" — "ḍā" for the locative; **ग्रामादीनां च** (फि. सू. २-१५) first-syllable acute. "Vahnibhiḥ" — **वहिश्रिश्रुयुद्रुग्लाहात्वरिभ्यो नित्** (उ. सू. ४-५१) the affix "ni"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Avindaḥ" — **शे मुचादीनाम्** (पा. ७-१-५९) the augment "num"; the augment "aṭ" acute (**लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः**, पा. ६-४-७१). "Usriyāḥ" — "vasanti" — from "vas" the affix "riyak" in the agent sense; the absence of "ṣ" is to be inferred by "bāhulaka" (as it is said, "what is not covered by the particular word, the affix and the root is to be inferred"); the "i" is acute by the affix accent. ॥५॥

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**(हे) इन्द्र (he indra)** — O Indra | **(त्वम्) (tvam)** — you | **वीळु चित् (vīḷu cit)** — even a strong, or very firm, difficult-of-approach place, together | **आरुजत्नुभिः (ārujatnubhiḥ)** — those with the capacity to break | **वह्निभिः (vahnibhiḥ)** — the Maruts, who have the capacity to carry (carry off) (with the help of the Marut-deities) | **गुहा चित् (guhā cit)** — (stolen by a Paṇi, and) hidden in a cave | **उस्रियाः (usriyāḥ)** — cows | **अनु अविन्दः (anu avindaḥ)** — you have found, you have brought back.

### Page 228 — Rik 6.5: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening) — the legend of Saramā and the Paṇis

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose translated; English as printed; references re-read from the better scan.)*

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

The Marut-deities are of very great capacity. They are able to break and destroy places of difficult approach — mountains and the like, however strong; and they have the capacity to carry everything. O Indra! With the help of such Marut-deities you found and brought back the cows that were hidden in a cave (after being carried off by demons called Paṇi).

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"Associated with the conveying Maruts, the traversers of places difficult of access, O Indra, you have found out the cows hidden in the cave."

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The Bhāṣyakāra cites here a legend (upākhyāna). The demons called Paṇi carried off cows that were in the world of the gods, and hid them in the cave of a mountain. To find them, Indra sent a divine bitch ("deva-śunī") called **Saramā**. That bitch went to the Paṇis and, by good words and by friendship, helped to bring back the cows. With the help of the Maruts Indra, destroying the cave, brought back the cows that were there — so it is said in the legend. In the 108th sūkta of the tenth Maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā there is a long conversation between the divine bitch Saramā and the demons called Paṇi. We shall describe this matter at length, further on, when we explain the subject of "*paṇineva gāvaḥ*" in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-11.

**वीळु (vīḷu)** — Among the twenty-eight words that are signs of strength, beginning with "ojaḥ," the words "dakṣaḥ," "vīḷu" and "cyautnam" are read (Ni. 3-9 [as printed]). The senses of this word: strong, firm, solid, fearless.

**चित् (cit)** — "eva" (emphasis). **आरुजत्नुभिः (ārujatnubhiḥ)** — "bhañjadbhiḥ" — "those who have the capacity to break, to destroy." **वह्निभिः (vahnibhiḥ)** — "voḍhṛbhiḥ" — those who carry, those who bear. **गुहा (guhā)** — in a cave, in a place that no one knows, in a solitary place, in a hidden spot; this word is generally used in the seventh case in the sense of "in a cave": "*guhā hitaṃ guhyaṃ gūḷhaṃ*" (गुहा हितं गुह्यं गूळ्हं — "placed in a cave, secret, hidden," ṛ. saṃ. 2-11-5) and so on. **उस्रियाः (usriyāḥ)** — among the nine words that signify cows beginning with "aghnyā," the word "usriyāḥ" is read (Ni. 3-9 [as printed]).

### Page 229 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.5 (Kannada) — characterized

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 11 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Pure grammar in Kannada prose, restating the Sanskrit of p. 227; **characterized in outline**; sūtras kept; re-read from the better scan.)*

**"Vīḷu"** — by the bare-stem accent, end-acute. **"Cit"** — as it belongs to the "cādi" group, **चादयोऽनुदात्ताः** (फि. सू. ८४) it is unaccented. **"Ārujatnubhiḥ"** — "ā" is a prefix; after the root "ruja bhaṅge" (to break) the Uṇādi affix "tnuc" (no sūtra printed); "kit," so no guṇa for the light penultimate; "c"-marked, so end-acute; the compound with "ā" takes the kṛt-final member's accent by **गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्** (पा. ६-२-१३९). **"Guhā"** — for the seventh-case singular the substitute "ḍā" (**सुपां सुलुक्…**, पा. ७-१-३९); **ग्रामादीनां च** (फि. सू. ३८ [as printed]; "2-15" on p. 227) — the "grāma"-class words are first-syllable acute, so "guhā" is first-syllable acute. **"Vahnibhiḥ"** — **वहिश्रिश्रुयुद्रुग्लाहात्वरिभ्यो निः** (उ. सू. ४-५१) after these roots the affix "ni," which is "nit" ("n"-marked), so from "vah" "vahni" is first-syllable acute (**ञित्यादिर्नित्यम्**). **"Avindaḥ"** — "vidḷ lābhe" (to obtain), a tudādi root; the second-person singular "sip" in "laṅ"; **तुदादिभ्यः शः** (पा. ३-१-७७) the vikaraṇa "śa"; **शे मुचादीनाम्** (पा. ७-१-५९) — the "num" augment comes to the "muc"-class roots when "śa" follows: "vind + a + s"; **लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः** (पा. ६-४-७१) the augment "aṭ"; **ससजुषो रुः** and visarga → "avindaḥ." **"Usriyāḥ"** — "vasanti iti usriyāḥ": after the root "vas" the affix "riyak" in the sense of the agent, and the substitution of "s" for "ṣ"? — the print says: **शासिवसिघसीनां च** (पा. ८-३-६०) gives "ṣ" for the "s" of these roots after "i/ku"; but that is not seen here, and so "bahulaṃ" in **उणादयो बहुलम्** (पा. ३-३-१) must be supplied; the print quotes **नाम च धातुजमाह निरुक्ते व्याकरणे शकटस्य च तोकम् । यन्न विशेषपदार्थसमुत्थं प्रत्ययतः प्रकृतेश्च तदूह्यम्** (*nāma ca dhātujam āha nirukte vyākaraṇe śakaṭasya ca tokam | yan na viśeṣa-padārtha-samutthaṃ pratyayataḥ prakṛteś ca tad ūhyam*, पा. ३-३-१-म. १) — "the Nirukta, and in grammar the son of Śakaṭa (Śākaṭāyana), say that the noun is born of a root; what does not arise from a particular word-sense is to be inferred from the affix and from the root" — explained in the Kannada: where the root is well known, a fitting affix is to be inferred, and where the affix is known, a fitting root — and the print concludes that "riyak" is the inferred affix; since it is "k"-marked, the "samprasāraṇa" of "vas" (**वचिस्वपियजादीनां किति**, पा. ६-१-१५) gives "us" (the "va" → "u"), and **संप्रसारणाच्च** (पा. ६-१-१०८) the pūrvarūpa; "usriya"; the first-case plural → "usriyāḥ"; the "i" is acute by the affix's accent. ॥५॥

### Page 230 — Rik 6.5 grammar concluded; Sūkta 6, Sixth Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Sanskrit printed in Kannada script, re-read from the better scan. Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

### Sūkta 6, The Sixth Mantra

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> दे॒वयंतो यथा॑ म॒तिमच्छा॑ वि॒दद्व॑सुं॒ गिरः ।
> म॒हा॑मनूषत श्रुतं ॥६॥
>
> *deváyaṃto yáthā matímácchā vidádvasuṃ gíraḥ |*
> *mahāmanūṣata śrutaṃ ||6||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> देवऽयन्तः । यथा । मतिम् । अच्छ । विदत्ऽवसुम् । गिरः ।
> महाम् । अनूषत । श्रुतम् ॥६॥

*(Reading note: the printed Saṃhitā "acchā" in the first pāda is the sandhi-lengthened form of the Pada's "accha"; the Pada text divides "vidat-vasum" as a compound.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> देवयन्तो मरुत्संज्ञकान्देवानिच्छन्तो गिरः स्तोतार ऋत्विजो महां प्रौढं मरुद्गणमच्छ प्राप्तुमनूषत । स्तुतवन्तः । कीदृशं मरुद्गणम् । विदद्वसुम् । वेदयद्भिः स्वमहिमप्रख्यापकैर्वसुभिर्धनैर्युक्तं श्रुतं विख्यातम् । मरुद्गणस्य दृष्टान्तः । यथा मतिम् । मन्तारमिन्द्रं यथा स्तुवन्ति तथेत्यर्थः ॥ देवयन्तः । देवानात्मन इच्छन्तः । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । पा. ३-१-८ ॥ क्यचि च । पा. ७-४-३३ । इतीत्त्वम् । अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः । पा. ७-४-२५ । इति दीर्घत्वं च न भवति । न च्छन्दस्यपुत्रस्य । पा. ७-४-३५ । इत्यनेन क्यचि यत्प्राप्तमीत्त्वं दीर्घत्वं वा तस्य सर्वस्य प्रतिषेधात् । यद्यपीत्त्वमेव प्रकृतं तथापि व्यवहितस्यापि दीर्घत्वस्य स प्रतिषेध इति विज्ञायते । अश्वाघस्यात् । पा. ७-४-३७ । इत्यात्त्वविधानादिति ह्युक्तम् । क्यजन्ताच्छतृप्रत्ययः । क्यचश्चित्त्वाच्चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । शपः पित्त्वेन शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणानुदात्तत्वे एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । यथा । प्रकारवचने थाल् । पा. ५-३-२३ । लिति । पा. ६-१-१९३ । इति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वमुदात्तत्वम् । मतिम् । मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनेत्यादिना । पा. ३-३-९६ । क्तिन्नुदात्तः …
> *devayanto marutsaṃjñakāndevānicchanto giraḥ stotāra ṛtvijo mahāṃ prauḍhaṃ marudgaṇamaccha prāptumanūṣata | stutavantaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ marudgaṇam | vidadvasum | vedayadbhiḥ svamahimaprakhyāpakairvasubhirdhanairyuktaṃ śrutaṃ vikhyātam | marudgaṇasya dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yathā matim | mantāramindraṃ yathā stuvanti tathetyarthaḥ ‖ devayantaḥ | devānātmana icchantaḥ | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | pā. 3-1-8 ‖ kyaci ca | pā. 7-4-33 | itīttvam | akṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ | pā. 7-4-25 | iti dīrghatvaṃ ca na bhavati | na cchandasyaputrasya | pā. 7-4-35 | ityanena kyaci yatprāptamīttvaṃ dīrghatvaṃ vā tasya sarvasya pratiṣedhāt | yadyapīttvameva prakṛtaṃ tathāpi vyavahitasyāpi dīrghatvasya sa pratiṣedha iti vijñāyate | aśvāghasyāt | pā. 7-4-37 | ityāttvavidhānāditi hyuktam | kyajantācchatṛpratyayaḥ | kyacaścittvāccita ityantodāttatvam | śapaḥ pittvena śatuśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇānudāttatve ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttaḥ | yathā | prakāravacane thāl | pā. 5-3-23 | liti | pā. 6-1-193 | iti pratyayātpūrvamudāttatvam | matim | mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanetyādinā | pā. 3-3-96 | ktinnudāttaḥ …*
> *(Re-read in full from the better scan; the grammar continues on p. 231.)*

**Translation:** "'Devayantaḥ' — wishing for the gods called Maruts, 'giraḥ' — the singers, the priests, 'mahām' — the mighty Marut-host — 'accha' — in order to reach it, 'anūṣata' — have praised. What kind of Marut-host? 'Vidadvasum' — endowed with riches that make their greatness known, famous (heard-of): 'śrutam' — widely renowned. An illustration for the Marut-host: 'yathā matim' — as they praise Indra, the thinker, so (they praise the Marut-host). 'Devayantaḥ' — 'devān ātmana icchantaḥ' — wishing the gods for themselves; the affix 'kyac' after a subanta in the sense of one's own wish (Pāṇini 3-1-8); the 'ī' by 'kyaci ca' (Pāṇini 7-4-33); by 'na chandasy aputrasya' (7-4-35) the 'ī' and the lengthening (7-4-25) are both barred in the Veda; the 'śatṛ' after the 'kyac'-ending, end-acute as 'c'-marked; 'yathā' — 'thāl' (5-3-23), acute before the affix by 'liti' (6-1-193); 'matim' — 'ktin,' acute by 3-3-96 …" *(the grammar continues on the next page).*

### Page 231 — Rik 6.6: grammar of the Bhāṣya (concluded); Pada-meanings; Bhāvārtha; English rendering

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." The top of the page ends the Sanskrit grammar of the Bhāṣya; re-read from the better scan and given in outline with the sūtras. English as printed.)*

**Grammar (in outline):** "Matim" (concluded) — the word, meaning knowledge, here stands for Indra; or, as "tattva-viśeṣa" (a particular entity), it is a name of Indra: by **क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम्** (पा. ३-३-१७४) "ktic" after "man" in the agent sense; by **एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्** (पा. ७-२-१०) no "iṭ"; "c"-marked, so end-acute. "Accha" — by **अच्छ गत्यर्थवदेषु** (पा. १-४-६९) a "gati" in connection with verbs of going, and also a particle (**गतिश्च**, पा. १-४-६०, co-occurring); first-syllable acute by **निपाता आद्युदात्ताः** (फि. सू. ४-१२). "Vidadvasum" — "vida jñāne" with the causal sense included and "śatṛ": "vidanti" — they make known — "vasūni dhanāni yaṃ sa vidadvasuḥ"; the "śap" after "vid" is elided by **अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः** (पा. २-४-७२); the "śatṛ" is acute by the affix accent; in the bahuvrīhi the first member's accent is kept. "Giraḥ" — "gṛṇanti stuvanti" — from "gṝ" with "kvip," **ऋत इद्धातोः** (पा. ७-१-१००) "ir" and "r"; the root accent. "Mahām" — "mahāntam": the "n" and "t" are elided as a Vedic licence; the stem accent. "Anūṣata" — "ṇu stutau," by vyatyaya the ātmanepada; "luṅ"; "jhas" replaced by "at" (पा. ७-१-५); in "sic," as a "kuṭādi" root, it is "ṅit" (पा. १-२-१), so no guṇa; the absence of "iṭ" and the lengthening of "u" are Vedic; unaccented by nighāta. "Śrutam" — the affix accent.

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**देवयन्तः (devayantaḥ)** — those who wish to praise the deities called Maruts | **गिरः (giraḥ)** — the priests who sing stotras | **मतिम् (matim)** — (as they praise Indra) who gives understanding | **यथा (yathā)** — in whatever manner (they praise) | **विदद्वसुम् (vidadvasum)** — (the Marut-host) able to bestow wealth and lordship by their greatness | **श्रुतम् (śrutam)** — famous | **महाम् (mahām)** — great (the great host of Maruts) | **अच्छ (accha)** — in order to reach | **अनूषत (anūṣata)** — they praise.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

The priests and other people who wish to praise the Marut-deities praise the Marut-deities in the same way as they praise Indra, who gives understanding or who is wise. These Marut-deities are able to give wealth and lordship by their greatness; they are great and famous. They praise such Marut-deities with love.

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"The reciters of praises praise the mighty (troop of Maruts) who are celebrated and conscious of the power of bestowing wealth, just as they praise the counseller (Indra)."

### Page 232 — Special topics on Rik 6.6

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose translated; the Sanskrit of Skandasvāmī's gloss is given in three layers, read at ordinary enlargement and flagged where unclear.)*

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

Because the meaning of this Ṛk is not plain, many words must be supplied in order to obtain a proper sense; and besides, the senses of some words have to be changed slightly.

**देवयन्तः (devayantaḥ)** — "devān marutaḥ icchantaḥ devayantaḥ" — "those who wish for the gods, the Maruts"; that is, those who wish to praise the Marut-deities. **Skandasvāmī** has explained it likewise.

**मतिम् (matim)** — *"mantāram indraṃ yathā stuvanti tathety arthaḥ | matiśabdo jñāna-paro 'py upacārāj jñātari indre vartate"* (मन्तारमिन्द्रं यथा स्तुवन्ति तथेत्यर्थः । मतिशब्दो ज्ञानपरोऽप्युपचाराज्ज्ञातरीन्द्रे वर्तते — "the sense is 'as they praise Indra, the thinker' — the word 'mati,' though it has the sense of knowledge, is by figurative use applied to Indra, the knower"). *"athavā padāntare viśeṣyānupādānād indrasyaiṣā saṃjñā"* (अथवा पदान्तरे विशेष्यानुपादानादिन्द्रस्यैषा संज्ञा — "or, since no other word is supplied as the noun qualified, this is a name of Indra"), Sāyaṇa says. the word "mati" stands for the sense of knowledge; hence here it is used in the sense of "one who has knowledge, who has understanding," in reference to Indra. Or, in another word it can be understood as a qualifier. In such a context this word refers to Indra himself. **Skandasvāmī** says: "*manyate stūyate 'sāv iti matir indraḥ | jñātā vā matir vidvān brāhmaṇaḥ | yathā sarvastutyam indraṃ vidvāṃsaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ tadvat*" (मन्यते स्तूयतेऽसाविति मतिरिन्द्रः । ज्ञाता वा मतिर्विद्वान् ब्राह्मणः । यथा सर्वस्तुत्यमिन्द्रं विद्वांसं वा ब्राह्मणं तद्वत् — "'mati' is Indra, since he is thought of, praised; or 'mati' is a knower, a learned Brāhmaṇa; as one (praises) Indra, praiseworthy by all, or a learned Brāhmaṇa, so (the Maruts)"). That is, since he is "thought of — praised," "mati" is the name of Indra; or one who has knowledge, a wise man, a Brāhmaṇa — this too is the sense of this word; so Skandasvāmī says that "matim" may be explained as Indra, who is like a Brāhmaṇa full of knowledge, praised by all.

**अच्छ (accha)** — The Bhāṣyakāra explains it as "prāptum" (to reach). On this matter he cites *"adhyāhṛta-gacchaty-artha-yogād accha gatyarthavadeṣu"* (अध्याहृतगच्छत्यर्थयोगादच्छ गत्यर्थवदेषु — "from its connection with the sense of 'gacchati' (goes), which is supplied: 'accha gatyarthavadeṣu'"), naming the Pāṇinian sūtra (पा. सू. १-४-६९). This word is always used with a lengthened final vowel in the saṃhitā-text when it occurs in the middle of a Ṛk.

**विदद्वसुम् (vidadvasum)** — *"vida jñāna ity asmāt vidantyādāryātiśayavattayā jñāpayanti vasūni dhanāni yaṃ sa vidadvasuḥ"* (विद ज्ञान इत्यस्मात् विदन्त्यादार्यातिशयवत्तया ज्ञापयन्ति वसूनि धनानि यं स विदद्वसुः — "from 'vida jñāne': he whom [they] make known … riches, wealth, is 'vidadvasu'"; "vidantyādārya-" as printed; the Kannada takes it as *audārya*, generosity) — the root "vid" means "knowing"; that is, those who have knowledge in the matter of giving wealth and the like, through the excess of their generosity. **Skandasvāmī** explains the root "vid" as "to obtain": *"vindater lābhārthasya vidac chabdaḥ | labdhadhanam ity arthaḥ"* (विन्दतेर्लाभार्थस्य विदच्छब्दः । लब्धधनमित्यर्थः — "the word 'vidat' is from 'vindati' in the sense of obtaining; the sense is 'one who has obtained wealth'") — he takes it as "those who have obtained wealth."

**गिरः (giraḥ)** — "gṛṇanti stuvantīti giraḥ" — those who praise. **महाम् (mahām)** — "mahāntam" (the great); here, for the convenience of the metre, the "n" and "t" are dropped.

### Pages 233–235 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.6 (Kannada) — characterized

*(Page headers: p. 233 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā"; p. 234 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6"; p. 235 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12." These three pages are **pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose** for "devayantaḥ," "yathā," "matim," "accha," "vidadvasum," "giraḥ," "mahām," "anūṣata" and "śrutam"; they do not bear on the sense of Rik 6.6 (pp. 230–232). They are **characterized in outline**, re-read from the better scan with every printed sūtra number.)*

**p. 233 — "devayantaḥ."** "Devān ātmana icchantaḥ" ("wishing the gods for themselves"): **सुप आत्मनः क्यच्** (पा. सू. ३-१-८) — "supaḥ" here means a word ending in a case-ending, by the paribhāṣā "pratyaya-grahaṇe tadanta-grahaṇam" (an affix named stands for what ends in it; परि. २३ [?], the first digit unclear); from **धातोः कर्मणः समानकर्तृकादिच्छायां वा** (पा. सू. ३-१-७) the three words "karmaṇaḥ icchāyām vā" carry over (the print explains "anuvṛtti": a word of an earlier sūtra joined, as the sense requires, to a later one); "karmaṇaḥ" is ablative, "from the object"; "ātmanaḥ" is a genitive of purpose, "for oneself"; the sense of the sūtra: after a subanta denoting the object that one wishes for one's own sake, "kyac" comes optionally in the sense "wishes." In "devayantaḥ" those who wish are the ṛtvijs, who wish the gods for their own purposes. The print quotes the kārikā on the denominative affixes ("san kyac kāmyac kyaṣ … yak āya īyaṅ ṇiṅ ceti dvādaśāmī sanādayaḥ" — the twelve "san" and the rest) [as read; the line is crowded]. **सनाद्यन्ता धातवः** (पा. सू. ३-१-३२) makes the "kyac"-ended form a root; **सुपो धातुप्रातिपदिकयोः** (पा. सू. २-४-७१) elides the case-ending "śas"; **क्यचि च** (पा. सू. ७-४-३३) would give "ī" for the "a" before "kyac," and **अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः** (पा. सू. ७-४-२५) a long vowel; but **न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्य** (पा. सू. ७-४-३५) forbids both in the Veda for words other than "putra." By the maxim "ananantarasya vidhir vā bhavati pratiṣedho vā" the prohibition would reach only the "ī" (the nearer rule), not the lengthening; but the sūtra **अश्वाघस्यात्** (पा. सू. ७-४-३७) shows (as a jñāpaka) that the lengthening is forbidden too — "aśvān ātmana icchantaḥ" gives "aśvāyantaḥ" only because 7-4-37 prescribes "ā" for "aśva" and "agha" before "kyac" *(continued on p. 234)*.

**p. 234 — "devayantaḥ" (concluded); "yathā," "matim," "accha."** If "kyaci ca" were held, by the maxim "ananantarasya," to forbid only the "ī," then "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" would lengthen and "aśvāya" would be obtained anyway, and the "ā" of 7-4-37 would be pointless; so, to have a purpose, it shows that "na chandasy aputrasya" forbids every operation before "kyac"; hence neither "ī" nor the long vowel arises in "devaya." Then "laṭ," its substitute "śatṛ," and the vikaraṇa "śap"; "kyac" being "c"-marked is end-acute by **चितः** (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३); "śap," "p"-marked, and "śatṛ," a lasārvadhātuka after an unaccented-marked base, are unaccented; the single substitute from "ato guṇe" is acute by **एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः** (पा. सू. ८-२-५). **"Yathā"** — **प्रकारवचने थाल्** (पा. सू. ५-३-२३): "prakāra" is a particular that distinguishes within the general ("sāmānyasya bhedako viśeṣaḥ prakāraḥ"), so "thāl" comes after "kim" and the like in their own sense, here after "yad"; "l"-marked, so the vowel before the affix is acute by **लिति** (पा. सू. ६-१-१९३). **"Matim"** — "ktin," acute by **मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्तः** (पा. सू. ३-३-९६); "k"-marked, so the "n" is elided by **अनुदात्तोपदेश…** (पा. सू. ६-४-३७); "mati" generally means knowledge, but here by upacāra it denotes Indra, the abode of knowledge; or, since no other word supplies the noun qualified, "mati" can be called a saṃjñā (name) of Indra: then by **क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम्** (पा. सू. ३-३-१७४) "ktic" after "mana jñāne," and, the root being unaccented, **एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात्** (पा. सू. ७-२-१०) forbids "iṭ." **"Accha"** — by **अच्छ गत्यर्थवदेषु** (पा. सू. १-४-६९) the indeclinable "accha" is a "gati" in connection with roots of going and "vad"; besides, the adhikāra **प्राग्रीश्वरान्निपाताः** (पा. सू. १-४-५६), running up to "adhirīśvare" (१-४-९७), makes it a "nipāta" as well; so both designations apply *(continued on p. 235)*.

**p. 235 — "accha" (concluded); "vidadvasum," "giraḥ," "mahām," "anūṣata."** The designations "gati" and "nipāta" do not exclude each other; they co-occur; so by **निपाता आद्युदात्ताः** (फि. सू. ८०) the first syllable is acute; and in the saṃhitā **निपातस्य च** (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६) lengthens a particle in the mantra. **"Vidadvasum"** — after "vida jñāne," with the sense of "ṇic" included, "laṭ," replaced by "śatṛ" (**लटः शतृशानचौ**, पा. सू. ३-२-१२४); in the neuter "vidat–vidatī–vidanti"; "vidanti = audāryātiśayavattayā jñāpayanti vasūni dhanāni yaṃ saḥ" — the Maruts whose riches make them known as eminently generous; the "śap" after "vid" is elided by **अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शपः** (पा. सू. २-४-७२); after the "luk," "śatṛ" no longer follows an unaccented-marked base, so **तास्यनुदात्तेत्…** (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६) does not make the lasārvadhātuka unaccented; by the affix accent "śatṛ" is acute; in the bahuvrīhi the first member's accent stays (**बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम्**, पा. सू. ६-२-१). **"Giraḥ"** — "gṛṇanti = stuvanti" — those who praise; "gṝ śabde" with "kvip"; **ऋत इद्धातोः** (पा. सू. ७-१-१००) "i" for the final "ṝ" of the aṅga, and **उरण् रपरः** (पा. सू. १-१-५१) "r" after it: "gir"; nominative plural "giraḥ," end-acute by the root accent. **"Mahām"** — "mahāntam": the "n" and "t" of "mahāntam" are elided as a Vedic licence; acute by the stem accent. **"Anūṣata"** — "ṇu stutau" is parasmaipadin, but by vyatyaya takes the ātmanepada; "luṅ," third plural "jha," replaced by "at" by **आत्मनेपदेष्वनतः** (पा. सू. ७-१-५); **च्लि लुङि** (पा. सू. ३-१-४३) and **च्लेः सिच्** (पा. सू. ३-१-४४) give "sic"; **गाङ्कुटादिभ्योऽञ्णिन्ङित्** (पा. सू. "–२-१" as printed, the first number missing) makes "sic" after the kuṭādi root "ṇu" "ṅit," so **क्ङिति च** (पा. सू. १-१-५) blocks the guṇa of **सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः** (पा. सू. ७-३-८४); **णो नः** (पा. सू. ६-१-६५) "n" for the initial "ṇ" *(the grammar of "anūṣata" continues on p. 236).*

### Page 236 — Rik 6.6 grammar concluded; Sūkta 6, Seventh Mantra: Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (opening)

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Saṃhitā accents as printed (Pada unaccented); Sanskrit re-read from the better scan. Grammar characterized.)*

*(Concluding "anūṣata":)* **णोनः** (पा. सू. ६-१-६५) — "n" for the initial "ṇ" of a root — makes "ṇu" → "nu"; **लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः** (पा. सू. ६-४-७१) the augment "aṭ"; the augment "iṭ" that would be prescribed by **आर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः** (पा. सू. ७-२-३५) does not come to "sic"; the lengthening of the "u" of "nu" is Vedic (so "nū"); **तिङ्ङतिङः** (पा. सू. ८-१-२८) makes the verb unaccented after "mahām." **"Śrutam"** — ends in the affix "kta"; the accent is that of the affix. ॥६॥

### Sūkta 6, The Seventh Mantra

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रे॑ण॒ सं हि दृक्ष॑से संजग्मा॒नो अबि॑भ्युषा ।
> म॒न्दू स॑मा॒नव॑र्चसा ॥७॥
>
> *índreṇa sáṃ hi dṛ́kṣase saṃjagmānó ábibhyuṣā |*
> *mandū́ samānávarcasā ||7||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रेण । सम् । हि । दृक्षसे । सम्ऽजग्मानः । अबिभ्युषा ।
> मन्दू इति । समानऽवर्चसा ॥७॥

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(opening)*

> हे मरुद्गण त्वमिन्द्रेण संजग्मानः संगच्छमानः सं दृक्षसे हि । सम्यग्दृश्येथाः खलु । अवश्यमस्माभिर्द्रष्टव्य इत्यर्थः । कीदृशेनेन्द्रेण । अबिभ्युषा भीतिरहितेन । कीदृशौ चेन्द्रमरुद्गणौ । मन्दू नित्यप्रमुदितौ समानवर्चसा तुल्यदीप्ती । पुरा कदाचिद्वृत्रवधदशायामिन्द्रस्य सखायः सर्वे देवा वृत्रश्वासेनापसारिताः । तदानीमिन्द्रस्य वृत्रसंबन्धिसकलसेनाजयार्थं मरुद्भिः संगनोऽभूत् । सोऽयमर्थो वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथात् । ऋग्वे. ८-९६-७ । इति मन्त्रे संगृहीत इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हनिष्यन् । ऐ. ब्रा. ३-२० । इति ब्राह्मणे प्रपंचितश्च । इन्द्रशब्दः परमैश्वर्यवन्तं मरुद्गणं वाभिधत्ते । तदानीमिन्द्रस्य संबोधनं बहिरेवाध्याहर्तव्यम् । तथा चेयमृग्यास्केन व्याख्याता । इन्द्रेण हि संदृश्यसे संगच्छमानोऽबिभ्युषा गणेन मन्दू मदिष्णू युवां स्थोऽपि वा मन्दुना तेनेति स्यात्समानवर्चसेत्येतेन व्याख्यातम् । नि. ४-१२ । इति ॥ सं दृक्षसे । संपश्येथाः । दृशेश्चेति वक्तव्यम् । पा. १-३-२९-२ । इत्यात्मनेपदं । दृशेर्लिङर्थे लेट् । पा. ३-४-७ । इति प्रार्थनायां …
> *he marud-gaṇa tvam indreṇa saṃjagmānaḥ saṃgacchamānaḥ saṃ dṛkṣase hi | samyag dṛśyethāḥ khalu | avaśyam asmābhir draṣṭavya ity arthaḥ | kīdṛśenendreṇa | abibhyuṣā bhīti-rahitena | kīdṛśau cendra-marud-gaṇau | mandū nitya-pramuditau samāna-varcasā tulya-dīptī | purā kadācid vṛtra-vadha-daśāyām indrasya sakhāyaḥ sarve devā vṛtra-śvāsenāpasāritāḥ | tadānīm indrasya vṛtra-sambandhi-sakala-senā-jayārtham marudbhiḥ saṃgano 'bhūt | so 'yam artho vṛtrasya tvā śvasathāt | ṛgve. 8-96-7 | iti mantre saṅgṛhīta indro vai vṛtraṃ haniṣyan | ai. brā. 3-20 | iti brāhmaṇe prapañcitaś ca | indra-śabdaḥ paramaiśvaryavantaṃ marud-gaṇaṃ vābhidhatte | tadānīm indrasya sambodhanaṃ bahir evādhyāhartavyam | tathā ceyam ṛg yāskena vyākhyātā | indreṇa hi saṃ dṛśyase saṃgacchamāno 'bibhyuṣā gaṇena mandū madiṣṇū yuvāṃ stho 'pi vā mandunā teneti syāt samānavarcasety etena vyākhyātam | ni. 4-12 | iti || saṃ dṛkṣase | saṃpaśyethāḥ | dṛśeś ceti vaktavyam | pā. 1-3-29-2 | ity ātmanepadaṃ | dṛśer liṅarthe leṭ | pā. 3-4-7 | iti prārthanāyāṃ …*
> *(Reading notes: "saṃgano 'bhūt" as printed; the Bhāṣya continues on p. 237.)*

**Translation (sense in full; grammar in outline):** "O troop of Maruts! You, 'saṃjagmānaḥ' — joining Indra — 'saṃ dṛkṣase hi' — you are indeed well seen; the sense is 'you must certainly be seen by us.' With what kind of Indra? 'Abibhyuṣā' — one free of fear. And what kind of Indra and Marut-troop? 'Mandū' — ever delighted, 'samānavarcasā' — of equal radiance. Once, in the time of the slaying of Vṛtra, all the gods, friends of Indra, were driven away by Vṛtra's breath. Then, in order that Indra might conquer all of Vṛtra's army, there was a union with the Maruts. This sense is gathered into the mantra (Ṛg. 8-96-7): '*from the snorting of Vṛtra, you* …' and it is elaborated in the Brāhmaṇa: '*Indra, about to slay Vṛtra*' (Aitareya-brāhmaṇa 3-20). The word 'Indra' here denotes the supremely powerful Marut-troop, or Indra; at that time the vocative 'Indra' must be supplied from outside. That is how Yāska explains this Ṛk: '*By Indra you are seen united, by the fearless troop: "mandū" — the two who gladden, you both, or (you two) are; or "mandunā tena" (with that gladdening one) — this would be "samānavarcasā"*' (Nirukta 4-12). 'Saṃ dṛkṣase' — 'you should be seen together'; (the Bhāṣya on the form of 'dṛkṣase':) the ātmanepada by the vārttika "dṛśeś ceti vaktavyam" (पा. १-३-२९-२); 'leṭ' of the root 'dṛś' in the sense of 'liṅ,' (पा. ३-४-७), in the sense of prayer …" *(continues on the next page).*

### Page 237 — Rik 6.7: grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized); Pada-meanings

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." The top of the page continues the Sanskrit grammar of the Bhāṣya on "dṛkṣase," "saṃjagmānaḥ," "abibhyuṣā," "mandū" and "samānavarcasā"; re-read from the better scan and **characterized, not transcribed**, with every printed reference.)*

**Grammar (characterized):** "Dṛkṣase" — "leṭ"; **थासः से** (पा. ३-४-८०); **लेटोऽडाटौ** (पा. ३-४-९४) the augment "aṭ"; **सिब्बहुलं लेटि** (पा. ३-१-३४) "sip"; by "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" no guṇa; "ṣ" by "vraśca…" (पा. ८-२-३६); **षढोः कः सि** (पा. ८-२-४१) "k"; **आदेशप्रत्यययोः** (पा. ८-३-५९) "ṣ" for the "s" of "sip"; by the word "bahula," "śap" too comes after "sip" (पा. २-४-७३); because "sip" intervenes, the "paśya" substitute does not arise (पा. ७-३-७८); "śap," "p"-marked, and the following lasārvadhātuka are unaccented, so the root accent alone remains; and because of "hi," the nighāta of "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not apply, by the prohibition **हि च** (पा. ८-१-३४). "Saṃjagmānaḥ" — "gamlṛ" with "sam": **छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः** (पा. ३-४-६) "liṭ" in the present; since **समो गम्यृच्छिभ्याम्** (पा. १-३-२९) gives the ātmanepada, "kānac" replaces "liṭ" (पा. ३-२-१०६); doubling (पा. ६-१-८); **हलादिः शेषः** (पा. ७-४-६०); palatal for the reduplicate (पा. ७-४-६२); **गमहन…** (पा. ६-४-९८) loss of the penultimate; "kānac" being "c"-marked is end-acute; in the gati-compound the accent of the kṛt-final second member stays. "Abibhyuṣā" — "ñibhī bhaye," "liṭ" as before; **शेषात्कर्तरि परस्मैपदम्** (पा. १-३-७८); **क्वसुश्च** (पा. ३-२-१०७) "kvasu" for "liṭ"; "k"-marked, so no guṇa; doubling; shortening and "jaś" of the reduplicate (पा. ७-४-५९; ८-४-५४); the "iṭ" that **वस्वेकाजाद्घसाम्** (पा. ७-२-६७) would give is excluded by the "kryādi" restriction (पा. ७-२-१३); in the nañ-compound, in the instrumental singular, being "bha," **वसोः संप्रसारणम्** (पा. ६-४-१३१) "u" for "v"; **संप्रसारणाच्च** (पा. ६-१-१०८) single substitute; **शासिवसिघसीनां च** (पा. ८-३-६०) "ṣ"; **एरनेकाचोऽसंयोगपूर्वस्य** (पा. ६-४-८२) "y" (setting aside "iyaṅ"); the indeclinable first member keeps its accent; in the saṃhitā the "o" before it would take the prior form by **एङः पदान्तादति** (पा. ६.१.१०९, so printed with dots), but **प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे** (पा. ६-१-११५) keeps it unchanged ("saṃjagmāno abibhyuṣā"). "Mandū" — "madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu"; **इदितो नुम् धातोः** (पा. ७-१-५८) "num"; an Uṇādi affix "ku" by a sūtra cited as **उ. १-३७** [?] (the last digit unclear), with "kuḥ" read from it by anuvṛtti; acute on the end by the affix accent; **द्विवचनमौ** (as printed, पा. ४-१-२); **प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः** (पा. ६-१-१०२); or, taken as an instrumental singular, the long vowel by "supāṃ suluk…". "Samānavarcasā" — "samānaṃ varco yayoḥ" or "yasya" — a bahuvrīhi; in the dual "ā" by "supāṃ suluk…"; "samāna" is end-acute by the stem accent, which stays by **बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम्** (पा. ६-२-१). ॥७॥

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

**(हे मरुद्गण) (he marudgaṇa)** — O host of Maruts, that is, O company of the Marut-deities | **(nīvu)** — you | **अबिभ्युषा (abibhyuṣā)** — one free of fear | **इन्द्रेण (indreṇa)** — together with Indra | **संजग्मानः (saṃjagmānaḥ)** — as though going along | **सं हि दृश्यसे (saṃ hi dṛśyase)** — you are seen (so printed here, "dṛśyase") | **(nīvibbarū) मन्दू (mandū)** — (both of you) always full of delight | **समानवर्चसा (samānavarcasā)** — endowed with equal radiance (you are).

### Page 238 — Rik 6.7: Bhāvārtha; English rendering; Special topics (opening): the Vṛtra legend

*(Page header: "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6." Kannada prose translated; English as printed. The Ṛg-vedic verse and its references re-read from the better scan; the gloss is the source's own English.)*

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada, translated)*

O Marut-deities! That you go about together with the fearless Indra is seen by all. Not only that: the two of you — Indra and the Marut-deities — are always full of delight, and your radiance and your power and capacity are equal. That is, Indra and the Marut-deities, you two are alike in radiance, power and capacity.

**English Translation** *(printed in English in the source itself):*

"You are seen, O Maruts, marching forth together with Indra who is not frightened; (both) rejoicing and of equal splendour."

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The Bhāṣyakāra here indicates an ancient legend. In the battle that took place long ago, when Indra destroyed the demon Vṛtra, the gods who were with Indra were frightened by the terrible snorting and roaring of the demon Vṛtra, and fled. But the Marut-deities alone, without any fear, remained with Indra to help him. This matter is described in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-7 and in the Aitareya-brāhmaṇa (3-20):

> वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः ।
> मरुद्भिरिन्द्र सख्यं ते अस्त्वथेमा विश्वाः पृतना जयासि ॥ (ऋ. सं. ८-९६-७)
> *vṛtrasya tvā śvasathād īṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahur ye sakhāyaḥ |*
> *marudbhir indra sakhyaṃ te astv atheme viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi || (ṛ. saṃ. 8-96-7)*
> **English, as printed in the source:** "Before the snorting of Vritra, all the gods, your comrades beating a hasty retreat abandoned you. Let your friendship be, O Indra, with the Maruts; then you will conquer all battles."

The meaning of this: O Indra! From the terrible breath of the demon Vṛtra, all the gods who were your friends were frightened and, leaving your side, ran away. But let there be friendship for you with the Marut-deities. (With their help) you will be victorious in all the battles. For this very reason, it is said here that the Marut-deities may be seen going about with Indra; that is, the sense is that since the Marut-deities are friendly with Indra, they help Indra in battles and the like.

**इन्द्रेण (indreṇa)** — the word "Indra" can be explained as meaning "supreme lordship." If so, the word "indreṇa" may be applied, together with the word "abibhyuṣā," as a qualifier of "marudgaṇa" … *(continues on the next page)*

### Page 239 — Special topics on Rik 6.7 (concluded); Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (opening)

*(Page header: "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12 · Ṛgveda-saṃhitā." Kannada prose translated; grammar characterized; re-read from the better scan.)*

*(Continuing from p. 238:)* …then "indreṇa abibhyuṣā" means "by the host of Marut-deities, who have supreme lordship and are free of fear."

The sage **Yāska**, in his Nirukta, explains this Ṛk thus: "*indreṇa hi saṃdṛśyase saṅgacchamāno 'bibhyuṣā gaṇena mandū madiṣṇū yuvāṃ stho 'pi mandunā teneti syāt samānavarcasety etena vyākhyātam*" (इन्द्रेण हि संदृश्यसे संगच्छमानोऽबिभ्युषा गणेन मन्दू मदिष्णू युवां स्थोऽपि मन्दुना तेनेति स्यात्समानवर्चसेत्येतेन व्याख्यातम् — as in the Bhāṣya on p. 236, here without "vā"; no reference printed). This is as the Bhāṣyakāra explained it. But Yāska has taken the words "mandū" and "samānavarcasā" as if they were dual words, and so has said that they are qualifiers of both Indra and the Maruts; whereas the Bhāṣyakāra has taken these words as third-case (instrumental) forms and used them, with the four words "indreṇa," "abibhyuṣā," "mandū" and "samānavarcasā," as qualifiers of the Marut-host only. Then, in place of the Marut-host, Indra himself must be addressed: "O Indra! You are seen, we may say, going with the Marut-deities, who are possessed of supreme lordship, fearless and of equal radiance." **Skandasvāmī** explains it in the same way. Since the chief intention of the two kinds of meaning is one, one may say it either way.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(Kannada; characterized, sūtras kept)* **"Saṃdṛkṣase"** — "saṃpaśyethāḥ" — the "laṭ"-like "leṭ" in the sense of "liṅ" (**लिङर्थे लेट्**, पा. ३-४-७), after the root "dṛś" in the sense of prayer; under the sūtra **समो गम्यृच्छिभ्याम्** (पा. सू. १-३-२९) the Vārttika **अर्तिश्रुदृशिभ्यश्चेति वक्तव्यम्** gives the ātmanepada for the "la" after "ṛ," "śru" and "dṛś" with the prefix "sam"; "thās" (second-person singular ātmanepada) → **थासः से** (पा. ३-४-८०) "se" → "dṛś + se"; **लेटोऽडाटौ** (पा. ३-४-९४) the augment; "sip" variably in "leṭ" (**सिब्बहुलं लेटि**, पा. ३-१-३४); the guṇa of the light penultimate would arise by **पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च** (पा. ७-३-८६) but is set aside by the "saṃjñā-pūrvaka" principle (**संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः**, परिभा. ९-३-१, as printed); **व्रश्चभ्रस्जसृजमृजयजराजभ्राजच्छशां षः** (पा. ८-२-३६) — "ṣ" for the final of "vraśc," "bhrasj," "sṛj," "mṛj," "yaj," "rāj," "bhrāj," "ch" and "śā" — whether before a "jhal" or at the end of a pada, the final of these seven roots and of words ending in "ch" and "ś" becomes "ṣ": so the "ś" of "dṛś" before the "jhal" "s"; "dṛṣ + s + ase" — then **षढोः कः सि** … (the sūtra and its number on p. 240) *(continues on the next page)*

### Pages 240–242 — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā for Rik 6.7 (Kannada) — characterized; Sūkta 6, Eighth Mantra: Saṃhitā

*(Page headers: p. 240 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā · Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 6"; p. 241 "Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 1, Varga 12"; p. 242 "Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā." These three pages are **pure Pāṇinian derivation in Kannada prose** for "dṛkṣase," "saṃjagmānaḥ," "abibhyuṣā," "mandū" and "samānavarcasā," together with a note on the saṃhitā-sandhi of "saṃjagmāno abibhyuṣā." They do not bear on the sense of Rik 6.7. Re-read from the better scan; **characterized in outline**, with the printed sūtra numbers.)*

**p. 240.** *(Continuing "dṛkṣase":)* …**षढोः कः सि** (पा. सू. ८-२-४१) — "ṣ" and "ḍh" become "k" before "s" — so the "ṣ" becomes "k"; "dṛk + s + ase": **आदेशप्रत्यययोः** (पा. सू. ८-३-५९) — after "iṇ" and the k-class, an "s" that is a substitute or part of an affix becomes "ṣ" — so the "s" after "k" becomes "ṣ." Because the sūtra that elides "śap," **बहुलं छन्दसि** (पा. सू. २-४-७३), says "bahula," "śap" also comes after "sip": "dṛk + ṣ + a + ase." Even with "śap," the "paśya" substitute of **पाघ्राध्मास्थाम्नादाण्दृश्यर्तिसर्तिशदसदां पिबजिघ्रधमतिष्ठमनयच्छपश्यर्च्छधौशीयसीदाः** (पा. सू. ७-३-७८), which comes before a "ś"-marked affix, does not arise, because "sip" intervenes and the "ś"-affix does not immediately follow. "Śap," "p"-marked, is unaccented by "anudāttau supitau"; the following "ase" is unaccented by **तास्यनुदात्तेत्…** (पा. सू. ६-१-१८६); in "dṛś" the root accent stays; the two short "a"s become one by **अतो गुणे** (पा. सू. ६-१-९७): "dṛkṣase." By **हि च** (पा. सू. ८-१-३४) a verb joined with "hi" is not made unaccented, so "dṛkṣase" after "hi" escapes the nighāta of **तिङ्ङतिङः** (पा. सू. ८-१-२८). **"Saṃjagmānaḥ"** — "gamḷ gatau" with the prefix "sam": by **छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः** (पा. सू. ३-४-६) — in the Veda these affixes come in all three times, by the relation of the verbal senses — "liṭ" in the present sense; **समो गम्यृच्छिभ्याम्** (पा. सू. १-३-२९) prescribes the ātmanepada after the intransitive "gam" and "ṛ" preceded by "sam," so by **लिटः कानज्वा** (पा. सू. ३-२-१०६) "kānac," which counts as ātmanepada; **लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य** (पा. सू. ६-१-८) doubling; **हलादिः शेषः** (पा. सू. ७-४-६०) — of the reduplicate only the first consonant remains (the print explains "śeṣa"); **कुहोश्चुः** (पा. सू. ७-४-६२) "g" → "j"; **गमहनजनखनघसां लोपः क्ङित्यनङि** (पा. सू. ६-४-९८) the penultimate of "gam" is lost before a "kit/ṅit" affix beginning with a vowel, other than "aṅ": "ja + gm + āna" = "jagmāna"; with "sam," "saṃjagmāna"; "kānac," "c"-marked, is end-acute by "citaḥ." By **कुगतिप्रादयः** (पा. सू. २-२-१८) the compound with "sam," and by **गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्** (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९) the kṛt-final second member keeps its accent.

**p. 241 — "abibhyuṣā."** "Ñibhī bhaye": "liṭ" by **छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः** (पा. सू. ३-४-६); since **शेषात्कर्तरि परस्मैपदम्** (पा. सू. १-३-७८) prescribes the parasmaipada for a root lacking the ātmanepada conditions, **क्वसुश्च** (पा. सू. ३-२-१०७) gives "kvasu" for "liṭ"; the affix is "kit," so no guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ"; **लिटि धातोरनभ्यासस्य** (पा. सू. ६-१-८) doubling; **ह्रस्वः** (पा. सू. ७-४-५९) shortening of the reduplicate; **अभ्यासे चर्च** (पा. सू. ८-४-५४) "jaś": "bi + bhī + vas." **कृसृभृवृस्तुद्रुस्रुश्रुवो लिटि** (पा. सू. ७-२-१३) — whatever prohibition of "iṭ" exists, whether conditioned by the root or by the affix, applies to "liṭ" only after these eight roots "kṛ, sṛ" etc.; this is the "kryādi-niyama"; by it "bhī," not among them, would take "iṭ" before "vas"; but **वस्वेकाजाद्घसाम्** (पा. सू. ७-२-६७) restricts "iṭ" before "vasu" to roots that are monosyllabic after doubling, roots ending in "ā," and "ghas," so "bibhī" takes no "iṭ." With "nañ" compounded and the instrumental singular: "abibhīvas + ā"; being "bha," **वसोः संप्रसारणम्** (पा. सू. ६-४-१३१) "u" for "v"; **संप्रसारणाच्च** (पा. सू. ६-१-१०, as printed) the prior form: "bibhī + us + ā." Setting aside the "iyaṅ" of **अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां य्वोरियङुवङौ** (पा. सू. ६-४-७७), **एरनेकाचोऽसंयोगपूर्वस्य** (पा. सू. ६-४-८२) gives "y" for the "ī" of a many-voweled aṅga ending in a root whose "i/ī" is not preceded by a conjunct (the print explains why "abibhī" qualifies); by **अलोऽन्त्यस्य** (पा. सू. १-१-५२ [?], the last digits unclear) it replaces the final "ī": "abibhy + us + ā"; **आदेशप्रत्यययोः** (पा. सू. ८-३-५९ [?], the print is blurred here) "ṣ": "abibhyuṣā." The print adds that **शासिवसिघसीनां च** (पा. सू. ८-३-६०) is a rule for what "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" does not reach — the "s" of "śās" and the rest is neither a substitute nor part of an affix — so that it is this sūtra that applies to "vas"…

**p. 242 — "abibhyuṣā" (concluded); "mandū," "samānavarcasā."** Only "vasi" (the root) is taken there, not the affix "vasu": by **इक्श्तिपौ धातुनिर्देशे** (पा. सू. ३-३-१०८-२०, a vārttika) the "i" in "vasi" marks it as the root. Mādhavācārya too, deriving "tasthuṣaḥ" in the first mantra of this sūkta, obtained the "ṣ" of the affix "vasu" by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ"; so here too it is right to give the "ṣ" by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ." By **तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ…** (पा. सू. "६-२-२-" as printed) the indeclinable first member keeps its accent. In the saṃhitā, "saṃjagmāno + abibhyuṣā": **एङः पदान्तादति** (पा. सू. ६-१-१०९) would make the "e/o" at a word-end and the following short "a" a single prior form, but **प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे** (पा. सू. ६-१-११५) keeps the natural form of such "e/o" inside a pāda before a short "a" not followed by "v" or "y." **"Mandū"** — "madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu": the root is "i"-marked, so **इदितो नुम् धातोः** (पा. सू. ७-१-५८) "num"; **खरुशङ्कुपीयुनीलङ्गुलिगु** (उ. सू. १-३६) forms five words with the affix "ku" by nipātana; since the sūtra's words are given without case-endings, "ku" comes after other roots too, as after "han," and so after "mad"; or by **मृगय्वादयश्च** (उ. सू. १-३७ [?], the last digit unclear), the "mṛgayu"-list being an open class (as with "kaṇḍuḥ," "pīluḥ"), "ku" after "mad"; end-acute by the affix accent. In the dual, "mandu + au": **प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः** gives the long vowel; on the instrumental-singular view, **सुपां सुलुक्…** (पा. सू. ७-१-३९) gives the long vowel. **"Samānavarcasā"** — dual "samānaṃ varco yayos tau," or instrumental singular "samānaṃ varco yasya saḥ" — a bahuvrīhi; in the dual "ā" by "supāṃ suluk…"; "samāna" is end-acute by the stem accent, which stays in the bahuvrīhi by **बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम्** (पा. सू. ६-२-१). ॥७॥
