### Sūkta 7, Rik 2

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्र॒ इद्धर्योः॒ सचा॒ संमि॑श्ल॒ आ व॑चो॒युजा॑ ।
> इन्द्रो॑ व॒ज्री हि॑र॒ण्ययः॑ ॥२॥
>
> *índra íd dháryoḥ sácā sáṃmiśla ā́ vacoyújā |*
> *índro vajrī́ hiraṇyáyaḥ ||2||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रः । इत् । हर्योः । सचा । सम्ऽमिश्लः । आ । वचःऽयुजा ॥
> इन्द्रः । वज्री । हिरण्ययः ॥२॥
>
> *indraḥ | it | haryoḥ | sacā | sam-miślaḥ | ā | vacaḥ-yujā ||*
> *indraḥ | vajrī | hiraṇyayaḥ ||2||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> इन्द्र इदिन्द्र एव हर्योर्हरिनामकयोरश्वयोः सचा सह युगपदा सम्मिश्लः सर्वतः सम्यग्मिश्रयिता । कीदृशयोर्हर्योः । वचोयुजा । इन्द्रस्य वचनमात्रेण रथे युज्यमानयोः सुशिक्षितयोरित्यर्थः । अयमिन्द्रो वज्री वज्रयुक्तो हिरण्ययो हिरण्मयः । सर्वाभरणभूषित इत्यर्थः ॥
>
> *indra id indra eva haryor hari-nāmakayor aśvayoḥ sacā saha yugapad ā sammiślaḥ sarvataḥ samyag-miśrayitā | kīdṛśayor haryoḥ | vacoyujā | indrasya vacana-mātreṇa rathe yujyamānayoḥ suśikṣitayor ity arthaḥ | ayam indro vajrī vajra-yukto hiraṇyayo hiraṇmayaḥ | sarvābharaṇa-bhūṣita ity arthaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "Indra himself, together with (*sacā*) — simultaneously with — his two horses named Hari, comes, being the all-round good mixer/combiner (*sammiślaḥ*). What kind of horses? *Vacoyujā*: yoked to the chariot at Indra's mere word — that is, well-trained. This Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt (*vajrī*), is golden (*hiraṇyayaḥ*, = *hiraṇmayaḥ*) — adorned with all ornaments."

*(Sāyaṇa's grammatical notes follow on page 264 — in the Sanskrit itself — and are characterized there.)*

### Page 264

*(The first part of this page is the Sanskrit grammar of Rik 2 inside the bhāṣya itself. Characterized, not transcribed. Points of substance: **हर्योः (*haryoḥ*)** — "harata iti harī," from *hṛ* with the suffix *in*, "n"-marked, so initial-udātta. **सचा (*sacā*)** — glossed "with" (Nirukta 5-5, "sacā saheti"). **सम्मिश्लः (*sammiślaḥ*)** — "mixing" from *miśra* + *ghañ* (Pā. 3-3-18) with a Vedic *l* for *r*, so "one who mixes thoroughly"; accent of the first member retained in the bahuvrīhi. **वचोयुजा (*vacoyujā*)** — "yoked with a word"; the dual case-ending replaced by *ā*; the second member *yuj* has the final accent. **वज्री (*vajrī*)** — "having a vajra", suffix *ini* (Pā. 5-2-115). **हिरण्ययः (*hiraṇyayaḥ*)** — by **ऋत्व्यवास्त्व्यवास्त्वमाध्वीहिरण्ययानि छन्दसि** (Pāṇini 6-4-175), the *m* of *hiraṇmaya* is dropped irregularly in the Veda, so *hiraṇyaya* is the form; it is udātta on the *ā* by the suffix-accent.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**सम्मिश्लः (sammiślaḥ)** — the one who thoroughly mixes everything | **इन्द्र इत् (indra it)** — Indra himself | **वचोयुजा (vacoyujā)** — yoked to the chariot at Indra's mere word | **हर्योः (haryoḥ)** — with the horses called Hari (of Indra) | **सचा (sacā)** — together with | **आ (yāti)** — comes hither | **इन्द्रः (indraḥ)** — Indra | **वज्री (vajrī)** — the wielder of the thunderbolt | **हिरण्ययः (hiraṇyayaḥ)** — the golden one, that is, adorned with golden ornaments.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Indra, who mixes [combines with] everything, is coming here. At his mere word, his horses are yoked to the chariot. Seated in the chariot to which such horses are yoked, he comes here. That Indra, adorned with ornaments of gold, bears the thunderbolt.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra, the good mixer of all things comes verily with his horses that are harnessed at his word; Indra, the richly-decorated (with gold), the weilder [sic] of the thundorbolt [sic].

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Sacā"** — *saha*: with, together, in company.

**"Sammiślaḥ"** — The Bhāṣyakāra explains this word as **सम्मिश्लः सर्वतः सम्यग्मिश्रयिता** (*sammiślaḥ sarvataḥ samyag miśrayitā*) — "one who mixes well, in every way." Following him, Western scholars such as Wilson … *(continues on p. 265)*

### Page 265

*(Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 13." Re-read from the better scan; the Ṛks and their references as printed.)*

…Western scholars such as Wilson have given the meanings "Blender, mixer, mixing oneself very much with, attached to" (English in the source). The component sense of the word is:

> सम्मिश्लः । मिश्रणं मिश्रः । मिश्रयतेर्घञ् । पा. सू. ३-३-१८ । सम्यक् मिश्रो यस्यासौ सम्मिश्रः । लत्वं छान्दसम् । सम्यक् मिश्रयितेत्यर्थः ।
> *sammiślaḥ | miśraṇaṃ miśraḥ | miśrayater ghañ | pā. sū. 3-3-18 | samyak miśro yasyāsau sammiśraḥ | latvaṃ chāndasam | samyak miśrayitety arthaḥ |*
> "*Sammiślaḥ*: 'mixing' is *miśra*; [formed from] *miśrayati* with *ghañ* (Pāṇini 3-3-18). 'He of whom the mixing is thorough' is *sammiśra*; the *l* [for *r*] is Vedic. The sense: one who mixes thoroughly."

**Though this sense is right for the word, it does not fit "sammiśla" in this Ṛk.** If "sammiślaḥ" is taken to mean "saṃyuktaḥ" (joined) or "sahitaḥ" (accompanied), the sense runs right. The Bhāṣyakāra too, on the word "sammiślāsaḥ" in the Ṛk

> विश्वे देवासो रयिभिः समोकसः संमिश्लासस्तविषीभिर्विरप्शिनः ॥
> *viśve devāso rayibhiḥ samokasaḥ saṃmiślāsas taviṣībhir virapśinaḥ ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-10)

explains it as "*sammiśrāḥ saṃyuktā ity arthaḥ*" (mixed, that is, joined). Ṛks containing the word are given here for illustration:

> यः संमिश्लो हर्योर्यः सुते सचा वज्री रथो हिरण्ययः ॥
> *yaḥ saṃmiślo haryor yaḥ sute sacā vajrī ratho hiraṇyayaḥ ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-33-4)

In this Ṛk too the words and sense of the present Ṛk recur with no great difference.

> प्रभंगी शूरो मघवा तुवीमघः संमिश्लो वीर्याय कम् ॥
> *prabhaṃgī śūro maghavā tuvīmaghaḥ saṃmiślo vīryāya kam ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-61-18)

> संमिश्लो अरुषो भव सूपस्थाभिर्न धेनुभिः ॥
> *saṃmiślo aruṣo bhava sūpasthābhir na dhenubhiḥ ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-61-21)

> मन्द्रो होता स जुह्वा यजिष्ठः संमिश्लो अग्निरा जिघर्ति देवान् ॥
> *mandro hotā sa juhvā yajiṣṭhaḥ saṃmiślo agnir ā jigharti devān ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-6-4)

> मन्द्राः सुजिह्वाः स्वरितार आसभिः संमिश्ला इन्द्रे मरुतः परिष्टुभः ॥
> *mandrāḥ sujihvāḥ svaritāra āsabhiḥ saṃmiślā indre marutaḥ pariṣṭubhaḥ ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-166-11)

> यज्ञैः संमिश्लाः पृषतीभिरृष्टिभिर्यामञ्छुभ्रासो अञ्जिषु प्रिया उत ॥
> *yajñaiḥ saṃmiślāḥ pṛṣatībhir ṛṣṭibhir yāmañ chubhrāso añjiṣu priyā uta ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-36-2)

> प्र यन्तु वाजास्तविषीभिरग्नयः शुभे संमिश्लाः पृषतीरयुक्षत ॥
> *pra yantu vājās taviṣībhir agnayaḥ śubhe saṃmiślāḥ pṛṣatīr ayukṣata ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-26-4)

> यामं येष्ठाः शुभा शोभिष्ठाः श्रिया संमिश्ला ओजोभिरुग्राः ॥
> *yāmaṃ yeṣṭhāḥ śubhā śobhiṣṭhāḥ śriyā saṃmiślā ojobhir ugrāḥ ||* — (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-6 (3))

In all these riks, the sense "joined, accompanied" is the one that fits the word *sammiśla*. **The word occurs nowhere in the Ṛgveda other than the riks listed above.**

**"Vacoyujā"** — the Bhāṣyakāra: **इन्द्रस्य वचनमात्रेण रथे युज्यमानयोः सुशिक्षितयोरित्यर्थः** (*indrasya vacana-mātreṇa rathe yujyamānayoḥ suśikṣitayor ity arthaḥ*) — "of the two [horses] being yoked to the chariot at Indra's mere word, i.e., well-trained." That is: at the mere word of Indra they come ready to be yoked to the chariot; the sense is of **well-trained horses**.

### Page 266

Some Western scholars have rendered this word **"horses which harness themselves."** But how could horses harness themselves to a chariot without the help of a charioteer and others? *They have not considered whether this is possible.* The Bhāṣyakāra's sense — "yoked at Indra's word, or at his command" — is therefore the fitting one.

**"Vajrī"** — **वज्रमस्यास्तीति वज्री** (*vajram asyāstīti vajrī*) — "he who has the vajra" — the wielder of the thunderbolt. Indra's weapon is famous as the vajra (**Thunderbolt**). The Ṛgveda mentions it in many places. For example, Indra himself says:

> मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासो ऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुम् ॥
> *mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajram atakṣad āyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjann api kratum ||* — (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-48-3)
>
> "For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron thunderbolt; in me the gods have set [wisdom/resolve]." *(The Kannada gloss in the source reads: "the divine craftsman Tvaṣṭṛ made me a thunderbolt of iron.")*

**"Hiraṇyayaḥ"** — *hiraṇmayaḥ* — "made of gold," that is, adorned with golden ornaments. One may say that in place of *hiraṇmaya* the form *hiraṇyaya* was then current. Riks containing *hiraṇyaya*-type words — such as **हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेन** (*hiraṇyayena savitā rathena*, "Savitṛ, with a golden chariot") — are plentiful.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

*(Pages 266–268: the Kannada grammar of Rik 2 — characterized, numbers as printed.)*

- **हर्योः (*haryoḥ*)** — *harataḥ rathaṃ iti harī* ("the two that draw the chariot are the *harī*") — from *hṛ* with the suffix *in* by **हृपिषिरुहिवृतिविदिछिदिकीर्तिभ्यश्च** (उ. सू. ४-[?], the printed figures look like "५५८"); the guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (पा. सू. ७-३-८४), with "r" after it by **उरण् रपरः** (पा. सू. १-१-५१).
- **सचा (*sacā*)** — Yāska (Nirukta 5-5) glosses it "saha" — hence "at the same time."
- **सम्मिश्लः (*sammiślaḥ*)** — "miśra saṃparke" is a root of the curādi (tenth) class, so **चुरादिभ्यो णिच्** (पा. सू. ३-१-२५) "ṇic"; then by **भावे** (पा. सू. ३-३-१८) — the verbal sense, in its "accomplished" (siddha) aspect, as against the "to-be-accomplished" (sādhya) aspect seen in "pacati," is called "bhāva" — "ghañ"; **णेरनिटि** (पा. सू. ६-४-५१) drops "ṇi": "miśra"; *sam* + *miśra* as bahuvrīhi, with the Vedic *l* for *r*; the first member's accent retained by Pā. 6-2-1.
- **वचोयुजा (*vacoyujā*)** — "vacasā yujyete iti vacoyujau, tayoḥ" (horses that join the chariot of themselves at Indra's mere word); the genitive dual becomes "ā" by **सुपां सुलुक्…** (पा. सू. ७-१-३९); "yuj" is acute on its final by **धातोः** (पा. सू. ६-१-१६२); after compounding, the kṛt-final second member keeps that accent by **गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्** (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९).
- **वज्री (*vajrī*)** — "vajram asyāsti": **अत इनिठनौ** (पा. सू. ५-२-११५) "ini"; **यस्येति च** (पा. सू. ६-४-१४८) drops the "a"; in the nominative singular **सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ** (पा. सू. ६-४-८) lengthens the penultimate; **हल्ङ्याब्भ्यो दीर्घात्सुतिस्यपृक्तं हल्** (पा. सू. ६-१-६८) drops the "s," which is "apṛkta" by **अपृक्त एकाल्प्रत्ययः** (पा. सू. १-२-४१); **नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य** (पा. सू. ८-२-७) drops the "n": "vajrī," with the affix accent.
- **हिरण्ययः (*hiraṇyayaḥ*)** — "harya gati-kāntyoḥ": **हर्यतेः कन्यन् हिरच्** (उ. सू. ५-[?], the figures unclear) "kanyan," with "hir" for "harya"; "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute, the two final "a"s unaccented by śeṣanighāta; in "hiraṇyapāṇim ūtaye" (ऋ. सं. १-२२-५) "hiraṇya" is shown first-syllable acute by **नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्य** (फि. सू.). In the sense "hiraṇyasya vikāraḥ," **मयड्वैतयोर्भाषायामभक्ष्याच्छादनयोः** (पा. सू. ४-३-१४३) "mayaṭ": "hiraṇmaya"; **ऋत्व्यवास्त्व्यवास्त्वमाध्वीहिरण्ययानि छन्दसि** (पा. सू. ६-४-१७५) … *(continues on p. 268)*

### Page 267, 268 (grammar of Rik 2, continued)

*(Page 267 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 13." The Rik 2 grammar of "hiraṇyayaḥ" is given above under p. 266; p. 268 closes it.)* "Hiraṇyaya" is formed by nipātana (6-4-175: "y" for "ṛtu" and "vāstu" before "yat," and before "aṇ" for "madhu" in the feminine, and the loss of the "m" of "mayaṭ" after "hiraṇya"). If the loss of "m" is so explained that the affix accent must hold, "hiraṇya + aya" gives one substitute by **अतो गुणे** (पा. सू. ६-१-९७); the "a" of "aya" is acute by the affix accent, the final "a" of "hiraṇya" unaccented by śeṣanighāta, and the single substitute acute by **एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्तः** (पा. सू. ८-२-५); so "hi" and "ra" are unaccented, "ṇya" acute, and "yaḥ" svarita by **उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः** (पा. सू. ८-४-६६) — so Mādhavācārya. Some hold that, with the loss of "m," **यस्येति च** (पा. सू. ६-४-१४८) drops the "a" of "hiraṇya," so that the affix's "a" is heard and the intended accent results. But with the loss of "m" treated as not effected by **असिद्धवदत्राभात्** (पा. सू. ६-४-२२), there is no "bha" designation (no "y"-initial affix follows), so "yasyeti ca" cannot apply; and **अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः** (पा. सू. ७-४-२५) would lengthen, not being in the "bha" section; the lengthening is barred by **अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिः** (परिभा. ९३), but the intended accent still fails; and with the "m" loss taken as asiddha, "yasyeti ca" cannot drop the "a." If the whole word ("maya") is lost, "hiraṇya" would be end-acute. So it is proper, as in the Veda-bhāṣya, to accept the loss of the letter, give the later form, and make the single substitute acute by 8-2-5. ॥२॥
### Sūkta 7, Rik 3

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The print sets the svarita stroke over "sū" (not over "ryaṃ"), and over "bhi" of "gobhir" both a stroke and a bar (only the bar is given); hence [accent ?].)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रो॑ दी॒र्घाय॒ चक्ष॑स॒ आ सू॑र्यं रोहयद्दि॒वि । [accent ?]
> वि गोभि॒रद्रिमैरयत् ॥३॥ [accent ?]
>
> *índro dīrghā́ya cákṣasa ā́ sūryaṃ rohayad diví |* [accent ?]
> *ví góbhir ádrim airayat ||3||* [accent ?]

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रः । दीर्घाय । चक्षसे । आ । सूर्यम् । रोहयत् । दिवि ॥
> वि । गोभिः । अद्रिम् । ऐरयत् ॥३॥
>
> *indraḥ | dīrghāya | cakṣase | ā | sūryam | rohayat | divi ||*
> *vi | gobhiḥ | adrim | airayat ||3||*

*(Pada as printed on p. 269, re-read from the better scan.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> अयमिन्द्रो दीर्घाय प्रौढाय निरन्तराय चक्षसे दर्शनाय दिवि द्युलोके सूर्यमा रोहयत् । पुरा वृत्रासुरेण जगति यदाप्रातं तमस्तन्निवारणेन प्राणिनां वृष्टिसिद्ध्यर्थमादित्यं द्युलोके स्थापितवानित्यर्थः । स च सूर्यो गोभिः स्वकीयै रश्मिभिरद्रिं पर्वतप्रमुखं सर्वं जगद्व्यैरयत् । विशेषेण दर्शनार्थं प्रेरितवान् । प्रकाशितवानित्यर्थः । अथवा इन्द्र एव गोभिर्जलैर्वृष्टिनिमित्तभूतैरद्रिं मेघं व्यैरयत् । विशेषेण प्रेरितवान् । पञ्चदशसंख्याकेषु रश्मिनामसु खेदयः किरणा गाव इति पठितम् । त्रिंशत्संख्याकेषु मेघनामस्वद्रिग्रावेति पठितम् ॥
>
> *ayam indro dīrghāya prauḍhāya nirantarāya cakṣase darśanāya divi dyuloke sūryam ā rohayat | purā vṛtrāsureṇa jagati yad āprātaṃ tamas tan-nivāraṇena prāṇināṃ vṛṣṭi-siddhy-artham ādityaṃ dyuloke sthāpitavān ity arthaḥ | sa ca sūryo gobhiḥ svakīyai raśmibhir adriṃ parvata-pramukhaṃ sarvaṃ jagad vyairayat | viśeṣeṇa darśanārthaṃ preritavān | prakāśitavān ity arthaḥ | athavā indra eva gobhir jalair vṛṣṭi-nimitta-bhūtair adriṃ megham vyairayat | viśeṣeṇa preritavān | pañcadaśa-saṃkhyākeṣu raśmi-nāmasu khedayaḥ kiraṇā gāva iti paṭhitam | triṃśat-saṃkhyākeṣu megha-nāmasv adri-grāvety paṭhitam ||*

**Translation:** "This Indra caused the sun to ascend in heaven, the world of light, **for long (*dīrghāya*) — for vast, uninterrupted — seeing (*cakṣase*)**; that is: formerly, when darkness had enveloped the world by the demon Vṛtra, Indra, to remove that darkness and to bring about rain for living beings, established the sun in the heavenly world. And that sun, with his own rays (*gobhiḥ*), set in motion (*vyairayat*) all the world headed by the mountain (*adri*) — especially, *sent out* [his light] for sight; that is, illuminated it. **Or else:** Indra himself, with the waters (*gobhiḥ*) that serve as the cause of rain, set the *adri* — the cloud — in motion in particular. Among the fifteen names for 'ray' *khedayaḥ*, *kiraṇāḥ* and *gāvaḥ* are listed. Among the thirty names for 'cloud' — *adri* and *grāvā* are listed."

**Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed):** "Dīrghāya" — end-acute by the stem accent. "Cakṣase" — **चक्षेः सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन्** (उ. ४-१८८) "asun"; by the word "bahula" no "khyāñ" substitute; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Sūryam" — "suvati prerayatīti sūryaḥ," "ṣū preraṇe," "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ"; **राजसूयसूर्य…** (पा. ३-१-११४) "kyap" with the augment "ruṭ" by nipātana; "kyap," "k"-marked, so no guṇa, and "p"-marked, so unaccented; the root accent remains. "Rohayat" — "ruh" with "ṇic," "laṅ"; **बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपि** (पा. ६-४-७५) no augment "aṭ"; nighāta. "Divi" — the case-ending acute by "ūḍidam…". "Adrim" — **अदिशदिभूशुभिभ्यः क्रिन्** (उ. ४-६५) "krin": "atti patavas tṛṇādikam ity adriḥ"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Airayat" — "īra gatau" with "ṇic," "laṅ"; nighāta.

### Page 269 — Rik 3 continued

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**इन्द्रः (indraḥ)** — Indra | **दीर्घाय चक्षसे (dīrghāya cakṣase)** — continuously, that is, so that [beings] may see always (for the sake of seeing, for light) | **सूर्यम् (sūryam)** — the sun | **दिवि (divi)** — in the heavenly world (in the sky) | **आ रोहयत् (ā rohayat)** — set up (caused to climb) | (that sun) **गोभिः (gobhiḥ)** — with his rays | **अद्रिम् (adrim)** — the mountain (that is, the whole world, mountains and the rest) | **वि ऐरयत् (vi airayat)** — impelled specially, that is, illuminated.

**Or:**

### Page 270

**इन्द्रः (indraḥ)** — Indra | **गोभिः (gobhiḥ)** — with the *gāvaḥ* (waters) that serve as the cause of rain | **अद्रिम् (adrim)** — the cloud | **वि ऐरयत् (vi airayat)** — impelled specially.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

In ancient times the demon Vṛtra made the world a mass of darkness. Indra slew Vṛtra and — so that there should be light in the world until the time of dissolution — set the sun in the heavens (the *antarikṣa*). The sun, too, illuminated the whole world — mountains, and so on — with his rays, and made all beings, who had been unable to do any work on account of the darkness, take up their several tasks. **Or:** after setting the sun in the sky, Indra sent the cloud to rain upon the people (or living beings), so that grain, which is food, might grow.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra established the sun in the heaven to render all things visible. He illuminated the mountain (i.e. the world) with his rays or Indra charged the clouds with water.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**An earlier legend.** The Bhāṣyakāra and **Skandasvāmī** both mention an ancient story here. In former days the demon Vṛtra made the whole world dark. People and living creatures, having no light, were unable to do their work. Seeing this, Indra slew Vṛtra and established the sun in the sky so that there would be light in the world. In accord with this, this rik says that Indra established the sun in the sky.

**"Dīrghāya"** — *nirantarāya*, "uninterrupted" — *pralaya-paryantam*: "until dissolution" — "always, as long as the world lasts."

**"Cakṣase"** — sight, light, brilliance, etc. Without the sun, neither light nor strength nor capacity would belong to living beings; the business of the world would not go on. That is why it is said: **सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च** (*sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthuṣaś ca*) — "the sun is the self of the moving and the unmoving world" (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-115-1) — the sun is the very self (as life is chief to the body) of all the world, animate and inanimate.

### Page 271

**"Vi gobhir adrim airayat"** — **The meaning of this sentence is not clear.** The poet may have so described it because, when the sun rises, his rays first fall upon the lofty mountains. The other sense — that Indra impelled the cloud for water, that is, for the work of rain — is also fitting.

**"Gobhiḥ"** — with rays; with water. Among the fifteen words for "ray," beginning with *khedayaḥ*, the words **किरणाः** (*kiraṇāḥ*) and **गावः** (*gāvaḥ*) are listed.

**"Adrim"** — mountain, cloud. Among the thirty words for "cloud," beginning with *adriḥ grāvā*, the word *adri* is listed.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

*(Pages 271–272. Characterized; numbers as printed.)*

- **दीर्घाय (*dīrghāya*)** — by the prātipadika accent, *dīrgha* is final-udātta.
- **चक्षसे (*cakṣase*)** — "cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci": "asun" carried from **सर्वधातुभ्योऽसुन्** (उ. सू. ४-६७ [?]) by **चक्षेर्बहुलं शिच्च** (उ. सू. ४-६८ [?]); "asun" is optionally "ś"-marked, so here, being "śit," it is sārvadhātuka by **तिङ्शित्सार्वधातुकम्**, not ārdhadhātuka, and the "khyāñ" of **चक्षिङः ख्याञ्** (पा. सू. २-४-५४) does not come; "n"-marked, so first-syllable acute.
- **सूर्यम् (*sūryam*)** — from *sū* ("to impel") — "he who impels (the world)"; *ṣa→sa* for the initial by Pā. 6-1-64; and the *kyap* suffix by the sūtra *rājasūya-sūrya-mṛṣodya-rucya-kupya-kṛṣṭapacya-avyathyāḥ* (Pā. 3-1-114): these seven words are formed by nipātana with *kyap*, and in "sūrya" the *ruṭ* augment is by nipātana; or from *sṛ gatau* ("sarati gacchati ākāśe"), with "u" by nipātana, "r" by **उरण् रपरः** (पा. सू. १-१-५१), and the long vowel by **हलि च** (पा. सू. ८-२-७७); on the first view "kyap," "k"-marked, gives no guṇa, and "p"-marked is unaccented by **अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ** ("३-१-४"), so the root accent stays.
- **रोहयत् (*rohayat*)** — "ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca" with *ṇic*, "laṅ"; by **बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपि** (पा. सू. ६-४-७५) no augment "aṭ"; unaccented by **तिङ्ङतिङः** (पा. सू. ८-१-२८).
- **दिवि (*divi*)** — the case-ending is udātta by the *ūḍidam-padādy-appum-raidyubhyaḥ* rule (Pā. 6-1-171).
- **अद्रिम् (*adrim*)** — **अदिशदिभूशुभिभ्यः क्रिन्** (उ. सू. ४-५०३ as printed [?]) "krin" after "ad bhakṣaṇe" ("adanti paśavas tṛṇādikam atra," where beasts eat grass): "adri"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute.
- **ऐरयत् (*airayat*)** — "īra gatau" with *ṇic* + *laṅ*, third singular parasmaipada; unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ."

**॥३॥**

*(These last items are on p. 272.)*

### Page 272 — Sūkta 7, Rik 4

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्र॒ वाजे॑षु नो ऽव स॒हस्र॑प्रधनेषु च ।
> उ॒ग्र उ॒ग्राभि॑रू॒तिभिः॑ ॥४॥
>
> *índra vā́jeṣu no 'va sahásrapradhaneṣu ca |*
> *ugrá ugrā́bhir ūtíbhiḥ ||4||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्र । वाजेषु । नः । अव । सहस्रऽप्रधनेषु । च ॥
> उग्रः । उग्राभिः । ऊतिऽभिः ॥४॥
>
> *indra | vājeṣu | naḥ | ava | sahasra-pradhaneṣu | ca ||*
> *ugraḥ | ugrābhiḥ | ūti-bhiḥ ||4||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र उग्रः शत्रुभिरप्रधृष्यस्त्वमुग्राभिरप्रधृष्याभिरूतिभिरस्मद्विषयरक्षाभिर्वाजेषु युद्धेषु नो ऽस्मानव रक्ष । तथा सहस्रप्रधनेषु च । सहस्रसंख्याकगजाश्वादिलाभयुक्तेषु महायुद्धेष्वपि रक्ष ॥
>
> *he indra ugraḥ śatrubhir apradhṛṣyas tvam ugrābhir apradhṛṣyābhir ūtibhir asmad-viṣaya-rakṣābhir vājeṣu yuddheṣu no 'smān ava rakṣa | tathā sahasra-pradhaneṣu ca | sahasra-saṃkhyāka-gajāśvādi-lābha-yukteṣu mahā-yuddheṣv api rakṣa ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra! You — *ugra*, unassailable to enemies — with your *ugra* protections (*ūtibhiḥ*), unassailable, directed to our concerns, protect us (*naḥ ava*) in battles (*vājeṣu*) — and likewise in the *sahasra-pradhanas*, that is, even in great battles that bring the winning of thousands of elephants, horses and the like, protect us."

**Grammar of the Bhāṣya (pp. 272–273; characterized, references as printed):** "Vājeṣu" — first-syllable acute by **वृषादीनां च** (पा. ६-१-२०३). "No 'va" — the "o" from "nas" stays unchanged by "prakṛtyāntaḥpādam…" is not applicable, because of the prohibition "avyapare" (पा. ६-१-११५). "Ava" — "ava rakṣaṇe"; nighāta by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ." Although, in relation to the verb to be supplied with "sahasrapradhaneṣu ca," "ava" is the first verb, and **चवायोगे प्रथमा** (पा. ८-१-५९) would forbid the nighāta, here in "vājeṣu" the "ca" is elided, and by **चादिलोपे विभाषा** (पा. ८-१-६३) the prohibition is optional, so the nighāta applies. "Sahasra" — **कर्दमादीनां च** (फि. ३-१०) middle-acute; in the bahuvrīhi the first member's accent stays. "Ugraḥ" — "uca samavāye," "c" → "g," "ran" by "ṛjrendra…"; end-acute by vyatyaya. "Ūtibhiḥ" — "ktin" acute by "ūtiyūti…".

### Page 273

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **(त्वम्)** — you | **उग्रः (ugraḥ)** — one who cannot be conquered by enemies | (such you) **उग्राभिः (ugrābhiḥ)** — with those that cannot be overcome by enemies | **ऊतिभिः (ūtibhiḥ)** — with protections | **नः (naḥ)** — us | **वाजेषु (vājeṣu)** — in battles | **सहस्रप्रधनेषु (sahasrapradhaneṣu)** — in great battles in which unlimited spoil of elephants, horses, chariots and the like is obtained | **अव (ava)** — protect.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! You are *apradhṛṣya* — that is, enemies cannot conquer you. Such as you are: with your invincible protections (that is, helps), protect us in the great battles which we wage with our enemies for the gain of elephants, horses, chariots and the like.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, You are invincible; protect us with insuperable aids in battles where thousand-fold spoils are gained.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

### Page 274

*(The Special Topics begin at the foot of p. 273.)*

**"Sahasrapradhaneṣu"** — *pradhana* or *mahādhana* means battle. (The word *mahādhana* is read among the **forty-six** words for "battle," beginning with *raṇa* — "Ni. 3-9" as printed [?]; the usual place is Nighaṇṭu 2-17.) Since this rik already contains **another** word for battle, *vājeṣu*, to take *pradhaneṣu* in *sahasrapradhaneṣu* as "battle" would bring about the fault of repetition (*dviruktidoṣa*) and the sense would not fit well. **The Bhāṣyakāra's component-sense is therefore the right one**: when one fights and conquers enemies, the elephants, horses, weapons, wealth, gold, vehicles and all other possessions that were with those enemies naturally come under the power of the victors. Thus Indra is prayed to give us suitable help in thousands of battles, so that we may conquer our enemies and take all their wealth, and that, at the same time, we may be protected, with no danger to our lives from the enemy.

**"Ugraḥ"** — may be taken in the senses *apradhṛṣya* (unassailable), *ajeya* (unconquerable), *sahisalaśakya* (not to be borne, i.e. irresistible), *parākramī* (valiant), *krūra* (fierce), etc.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

*(Pages 274–275. Characterized; numbers as printed.)*

- **वाजे (*vāje*)** — initial-udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 6-1-203); *vāja* is to be reckoned among the *vṛṣādi* words because that group is an *ākṛti-gaṇa*.
- **नो ऽव (*no 'va*)** — **बहुवचनस्य वस्नसौ** (पा. सू. ८-१-२१): after a word, not at the start of a pāda, the plural genitive, dative and accusative of "yuṣmad, asmad" become the unaccented "vas, nas"; so "asmān" → "nas"; **ससजुषो रुः** (पा. सू. "९-२-६६" as printed, i.e. 8-2-66) "ru"; **अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते** (पा. सू. ६-१-११३) "u"; **आद्गुणः** (पा. सू. ६-१-८७) "no + ava." **प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपरे** (पा. सू. ६-१-११५) would keep "e, o" unchanged inside a pāda before a short "a," but not before an "a" followed by "v" or "y" ("avyapare"); here the "a" is followed by "v," so **एङः पदान्तादति** (पा. सू. ६-१-१०९) gives the prior form: "no 'va."
- **अव (*ava*)** — "ava rakṣaṇe," unaccented by **तिङ्ङतिङः** (पा. सू. ८-१-२८). There are two sentences ("indra vājeṣu no 'va" and "sahasrapradhaneṣu ca no 'va"); the "ava" of the first is "first-uttered" with respect to the one supplied in the second, so **चवायोगे प्रथमा** (पा. सू. ८-१-५९) would forbid its nighāta; but **चादिलोपे विभाषा** (पा. सू. ८-१-६३) makes the prohibition optional when "ca, vā, ha, aha, eva" are "lost," that is, not uttered — here no "ca" is uttered in the first sentence — so where the prohibition does not apply the verb is unaccented.
- **सहस्रप्रधनेषु (*sahasrapradhaneṣu*)** — by **कर्दमादीनां च** (फि. सू. ५९ [?]) the words of this list are acute on the first or the second syllable, so "sahasra" has the acute on "ha": middle-acute; as a bahuvrīhi it retains the first member's accent (Pā. 6-2-1).
- **उग्रः (*ugraḥ*)** — from *uc* ("to be pleased, to gather") with the *ran* suffix of the Uṇādi-sūtra (**ऋज्रेन्द्राग्रवज्रविप्रकुब्रचुब्रक्षुरखुरभद्रोग्रभेरभेलशुक्रशुक्लगौरवन्नेरमालाः**, उ. सू. २-१८६), which forms these nineteen words with "ran"; "c" → "g" by the nipātana of "ugra"; though the affix is "n"-marked, by vyatyaya end-acute.
- **ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)** — *ūtiyūtijūti-sātihetikīrtayaś ca* (Pā. 3-3-97): *ūti*, etc., are irregularly formed *ktin* words, final-udātta; and thus *ūti* has the udātta *ktin* suffix.

**॥४॥**

### Page 275 — Sūkta 7, Rik 5

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The bar under the last syllable of "havāmahe" stands before "yújam" of the next line.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रं॑ व॒यं म॑हाध॒न इन्द्र॒मर्भे॑ हवामहे॒ ।
> युजं॑ वृ॒त्रेषु॑ व॒ज्रिण॑म् ॥५॥
>
> *índraṃ vayám mahādhaná índram árbhe havāmahe |*
> *yújaṃ vṛtréṣu vajríṇam ||5||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रम् । वयम् । महाऽधने । इन्द्रम् । अर्भे । हवामहे ॥
> युजम् । वृत्रेषु । वज्रिणम् ॥५॥
>
> *indram | vayam | mahā-dhane | indram | arbhe | havāmahe ||*
> *yujam | vṛtreṣu | vajriṇam ||5||*

---

### Page 276 — Rik 5: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> वयमनुष्ठातारो महाधने प्रभूतधननिमित्तमिन्द्रं हवामहे । आह्वयामः । अर्भे ऽर्भके स्वल्पे ऽपि धने निमित्तभूते सतीन्द्रं हवामहे । कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । युजं सहकारिणं समाहितं वा । वृत्रेषु शत्रुषु धनलाभविरोधिषु प्राप्तेषु तन्निवारणाय वज्रिणं वज्रोपेतम् ॥ महाधनशब्दो यद्यपि संग्रामनामसु पठितस्तथापि महद्धनमत्र संग्राम इति बहुव्रीहित्वे सत्यन्तोदात्तत्वासिद्धेर्नात्र तद्गृहीतम् । महाधने महच्च तद्धनं चेति समासस्येत्यन्तोदात्तः ।
>
> *vayam anuṣṭhātāro mahādhane prabhūta-dhana-nimittam indraṃ havāmahe | āhvayāmaḥ | arbhe 'rbhake svalpe 'pi dhane nimitta-bhūte satīndraṃ havāmahe | kīdṛśam indram | yujaṃ saha-kāriṇaṃ samāhitaṃ vā | vṛtreṣu śatruṣu dhana-lābha-virodhiṣu prāpteṣu tan-nivāraṇāya vajriṇaṃ vajropetam || mahādhana-śabdo yadyapi saṃgrāma-nāmasu paṭhitas tathāpi mahad dhanam atra saṃgrāma iti bahuvrīhitve saty antodāttatvāsiddher nātra tad gṛhītam | mahādhane mahac ca tad dhanaṃ ceti samāsasyety antodāttaḥ |*

**Translation:** "We, the performers [of the rite], call upon Indra *in the mahādhana* — on account of abundant wealth; we summon him. *In the arbha* — when even a small, slight wealth is the occasion — we call Indra. What kind of Indra? *Yujam* — the helper, the co-operator, or [alternatively] the composed one. *In the vṛtras* — when enemies, who obstruct the gain of wealth, have arrived, to ward them off, [we call] the *vajriṇam* — the one equipped with the thunderbolt. Although the word *mahādhana* is read among the names for 'battle,' it is *not* so taken here: if it were analysed as a bahuvrīhi ('that in which there is great wealth, i.e., battle'), final-udātta accent would not be established [for the word as it stands in the rik]. [Hence] *mahādhane* = 'great and that wealth' (*mahac ca tad dhanaṃ ca*), a karmadhāraya compound, final-udātta by the sūtra on compounds."

**Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed):** "Arbhe" — **अर्तिगृभ्यां भन्** (उ. ३-१५२ [?]) "bhan"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Havāmahe" — "hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca"; **स्वरितञितः कर्त्रभिप्राये क्रियाफले** (पा. १-३-७२) the ātmanepada; "laṭ," "mahiṅ" (पा. ३-४-७८); **टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे** (पा. ३-४-७९) "e"; **कर्तरि शप्** (पा. ३-१-६८); **ह्वः संप्रसारणम्** (पा. ६-१-३२) carried on with **बहुलं छन्दसि** (पा. ६-१-३४): samprasāraṇa, "u" for "v," the prior form, guṇa and "av"; **अतो दीर्घो यञि** (पा. ७-३-१०१) the long vowel; nighāta by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ." "Yujam" — "yuja samādhau," "kvip"; **युजेरसमासे** (पा. ७-१-७१) would give "num," but not here: the sūtra names "yuji" with "i," so it does not apply to the root without "i" ("yuja samādhau"); or the augment is anitya. "Vṛtreṣu" — "vṛtu vartane," "pratikūlatayā vartanta iti vṛtrāṇi śatrukulāni"; **स्फायितञ्चि…** (उ. २-१३) "rak"; "k"-marked, no guṇa; the affix accent. "Vajriṇam" — "ata iniṭhanau": "ini"; the affix accent. ॥५॥

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**वयम् (vayam)** — we | **इन्द्रम् (indram)** — Indra | **महाधने (mahādhane)** — for the gaining of vast wealth | **हवामहे (havāmahe)** — we invoke (call) | **अर्भके (arbhake)** — even for the gaining of small wealth | **इन्द्रम् (indram)** — Indra (we invoke) | **युजम् (yujam)** — who is our helper (and) | **वृत्रेषु (vṛtreṣu)** — when enemies (opponents to our gain of wealth) come, for their subjugation | **वज्रिणम् (vajriṇam)** — who holds the thunderbolt | (**इन्द्रम्** — Indra — **हवामहे** — we invoke).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Whether we need a little wealth or much, for obtaining that wealth we invoke Indra himself. Further, that Indra not only helps us in our undertakings, but, when enemies who oppose us come, he stands ready to use his thunderbolt to subdue them. Such an Indra we invoke.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> We invoke Indra for great wealth ; Indra for (even) little weath [sic] ; Indra [is] our ally and weilder [sic] of the thunderbolt against enemies

### Page 277 — Rik 5: Special Topics

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**A divergence from the Bhāṣyakāra.** In fixing the sense of this rik, **Skandasvāmī's explanation is more acceptable than the one the Bhāṣyakāra gives**, and it is given below.

**Skandasvāmi-bhāṣyam** (as quoted in the Kannada script of the source):

> महाधने । संग्रामनामैतत् । महति संग्रामे । इन्द्रमेव अर्भे । अल्पनामैतत् । अल्पे । क्व । पूर्वत्र निर्देशात् संग्राम एव । हवामहे आह्वयामः । युजं युज्यतेऽसाविति युक् सहायः तम् । वृत्रेषु संग्रामव्यतिरिक्तेष्वपि च शत्रुषु इन्द्रमेव समाह्वयामः वज्रिणम् ॥
>
> *mahādhane | saṃgrāma-nāmaitat | mahati saṃgrāme | indram eva | arbhe | alpa-nāmaitat | alpe | kva | pūrvatra nirdeśāt saṃgrāma eva | havāmahe āhvayāmaḥ | yujaṃ yujyate 'sāv iti yuk sahāyaḥ tam | vṛtreṣu saṃgrāma-vyatirikteṣv api ca śatruṣu indram eva samāhvayāmaḥ vajriṇam ||*
>
> **Translation:** "*Mahādhane* — this is a name for battle: in a great battle. [We call] Indra alone. *Arbhe* — this is a name for 'small': in a small [battle]. In what? Because of the earlier mention, [it must be] in battle only. *Havāmahe* — we summon. *Yujam* — "he is joined" (*yujyate 'sau*), so *yuk*, a helper — him. *Vṛtreṣu* — in the enemies apart from [formal] battle as well, we call Indra alone — him, the wielder of the thunderbolt."

**Anuvāda (the Kannada rendering of Skandasvāmī, as printed):** *Mahādhana* means battle — a great battle. *Arbhe* means a small battle. So, whether the battle is small or great, we call upon Indra alone for our help. And not only in matters of battle but in other matters too, for the removal of our enemies, we call upon Indra alone, the thunderbolt-bearer.

**The translator's judgment.** Since the **previous rik** treats the subject of battle, the sense "in both the small and the great battles mentioned in this rik we seek Indra's help alone" is coherent. It is therefore **more fitting to take *mahādhane* as "in a great battle"** than as "for obtaining much wealth." Moreover, the word *ūtaye* ("for our protection") in the previous rik *(as the source quotes it)*, and the word *vajriṇam* ("endowed with the thunderbolt") in this rik, both point to protection and to the subduing of enemies — matters pertaining to battle. For these reasons, **Skandasvāmī's explanation is the one to be accepted here.**

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

*(Pp. 277–279. Characterized; numbers as printed.)*

- **महाधने (*mahādhane*)** — Yāska does list *mahādhana* among the names for battle; but if taken that way here it would be a bahuvrīhi (*mahat dhanam atra saṃgrāme*, "in which there is great wealth") and would then take the accent of its first member (*pūrvapada-prakṛti-svara*), so final-udātta could not be explained. Hence it is taken as a karmadhāraya *mahac ca tad dhanaṃ ca* ("great, and that wealth"), which is final-udātta by **समासस्य** (पा. सू. ६-१-२२३); *mahat* → *mahā* by **आन्महतः समानाधिकरणजातीययोः** (पा. सू. ६-३-४६).
- **अर्भे (*arbhe*)** — root *ṛ* + *bhan* by **अर्तिगृभ्यां भन्** (उ. सू. ३-४०२ [?], as printed; the bhāṣya gives "उ. ३-१५२"), with *guṇa*; locative singular; *nit* so initial-udātta.
- **हवामहे (*havāmahe*)** — root *hve ñ* ("to call; to vie; to sound"); ātmanepada by Pā. 1-3-72 (the fruit of the act accrues to the agent); *laṭ*, first-person plural *mahiṅ*, with *e* by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e"; *śap*; Vedic *saṃprasāraṇa* of *hve* (*hu+a+mahe*), then *guṇa* and lengthening, giving *havāmahe*; unaccented as a finite verb.
- **युजम् (*yujam*)** — root *yuja samādhau* + *kvip* with total loss of the suffix; the question whether the augment *num* arises (by "yujer asamāse," Pā. 7-1-71) is argued and answered in the negative here.
- **वृत्रेषु (*vṛtreṣu*)** — root *vṛtu vartane* ("to be; to stand"), "those that stand in opposition"; a *rak* suffix, *kit*, so no *guṇa*; final-udātta by the suffix. *(Page 279's first lines list the thirty-odd roots after which* rak *comes, including this one.)*
- **वज्रिणम् (*vajriṇam*)** — *vajra* + *ini* (Pā. 5-2-115); accent by the suffix.

### Page 278

*(Rik 5 grammar, continued; Kannada; numbers as printed.)* **"Havāmahe"** — **स्वरितञितः कर्त्रभिप्राये क्रियाफले** (पा. सू. १-३-७२) the ātmanepada; "mahiṅ" by **तिप्तस्झि…** (पा. सू. ३-४-७८); **टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे** (पा. सू. ३-४-७९) "mahe"; **कर्तरि शप्** (पा. सू. ३-१-६८); **बहुलं छन्दसि** (पा. सू. ६-१-३४), with **ह्वः संप्रसारणम्** (पा. सू. ६-१-३२) carried on: "hu + a + a + mahe"; **संप्रसारणाच्च** (पा. सू. ६-१-१०८) the prior form; guṇa by **सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः** (पा. सू. ७-३-८४); **एचोऽयवायावः** (पा. सू. ६-१-७८) "av"; **अतो दीर्घो यञि** (पा. सू. ७-३-१०१) the long "ā": "havāmahe"; unaccented by **तिङ्ङतिङः** (पा. सू. ८-१-२८). **"Yujam"** — "yuja samādhau" + "kvip": its "p" is "it" by **हलन्त्यम्** (पा. सू. १-३-३), the "i" by **उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत्** (पा. सू. १-३-२), the "k" by **लशक्वतद्धिते** (पा. सू. १-३-८), all dropped by **तस्य लोपः** (पा. सू. १-३-९); the apṛkta "v" by **वेरपृक्तस्य** (पा. सू. ६-१-६७): the whole affix is lost. In the accusative "yuj + am," **युजेरसमासे** (पा. सू. ७-१-७१) would give "num" before a sarvanāmasthāna; but the sūtra names "yuji" (with "i"), i.e. "yujir yoge," not "yuja samādhau," so no "num"; and even if "yujir yoge" is taken, by **अनित्यमागमशासनम्** (परिभा. ९३-२) the augment rule is anitya, so "num" is to be withheld. **"Vṛtreṣu"** — "vṛtu vartane": "pratikūlatayā vartanta iti" (those standing in opposition), "vṛtrāṇi," hosts of enemies; **स्फायितञ्चिवञ्चिशकिक्षिपिक्षुदिसृपितृपिदृपिवन्द्युन्दिश्वितिवृत्य…** *(continues on p. 279)*

### Sūkta 7, Rik 6

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> स नो॑ वृषन्न॒मुं च॒रुं सत्रा॑दाव॒न्नपा॑ वृधि ।
> अ॒स्मभ्य॒मप्र॑तिष्कुतः ॥६॥
>
> *sá no vṛṣann amúṃ carúṃ sátrādāvann ápā vṛdhi |*
> *asmábhyam ápratiṣkutaḥ ||6||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> सः । नः । वृषन् । अमुम् । चरुम् । सत्राऽदावन् । अप । वृधि ॥
> अस्मभ्यम् । अप्रतिऽस्कुतः ॥६॥
>
> *saḥ | naḥ | vṛṣan | amum | carum | satrā-dāvan | apa | vṛdhi ||*
> *asmabhyam | aprati-ṣkutaḥ ||6||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे सत्रादावन् अस्मदभीष्टानां सर्वेषां फलानां सह प्रदातः । अतो व्रीह्यादिनिष्पत्त्यर्थं हे वृषन् वृष्टिप्रदेन्द्र नो ऽस्मदर्थममुं दृश्यमानं चरुं मेघमपा वृधि । उद्घाटय । तथैवास्मभ्यमस्मदर्थमप्रतिष्कुतः । प्रतिशब्दरहितः । यद्यस्माभिर्याच्यते तत्र सर्वत्र नेति प्रतिशब्दं नोच्चारयसि । अतो ऽस्मद्विषये कदाचिदप्यप्रतिस्खलितः । एतदेवाभिप्रेत्य यास्क आह । अप्रतिष्कुतो ऽप्रतिष्कृतो ऽप्रतिस्खलितो वा । नि. ६-१६ । इति ॥
>
> *he satrādāvan asmad-abhīṣṭānāṃ sarveṣāṃ phalānāṃ saha pradātaḥ | ato vrīhy-ādi-niṣpatty-arthaṃ he vṛṣan vṛṣṭi-pradendra no 'smad-artham amuṃ dṛśyamānaṃ caruṃ megham apā vṛdhi | udghāṭaya | tathaivāsmabhyam asmad-artham apratiṣkutaḥ | prati-śabda-rahitaḥ | yad yasmābhir yācyate tatra sarvatra neti prati-śabdaṃ noccārayasi | ato 'smad-viṣaye kadācid apy apratiskhalitaḥ | etad evābhipretya yāska āha | apratiṣkuto 'pratiṣkṛto 'pratiskhalito vā | ni. 6-16 | iti ||*

**Translation:** "O *Satrādāvan*, together-giver of all the fruits we desire! Therefore, for the growing of rice, barley and the like, O *Vṛṣan* — O Indra, giver of rain — **open** (*apā vṛdhi*) for our sake **this cloud** (*caruṃ*) that is seen — unclose it. And likewise be *apratiṣkuta* toward us, for our sake: without a *prati-śabda* (a counter-word); that is, in whatever is asked of us you never utter a 'no'; hence in our matter you are at no time obstructed. With just this in mind, Yāska says: '*apratiṣkuta* is *apratiṣkṛta*, or *apratiskhalita*' (Nirukta 6-16)."

**Grammar of the Bhāṣya (p. 280; characterized, references as printed):** "Vṛṣan" — vocative nighāta. "Amum" — end-acute by the stem accent. "Carum" — "caratīti caruḥ": **भृमृशीतृचरित्सरितनिधनिमिमस्जिभ्य उः** (उ. १-७) "u"; end-acute by the affix accent. "Satrādāvan" — "satrā" in the sense "together"; "abhimata-phala-jātaṃ sakalaṃ saha dadātīti satrādāvā"; **आतो मनिन्क्वनिब्वनिपश्च** (पा. ३-२-७४) "vanip"; vocative first-syllable acute by "āmantritasya ca"; being pāda-initial, no nighāta. "Apa" — **निपातस्य च** (पा. ६-३-१३६) lengthening; first-syllable acute as a particle. "Vṛdhi" — "vṛñ varaṇe," "loṭ," "sip," "hi" by **सेर्ह्यपिच्च** (पा. ३-४-८७); **स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः** (पा. ३-१-७३) "śnu," elided by "bahulaṃ chandasi"; **श्रुशृणुपृकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसि** (पा. ६-४-१०२) "dhi" for "hi"; "ṅit," so no guṇa of the preceding vowel; nighāta. "Asmabhyam" — **भ्यसो भ्यम्** (पा. ७-१-३०); **शेषे लोपः** (पा. ७-२-९०) loss of "d"; **बहुवचने झल्येत्** (पा. ७-३-१०३) does not apply, by "aṅgavṛtte punarvṛttāv avidhir niṣṭhitasya" (म. ७-१-३०); the "a" acute by the stem accent; on the view that "bhyam" replaces "bhyas," the "ad" of "asmad" up to "ma" is lost by "śeṣe lopaḥ," and by the accent of the removed acute (**…उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वर…**, पा. ६-१-१६१) the "a" of "bhyam" is acute. "Apratiṣkutaḥ" — "kenacid apratiśabditaḥ": "kuṅ śabde," niṣṭhā "kta" in the passive (पा. ३-२-१०२); after "prati" the augment "suṭ" by the "pāraskarādi" class, an ākṛtigaṇa (पा. ६-१-१५७); "ṣ" by the "suṣāmādi" class, an ākṛtigaṇa (पा. ८-३-९८); in the nañ-compound the indeclinable first member keeps its accent.

### Page 280 — Rik 6 continued

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**सत्रादावन् (satrādāvan)** — O giver of all our desired things! (for that very reason) | **वृषन् (vṛṣan)** — O Indra, giver of rain! | **सः (त्वम्) (saḥ [tvam])** — such as you are | **नः (naḥ)** — for us | **अमुम् (amum)** — this, which is visible to our eyes | **चरुम् (carum)** — the cloud | **अपा वृधि (apā vṛdhi)** — cause it to rain | (because you) **अस्मभ्यम् (asmabhyam)** — for us, or in our regard | **अप्रतिष्कुतः (apratiṣkutaḥ)** — have not turned away.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! You are the one who fulfils all our desires. For that very reason, make the cloud that is now visible to our eyes in the sky pour down rain. You have never been one to refuse our prayer.

*(The printed page carries no separate "English Translation" block for this rik; none is supplied here.)*

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Vṛṣan"** — the giver of rain, the one who causes rain. In modern Sanskrit the word *vṛṣa* has several senses — bull, ox, "excellent," "full of manliness." In the Ṛgveda this word is used of Indra in many places.

### Page 281

**"Carum"** — **अन्तरिक्षे चरतीति चरुः** (*antarikṣe caratīti caruḥ*) — "that which moves in the atmosphere is *caru*": the cloud is called *caru* because it travels in the sky. Among the thirty names for 'cloud', beginning with *adriḥ*, the word *caruḥ* is listed (Ni. 2-21 [?], the first digit unclear).

**"Satrādāvan"** — the Bhāṣyakāra explains *satrā* as "together" (*saha*); thus "one who gives everything together." In the Nirukta, however, *satrā* is read among the six words for "truth" beginning with *bāṭ* (Ni. 3-10). Therefore *satrādāvan* may also be understood as "one who *truly* gives (what we desire)."

**"Apa"** — for the convenience of the meter, the *p-a* of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha *(i.e., the Saṃhitā reads* apā*)*.

**"Apratiṣkutaḥ"** — Yāska explains this in his Nirukta: *apratiṣkuto 'pratiṣkṛto 'pratiskhalito vā* — that is, one who does not reject [our prayer], who does not fail [to keep] his word.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

*(Pp. 281–283. Characterized; numbers as printed.)*

- **वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)** — a vocative, hence unaccented (anudātta) by "āmantritasya ca" (पा. सू. ८-१-१९).
- **अमुम् (*amum*)** — the demonstrative *adas* in the accusative singular; final-udātta by its base (*prātipadika*) accent.
- **चरुम् (*carum*)** — *carati iti caruḥ*; from root *car* ("to move; to eat") with the Uṇādi *u* suffix by **भृमृशीतृचरित्सरितनिधनिमिमस्जिभ्य उः** (उ. सू. १-७; the roots glossed one by one); final-udātta by the suffix; accusative singular *carum*.
- **सत्रादावन् (*satrādāvan*)** — *satrā* ("together"), *dā* ("to give"), with *vanip* (Pā. 3-2-74); as the word begins the second pāda, the Aṣṭamādhyāyī rule that unaccents a vocative does not apply, and it is initial-udātta by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198).
- **अप (*apa*)** — a nipāta (particle), initial-udātta (फि. सू. ८०); lengthened in the mantra by **निपातस्य च** (पा. सू. ६-३-१३६) to *apā*.
- **वृधि (*vṛdhi*)** — "vṛñ varaṇe," "loṭ," second singular "sip," "hi" by **सेर्ह्यपिच्च** (पा. सू. ३-४-८७); **स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः** (पा. सू. ३-१-७३), whose "śnu" is sometimes elided by "bahula" in **बहुलं छन्दसि** (पा. सू. २-४-७३); **श्रुशृणुपृकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसि** (पा. सू. ६-४-१०२) "dhi" for "hi"; "hi" being "apit" is "ṅit" by **सार्वधातुकमपित्** (पा. सू. १-२-४), so **क्ङिति च** (पा. सू. १-१-५) blocks the guṇa of **सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः** (पा. सू. ७-३-८४); unaccented by **तिङ्ङतिङः** (printed "१८-१-२८," i.e. 8-1-28).
- **अस्मभ्यम् (*asmabhyam*)** — the dative plural "bhyas" becomes "bhyam" by **भ्यसो भ्यम्** (पा. सू. ७-१-३०); **शेषे लोपः** (पा. सू. ७-२-९०), with "vibhaktau" carried from **अष्टन आ विभक्तौ** (पा. सू. ७-२-८४), drops the final "d" before an ending that conditions neither "ā" nor "y": "asma + bhyam"; **बहुवचने झल्येत्** (पा. सू. ७-३-१०३) would give "e," but by **अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिर्निष्ठितस्य** (पा. म. ७-१-३०) once one aṅga-rule ("śeṣe lopaḥ") has applied and the form is settled, another aṅga-rule does not apply; so too no lengthening by **सुपि च** (पा. सू. ७-३-१०२). In "asma," "sma" is acute by **फिषोऽन्त उदात्तः** (फि. सू. १), "bhyam" unaccented by **अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ** ("३-१-४") and svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ," the first "a" unaccented by śeṣanighāta. Or, dividing **भ्यसोऽभ्यम्** (पा. सू. ७-१-३०) as "abhyam": "asmad + abhyam," "śeṣe lopaḥ" drops the "ad" after "ma" (the locative "śeṣe" standing for the substituend): "asm + abhyam," with no "e" or lengthening; since the acute "a" of "asmad" is lost before the unaccented "a," **अनुदात्तस्य च यत्रोदात्तलोपः** (पा. सू. ६-१-१६१) makes that unaccented vowel acute…
- **अप्रतिष्कुतः (*apratiṣkutaḥ*)** — see p. 283 above (Rik 6 grammar concluded there).

### Page 282, 283

*(Page 283 header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 14." The grammar of "asmabhyam" and "apratiṣkutaḥ" is characterized above under p. 281.)* On the "abhyam" view (p. 283), "asma + abhyam" gives no "e" or lengthening; by **अतो गुणे** (पा. सू. ६-१-९७) the later form, and by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" "sma" is acute. **"Apratiṣkutaḥ"** — "kenacid apratiśabditaḥ" (one who does not utter "no" for any reason): "kuṅ śabde," **निष्ठा** (पा. सू. ३-२-१०२) "kta" in the past sense; "prati" before it; **पारस्करप्रभृतीनि च संज्ञायाम्** (पा. सू. ६-१-१५७) — the "pāraskarādi" class, an ākṛtigaṇa, takes "suṭ": "prati + skuta"; **सुषामादिषु च** (पा. सू. ८-३-९८), also an ākṛtigaṇa, "ṣ": "pratiṣkutaḥ"; in the nañ-compound **तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ…** (पा. सू. ६-२-२) keeps the accent of the indeclinable first member. ॥६॥

### Sūkta 7, Rik 7

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed (print anusvāra kept in "तुंजे"); Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तुं॒जेतुं॑जे॒ य उत्त॑रे॒ स्तोमा॒ इन्द्र॑स्य व॒ज्रिणः॑ ।
> न वि॑न्धे अस्य सुष्टु॒तिम् ॥७॥
>
> *tuñjé-tuñje yá úttare stómā índrasya vajríṇaḥ |*
> *ná vindhe asya suṣṭutím ||7||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तुञ्जेऽतुञ्जे । ये । उत्ऽतरे । स्तोमाः । इन्द्रस्य । वज्रिणः ॥
> न । विन्धे । अस्य । सुऽस्तुतिम् ॥७॥
>
> *tuñje-tuñje | ye | ut-tare | stomāḥ | indrasya | vajriṇaḥ ||*
> *na | vindhe | asya | su-stutim ||7||*

*(The pada line prints* तुञ्जेतुञ्जे *with an avagraha between the two halves, i.e. as a single repeated word.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> तुञ्जे तुञ्जे तस्मिन्स्तस्मिन्फलदातरि देवान्तरे ये सोमाः स्तोत्रविशेषा उत्तरे उत्कृष्टाः सन्ति तैः स्तोमैः सर्वैरपि वज्रिणो वज्रयुक्तस्यास्येन्द्रस्य सुष्टुतिं योग्यां शोभनस्तुतिं न विन्धे । न विन्दामि । इन्द्रस्यात्यन्तगुणबाहुल्येन देवान्तरेषूत्तमत्वेन प्रसिद्धान्यपि स्तोत्राणि न पर्याप्तानीत्यर्थः । एतामृचं यास्क एवं व्याचष्टे । तुञ्जस्तुञ्जतेर्दानकर्मणः । दाने दाने य उत्तरे स्तोमा इन्द्रस्य वज्रिणो नास्य तैर्विन्दामि समाप्तिं स्तुतेः । नि. ६-१८ । इति ॥
>
> *tuñje tuñje tasmin tasmin phala-dātari devāntare ye somāḥ stotra-viśeṣā uttare utkṛṣṭāḥ santi taiḥ stomaiḥ sarvair api vajriṇo vajra-yuktasyāsyendrasya suṣṭutiṃ yogyāṃ śobhana-stutiṃ na vindhe | na vindāmi | indrasyātyanta-guṇa-bāhulyena devāntareṣūttamatvena prasiddhāny api stotrāṇi na paryāptānīty arthaḥ | etām ṛcaṃ yāska evaṃ vyācaṣṭe | tuñjas tuñjater dāna-karmaṇaḥ | dāne dāne ya uttare stomā indrasya vajriṇo nāsya tair vindāmi samāptiṃ stuteḥ | ni. 6-18 | iti ||*

**Translation:** "*Tuñje tuñje*: in each and every other deity, a giver of fruits, whatever *stomas* ("somāḥ" as printed) — special hymns of praise — are superior and excellent; with all those stomas I do not find (*na vindhe*, I do not obtain) a proper, fine praise (*suṣṭuti*) of this thunderbolt-bearing Indra. The sense: because of the extreme abundance of Indra's qualities, even those hymns famed as the best addressed to other gods are not sufficient. Yāska explains this rik thus: '*tuñja* is from *tuñjati*, a verb of giving. In each giving, whatever superior stomas there are of Indra the vajrin — with them I do not find the completion of his praise' (Nirukta 6-18)."

*(The rest of the Sanskrit on pp. 284–285 is Sāyaṇa's grammar of* तुञ्जे*,* उत्तरे*,* स्तोमाः*,* विन्धे*,* अस्य*,* सुष्टुतिम्*, **dominated by a long scholastic argument** (an objection and replies) on whether the prefix* su *in* suṣṭutim *is an* upasarga *whose presence causes* s *to become* ṣ *and fixes the accent, or whether it qualifies the instrument of praise rather than the act of praising. Characterized, not transcribed (Convention 5); the conclusion that bears on the sense is given at the end of p. 285 and translated there.)*

### Page 284

*(Sāyaṇa's grammar of Rik 7, characterized; references as printed.)* "Tuñje tuñje" — "tuñjatir dānakarmā": **कर्तरि पचाद्यच्** (as printed; पा. ३-१-१३४) "ac," "c"-marked, end-acute; doubled by **नित्यवीप्सयोः** (पा. ८-१-४); the second is "āmreḍita" (पा. ८-१-२) and unaccented (पा. ८-१-३); "dātari dātari" — the Nirukta's "dāne dāne" explains the sense. "Uttare" — "tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ," **भावे ऋदोरप्** (as printed; पा. ३-३-५७); "ut" in the sense of excellence; "utkṛṣṭas taro yasya," a bahuvrīhi; "ut" first-syllable acute as a nipāta, kept by the bahuvrīhi rule. "Stomāḥ" — "artistusu…" (उ. १-१३९), "man"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Vindhe" — "vidḷ lābhe," "laṭ," ātmanepada as "svaritet"; first singular "iṭ" (पा. ३-४-७८); **तुदादिभ्यः शः** (पा. ३-१-७७); "num" by **शे मुचादीनाम्** (पा. ७-१-५९); "dh" for "d" by vyatyaya. "Asya" — of Indra, the subject at hand: "idam" → "aś" by **इदमोऽश्** (as printed; पा. २-४-३२), "ś"-marked, replacing the whole, unaccented. "Suṣṭutim" — "ṣṭuñ stutau," "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (पा. ६-१-६४); **स्त्रियां क्तिन्** (पा. ३-३-९४) "ktin" in the action sense; acute by "ūtiyūti…"; compounded with "su" by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (पा. २-२-१८); "ṣ" by **उपसर्गात्सुनोति…** (पा. ८-३-६५). The accent of the indeclinable first member would hold, but is set aside by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (पा. ६-२-१३९), and that in turn by **तादौ च निति कृत्यतौ** (पा. ६-२-५०), so the gati "su" would be acute; that too is set aside by **मन्क्तिन्व्याख्यान…** (पा. ६-२-१५१), giving the end-acute of the second member, as in "suhavāṃ suṣṭutī huve" (ऋग्वे. २-३२-४), "vṛṣṇe codasva suṣṭutim" (ऋग्वे. ८-६४-६ [?]), "yās te rāke sumatayaḥ" (ऋग्वे. २-३२-५). But "kārakād dattaśrutayor evāśiṣi" (पा. ६-२-१४८) shows that "kāraka" carries on, so "manktin…" applies only after a kāraka, as with "prakṛtiḥ, prahṛtiḥ"; to this the reply is that "stūyate 'nayeti stutiḥ" — "ktin" in the instrument sense — and "su" qualifies the instrument, so it is a kāraka … An objection follows: then "su," not joined to the action, is no upasarga by **उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे** (पा. १-४-५९), and no "ṣ" … *(the argument continues on p. 285).*
### Page 285 — Rik 7

*(Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 14." The upper part ends the "suṣṭutim" debate: "su" connects with the act through the instrument, so it is an upasarga by implication and the "ṣ" holds; or, since the accent is settled by taking the two affixes' sense, the "ṣ" may be taken as Vedic; or, as a bahuvrīhi "śobhanā stutir yasya," the end-acute comes by **नञ्सुभ्याम्** (पा. ६-२-१७२). The Sanskrit tail is translated here.)*

> अथवा सुष्ठु स्तुवन्तीति सुष्टुतय इति करणभूता ऋचः स्तुतिशब्देनोच्यन्ते । क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम् । पा. ३- -१७४ । इति क्तिच्प्रत्यये सति चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तता भविष्यति । न च करणीभूतानामृचां कर्तृप्रत्ययेन क्रिया कथमभिधानमिति वाच्यम् । काष्ठानि पचन्तीतिवत्तासामपि स्वव्यापारप्राधान्यविवक्षया करणत्वोपपत्तेरिति ॥
>
> *athavā suṣṭhu stuvantīti suṣṭutaya iti karaṇa-bhūtā ṛcaḥ stuti-śabdenocyante | ktic-ktau ca saṃjñāyām | pā. 3- -174 | iti ktic-pratyaye sati cittvād antodāttatā bhaviṣyati | na ca karaṇībhūtānām ṛcāṃ kartṛ-pratyayena kriyā katham abhidhānam iti vācyam | kāṣṭhāni pacantīti-vat tāsām api sva-vyāpāra-prādhānya-vivakṣayā karaṇatvopapatter iti ||*

**Translation:** "Or else, in the analysis '*those which praise well* — *suṣṭutayaḥ*', the ṛks that are the instruments [of praise] are called by the word *stuti*. By the sūtra '*ktic-ktau ca saṃjñāyām*' (printed "Pā. 3- -174," the middle number missing; 3-3-174), when the suffix *ktic* is added, final-udātta accent results, because of the marker *c*. Nor should it be objected: 'how can ṛks that are mere instruments be spoken of by an agent-suffix, as doing the act?' — for, as in '*kāṣṭhāni pacanti*' ('the logs cook'), where the log, though instrumental to cooking, is given independence in its own function (*svatantraḥ kartā*, Pā. 1-4-54), in the same way, taking the activity of the ṛks as principal, their instrumentality is perfectly consistent even though an agent-suffix is used."



**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**तुञ्जे तुञ्जे (tuñje tuñje)** — in (the other deities who bestow the fruit of) [each] | **उत्तरे (uttare)** — excellent | **ये स्तोमाः (ye stomāḥ)** — whatever hymns (there are) [those, with them] | **वज्रिणः (vajriṇaḥ)** — [of him] who holds the thunderbolt | **अस्य इन्द्रस्य (asya indrasya)** — of this Indra (in regard to) | **सुष्टुतिम् (suṣṭutim)** — the excellent hymn | **न विन्धे (na vindhe)** — it is not possible to obtain (to compose).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

However excellent the hymns we make to the other deities, who bestow many fruits on me, those hymns do not amount to a good praise of the thunderbolt-bearing Indra. That is: the hymns we make toward other deities may be very excellent; but in the case of Indra, since those hymns are incapable of describing the excess of Indra's qualities, they do not count as excellent. The sense is that to praise Indra, hymns far more excellent than those of other deities are required.

### Page 286

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Whatever praise-hymns are excellent for rewarding (other deity) I cannot find (even with these hymns) a hymn good enough to Lard [sic] Indra, the weilder [sic] of thunderbolt.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Tuñje-tuñje"** — Yāska in the Nirukta explains this rik as follows:

> तुञ्जस्तुञ्जतेर्दानकर्मणः । दाने दाने य उत्तरे स्तोमा इन्द्रस्य वज्रिणो नास्य तैर्विन्दामि समाप्तिं स्तुतेः ।
> *tuñjas tuñjater dāna-karmaṇaḥ | dāne dāne ya uttare stomā indrasya vajriṇo nāsya tair vindāmi samāptiṃ stuteḥ |*
> "*Tuñja* is from *tuñjati*, a verb of giving. In each giving, whatever superior stomas there are of Indra the vajrin — with them I do not find the end of the praise of him."

That is, the word *tuñja* means giving, bestowing. The word *tuñje-tuñje* in this rik means "in regard to the deity who gives fruits." Since the word *tuñje* is printed twice, it means "in regard to every deity" — that is, all the deities. However excellent the hymns used for other deities (other than Indra), they are not enough for Indra; more are needed. As one says, "enough of this praise of Indra; it has come to its end," — however much one praises, the qualities of Indra remain more; there is no end to them.

**"Uttare"** — this word has two separate parts, *ut* + *tare*. The Bhāṣyakāra explains it thus: *uttare — tvaplavana-taraṇayoḥ* (the root *tṝ*, "to cross/swim") — *bhāve ṛdor ap* (Pā. 3-3-57) — *ut* means "excellent"; *utkṛṣṭas taro yasya* — a bahuvrīhi: "one whose crossing is excellent." The word *tara* is formed from the root *tṝ*. *Ut* means "excellent." Hence the word *ut-tara* = *uttara* means "more excellent."

**"Suṣṭutim" or "Sustutim"** — *stūyate 'nayeti stutiḥ* — "that by which one praises is a *stuti*." By the word *su* the *instrument* is qualified, not the meaning of the root. **Or:** *suṣṭhu stuvantīti suṣṭutayaḥ* — "the ṛks that are the instruments are called by the word *stuti*." That is, *stuti* is the name for praising; *suṣṭuti* means "praising well," or, because the ṛks praise well, such mantras or ṛks are customarily called *stuti*.

### Page 287 — Rik 7: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

*(Pp. 287–290. Page header p. 287: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 14." Characterized; numbers as printed.)*

- **तुञ्जेतुञ्जे (*tuñje-tuñje*)** — "tuñjas tuñjater dānakarmaṇaḥ" (निरु. "६-१७-१८" as printed): Yāska takes "tuñj" as a verb of giving. "Tuñj," of the pacādi class, takes "ac" in the agent sense by **नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः** (पा. सू. ३-१-१३४); "c"-marked, end-acute by **चितः** (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३); locative singular "tuñje"; doubled by **नित्यवीप्सयोः** (पा. सू. ८-१-४); the second is "āmreḍita" by **तस्य परमाम्रेडितम्** (पा. सू. ८-१-२) and unaccented by **अनुदात्तं च** (पा. सू. ८-१-३). "Dātari dātari" — "in each giver"; the Nirukta's "dāne dāne" explains the root sense, setting aside the affix sense.
- **उत्तरे (*uttare*)** — "tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ": **ऋदोरप्** (पा. सू. ३-३-५७) "ap" in the action sense; "ut" means "excellent"; "utkṛṣṭas taro yasya," a bahuvrīhi; "ut," a nipāta, first-syllable acute by **निपाता आद्युदात्ताः** (फि. सू. ८०), kept by **बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम्** (पा. सू. ६-२-१).
- **स्तोमाः (*stomāḥ*)** — **अर्तिस्तुसु…** (उ. सू. १-१४२ [?], the figures unclear) "man"; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute.
- **विन्धे (*vindhe*)** — "vidḷ lābhe," "laṭ"; the root being "svaritet," the ātmanepada by **स्वरितञितः कर्त्रभिप्राये क्रियाफले** (पा. सू. १-३-७२); first singular "iṭ" by **तिप्तस्झि…** (पा. सू. ३-४-७८): "vid + i"; **तुदादिभ्यः शः** (पा. सू. ३-१-७७); **शे मुचादीनाम्** (पा. सू. ७-१-५९) "num"; "dh" for "d" by vyatyaya; **आद्गुणः** (पा. सू. ६-१-८७): "vindhe."
- **अस्य (*asya*)** — refers back to Indra, the subject in hand, so anvādeśa: **इदमोऽन्वादेशेऽशनुदात्तस्तृतीयादौ** "aś" for "idam"; "ś"-marked, it replaces the whole by **अनेकाल्शित्सर्वस्य** (पा. सू. १-१-५५).
### Pages 288–290 — Rik 7: the *suṣṭutim* debate (grammar)

*(Characterized, not transcribed. The argument, in outline, as the Kannada commentary gives it:)*

**Page 288.** **सुष्टुतिम् (*suṣṭutim*)** — "ṣṭuñ stutau": **धात्वादेः षः सः** (पा. सू. ६-१-६४) "s" for "ṣ," and the "ṭ" it caused reverts: "stu"; **स्त्रियां क्तिन्** (पा. सू. ३-३-९४) "ktin" in the action sense; with the acute upasarga "su," the prādi compound by **कुगतिप्रादयः** (पा. सू. २-२-१८); "ṣ" by **उपसर्गात्सुनोतिसुवतिस्यतिस्तौतिस्तोभतिस्थासेनयसेधसिचसञ्जस्वञ्जाम्** (पा. सू. ८-३-६५) and "ṭ" by **ष्टुना ष्टुः** (पा. सू. ८-४-४१): accusative "suṣṭutim." The accent of the indeclinable first member (**तत्पुरुषे तुल्यार्थ…**, पा. सू. ६-२-२) is set aside by **गतिकारकोपपदात्कृत्** (पा. सू. ६-२-१३९), which in turn gives way to **तादौ च निति कृत्यतौ** (पा. सू. ६-२-५०) — before a kṛt beginning with "t" and "n"-marked, other than "tu," the gati keeps its accent, so "su" would be acute; but **मन्क्तिन्व्याख्यानशयनासनस्थानयाजकादिक्रीताः** (पा. सू. ६-२-१५१) makes these second members end-acute, setting "tādau ca" aside: so "suṣṭutim" is end-acute, as also "suhavāṃ suṣṭutī huve" (ऋ. सं. २-३२-४), "vṛṣṇe codasva suṣṭutim" (ऋ. सं. ८-६४-६ [?], the middle figures unclear), "yās te rāke sumatayaḥ" (ऋ. सं. २-३२-५), say those who know. The Kāśikā takes "kārakāt" as carried into "manktin…" from **कारकाद्दत्तश्रुतयोरेवाशिषि** (पा. सू. ६-२-१४८), so that only after a kāraka are "man"-ending etc. second members end-acute ("pāṇinikṛtiḥ" the example, "prakṛtiḥ, prahṛtiḥ" the counter-examples, "kārakād ity eva" — Kā. ६-२-१५१); on that view "su," a gati, is no kāraka, and "manktin" would not give the end-acute. Whether that can be met is considered next: "stūyate anayā iti stutiḥ" (praise as the instrument, the ṛk…) *(continues on p. 289)*.

**Page 289.** The discussion pursues whether *su* here is an upasarga (and so induces *ṣatva*) at all. *(Page header: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 14.")* The argument runs: by **उपसर्गाः क्रियायोगे** (पा. सू. १-४-५९) an upasarga must be connected to a *verbal action*; *su* here qualifies the *karaṇa* (instrument — the *stuti*), and therefore, in this view, is not connected to the verbal meaning; the *ṣatva* would then be unjustified. The reply is that *su* qualifies the instrument *by way of* the verbal meaning of *stu*, and so is an upasarga after all. The Bhāṣyakāra's analysis is shown consistent with the Vṛttikāra's example of *su* in *su-ṣṭutim*. The page ends in a sub-argument about whether the double qualification (of the root and of the suffix-sense) operates simultaneously, successively, or by repetition (*āvṛtti*) — "whether *su* qualifies both, together or in sequence."

**Page 290.** If "su" is taken with the root sense and the affix sense in sequence, the operation stops and resumes ("viramya vyāpāra"), which nobody accepts for words; so "su" cannot be construed with both by the power of the word alone. If with one verbally and the other by implication: taken with the root sense by implication, the "ṣ" is not obtained; with the affix sense by implication, the "manktin" accent is not obtained. And even a merely implied kāraka relation makes "suṣṭuti" an example of "manktin," so "prakṛtiḥ, prahṛtiḥ" cannot be counter-examples — who could stop an implied relation of "pra" with the instrument contained in the root sense? So the accent is not obtained from an implied kāraka relation. Hence on this view "su" is construed only with the affix sense, the "manktin" accent holds, and the "ṣ" is Vedic. Or, taken as a bahuvrīhi "śobhanā matir yasyāḥ," the end-acute comes by **नञ्सुभ्याम्** (पा. सू. ६-२-१७२). Or, "suṣṭhu stuvantīti suṣṭutayaḥ": the ṛks, the instruments of praise, are called "stuti"; **क्तिच्क्तौ च संज्ञायाम्** (पा. सू. "१३-३-१७४" as printed, i.e. 3-3-174) "ktic" in the agent sense; "c"-marked, end-acute by **चितः** (पा. सू. ६-१-१६३). To the objection how an agent affix can denote ṛks that are instruments: as in "kāṣṭhāni pacanti" (the logs cook), where the logs, an instrument of cooking, are given independence in their own activity and so are agents by **स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता** (पा. सू. १-४-५४), so too the ṛks, their activity taken as principal, are rightly instruments though an agent affix is used. ॥७॥

### Sūkta 7, Rik 8

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> वृषा॑ यू॒थेव॒ वंस॑गः कृष्टीरि॑य॒र्त्योज॑सा ।
> ईशा॑नो॒ अप्र॑तिष्कुतः ॥८॥
>
> *vṛ́ṣā yūthéva váṃsagaḥ kṛṣṭī́r iyarty ójasā |*
> *ī́śāno ápratiṣkutaḥ ||8||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> वृषा । यूथाऽइव । वंसगः । कृष्टीः । इयर्ति । ओजसा ॥
> ईशानः । अप्रतिऽस्कुतः ॥८॥
>
> *vṛṣā | yūthā-iva | vaṃsagaḥ | kṛṣṭīḥ | iyarti | ojasā ||*
> *īśānaḥ | aprati-skutaḥ ||8||*

*(Pada printed on p. 291.)*

### Page 291 — Rik 8: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> वृषा कामानां वर्षितेन्द्र ओजसा स्वकीयबलेनानुग्रहीतुं कृष्टीर्मनुष्यानियर्ति । प्राप्नोति । कीदृश इन्द्रः । ईशानः समर्थो ऽप्रतिष्कुतः प्रतिशब्दरहितः । याच्यमानं न परिहरतीत्यर्थः । इन्द्रस्य दृष्टान्तः । वंसगो वननीयगतिर्वृषभो यूथेव गोयूथानि यथा प्राप्नोति तद्वत् ॥
>
> *vṛṣā kāmānāṃ varṣitendra ojasā svakīya-balenānugrahītuṃ kṛṣṭīr manuṣyān iyarti | prāpnoti | kīdṛśa indraḥ | īśānaḥ samartho 'pratiṣkutaḥ prati-śabda-rahitaḥ | yācyamānaṃ na pariharatīty arthaḥ | indrasya dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vaṃsago vananīya-gatir vṛṣabho yūtheva go-yūthāni yathā prāpnoti tadvat ||*

**Translation:** "Indra, the showerer (*varṣitā*) of desires, with his own strength (*ojasā*), in order to favour them, approaches (*iyarti* — reaches) the *kṛṣṭīḥ*, the people. What kind of Indra? *Īśānaḥ* — the capable, the lord; *apratiṣkutaḥ* — without a counter-word; that is, he who does not turn away from what is asked of him. An illustration for Indra: the *vaṃsaga* — the bull of lovely gait — as [a bull] goes to its herds, the herds of cows, so [Indra goes to people]."

**Grammar of the Bhāṣya (characterized, references as printed; page header "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 14"):** "Vṛṣā" — **कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः** (उ. १-१५६) "kanin" after "vṛṣ"; "k"-marked, no guṇa; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Yūthā iva" — "yuvanti miśrībhavantīti yūthāni," "yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ": **तिथपृष्ठगूथयूथप्रोथाः** (उ. २-१२) "thak," end-acute by nipātana; the long vowel by nipātana; the "ā" acute by the affix accent; **शेश्छन्दसि बहुलम्** (पा. ६-१-७०) "luk"; "iva" — no loss of case-ending; with "iva," compounding and the first member's accent by the vārttika (पा. २-१-४-२). "Vaṃsagaḥ" — the intended accent by the "pṛṣodarādi" class (पा. ६-३-१०९). "Kṛṣṭīḥ" — "karṣantīti kṛṣṭayaḥ," "ktic" by "ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām"; "c"-marked, end-acute. "Iyarti" — "ṛ sṛ gatau," "tip," "śap" → "ślu," doubling (पा. ६-१-१०); **अभ्यासस्यासवर्णे** … "i" for the reduplicate "a" by **अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च** (पा. ७-४-७७); "iy" by "abhyāsasyāsavarṇe" (पा. ६-४-७८); guṇa of the aṅga, with "r." "Ojasā" — **उब्जेर्बलोपश्च** (उ. ४-१९१) "asun," with loss of "b"; guṇa of the light penultimate (पा. ७-३-८६); "n"-marked, first-syllable acute. "Īśānaḥ" — "īśa aiśvarye," "laṭ," "śānac"; "śap" elided by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ"; the "c"-accent set aside, the lasārvadhātuka is unaccented after an anudāttet root, so the root accent remains. "Apratiṣkutaḥ" — "apratiśabditaḥ," "ku śabde," "kta" in the passive; "suṭ" (pāraskarādi), "ṣ" (suṣāmādi); nañ-compound, the indeclinable first member's accent.

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**वृषा (vṛṣā)** — the bestower of what is desired | **ईशानः (īśānaḥ)** — the capable one | **अप्रतिष्कुतः (apratiṣkutaḥ)** — (Indra) who has no opponent | **वंसगः (vaṃsagaḥ)** — a bull (the leader of a herd of cows) | **यूथा इव (yūthā iva)** — as it goes toward its herd (of cows) | **कृष्टीः (kṛṣṭīḥ)** — to human beings | **ओजसा (ojasā)** — with his strength and might | **इयर्ति (iyarti)** — reaches (that is, comes near to men).

### Page 292

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Indra is the one who fulfils the desires of men; he is all-capable; he has no rival — he is *apratiṣkuta*. Such an Indra goes near men as a bull, the leader of a herd of cattle, goes toward its herd.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra, granter of all desires, the lord unopposed and the mighty approaches men with his strength like a bull walking towards his herds.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**The main sense:** Indra is the lord, all-capable, and none can oppose his word. Such an Indra, by the might he has, comes near men in order to grant people's desired ends. As a bull that is attached to the welfare of its herd goes near the herd to protect it, so Indra, being attached to our welfare, will come near us. That is the sense.

**"Vṛṣā"** — *kāmānāṃ varṣitā*: "the one who showers desires." *Varṣitā* means "one who causes rain to fall"; that is, the one who rains down the desires of the people — the granter of what is wished.

**"Yūtheva"** — here the word-division is *yūthā iva*. In the Ṛgveda the word *iva* is not counted as a separate word but is customarily read together with the word it belongs to. By this, as the Bhāṣyakāra says (*vibhakter lopaḥ*), the case-ending of the principal word suffers no obstruction of any kind; that is, if the two words *yūthā* and *iva* are present, the meaning that belongs to them is the same for the single combined word. Examples: **अग्नेरिव** (*agner iva*, = *agneḥ iva*); **अजेव** (*ajeva*, = *ajā iva*); **अञ्जसेव** (*añjaseva*, = *añjasā iva*); **अप्रशस्ता इव** (*apraśastā iva*, = *apraśastāḥ iva*); **अभ्रमिव** (*abhram iva*, = *abhraṃ iva*); **अमृतादिव** (*amṛtād iva*, = *amṛtāt iva*), and so on. The word *yūthā* is derived from the root *yu* "to join, to mix"; *yuvanti miśrībhavantīti yūthāni* — "those that join, that mix together, are *yūthas*." In the Veda the final syllable *ni* is dropped, so *yūthā* appears.

**"Vaṃsagaḥ"** — **वननीयगतिर्वृषभः** (*vananīya-gatir vṛṣabhaḥ*) — "the bull of lovely gait," the leader of the herd, the chief; *leader, protector.*

**"Kṛṣṭīḥ"** — **कर्षन्तीति कृष्टयः** (*karṣantīti kṛṣṭayaḥ*) — "those who plough" — those who till, who cultivate (by ploughing the earth). This word is accusative plural.

**"Īśānaḥ"** — a form of the root *īśa aiśvarye* ("to be master"); the lord; the all-capable.

### Page 293

**"Apratiṣkutaḥ"** — Sāyaṇa's gloss: **अप्रतिशब्दितः । कु शब्दे । कर्मणि क्तः ॥** (*apratiśabditaḥ | ku śabde | karmaṇi ktaḥ ||*) — "one to whom no counter-word is spoken; [root] *ku* in the sense of sound; *kta* in the passive." That is, the root *ku* means "to make a sound." The word *apratiṣkutaḥ*, formed from this root, means *apratiśabditaḥ* — one whose word has no opposition, no equal, who is unobstructed.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥**

*(Pp. 293–294. Page header p. 293: "A. 1, A. 1, Va. 14." Characterized; numbers as printed.)*

- **वृषा (*vṛṣā*)** — from root *vṛṣu secane* ("to sprinkle, shower") with "kanin" by **कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः** (उ. सू. १-१५४ [?], the last digit unclear; the bhāṣya gave "१-१५६"), the roots glossed one by one; "kit," so no guṇa of the light penultimate; "n"-marked, first-syllable acute.
- **यूथा इव (*yūthā iva*)** — root *yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ* ("to join, to separate") with *thak*, formed irregularly (*nipātita*) by **तिथपृष्ठगूथयूथप्रोथाः** (उ. सू. २-१२); the long vowel arises from that irregularity; *ā* is udātta by the suffix; "śi" for "jas" by **जश्शसोः शिः** (पा. सू. ७-१-२०), elided by **शेश्छन्दसि बहुलम्** (पा. सू. ६-१-७०) — since "lopaḥ" carries on from **लोपो व्योर्वलि** (पा. सू. ६-१-६६) and "luk" does not, it is wrong to explain it as "luk"; the compound with *iva* (*ivena samāsaḥ vibhakty-alopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca vaktavyam*, Pā. 2-1-4 *vārttika* 2) keeps the first member's accent.
- **वंसगः (*vaṃsagaḥ*)** — a *pṛṣodarādi* form (Pā. 6-3-109): the desired shape and accent are established.
- **कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*)** — *karṣanti iti kṛṣṭayaḥ*; *ktic* suffix by "ktic-ktau ca saṃjñāyām" (Pā. 3-3-174); final-udātta by *cit* (Pā. 6-1-163).
- **इयर्ति (*iyarti*)** — root *ṛ* ("to go") + *laṭ*, third singular *tip*; *śap* then *śluḥ* by "juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ" (Pā. 2-4-75); doubling by **श्लौ** (पा. सू. ६-१-१०); **उरत्** (पा. सू. ७-४-६६) "a" for the reduplicate "ṛ," with "r" by **उरण् रपरः** (पा. सू. १-१-५१); in "ar-ṛ-ti" **हलादिः शेषः** (पा. सू. ७-४-६०) keeps only the first consonant (by the class view of "abhyāsa"), so "r" is lost; or, in the Aṣṭādhyāyī as recited in saṃhitā, "hrasvo 'halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" is divided as **ह्रस्वः** (पा. सू. ७-४-५९), "ahal," "ādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (७-४-६०)… (p. 294:) "ahal" removes the "r"; **अर्तिपिपर्त्योश्च** (पा. सू. ७-४-७७) "i" for the reduplicate of "ṛ" and "pṝ" before "ślu"; "iyaṅ" by **अभ्यासस्यासवर्णे** (पा. सू. ६-४-७८); guṇa with "r" (पा. सू. ७-३-८४): "iyarti." The Bālamanoramā holds that "arti-pipartyoś ca" should set aside "urat" from the start; but by the paribhāṣā **अभ्यासविकारेषु बाध्यबाधकभावो नास्ति** (परिभा. ६४), and since Kaiyaṭa, on 7-4-77, gives the order "tip, śap, ślu, doubling, urat, it, iyaṅ, guṇa with r," the process first given, following the Veda-bhāṣya, is right.
- **ओजसा (*ojasā*)** — root *ubja ārjave* ("to be straight/strong"); *asun* with loss of *b* by **उब्जेर्बले बलोपश्च** (उ. सू. ४-६९१ [?], as printed; the bhāṣya gave "४-१९१") in the sense of strength; guṇa of the light penultimate by **पुगन्तलघूपधस्य च** (पा. सू. ७-३-८६); "n"-marked, first-syllable acute.
- **ईशानः (*īśānaḥ*)** — root *īśa aiśvarye* + *śānac* in place of *laṭ* by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau"; *śap* dropped by "ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ"; the *cit* suffix would give final-udātta (Pā. 6-1-163), but the root is *anudātteṭ* so the following *sārvadhātuka* ending *śānac* is unaccented, and the *dhātu*-accent remains (Pā. 6-1-186).
- **अप्रतिष्कुतः (*apratiṣkutaḥ*)** — "one who has nothing answering"; root *ku śabde* + *kta* in the passive sense with *prati* before; *suṭ* by "pāraskarādīni ca saṃjñāyām" (पा. सू. ६-१-१५७) — the *pāraskarādi* group is an *ākṛti-gaṇa* (a class identified by its character), the word is to be counted in it; *s→ṣ* by "suṣāmādiṣu ca" (Pā. 8-3-98), also an *ākṛti-gaṇa*; *prati-ṣkuta*, then the *naṅ* compound *a-pratiṣkuta*; accent of the first member by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2).

### Page 294

*(Completes the grammar above (characterized there), ending with the accent of* apratiṣkutaḥ *by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (पा. सू. ६-२-२) and the number* ॥८॥*.)*

**॥८॥**
