### Page 361 — Sūkta 9, Rik 6

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒स्मान्त्सु तत्र॑ चोद॒येन्द्र॑ रा॒ये रभ॑स्वतः ।
> तुवि॑द्युम्न॒ यश॑स्वतः ॥६॥
>
> *asmā́nt su tátra codayéndra rāyé rábhasvataḥ |*
> *túvidyumna yáśasvataḥ ||6||*

*(In the Saṃhitā the words* asmān su *are joined as* asmān tsu*: a* t *is inserted between the* n *and the* s *by the Vedic sandhi rule, as the Special Topics below explain.)*

### Page 362 — Rik 6: Pada text, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अस्मान् । सु । तत्र । चोदय । इन्द्र । राये । रभस्वतः ॥
> तुविऽद्युम्न । यशस्वतः ॥६॥
>
> *asmān | su | tatra | codaya | indra | rāye | rabhasvataḥ ||*
> *tuvi-dyumna | yaśasvataḥ ||6||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे तुविद्युम्न प्रभूतधनेन्द्र राये धनसिद्ध्यर्थमस्माननुष्ठातॄन् तत्र कर्मणि सु चोदय । सुष्ठु प्रेरय । कीदृशानस्मान् । रभस्वत उद्योगवतो यशस्वतः कीर्तिमतः ॥ तत्र । तच्छब्दात्सप्तम्यास्त्रल् । पा. ५-३-१० । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । इन्द्र । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । राये । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । रभस्वतः । रभ राभस्ये । राभस्यं कार्योपक्रमः । सर्वधातुभ्यो ऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । मतुपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । स्वादिष्वसर्वनामस्थाने । पा. १-४-१७ । इति न पदत्वं तसौ मत्वर्थे । पा. १-४-१९ । इति भसंज्ञया बाधितत्वात् । आ कडारादेका संज्ञा । पा. १-४-१ । इति नियमात् तुविद्युम्न । तुवि बहु द्युम्नं धनं यस्य । षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । यशस्वतः । यशो ऽस्यास्तीति मतुप् । अस्मायामेधास्रजो विनिः । पा. ५-२-१२१ । इति विनिना न बाध्यते मतुपः सर्वत्र समुच्चयात् । यशश्शब्दो नब्विषयस्यानिसन्तस्येत्याद्युदात्तः । मतुपः पित्त्वात्तस्य शिष्यते ॥
>
> *he tuvidyumna prabhūtadhanendra rāye dhanasiddhyarthamasmānanuṣṭhātṝn tatra karmaṇi su codaya | suṣṭhu preraya | kīdṛśānasmān | rabhasvata udyogavato yaśasvataḥ kīrtimataḥ || tatra | tacchabdātsaptamyāstral | pā. 5-3-10 | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | indra | āmantritādyudāttatvam | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | rāye | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | rabhasvataḥ | rabha rābhasye | rābhasyaṃ kāryopakramaḥ | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | matupaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | svādiṣvasarvanāmasthāne | pā. 1-4-17 | iti na padatvaṃ tasau matvarthe | pā. 1-4-19 | iti bhasaṃjñayā bādhitatvāt | ā kaḍārādekā saṃjñā | pā. 1-4-1 | iti niyamāt tuvidyumna | tuvi bahu dyumnaṃ dhanaṃ yasya | ṣāṣṭhikamāmantritādyudāttatvam | yaśasvataḥ | yaśo 'syāstīti matup | asmāyāmedhāsrajo viniḥ | pā. 5-2-121 | iti vininā na bādhyate matupaḥ sarvatra samuccayāt | yaśaśśabdo nabviṣayasyānisantasyetyādyudāttaḥ | matupaḥ pittvāttasya śiṣyate ||*

**Translation:** "O *tuvidyumna* — Indra of abundant wealth! For *rāye*, the achievement of wealth, *su codaya* — urge well — us, who perform the rites, in that rite. What kind of us? *Rabhasvataḥ* — enterprising, industrious; *yaśasvataḥ* — renowned. *(Grammar:* tatra — *formed with* tral *after the word* tad *in the seventh case (Pā. 5-3-10), the syllable before the suffix being udātta since* tral *is* l-*marked;* indra *— the vocative, initially udātta, but as the first word of a pāda not lowered;* rāye *— the case-ending udātta by "ūḍidam…";* rabhasvataḥ — *root* rabha rābhasye*, 'the beginning of an act'; the suffix* asun*, initial-udātta since* nit*;* matup *is* pit *and so unaccented; by Pā. 1-4-17 and 1-4-19 the word is not a* pada *before* matup*, but has the technical* bha *status, which blocks the* pada *status;* tuvidyumna *— 'he whose wealth (*dyumna*) is much (*tuvi*)', a bahuvrīhi, the vocative initially udātta;* yaśasvataḥ *— 'who has fame' with* matup*, not barred by* vini *(Pā. 5-2-121) since the two are combined everywhere; the word* yaśas *initial-udātta as a neuter not ending in* -isan*.)*"

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**तुविद्युम्न (tuvidyumna)** — O Indra, who are endowed with abundant wealth | **(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **रभस्वतः (rabhasvataḥ)** — who are enterprising (engaged in sacrificial and other works) | **यशस्वतः (yaśasvataḥ)** — who are possessed of fame | **अस्मान् (asmān)** — us | **राये (rāye)** — for obtaining wealth | **तत्र (tatra)** — in that rite | **सु चोदय (su codaya)** — urge well.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! You are endowed with abundant wealth — that is, you possess great riches. Therefore urge us, who are always engaged in sacrificial and other works and are renowned, to engage ardently in sacrificial and other rites for obtaining wealth.

### Page 363 — Rik 6: English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra, you are very rich ; encourage us in this rite for the acquirement of wealth, for we are deligent [sic] and renowned.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Asmān + su = asmān tsu"** — when *s* follows the *n* of a word-ending (here, an accusative-plural *n*), in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha the two are combined by sandhi and, in pronouncing, a *t* is inserted between the *n* and the *s*, giving *nts*; this is customary. In this connection:

> स गा अविन्दत्सो अविन्ददश्वान्त्स ओषधीः सो अपः सवनानि ॥ (ऋ. सं. १-१०३-५)
> *sa gā avindat so avindad aśvānt sa oṣadhīḥ so apaḥ savanāni || (Ṛg. Saṃ. 1-103-5)*
> *("He found the cows, he found the horses, he the herbs, he the waters, the pressings." — mine and tentative; the source gives only the citation.)*

> कविर्गीर्भिः काव्येना कविः सन्त्सोमः पवित्रमत्येति रेभन् ॥ (ऋ. सं. ९-९६-१७)
> *kavir gīrbhiḥ kāvyenā kaviḥ san tsomaḥ pavitram aty eti rebhan || (Ṛg. Saṃ. 9-96-17)*
> *("The seer [Soma], a seer with his songs and poetic power, being [pressed], passes through the filter, murmuring." — mine and tentative.)*

Many more examples could be given.

**"Rabhasvataḥ"** — **रभ राभस्ये । राभस्यं कार्योपक्रमः** (*rabha rābhasye | rābhasyaṃ kāryopakramaḥ*) — "[root] *rabha* in the sense of *rābhasya* — the beginning of a work." *Rābhasya* is derived from the root *rabh*; it means starting an undertaking; being industrious, enterprising. *Rabhasvataḥ* is the accusative plural of *rabhasvān*.

**"Tuvidyumna"** — "of abundant wealth": *tuvi* is much; *dyumna* is wealth. So, "he who has much wealth" — a bahuvrīhi. "Of much wealth."

**"Yaśasvataḥ"** — *yaśo 'syāstīti yaśasvān*, "those who have fame"; renowned. *Rabhasvataḥ* and *yaśasvataḥ* both qualify the word *asmān* ("us").

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 363–365, noted briefly)*

**तत्र (*tatra*)** — "in that"; the *tral* suffix after the seventh-case pronouns *tad*, *kim*, *sarva* etc. (Pā. 5-3-10, "saptamyās tral"); *tral* is *taddhita*, so the word is a *prātipadika*; the *sup* ending is dropped by *supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ* (Pā. 2-4-71); *d* → *a* by *tyadādīnām aḥ* (Pā. 6-2-102 [as printed]); *a* + *a* → pararūpa by *ato guṇe* (Pā. 6-1-97); *tral* is *l*-marked, so by *liti* (Pā. 6-1-193) the syllable before the suffix is udātta. **इन्द्र (*indra*)** — the second pāda's first syllable; since this is the beginning of the pāda, there is no lowering by *apādādau*; as a vocative it is initial-udātta by *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. 6-1-198). **राये (*rāye*)** — *rai* + the dative ending *e*; after the *ai*-ending word *rai*, the dative ending is udātta (*ūḍidam-pada-ādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ*, Pā. 6-1-171). **रभस्वतः (*rabhasvataḥ*)** — root *rabha rābhasye*; *asun* by *sarvadhātubhyo 'sun* (Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]) gives *rabhas*, initial-udātta as *nit*; *matup* after it by *tad asyāsty asminn iti matup* (Pā. 5-2-94), its *m* → *v* by *mādupadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-9); the question of whether *rabhas* is a *pada* before *matup* (which would block *ruṭ* etc.) (by *svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne*, Pā. 1-4-17) or has *bha* status (by *tasau matvarthe*, Pā. 1-4-19) is argued: *pada* status and *bha* status are both prescribed, and the source concludes by the maxim "ā kaḍārād ekā saṃjñā" (Pā. 1-4-1) that among the technical names prescribed from there up to *kaḍārāḥ karmadhāraye* (Pā. 2-2-38) only one applies, the later (*para*) one, *bha*; so *pada*-status is inapplicable and the rules (such as *ruṭv*-rules) that depend on it do not operate. **तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*)** — *tuvi* (much) + *dyumna* (wealth) as a bahuvrīhi; a vocative, initial-udātta by the vocative rule of the sixth adhyāya (no number printed). **यशस्वतः (*yaśasvataḥ*)** — "yaśo 'syāstīti yaśasvān": *matup*, with the *m* → *v* as in *rabhasvataḥ*; the long discussion (pp. 364–365) concerns whether the *vini* suffix of the sūtra "asmāyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121) blocks *matup* here — answered that, by the carried-over word "anyatarasyām" ("optionally"), *vini* is only optional — the "nityam" of *ekago-pūrvāṭ ṭhañ nityam* (Pā. 5-2-118) breaks the carrying-over, but it resumes in *tasau matvarthe* (Pā. 1-4-19), where the Mahābhāṣya gives the examples *yaśasvī / yaśasvān*; and by the Vedabhāṣya's general statement that *matup* has the sense of inclusion everywhere (*samuccaya*), and by Kaiyaṭa on the Mahābhāṣya on "keśād vo 'nyatarasyām" (Pā. 5-2-109; printed 5-3-109 on p. 365 [as printed]); *yaśas* is initial-udātta as a neuter noun not ending in *-isan* (Phiṭ-sūtra 26); *matup* is *pit*, hence unaccented; so the initial accent of *yaśas* stands. *(Sūtra numbers read from small print; pointers only.)*

**॥६॥**

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

> सं गोम॑दिन्द्र॒ वाज॑वद॒स्मे पृ॒थु श्रवो॑ बृ॒हत् ।
> वि॒श्वायु॑र्धेह्य॑क्षितम् ॥७॥

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> सम् । गोऽमत् । इन्द्र । वाजऽवत् । अस्मे इति । पृथु । श्रवः । बृहत् ॥

### Page 366 — Rik 7: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र श्रवो धनमस्मे सं धेहि । अस्मभ्यं सम्यक् प्रयच्छ । कीदृशं श्रवः । गोमत् बह्वीभिर्गोभिरुपेतं वाजवत् प्रभूतेनान्नेनोपेतं पृथु परिमाणेनाधिकं बृहत् गुणैरधिकं विश्वायुः कृत्स्नायुष्यकारणं अक्षितं विनाशरहितम् । गोमत् । वाजवत् । उभयत्र मतुपो ऽनुदात्तत्वात्प्रातिपदिकस्वर एव । वाजशब्दो वृषादिराद्युदात्तः । अस्मे । अस्मच्छब्दाच्चतुर्थीबहुवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना शे आदेशः । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । शेषे लोपः । टिलोप इति पक्षे । पा. ७-२-९० । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अन्त्यलोपपक्षे ऽतो गुण इति पररूपे एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तत्वम् । पृथु । प्रथ प्रख्याने । प्रथिम्रदिभ्रस्जां संप्रसारणं सलोपश्च । उ. १-२९ । इति कुप्रत्ययः । रेफस्य संप्रसारणमृकारः । परपूर्वत्वम् । कोः कित्त्वान्न लघूपधगुणः । श्रूयत इति श्रवो धनम् । असुन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । बृहत् । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । विश्वायुः । विश्वमायुर्यस्मिन्धने । विश्वशब्दः क्वन्प्रत्ययान्तः । तस्य बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्याद्युदात्तः । अक्षितम् । क्षि क्षये इत्यस्मादन्तर्णीतण्यर्थात्कर्मणि निष्ठा । तेन स्यदर्थत्वान्निष्ठायामण्यदर्थे [? as printed] । पा. ६-४-६० । इति न दीर्घत्वम् । अत एव क्षियो दीर्घात् । पा. ८-२-४६ । इति न निष्ठानत्वम् । नञ्समासे ऽव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥
>
> *he indra śravo dhanamasme saṃ dhehi | asmabhyaṃ samyak prayaccha | kīdṛśaṃ śravaḥ | gomat bahvībhirgobhirupetaṃ vājavat prabhūtenānnenopetaṃ pṛthu parimāṇenādhikaṃ bṛhat guṇairadhikaṃ viśvāyuḥ kṛtsnāyuṣyakāraṇaṃ akṣitaṃ vināśarahitam | gomat | vājavat | ubhayatra matupo 'nudāttatvātprātipadikasvara eva | vājaśabdo vṛṣādirādyudāttaḥ | asme | asmacchabdāccaturthībahuvacanasya supāṃ sulugityādinā śe ādeśaḥ | śittvātsarvādeśaḥ | prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttatvam | śeṣe lopaḥ | ṭilopa iti pakṣe | pā. 7-2-90 | udāttanivṛttisvareṇa vibhakterudāttatvam | antyalopapakṣe 'to guṇa iti pararūpe ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttatvam | pṛthu | pratha prakhyāne | prathimradibhrasjāṃ saṃprasāraṇaṃ salopaśca | u. 1-29 | iti kupratyayaḥ | rephasya saṃprasāraṇamṛkāraḥ | parapūrvatvam | koḥ kittvānna laghūpadhaguṇaḥ | śrūyata iti śravo dhanam | asunpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | bṛhat | prātipadikasvaraḥ | viśvāyuḥ | viśvamāyuryasmindhane | viśvaśabdaḥ kvanpratyayāntaḥ | tasya bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamiti pūrvapadāntodāttatvam | ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityādyudāttaḥ | akṣitam | kṣi kṣaye ityasmādantarṇītaṇyarthātkarmaṇi niṣṭhā | tena syadarthatvānniṣṭhāyāmaṇyadarthe [? as printed] | pā. 6-4-60 | iti na dīrghatvam | ata eva kṣiyo dīrghāt | pā. 8-2-46 | iti na niṣṭhānatvam | nañsamāse 'vyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra! *Śravaḥ* — wealth — *asme* — to us — *saṃ dhehi*: bestow well. What kind of *śravaḥ*? *Gomat* — furnished with many cows; *vājavat* — furnished with abundant food; *pṛthu* — larger in measure; *bṛhat* — superior in qualities; *viśvāyuḥ* — the cause of a whole lifetime; *akṣitam* — free of destruction." *(The accompanying grammar, noted briefly: *gomat* and *vājavat* take their stem accent because* matup *is unaccented; *vāja* is a* vṛṣādi *word, initial-udātta;* asme *is formed by the substitute* śe *for the plural dative ending after* asmad*, replacing the whole as it is* śit*, final-udātta by the stem accent; by* śeṣe lopaḥ *(Pā. 7-2-90) — on the view that the* ṭi *is dropped, the case-ending is udātta by the accent of the lost udātta; on the view that the final is dropped, the pararūpa by* ato guṇe *is a single substitute udātta by* ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ*;* pṛthu *— root* prtha prakhyāne *with the suffix* ku *and* saṃprasāraṇa *of* r *to* ṛ *(Uṇ. 1-29);* śravaḥ *— 'that which is heard' = wealth, with* asun*, initial-udātta;* viśvāyuḥ *— a bahuvrīhi 'in which wealth the whole life [is]'; the first-member accent of a bahuvrīhi being displaced by* parādiś chandasi bahulam *to the end of the first member, and the single substitute udātta, so initial-udātta;* akṣitam *— from* kṣi kṣaye *with the causative sense inside, the past-participle suffix in the passive; no lengthening by Pā. 6-4-60 and hence no* n*-substitution by* kṣiyo dīrghāt *(Pā. 8-2-46); the* nañ *compound has the accent of its indeclinable first member. One word, printed* syadarthatvāt*, is kept as printed [?].)*"

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **अस्मे (asme)** — to us | **पृथु (pṛthu)** — abundant | **बृहत् (bṛhat)** — superior in qualities | **गोमत् (gomat)** — endowed with cows (in the form of cattle) | **वाजवत् (vājavat)** — endowed with food (in the form of food, nourishment) | **विश्वायुः (viśvāyuḥ)** — the cause of long life | **अक्षितम् (akṣitam)** — without destruction | **श्रवः (śravaḥ)** — wealth | **धेहि (dhehi)** — give.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! Give us abundant wealth: the best, in the form of cattle, horses and other animals and wealth, and in the form of grain and nourishing food — wealth that is the means of living a long life and that is imperishable. Give us such wealth in great abundance.

### Page 367 — Rik 7: English, Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Grant us, Indra, wealth beyond measure or calculation, inexhaustible the source of cattle, of food, of all life.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Gomat"** — **बह्वीभिर्गोभिरुपेतम्** (*bahvībhir gobhir upetam*) — "furnished with many cows." *Or:* *gāvo yasmin santi tat gomat* — "that in which there are cows"; *gomat* — wealth in the form of animals, with plenty of cows.

**"Vājavataḥ"** — wealth consisting of food (*anna*) and the like, of foodstuffs.

**"Asme"** — means *asmabhyam* (to us). In the Ṛgveda *asme* is used in many places in place of *asmabhyam*.

**"Śravaḥ"** — among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with *magham*, the word *śravaḥ* is read (Nirukta 3-9). **"Bṛhat"** — excellent, full of substance, excellent in qualities.

**"Viśvāyuḥ"** — **कृत्स्नायुष्यकारणम्** (*kṛtsnāyuṣya-kāraṇam*) — "the cause of a whole lifetime"; the Bhāṣyakāra explains it as wealth that serves for living for a long time. To explain it so, it is better to take *viśvāyuḥ* as a qualifier of *śravaḥ* (wealth) than as a qualifier in the sense "one who has a long life": the use of *viśvāyuḥ* as a *viśeṣya* word meaning "one who lives long" is more fitting. Skandasvāmī's meaning is likewise.

**"Akṣitam"** — free from destruction, inexhaustible.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 367–368, noted briefly)*

**गोमत्, वाजवत् (*gomat, vājavat*)** — "gaur asyāsti iti gomat; vājo 'sya asti iti vājavat": in both, *matup* is *pit*, hence unaccented, so the stem accent stands; *vāja* is a *vṛṣādi* word, so initial-udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 6-1-203). **अस्मे (*asme*)** — *asmad* + the dative-plural *bhyas*; this is replaced by *śe* by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39); the *ś* of *śe* is *it* by "lasakvataddhite" (Pā. 1-3-8), the substitute being *śit* replaces the whole of *bhyas* by "anekāl śit sarvasya" (Pā. 1-1-55); *asmad* is final-udātta by its stem accent; [on the view that the *ṭi* is dropped,] the *e* is udātta by the accent of the lost udātta, "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-161); [on the other view] the final *d* of *asmad* is dropped by "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-2-90); *asma* + *e* → *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), a single substitute that takes the udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). **पृथु (*pṛthu*)** — root *pṛtha prakhyāne* ("to spread"), and the rule "prathimradibhrasjāṃ saṃprasāraṇaṃ salopaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-28 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 366 prints 1-29): the suffix *ku* after *prath*, *mrad*, *bhrasj*, with *saṃprasāraṇa* of *r* to *ṛ* and loss of *s* in *bhrasj*; *pṛ* + *th* + *u* → *pṛthu* by the pūrvarūpa of "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108); *ku* is *kit*, so no *guṇa* by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86). **श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)** — "śrūyate iti": root *śru* + *asun* ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," no number printed); *guṇa* of *u* → *o* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84); *ov* → *av* by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78); the nominative/accusative singular ending *am*/*su* dropped by "svamor napuṃsakāt" (Pā. 7-1-23); *ru*-and-visarga; initial-udātta. **बृहत् (*bṛhat*)** — stem accent. **विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)** — a bahuvrīhi "viśvam āyur yasmin dhane"; *viśva* is formed with *kvan* (by "aśūpruṣi…", Uṇ. 1-149, from *aśū vyāptau*) and is *nit*, so initial-udātta; the bahuvrīhi rule "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1) would keep the first-member accent, but with the Vedic "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199) the end of the first member takes the udātta; *viśva* + *āyuḥ* → single substitute *ā*, udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). **अक्षितम् (*akṣitam*)** — root *kṣi kṣaye* in the sense including the causative; *kta* in the passive; by "niṣṭhā-yoṇya-darthe" (Pā. 6-4-60) the lengthening is prohibited since the word does not have the sense "not to be…"; and since the lengthening does not arise, the *n*-substitution of "kṣiyo dīrghāt" (Pā. 8-2-46) does not arise; the *nañ* compound with the negative takes the first-member accent of "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2) as with indeclinables.

**॥७॥**

### Page 369 — Sūkta 9, Rik 8

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒स्मे धे॑हि॒ श्रवो॑ बृ॒हद्द्यु॒म्नं स॑हस्र॒सात॑मम् ।
> इन्द्र॒ ता र॒थिनी॒रिषः॑ ॥८॥
>
> *asmé dhehi śrávo bṛhád dyumnáṃ sahasrasā́tamam |*
> *indra tā́ rathínīr íṣaḥ ||8||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अस्मे इति । धेहि । श्रवः । बृहत् । द्युम्नम् । सहस्रऽसातमम् ॥
> इन्द्र । ताः । रथिनीः । इषः ॥८॥
>
> *asme iti | dhehi | śravaḥ | bṛhat | dyumnam | sahasra-sātamam ||*
> *indra | tāḥ | rathinīḥ | iṣaḥ ||8||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र बृहच्छ्रवो महतीं कीर्तिमस्मे धेहि । अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छ । तथा सहस्रसातममतिशयेन सहस्रसंख्यादानोपेतं द्युम्नं धनमस्मे धेहि । तथा ता व्रीहियवादिरूपेण प्रसिद्धा रथिनीर्बहुरथोपेता इषो ऽन्नान्यस्मे धेहि ॥ अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना शे आदेशः । धेहि । घ्वसोरेद्धावभ्यासलोपश्च । पा. ६-४-११९ । इत्येत्वाभ्यासलोपौ । श्रूयत इति श्रवः । असुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सहस्रं सुनुते ददातीति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । पा. ३-२-६७ । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् । पा. ६-४-४१ । इत्याकारादेशः । धातुस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । पुनः कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते । रथा आसां सन्तीति रथिन्य इति प्रत्ययस्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् । पा. ४-१-५ । स च पित्त्वादनुदात्तः । इषो योगिकत्वे धातुस्वरः । रूढत्वे प्रातिपदिकस्वरः ॥
>
> *he indra bṛhacchravo mahatīṃ kīrtimasme dhehi | asmabhyaṃ prayaccha | tathā sahasrasātamamatiśayena sahasrasaṃkhyādānopetaṃ dyumnaṃ dhanamasme dhehi | tathā tā vrīhiyavādirūpeṇa prasiddhā rathinīrbahurathopetā iṣo 'nnānyasme dhehi || asme | supāṃ sulugityādinā śe ādeśaḥ | dhehi | ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaśca | pā. 6-4-119 | ityetvābhyāsalopau | śrūyata iti śravaḥ | asuno nittvādādyudāttatvam | sahasraṃ sunute dadātīti sahasrasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | pā. 3-2-67 | viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt | pā. 6-4-41 | ityākārādeśaḥ | dhātusvareṇāntodāttaḥ | punaḥ kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇa sa eva śiṣyate | rathā āsāṃ santīti rathinya iti pratyayasyādyudāttatvam | ṛnnebhyo ṅīp | pā. 4-1-5 | sa ca pittvādanudāttaḥ | iṣo yogikatve dhātusvaraḥ | rūḍhatve prātipadikasvaraḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra, *bṛhac-chravaḥ* — O you of great renown: give us (*asme dhehi*) great fame. And likewise bestow on us *sahasra-sātamam* — in extreme degree accompanied by gifts reckoned in thousands — *dyumnam*, wealth. And likewise *tāḥ* — those famous in the forms of rice, barley and the like — *rathinīḥ*, furnished with many chariots — *iṣaḥ*: foods; bestow them on us." *(Grammar noted briefly:* asme *as in Rik 7;* dhehi — *the root* dhā *with* hi*, with the substitution of* e *for* ā *and loss of the reduplicate (Pā. 6-4-119);* śravaḥ *with* asun*;* sahasrasā *— 'one who gives a thousand': root* ṣaṇu dāne *with* viṭ *(Pā. 3-2-67),* ā *for the nasal (Pā. 6-4-41), final-udātta by the root, then the second-member rule;* rathinyaḥ *— 'those who have chariots,' feminine in* ṅīp *(Pā. 4-1-5), unaccented because* pit*;* iṣaḥ *takes the root accent if taken in its component sense and the stem accent if taken as a settled word.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **अस्मे (asme)** — to us | **बृहत् (bṛhat)** — great, excellent | **श्रवः (śravaḥ)** — fame | **सहस्रसातमम् (sahasrasātamam)** — greatly helpful for giving thousands of different things | **द्युम्नम् (dyumnam)** — wealth | **रथिनीः (rathinīḥ)** — brought in chariots or carts | **ताः (tāḥ)** — those in the form of grains such as rice and barley | **इषः (iṣaḥ)** — foods | **धेहि (dhehi)** — give.

### Page 370 — Rik 8: overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! Give us exceedingly great fame and thousand-fold wealth, and grain and other food in cartloads (chariot-loads).

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, grant us great fame, and wealth acquired in a thousand ways and those (articles) of food (which are brought from the field) in carts.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The sense of this rik is easy to grasp; there are no special difficulties.

**"Śravaḥ"** — for this word Yāska, in his Nirukta, gives two or three different senses. Since the word *śravaḥ* is read among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with *magham* and *reknaḥ* (Nirukta 3-9), the sense "wealth" is also possible. In explaining the rik *uta svainaṃ* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 4-38-5) he says: "*śravaś cāpi paśum ucche yūthaṃ praśaṃsāṃ ca yūthaṃ dhanaṃ ca yūthaṃ ceti vā*" (as printed) — that is, *śravaḥ* is "praise (fame)" or "wealth" (Nirukta 4-24); and in the rik *amandān stomān* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-126-1; the first digit of the middle number is damaged in the print) he explains the word *śrava icchamānāḥ* as "wishing for praise" (Nirukta 9-11). In the explanation of the rik *pra vo mahe mandamānāya* (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-50-1) he explains *śravaḥ* as *mahac chravaṇīyaṃ yaśaḥ* — "great, worthy-of-hearing glory" (Nirukta 11-10). Since in this rik, besides this, the word *dyumnam* ("wealth") also occurs — a word for wealth — to render *śravaḥ* as "wealth" would produce the fault of repetition; so to give it the sense of "fame" is quite fitting.

**"Sahasrasātamam"** — **सहस्रं सनुते ददातीति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने** (*sahasraṃ sanute dadātīti sahasrasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne*) — "one who gives a thousand; the root *ṣaṇu* in the sense of giving." Therefore *sahasrasātamam* means "that which gives thousands, that is, that gives in the greatest abundance."

**"Tāḥ"** — a feminine accusative plural of *tad*, and an adjective of the word *iṣaḥ*. The necessity of this word is not evident in this rik; probably it is used for filling out the pāda.

**"Rathinīḥ"** — **रथा आसां सन्तीति रथिन्यः** (*rathā āsāṃ santīti rathinyaḥ*) — "those that have chariots": [loads] related to chariots — that is, filling the chariots or carts, in great abundance. The grain that a single man carries on his head is not very much; but in a cart, how much more — as many people can carry. Hence the grain that fills a cart is a very great amount of grain.

### Page 371 — Rik 8: grammar

**"Iṣaḥ"** — although the word has the sense "food," here it is used in a general sense, "food or grain." The adjective *rathinīḥ* supports this sense.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

**अस्मे (*asme*)** — the plural dative ending after *asmad* is replaced by *śe* by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39). **धेहि (*dhehi*)** — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ* ("to hold, to nourish"); *loṭ* parasmaipada second singular *sip*; *sip* → *hi* by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-80 [as printed]); the vikaraṇa *śap* (no number printed), dropped by *ślu* after the juhotyādi class, "juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ" (Pā. 2-4-75); doubling by *ślau* (Pā. 6-1-10); *dhā* + *hi*: by "ghvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaś ca" (Pā. 6-4-119) the roots called *ghu* and *as*, before *hi*, take *e* in place of the final *ā*, and the reduplicate vowel is dropped; so *dhehi*; wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)** — formed with *asun*; initial-udātta by the suffix. **सहस्रसातमम् (*sahasrasātamam*)** — *sahasraṃ sanute dadāti iti sahasrasāḥ*; root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *ṣ* → *s* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ"; *viṭ* after *jana*, *sana*, *khana*, *krama*, *gam* in the Veda (Pā. 3-2-67); the *ā* substituted for the nasal (Pā. 6-4-41); the whole *viṭ* dropped; *sahasra* + *sā*; final-udātta by the root accent, and after compounding the second member's accent stands by "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139); then *tamap* in the sense of excess by "atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau" (Pā. 5-3-55), *pit* and so unaccented. **रथिनीः (*rathinīḥ*)** — *rathāḥ āsāṃ santi*; *ini* by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); *a* of *ratha* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); *ini* is initial-udātta by the suffix accent; the stem *rathin* ends in *n*; the feminine *ṅīp* after *ṛ*- and *n*-ending stems (Pā. 4-1-5, "ṛnnebhyo ṅīp"); *ṅīp* is *pit*, so unaccented. **इषः (*iṣaḥ*)** — if taken in its component sense, the root accent stands (*i* udātta); if taken as a settled word, the stem accent applies.

**॥८॥**

### Page 372 — Sūkta 9, Rik 9

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> वसो॒रिन्द्रं॒ वसु॑पतिं गी॒र्भिर्गृ॒णन्त॑ ऋ॒ग्मियं॑ ।
> होम॒ गन्ता॑रमू॒तये॑ ॥९॥
>
> *vasor índraṃ vásupatiṃ gīrbhír gṛṇánta ṛgmíyaṃ |*
> *homa gántāram ūtáye ||9||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> वसोः । इन्द्रम् । वसुऽपतिम् । गीःऽभिः । गृणन्तः । ऋग्मियम् ॥
> होम । गन्तारम् । ऊतये ॥९॥
>
> *vasoḥ | indram | vasu-patim | gīḥ-bhiḥ | gṛṇantaḥ | ṛgmiyam ||*
> *homa | gantāram | ūtaye ||9||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> वसोर्वसुनो ऽस्मदीयस्य धनस्योतये रक्षार्थमिन्द्रं होम । वयमाह्वयामः । किं कुर्वन्तः । गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्गृणन्तः स्तुवन्तः । कीदृशमिन्द्रम् । वसुपतिं धनपालकं ऋग्मियं ऋचां मातारं गन्तारं यागदेशे गमनशीलम् ॥ वसोः । वस निवासे । शृस्वृस्निहीत्यादिना । उ १-११ । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वसुपतिम् । समासान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते पत्यावैश्वर्ये । पा. ६-२-१८ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । गीर्भिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । गृणन्तः । गॄ शब्दे । लटः शतृ । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । पा. ३-१-८१ । शतुः सार्वधातुकमपिदिति ङित्त्वात् श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः । पा. ६-४-११२ । इत्याकारलोपः । शतुरकारस्य प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । ऋग्मियम् । ऋचो मिमित [sic: मिमीते] इत्यृग्मीः । तमृग्मियं । माङ् माने शब्दे च । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । घुमास्थेत्यादिना । पा. ६-४-६६ । ईत्त्वं । चकारस्य चोः कुः । झलां जशो ऽन्ते । पा. ८-२-३९ । इति जश्त्वं । गकारः । द्वितीयैकवचने ऽचि श्नुधात्वित्यादिना । पा. ६-४-७७ । इयङादेशः । एरनेकाच इति यणादेशः । पा. ६-४-८२ । सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति न भवति । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । होम । आह्वयामः । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । लट् । तस्यास्मदो बहुत्वे ऽपि व्यत्ययेन मिप् । इकारस्य व्यत्ययेनाकारः । शपो बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । बहुलं छन्दसि । पा. ६-१-३४ । इति ह्वः संप्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वं गुणः । धातोः । पा. ६-१-१६२ । इत्योकार उदात्तः । मिपः पित्स्वरेणानुदात्तत्वम् । गन्तारम् । गम्लृ सृप्लृ गतौ । ताच्छील्ये तृन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ऊतये । ऊतियूतीत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तो निपातितः ॥
>
> *vasorvasuno 'smadīyasya dhanasyotaye rakṣārthamindraṃ homa | vayamāhvayāmaḥ | kiṃ kurvantaḥ | gīrbhiḥ stutibhirgṛṇantaḥ stuvantaḥ | kīdṛśamindram | vasupatiṃ dhanapālakaṃ ṛgmiyaṃ ṛcāṃ mātāraṃ gantāraṃ yāgadeśe gamanaśīlam || vasoḥ | vasa nivāse | śṛsvṛsnihītyādinā | u 1-11 | upratyayaḥ | nidityanuvṛtternittvādādyudāttaḥ | vasupatim | samāsāntodāttatve prāpte patyāvaiśvarye | pā. 6-2-18 | iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | gīrbhiḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | gṛṇantaḥ | gṝ śabde | laṭaḥ śatṛ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | pā. 3-1-81 | śatuḥ sārvadhātukamapiditi ṅittvāt śnābhyastayorātaḥ | pā. 6-4-112 | ityākāralopaḥ | śaturakārasya pratyayasvareṇodāttatvam | ṛgmiyam | ṛco mimita [sic: mimīte] ityṛgmīḥ | tamṛgmiyaṃ | māṅ māne śabde ca | kvipceti kvip | ghumāsthetyādinā | pā. 6-4-66 | īttvaṃ | cakārasya coḥ kuḥ | jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte | pā. 8-2-39 | iti jaśtvaṃ | gakāraḥ | dvitīyaikavacane 'ci śnudhātvityādinā | pā. 6-4-77 | iyaṅādeśaḥ | eranekāca iti yaṇādeśaḥ | pā. 6-4-82 | sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti na bhavati | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | homa | āhvayāmaḥ | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | laṭ | tasyāsmado bahutve 'pi vyatyayena mip | ikārasya vyatyayenākāraḥ | śapo bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | bahulaṃ chandasi | pā. 6-1-34 | iti hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvaṃ guṇaḥ | dhātoḥ | pā. 6-1-162 | ityokāra udāttaḥ | mipaḥ pitsvareṇānudāttatvam | gantāram | gamlṛ sṛplṛ gatau | tācchīlye tṛn | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | ūtaye | ūtiyūtītyādinā ktinnudātto nipātitaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "For the *ūtaye* — the protection — of our *vasu*, our wealth, we call (*homa*) Indra. What are we doing? *Gīrbhiḥ gṛṇantaḥ* — praising with hymns. What kind of Indra? *Vasupatim* — the guardian of wealth; *ṛgmiyam* — the measurer (*mātṛ*) of the ṛks; *gantāram* — the one who is in the habit of going to the place of sacrifice." *(Grammar, noted briefly: *vasoḥ* — root* vasa nivāse *with the suffix* u *(Uṇ. 1-11);* vasupatim *— the first-member accent by Pā. 6-2-18 when* pati *means 'lord';* gṛṇantaḥ *— root* gṝ śabde*,* śatṛ *with* śnā*, the* ā *of* śnā *dropped before the* śatṛ *since it is treated as* ṅit*;* ṛgmiyam *— 'one who measures the ṛks' (*ṛco mimīte*): root* māṅ māne śabde ca *with* kvip*, the* ī *by Pā. 6-4-66, the voicing of the final consonant (Pā. 8-2-39); before the accusative ending the* iyaṅ *substitute (Pā. 6-4-77), not the* yaṇ *of Pā. 6-4-82; the* i *udātta by the second-member accent;* homa *— root* hveñ *with the first-person plural* mip *by Vedic exchange,* śap *dropped, the* saṃprasāraṇa *of* hve *(Pā. 6-1-34), giving* homa*, the* o *udātta by* dhātoḥ *(Pā. 6-1-162);* gantāram *— root* gamlṛ *with* tṛn *in the sense of habit, initial-udātta since* nit*;* ūtaye *— the* ktin *of* ūti*, udātta by the irregular formation.)*"

### Page 373 — Rik 9: word-meanings, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**वसोः (vasoḥ)** — (our) wealth's | **ऊतये (ūtaye)** — for protection | **वसुपतिम् (vasupatim)** — the lord of wealth and splendour | **ऋग्मियम् (ṛgmiyam)** — worthy of being praised by ṛks | **गन्तारम् (gantāram)** — one who goes to the sacrificial ground (for the protection of the sacrificer) | **इन्द्रम् (indram)** — Indra | **गीर्भिः (gīrbhiḥ)** — with hymns in the form of speech | **गृणन्तः (gṛṇantaḥ)** — praising | **होम (homa)** — we call.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Indra is the lord of wealth and splendour; he is worthy of being praised with ṛks (Vedic mantras); he goes to the sacrificial ground and protects the sacrificers and others. We call such an Indra with hymns for the protection of our wealth.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Praising with songs we invoke Indra, the lord of riches, who deserves to be praised and who goes (to protect his worshipper).

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Vasupatim"** — *vasu* is wealth, *pati* is lord; the lord of wealth, the master of wealth. Although the word *vasoḥ* is already in this rik, the word *vasupatim* is used again — would there not then be a fault of repetition? No: such usages are found especially often in the Ṛgveda. When using a customary (settled) group of words, one need not attend to whether it is faulty by repetition or contrary to the rules of grammar. Because everyone uses what is settled in usage, its use is regarded as right; for the rules of grammar and the like are composed following the established practice of the language. The root of grammar is language, not the root of language grammar. Such usages with repetition are needed in the Ṛgveda in plenty. We give a couple of examples:

> ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनाम् ॥
> *ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tam ā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnām ||*
> (ऋ. सं. ३-३०-१९ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3-30-19)
> *("As if like an expanse my desire has spread [for me]; fill it, O lord of riches, of the riches." — mine and tentative.)*

> आ तू भर माकिरेतत्परिष्ठाद्विद्मा हि त्वा वसुपतिं वसूनाम् ॥
> *ā tū bhara mākir etat pariṣṭhād vidmā hi tvā vasupatiṃ vasūnām ||*
> (ऋ. सं. ३-३६-९ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3-36-9)
> *("Bring [it] now; let none hinder this; for we know you as lord of riches of riches." — mine and tentative.)*

### Page 374 — Rik 9: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

*(The page opens with the end of the second quoted rik from p. 373, and a third:)*

> सत्राभवो वसुपतिर्वसूनां दत्रे विश्वा अधिथा इन्द्र कृष्टीः ॥
> *satrābhavo vasupatir vasūnāṃ datre viśvā adhithā indra kṛṣṭīḥ ||*
> (ऋ. सं. ४-१७-६ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 4-17-6)
> *("You were the lord of riches, of riches in giving; you held all the peoples, O Indra." — mine and tentative.)*

*"…and so on."* All these riks are addressed to Indra. So it may be said that calling Indra *vasupati* is an established usage.

**"Ṛgmiyam"** — **ऋचो मिमीत इत्यृग्मियः । ऋचां मातारम्** (*ṛco mimīta ity ṛgmiyaḥ | ṛcāṃ mātāram*) — "one who measures the ṛks is *ṛgmiya*; the 'maker' of the ṛks": the Bhāṣyakāra explains it as "one who is praised by ṛks," i.e., one who is hymned. **Skandasvāmī:** **ऋग्मियं । ऋचि स्तुतौ । अर्चना ऋक् । संपदादित्वात् क्विप् । तद्वन्तं स्तुतियोग्यमित्यर्थः** (*ṛgmiyaṃ | ṛci stutau | arcanā ṛk | saṃpadāditvāt kvip | tadvantaṃ stuti-yogyam ity arthaḥ*) — "*ṛgmiya*: [root] *ṛc* in the sense of praise; *ṛk* is worship (*arcanā*), with *kvip* as it belongs to the *saṃpadādi* group; [the one] possessed of it, that is, worthy of praise." That is, *ṛgmiya* means "worthy of being praised." **Veṅkaṭamādhava** says *ṛgarham* — "worthy of ṛks," that is, worthy of being praised with ṛks.

**"Homa"** — *āhvayāmaḥ*, "we invoke, we call." The word is the first-person plural *laṭ* of the root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*. For its derivation see the grammar section.

**"Gantāram"** — the accusative singular of the *ṛ*-ending word *gantṛ*. The meaning is "one who goes." Where does he go? The Bhāṣyakāra says to supply the words **यागदेशे गमनशीलम्** (*yāgadeśe gamanaśīlam*) — "in the habit of going to the place of sacrifice" — to make the sense: one who goes to the sacrificial ground to protect the sacrificer.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 374–376, noted briefly)*

**वसोः (*vasoḥ*)** — root *vasa nivāse*; the Uṇādi sūtra "śṝ-svṛ-snihi-trapy-asi-vasi-hani-klidi-bandhi-manibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-10) gives the suffix *u* after the roots *śṝ hiṃsāyām*, *svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ*, *ṣṇiha upatāpe* [as printed], *trapūṣ lajjāyām*, *asu kṣepaṇe*, *vasa nivāse*, *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*, *klidū ārdrībhāve*, *bandha bandhane*, *mana jñāne*; the suffix is *nit*, so *vasu* is initial-udātta. **वसुपतिम् (*vasupatim*)** — compound accent: by "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223) final-udātta would be expected; this is set aside by "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-1-18 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 372 prints 6-2-18) — when *pati* in the sense of lordship is the second member, the first member keeps its natural accent. **गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)** — "sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168): the case ending is udātta. **गृणन्तः (*gṛṇantaḥ*)** — root *gṝ śabde* ("to sound; praise") with *laṭ*, replaced by *śatṛ* by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau" (Pā. 3-2-124); *śnā* after the *kryādi* class (Pā. 3-1-81); the root vowel shortened by "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-3-80); *śatṛ*, being *apit*, is *ṅit* by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4), so the *ā* of *śnā* is dropped by "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-112); the *n* of *śnā* becomes *ṇ* by the vārttika "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam" (vārttika 8-4-1); *num* before *jas* by "ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-70); the suffix-accent makes the *a* of *śatṛ* udātta. **ऋग्मियम् (*ṛgmiyam*)** — "ṛco mimīte": root *māṅ māne śabde ca* + *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76); by "ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali" (Pā. 7-4-66 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 372 prints 6-4-66) the *ā* → *ī*; "ver apṛktasya" (Pā. 6-1-67) removes the *v* — with a discussion of *antaraṅga* and *bahiraṅga* (paribhāṣā 50, "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge"), *sthānivad ādeśo 'nalvidhau* (Pā. 1-1-56) and "varṇāśraye nāsti pratyayalakṣaṇam" (paribhāṣā 21), concluding that in Vedic usage *sthānivadbhāva* sometimes applies even in an *al*-rule; *c* → *k* by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30) and *k* → *g* by "jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte" (Pā. 8-2-39); accusative singular *am*; the *ī* before the vowel becomes *iy* (*iyaṅ*, "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau", Pā. 6-4-77), with a discussion of the rule "er anekāco 'saṃyogapūrvasya" (Pā. 6-4-82) (*yaṇ* for the final *i*/*ī* of a root of more than one syllable) and why it does not arise here (by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante", paribhāṣā 35); finally "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the *ī*-syllable the udātta. **होम (*homa*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *laṭ* first plural *mas*, replaced by *mip* by Vedic inversion; *i* of *mip* → *a*; *śap* dropped by *bahulaṃ chandasi* (Pā. 2-4-73); *saṃprasāraṇa* of *hve* by the "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34) that follows "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. 6-1-32); *pūrvarūpa* by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108) and *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) give *homa*; the *o* is udātta by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-162); *mip* is *pit*, so the *ma* is unaccented. **गन्तारम् (*gantāram*)** — root *gamlṛ sṛplṛ gatau* with *tṛn* in the sense of habitual action (Pā. 3-2-135); *nit*, initial-udātta. **ऊतये (*ūtaye*)** — the irregular *ktin* of "ūtiyūtijūti…" (Pā. 3-3-97), udātta.

**॥९॥**

### Page 377 — Rik 10: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> आकार इच्छब्दश्च पादपूरणौ । यद्वा । व्याप्तिवचन आकारः । आङीषदर्थे ऽभिव्याप्तौ । अमु. ३-४-३२ । इत्यभिधानात् । इच्छब्दो ऽपिशब्दार्थः । इयर्ति गच्छत्यनुष्ठेयं कर्म प्राप्नोतीत्यरिर्यजमानः । एदरिः सर्वो ऽपि यजमान इन्द्राय सुते सुत इन्द्रार्थमभिषुते तत्र तत्र सोमे शूषं बलमर्चति स्तौति । इन्द्रस्य पराक्रमं प्रशंसतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशं शूषम् । बृहत् प्रौढम् । कीदृशायेन्द्राय । न्योकसे नियतस्थानाय बृहते प्रौढाय ॥ सुते सुते । षुञ् अभिषवे । क्तप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति वीप्सायां द्विर्भावः । तस्य परमाम्रेडितमिति द्वितीयस्याम्रेडितत्वेनानुदात्तं च । पा. ८-१-३ । इत्यनुदात्तत्वम् । न्योकसे । नियतमोको यस्य तस्मै । निशब्दो निपाता आद्युदात्ता इत्युदात्तः । तस्य यणादेश उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः स्वरितो ऽनुदात्तस्य । पा. ८-२-४ । इत्योकारः स्वरितः । बृहते । बृहन्महतोरुपसंख्यानम् । पा. ६-१-१७३-१ । इत्यजादिविभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अरिः । ऋ गतौ । अच इः । उ. ४-१३८ । इतीकारप्रत्ययः । गुणो रपरत्वम् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । इन्द्राय । ऋज्रेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन्प्रत्यय इकार उदात्तः । शूषम् । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । अर्चति । निघातस्वरः ॥ १८ ॥
>
> *ākāra icchabdaśca pādapūraṇau | yadvā | vyāptivacana ākāraḥ | āṅīṣadarthe 'bhivyāptau | amu. 3-4-32 | ityabhidhānāt | icchabdo 'piśabdārthaḥ | iyarti gacchatyanuṣṭheyaṃ karma prāpnotītyariryajamānaḥ | edariḥ sarvo 'pi yajamāna indrāya sute suta indrārthamabhiṣute tatra tatra some śūṣaṃ balamarcati stauti | indrasya parākramaṃ praśaṃsatītyarthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ śūṣam | bṛhat prauḍham | kīdṛśāyendrāya | nyokase niyatasthānāya bṛhate prauḍhāya || sute sute | ṣuñ abhiṣave | ktapratyayaḥ | pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | nityavīpsayoriti vīpsāyāṃ dvirbhāvaḥ | tasya paramāmreḍitamiti dvitīyasyāmreḍitatvenānudāttaṃ ca | pā. 8-1-3 | ityanudāttatvam | nyokase | niyatamoko yasya tasmai | niśabdo nipātā ādyudāttā ityudāttaḥ | tasya yaṇādeśa udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya | pā. 8-2-4 | ityokāraḥ svaritaḥ | bṛhate | bṛhanmahatorupasaṃkhyānam | pā. 6-1-173-1 | ityajādivibhakterudāttatvam | ariḥ | ṛ gatau | aca iḥ | u. 4-138 | itīkārapratyayaḥ | guṇo raparatvam | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | indrāya | ṛjrendretyādinā ranpratyaya ikāra udāttaḥ | śūṣam | prātipadikasvaraḥ | arcati | nighātasvaraḥ || 18 ||*

**Translation:** "The syllable *ā* and the word *it* are pāda-fillers. *Or:* the *ā* has the sense of 'pervading', according to the statement [of the Amarakośa], '*āṅ* in the sense of "a little" and of "pervading"' (Amara 3-4-32); the word *it* has the sense of *api* ('also'). *Ariḥ* is the sacrificer: 'he who goes (*iyarti*) — attains — the rite to be performed.' *Ed ariḥ*: every sacrificer, *sute-sute*, in each Soma that is pressed for Indra's sake, *arcati* — praises — *śūṣam*, [his] strength, that is, extols Indra's prowess. What kind of *śūṣa*? *Bṛhat* — vast. For what kind of Indra? *Nyokase* — one whose dwelling is fixed; *bṛhate* — great."

*(Grammar, noted briefly:* sute-sute *— root* ṣuñ abhiṣave *with* kta*, udātta by the suffix; doubled in the distributive sense ("nityavīpsayoḥ"), the second, as* āmreḍita*, unaccented (Pā. 8-1-3);* nyokase *— "he whose abode (*okas*) is fixed"; the particle* ni *initial-udātta; with* yaṇ*, the* o *becomes svarita (Pā. 8-2-4);* bṛhate *— the case ending udātta by the upasaṃkhyāna "bṛhanmahatoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-173, vārttika 1);* ariḥ *— root* ṛ gatau *with* i *(Uṇ. 4-138),* guṇa *and* r*, the* i *udātta;* indrāya *— the suffix* ran *(by "ṛjrendra…"), the* i *udātta;* śūṣam *— stem accent;* arcati *— unaccented as a finite verb. The bhāṣya ends "॥ १८ ॥", the close of the eighteenth varga.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अरिः (ariḥ)** — the sacrificer who performs the rite, or who offers praise | **न्योकसे (nyokase)** — to the one who dwells in his appointed place | **बृहते (bṛhate)** — mighty, of great capacity | **इन्द्राय (indrāya)** — for Indra | **सुतेसुते (sute-sute)** — in each pressing, for Indra, of the Soma-juice prepared | **बृहत् (bṛhat)** — vast | **शूषम् (śūṣam)** — (Indra's) strength (power of capacity) | **आ अर्चति इत् (ā arcati it)** — praises indeed.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The strength, or capacity, of Indra is exceedingly great. The sacrificer who performs the rite praises with hymns and the like, in each pressing — the morning pressing and the other two — Indra's strength and capacities, and calls him.

### Page 378 — Rik 10: English, Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The sacrificer glorifies the vast prowess of Indra, the mighty, the dweller in his permanent abode in every rite where soma is prepared.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In this rik, although a third-person verb has been used — "the sacrificer praises Indra" — the poet indirectly states the sense of a first-person usage: "I praise Indra."

**"Sute sute"** — "at each pressing." By "nityavīpsayoḥ" (no number printed) a word is doubled to show "each one." Using a single word twice to convey "each" is established usage in the Ṛgveda and in other texts: *bhare-bhare*, *have-have*, *aharahaḥ*, etc. *Sute-sute* means "in the rite of each pressing, and in each rite where Soma-juice is drawn."

**"Nyokase"** — *ni* + *okase*. Here *ni* is a prefix (*upasarga*). The word *okaḥ*, ending in *s*, means a dwelling, one's own place, a place where one always lives: *permanent dwelling, abode*, etc. [the source's own English]. For the word *divaukasaḥ* — "those who dwell in heaven," as their own place — means "gods." Similarly in *ni-okase* = *nyokase*, the *ni* is a particle (*upasarga*), here meaning "fixed." So *nyokase* means "one whose place is fixed."

**"Ā it"** — these words have no necessary meaning in this rik; they are used for filling out the pāda. Or the Bhāṣyakāra's view is that the word *ā* may be given the sense of *api* ("also").

**"Bṛhate"** — **महते, महतः शरीरेण वीर्येण वा** (*mahate, mahataḥ śarīreṇa vīryeṇa vā*) — "great — great in body or in valour"; that is, great in body and also in prowess.

**"Ariḥ"** — **ऋ गतौ । इयर्ति गच्छतीत्यनुष्ठेयं कर्म प्राप्नोतीत्यरिर्यजमानः** (*ṛ gatau | iyarti gacchatīty anuṣṭheyaṃ karma prāpnotīty arir yajamānaḥ*) — the root *ṛ* means "to go, to attain": the one who attains the rite to be performed, i.e., one who performs the rite, the sacrificer.

**"Śūṣam"** — strength, capacity. Among the twenty-eight words for strength beginning with *ojaḥ*, *pājaḥ*, the word *śūṣam* is read (Nirukta 2-9). Indra's powers, valour, glory, and so on. Although *śūṣa* has this sense, when the word is used with Indra in view, the sense "hymn" (*stotra*) generally fits best. A few examples are given on this point:

### Page 379 — Rik 10: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

> प्र मन्महे शवसानाय शूषमाङ्गूषं गिर्वणसे अङ्गिरस्वत् ।
> *pra manmahe śavasānāya śūṣam āṅgūṣaṃ girvaṇase aṅgirasvat |*
> (ऋ. सं. १-६२-१ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 1-62-1)
> *("We offer a hymn — a śūṣa, an āṅgūṣa — to the powerful one, the hymn-loving, as the Aṅgirases did." — mine and tentative.)*

> इनम् महे विदथ्याय शूषं शश्वत्कृत्व ईड्याय प्र जभ्रुः ।
> *inam mahe vidathyāya śūṣaṃ śaśvat-kṛtva īḍyāya pra jabhruḥ |*
> (ऋ. सं. ३-५४-१ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 3-54-1)
> *("To the great lord, worthy of the assembly, worthy of praise, they have brought a hymn, perpetually acting." — mine and tentative.)*

> उप व एषे वन्द्येभिः शूषैः प्र यह्वी दिवश्चितयद्भिरर्कैः ।
> *upa va eṣe vandyebhiḥ śūṣaiḥ pra yahvī divaś citayadbhir arkaiḥ |*
> (ऋ. सं. ५-४१-६ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 5-41-6)
> *("I approach you with praiseworthy hymns, with hymns that make [the heavens] shine." — mine and tentative.)*

> आ यं पृणन्ति हरिभिर्न धेनव इन्द्राय शूषं हरिवन्तमर्चत ॥
> *ā yaṃ pṛṇanti haribhir na dhenava indrāya śūṣaṃ harivantam arcata ||*
> (ऋ. सं. १०-९६-२ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 10-96-2)
> *("…whom [the hymns] fill as milch-cows [fill a calf]; sing a hymn to Indra, the lord of bay horses." — mine and tentative.)*

Many more examples could be given.

**"Arcati"** — *arcati* is read among the forty-four verbs [*roots*] of the sense "to worship, praise," beginning with *arcati*, *gāyati* (Nirukta 3-19); so *arcati* means *gāyati*, *stauti* — "he praises, he extols."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 379–380, noted briefly)*

**सुतेसुते (*sute-sute*)** — root *ṣuñ abhiṣave* ("to press") + *kta*; initial/final-udātta by the suffix; locative singular *ṅi* → *e*; doubling by "nityavīpsayoḥ" (Pā. 8-1-4); for the second member the technical name *āmreḍita* arises ("tasya paramāmreḍitam," Pā. 8-1-2), and "anudāttaṃ ca" (8-1-3, printed "va. sū." [sic]) makes it unaccented. **न्योकसे (*nyokase*)** — "niyatam okaḥ yasya": *ni* is a *nipāta*, initial-udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Phiṭ-sūtra 80); the udātta *i* is replaced by *y* ("iko yaṇ aci," Pā. 6-4-77 [as printed]), and the *o* after the udātta *y* is *svarita* by "udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya" (Pā. 8-2-4). **बृहते (*bṛhate*)** — "bṛhan-mahator upasaṃkhyānam" (Pā. 6-1-173, vārttika 1): after *bṛhat* and *mahat* the case-ending that has *nadī* status (and the vowel-initial endings) is udātta; so the *e* in *bṛhate* is udātta; although the sūtra "vartamāne pṛṣad-bṛhan-mahaj-jagac-chatṛvac ca" (Uṇ. 2-2-42 [?], as printed in three parts) says *śatṛvat* (treated like *śatṛ*), by which "śatur anumo nadyajādī" (Pā. 6-1-173) would already give the udātta, a *vārttika* is needed to fix the rule so that it applies only after *bṛhat* and *mahat* and not after *pṛṣat* and *jagat*; hence "bṛhan-mahator upasaṃkhyānam" is necessary. **अरिः (*ariḥ*)** — root *ṛ gatau* + the suffix *i* by "aca iḥ" (Uṇ. 4-578 [as printed]; the bhāṣya on p. 377 prints 4-138); guṇa by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) and *raparatva* by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51); *ari* is final-udātta by the suffix. **इन्द्राय (*indrāya*)** — *ran* by "ṛjrendrāgra-vajra…" (Uṇ. 2-186); the suffix is *nit*, so initial-udātta. **शूषम् (*śūṣam*)** — base accent by the Phiṭ-sūtra "phiṣaḥ" (Phiṭ 1). **अर्चति (*arcati*)** — wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

**॥१०॥**

**इति नवमं सूक्तं समाप्तम् ।**
*iti navamaṃ sūktaṃ samāptam |*
"Thus the ninth sūkta is completed." *(Printed in Sanskrit at the end of the grammar, p. 380.)*

**End of Sūkta 9.** *(The same page, 380, then opens the tenth sūkta, "gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ", with its application note; its heading, with the varga numerals and Rik 1 text, is on p. 381.)*

### Page 380 (lower half) — opening of Sūkta 10 (third anuvāka)

**॥ ಹತ್ತನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 10 — *"gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ"* ("The Tenth Sūkta")**

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)**

> गायन्तीति सूक्तस्य मन्त्रसंख्या छन्दोविशेषश्चैवमनुक्रम्यते । गायन्ति द्वादशानुष्टुभं त्विति । तुहिहवेत्यादिपरिभाषायाम् । अनु १२-३ । तुशब्दस्य सूक्तद्वये परिभाषितत्वादस्य सूक्तस्य वक्ष्यमाणस्य चानुष्टुभत्वं द्रष्टव्यम् । ऋषिदेवते पूर्ववत् । अभिप्लवषडहस्योक्थ्येषु तृतीयसवने ऽच्छावाकस्य गायन्तीति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । एह्यूष्विति खण्डे गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिण आ त्वा गिरो रथीरिव । आ. ७-८ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥
>
> *gāyantīti sūktasya mantrasaṃkhyā chandoviśeṣaścaivamanukramyate | gāyanti dvādaśānuṣṭubhaṃ tviti | tuhihavetyādiparibhāṣāyām | anu 12-3 | tuśabdasya sūktadvaye paribhāṣitatvādasya sūktasya vakṣyamāṇasya cānuṣṭubhatvaṃ draṣṭavyam | ṛṣidevate pūrvavat | abhiplavaṣaḍahasyokthyeṣu tṛtīyasavane 'cchāvākasya gāyantīti stotriyastṛcaḥ | ehyūṣviti khaṇḍe gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇa ā tvā giro rathīriva | ā. 7-8 | iti sūtritam ||*

**Translation:** "The number of mantras and the special meter of the sūkta *gāyanti* are laid down in the Anukramaṇī thus: '*gāyanti dvādaśānuṣṭubhaṃ tv iti*' ("*gāyanti*: twelve, in Anuṣṭubh — *tu*"); and by the rule beginning *tuhihava* in the Paribhāṣā (Anukramaṇī 12-3), since the word *tu* is declared to apply to two sūktas, this sūkta and the next are both to be understood as Anuṣṭubh. Ṛṣi and deity are as before. Its special application: in the *ukthya* [rites] of the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha, in the third pressing, the opening triplet (*stotriya*) of the Acchāvāka is *gāyanti*. In the section *ehy ū ṣu* it is laid down: '*gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ*, *ā tvā giro rathīr iva*' (Āśvalāyana 7-8)."

**॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥** The mantra-count and the meter of the sūkta *gāyanti tvā* are given in the Sūkta-anukramaṇī as "*gāyanti dvādaśānuṣṭubhaṃ tv iti*" — twelve riks, in the Anuṣṭubh meter (Anu. 12-3). Here the word *tu* [in the Paribhāṣā] is used so as to make known that this sūkta and the next share the same meter, Anuṣṭubh, as the two sūktas it governs. The ṛṣi and deity of this sūkta are as in the previous sūkta. Its application: in the sacrifice called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, at the third pressing, when the *ukthya* mantras are recited, the Acchāvāka priest [recites] the triplet *gāyanti*, as a *stotriya* [opening triplet] śastra-mantra. Āśvalāyana says in his Śrauta-sūtra, in the section *ehy ū ṣu* (Āś. Sū. 7-8), that the riks *gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-1; Sāma 342; 1344) and *ā tvā giro rathīr iva* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-95-1; Sāma 349) are to be recited.

### Page 381 — Sūkta 10, Rik 1

**॥ Sūkta — 10 ॥**
**॥ Maṇḍala — 1 ॥ Anuvāka — 3 ॥ Sūkta — 10 ॥**
**॥ Aṣṭaka — 1 ॥ Adhyāya — 1 ॥ Varga — 19, 20 ॥**
**॥ Mantras contained in this sūkta: 1–12 ॥**
**॥ Ṛṣi — Madhucchandā Vaiśvāmitra ॥**
**॥ Devatā — Indra ॥**
**॥ Chandaḥ — Anuṣṭubh ॥**

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> गाय॑न्ति त्वा गाय॒त्रिणो ऽर्च॑न्त्य॒र्कम॒र्किणः॑ ।
> ब्र॒ह्मा॑णस्त्वा शतक्र॒त उद्वं॒शमि॑व येमिरे ॥१॥
>
> *gā́yanti tvā gāyatríṇó 'rcanty arkám arkíṇaḥ |*
> *brahmāṇas tvā śatakratá ud vaṃśám iva yemire ||1||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> गायन्ति । त्वा । गायत्रिणः । अर्चन्ति । अर्कम् । अर्किणः ॥
> ब्रह्माणः । त्वा । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो । उत् । वंशम्ऽइव । येमिरे ॥१॥
>
> *gāyanti | tvā | gāyatriṇaḥ | arcanti | arkam | arkiṇaḥ ||*
> *brahmāṇaḥ | tvā | śatakrato iti śata-krato | ut | vaṃśam-iva | yemire ||1||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन्बहुप्रज्ञ वेन्द्र त्वां गायत्रिण उद्गातारो गायन्ति । स्तुवन्ति । अर्किणो ऽर्चनहेतुमन्त्रयुक्ता होतारो ऽर्कमर्चनीयमिन्द्रमर्चन्ति । शस्त्रगतैर्मन्त्रैः प्रशंसन्ति । ब्रह्माणो ब्रह्मप्रभृतय इतरे ब्राह्मणास्त्वामुद्येमिरे । उन्नतिं प्रापयन्ति । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । वंशमिव । यथा वंशाग्रे नृत्यन्तः शिल्पिनः प्रौढं वंशमुत्पन्नं कुर्वन्ति । यथा वा सन्मार्गवर्तिनः स्वकीयं कुलमुन्नतं कुर्वन्ति तद्वत् । एतामृचं यास्क एवं व्याचष्टे । गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिणः प्रार्चन्ति ते ऽर्कमर्किणो ब्रह्माणस्त्वा शतक्रत उद्येमिरे वंशमिव । वंशो वनशयो भवति वननाच्छ्रूयत इति वा । नि. ५-५ । अर्कशब्दं च बहुधा व्याचष्टे । अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चन्त्यर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्त्यर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतान्यर्को वृक्षो भवति स वृतः कटुकिम्ना । नि. ५-४ । इति ॥ गायन्ति । शप्तिङौ पित्त्वात्सार्वधातुकत्वाच्चानुदात्तौ । धातुरुदात्तः । गायत्रिणः । गायत्रं साम येषामुद्गातॄणामस्ति ते । अत इनिठनौ । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । अर्चन्ति । अर्च पूजायाम् । भौवादिकः । शप्तिङावनुदात्तौ धातुस्वर एव । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । अर्कम् । अर्चन्त्येभिरित्यर्का मन्त्राः । तैरर्चनीयतया तदात्मक इन्द्रो ऽपि लक्षणयार्कः । पुंसि संज्ञायां घः प्रायेण । पा. ३-३-११८ । इति करणे घः । चजोः कु घिण्ण्यतोः । पा. ७-३-५२ । इति चकारस्य कुत्वम् । ककारः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । अर्का मन्त्रा एषां सन्तीत्यर्किणो होतारः । एकाक्षरात्कृतो जातेः सप्तम्यां च न तौ स्मृतौ । पा. ५-२-११५-२ । इति कृदन्तादिनिठनौ यद्यपि प्रतिषिद्धौ तथाप्यत्र व्यत्ययादिनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । ब्रह्माणः । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । शतक्रतो । निघातः । संहितायामवादेशे लोपः शाकल्यस्य । पा. ८-३-१९ । इति वकारलोपः । वंशशब्दः प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च । पा. २-१-४-२ । इति स एव शिष्यते । येमिरे । यम उपरमे । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥
>
> *he śatakrato bahukarmanbahuprajña vendra tvāṃ gāyatriṇa udgātāro gāyanti | stuvanti | arkiṇo 'rcanahetumantrayuktā hotāro 'rkamarcanīyamindramarcanti | śastragatairmantraiḥ praśaṃsanti | brahmāṇo brahmaprabhṛtaya itare brāhmaṇāstvāmudyemire | unnatiṃ prāpayanti | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | vaṃśamiva | yathā vaṃśāgre nṛtyantaḥ śilpinaḥ prauḍhaṃ vaṃśamutpannaṃ kurvanti | yathā vā sanmārgavartinaḥ svakīyaṃ kulamunnataṃ kurvanti tadvat | etāmṛcaṃ yāska evaṃ vyācaṣṭe | gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ prārcanti te 'rkamarkiṇo brahmāṇastvā śatakrata udyemire vaṃśamiva | vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vananācchrūyata iti vā | ni. 5-5 | arkaśabdaṃ ca bahudhā vyācaṣṭe | arko devo bhavati yadenamarcantyarko mantro bhavati yadenenārcantyarkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtānyarko vṛkṣo bhavati sa vṛtaḥ kaṭukimnā | ni. 5-4 | iti || gāyanti | śaptiṅau pittvātsārvadhātukatvāccānudāttau | dhāturudāttaḥ | gāyatriṇaḥ | gāyatraṃ sāma yeṣāmudgātṝṇāmasti te | ata iniṭhanau | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | arcanti | arca pūjāyām | bhauvādikaḥ | śaptiṅāvanudāttau dhātusvara eva | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | arkam | arcantyebhirityarkā mantrāḥ | tairarcanīyatayā tadātmaka indro 'pi lakṣaṇayārkaḥ | puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa | pā. 3-3-118 | iti karaṇe ghaḥ | cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ | pā. 7-3-52 | iti cakārasya kutvam | kakāraḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | arkā mantrā eṣāṃ santītyarkiṇo hotāraḥ | ekākṣarātkṛto jāteḥ saptamyāṃ ca na tau smṛtau | pā. 5-2-115-2 | iti kṛdantādiniṭhanau yadyapi pratiṣiddhau tathāpyatra vyatyayādiniḥ | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | brahmāṇaḥ | prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | śatakrato | nighātaḥ | saṃhitāyāmavādeśe lopaḥ śākalyasya | pā. 8-3-19 | iti vakāralopaḥ | vaṃśaśabdaḥ prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca | pā. 2-1-4-2 | iti sa eva śiṣyate | yemire | yama uparame | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O *śatakrato* — O Indra of many deeds, of much wisdom — the *gāyatriṇaḥ*, the udgātṛ priests, sing of you (*gāyanti*): they praise. The *arkiṇaḥ*, the hotṛ priests, equipped with the mantras that are the means of worship, worship (*arcanti*) Indra, the *arka* — the worshipful one: they praise [him] with the mantras of the śastra. The *brahmāṇaḥ* — Brahmā and the other brāhmaṇas — *ud yemire*: raise you aloft, they bring about your elevation. The illustration: *vaṃśam iva* — as craftsmen dancing at the tip of a bamboo pole set the grown bamboo upright, or as those who follow the good path raise their own family high, so [they raise you]. This rik Yāska explains thus: '*gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ*, *prārcanti te 'rkam arkiṇaḥ*, *brahmāṇas tvā śatakrata udyemire vaṃśam iva*; a *vaṃśa* (bamboo) is "that which lies in the forest" (*vanaśaya*), or "that which is heard of (*śrūyate*) because of its being enjoyed (*vananāt*)"' (Nirukta 5-5). And he explains the word *arka* in many ways: '*arka* is a god, because they worship him (*arcanti*); *arka* is a mantra, because with it they worship; *arka* is food, because beings honour it; *arka* is a tree (*vṛkṣa*): it is covered with pungency' (Nirukta 5-4)."

*(Grammar, noted briefly:* gāyanti *— the root accent stands, śap and tiṅ being unaccented;* gāyatriṇaḥ *— "those udgātṛs who have the gāyatra sāman", with* ini*, the* i *udātta;* arcanti *— root* arca pūjāyām*, root accent, not lowered as first in the pāda;* arkam *— "the mantras with which they worship", hence by implication Indra; the suffix* gha *in the instrumental sense (Pā. 3-3-118),* c → k *(Pā. 7-3-52), final-udātta;* arkiṇaḥ *— the hotṛs "who have the arka-mantras", with* ini *by Vedic exchange though the vārttika (Pā. 5-2-115-2) forbids it after a kṛt stem;* brahmāṇaḥ *— stem accent;* śatakrato *— vocative, lowered; the* v *dropped in the Saṃhitā (Pā. 8-3-19);* vaṃśam iva *— no loss of the case ending, first-member accent (Pā. 2-1-4-2);* yemire *— root* yama uparame*, lowered as a finite verb.)*

### Page 382 — Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) शतक्रतो ((he) śatakrato)** — O Indra, who perform many daring deeds, or who are of much wisdom | **त्वाम् (tvām)** — you | **गायत्रिणः (gāyatriṇaḥ)** — the priests called udgātṛ, singers of the Sāman | **गायन्ति (gāyanti)** — praise with Sāma-Veda mantras | **अर्किणः (arkiṇaḥ)** — the priests called hotṛ, who praise with ṛks of the Ṛgveda | **अर्कम् (arkam)** — Indra, worthy of worship or praise | **अर्चन्ति (arcanti)** — extol with the *śastra* mantras | **ब्रह्माणः (brahmāṇaḥ)** — the other brāhmaṇas, headed by Brahmā | **त्वाम् (tvām)** — you | **वंशम् इव (vaṃśam iva)** — like a bamboo | **उत् येमिरे (ut yemire)** — raise aloft (praise specially).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! You do many daring deeds or are of much wisdom. In sacrifices and other rites the priests called udgātṛ praise you by singing Sāmans; the priests called hotṛ, who are worthy to be worshipped with the mantras of their own Veda, the Ṛgveda, praise you; Brahmā and the other brāhmaṇas praise you with hymns and the like, as one raises a bamboo aloft, and so increase your fame.

### Page 383 — Rik 1: English and Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, with many daring deeds or great knowledge, the chanters of the Sama sing about you, the reciters of the Riks praise you who are worthy of praise, and the (priests called) Brahmanas raise you aloft like a bamboo pole.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

This rik is found, besides in this sūkta, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (1-6-12-2), the Sāma-Veda (342; 1344) and the Nirukta (5-5). The sense of this rik, or the matter stated in it, is almost the same as the sense of the first rik of the seventh sūkta. The sense of the first half (that is, the first and second pādas) is clear, but what is said in the third pāda is somewhat strained. Here the sense of the word *brahmāṇaḥ* does not fit well. In the sacrificial rite, the three priest-groups — hotṛ, adhvaryu and udgātṛ — need one priest, called *brahmā*, to see to it that their duties are properly carried out. He must know all three Vedas and the order of performance of the sacrifice. Although he does not take a special part in the actual duties of the rite, he takes care that the sacrifice proceeds properly, and gives permission for the necessary actions of the other priests, so that the sacrifice goes on with all its limbs: he is the supervisor. The Bhāṣyakāra explains the word *brahmāṇaḥ* as the priests of the *brahma* class and the other brāhmaṇas. Or, *brahma* has the sense of "praise (*stotra*)," and so one may give the word *brahmāṇaḥ* the sense "those who praise."

The comparison *vaṃśam iva* in the third pāda is also strained. *Vaṃśa* is a kind of tree: bamboo, reed. The comparison "like raising [or lifting high] a bamboo" is not well fitted. [The meaning:] those who raise you as one raises a bamboo — that is, they praise you and so increase your fame and renown; by singing of your qualities they provide you with a high station: this may be taken as the poet's idea. Or, since *vaṃśa* has another meaning — family, lineage — then "as those who raise their family's honour by right conduct, or raise the esteem of the family by special deeds of daring, so [they raise you]": this is the sense one may give. The Bhāṣyakāra gives both of these senses.

### Page 384 — Rik 1: Special Topics (continued)

**"Gāyatriṇaḥ"** — **गायत्रं साम येषामुद्गातॄणामस्ति ते** (*gāyatraṃ sāma yeṣām udgātṝṇām asti te*) — "those udgātṛs who have the Gāyatra Sāman": those who sing the Sāman called Gāyatra; or, since many of the mantras sung in the Sāma-Veda are Ṛgveda mantras in the Gāyatrī meter, it is the customary usage to call the udgātṛ priests who sing them *gāyatriṇaḥ* — "singers of Gāyatrī-meter ṛks."

**"Arcanti"** — *arca pūjāyām* — the root *arc*: to worship; that is, to praise.

**"Arkam"** — **अर्चन्त्येभिरित्यर्काः मन्त्राः** (*arcanty ebhir ity arkāḥ mantrāḥ*) — "those with which they worship are *arkas*, the mantras": since they are used for praising, mantras are called *arkas*. Here *arkam* means Indra, who is praised by such *arkas* or mantras.

For this rik the sage Yāska has given, in his Nirukta, an explanation in this manner:

> अर्कः ॥ अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चन्ति ॥
> अर्को मन्त्रो भवति यदेनेनार्चन्ति ॥
> अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि ॥
> अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥
> *arkaḥ || arko devo bhavati yad enam arcanti ||*
> *arko mantro bhavati yad anenārcanti ||*
> *arkam annaṃ bhavaty arcati bhūtāni ||*
> *arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā ||*
> *(No reference is printed with this block; the bhāṣya on p. 382 cites it as Ni. 5-4, reading* sa vṛtaḥ*.)*

Four different senses of the word *arka* are stated:

**Devaḥ** — **तावत्सर्व एवार्क इत्युच्यते यत्-यस्मात् एनं-देवम् अर्चन्ति स्तोतारः** (*tāvat sarva evārka ity ucyate yat-yasmāt enaṃ-devam arcanti stotāraḥ*) — "first, every [god] is called *arka*, because (*yat* = *yasmāt*) the praisers worship him (*enam* = the god)" — *arka* is the god; for the worshippers, using this word, say "*arka*" of whom they worship. That is, the deity worshipped by the devotees is called *arka*.

**अर्को मन्त्रो भवति — यत्-यस्मात्, अनेन-मन्त्रेण, अर्चन्ति स्तोतारः तस्मादर्कः** (*arko mantro bhavati — yat-yasmāt, anena-mantreṇa, arcanti stotāraḥ tasmād arkaḥ*) — "*arka* is a mantra, because with it (= the mantra) the praisers worship; therefore *arka*"; those who praise worship the deity with this (the *arka*, or mantra); hence *arka* means "mantra."

**अर्कमन्नं भवति — तद्धि अर्चति भूतानि, यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते, पूज्यं च सर्वस्यैवान्नम्** (*arkam annaṃ bhavati — tad dhi arcati bhūtāni, yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnam api saṃskāra-viśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate, pūjyaṃ ca sarvasyaivānnam*) — "*arka* is food, for it honours (sustains) beings; for whoever is worthy of honour, his food too is prepared with special care and used in worship; and food is honoured by everyone": food (*āhāra*) is necessary to all living beings, and everyone honours and seeks it with respect and love; so *arka* also means food.

**अर्को वृक्षो भवति य एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृत्तः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्ना कटुकभावेन भवति** (*arko vṛkṣo bhavati ya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛttaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimnā kaṭuka-bhāvena bhavati*) — "that well-known tree *arka* [the *Calotropis*, in Kannada *ಎಕ್ಕ*] is covered all round with pungency (*kaṭu*)." The name *arka* for a tree (*vṛkṣa*) is well established, too.

### Page 385 — Rik 1: Special Topics (continued)

*(…"Arka" means *ekka* tree, in Kannada.)* Its twigs are used in the *homa* rites, and it is also well known to all as a herbal medicine; therefore the *arka* tree is a thing known to all. As its sap is acrid, he says *kaṭukimnā* ("by pungency").

As an example to explain the word *arka*, Yāska has quoted this very rik *gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ*, and in it has also given an explanation of the meaning of the word *vaṃśa* in it:

> गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिणः प्रार्चन्ति ते ऽर्कमर्किणो ब्राह्मणास्त्वा शतक्रतो उद्येमिरे वंशमिव वंशो वनशयो भवति वननाच्छ्रूयत इति वा ॥
> *gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ prārcanti te 'rkamarkiṇo brāhmaṇāstvā śatakrato udyemire vaṃśamiva vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vananācchrūyata iti vā ||* (नि. ५-४ — Nirukta 5-4 as printed; the bhāṣya on p. 382 cites it as 5-5)
> *(Yāska's text reads* brāhmaṇās tvā śatakrato *for the Saṃhitā's* brahmāṇas tvā śatakrata*.)*

Durgācārya's commentary on this runs:

> गायन्ति त्वा गायत्रिणः — स्तुवन्ति त्वां सामगाः सामभिः । अर्चन्त्यर्कमर्किणः — पूजयन्ति त्वां ऋग्भिः होतारो मन्त्रिणः । एवमनेन प्रकारेण सर्व एते ब्राह्मणा यज्ञे कर्मणि हे शतक्रतो उद्वंशमिव येमिरे — उद्येमिरे वंशमिव त्वां स्तुतिभिः हविर्भिश्च यज्ञेषु तवैव महिमानं वर्धयन्तीत्यर्थः । वंशो वनशयो भवति वने शयित इवास्ते, वननाच्छ्रूयत इति वा संभजनाद्वा वल्लिभिः ॥ एवमत्र देवः अर्कशब्देनोच्यते मन्त्रस्यार्कशब्दवाच्यत्वे अर्चन्त्यर्कमर्किण इत्येष एव निगमः । अर्किणो हि मन्त्रिण एवाभिप्रेताः । वृक्षस्तु प्रसिद्ध एव । तेन निगमस्तदभिधायको नैवास्ति ॥
> *gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ — stuvanti tvāṃ sāmagāḥ sāmabhiḥ | arcantyarkamarkiṇaḥ — pūjayanti tvāṃ ṛgbhiḥ hotāro mantriṇaḥ | evamanena prakāreṇa sarva ete brāhmaṇā yajñe karmaṇi he śatakrato udvaṃśamiva yemire — udyemire vaṃśamiva tvāṃ stutibhiḥ havirbhiśca yajñeṣu tavaiva mahimānaṃ vardhayantītyarthaḥ | vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vane śayita ivāste, vananācchrūyata iti vā saṃbhajanādvā vallibhiḥ || evamatra devaḥ arkaśabdenocyate mantrasyārkaśabdavācyatve arcantyarkamarkiṇa ityeṣa eva nigamaḥ | arkiṇo hi mantriṇa evābhipretāḥ | vṛkṣastu prasiddha eva | tena nigamastadabhidhāyako naivāsti ||*

— "*Gāyanti tvā gāyatriṇaḥ*: the Sāma-singers praise you with Sāmans. *Arcanty arkam arkiṇaḥ*: the hotṛs, with mantras, worship you with ṛks. In this way all these brāhmaṇas, in the sacrificial rite, O *śatakrato*, *ud yemire* — raise you aloft like a bamboo; with praises and offerings in sacrifices they increase your greatness. A *vaṃśa* is *vanaśaya*, lying in the forest; or, *vananāc chrūyate* — it is heard of because of being enjoyed, or because creepers resort to it. Thus here the god is meant by the word *arka*; for *arka* meaning the mantra, this very passage *arcanty arkam arkiṇaḥ* is the instance, for by *arkiṇaḥ* those who have the mantras are meant; the tree is well known, and so there is no passage naming it."

Here Yāska gives the word *brahmāṇaḥ* the sense *brāhmaṇāḥ*: *brāhmaṇa* means those of the brāhmaṇa caste and also the priests, headed by Brahmā, who take part in sacrifices and the like. For *vaṃśa* he says: *vaṃśo vanaśayo bhavati vananāc chrayata iti vā* — "because it lies in the forest it is called *vaṃśa*; or because, when the wind blows, the bamboos rub against one another and make a sound, it is called *vaṃśa*; or because creepers climb it, it is called *vaṃśa*": so he explains.

**"Arkiṇaḥ"** — **अर्चनहेतुमन्त्रयुक्ताः होतारः । अर्का मन्त्रा एषां सन्तीत्यर्किणः होतारः** (*arcana-hetu-mantra-yuktāḥ hotāraḥ | arkā mantrā eṣāṃ santīty arkiṇaḥ hotāraḥ*) — "the hotṛs, equipped with the mantras that are the means of worship; those who have *arka* mantras are *arkiṇaḥ*, the hotṛs." Since *arka* has the sense "mantra," those who praise with them are called *arkiṇaḥ* — that is, the priests of the hotṛ group who recite the ṛks in the form of *śastra*.

**"Brahmāṇaḥ"** — the Bhāṣyakāra gives this word the sense of priests headed by Brahmā, and other brāhmaṇas. Yāska gives it a general sense, "brāhmaṇas."

**"Śatakrato"** — the explanation of this word was already given earlier.

**"Vaṃśam iva"** — the explanation of this word is also in Yāska's exposition above.

### Page 386 — Rik 1: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 386–387, noted briefly)*

**गायन्ति (*gāyanti*)** — root *gai śabde* with *laṭ* parasmaipada third plural *jhi*; *jh* → *ant* by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-3); *śap*; since the suffix is *śit*, "ād eca upadeśe 'śiti" (Pā. 6-1-45) does not give *ā* for the *ai*; "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78) gives *āy*, so *gāyanti*; *śap* is *pit*, hence unaccented; the ending *anti*, a *lasārvadhātuka*, follows *śap*, an *adupadeśa*, and so is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. 6-1-186); the *ā* of *gā* takes the root accent, udātta. **गायत्रिणः (*gāyatriṇaḥ*)** — *gāyatra* is the name of a Sāman; "gāyatraṃ sāma yeṣām udgātṝṇām asti te" ("those udgātṛs who have the Gāyatra Sāman") — in the compound analysis *ini* by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); *a* of *gāyatra* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); nominative plural *gāyatriṇaḥ*; the *i* is udātta by the suffix. **अर्चन्ति (*arcanti*)** — root *arca pūjāyām* (bhvādi class); *śap* is *pit*, so unaccented; the *anti* is unaccented as a *lasārvadhātuka* following the *adupadeśa* *śap*; the root accent stands; since the word stands at the beginning of the pāda there is no lowering of the verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **अर्कम् (*arkam*)** — "arcanty ebhiḥ iti arkāḥ, mantrāḥ" ("the mantras with which they worship"); Indra, worshipped with them, is by implication also called *arka*; from *arc* with *gha* by "puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇa" (Pā. 3-3-118), in the sense of instrument or location, in a masculine name; *gha* is *ghit* (its *gh* is *it*), so by "cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-52) the *c* takes the *k*-class before a *ghit* or *ṇyat* suffix, giving *arka*; final-udātta by the suffix accent. **अर्किणः (*arkiṇaḥ*)** — "arkāḥ mantrāḥ eṣāṃ santi" — "the hotṛs": the *ini* suffix by "ata ini-ṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); although *arka* is a *kṛdanta*, and the Mahābhāṣya's "ekākṣarāt kṛto jāteḥ saptamyāṃ ca na tau smṛtau" (pā. ma. 5-2-115-1) says that *ini* and *ṭhan* do not come after a one-syllable word, a *kṛdanta*, a word for a class, or in the locative sense, *ini* arises here by Vedic inversion (continued on p. 387); the *i* is udātta by the suffix.

### Page 387 — Rik 1 grammar closes; Rik 2

**ब्रह्माणः (*brahmāṇaḥ*)** — final-udātta by the stem accent. **शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)** — unaccented as a vocative by "āmantritasya ca" (8-1-19); in the Saṃhitā, with *u* before a vowel, the *o* → *av* by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78), then the *v* is lost by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19); and since this loss is treated as not having taken place (*pūrvatrāsiddham*, Pā. 8-2-1), the *guṇa* of "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-87) does not occur. **वंशमिव (*vaṃśam iva*)** — *vaṃśa* is final-udātta by the stem accent; with *iva* it becomes a compound and the case-ending is dropped, the first member's accent staying ("ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ ca," Pā. 2-1-4). **येमिरे (*yemire*)** — root *yamu uparame* ("to restrain; to hold up") with *liṭ* ātmanepada third plural *jha*; *jha* → *irec* by "liṭas tajhayor eśirec" (3-4-81, printed "pā. sada." [sic]); doubling by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-8); by "ata ekahalmadhye 'nādeśāder liṭi" (Pā. "6-4-1-20" as printed, i.e. 6-4-120), before a *kit* *liṭ* the short *a* between single consonants of a root whose initial is not changed in reduplication takes *e*, with loss of the reduplicate; so *yemire*; although the root *yam* is parasmaipadī in the bhvādi class, here it is ātmanepada by Vedic inversion; wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).
