### Page 388 — Rik 2: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> यद्यदा सानोः सानुमारुहत् यजमानः सोमवल्लीसमिदाद्याहरणायैकस्मात्पर्वतभागादपरं पर्वतभागमारूढवान् । तथा भूरि प्रभूतं कर्त्वं कर्म सोमयागरूपमस्पष्ट स्पृष्टवान् । उपक्रान्तवानित्यर्थः । तत्तदानीमिन्द्रो ऽर्थं यजमानस्य प्रयोजनं चेतति । जानाति । ज्ञात्वा च वृष्णिः कामानां वर्षिता सन् यूथेन मरुद्गणेन सहैजति । कम्पते । स्वस्थानाद्यज्ञभूमिमागन्तुमुद्युक्त इत्यर्थः ॥ सानोः । षणु दाने । सनोति ददाति निवसतामवकाशमिति सानुः । दृसनिजनिचरिचटिरहिभ्यो ञुण् । उ. १-३ । णित्त्वादुपधाया वृद्धिः । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं च । अरुहत् । रुहेर्लुङि तिपि शपि संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः । परि ९३-१ । इति लघूपधगुणो न भवति । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्तः । सति शिष्टत्वात्स एव शिष्यते । निपातैर्यद्यदिहन्तेति । पा. ८-१-३० । निषेधान्निघातो न भवति । भूरि । अदिशदिभूशुभिभ्यः क्रिन् । उ. ४-६५ । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अस्पष्ट । स्पश बाधनस्पर्शनयोः । स्वरितञित इत्यात्मनेपदम् । लङः प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनं त । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । व्रश्चादिषत्वष्टुत्वे । पा. ८-२-३६ ; ८-४-४१ । लुङ्लङ्लृङ्क्ष्वडुदात्त इत्यडागम उदात्तः । स एव शिष्यते । अनुषङ्गेण यच्छब्दयोगान्निघाताभावः । कर्त्वम् । डुकृञ् करणे । अन्येभ्यो ऽपि दृश्यन्ते । पा. ३-२-७५ । इति विच् । गुणो रपरत्वम् । विचः सर्वापहारी लोपः । करो भावः कर्त्वम् । अर्थम् । अर्तेरुषिकुषिगार्तिभ्यस्थन् । उ. २-४ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । यूथेन । तिथपृष्ठगूथयूथप्रोथाः । उ. २-१२ । इति थक्प्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । वृष्णिः । निरित्यनुवृत्तौ सृवृषिभ्यां कित् । उ. ४-४९ । इति निप्रत्ययान्तः । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । एजति । एजृ कम्पने । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥
>
> *yadyadā sānoḥ sānumāruhat yajamānaḥ somavallīsamidādyāharaṇāyaikasmātparvatabhāgādaparaṃ parvatabhāgamārūḍhavān | tathā bhūri prabhūtaṃ kartvaṃ karma somayāgarūpamaspaṣṭa spṛṣṭavān | upakrāntavānityarthaḥ | tattadānīmindro 'rthaṃ yajamānasya prayojanaṃ cetati | jānāti | jñātvā ca vṛṣṇiḥ kāmānāṃ varṣitā san yūthena marudgaṇena sahaijati | kampate | svasthānādyajñabhūmimāgantumudyukta ityarthaḥ || sānoḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | sanoti dadāti nivasatāmavakāśamiti sānuḥ | dṛsanijanicaricaṭirahibhyo ñuṇ | u. 1-3 | ṇittvādupadhāyā vṛddhiḥ | ñittvādādyudāttatvaṃ ca | aruhat | ruherluṅi tipi śapi saṃjñāpūrvako vidhiranityaḥ | pari 93-1 | iti laghūpadhaguṇo na bhavati | luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣvaḍudāttaḥ | sati śiṣṭatvātsa eva śiṣyate | nipātairyadyadihanteti | pā. 8-1-30 | niṣedhānnighāto na bhavati | bhūri | adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin | u. 4-65 | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | aspaṣṭa | spaśa bādhanasparśanayoḥ | svaritañita ityātmanepadam | laṅaḥ prathamapuruṣaikavacanaṃ ta | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | vraścādiṣatvaṣṭutve | pā. 8-2-36 ; 8-4-41 | luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣvaḍudātta ityaḍāgama udāttaḥ | sa eva śiṣyate | anuṣaṅgeṇa yacchabdayogānnighātābhāvaḥ | kartvam | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante | pā. 3-2-75 | iti vic | guṇo raparatvam | vicaḥ sarvāpahārī lopaḥ | karo bhāvaḥ kartvam | artham | arteruṣikuṣigārtibhyasthan | u. 2-4 | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | yūthena | tithapṛṣṭhagūthayūthaprothāḥ | u. 2-12 | iti thakpratyayānto nipātitaḥ | vṛṣṇiḥ | nirityanuvṛttau sṛvṛṣibhyāṃ kit | u. 4-49 | iti nipratyayāntaḥ | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | ejati | ejṛ kampane | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "*Yad* — when — the sacrificer *sānoḥ sānum āruhat*: in order to fetch Soma-creepers, fuel-sticks and the like, climbs from one part of the mountain to another part. And *bhūri* — a great — *kartvam*, a work (*karma*) in the form of a Soma-sacrifice, *aspaṣṭa* — has touched: has begun. *Tat* — then — Indra *artham cetati*: knows the sacrificer's purpose. Having known it, being *vṛṣṇiḥ*, the showerer of desires, he *ejati* — stirs, is set in motion — *yūthena*, together with the troop of Maruts: he is ready to come from his own place to the sacrificial ground." *(Grammar, noted briefly:* sānoḥ *— root* ṣaṇu dāne*, "that which gives room to those who dwell", suffix* ñuṇ *(Uṇ. 1-3), vṛddhi, initial-udātta;* aruhat *— luṅ of* ruh*, no guṇa since the rule is not obligatory (paribhāṣā 93-1); the augment* aṭ *udātta, not lowered after* yat *(Pā. 8-1-30);* bhūri *— suffix* krin *(Uṇ. 4-65), initial-udātta;* aspaṣṭa *— root* spaśa *, ātmanepada, laṅ third singular, śap dropped,* ṣ *and* ṭ *by Pā. 8-2-36 and 8-4-41, the augment udātta;* kartvam *— root* ḍukṛñ *with* vic *(Pā. 3-2-75), "the doing";* artham *— suffix* than *(Uṇ. 2-4);* yūthena *— an irregular* thak *formation (Uṇ. 2-12);* vṛṣṇiḥ *— suffix* ni*, kit (Uṇ. 4-49), final-udātta;* ejati *— root* ejṛ kampane*, lowered as a finite verb.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**यत् (yat)** — when | *(the sacrificer, to fetch the Soma-creeper and the fuel-sticks)* **सानोः (sānoḥ)** — from one mountain-top | **सानुम् (sānum)** — to another peak | **आ अरुहत् (ā aruhat)** — climbs | *(and)* **भूरि (bhūri)** — a great | **कर्त्वम् (kartvam)** — *(Soma-sacrificial)* work | **अस्पष्ट (aspaṣṭa)** — has begun | **तत् (tat)** — then | **इन्द्रः (indraḥ)** — Indra | **अर्थम् (artham)** — the sacrificer's wish | **चेतति (cetati)** — knows | *(after knowing)* **वृष्णिः (vṛṣṇiḥ)** — Indra, the granter of desires, the giver of rain | **यूथेन (yūthena)** — together with the troop of Maruts | **एजति (ejati)** — leaves (that is, leaving his own dwelling, sets out to come near the sacrificer).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The sacrificer goes to the mountain, and there climbs from one peak to another, to bring the Soma-creeper that has grown on the hills and the fuel-sticks required for the sacrifice; thereby he begins the sacrifice. Indra, knowing this, since he grants the desired ends of the sacrificer, sets out from his own place for the sacrificial ground, together with his friendly troop of Maruts.

### Page 389 — Rik 2: English and Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> When Indra the showerer of blessings knows the object of the worshipper who has wandered from one ridge of the mountain to the other in quest of soma plant and who has just begun the sacrifice, he (Indra) approaches the sacrificial place with the troop of (Maruts).

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

To give the sense of this rik, many words have to be supplied. **"Sānoḥ sānum āruhat"** — "climbs from one peak [or table-land] of the mountain to another": that is, the question of "who climbs?" and "why?" arises. To fit the sense, the Bhāṣyakāra supplies the words "the sacrificer — for fetching the Soma-creeper, fuel-sticks and the other means of sacrifice." And since the word *yūtha* means a herd, a group, the word "Maruts" is supplied: "the troop (*gaṇa*) of Maruts." The word *vṛṣṇi* means *varṣitā*, "giver of rain": though "he comes with the Maruts who are helpers for rain" would fit, the Bhāṣyakāra explains *vṛṣṇi* as *kāmānāṃ varṣitā* — "the one who rains desired ends," and so a doubt arises as to whether the help of the Maruts is necessary for giving desired things other than rain. Hence it is doubtful whether *yūthena* in this rik is the poet's intended "with the troop of Maruts." **Veṅkaṭamādhava** gives the sense *vasusamūhena* — "with the assembly of the Vasus"; so it seems more fitting to say "with the assembly of the gods."

**"Yat," "tat"** — here these words are not the relative-demonstrative words *yad* and *tad* in any case or number; they are indeclinables. For them the sense *yadā*, "when," and *tadā*, "then," must be given.

**"Sānoḥ, sānum"** — the mountain-peak or the table-land of the hill. Since the Soma-creeper grows especially in the hill regions, and since the creeper growing in the high regions of the hills gives a more abundant and better juice than the creeper that grows on the level ground, it was then the custom to go to the higher hills, often, to bring the Soma-creeper. This matter is mentioned in many places in the Ṛgveda.

### Page 390 — Rik 2: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Aspaṣṭa"** — *spaśa bādhana-sparśanayoḥ* — "has touched"; that is, "has begun."

**"Kartvam"** — *karma*, "work." Among the twenty-six words for "work" beginning with *apaḥ* and *apnaḥ*, the word *kartvam* is read (Ni. 3-2).

**"Vṛṣṇiḥ"** — **कामानां वर्षिता अथवा वर्षिता** (*kāmānāṃ varṣitā athavā varṣitā*) — "the showerer of desires, or the giver of rain." The word *vṛṣṇi* is used in many places in the Ṛgveda, in passages describing Indra's qualities.

**"Ejati"** — *ejṛ kampane* — the root *ej*, to tremble, to move. Here "moves" means "sets out from his own place to come to the sacrificer's side."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 390–391, noted briefly)*

**सानोः (*sānoḥ*)** — root *ṣaṇu dāne* ("to give"): *sanoti dadāti nivasatām avakāśam iti sānuḥ* ("that which gives room to those who dwell") — *ñuṇ* suffix by "dṛsanijanicaricaṭirahibhyo ñuṇ" (Uṇ. 1-3), after *dṛ vidāraṇe*, *ṣaṇu dāne*, *jana janane*, *cara gatau*, *caṭa bhedane*, *raha tyāge*; *ṣ* → *s* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 6-1-64), and with the *ṣ* gone the *ṇ* it caused goes too; "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. 7-2-116) gives the *vṛddhi*; the suffix is *ñit*, so initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). **आरुहत् (*āruhat*)** — root *ruha bījajanmani prādurbhāve ca* with *laṅ*, third singular *tip*; *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68); since "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" (paribhāṣā 93-1), the *laghūpadha-guṇa* of "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86) does not apply; the *i* of *tip* is dropped by "itaś ca" (Pā. 3-4-100); the *aṭ* augment is udātta by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71), and being taught later (*satiśiṣṭa*) it alone stands; "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) would make the verb unaccented, but because *yat* ("when"), *yadi*, *hanta*, *kuvit*, *neta*, *cet*, *caṇ*, *kaccit*, *yatra* and other particles occur, the lowering is prohibited by "nipātair yadyadihantakuvinnetcetcaṇkaccidyatrayuktam" (Pā. 8-1-30); so the verb stays accented. **भूरि (*bhūri*)** — "adiśadibhūśubhibhyaḥ krin" (Uṇ. 4-505 [as printed]; the bhāṣya prints 4-65): after the roots *ada bhakṣaṇe*, *śadḷ śātane*, *bhū sattāyām*, *śubha śumbha śobhārthe* the suffix *krin*; *kit*, so by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5) the *guṇa* of "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) does not apply; the suffix is *nit*, so initial-udātta. **अस्पष्ट (*aspaṣṭa*)** — root *spaśa bādhana-sparśanayoḥ* ("to touch"), anudātta-*it* by the marker *iṅ*-like; it is *svarita*-marked, so the *ātmanepada* by "svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyāphale" (1-3-72, printed "sā. sū." [sic]); *laṅ*, third singular *ta*; *śap* dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); *ś* → *ṣ* by "vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājachaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-36) and *ṭ* by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41); the *aṭ* augment is udātta by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71) and its accent stands; the word *yat* carried over from the first half brings the prohibition of lowering by "nipātair yadyadi…" (Pā. 8-1-30). **कर्त्वम् (*kartvam*)** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe* with *vic* ("anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante," Pā. 3-2-75); *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) with *raparatva* by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51); all the letters of *vic* drop, giving *kar*; in the sense *karor bhāvaḥ* ("the doing"), *tva* by "tasya bhāvas tvatalau" (Pā. 5-1-119), giving *kartvam*. **अर्थम् (*artham*)** — root *ṛ gatau* with *than* ("uṣikuṣigārtibhyas than," printed "pā. sū. 2-161" [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives Uṇ. 2-4), after *uṣa dāhe*, *kuṣa niṣkarṣe*, *gai śabde* and *ṛ gatau*; *guṇa* and *raparatva*; initial-udātta (*nit*). **यूथेन (*yūthena*)** — "tithapṛṣṭhagūthayūthaprothāḥ" (printed "pā. sū. 2-169" [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives Uṇ. 2-12): an irregular formation with *thak*. **वृष्णिः (*vṛṣṇiḥ*)** — "sṛvṛṣibhyāṃ kit" (Uṇ. 4-486 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 4-49) after *sṛ* (to go) and *vṛṣu secane*, the suffix *ni*; *kit*, so no *guṇa*; final-udātta by the suffix. **एजति (*ejati*)** — root *ejṛ kampane*; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

**॥२॥**

### Page 392 — Sūkta 10, Rik 3

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> यु॒क्ष्वा हि के॒शिना॒ ह॒री वृष॑णा कक्ष्यप्रा ।
> अथा॑ न इन्द्र सोमपा गि॒रामु॒प॑श्रुतिं चर ॥३॥
>
> *yukṣvā́ hi keśínā harī́ vṛ́ṣaṇā kakṣyaprā |*
> *áthā na indra somapā girā́m upaśrutiṃ cara ||3||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> युक्ष्व । हि । केशिना । हरी इति । वृषणा । कक्ष्यऽप्रा ॥
> अथ । नः । इन्द्र । सोमऽपाः । गिराम् । उपऽश्रुतिम् । चर ॥३॥
>
> *yukṣva | hi | keśinā | harī iti | vṛṣaṇā | kakṣya-prā ||*
> *atha | naḥ | indra | soma-pāḥ | girām | upa-śrutim | cara ||3||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे सोमपाः सोमपानयुक्तेन्द्र हरी त्वदीयावश्वौ युक्ष्वा हि । सर्वथा संयोजय । अथानन्तरं नो ऽस्मदीयानां गिरां स्तुतीनामुपश्रुतिं समीपे श्रवणमुद्दिश्य चर । तत्प्रदेशं गच्छ । कीदृशौ हरी । केशिना स्कन्धप्रदेशे लम्बमानकेशयुक्तौ वृषणा सेचनसमर्थौ युवानौ कक्ष्यप्रा । अश्वस्योदरबन्धनरज्जुः कक्ष्या तस्याः पूरकौ । पुष्टाङ्गावित्यर्थः ॥ युक्ष्व । श्नमो लोपश्छान्दसः । सति शिष्टत्वेन प्रत्ययस्वरः शिष्यते । द्व्यचो ऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् । केशिना । प्रशस्ताः केशा अनयोः सन्तीति मत्वर्थीय इनिः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना द्विवचनस्याकारादेशः । वृषणा । पृषु वृषु मृषु सेचने । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. १-१५६ । इति कनिन् । ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तः । वा षपूर्वस्य निगमे । पा. ६-४-९ । इत्युपधायाः पक्षे दीर्घाभावः । पूर्ववदाकारः । कक्ष्यप्रा । कक्ष्ययोर्भवं कक्ष्यं सूत्रम् । तत्प्रातः पूरयतः पुष्टत्वादिति कक्ष्यप्रौ । प्रा पूरणे । आतो ऽनुपसर्गे कः । पा. ३-२-३ । इति कप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वम् । आकारः पूर्ववत् । अथ । निपातस्येति संहितायां दीर्घः । नः । अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादावित्यनुवृत्तौ बहुवचनस्य वस्नसौ । पा. ८-१-२१ । इति नसादेशो ऽनुदात्तः । इन्द्र सोमपा । उभावामन्त्रितस्य चेति सर्वानुदात्तौ । गिराम् । सावेकाचस्तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिरिति विभक्तिरुदात्ता । उपशब्दो निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । श्रुतिशब्देन प्रादिसमासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते तादौ च निति कृत्यतौ । पा. ६-२-५० । इति तुवर्जिततादिपरत्वाद्गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरः । चर । निघातः ॥
>
> *he somapāḥ somapānayuktendra harī tvadīyāvaśvau yukṣvā hi | sarvathā saṃyojaya | athānantaraṃ no 'smadīyānāṃ girāṃ stutīnāmupaśrutiṃ samīpe śravaṇamuddiśya cara | tatpradeśaṃ gaccha | kīdṛśau harī | keśinā skandhapradeśe lambamānakeśayuktau vṛṣaṇā secanasamarthau yuvānau kakṣyaprā | aśvasyodarabandhanarajjuḥ kakṣyā tasyāḥ pūrakau | puṣṭāṅgāvityarthaḥ || yukṣva | śnamo lopaśchāndasaḥ | sati śiṣṭatvena pratyayasvaraḥ śiṣyate | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam | keśinā | praśastāḥ keśā anayoḥ santīti matvarthīya iniḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | supāṃ sulugityādinā dvivacanasyākārādeśaḥ | vṛṣaṇā | pṛṣu vṛṣu mṛṣu secane | kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ | u. 1-156 | iti kanin | ñnityādirnityamityādyudāttaḥ | vā ṣapūrvasya nigame | pā. 6-4-9 | ityupadhāyāḥ pakṣe dīrghābhāvaḥ | pūrvavadākāraḥ | kakṣyaprā | kakṣyayorbhavaṃ kakṣyaṃ sūtram | tatprātaḥ pūrayataḥ puṣṭatvāditi kakṣyaprau | prā pūraṇe | āto 'nupasarge kaḥ | pā. 3-2-3 | iti kapratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvareṇāntodāttatvam | ākāraḥ pūrvavat | atha | nipātasyeti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | naḥ | anudāttaṃ sarvamapādādāvityanuvṛttau bahuvacanasya vasnasau | pā. 8-1-21 | iti nasādeśo 'nudāttaḥ | indra somapā | ubhāvāmantritasya ceti sarvānudāttau | girām | sāvekācastṛtīyādirvibhaktiriti vibhaktirudāttā | upaśabdo nipātatvādādyudāttaḥ | śrutiśabdena prādisamāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte tādau ca niti kṛtyatau | pā. 6-2-50 | iti tuvarjitatādiparatvādgateḥ prakṛtisvaraḥ | cara | nighātaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O *somapāḥ* — O Indra, drinker of Soma! *Harī* — your two horses (*tvadīyāv aśvau*) — *yukṣvā hi*: yoke [them] fully. *Athā* — thereafter — *cara*: go to the place, with a view to *upaśruti* — listening near at hand — of *naḥ girām*, our praises. What kind of two horses? *Keśinā* — having manes hanging down on the shoulder region; *vṛṣaṇā* — able to sprinkle (to rain), young; *kakṣyaprā* — *kakṣyā* is the rope that binds the horse's belly; they are *prā*, 'fillers' of it: that is, of well-nourished (full) bodies." *(Grammar noted briefly:* yukṣva *— the loss of* śnam *is Vedic, the suffix accent stands, and the final is lengthened in the Saṃhitā ("dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ");* keśinā *— "having handsome manes," with* ini*;* vṛṣaṇā *— root* vṛṣu secane *with* kanin *(Uṇ. 1-156), initial-udātta; optionally no lengthening (Pā. 6-4-9); dual in* ā *by "supāṃ suluk…";* kakṣyaprā *— "those who fill the* kakṣya *(the girth-cord) because they are well fed," root* prā pūraṇe *with* ka *(Pā. 3-2-3), final-udātta by the second-member rule;* athā *— the particle lengthened in the Saṃhitā;* naḥ *— substitute* nas *for* asmān/asmākam *(Pā. 8-1-21), unaccented;* indra, somapā *— vocatives, both unaccented;* girām *— case-ending udātta;* upaśrutim *— the prefix* upa *is initial-udātta as a particle, and by "tādau ca niti kṛty atau" (Pā. 6-2-50) the prefix keeps its accent;* cara *— unaccented.)

### Page 393 — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**सोमपाः (somapāḥ)** — O Indra who drink Soma (so absorbed in it) | **केशिना (keśinā)** — having manes (the long hair that grows upright on the neck) | **वृषणा (vṛṣaṇā)** — able to sprinkle, that is, in the prime of youth | **कक्ष्यप्रा (kakṣyaprā)** — with fully nourished bodies, such that the girth-rope tied about the belly is filled out | **हरी (harī)** — your two horses | **युक्ष्व हि (yukṣva hi)** — yoke [them to the chariot] | **अथ (atha)** — then | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **गिराम् (girām)** — of the words in the form of praise | **उपश्रुतिम् (upaśrutim)** — to hear them (for hearing) near at hand | **चर (cara)** — come.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra, absorbed in drinking Soma! Your horses have manes — long hair grown upright on the neck — are youthful, and have bodies so well nourished that the girth-rope tied about the belly is filled out. Yoke such horses to your chariot, and then come to us to hear, near at hand, our words of praise.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra, drinker of soma, harness your pair of long-maned youthful and well-conditioned horses and then come to hear our praises.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Yukṣvā"** — for the convenience of the meter the final vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha. The word means "join, yoke to the chariot."

**"Keśinā"** — **स्कन्धप्रदेशे लम्बमानकेशयुक्तौ** (*skandha-pradeśe lambamāna-keśa-yuktau*) — "furnished with manes hanging in the region of the shoulder": *pralamba-keśarau*, i.e., with manes grown up on the neck, *long-maned*.

**"Vṛṣaṇā"** — **रेतःसेचनसमर्थौ** (*retaḥ-secana-samarthau*) — "able to impregnate": that is, in the prime of life, in youth.

**"Kakṣyaprā"** — **कक्ष्यप्रा अश्वस्योदरबन्धनरज्जुः कक्ष्या । तस्याः पूरकौ । पुष्टाङ्गावित्यर्थः** (*kakṣyaprā aśvasyodara-bandhana-rajjuḥ kakṣyā | tasyāḥ pūrakau | puṣṭāṅgāv ity arthaḥ*) — "*kakṣyā* is the rope that binds the belly of the horse: the two are 'fillers' of it: well-nourished in body." *Kakṣyā* is the girth tied round the belly when a horse is yoked to a chariot; horses whose bellies have grown stout (*filling out their girth*) are meant.

**"Somapāḥ"** — **सोमस्य पाता** (*somasya pātā*), "drinker of Soma"; this is a vocative singular, an epithet of the word *indra*.

### Page 394 — Rik 3: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Girām"** — *gīḥ* is the genitive plural. The use of words like *gīḥ*, *girām*, *gīrbhiḥ* in the senses of hymns, praises and eulogies is customary in the Ṛgveda. So *naḥ girām* means "of the hymns that we make."

**"Upaśrutim"** — **समीपे श्रवणमुद्दिश्य । श्रुतेः समीपम्** (*samīpe śravaṇam uddiśya | śruteḥ samīpam*) — "with a view to hearing near at hand": for the sake of hearing, [coming] near, standing near to hear.

**"Cara"** — "come": be the one who comes.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 394–395, noted briefly)*

**युक्ष्व (*yukṣva*)** — root *yujir yoge* ("to join"), ubhayapadī, with *loṭ* ātmanepada middle-second singular *thās*; *thās* → *se* by "thāsaḥ se" (Pā. 3-4-80); "savābhyāṃ vāmau" (Pā. 3-4-91) replaces *e* by *va*; *yuj* + *sva*; the vikaraṇa *śnam* is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73) — the source notes that this sūtra prescribes *luk* for *śap*, but in Ṛ. Saṃ. Aṣṭaka 1, Sūkta 9, mantra 1 (the word *matsi*) the Bhāṣyakāra gives the same *luk* for *śyan* by this sūtra, so the *luk* of *śnam* may be said here too, by the word *bahula*; *j* → *g* by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30), *g* → *k* by "khari ca" (Pā. 8-4-55), and *s* → *ṣ* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59), giving *yukṣva*; the suffix accent stands, being taught later (*satiśiṣṭa*); in the Saṃhitā the final is lengthened by "dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-135). **केशिना (*keśinā*)** — "praśastāḥ keśā anayor santi": *ini* in the possessive sense by "ata iniṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); the *a* of *keśa* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (6-4-148); suffix accent; the accusative dual ending *au* replaced by *ā* by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39). **वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)** — root *pṛṣu, vṛṣu, mṛṣu secane*; *kanin* by "kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. 1-154 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 1-156); "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197) gives initial-udātta; "vā ṣapūrvasya nigame" (Pā. 6-4-9): the lengthening of the penultimate vowel before the *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix is optional after *ṣ*, and so does not arise here; the accusative dual ending → *ā* by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39). **कक्ष्यप्रा (*kakṣyaprā*)** — *kakṣyayor bhavaṃ kakṣyam* (that which is in the *kakṣyā*): the girth; "that which fills it" — root *prā pūraṇe* with *ka* ("āto 'nupasarge kaḥ," Pā. 3-2-3); *ā* dropped before *ka* by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (printed "6-2-139" [as printed], the number of the next sūtra; usually 6-4-64); final-udātta by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139); the dual ending as above. **अथ (*atha*)** — the particle is lengthened in the Saṃhitā (*athā*) by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. 6-3-136). **नः (*naḥ*)** — the rule "bahuvacanasya vasnasau" (Pā. 8-1-21) with the carried-over "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (Pā. 8-1-18): *nas* replaces the plural genitive of *asmad*, unaccented, since the word is not at the beginning of the pāda. **इन्द्र, सोमपाः (*indra, somapāḥ*)** — both are vocatives, wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). **गिराम् (*girām*)** — "sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168) — the case-ending is udātta. **उप (*upa*)** — a *nipāta*, initial-udātta (Phiṭ-sūtra 80); with *śruti* it forms a *prādi*-compound ("kugatiprādayaḥ," Pā. 2-2-18); the rule "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) would give the second member's accent, but by "tādau ca niti kṛty atau" (6-2-50) — before a *kṛt* suffix beginning with *t* (other than *tu*) the preceding *gati* keeps its own accent — *upa* retains its natural accent. **चर (*cara*)** — wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).

**॥३॥**

### Page 396 — Sūkta 10, Rik 4

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> विशेषविनियोगस्तु यत्र श्रौतो न सूत्रितः । स्मार्तं तत्र विजानीयादृग्विधानादिसूत्रतः ॥ एहि स्तोमानित्येषा सूत्रे विशेषाकारेण न विनियुक्ता । साधारणविनियोगस्तु ब्रह्मयज्ञादौ सर्वत्रानुसंधेयः ॥
>
> *viśeṣaviniyogastu yatra śrauto na sūtritaḥ | smārtaṃ tatra vijānīyādṛgvidhānādisūtrataḥ || ehi stomānityeṣā sūtre viśeṣākāreṇa na viniyuktā | sādhāraṇaviniyogastu brahmayajñādau sarvatrānusaṃdheyaḥ ||*
>
> हे वसो निवासकारणभूतेन्द्र एहि । अस्मिन्कर्मण्यागच्छ । आगत्य च स्तोमानुद्गातृप्रयुक्तानि स्तोत्राण्यभि स्वर । अभिलक्ष्य प्रशंसारूपं शब्दं कुरु । तथाध्वर्युमभिलक्ष्य गृणीहि । शब्दं कुरु । तथा होतृप्रयुक्तानि शस्त्राण्यालक्ष्य रुव । शब्दं कुरु । परितोषेण सर्वानृत्विजः प्रशंसेत्यर्थः । तत ऊर्ध्वं नो ऽस्माकं ब्रह्म चान्नं च यज्ञं चानुष्ठीयमानं कर्म च सचा सह वर्धय । सांगत्वसंपादनेन यज्ञं वर्धयित्वा तत्फलमन्नं च प्रवृद्धं कुरु । अन्ध इत्यादिष्वष्टाविंशत्यन्ननामसु ब्रह्म वर्ज इति पठितम् ॥ इहि । इण् गतौ । सेर्हिः । हेरपित्त्वेन ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । निघातः । आङा सह गुण एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । स्तोमान् । अर्तिस्तुसु इत्यादिना मन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । उत्तरपदेन संहितायां नकारस्य दीर्घादटि समानपादे इति रुत्वम् । आतो ऽटि नित्यमित्याकारस्यानुनासिकः । भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य यो ऽशीति यत्वम् । तस्य लोपः शाकल्यस्येति लोपः । तस्यासिद्धत्वात्स्वरसन्धिर्न भवति । अभि । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तोदात्तः । स्वर । स्वृ शब्दोपतापयोः । निघातः । अभि । गतम् । गृणीहि । गॄ शब्दे । सेर्ह्यपिच्चेति हिः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । ई हल्यघोः । पा. ६-४-११३ । इतीत्त्वम् । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः । पा. ७-३-८० । इत्यृकारस्य ऋकारः । ऋवर्णाच्चेति वक्तव्यम् । का. ८-४-१-१ । इति णत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । रुव । रु शब्दे । सेर्ह्यपिच्च । शपि प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेन शः । तस्य ङित्त्वेन गुणाभावादुवङादेशः । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । ब्रह्म । तृहि वृहि वृद्धौ । मनिन्नित्यनुवृत्तौ वृंहेरम् न लोपश्च । उ. ४-१४५ । इति मनिन् । तत्संनियोगेन नलोपः । अमागमश्च । मिदचो ऽन्त्यात्परः । पा. १-१-४७ । इत्यृकारात्परः । यणादेशः । मनिनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । वसो । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । यज्ञम् । यजयाचेत्यादिना । पा. ३-३-९० । नङ् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । वर्धय । निघातः । अत्र चकारद्वयश्रवणादियमेव तिङ्विभक्तिः पूर्ववाक्ये ऽप्यनुषज्यते । अतो ऽनुषक्तैव प्रथमा न श्रुतेत्यश्रुतायाश्च वायोगे प्रथमा । पा. ८-१-५९ । इति निघातनिषेधो न भवति ॥
>
> *he vaso nivāsakāraṇabhūtendra ehi | asminkarmaṇyāgaccha | āgatya ca stomānudgātṛprayuktāni stotrāṇyabhi svara | abhilakṣya praśaṃsārūpaṃ śabdaṃ kuru | tathādhvaryumabhilakṣya gṛṇīhi | śabdaṃ kuru | tathā hotṛprayuktāni śastrāṇyālakṣya ruva | śabdaṃ kuru | paritoṣeṇa sarvānṛtvijaḥ praśaṃsetyarthaḥ | tata ūrdhvaṃ no 'smākaṃ brahma cānnaṃ ca yajñaṃ cānuṣṭhīyamānaṃ karma ca sacā saha vardhaya | sāṃgatvasaṃpādanena yajñaṃ vardhayitvā tatphalamannaṃ ca pravṛddhaṃ kuru | andha ityādiṣvaṣṭāviṃśatyannanāmasu brahma varja iti paṭhitam || ihi | iṇ gatau | serhiḥ | herapittvena ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nighātaḥ | āṅā saha guṇa ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttaḥ | stomān | artistusu ityādinā man | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | uttarapadena saṃhitāyāṃ nakārasya dīrghādaṭi samānapāde iti rutvam | āto 'ṭi nityamityākārasyānunāsikaḥ | bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śīti yatvam | tasya lopaḥ śākalyasyeti lopaḥ | tasyāsiddhatvātsvarasandhirna bhavati | abhi | evamādīnāmanta ityantodāttaḥ | svara | svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ | nighātaḥ | abhi | gatam | gṛṇīhi | gṝ śabde | serhyapicceti hiḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | ī halyaghoḥ | pā. 6-4-113 | itīttvam | pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ | pā. 7-3-80 | ityṛkārasya ṛkāraḥ | ṛvarṇācceti vaktavyam | kā. 8-4-1-1 | iti ṇatvam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | ruva | ru śabde | serhyapicca | śapi prāpte vyatyayena śaḥ | tasya ṅittvena guṇābhāvāduvaṅādeśaḥ | ato heriti herluk | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | brahma | tṛhi vṛhi vṛddhau | maninnityanuvṛttau vṛṃheram na lopaśca | u. 4-145 | iti manin | tatsaṃniyogena nalopaḥ | amāgamaśca | midaco 'ntyātparaḥ | pā. 1-1-47 | ityṛkārātparaḥ | yaṇādeśaḥ | manino nittvādādyudāttatvam | vaso | āmantritanighātaḥ | yajñam | yajayācetyādinā | pā. 3-3-90 | naṅ | pratyayasvaraḥ | vardhaya | nighātaḥ | atra cakāradvayaśravaṇādiyameva tiṅvibhaktiḥ pūrvavākye 'pyanuṣajyate | ato 'nuṣaktaiva prathamā na śrutetyaśrutāyāśca vāyoge prathamā | pā. 8-1-59 | iti nighātaniṣedho na bhavati ||*

**Translation:** "Where the special application has not been laid down in the Śrauta [texts], one is to know the Smārta one, from the Ṛgvidhāna and other texts. This rik *ehi stomān* has not been assigned a special application in the sūtra; its general application is to be understood everywhere, in the Brahmayajña and so on. *O vaso* — O Indra, the cause of dwelling: *ehi* — come to this rite. Having come, *stomān abhi svara*: make a sound of praise toward the *stomas*, the hymns sung by the udgātṛs. Likewise, *gṛṇīhi*: with the adhvaryu in view, make a sound. Likewise, *ā ruva*: with the *śastras* recited by the hotṛs in view, make a sound — praise all the priests with pleasure. After that, *sacā* — together — *vardhaya*: make grow *naḥ brahma* — our food — and the sacrifice, that is, the rite being performed. Having made the sacrifice grow by getting it completed with all its limbs, make its fruit — food — abundant. Among the twenty-eight words for food beginning with *andhaḥ*, *brahma* is read [the print reads "brahma varja"]."

*(Grammar, noted briefly:* ihi *— root* iṇ gatau *with* hi*, which is* ṅit*-like, so no guṇa; with* ā *a single substitute udātta;* stomān *— suffix* man *("artistusu…"), initial-udātta; in the Saṃhitā the final* n *becomes* ru*, the* ā *nasalised, the* r *→* y *and dropped ("lopaḥ śākalyasya"), without vowel sandhi;* abhi *— final-udātta;* svara *— root* svṛ*, lowered;* gṛṇīhi *— root* gṝ śabde*, śnā*,* ī *by "ī halyaghoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-113), the root vowel shortened (Pā. 7-3-80),* ṇ *by the Kāśikā's addition to 8-4-1;* ruva *— root* ru śabde*, śa *for* śap *by Vedic exchange,* uvaṅ*, loss of* hi*;* brahma *— root* bṛhi vṛddhau *with* manin *(Uṇ. 4-145), the* n *dropped and* am *inserted after the last vowel (Pā. 1-1-47), initial-udātta;* vaso *— vocative, lowered;* yajñam *— naṅ (Pā. 3-3-90);* vardhaya *— lowered; since* ca *is used twice, this verb is understood in the earlier clause as well, so the rule "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. 8-1-59) does not prevent the lowering.)*

### Page 397 — Rik 4: grammar close, word-meanings, overall sense, English

*(The first lines of the page finish Sāyaṇa's grammar, given in full with p. 396 above.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**वसो (vaso)** — O Indra, you who are excellent (or the cause of our dwelling-places) | **(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **एहि (ehi)** — come (to this sacrificial ground that we perform) | **स्तोमान् (stomān)** — the hymns that the priests called udgātṛ, singers of the Sāman, recite, or sing | **अभि स्वर (abhi svara)** — listen with attention and give praise (that is, express approval) | **अभि गृणीहि (abhi gṛṇīhi)** — praise (the rites, that the adhvaryu performs) | **आ रुव (ā ruva)** — listen to the *śastra* mantras recited by the priests of the hotṛ group and signify your approval | *(then)* **नः (naḥ)** — to us | **ब्रह्म च (brahma ca)** — food too | **यज्ञं च (yajñaṃ ca)** — our sacrifice too | **सचा (sacā)** — being together (that is, being here) | **वर्धय (vardhaya)** — increase (that is, bring our sacrifice to completion, along with all its limbs, and bestow on us the food and the other foodstuffs that are its fruit).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! You are the cause of our dwellings — that is, it is you who give us the places where we live. Such as you are, O Indra, endowed with the quality of excellence! Come here, to the sacrifice we are performing; listen to the hymns sung with Sāmans by the priests called udgātṛ, to the adhvaryu, and to the *śastra*-mantras recited by the priests of the hotṛ group — to the hymns that each of them performs — and signify your approval of them by sound. Then grant that our sacrifice grows and is completed; and bestow upon us food and other nourishment.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Come hither, O good Indra, applaud our prayers, praise them, receive them approvingly. O Indra, bless our sacrifice and bestow upon us abundant food.

### Page 398 — Rik 4: Special Topics

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

On the matter of the special application of this rik, the Bhāṣyakāra, following the rule —

> विशेषविनियोगस्तु यत्र श्रौतो न सूत्रितः ।
> स्मार्तं तत्र विजानीयादृग्विधानादिसूत्रतः ॥
> *viśeṣa-viniyogas tu yatra śrauto na sūtritaḥ |*
> *smārtaṃ tatra vijānīyād ṛgvidhānādi-sūtrataḥ ||*
> "Where the special application [of a mantra] has not been laid down in the Śrauta [texts], one is to know the Smārta one from the Ṛgvidhāna and other texts."

— says that where the special application of a mantra is not stated in the Śrauta sūtras, in the performance of Smārta rites one must learn the application of that mantra from works such as the *Ṛgvidhāna*; and since no special application has been stated in the Śrauta sūtras for this rik *ehi stomān*, its general application in rites such as the Brahmayajña is to be understood.

In this rik there are three verbs, *svara*, *gṛṇīhi*, *ruva*: *svara* — root *svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ*; *gṛṇīhi* — root *gṝ śabde*; *ruva* — root *ru śabde*. Since these are given in the Dhātupāṭha, all three have the one meaning "make a sound." When one adds the prefix *abhi* — *abhilakṣya* — and renders it "make a sound of praise," that is, "praise, approve by sound (or by speech)," Skandasvāmī and Veṅkaṭamādhava likewise give this same sense; so it is this that should be accepted.

**"Vaso"** — *nivāsakāraṇabhūtendra* — "O Indra, the cause of dwelling-places": the Bhāṣyakāra's sense. **Skandasvāmī:** **वसो । शतपथे वसिष्ठ इति वसुशब्दस्यातिशयितप्रत्ययान्तस्य "यद्वै नः श्रेष्ठस्तेन वसिष्ठः" इति प्रशस्यतमेन वचनेन श्रेष्ठशब्देनार्थविवरणदर्शनात् वसुशब्दः प्रशस्यनाम** (*vaso | śatapathe vasiṣṭha iti vasuśabdasyātiśayitapratyayāntasya "yadvai naḥ śreṣṭhastena vasiṣṭhaḥ" iti praśasyatamena vacanena śreṣṭhaśabdenārthavivaraṇadarśanāt vasuśabdaḥ praśasyanāma*) — "*vaso*: since in the Śatapatha the word *vasiṣṭha* — *vasu* with the superlative suffix — is explained by the word *śreṣṭha* in the statement 'he is our best, therefore Vasiṣṭha', the word *vasu* is a name for 'excellent'": as stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa of the Śukla Yajurveda, *vasu* is explained as *śreṣṭha* ("best") and *praśasya* ("praiseworthy"). Or, since *vasu* also means wealth, the sense "O Indra, who are wealthy" may be given as well.

**"Brahma"** — *andhaḥ* — among the twenty-eight words for food beginning with *vājaḥ*, the word *brahma* is read (Ni. 3-9 as printed); so *brahma* means food. It is customary to call anything fit to be eaten "food." Besides, Yāska in the Nirukta says: **अन्नं कस्मादानतं भूतेभ्यो ऽत्तेर्वा अभिमुख्येन ह्येतत् नतं प्रह्वीभूतं भवति भोजनाय भूतानाम् । अत्तेर्वा । … अद्यते ऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यत इति** (*annaṃ kasmādānataṃ bhūtebhyo 'ttervā abhimukhyena hyetat nataṃ prahvībhūtaṃ bhavati bhojanāya bhūtānām | attervā | … adyate 'tti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ taducyata iti*) *(the source breaks the quotation after* atter vā *with "having said", then continues)* — "Why is it *anna* (food)? It is *ānata*, bowed down towards beings, or from *ad* ('to eat'): for it is bent, humbled, before beings for their eating; or from *ad*: it is eaten and it eats beings; therefore it is called *anna*." Thus he gives the etymology of the word.

### Page 399 — Rik 4: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Sacā"** — "together" — *sahitaḥ*. In this rik no use of this word seems evident; the sense may be given: "being together, that is, directly (in person)."

**"Vardhaya"** — "increase; bring to completion; fulfil without obstacle." The usage of this root is special in the Ṛgveda. Besides the general sense "increase," it must be given a meaning according to context in many places. For example, in the sentence *tvāṃ vardhantu no giraḥ* the word *vardhantu* has the sense "let them praise." In this rik *brahma ca vardhaya* — "increase the food" — means "give us abundant food"; likewise *yajñaṃ ca vardhaya* — "increase the sacrifice" — means "grant that the sacrifice be completed without obstacle."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 399–401, noted briefly)*

**एहि (*ehi*)** — root *iṇ gatau* ("to go"), *loṭ* second singular *sip*; *sip* → *hi* by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87); the *śap* vikaraṇa is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); *hi* is not *pit*, hence by "sārvadhātukam apit" (printed "1-6-4" [as printed], i.e. 1-2-4) it is *ṅit*, and "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5) prevents *guṇa*; "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) makes it unaccented; with the prefix *ā*, the *guṇa* arises as a single substitute and gives *ehi*; *ā* is a *nipāta*, hence udātta, and the single substitute *e* takes the udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5). **स्तोमान् (*stomān*)** — root *ṣṭuñ stutau* with *man* ("arti-stu-su…," Uṇ. 1-142); *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84); accusative plural *stomān*. **The Saṃhitā sandhi** — with the following word: "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9): the *n* after a long vowel, when followed by an *aṭ*-letter in the same pāda, is replaced by *ru*; *stomār* + *abhi*: by "āto 'ṭi nityam" (Pā. 8-3-3) the long *ā* before that *ru* is always nasalized, giving *stomā̐*; "bho-bhago-agho-apūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. 8-3-17): *y* replaces *ru* after *bho*, *bhago*, *agho* and *a*/*ā* before a voiced sound; then "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19) drops the *y*; the source argues that by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. 8-2-1) the *savarṇa-dīrgha* of "akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-101) does not apply (the *y* having been "unseen" — the elision of *y* is in the last three pādas and invisible to the earlier rule), so *stomā̐* + *abhi* stays as two syllables. **अभि (*abhi*)** — final-udātta by "evādīnām antaḥ" (Phiṭ-sūtra 82). **स्वर (*svara*)** — root *svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ*, *loṭ* second singular with the ending dropped, unaccented. **गृणीहि (*gṛṇīhi*)** — root *gṝ śabde*, *loṭ* second singular *sip*; *sip* → *hi* by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87); the vikaraṇa *śnā* by "kryādibhyaḥ śnā" (Pā. 3-1-81); "ī halyaghoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-113): the *ā* of *śnā* and of an *abhyasta* other than a *ghu* root becomes *ī* before a consonant-initial *kit*/*ṅit* ending, giving *gṝ* + *nī* + *hi*; "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-3-80): before a *śit* suffix *pūñ* and the like shorten, so *gṛ*; *ṇatva* by "raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade" (Pā. 8-4-1) with the vārttika "raṣābhyāṃ ṇatve ṛkāragrahaṇam", which the Mahābhāṣya states as "ṛkārāc ceti vaktavyam"; where the vārttika is set aside, the Mahābhāṣya divides "chandasy avagrahāt" (Pā. 8-4-26) into "ṛtaḥ" and "chandasy avagrahāt", the first part giving *ṇ* after *ṛ*: *gṛṇīhi*; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **रुव (*ruva*)** — root *ru śabde*, *loṭ* second singular *sip*, → *hi* by "seryapicca" (adādi class, hence the vikaraṇa *śap* is dropped by "ādiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ"; the source notes that, by Vedic inversion, a *śa*-type vikaraṇa arises here instead) *(continues on p. 400)*.

### Pages 400–401 — Rik 4 grammar closes

*(Grammar page, noted briefly.)* **रुव (*ruva*)** — *ru śabde* (adādi), *loṭ* second singular *sip*, *sip* → *hi* by "seryapicca". The adādi vikaraṇa *śap* ought to be dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); here instead, by Vedic inversion, the vikaraṇa *śa* arises, which by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4) is *ṅit*, so no guṇa; the *u* of *ru* takes *uvaṅ* by "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. 6-4-77), giving *ruv* + *a* + *hi*; *hi* is dropped by "ato heḥ" (Pā. 6-4-105), so *ruva*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **ब्रह्म (*brahma*)** — root *bṛha vṛddhau* ("to grow"), an *idit* root, so *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (printed "6-1-58" [as printed], i.e. 7-1-58), giving *bṛnh*; then *manin* (carried from "sarvadhātubhyo manin") by "bṛṃher am nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. 3-585 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 4-145), with the augment *am* and loss of the *n* of *num*; the *am* goes after the last vowel by "mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ" (Pā. 1-1-47); some read the Uṇādi sūtra as "bṛṃher no 'c ca" (Uṇ. 4-585 [as printed]), the *n* becoming *a*; the *ṛ* → *r* by "iko yaṇ aci" (6-1-77, printed "jā. sū." [sic]), giving *brahman*; *manin* is *nit*, so initial-udātta. **वसो (*vaso*)** — a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). **यज्ञम् (*yajñam*)** — *naṅ* by "yajayācayatavicchapracharakṣo naṅ" (Pā. 3-3-90) after *yaj*; *j* + *n* → *jñ* by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-40). **वर्धय (*vardhaya*)** — a finite verb, unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28); but since in this mantra two *ca*'s are heard (*brahma ca vardhaya*, *yajñaṃ ca vardhaya*), the verb is connected with the earlier clause too — so that the *vardhaya* of the earlier clause is the first finite verb of the joined sentence, and the rule "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. 8-1-59) prevents the lowering of the first verb in a sentence joined by *ca* and *vā*; hence no lowering applies where the first-uttered verb is concerned.

**॥४॥**

> अभिप्लवषडहगतोक्थ्येष्वच्छावाकस्य तृतीयसवन उक्थमिन्द्राय शंस्यमित्यनुरूपस्तृचः । एह्यूष्विति खण्ड इन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्नुक्थमिन्द्राय शंस्यम् । आ. ७-८ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ इन्द्रायेन्द्रार्थं वर्धनं **Translation:** "In the *ukthya* [rites] of the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha, in the Acchāvāka's third pressing, the triplet beginning *uktham indrāya śaṃsyam* is the *anurūpa*. In the section *ehy ū ṣu* it is laid down: '*indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhan*, *uktham indrāya śaṃsyam*' (Āśvalāyana 7-8). *Indrāya* — for Indra's sake — *vardhanam* — the means of increase — *uktham*, the *śastra* — is *śaṃsyam*, to be recited by us. For what kind of Indra? *Puruniṣṣidhe* — for him who bars many enemies. *Śakraḥ* — Indra — *yathā* — in whatever manner — *rāraṇat* would, in the highest degree, make a sound [of approval] regarding *naḥ*, our *suteṣu* (sons) and *sakhyeṣu* (friendships) — so [the *śastra*] is to be recited: this is the connection with what precedes. The sense is: Indra, pleased with our *śastra*, praises our sons and our friends in many ways." *(Grammar, noted briefly:* uktham *— from* vac *with* thak *(Uṇ. 2-2);* śaṃsyam *— root* śaṃsu stutau *with* yat*, initial-udātta;* vardhanam *— lyuṭ in the instrumental sense (Pā. 3-3-117), the syllable before the suffix udātta;* puruniṣṣidhe *— root* ṣidha gatyām *with* kvip *after* nis *(Pā. 2-2-18), the* ṣ *by Pā. 8-3-65 and 8-4-41, compounded with* puru *as its object, the root accent standing;* śakraḥ *— with* rak *(Uṇ. 2-13);* yathā *— thāl (Pā. 5-3-23);* suteṣu *— with* kta*;* ṇaḥ *— the* ṇ *in the Saṃhitā by Pā. 8-4-27;* rāraṇat *— root* raṇa *with* yaṅ *(Pā. 3-1-22) dropped (Pā. 2-4-74), doubling, lengthening (Pā. 7-4-83), the* leṭ *in the sense of* liṅ *(Pā. 3-4-7, 3-3-156), not lowered after* yathā *(Pā. 8-1-36);* sakhyeṣu *— "the acts of a friend", suffix* ya *(Pā. 5-1-126), the* i *dropped (Pā. 6-4-148).)*

### Page 403 — Rik 5: word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**पुरुनिष्षिधे (puruniṣṣidhe)** — who destroys many enemies | **इन्द्राय (indrāya)** — for Indra | **वर्धनम् (vardhanam)** — a means of increase | **उक्थम् (uktham)** — a mantra in the form of a *śastra*, or a hymn | **शंस्यम् (śaṃsyam)** — to be praised by us | **यथा (yathā)** — in which manner (by such a hymn) | **शक्रः (śakraḥ)** — mighty Indra | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **सुतेषु (suteṣu)** — among our sons | **सख्येषु च (sakhyeṣu ca)** — and among those of friendly disposition toward us | **रारणत् (rāraṇat)** — [by this word] he makes known his approval.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Indra destroys many enemies. For Indra's satisfaction we must recite *śastra* mantras, hymns; or we must praise Indra's qualities with *śastra* mantras. By praising Indra in this manner, Indra will be pleased and will make known his approval toward us, toward our sons, and toward our friends and others dear to us.

### Page 404 — Rik 5: English and Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> An agreeable hymn is to be sung to Indra, the destroyer of many enemies, so that the mighty Indra may speak with kindness to our sons and to our friends.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In the rite called Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, in the third pressing, when the priest called Acchāvāka recites the *ukthya* mantras, he is to recite the triplet *uktham indrāya śaṃsyam*; Āśvalāyana states this special application in the section *ehy ū ṣu* of his Śrauta-sūtra (Āś. Sū. 7-8), in the sūtra *indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhann uktham indrāya śaṃsyam*.

**"Vardhanam"** — **वृद्धिसाधनम्** (*vṛddhi-sādhanam*) — "the means of increase": that is, by praising Indra [with it] increase [of fortune] comes to us. *Or*: the sense of the root *vṛdh* used in the Ṛgveda is "increase," that is, "praise," "cause satisfaction"; so the word *vardhanam* here may mean "that which brings satisfaction to Indra."

**"Puruniṣṣidhe"** — **बहूनां शत्रूणां निषेधकारिणे** (*bahūnāṃ śatrūṇāṃ niṣedha-kāriṇe*) — "to him who is the barrier of many enemies": the Bhāṣyakāra explains the word so. *Puru* in this word means "much" — it only means "many"; the word "enemies" is supplied.

**"Śakraḥ"** — *śaktimān* — "one who is able, who is strong." In modern Sanskrit and also in the Vedas, the word *śakra* is especially established with the sense of Indra.

**"Yathā"** — since only *yathā* appears in this rik, the word *tathā* must be supplied. The second half, *śakro yathā rāraṇat sakhyeṣu ca*, is dependent upon the first half, *uktham indrāya*.

**"Rāraṇat"** — the root underlying this word is *raṇa*, meaning "to make a sound." To say that he "makes a sound among sons and friends" gives no particular object; so the sense "makes known his approval" is given. Unless certain words are supplied, one cannot explain this rik satisfactorily.

**"Suteṣu"** — in the Ṛgveda the various forms of the word *suta* have the general meaning "the juice of the Soma creeper that has been pressed out"; but in some contexts, rarely, *suta* has the sense "son"; this is such a case.

*(Special Topics, p. 404, ends on p. 405 with the remaining examples of* suta *in the sense "son":)*

> प्र नु वोचा सुतेषु वां वीर्या ३ यानि चक्रथुः ॥
> *pra nu vocā suteṣu vāṃ vīryā yāni cakrathuḥ ||*
> (ऋ. सं. ६-५९-१ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 6-59-1)
> *("Let me now proclaim among [your] sons the heroic deeds that you two have done." — mine and tentative; the page prints the verse with the prolongation mark ३.)*

"…and so on" — more examples may be given.

### Pages 405–409 — Rik 5 grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 405–409, noted briefly; the scholastic arguments on pp. 406–408 are characterized in outline only)*

**उक्थम् (*uktham*)** — root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; the suffix *thak* by "pātṛtudivaciricisicibhyas thak" (Uṇ. 2-164); "vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti" (Pā. 6-1-15) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*; *va* → *u* with *pūrvarūpa* by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca"; *c* → *k* by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30); the accent is by the suffix. **शंस्यम् (*śaṃsyam*)** — root *śaṃsu stutau* + *ṇic*; the suffix *yat* by "aco yat" (Pā. 3-1-97); *ṇi* dropped by "ṇer aniṭi" (Pā. 6-4-51); the *svarita* that would arise by "tit svaritam" (Pā. 6-1-185) is set aside by "yato 'nāvaḥ" (printed "6-4-213" [as printed], i.e. 6-1-213), so initial-udātta. **वर्धनम् (*vardhanam*)** — "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca" (Pā. 3-3-117): *lyuṭ*; *yu* → *ana* by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. 7-1-1); *laghūpadha-guṇa*; "liti" (Pā. 6-1-193): the vowel before a *l*-marked suffix is udātta. **पुरुनिष्षिधे (*puruniṣṣidhe*)** — *puru* ("many") + *niṣṣidh* "he who bars"; the root *ṣidhu gatyām* (*ṣ* → *s* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ," Pā. 6-1-64); the prefix *nis*, in the sense of *ni*, stands before it; *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76), with all of *kvip* dropped; the *prādi* compound by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. 2-2-18). **The scholastic discussion (pp. 405–408):** between the *s* of the prefix *nis* and the root's *s* (here, *ṣidh*), the question is whether the *s* of *nis* "intervenes" (*vyavadhāna*) so that the retroflexion of the root's *s* by "upasargāt sunoti-suvati-syati-stauti-stobhati-sthā-senaya-sedha-sica-sañja-svañjām" (Pā. 8-3-65) is blocked — with "sahe sāḍaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 8-3-56), "apadāntasya mūrdhanyaḥ" (Pā. 8-3-55) and "iṇkoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-57) carried over (p. 405); the *iṇ* of the prefix is taken as a qualifier by "yena vidhis tadantasya" (Pā. 1-1-72); the vārttika "upasargāt ṣatve niso upasaṃkhyānam aniṇantatvāt" (8-3-65 vārttika 1) and its rejoinder "na vā varṇāśrayatvāt" (8-3-65 vārttika 2) are cited; it is answered that by "numvisarjanīyaśarvyavāye 'pi" (Pā. 8-3-58) the intervention of *num*, *visarga* and *ś*, *ṣ*, *s* does not prevent the retroflexion, as the Mahābhāṣya says, "tatra śarvyavāye ity eva siddham"; the Vedabhāṣya's opinion that, because the intervention of the sibilant is "unobserved" in the Veda, the retroflexion arises, is discussed and is stated to be needless effort. "*Niṣ*" + "*ṣidh*": the *ṣ* is retained, and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) the *s* of *nis* becomes *ṣ*, giving *niṣṣidh*; the compound with the genitive-dependent *puru* (*puru* is the object, "they bar many") gives *puruniṣṣidh* — a compound that, by "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139), keeps the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member. *Niṣṣidh* is a *kṛdanta* because *kvip* was added even though lost (by "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam"; *kvip* comes only after a root, under the heading "dhātoḥ," Pā. 3-1-91); the long argument that the compound is formed with a verb-noun that is not itself a *kṛdanta* by the usual "kṛd-grahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" paribhāṣā (Paribhāṣā 28) settles that the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member stands. The remaining syllables are unaccented by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158); the dative ending *e* of *puruniṣṣidhe* (*ṅe*) is unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. 3-1-4), and then becomes *svarita* by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (8-4-66, printed "pā. rū." [sic]). **शक्रः (*śakraḥ*)** — "sphāyitañcivañciśaki…" (Uṇ. 2-170 [?] as printed, the second digit 7 or 2; the bhāṣya gives 2-13): the root *śakḷ śaktau* with *rak*; the accent by the suffix. **यथा (*yathā*)** — "prakāravacane thāl" (Pā. 5-3-23); *thāl* is *l*-marked, so the vowel before it is udātta by "liti" (Pā. 6-1-193). **सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)** — root *ṣuñ abhiṣave* + *kta*; udātta by the suffix. **नः (*naḥ*)** — *nas* is substituted for *asmākam* by "bahuvacanasya vasnasau" (Pā. 8-1-21); unaccented; in the Saṃhitā the *n* of *nas* is retroflexed to *ṇ* ("naś ca dhātustho-ru-ṣubhyaḥ," Pā. 8-4-27: after a cause of retroflexion in a root, and after *uru* and *ṣu*); *suteṣu* ends in *ṣ* with *pu*-type words so that the *n* of the following *nas* becomes *ṇ*: *suteṣu ṇaḥ*; the Śekharakāra holds that *ṣu* there imitates the root *ṣuñ* with its *ṣ* ("ṣu iti kṛtaṣatvasya suño 'nukaraṇam," Śe. on 8-4-27), and so explains why there is no *ṇatva* in *gṛ(gra) heṣunaḥ*; the Subodhinī agrees, and Bhaṭṭojidīkṣita in the Kaumudī gives examples such as *abhīṣuṇaḥ*; how *ṇatva* applies in the present case "is to be considered" (*cintanīya*). **रारणत् (*rāraṇat*)** — root *raṇa śabdārthaḥ* ("to sound"); *yaṅ* by "dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ" (Pā. 3-1-22); *yaṅ* then dropped by "yaṅo 'ci ca" (Pā. 2-4-74), with "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam" (Pā. 1-1-62) keeping it as *yaṅanta*; doubling by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-9); "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-60) drops the *ṇ* of the reduplicate; its lengthening by "dīrgho 'kitaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-83); "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32) gives root-status; then *leṭ* by "liṅarthe leṭ" (Pā. 3-4-7) in the sense of consequence ("hetuhetumadbhāva"): here Indra's making a sound of approval is the consequence of the reciting of the *śastra*; *tip*, with *i* dropped by "itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu" (Pā. 3-4-97), augment *aṭ* by "leṭo 'ḍāṭau" (Pā. 3-4-94), *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68) — which, since the *yaṅluk* form is treated like the *adādi* class ("carkarītaṃ ca"), should be dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72) but is *not* dropped here by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); *śap* is *pit*, hence unaccented; the root's accent stands — "dhātoḥ" (Pā. 6-1-162) — *rāraṇ* final-udātta; since *śap* intervenes before the *lasārvadhātuka* *at*, "abhyastānām ādiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-189) does not make it initial-udātta; the *a* of *śap* and of the augment combine by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97); "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) does not lower it, since the particle *yathā* occurs ("yāvadyathābhyām," Pā. 8-1-36), the verb is not unaccented; or, by the *ca* in *sakhyeṣu ca*, the verb *rāraṇat* of the later clause is supplied from the earlier and so is the first-uttered finite verb, and "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. 8-1-59) prevents lowering. **सख्येषु (*sakhyeṣu*)** — *sakhyuḥ karmāṇi sakhyāni*: "sakhyur yaḥ" (Pā. 5-1-126), with "karmaṇi ca" carried from "guṇavacanabrāhmaṇādibhyaḥ karmaṇi ca" (Pā. 5-1-124), gives *ya* in the sense of act; the stem takes *bha* status by "yaci bham" (Pā. 1-4-18); *i* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); locative plural *sakhyeṣu*; *ya* is udātta by "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. 3-1-3).

**॥५॥**

### Page 409 — Sūkta 10, Rik 6

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The print ends line 1 with ॥.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तमित्स॑खि॒त्व ई॑महे॒ तं रा॒ये तं सु॒वीर्ये॑ ।
> स श॒क्र उ॒त नः॑ श॒कदिन्द्रो॒ वसु॒ द॑यमानः ॥६॥
>
> *tam ít sakhitvá īmahe táṃ rāyé taṃ suvī́rye |*
> *sa śakrá utá naḥ śakád indro vásu dayamānaḥ ||6||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तम् । इत् । सखिऽत्वे । ईमहे । तम् । राये । तम् । सुऽवीर्ये ॥
> सः । शक्रः । उत । नः । शकत् । इन्द्रः । वसु । दयमानः ॥६॥
>
> *tam | it | sakhi-tve | īmahe | tam | rāye | tam | su-vīrye ||*
> *saḥ | śakraḥ | uta | naḥ | śakat | indraḥ | vasu | dayamānaḥ ||6||*

*(In the Saṃhitā the word* सखित्वे *prints as* सखित्व *before the following* ई*; the pada text gives the full locative.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> सखित्वे निमित्तभूते सति तमित्तमेवेन्द्रमीमहे । प्राप्नुमः । तथा राये धनार्थं तमीमहे । तथा सुवीर्ये शोभनसामर्थ्यनिमित्तं तमीमहे । उतापि च शक्रः शक्तिमान्स इन्द्रो नो ऽस्मभ्यं वसु धनं दयमानः प्रयच्छन् शकत् । अस्मदीयरक्षणे शक्तो ऽभूत् । सप्तदशयाच्ञाकर्मस्वीमहे यामीति पठितम् । तदनुसारेणेन्द्रं याचामह इति व्याख्येयम् ॥ सख्युर्भावः सखित्वम् । तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ । पा. ५-१-११९ । इति त्वः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । ईमहे । ईङ् गतौ । ङित्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । पा. १-३-१२ । दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् । बहुलं छन्दसीति श्यनो लुक् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । राये । ऊडिदमिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । सुवीर्ये । शोभनं वीर्यं यस्यासौ सुवीर्यः । भवितृवाचिनानेन भावो लक्ष्यते । सुवीर्यत्व इत्यर्थः । बहुव्रीहावित्यनुवृत्तौ वीरवीर्यौ च । पा. ६-२-१२० । इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । शक्नोतीति शक्रः । स्फायितञ्चिवञ्चिशकीत्यादिना रक् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । शकत् । शक्लृ शक्तौ । धातुसंबन्धाधिकारे छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः । पा. ३-४-६ । इति लुङ् । यतः शक्नोत्यतस्तमीमह इति धातुसंबन्धः । लुङस्तिप् । पुषादिद्युताद्य्लृदितः परस्मैपदेषु । पा. ३-१-५५ । इति च्लेरङादेशः । बहुलं छन्दसि । पा. ६-४-७५ । इत्यडागमाभावः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । वसु । निदित्यनुवृत्तौ वसेरुप्रत्ययः । उ. १-११ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । दयमानः । दय दानगतिरक्षणहिंसादानेषु । अनुदात्तेत्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । लटः शानजादेशः । पा. ३-२-१२४ । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शानचश्चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं बाधित्वादुपदेशाच्छप उत्तरत्वेन परत्वाल्लसार्वधातुकत्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते ॥ १९ ॥
>
> *sakhitve nimittabhūte sati tamittamevendramīmahe | prāpnumaḥ | tathā rāye dhanārthaṃ tamīmahe | tathā suvīrye śobhanasāmarthyanimittaṃ tamīmahe | utāpi ca śakraḥ śaktimānsa indro no 'smabhyaṃ vasu dhanaṃ dayamānaḥ prayacchan śakat | asmadīyarakṣaṇe śakto 'bhūt | saptadaśayācñākarmasvīmahe yāmīti paṭhitam | tadanusāreṇendraṃ yācāmaha iti vyākhyeyam || sakhyurbhāvaḥ sakhitvam | tasya bhāvastvatalau | pā. 5-1-119 | iti tvaḥ | pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | īmahe | īṅ gatau | ṅittvādātmanepadam | pā. 1-3-12 | divādibhyaḥ śyan | bahulaṃ chandasīti śyano luk | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | rāye | ūḍidamiti vibhakterudāttatvam | suvīrye | śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasyāsau suvīryaḥ | bhavitṛvācinānena bhāvo lakṣyate | suvīryatva ityarthaḥ | bahuvrīhāvityanuvṛttau vīravīryau ca | pā. 6-2-120 | ityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | śaknotīti śakraḥ | sphāyitañcivañciśakītyādinā rak | pratyayasvaraḥ | śakat | śaklṛ śaktau | dhātusaṃbandhādhikāre chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ | pā. 3-4-6 | iti luṅ | yataḥ śaknotyatastamīmaha iti dhātusaṃbandhaḥ | luṅastip | puṣādidyutādylṛditaḥ parasmaipadeṣu | pā. 3-1-55 | iti cleraṅādeśaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasi | pā. 6-4-75 | ityaḍāgamābhāvaḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | vasu | nidityanuvṛttau vaserupratyayaḥ | u. 1-11 | nittvādādyudāttatvam | dayamānaḥ | daya dānagatirakṣaṇahiṃsādāneṣu | anudāttettvādātmanepadam | laṭaḥ śānajādeśaḥ | pā. 3-2-124 | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | śānacaścita ityantodāttatvaṃ bādhitvādupadeśācchapa uttaratvena paratvāllasārvadhātukatvādanudāttatvam | dhātusvara eva śiṣyate || 19 ||*

**Translation:** "*Sakhitve* — for the sake of friendship — *tam it*, him, Indra, indeed, *īmahe* — we approach, we obtain [his favour]. Likewise *rāye*, for wealth, we approach him; likewise *suvīrye*, for the sake of fine capacity [valour], we approach him. And *uta* — also — *śakraḥ*, the mighty Indra, *naḥ* to us, *vasu*, wealth, *dayamānaḥ* — giving — *śakat*: has been able, has proved able in protecting us. Among the seventeen verbs meaning *yācñā* ('request') *īmahe* and *yāmi* are read; in accordance with this, it is to be explained: 'we request Indra.'" *(Grammar, noted briefly:* sakhitvam *— "the state of a friend," with* tva *(Pā. 5-1-119);* īmahe *— root* īṅ gatau*, ātmanepada since* ṅ*-marked (Pā. 1-3-12),* śyan *of the* divādi *class dropped by* luk *under* bahulam chandasi*;* rāye *— case-ending udātta;* suvīrye *— "he whose valour is fine," the abstract sense suggested by this word for the possessor,* suvīryatva*, with the second-member initial udātta by "vīravīryau ca" (Pā. 6-2-120);* śakraḥ *— "he who is able," with* rak*;* śakat *— root* śakḷ śaktau*, by the rule that the Veda uses* luṅ*,* laṅ *and* liṭ *interchangeably (Pā. 3-4-6), the* aorist *of* śak *with* aṅ *substitute for* cli *(Pā. 3-1-55), the augment* aṭ *not occurring by* bahulaṃ chandasi *(Pā. 6-4-75), unaccented;* vasu *— root* vasa *with* u *(Uṇ. 1-11), initial-udātta;* dayamānaḥ *— root* daya *with* śānac *for* laṭ*, unaccented* śap*, the root accent remaining. The bhāṣya closes "॥ १९ ॥", the nineteenth varga.)*

### Page 410 — Rik 6: word-meanings, overall sense, English

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(वयम्) सखित्वे ((vayam) sakhitve)** — for the sake of friendship | **तम् इत् (tam it)** — to him alone (to Indra) | **ईमहे (īmahe)** — we pray | **राये (rāye)** — for the sake of wealth and prosperity | **तम् (tam)** — that Indra | *(we pray)* | **सुवीर्ये (suvīrye)** — for greater valour | **तम् (tam)** — that Indra | *(we pray)* | **उत (uta)** — and | **शक्रः (śakraḥ)** — the mighty one | **सः इन्द्रः (saḥ indraḥ)** — that Indra | **नः (naḥ)** — to us | **वसु (vasu)** — wealth | **दयमानः (dayamānaḥ)** — giving | **शकत् (śakat)** — may he be able to protect us.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

We pray to Indra for friendship, for wealth, and for powers of valour. That Indra, being mighty, is able not only to give us wealth but also to protect us.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> To him (Indra) alone we pray for friendship, to him for wealth, to him for great valour. For he, the powerful Indra conferring wealth is able to protect us.

### Page 411 — Rik 6: Special Topics and grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Īmahe"** — among the seventeen verbs *īmahe*, *yāmi*, *manmahe* and others, denoting the act of requesting (*yācñā-karma*), the word *īmahe* is read (Ni. 3-19); so *īmahe* means "we ask, we beseech."

**"Suvīrye"** — *su* — good, abundant; *vīrya* = valour, power, capacity. *Great valour, grat* [sic] *power*, and so on [the source's own English].

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 411–412, noted briefly)*

**सखित्वे (*sakhitve*)** — *sakhyuḥ bhāvaḥ sakhitvam*, locative *ṅi* → *e*; *tva* by "tasya bhāvas tvatalau" (Pā. 5-1-119); udātta by the suffix. **ईमहे (*īmahe*)** — root *īṅ gatau*; since it is *ṅ*-marked, the ātmanepada by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. 1-3-12); *laṭ* first plural *mahiṅ*; *e* by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. 3-4-79); the *śyan* of "divādibhyaḥ śyan" (Pā. 3-1-69), dropped by *luk* under "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **रायै (*rāye*)** — *rai* + *ṅe*, "ūḍidam-padādy-appum-raidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-171): after *rai* the ending is udātta. **सुवीर्ये (*suvīrye*)** — "śobhanaṃ vīryaṃ yasyāsau suvīryaḥ": the abstract sense *suvīryatva* ("fine valour") is suggested by a word whose own sense is that-which-has-it; the abstract-denoting use of *suvīrya* for *suvīryatva*; "vīra-vīryau ca" (Pā. 6-2-120), with "bahuvrīhau" carried over from "bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām" (Pā. 6-2-106): in a bahuvrīhi the words *vīra* and *vīrya* after *su* are initial-udātta in the Veda, so the initial of *vīrya* is udātta. **शक्रः (*śakraḥ*)** — "śaknoti iti śakraḥ": root *śakḷ śaktau* with *rak* by "sphāyitañcivañciśaki…" (Uṇ. 2-170 [?] as printed, the second digit 7 or 2); accent by the suffix. **शकत् (*śakat*)** — root *śakḷ śaktau* — under the heading "dhātusaṃbandhe pratyayāḥ" (Pā. 3-4-1) the rule "chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-6) allows *luṅ* here; the source notes the connection of the verb with *īmahe* ("because he is able, therefore we approach him"): "*yataś śaknoti ataḥ tam īmahe*"; *luṅ*, *tip*; the *i* of *tip* dropped by "itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu" (Pā. 3-4-97). *(The grammar continues on p. 412.)*

### Page 412 — Rik 6 grammar closes; Sūkta 10, Rik 7

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

Closing the grammar of **शकत् (*śakat*)**: by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43) the *cli* arises after the root (*śak* + *cli* + *t*); for the *cli* after a root of the *puṣādi*, *dyutādi*, and *ḷdit* classes in the parasmaipada, *aṅ* is substituted by "puṣādi-dyutādi-ḷditaḥ parasmaipadeṣu" (Pā. 3-1-55); the augment *aṭ* that "lūṅ-laṅ-lṛṅ-kṣv aḍudāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71) would give does not arise, by "bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pi" (Pā. 6-4-75); wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **वसु (*vasu*)** — "śvā-svṛ-snihi-trapy-asi-vasi-hani-klidi-bandhi-manibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-10); *nit* is carried over from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. 1-9) and *uḥ* from "bhṛmṛśī…uḥ" (Uṇ. 1-7), so *u* comes after the ten roots *śvā* etc. and is *nit*; so *vasa nivāse* gives *vasu*, initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). **दयमानः (*dayamānaḥ*)** — root *daya dāna-gati-rakṣaṇa-hiṃsā-dāneṣu*; *anudātta-it*, so ātmanepada by "anudātta-ṅita ātmanepadam" (printed "1-3-1" [as printed], i.e. 1-3-12); *śānac* for *laṭ* by "laṭaḥ śatṛśānacāv aprathamāsamānādhikaraṇe" (Pā. 3-2-124); *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68); before *āna* the short *a* of the stem takes the augment *muk* by "āne muk" (Pā. 7-2-82), which is *kit* and so is added at the end ("ādyantau ṭakitau," Pā. 1-1-46): *day + a + mān + a*; *śap* is *pit* and so unaccented; the *śānac*, being *cit*, would give the final accent ("citaḥ," Pā. 6-1-163), but since it follows *śap*, an *adupadeśa*, the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented (*tāsyanudāttenṅid-adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam*, Pā. 6-1-186), this is set aside and only the root's accent stands: *day*.

**॥६॥**

### Page 412 (lower) — Sūkta 10, Rik 7

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> सु॒वि॒वृतं॑ सुनि॒रज॒मिन्द्र॒ त्वादा॑त॒मिद्यशः॑ ।
> गवा॒मप॑ व्र॒जं वृ॑धि कृणु॒ष्व राधो॑ अद्रिवः ॥७॥
>
> *suvivṛ́taṃ sunirájam índra tvā́dātam íd yáśaḥ |*
> *gavām ápa vrajáṃ vṛdhi kṛṇuṣvá rā́dho adrivaḥ ||7||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> सुऽविवृतम् । सुनिःऽअजम् । इन्द्र । त्वाऽदातम् । इत् । यशः ॥
> गवाम् । अप । व्रजम् । वृधि । कृणुष्व । राधः । अद्रिवः ॥७॥
>
> *su-vivṛtam | sunir-ajam | indra | tvā-dātam | it | yaśaḥ ||*
> *gavām | apa | vrajam | vṛdhi | kṛṇuṣva | rādhaḥ | adrivaḥ ||7||*

### Page 413 — Rik 7: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र यशो ऽन्नं कर्मफलभूतं सुविवृतं सुष्ठु सर्वत्र प्रसृतं सुनिरजं सुखेन निःशेषं प्राप्तुं शक्यं त्वादातमित्त्वया शोधितं च संपन्नमिति शेषः । अतः परं क्षीरादिरसलाभार्थं गवां व्रजं निवासस्थानमप वृधि । अपवृतमुद्घाटितद्वारं कुरु । हे अद्रिवः पर्वतोपलक्षितवज्रयुक्तेन्द्र राधो धनं कृणुष्व । संपादय ॥ सुविवृतम् । वृञ् वरणे । कर्मणि क्तप्रत्ययः । विशब्देन प्रादिसमासः । विवृतमित्यत्र कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरं बाधित्वा कर्मवाचिनि क्तान्ते परतो गतिरनन्तरः । पा. ६-२-४९ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलम् । ६-२-१९९ । इतीकार उदात्तः । पुनः सुशब्देन समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एवकार [sic] उदात्तः । ननु वृतमित्येव कृदन्तं न तु विवृतमिति प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात्स विहितस्तदादेस्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम् । परि. २३ । इति वचनात् । सुविवृतमित्यत्र च समासे वृतमित्येतावन्मात्रं नोत्तरपदं किंतु विवृतमिति । तत्कथं कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वमिति चेत् उच्यते । प्रत्ययग्रहणपरिभाषापवादेन कृद्ग्रहणे गतिकारकपूर्वस्यापि ग्रहणम् । परि. २८ । इत्यनेन विवृतमित्यस्यापि कृदन्तव्यपदेशोपपत्तेः । ननु विवृतमित्यस्य यथा कृदन्तव्यपदेशः । एवं क्तान्तव्यपदेशो ऽप्यस्ति तयैव परिभाषया । तथा च कर्मणि क्तान्त उत्तरपदे परतो गतिरनन्तर इति सुशब्दस्य प्रकृतिस्वरः प्राप्नोति । न चात्रापि परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्येवं नास्ति निस्तारः । तथा हि सति सुविवृतमित्यत्र विवृतमित्येवोत्तरपदमिति तदादिरिकार एवोदात्तः स्यात् । विवृतमिति समासे यद्यप्यृकारः पदादिर्भवति तथापि सुविवृतमिति समासस्य सति शिष्टत्वेन बलीयस्त्वात्तत्रत्य एवोत्तरपदादाविकार एवोदात्तस्वरेण भवितव्यमिति । उच्यते । गतिरनन्तर इत्यत्रानुवृत्तेः कृद्ग्रहणे कृद्ग्रहणपरिभाषा नाश्रीयते । तदाश्रयणे व्यवहितगतावपि प्रकृतिस्वरे सत्यनन्तरग्रहणमनर्थकं स्यात् । अनेनैव चाभिप्रायेणानन्तरग्रहणस्य प्रयोजनमभ्युद्धृतमित्यत्र व्यवहितस्याभिशब्दस्य मा भूदिति प्रत्युदाहृतम् । तस्मात्सुविवृतमित्यृकार एवोदात्त इति स्थितम् । सुनिरजम् । अनायासेन निरवशेषं प्राप्यम् । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः । सुनिसोरुपसर्गयोः प्राक्प्रयोगः । ईषद्दुःसुषु कृच्छ्राकृच्छ्रार्थेषु खल् । पा. ३-३-१२६ । न चात्र सुशब्दस्य निसा व्यवधानं शङ्कनीयम् । सुशब्दस्य ह्युपपदमात्रं खलो निमित्तं नानन्तर्यम् । अत एव सुपरिहरं दुष्परिहरमित्यादयः प्रयोगा इति । पूर्ववद्गतिसमासे लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वमुदात्तमिति धात्वकार उदात्तः । निसा समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते । पुनः सुशब्देन समासे कृद्ग्रहणे गतिकारकपूर्वस्यापि ग्रहणमिति परिभाषया कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते । त्वादातम् । त्वया शोधनेन विशदीकृतम् । दैप् शोधने । आदेच उपदेशे ऽशिति । पा. ६-१-४५ । इत्यात्त्वम् । सत्यपि हि पकारे नानुबन्धकृतमनेजन्तत्वम् । परि. ६ । इत्येजन्त एवायम् । निष्ठेति कर्मणि क्तः । दाधा घ्वदाप् । पा. १-१-२० । इत्यत्रादाबिति प्रतिषेधेन घुसंज्ञाया अभावाद्दो दद्घोः । पा. ७-४-४६ । इति ददादेशो न भवति । ननु दाप् लवन इति प्रतिपदोक्तस्यैव दापस्तत्रादाबिति निषेधः । न पुनर्लाक्षणिकस्य दैपः । लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः प्रतिपदोक्तस्यैव ग्रहणं न तु लाक्षणिकस्य । परि. १०५ । इति नियमादिति चेन्न । गामादाग्रहणेष्वविशेषः । परि. १०६ । इति प्रतिप्रसवात् । युष्मच्छब्दात्तृतीयैकवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगिति डादेशः । त्वमावेकवचने । पा. ७-२-९७ । इति मपर्यन्तस्य त्वादेशः । अतो गुण इति पररूपत्वम् । भसंज्ञायां टेरित्यद्शब्दस्य [?] लोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणाकार उदात्तः । कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलम् । पा. २-१-३२ । इति तृतीयासमासः । तत्पुरुषे कृति बहुलम् । पा. ६-३-१४ । इति तृतीयाया अप्यलुक् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते तृतीया कर्मणि । पा. ६-२-४८ । इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यशः । अशू व्याप्तौ । अशेर्युट्च । उ. ४-१९० । इत्यसुन् । तत्संनियोगेन धातोर्युडागमः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । गवाम् । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं प्राप्तं न गोश्वन्साववर्णेति निषिध्यते । वृधि । वृञ् वरणे । श्रुशृणुपॄकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसि । पा. ६-४-१०२ । इति हेर्धिरादेशः । बहुलं छन्दसीति श्नोरपि लुक् । निघातः । कृणुष्व । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । इदितो नुम् । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । लोटस्थास् । ३-४-७८ । थासः से । पा. ३-४-८० । सवाभ्यां वामौ । पा. ३-४-९१ । कर्तरि शपि प्राप्ते । पा. ३-१-६८ । धिन्विकृण्व्योरच्च । पा. ३-१-८० । इत्युप्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेन वकारस्य चाकारः । तस्यातो लोपः । पा. ६-४-४८ । इति लोपः । अचः परस्मिन्पूर्वविधौ । पा. १-१-५७ । इत्यकारलोपस्य स्थानिवद्भावाल्लघूपधगुणो न भवति । अत्र सति शिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेभ्य इति सति शिष्टमपि विकरणस्वरं बाधित्वा तिङ एव प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् । राधः । असुनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अद्रिवः । अद्रिर्वज्रम् । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । छन्दसीरः । पा. ८-२-१५ । इति वत्वम् । संबुद्धावुगिदचाम् । पा. ७-१-७० । इति नुम् । हल्ङ्यादिसंयोगान्तलोपौ । पा. ६-१-६८ । मतुवसो रु संबुद्धौ छन्दसि । पा. ८-३-१ । इति रुत्वम् । विसर्जनीयः । आमन्त्रितस्य च निघातः ॥
