**Translation:** "O Indra! *Yaśaḥ* — food, the fruit of the rite — *suvivṛtam*: well spread out everywhere; *sunirajam*: easily obtained, wholly; *tvādātam*: purified by you — has come about [supply 'is']. After this, for the sake of obtaining milk and other juices, *gavāṃ vrajam* — the cow-pen, the dwelling-place of cows — *apa vṛdhi*: open it — make its door opened. O *adrivaḥ* — O Indra, armed with the thunderbolt that is characterized by the mountain — *rādhaḥ* — wealth — *kṛṇuṣva*: bring about." *(Grammar, noted briefly:* suvivṛtam *— root* vṛñ varaṇe *with* kta*, compounded with* vi *and then* su*; the* i *of* vi *is udātta by "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199), setting aside Pā. 6-2-49; a long discussion with paribhāṣās 23 and 28 shows that, since "kṛdgrahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi" is not applied to "gatir anantaraḥ", the* ṛ *is udātta;* sunirajam *— root* aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ *with* khal *(Pā. 3-3-126) after* su *and* nis*;* tvādātam *— root* daip śodhane *with* kta*, not* dad- *since it is not* ghu *(Pā. 1-1-20, 7-4-46; paribhāṣās 6, 105, 106), compounded with* tvā *(Pā. 7-2-97, 2-1-32, 6-3-14), first-member accent (Pā. 6-2-48);* yaśaḥ *— Uṇ. 4-190;* gavām *— stem accent;* vṛdhi *— dhi for hi (Pā. 6-4-102);* kṛṇuṣva *— root* kṛvi *with* u *(Pā. 3-1-80), ātmanepada by Vedic exchange;* adrivaḥ *— matup with* v *(Pā. 8-2-15),* num *(Pā. 7-1-70),* ru *(Pā. 8-3-1), unaccented as a vocative.)*

### Page 414 — Rik 7: Sāyaṇa's grammar (briefly noted)

*(This page carries the rest of Sāyaṇa's grammar of Ṛk 7, given in full with p. 413 above.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(printed on p. 415)*

### Page 415 — Rik 7: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **सुविवृतम् (suvivṛtam)** — spread out well everywhere (that is, in great abundance) | **सुनिरजम् (sunirajam)** — easily obtained | **यशः (yaśaḥ)** — the food (nourishment) | **त्वादातम् इत् (tvādātam it)** — you are indeed the one who purifies it well | **(हे) अद्रिवः ((he) adrivaḥ)** — O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt | **गवाम् (gavām)** — of the cows | **व्रजम् (vrajam)** — the cow-pen | **अप वृधि (apa vṛdhi)** — open the door (that is, give us cows) | **राधः (rādhaḥ)** — wealth | **कृणुष्व (kṛṇuṣva)** — obtain (for us).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! Make abundant food available to us; it must be easily obtainable for us everywhere. Besides, open the pen of the cows and obtain for us many cows and wealth.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, the food is rendered abundant everywhere and easily obtainable; O weilder [sic] of thunderbolt, throw open, then the cow-fold and give us wealth.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Suvivṛtam"** — for this word the Bhāṣyakāra says **सुष्ठु सर्वत्र प्रसृतम्** (*suṣṭhu sarvatra prasṛtam*) — "well spread out everywhere"; Skandasvāmī says **सुष्ठु लोके प्रकाशम्** (*suṣṭhu loke prakāśam*) — "well available (manifest) in the world." The scholar Wilson renders it *rendered everywhere abundant*.

**"Sunirajam"** — **सुखेन निःशेषं प्राप्तुं शक्यम्** (*sukhena niḥśeṣaṃ prāptuṃ śakyam*) — "that which can be obtained wholly with ease" says the Bhāṣyakāra; and Skandasvāmī explains: **सुनिरजम् । निरित्येष नीत्येतस्य स्थाने । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः । सुनिक्षेपम् । यत्र यत्र विनियोक्तुमिष्यते तत्र तत्र प्रभूतत्वात्सुविनियोजमित्यर्थः ॥** (*sunirajam | nirityeṣa nītyetasya sthāne | aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ | sunikṣepam | yatra yatra viniyoktumiṣyate tatra tatra prabhūtatvātsuviniyojamityarthaḥ ||*) — "*sunirajam*: *nir* here stands for *ni*; root *aja* in the sense of going and throwing; *sunikṣepam*, 'easily laid down': wherever one wishes to apply it, there, because it is abundant, it is easily applied." That is: what can be obtained easily, being spread everywhere, is easily to be found.

**"Tvādātam"** — "purified by you" (*tvayā śodhanena viśadīkṛtam*), says the Bhāṣyakāra; Skandasvāmī gives *tvayā dattam* — "given by you." The Bhāṣyakāra takes the root *daip śodhane* — *(the page breaks off here; the Special Topics continue on p. 416)*.

### Page 416 — Rik 7: Special Topics (continued)

*(Continuing "**Tvādātam**":)* … *dāp śodhane*: "*daip śodhane* takes the form *dāp* by the rule *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti* (Pā. 6-1-45), and he explains it accordingly" — "purified by you, made clear," as the Bhāṣyakāra explains. According to Skandasvāmī's explanation, *tvādātam* is *tvayā dattam*, "given by you." The sense in the end is one, though the derivation of the word differs. The word *tvādātam* occurs not only in this rik but in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-40-6, 5-6-10 and 5-39-1; the word *tvādattaḥ* at Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-92-18, and *tvādatrebhiḥ* at Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-33-2. *(See also the explanation of the word* adrivaḥ *in this rik.)*

**"Yaśaḥ"** — since *yaśaḥ* is read among the twenty-eight words for food beginning with *andhaḥ*, *vājaḥ*, here *yaśaḥ* means food.

**"Apa vṛdhi"** — **उद्घाटितद्वारं कुरु** (*udghāṭita-dvāraṃ kuru*) — "make [it] with its door opened": *open the door*; i.e., *throw open the door (of cow-fold)* [the source's own English].

**"Vrajam"** — *goṣṭham*, or *gavāṃ nivāsasthānam* — "the cowshed, or the dwelling-place of cows": the cow-pen where cows are kept; *cow fold* [the source's own English].

Here the word *yaśaḥ* is taken as "water" (Ni. 2-24 as printed), and *vraja* and *adri* as "cloud" (Ni. 2-21 as printed); on that sense the meaning would run: "scatter the mass of clouds and make rain come, and so give us water" — which is also reasonable. Wilson, too, gives a similar sense: "the text is literally rendered: the meaning being that Indra as the sender of rain should fertilize the fields, and by providing abundant pasturage enable the cattle to yield store of milk" [the source's own English], supporting this view.

**"Adrivaḥ"** — **अद्रिर्वज्रम् । तदस्यास्तीति** (*adrir vajram | tad asyāstīti*) — "*adri* means the thunderbolt-weapon; so *adrivān* means 'one bearing the thunderbolt.'" Since in the Nirukta *adri* is explained as "mountain," the Bhāṣyakāra says "*parvatopalakṣita-vajra-yukta*" — "armed with the thunderbolt characterized by the mountain." Besides, the word *adri* has the name "cloud" (Ni. 2-21), and Yāska,

> यदिन्द्र चित्र मेहनास्ति त्वादातमद्रिवः ।
> राधस्तन्नो विदद्वस उभयाहस्त्या भर ॥
> *yad indra citra mehanāsti tvādātam adrivaḥ |*
> *rādhas tan no vidadvasa ubhayāhastyā bhara ||*
> (ऋ. सं. ५-३९-१ — Ṛgveda Saṃhitā 5-39-1)
> *("O wondrous Indra, whatever wealth there is, given by you, O wielder of the stone — that wealth, O finder of wealth, bring to us with both hands." — mine and tentative.)*

— in explaining this rik, he says **अद्रिवन् । अद्रिरादृणात्येतेन** (*adrivan | adrir ādṛṇāty etena*) — "*adri* [is so called] because one splits with it" — giving *adrivaḥ* the sense "O thunderbolt-bearer" (*he vajrin*), and to *tvādātam* the sense **त्वया नस्तद्दातव्यम्** (*tvayā nas tad dātavyam*), "that is to be given to us by you." Therefore Yāska's explanations of these two words, *adrivan* and *tvādātam*, are to be accepted.

### Pages 417–422 — Rik 7 grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 417–422, noted briefly; the scholastic arguments on pp. 417–419 are characterized in outline only)*

**सुविवृतम् (*suvivṛtam*)** — root *vṛñ varaṇe* with *kta* in the passive; *vi* + *vṛta* are joined as *prādi*, and *su* with *vivṛta* as a further compound ("kugatiprādayaḥ," Pā. 2-2-18); since *vṛta* is a *kṛdanta*, the rule "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) would give the accent of the second member; this is set aside by "gatir anantaraḥ" (Pā. 6-2-49) (when a *kta*-ending word in the passive sense is the second member, a directly preceding *gati* keeps its own accent), so that the *vi* would be initial-udātta; this too is set aside by "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199), making the first vowel (*ṛ*) of *vṛta* udātta. **The long argument (pp. 417–418):** when *su* is then compounded with *vivṛta*, "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" would again keep the accent of the second member, and that *ṛ* stays udātta. But the objection arises: in *su-vivṛta* is *vivṛta* a *kṛdanta*? — the paribhāṣā "pratyaya-grahaṇe yasmāt sa vihitas tad-ādes tad-antasya grahaṇam" (Paribhāṣā 23) says that where a suffix is named, the item beginning with that to which it was added and ending in that suffix is meant; *vivṛta* is not *vṛta* alone — and the counter-paribhāṣā "kṛd-grahaṇe gati-kāraka-pūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" (Paribhāṣā 28) says that a *kṛdanta* includes one preceded by a *gati* or a *kāraka*; hence *vivṛta* is a *kṛdanta*. A further difficulty (pp. 418): the sūtra "gatir anantaraḥ" with "anantara" ("immediately preceding") appears to bar the rule when something intervenes, as in *su-vi-vṛtam* where *vi* intervenes between *su* and *vṛta*; "kte ca" (printed "5-2-45" [as printed], i.e. 6-2-45) being carried into "gatir anantaraḥ", the answer is that, because of the word "anantara", the paribhāṣā "kṛd-grahaṇe…" is not present in that sūtra, and the counter-example *abhyuddhṛtam* (where the intervening *abhi* does not keep its own accent) is cited to show the use of the word *anantara*; the discussion concludes (p. 418) that in *suvivṛtam* the *ṛ* remains udātta. *(The page ends with "so ends this great-sentence discussion.")* **सुनिरजम् (*sunirajam*)** — the root *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ* with the prefixes *su* and *nis*; "īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal" (Pā. 3-3-126) gives *khal* after a root when *īṣat*, *duḥ* or *su* is the *upapada*, in senses of difficulty/ease; the argument whether *nis* intervening between *su* and *aja* prevents the *khal* is answered: the rule does not require that the *su* stand immediately before (cf. *suparihāram*, *duṣparihāram*); *khal* is *l*-marked, so the vowel before it (*a* of *aj*) is udātta by "liti"; with the *gati*-compound with *nis*, the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member (the root's *a* udātta) stands; compounding again with *su* gives the same by Paribhāṣā 28; the remaining syllables are lowered; the unaccented *a* of the suffix becomes *svarita* by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (no number printed). **त्वादातम् (*tvādātam*)** — root *daip śodhane* — the argument on pp. 419–420: by "ādeca upadeśe 'śiti" (Pā. 6-1-45) the *e* of the root becomes *ā* when a non-*śit* suffix follows; but the root is *daip* ending in *p*, with *ai*, which in the *upadeśa* is a diphthong-ending root? — the difficulty is resolved by the paribhāṣā "nānubandhakṛtam anejantatvam" (Paribhāṣā 6) that the diphthong-ending status of a root is not undone by a mere *it*-marker; *kta* in the passive by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. 3-2-102), giving *dā* + *ta*; the objection that *dā* + *ta* would then be *ghu*-class and so take *dad* in place of *dā* ("dādhā ghv adāp," Pā. 1-1-20; "do dad ghoḥ," Pā. 7-4-46) is answered, since *dāp lavane* and *daip śodhane* are specifically excluded and the substitute-from-*daip* *dā* is "lākṣaṇika," not *pratipadokta*; the paribhāṣā "lakṣaṇa-pratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam" is argued and disposed of by "gāmādāgrahaṇeṣv aviśeṣaḥ" (Paribhāṣā 106). *Tvā* — *yuṣmad* + *ṭā*, the third-case ending replaced by *ā* via *ḍā* ("supāṃ suluk…" Pā. 7-1-39); *tva* replaces the part up to *m* of *yuṣmad* ("tvamāv ekavacane," printed "8-2-97" [as printed], i.e. 7-2-97), *tva* + *ad* + *a*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97); with *bha*-status the *ṭi* (*ad*) is dropped by "ṭeḥ" (Pā. 6-4-143), giving *tvā*; *yuṣmad* itself is from *yuṣ* with *madik* (Uṇ. 1-136); the *a* is udātta by "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-161); the accent (pp. 420–421): the *ā* is udātta if a *prātipadika* accent applies; the third-case *tvā* compounds with the *kṛdanta* *dāta* by "kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam" (Pā. 2-1-32); the ending of the third-case word would be dropped by "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71) but is not dropped by "tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam" (Pā. 6-3-14); the *kṛdanta*'s second-member accent that would stand is set aside by "tṛtīyā karmaṇi" (Pā. 6-2-48): a third-case word followed by a *kta*-ending word in the passive sense keeps its own accent, so the first member's accent stands. **यशः (*yaśaḥ*)** — root *aśū vyāptau* + *asun* by "aśer yuṭ ca" (printed "pā. sū. 4-630" [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives Uṇ. 4-190), with the augment *yuṭ*; *yaśas*, with *su* dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal" (Pā. 6-1-68); *ru* and visarga; initial-udātta since the suffix is *nit*. **गवाम् (*gavām*)** — stem accent; the udātta of the case-ending that "sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168) would give is barred by "na go-śvannāvavarṇa-rāḍ-ṅkṛ-kṛd-bhyaḥ" (printed "1-182" [sic], i.e. 6-1-182), so the ending is unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau". **वृधि (*vṛdhi*)** — root *vṛñ varaṇe* + *loṭ* second singular *sip*; *sip* → *hi* by "seryapicca"; *śnu* by "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ" (Pā. 3-1-73), dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (2-4-73, printed "paṃ. sū." [sic]); after *śṛ*, *spṛ*, *kṛ*, *vṛ*, *bhṛ* in the Veda, *hi* → *dhi* ("śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi," Pā. 6-4-102); *hi* is *apit* so *ṅit*, hence no *guṇa* by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5); unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ". **कृणुष्व (*kṛṇuṣva*)** — root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*, *idit* so *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58), *num* being *mit* it stands after the last vowel ("mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ," Pā. 1-1-47); ātmanepada by inversion; *loṭ* with middle-second *thās* → *se* (Pā. 3-4-80), *se* → *sva* (Pā. 3-4-91); *kṛnv* + *sva*: the *śap* arising by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68) is set aside by "dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca" (Pā. 3-1-80): after *dhivi* and *kṛvi* — both *bhvādi* (first-class) roots, though Bopadeva takes them as *tanādi*, in whose view the *ca* of the sūtra is unnecessary — the *u*-vikaraṇa arises and the final of the root is changed to *a*, so *kṛṇ* + *u* + *sva* ("kṛn + a + u + sva"); "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-48) drops the *a* before the *ārdhadhātuka*-like *u*; the *laghūpadha-guṇa* of *kṛn* by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86) is argued away by "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. 1-1-57): the *a*-substitute counts as the original for the purposes of rules applying to what precedes; so the penultimate *ṛ* is treated as before an *a*... and no *guṇa* arises; *n* → *ṇ* by the vārttika "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam", *s* → *ṣ* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ"; the maxim "satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ" says that a later accent is stronger except for vikaraṇas, so the accent of the vikaraṇa *u* does not prevail and the *tiṅ* *sva* is initial-udātta by "ādyudāttaś ca", the rest unaccented. **राधः (*rādhaḥ*)** — "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]); initial-udātta since *nit*. **अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)** — "adriḥ asya asti": *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94); *m* → *v* in the Veda after a word ending in *i* or *r* ("chandasīraḥ," Pā. 8-2-15); *adri-vat* + vocative *su*; the *num* of "ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-70) arises after the last vowel by "mid aco 'ntyāt paraḥ"; then (p. 422, end) the *t* is dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ…" and "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ," the *s* becomes *ru* by "matuvasor ru sambuddhau chandasi" (Pā. 8-3-1), then visarga by "kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ" (Pā. 8-3-15); a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). *(The scholastic arguments are characterized in outline, not rendered line by line. The last lines of this grammar run onto the top of p. 423: the* su *is dropped by Pā. 6-1-68, the* t *of* adrivant *as the end of a conjunct (Pā. 8-2-23); the* n *is not dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7), because by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (printed "8-192" [as printed], i.e. 8-2-1) the loss of* t *is "unseen".)*

### Page 423 (lower half) — Sūkta 10, Rik 8

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> न॒हि त्वा॒ रोद॑सी उ॒भे ऋ॑घा॒यमा॑ण॒मिन्व॑तः ।
> जेषः॒ स्व॑र्वतीर॒पः सं गा अ॒स्मभ्यं॑ धूनुहि ॥८॥
>
> *nahí tvā ródasī ubhé ṛghāyámāṇam ínvataḥ |*
> *jeṣaḥ svarvatīr apáḥ saṃ gā asmábhyaṃ dhūnuhi ||8||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> नहि । त्वा । रोदसी इति । उभे इति । ऋघायमाणम् । इन्वतः ॥
> जेषः । स्वःऽवतीः । अपः । सम् । गाः । अस्मभ्यम् । धूनुहि ॥८॥
>
> *nahi | tvā | rodasī iti | ubhe iti | ṛghāyamāṇam | invataḥ ||*
> *jeṣaḥ | svaḥ-vatīḥ | apaḥ | sam | gāḥ | asmabhyam | dhūnuhi ||8||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र ऋघायमाणं शत्रुवधं कुर्वाणं त्वां रोदसी उभे द्यावापृथिव्यावपि त्वदीयं महिमानं नहीन्वतः । व्याप्तुं न समर्थे इत्यर्थः । तादृशस्त्वं स्वर्वतीः स्वर्लोकयुक्ता अपो वृष्टिरूपा जेषः । जयेः । प्रेरयेत्यर्थः । अपां स्वर्गसंबन्धश्चान्यत्र दिवो वृष्टिं च्यावयति । तै. सं. ३-३-४-१ । इति श्रुतम् । किंच वृष्टिप्रदानादन्नसंपत्तेरूर्ध्वमस्मभ्यं क्षीरादिरसप्रदा गाः सं धूनुहि । सम्यक्प्रेरय ॥ नहि । नञो हिशब्देन सह सुपा । पा. २-१-४ । इति समासः । समासत्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । त्वा । अनुदात्तं सर्वमित्यनुवृत्तौ त्वामौ द्वितीयायाः । पा. ८-१-२३ । इति त्वादेशः । रोदसी । रुदेरसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । उगितश्च । पा. ४-१-६ । इति ङीप् । उभे । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । श्या [as printed] सहैकादेश उदात्तः । ऋघायमाणम् । …न्तीत्यृघा [?] । अन्येभ्यो ऽपि दृश्यन्त इति विच् । दृशिग्रहणस्य विध्यन्तरोपसंग्रहणार्थत्वान्नकारलोपो हकारस्य च घकारः । अनृघा ऋघा भवतीत्यभूततद्भावे लोहितादिडाज्भ्यः क्यष् । पा. ३-१-१३ । इति क्यष्प्रत्ययो भवति । स ह्याकृतिगणः । लोपश्च हलः । पा. ३-१-१२ । इत्यनुवृत्तेर्नकारलोपश्च । वा क्यषः । पा. १-३-९० । इत्यात्मनेपदम् । लटः शानच् । शपो ऽदुपदेशात्परत्वाच्छानचो लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । क्यषः प्रत्ययस्वरः । एकादेशस्योदात्तत्वम् । इन्वतः । इवि व्याप्तौ । इदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । लडादेशस्य तसश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । हि चेति निषेधात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति । जेषः । जेः प्रार्थनायां लिङर्थे लेट् । तस्य मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनं सिप् । इतश्च लोपः परस्मैपदेष्वितीकारलोपः । कर्तरि शपि प्राप्ते तदपवादः सिब्बहुलं लेटीति सिप् । अडागमस्यानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । स्वरासामस्तीति सर्वत्यः [sic: स्वर्वत्यः] । न्यङ्स्वरौ स्वरितौ । फि. ४-६ । इति स्वःशब्दः स्वरितः । मतुब्ङीपौ पित्त्वादनुदात्तौ । संहितायां स्वरितात्संहितायामनुदात्तानाम् । पा. १-२-३९ । इत्येकश्रुतिः । स्वरित एव शिष्यते । अपः । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । धूनुहि । धूञ् कम्पने । लोट् । सेर्ह्यपिच्च । स्वादिभ्यः श्नुः । उतश्च प्रत्ययादसंयोगपूर्वात् । पा. ६-४-१०६ । इति प्राप्तस्य लुकश्छान्दसत्वादभावः ॥

hyākṛtigaṇaḥ | lopaśca halaḥ | pā. 3-1-12 | ityanuvṛtternakāralopaśca | vā kyaṣaḥ | pā. 1-3-90 | ityātmanepadam | laṭaḥ śānac | śapo 'dupadeśātparatvācchānaco lasārvadhātukānudāttatvam | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | kyaṣaḥ pratyayasvaraḥ | ekādeśasyodāttatvam | invataḥ | ivi vyāptau | idito num dhātoriti num | śapaḥ pittvādanudāttatvam | laḍādeśasya tasaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | hi ceti niṣedhāttiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati | jeṣaḥ | jeḥ prārthanāyāṃ liṅarthe leṭ | tasya madhyamapuruṣaikavacanaṃ sip | itaśca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣvitīkāralopaḥ | kartari śapi prāpte tadapavādaḥ sibbahulaṃ leṭīti sip | aḍāgamasyānudāttatvāddhātusvara eva śiṣyate | svarāsāmastīti sarvatyaḥ [sic: svarvatyaḥ] | nyaṅsvarau svaritau | phi. 4-6 | iti svaḥśabdaḥ svaritaḥ | matubṅīpau pittvādanudāttau | saṃhitāyāṃ svaritātsaṃhitāyāmanudāttānām | pā. 1-2-39 | ityekaśrutiḥ | svarita eva śiṣyate | apaḥ | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | dhūnuhi | dhūñ kampane | loṭ | serhyapicca | svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ | utaśca pratyayādasaṃyogapūrvāt | pā. 6-4-106 | iti prāptasya lukaśchāndasatvādabhāvaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra! Even *rodasī ubhe* — both heaven and earth — *nahi invataḥ*: are not able to encompass your greatness, you who are *ṛghāyamāṇam*, bringing about the slaying of enemies. Being such, *jeṣaḥ* — conquer, i.e., send forth — *svarvatīḥ apaḥ*: the waters that belong to the world of heaven, in the form of rain. [That the waters are connected with heaven is heard elsewhere: 'he makes the rain fall from heaven' (Tai. Saṃ. 3-3-4-1).] Moreover, after the giving of rain and the abundance of food, *saṃ dhūnuhi* — send well — to us *gāḥ*, cows that yield milk and other juices." *(Grammar, noted briefly:* nahi *— compound of* nañ *with* hi *(Pā. 2-1-4), final-udātta;* tvā *— substitute for the accusative (Pā. 8-1-23), unaccented;* rodasī *— from* rud *with* asun*, initial-udātta, feminine* ṅīp *(Pā. 4-1-6);* ṛghāyamāṇam *— a denominative with* kyaṣ *in the sense "becoming a destroyer" (Pā. 3-1-13, 3-1-12), ātmanepada (Pā. 1-3-90), with* śānac*; one word at its head is not legible [?];* invataḥ *— root* ivi vyāptau *with* num*, not lowered after* hi*;* jeṣaḥ *— leṭ of* ji *in the sense of request, with* sip*;* svarvatīḥ *— "having heaven", the* svar *svarita (Phiṭ 4-6), one-tone (Pā. 1-2-39);* apaḥ *— case-ending udātta;* dhūnuhi *— root* dhūñ kampane*, the expected loss of* hi *(Pā. 6-4-106) not made, as a Vedic form.)*

### Page 424 — Rik 8: word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**ऋघायमाणम् (ṛghāyamāṇam)** — who bring about the slaying of enemies | **त्वाम् (tvām)** — your *(greatness)* | **उभे रोदसी (ubhe rodasī)** — both heaven and earth (the sky) | **नहि इन्वतः (nahi invataḥ)** — are not able to contain | *(such as you are)* **स्वर्वतीः (svarvatīḥ)** — which are in the world of heaven | **अपः (apaḥ)** — water in the form of rain | **जेषः (jeṣaḥ)** — conquer (that is, make the water fall on the earth as rain) | *(after that)* **अस्मभ्यम् (asmabhyam)** — to us | **गाः (gāḥ)** — cows | **सं धूनुहि (saṃ dhūnuhi)** — send.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! Your greatness, which destroys enemies, is so very great that heaven and earth cannot contain it. Now cause the waters that are in heaven to fall upon the earth as rain, and send us cows that give milk.

### Page 425 — Rik 8: English and Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Heaven and earth are unable to hold you (your exploits) the destroyer of your enemies; command the waters of heaven (so that they may fall upon earth as rain) and send us cows.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Rodasī"** — *dyāvāpṛthivī*: the worlds of earth and sky (*antarikṣa*), or the earth and the world of heaven. The word *rodasī* is read among the twenty-four words for heaven-and-earth, beginning with *svadhe*, *purandhī* (Ni. 3-21 [?] as printed; the second digit could be 2 or 7).

**"Ṛghāyamāṇam"** — **न्यन् हन्तीत्यृघा** (*nyan hantīty ṛghā*) *(the first word as printed reads न्यन्; the phrase partly illegible at the head of the* ṛghāyamāṇam *grammar on p. 424 is probably the same)* — "*ṛghā* means one who kills [or strikes] men — that is, one who destroys enemies."

**"Tvā"** — "you," that is, "your greatness."

**"Invataḥ"** — *ivi vyāptau* — "to pervade"; "unable to pervade" means that your greatness is so great that even the vast earth and sky cannot contain it — that is the idea.

**"Jeṣaḥ"** — "conquer": that is, the capacity that makes the waters, or the rain, pour as rain is under your control.

**"Svarvatīḥ"** — "that are in the world of heaven." Since rain falls from the sky (*antarikṣa*), and since the world of heaven is understood to be above the *antarikṣa*, it is customary to say that the water in the form of rain belongs to heaven. In this connection:

> एतद्वा अपां नामधेयं गुह्यं यदाधावा मान्दासु ते शुक्र शुक्रमा धूनोमीत्याहापामेव नामधेयेन गुह्येन दिवो वृष्टिमव रुन्धे शुक्रं ते शुक्रेण गृह्णामीत्याहैतद्वा अह्नो रूपं यद्रात्रिस्सूर्यस्य रश्मयो वृष्ट्या ईशते ऽह्न एव रूपेण सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्दिवो वृष्टिं च्यावयत्यस्मिन्नुग्रा अचुच्यवुरित्याह यथायजुरेवैतत् ॥
> *etadvā apāṃ nāmadheyaṃ guhyaṃ yadādhāvā māndāsu te śukra śukramā dhūnomītyāhāpāmeva nāmadheyena guhyena divo vṛṣṭimava rundhe śukraṃ te śukreṇa gṛhṇāmītyāhaitadvā ahno rūpaṃ yadrātrissūryasya raśmayo vṛṣṭyā īśate 'hna eva rūpeṇa sūryasya raśmibhirdivo vṛṣṭiṃ cyāvayatyasminnugrā acucyavurityāha yathāyajurevaitat ||*
> *(Taittirīya Saṃhitā; "the Taittirīya Saṃhitā says so" is the source's own attribution, without numbers; the Devanagari is a best reading of compressed print, and I have not attempted a translation of this passage.)*

**"Dhūnuhi"** — *dhūñ kampane*. Although this root has the senses of "shake" and "move," the Bhāṣyakāra and others take the sense "impel, send, give."

### Pages 426–429 — Rik 8 grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 426–429, noted briefly)*

**नहि (*nahi*)** — by "saha supā" (Pā. 2-1-4), a *subanta* compounds with a capable *subanta*, so *nañ* compounds with *hi*; being a compound, final-udātta by "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223). **त्वा (*tvā*)** — *yuṣmad* + accusative singular *am*; by "ṅe prathamayor am" (Pā. 7-1-28) the *am* is replaced by *am*, so that the ending counts as a substitute and "yo 'ci" (Pā. 7-2-89, the *y*-substitute before a vowel-initial ending not causing *ā* or *y*) does not apply; "tvamāv ekavacane" (Pā. 7-2-97) gives *tva* for the part up to *m*: *tva* + *ad* + *am*; "dvitīyāyāṃ ca" (Pā. 7-2-87) gives *ā* before the accusative; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), *savarṇa-dīrgha* by "akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-101), *pūrvarūpa* by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-107): *tvām*; then, under the headings "padasya", "padāt" and "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (8-1-18), "tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ" (Pā. 8-1-23) gives the unaccented substitute *tvā* when not at the beginning of a pāda. **रोदसी (*rodasī*)** — root *rud* + *asun* ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]), *laghūpadha-guṇa*, *rodas*, initial-udātta since *nit*; the *u* of *asun* being *it*, *rodas* is *ugit*, so *ṅīp* in the feminine by "ugitaś ca" (Pā. 4-1-6); *ṅīp* is *pit*, so unaccented. **उभे (*ubhe*)** — *ubha* is final-udātta by the stem accent; *ṭāp* by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (printed "8-1-4" [as printed], i.e. 4-1-4), unaccented as *pit*; *ubha* + *ā* → *savarṇa-dīrgha*, udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ"; before the nominative/accusative dual *au*, "auṅa āpaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-18) gives *śī*, the *ś* dropped as *it*: *ubhā* + *ī*, the *ī* unaccented as a *sup*; "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-87) gives *e*, udātta as a single substitute. **ऋघायमाणम् (*ṛghāyamāṇam*)** — "nṝn hanti" ["he slays men"] gives *ṛghā* in the nominative singular: with *nṝn* as *upapada*, *han* takes *vic* by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. 3-2-75); all of *vic* drops; as a *kṛdanta* it is a *prātipadika*; the *śas* is dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71); the word "dṛśyante" in the sūtra serves to include other operations, so the *n* of *nṛ* is dropped and the *h* of *han* becomes *gh*: *ṛghan*. In the sense "becoming *ṛghā*, which one was not" (*abhūtatadbhāva*), *kyaṣ* by "lohitādiḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣ" (Pā. 3-1-13), the Lohitādi being an open (*ākṛti*) group; *k* and *ṣ* are *it*; with "lopaś ca halaḥ" carried from "bhṛśādibhyo bhuvy acver lopaś ca halaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-12), the final consonant is dropped; the *a* lengthened by "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (printed "7-8-35" [as printed], i.e. 7-4-25): *ṛghāya*; *laṭ*; by "vā kyaṣaḥ" (Pā. 1-3-90) the ātmanepada *śānac* ("laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau"); *śap*: *ṛghāya* + *a* + *āna*; *śap* is unaccented as *pit*, and the *śānac*, a *lasārvadhātuka* after the *adupadeśa* *śap*, is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. 6-1-186); *kyaṣ* has the suffix accent; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), the single substitute udātta; *muk* by "āne muk" (Pā. 7-2-82), *n* → *ṇ*: *ṛghāyamāṇa*. *This derivation follows the Vṛttikāra; but in fact* kyaṣ *does not come here: the Lohitādi group contains only vowel-final words, and even as an open group* kyaṣ *does not come after a consonant-final word — the Mahābhāṣya on "lohitā…" says plainly "nāyaṃ halantād vidhīyate"; Kaiyaṭa, the Udyotakāra and the Kaumudī are cited in support, and the vārttika "lohitaḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣvacanam" with its rejection of the word ādi; there is also the Mahābhāṣya's separate denial for* n-*final words, "nāyaṃ nāntād vidhīyate". So the right derivation is: "ṛghā iva ācarati", with* kyaṅ *by "kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca" (Pā. 3-1-11) after a subanta denoting the standard of comparison and the agent: *ṛghan* + *su* + *ya*; as a *sanādi* form it is a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32), the *su* drops by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ"; by "naḥ kye" (Pā. 1-4-15) the *n*-final stem is a *pada* before *kyac*/*kyaṅ*, so the *n* drops by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7); since "nalopaḥ supsvarasaṃjñātugvidhiṣu kṛti" (Pā. 8-2-2) makes the loss "unseen" only for those rules, it is not unseen for lengthening ("pūrvatrāsiddham," Pā. 8-2-1), and "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-4-25) lengthens: *ṛghāya*; *kyaṅ* being *ṅit*, the ātmanepada by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (printed "1-3-1" [as printed], i.e. 1-3-12); the rest as above. **इन्वतः (*invataḥ*)** — root *ivi vyāptau*, *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58); *laṭ* third dual *tas*; *śap*; *ru* and visarga; *śap* unaccented as *pit*; by "tāsyanudāttenṅid…" (Pā. 6-1-186) the *lasārvadhātuka* after the *adupadeśa* is unaccented, so the root accent stands; "hi ca" (Pā. 8-1-34), with "aprātilomye" carried from "aṅgāprātilomye" (Pā. 8-1-33) — *aprātilomya* means favourableness — forbids the lowering of a verb joined with *hi*, so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) does not apply. **जेषः (*jeṣaḥ*)** — root *ji jaye*; *leṭ* in the sense of *liṅ* (prayer); second singular *sip*, its *p* *it* by "halantyam" (Pā. 1-3-3); the *i* dropped by "itaś ca lopaḥ parasmaipadeṣu" (Pā. 3-4-97); *śap* is set aside by "sibbahulaṃ leṭi" (Pā. 3-1-34): *ji* + *s* + *s*; the augment *aṭ* by "leṭo 'ḍāṭau" (printed "4-4-94" [as printed], i.e. 3-4-94); *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84); the first *s* → *ṣ* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59); *ru* and visarga: *jeṣaḥ*; the augment being unaccented, only the root accent stands. **स्वर्वतीः (*svarvatīḥ*)** — "svaḥ āsām asti": *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94); its *m* → *v* by "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. 8-2-15), *svar* ending in *r*, and also by "mādupadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-9), *svar* having *a* as penultimate: *svarvat*; *ṅīp* by "ugitaś ca" (Pā. 4-1-6): *svarvatī*; *matup* and *ṅīp* are unaccented as *pit*; *svar* is *svarita* by "nyaṅsvarau svaritau" (Phiṭ-sūtra "24" [?], first digit 2 or 7); in the Saṃhitā the unaccented syllables after a *svarita* are one-toned (*pracaya*) by "svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām" (Pā. 1-2-39); so the *svarita* of *svar* stands. **अपः (*apaḥ*)** — "ūḍidam-padādy-appum-raidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-171): the ending *śas* after *ap* is udātta. **धूनुहि (*dhūnuhi*)** — root *dhūñ kampane*, *loṭ* second singular *sip*, → *hi* by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87); *śnu* by "svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ": *dhūnuhi*; "utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt" (Pā. 6-4-106) would drop *hi* after the short *u* of a suffix not preceded by a conjunct, but by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (Paribhāṣā 35) it does not here.

**॥८॥**

### Page 430 — Sūkta 10, Rik 9

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आश्रु॑त्कर्ण श्रु॒धी ह॒वं नू चि॑द्दधिष्व मे॒ गिरः॑ ।
> इन्द्र॒ स्तोम॑मि॒मं मम॑ कृ॒ष्वा यु॒जश्चि॒दन्त॑रम् ॥९॥
>
> *ā́śrutkarṇa śrudhī́ haváṃ nū́ cid dadhiṣva me gíraḥ |*
> *indra stómam imáṃ máma kṛṣvā́ yujáś cid ántaram ||9||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आश्रुत्ऽकर्ण । श्रुधि । हवम् । नु । चित् । दधिष्व । मे । गिरः ॥
> इन्द्र । स्तोमम् । इमम् । मम । कृष्व । युजः । चित् । अन्तरम् ॥९॥
>
> *āśrut-karṇa | śrudhi | havam | nu | cit | dadhiṣva | me | giraḥ ||*
> *indra | stomam | imam | mama | kṛṣva | yujaḥ | cit | antaram ||9||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे आश्रुत्कर्ण सर्वतः श्रोतारौ कर्णौ यस्य तादृगिन्द्र हवमस्मदीयमाह्वानं नु क्षिप्रं श्रुधि । शृणु । मे मम होतुर्गिरश्चित्स्तुतीरपि दधिष्व । चित्ते धारय । किंच मम मदीयमिमं स्तोमं स्तोत्ररूपं वाक्यसमूहं युजश्चित्त्वत्स्वकीयसख्युरप्यन्तरं कृष्व । आसन्नं कुरु । यथा वचनं तस्य प्रियं मन्यसे तद्वदस्मदीयस्तुतिष्वपि प्रीतिं कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥ आश्रुत्कर्ण । आ समन्ताच्छृणुत इत्याश्रुत् । क्विप् । ह्रस्वस्य तुक् । पा. ६-१-७१ । तादृशौ कर्णौ यस्य । आमन्त्रितस्य चेत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । श्रुधि । श्रु श्रवणे । लोटो हिः । श्रुवः शृ च । पा. ३-१-७४ । इति विहितश्नोर्बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । तत्संनियोगशिष्टत्वाच्छृभावो ऽपि निवर्तते । श्रुशृणुपॄकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसि । पा. ६-४-१०२ । इति हेर्धिरादेशः । सतिशिष्टत्वात्प्रत्ययस्वरः । आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् । पा. ८-१-७२ । इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वेन पदादपरत्वात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति । संहितायामन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घः । हवम् । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यनैमित्तिके संप्रसारणे कृते पश्चादुकारान्तत्वेन ऋदोरप् । पा. ३-३-५७ । इत्यप्प्रत्ययः । अपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । नु । संहितायामृचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणाम् । पा. ६-३-१३३ । इति दीर्घः । चित् । चादिरनुदात्तः । दधिष्व । दधातेर्लोट् । थासः से । सवाभ्यां वामौ । पा. ३-४-९१ । शपः श्लुः । अभ्यासस्य ह्रस्वत्वादि । छन्दस्युभयथेत्यार्धधातुकस्यापि स्वेरिडागमः । आकारलोपः । निघातः । मम । तवममौ ङसि । पा. ७-२-९६ । इत्यनेन मपर्यन्तस्य ममादेशः । प्रातिपदिकस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते युष्मदस्मदोर्ङसि । पा. ६-१-२११ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । कृष्व । डुकृञ् करणे । लोट् । थासः से । सवाभ्यां वामौ । शपो बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । सतिशिष्टत्वात्प्रत्ययस्वरः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । युजः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अन्तरम् । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥
>
> *he āśrutkarṇa sarvataḥ śrotārau karṇau yasya tādṛgindra havamasmadīyamāhvānaṃ nu kṣipraṃ śrudhi | śṛṇu | me mama hoturgiraścitstutīrapi dadhiṣva | citte dhāraya | kiṃca mama madīyamimaṃ stomaṃ stotrarūpaṃ vākyasamūhaṃ yujaścittvatsvakīyasakhyurapyantaraṃ kṛṣva | āsannaṃ kuru | yathā vacanaṃ tasya priyaṃ manyase tadvadasmadīyastutiṣvapi prītiṃ kurvityarthaḥ || āśrutkarṇa | ā samantācchṛṇuta ityāśrut | kvip | hrasvasya tuk | pā. 6-1-71 | tādṛśau karṇau yasya | āmantritasya cetyādyudāttatvam | śrudhi | śru śravaṇe | loṭo hiḥ | śruvaḥ śṛ ca | pā. 3-1-74 | iti vihitaśnorbahulaṃ chandasīti luk | tatsaṃniyogaśiṣṭatvācchṛbhāvo 'pi nivartate | śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaśchandasi | pā. 6-4-102 | iti herdhirādeśaḥ | satiśiṣṭatvātpratyayasvaraḥ | āmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat | pā. 8-1-72 | ityavidyamānavattvena padādaparatvāttiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati | saṃhitāyāmanyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti dīrghaḥ | havam | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | bahulaṃ chandasītyanaimittike saṃprasāraṇe kṛte paścādukārāntatvena ṛdorap | pā. 3-3-57 | ityappratyayaḥ | apaḥ pittvāddhātusvaraḥ | nu | saṃhitāyāmṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām | pā. 6-3-133 | iti dīrghaḥ | cit | cādiranudāttaḥ | dadhiṣva | dadhāterloṭ | thāsaḥ se | savābhyāṃ vāmau | pā. 3-4-91 | śapaḥ śluḥ | abhyāsasya hrasvatvādi | chandasyubhayathetyārdhadhātukasyāpi sveriḍāgamaḥ | ākāralopaḥ | nighātaḥ | mama | tavamamau ṅasi | pā. 7-2-96 | ityanena maparyantasya mamādeśaḥ | prātipadikasvareṇāntodāttatve prāpte yuṣmadasmadorṅasi | pā. 6-1-211 | ityādyudāttatvam | kṛṣva | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | loṭ | thāsaḥ se | savābhyāṃ vāmau | śapo bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | satiśiṣṭatvātpratyayasvaraḥ | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | yujaḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvam | antaram | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O *āśrutkarṇa* — O Indra, whose two ears hear from all sides! *Havam*, our invocation, *nu* — quickly — *śrudhi*: hear. *Me giraś cit* — the praises of me, the invoker, too — *dadhiṣva*: hold in your mind. And further: *mama imam stomam* — this *stoma* of mine, this collection of sentences in the form of praise — *yujaś cid antaram kṛṣva*: make it near, even nearer than your own friend; bring it close. The sense is: as you regard a friend's word as dear, so take pleasure in our praises too." *(Grammar, noted briefly:* āśrutkarṇa *— "he whose ears hear from all around"; āśrut with* kvip *and* tuk *(Pā. 6-1-71), a vocative, initial-udātta;* śrudhi *— root* śru *with* hi*; the* śnu *of Pā. 3-1-74 dropped, and with it the* śṛ*-substitute;* hi *→* dhi *(Pā. 6-4-102); not lowered, as the preceding vocative counts as absent (Pā. 8-1-72); lengthened in the Saṃhitā;* havam *— root* hveñ *with* saṃprasāraṇa*, then* ap *by "ṛdor ap" (Pā. 3-3-57);* nū *— lengthened by Pā. 6-3-133;* dadhiṣva *— root* dhā*, loṭ ātmanepada (Pā. 3-4-91),* ślu*, the augment* iṭ *on* sva*, lowered;* mama *— by "tavamamau ṅasi" (Pā. 7-2-96), initial-udātta by Pā. 6-1-211;* kṛṣva *— śap dropped, suffix accent, not lowered as first in the pāda;* yujaḥ *— case-ending udātta;* antaram *— initial-udātta as a vṛṣādi word.)*

### Page 431 — Rik 9: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) आश्रुत्कर्ण ((he) āśrutkarṇa)** — O Indra, whose ears have the capacity to hear everything | **हवम् (havam)** — my invocation (that we call you with) | **नु (nu)** — quickly | **श्रुधि (śrudhi)** — hear | **मे (me)** — my (of the invoker) | **गिरः चित् (giraḥ cit)** — also the words (in the form of praise) | **दधिष्व (dadhiṣva)** — hold in your mind | *(and)* **मम (mama)** — my (that is, the one I make) | **इमं स्तोमम् (imaṃ stomam)** — this hymn | **अन्तरं युजः चित् कृष्व (antaraṃ yujaḥ cit kṛṣva)** — regard as dear, as the word of your friend.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! Your ears are able to hear everything, everywhere. Therefore hear quickly the invocation that we make, calling you; keep my words in mind; and regard this hymn that I make, or these sentences in the form of praise, as exceedingly dear, like the words of your friend.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, whose ears hear all things, listen quickly to my invocation; hold my praises (in four [sic] heart); keep near this my hymn as it were the words of a friend.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Āśrutkarṇa"** — **आ समन्ताच्छृणुत इत्याश्रुत् । तादृशौ कर्णौ यस्य सः । सर्वतः श्रोतारौ कर्णौ यस्य तादृगिन्द्र** (*ā samantācchṛṇuta ityāśrut | tādṛśau karṇau yasya saḥ | sarvataḥ śrotārau karṇau yasya tādṛgindra*) — "*āśrut* is one who hears all round; he who has such ears is *āśrutkarṇa*": [the sense is] "O Indra, who hears from every place, everywhere"; one whose ears are such that wherever Indra may be he hears — that is the idea of the poet about the hymns and words that we make.

### Page 432 — Rik 9: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Śrudhi," "nu," "kṛṣva"** — the final syllable of these words is lengthened in the Saṃhitā-pāṭha for the convenience of the meter.

**"Dadhiṣva me giraḥ"** — "hold our words, or our prayer, in your mind": that is, listen to what we pray, and keep it in memory so that you do not forget it.

**"Yujaścid antaram"** — the Bhāṣyakāra explains it as "dear [to you] as the words of friends." Although no word is present in this phrase to indicate the term "friends," the Bhāṣyakāra supplies *sakhyuḥ* ("of a friend") so that the sense fits.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 432–435, noted briefly)*

**आश्रुत्कर्ण (*āśrutkarṇa*)** — "ā samantāt (from all sides) śṛṇuta (hear)": the root *śru śravaṇe* with *ā* before it, and *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76); all the letters of *kvip* drop, but by "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam" (Pā. 1-1-62) the suffix still counts; so by "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk" (Pā. 6-1-71) *tuk* is added after the short vowel of the root before a *pit* *kṛt* suffix, giving *āśrut*; "āśrutau karṇau yasya saḥ" (a bahuvrīhi) gives the vocative *āśrutkarṇa*; initial-udātta as a vocative at the beginning by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198). **श्रुधी (*śrudhī*)** — root *śru śravaṇe*, *loṭ* parasmaipada second singular *sip*; *sip* → *hi*; "śṛ" for "śru" by "śruvaḥ śṛ ca" (Pā. 3-1-74) — the *śnu* that arises in the Veda is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73), and, if the *śnu* vikaraṇa has disappeared, the *śṛ* substitute that was prescribed in connection with it is also withdrawn, by the maxim "tat-sanniyoga-śiṣṭānām anyatarāpāye ubhayor apy apāyaḥ" (Paribhāṣā 86); "śṛṇu pṛkṛ-vṛ-bhyaś chandasi" (Pā. 6-4-102) gives *dhi* for *hi*; in *śrudhi* the suffix accent stands, being taught later (*satiśiṣṭa*); since *śrudhi* follows the word *āśrutkarṇa*, "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" would make it unaccented, but *āśrutkarṇa* is a vocative, and by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (printed "8-1-2" [?], i.e. 8-1-72) it counts as absent, so the verb does not stand after a *pada* and is not lowered; in the Saṃhitā "anyeṣām api dṛśyate" (printed "6-3-132" [?], i.e. 6-3-137) gives the lengthening, *śrudhī*. *(The grammar continues on p. 433.)*

### Pages 433–435 — Rik 9 grammar closes

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 433–435, noted briefly; the argument on pp. 434–435 is given in outline)*

**हवम् (*havam*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34) *saṃprasāraṇa* arises (*hve* → *hu*), then *pūrvarūpa* by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108); since it now ends in *u*, "ṛdor ap" (Pā. 3-3-57) gives *ap*, with *guṇa* and *av*: the suffix *ap* after a root ending in *u*/*ṛ*, giving *hava*; *ap* is *pit*, so unaccented; the accusative singular *am* with *pūrvarūpa* ("ami pūrvaḥ," printed "8-1-23" [as printed], i.e. 6-1-107), *havam*. **नु (*nu*)** — in the Saṃhitā the vowel is lengthened by "ṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām" (Pā. 6-3-133), *nū*. **चित् (*cit*)** — belongs to the *cādi* class, so unaccented ("cādayo 'nudāttāḥ," Phiṭ-sūtra 84). **दधिष्व (*dadhiṣva*)** — root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ* (*juhotyādi*); *loṭ* ātmanepada middle-second *thās*, *thās* → *se* (Pā. 3-4-80), *se* → *sva* (Pā. 3-4-91); *śap* (Pā. 3-1-68) is replaced by *ślu* ("juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ," Pā. 2-4-75); doubling by "ślau" (Pā. 6-1-10); the reduplicate's vowel shortened by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-59); *dh* → *d* in the reduplicate ("abhyāse carca," Pā. 8-4-54), giving *da-dhā-sva*; since in the Veda a suffix enjoined in the section on roots has both *sārvadhātuka* and *ārdhadhātuka* status ("chandasy ubhayathā," Pā. 3-4-117), *sva* is treated as *ārdhadhātuka*, so the augment *iṭ* arises ("ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ," Pā. 7-2-35); since it is also *sārvadhātuka*, "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-112) drops the *ā* of the root before it (as it is treated as *ṅit*); *s* → *ṣ* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59); *dadhiṣva*; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **ममु (*mama*)** — *asmad* + genitive singular *ṅas* (printed "jas" [sic] throughout); "tavamamau ṅasi" (Pā. 7-2-96) gives *mama* for the part of *asmad* up to *m*: *mama* + *ad* + *as*; "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97 [?], last digit unclear) gives *pararūpa* of the two *a*'s; "yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś" (Pā. 7-1-27) replaces *ṅas* by *aś*, which, being *śit*, replaces the whole ending by "anekālśit sarvasya"; "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-2-90) drops the last *a* if the stem's end follows; in the alternative that the final letter is dropped, the *a* is dropped and *mama* results; the long argument here (p. 434) concerns whether *aś* (replacement of *ṅas*) is barred by *sya* (the substitute of "ṭā-ṅasi-ṅasām inātsyāḥ," Pā. 7-1-12); it is argued that the *aś* rule would be pointless if *sya* applied, and that "yo 'ci" (Pā. 7-2-89) blocks *yā*-substitution, and so on; the paribhāṣā "yenāprāpte yo vidhir ārabhyate sa tasya bādhako bhavati" (Paribhāṣā 56 [?], first digit unclear) is discussed; and the *aṅgādhikāra* maxim "aṅgavṛtte punarvṛttāv avidhiḥ" (Paribhāṣā 92 [?], second digit 2 or 7) is quoted to show that after one *aṅga*-rule applies a second *aṅga*-rule does not; others take *aṅga* as "an operation aimed at the stem", which conflicts with the Mahābhāṣya on "jyād ādīyasaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-160), quoted; the discussion ends (p. 435) with the conclusion that the *a* of *aś* is to be joined by *pararūpa* with the preceding *a*, so the *sya* substitution does not arise; and that *mama* is final-udātta by its stem accent, which is set aside by "yuṣmadasmador ṅasi" (printed "yuṣmadasmador jasi" [sic], Pā. 6-1-211): before *ṅas*-type endings the first syllable of *yuṣmad*/*asmad* is udātta, giving initial-udātta. **कृष्व (*kṛṣva*)** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, *loṭ* ātmanepada *thās* → *se* → *sva*; the *e* replaced by *va*; the *u*-vikaraṇa ("tanādikṛñbhya uḥ," Pā. 3-1-79) is dropped by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *ṣatva* ("ādeśapratyayayoḥ"); the Saṃhitā lengthening ("dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ," Pā. 6-3-135), *kṛṣvā*; *śit*-like suffix accent; not lowered since it begins the pāda. **युजः (*yujaḥ*)** — "sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168): the case-ending is udātta. **अन्तरम् (*antaram*)** — belongs to the *vṛṣādi* class, so initial-udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. 6-1-203).

**॥९॥**

### Page 435 — Sūkta 10, Rik 10

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> वि॒द्मा हि त्वा॒ वृष॑न्तमं॒ वाजे॑षु हवन॒श्रुतं॑ ।
> वृष॑न्तमस्य हूमह ऊ॒तिं स॑हस्र॒सात॑माम् ॥१०॥
>
> *vidmā́ hi tvā vṛ́ṣantamaṃ vā́jeṣu havanaśrútaṃ |*
> *vṛ́ṣantamasya hūmaha ūtíṃ sahasrasā́tamām ||10||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> विद्म । हि । त्वा । वृषन्ऽतमम् । वाजेषु । हवनऽश्रुतम् ॥
> वृषन्ऽतमस्य । हूमहे । ऊतिम् । सहस्रऽसातमाम् ॥१०॥
>
> *vidma | hi | tvā | vṛṣan-tamam | vājeṣu | havana-śrutam ||*
> *vṛṣan-tamasya | hūmahe | ūtim | sahasra-sātamām ||10||*

### Page 436 — Rik 10: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, English

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वां विद्म । जानीमः । कीदृशं त्वाम् । वृषन्तमं कामानामतिशयेन वर्षितारं वाजेषु संग्रामेषु हवनश्रुतमस्मदीयस्याह्वानस्य श्रोतारम् । वृषन्तममस्यातिशयेन कामादीनां वर्षितुस्तवोतिं रक्षामस्मद्विषयामुद्दिश्य हूमहे । त्वामाह्वयामः । कीदृशीमूतिम् । सहस्रसातमामतिशयेन धनसहस्राणां दात्रीम् ॥ विद्म । विदो लटो वा । पा. ३-४-८३ । इति मसो मादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । द्व्यचो ऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घः । वृषन्तमम् । पृषु वृषु मृषु सेचने । कनिन्युवृषितक्षिराजिधन्विद्युप्रतिदिवः । उ. १-१५६ । इति कनिन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तमपः पित्त्वात्स एव शिष्यते । अयस्मयादीनि छन्दसि । पा. १-४-२० । इति भत्वेन पदत्वाभावान्नलोपाभावः । पा. ८-२-७ । वाजेषु । वाजशब्दो वृषादिराद्युदात्तः । हवनश्रुतम् । हू इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति ल्युटि संप्रसारणम् । हवनं शृणोतीति क्विप् । तुगागमः । वृषन्तमस्य । उक्तम् । हूमहे । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । शप इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । ऊतिम् । ऊतियूतीत्यादिनान्तोदात्तो निपातितः । सहस्रसातमाम् । सहस्रं सनोतीति सहस्रसाः । षणु दाने । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । पा. ३-२-६७ । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् । पा. ६-४-४१ । इत्याकारादेशः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । तमपः पित्त्वात्स एव शिष्यते ॥
>
> *he indra tvāṃ vidma | jānīmaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ tvām | vṛṣantamaṃ kāmānāmatiśayena varṣitāraṃ vājeṣu saṃgrāmeṣu havanaśrutamasmadīyasyāhvānasya śrotāram | vṛṣantamamasyātiśayena kāmādīnāṃ varṣitustavotiṃ rakṣāmasmadviṣayāmuddiśya hūmahe | tvāmāhvayāmaḥ | kīdṛśīmūtim | sahasrasātamāmatiśayena dhanasahasrāṇāṃ dātrīm || vidma | vido laṭo vā | pā. 3-4-83 | iti maso mādeśaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | vṛṣantamam | pṛṣu vṛṣu mṛṣu secane | kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ | u. 1-156 | iti kanin | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | tamapaḥ pittvātsa eva śiṣyate | ayasmayādīni chandasi | pā. 1-4-20 | iti bhatvena padatvābhāvānnalopābhāvaḥ | pā. 8-2-7 | vājeṣu | vājaśabdo vṛṣādirādyudāttaḥ | havanaśrutam | hū ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti lyuṭi saṃprasāraṇam | havanaṃ śṛṇotīti kvip | tugāgamaḥ | vṛṣantamasya | uktam | hūmahe | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | śapa ityanuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | ūtim | ūtiyūtītyādināntodātto nipātitaḥ | sahasrasātamām | sahasraṃ sanotīti sahasrasāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | pā. 3-2-67 | viḍvanoranunāsikasyāt | pā. 6-4-41 | ityākārādeśaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | tamapaḥ pittvātsa eva śiṣyate ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra! *Tvāṃ vidma* — we know you. What kind? *Vṛṣantamam* — the one who rains desires to the utmost; *vājeṣu* — in battles; *havanaśrutam* — the one who hears our invocation. For the protection (*ūtim*) of you, the *vṛṣantama* — the supreme showerer of desires and the like — directed at us, *hūmahe*: we call you. What kind of protection? *Sahasrasātamām* — that which, to the utmost, gives thousands of riches." *(The grammar of* vidma*,* vṛṣantamam*,* havanaśrutam*,* hūmahe*,* ūtim*,* sahasrasātamām *follows in the Sanskrit and is noted briefly:* vidma *— the substitute* ma *for* mas *in the* laṭ *of* vid *(Pā. 3-4-83), with the Saṃhitā lengthening;* vṛṣantamam *— root* vṛṣu secane *with* kanin *(Uṇ. 1-156), initial-udātta, then* tamap *(unaccented since* pit*); no loss of* n *because in the Veda the stem has* bha *status and so is not a* pada*;* havanaśrutam *— the* lyuṭ *from root* hve *with saṃprasāraṇa, then* kvip *with* tuk*;* hūmahe *— with saṃprasāraṇa, and the loss of* śap *by* bahulaṃ chandasi*;* ūtim *— final-udātta by the irregular formation "ūtiyūti…";* sahasrasātamām *— root* ṣaṇu dāne *with* viṭ*, the* ā *for the nasal, the second-member accent, and* tamap *unaccented as* pit*.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **त्वाम् (tvām)** — you | **वृषन्तमम् (vṛṣantamam)** — (as the bestower of desired things) the giver of rain | **वाजेषु (vājeṣu)** — in battles | **हवनश्रुतम् (havanaśrutam)** — one who hears our invocation (our cry for help) | **विद्म (vidma)** — we know | **हि (hi)** — indeed | **वृषन्तमस्य (vṛṣantamasya)** — of you, who rain down desires | **सहस्रसातमाम् (sahasrasātamām)** — which gives in thousands of ways | **ऊतिम् (ūtim)** — protection (or, for our protection) | **हूमहे (hūmahe)** — we call (we pray for).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! We know you as the giver of desired things and as one who hears our call in battles. Therefore, for your manifold protection, you who are the giver of rain in the form of desired things, we call upon you.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, we know you, the rainer of blessings, the hearer of our call in battles; we invoke the thousand-fold protection of you, the showerer of bounties.

### Pages 437–438 — Rik 10: Special Topics and grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The sense of this rik is easy to understand. There are no special difficulties, and no words that need supplying.

**"Vidma"** — the final syllable is lengthened for the convenience of the meter in the Saṃhitā.

**"Vṛṣantamam," "vṛṣantamasya"** — *vṛṣṭi-prada*, "bestower of rain"; that is, the one who gives us the rain in the form of desired ends.

**"Havanaśrutam"** — one who hears our invocation, who attends to our cry.

**"Sahasrasātamām"** — the explanation of this word was already given earlier (see "Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-3-9" as printed [?]; the word was explained at Sūkta 9, Ṛk 8).

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 437–438, noted briefly)*

**विद्म (*vidma*)** — root *vida jñāne* ("to know") with *laṭ*; in the parasmaipada the first-person plural *mas*; *śap* is dropped by *luk* ("adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ," Pā. 2-4-72); "vido laṭo vā" (Pā. 3-4-83): for the nine parasmaipada endings of *laṭ* after *vid* the substitutes *ṇal, atus, us, thal, athus, a, ṇal, va, ma* are optionally given, so *mas* → *ma*, giving *vidma*; the Saṃhitā lengthening by "dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-135), *vidmā*. **वृषन्तमम् (*vṛṣantamam*)** — root *pṛṣu, vṛṣu, mṛṣu secane*; *kanin* by "kaninyuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ" (Uṇ. 1-154 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 1-156); the *k* and *n* of *kanin* are lost as *it*, leaving *vṛṣ* + *an* → *vṛṣan*; initial-udātta since *nit*; then *tamap* in the sense of excess, unaccented since *pit* (so the initial-udātta stands); by "ayasmayādīni chandasi" (Pā. 1-4-20) the *bha* status prevents the *pada* status, so the *n* is not dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7). **वा (*vā*)** — *vāja* is a *vṛṣādi* word, so initial-udātta. **हवनश्रुतम् (*havanaśrutam*)** — root *hveñ* with *lyuṭ*; *lyuṭ* → *ana*; *hve* + *ana*: by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34), with "hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. 6-1-32) carried over, the *saṃprasāraṇa* of *hve* — *hu* — arises; with *pūrvarūpa*, *guṇa* and *av*, *havana*; "havanaṃ śṛṇoti iti": *kvip* after the root *śru* with *havana* as *upapada*; by "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk" (Pā. 6-1-71), *tuk*, giving *havanaśrut*; the accusative singular *am* gives *havanaśrutam*. **वृषन्तमस्य (*vṛṣantamasya*)** — the derivation of *vṛṣantama* was given earlier in this mantra; genitive singular. **हूमहे (*hūmahe*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *laṭ* ātmanepada first plural *mahiṅ*; "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. 3-4-79 [?], printed digits unclear) gives *e*; *śap*, which is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); "bahulaṃ chandasi" (printed "6-4-34" [as printed], i.e. 6-1-34) carries *saṃprasāraṇa*; then *pūrvarūpa* by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca"; "halaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-2) lengthens the *saṃprasāraṇa* at the end of an *aṅga* after a consonant: *hūmahe*. **ऊतिम् (*ūtim*)** — "ūtiyūtijūtisātihetikīrtayaś ca" (Pā. 3-3-97): these *ktin* words are irregularly udātta on the end. **सहस्रसातमाम् (*sahasrasātamām*)** — "sahasraṃ sanoti iti sahasrasāḥ": root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *ṣ* → *s* (Pā. 6-1-64), *ṇ* → *n*; *viṭ* after *jana*, *sana*, *khana*, *krama*, *gama* in the Veda (Pā. 3-2-67); the nasal replaced by *ā* before *viṭ* and *van* (Pā. 6-4-41); *savarṇa-dīrgha*, *sahasrasā*; second-member accent; *tamap* is *pit*, so unaccented; *sahasrasā* keeps the accent of the earlier formation; being feminine, *tamā* + *ṭāp* ("ajādyataṣṭāp," no number printed); *ṭāp* is *pit*; *savarṇa-dīrgha* (by "antaratamaḥ" the *ā* in place of the two) is unaccented; accusative singular *am*, *pūrvarūpa* by "ami pūrvaḥ" (printed "8-1-23" [as printed], i.e. 6-1-107): *sahasrasātamām*.

**॥१०॥**

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 2: a stroke over स of सहस्र followed by a bar under ह, as printed — [accent ?].)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आ तू न॑ इन्द्र कौशिक मन्दसा॒नः सु॒तं पि॑ब ।
> न॒व्यमायुः॒ प्र सू ति॑र कृ॒धी स॑ह॒स्रसामृ॑षिम् ॥११॥ [accent ?]
>
> *ā tū́ na indra kauśika mandasānáḥ sutáṃ piba |*
> *navyám āyuḥ prá sū́ tira kṛdhī́ sahasrásā́m ṛṣim ||11||* [accent ?]

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आ । तु । नः । इन्द्र । कौशिक । मन्दसानः । सुतम् । पिब ॥
> नव्यम् । आयुः । प्र । सु । तिर । कृधि । सहस्रऽसाम् । ऋषिम् ॥११॥
>
> *ā | tu | naḥ | indra | kauśika | mandasānaḥ | sutam | piba ||*
> *navyam | āyuḥ | pra | su | tira | kṛdhi | sahasra-sām | ṛṣim ||11||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र तु क्षिप्रं नो ऽस्मान्प्रत्या गच्छेति शेषः । हे कौशिक कुशिकस्य पुत्रेन्द्र मन्दसानो हृष्यो भूत्वा सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पिब । यद्यपि विश्वामित्रः कुशिकस्य पुत्रस्तथापि तद्रूपेणेन्द्रस्यैवोत्पन्नत्वात्कुशिकपुत्रत्वमविरुद्धम् । अयं वृत्तान्तो ऽनुक्रमणिकायामुक्तः । कुशिकस्त्वैषीरथिरिन्द्रतुल्यं पुत्रमिच्छन्ब्रह्मचर्यं चकार । तस्येन्द्र एव गाथी पुत्रो जज्ञे । अनु. ऋग्वे. ३-१ । इति । हे इन्द्र नव्यं सर्वैर्देवैः स्तुत्यं कर्मानुष्ठानपरमायुर्जीवितं प्र सू तिर । प्रकर्षेण सुष्ठु वर्धय । ततो मां सहस्रसां सहस्रसंख्याकलाभोपेतमृषिमतीन्द्रियद्रष्टारं कृधि । कुरु ॥ तु । संहितायामृचि तुनुघमक्षुतङ्कुत्रोरुष्याणामिति दीर्घः । नः । संहितायामुदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः । इन्द्र । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । कौशिक । निघातः । मन्दसानः । हृष्यन् । मदि स्तुतिमोदमदस्वप्नकान्तिगतिषु । आसानजित्यनुवृत्तौ वञ्जिवृधिमन्दिसहिभ्यः कित् । उ. २-८६ । इत्यसानच्प्रत्ययः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । सुतम् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । नव्यम् । णु स्तुतौ । अचो यत् । गुणः । वान्तो यि प्रत्यये । पा. ६-१-७९ । इत्यवादेशः । यतो ऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । आयुः । उसिनिदित्यनुवृत्तावेतेर्णिच्च । उ. २-११९ । इत्युसिप्रत्ययः । णित्त्वाद्वृद्ध्यायादेशौ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सु । निपातस्य चेति संहितायां दीर्घत्वम् । तिर । तरतेर्व्यत्ययेन शः । ऋत इद्धातोः । पा. ७-१-१०० । इतीत्त्वम् । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । कृधि । डुकृञ् करणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपो लुक् । श्रुशृणुपॄकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसीति हेर्धिरादेशः । सहस्रसाम् । उक्तम् । ऋषिम् । ऋषी गतौ । इन्नित्यनुवृत्तावि गुपधात्कित् । कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥
>
> *he indra tu kṣipraṃ no 'smānpratyā gaccheti śeṣaḥ | he kauśika kuśikasya putrendra mandasāno hṛṣyo bhūtvā sutamabhiṣutaṃ somaṃ piba | yadyapi viśvāmitraḥ kuśikasya putrastathāpi tadrūpeṇendrasyaivotpannatvātkuśikaputratvamaviruddham | ayaṃ vṛttānto 'nukramaṇikāyāmuktaḥ | kuśikastvaiṣīrathirindratulyaṃ putramicchanbrahmacaryaṃ cakāra | tasyendra eva gāthī putro jajñe | anu. ṛgve. 3-1 | iti | he indra navyaṃ sarvairdevaiḥ stutyaṃ karmānuṣṭhānaparamāyurjīvitaṃ pra sū tira | prakarṣeṇa suṣṭhu vardhaya | tato māṃ sahasrasāṃ sahasrasaṃkhyākalābhopetamṛṣimatīndriyadraṣṭāraṃ kṛdhi | kuru || tu | saṃhitāyāmṛci tunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇāmiti dīrghaḥ | naḥ | saṃhitāyāmudāttādanudāttasya svaritaḥ | indra | āmantritanighātaḥ | kauśika | nighātaḥ | mandasānaḥ | hṛṣyan | madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu | āsānajityanuvṛttau vañjivṛdhimandisahibhyaḥ kit | u. 2-86 | ityasānacpratyayaḥ | cittvādantodāttaḥ | sutam | pratyayasvaraḥ | navyam | ṇu stutau | aco yat | guṇaḥ | vānto yi pratyaye | pā. 6-1-79 | ityavādeśaḥ | yato 'nāva ityādyudāttatvam | āyuḥ | usinidityanuvṛttāveterṇicca | u. 2-119 | ityusipratyayaḥ | ṇittvādvṛddhyāyādeśau | nittvādādyudāttatvam | su | nipātasya ceti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvam | tira | taratervyatyayena śaḥ | ṛta iddhātoḥ | pā. 7-1-100 | itīttvam | ato heriti herluk | kṛdhi | ḍukṛñ karaṇe | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaśchandasīti herdhirādeśaḥ | sahasrasām | uktam | ṛṣim | ṛṣī gatau | innityanuvṛttāvi gupadhātkit | kittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra, *tu* — quickly — come to us (this is to be supplied). O *kauśika* — O Indra, son of Kuśika — *mandasānaḥ* — being glad — *sutam piba*: drink the pressed Soma. Although Viśvāmitra is the son of Kuśika, yet since Indra himself was born in that form, his being Kuśika's son is not contradictory. This story is told in the Anukramaṇikā: 'Kuśika, the son of Iṣīratha, wishing for a son equal to Indra, practised celibacy; Indra himself was born to him as his son Gāthin' (Anu. Ṛgve. 3-1). O Indra, *navyam āyuḥ pra sū tira*: increase greatly and well [our] *āyuḥ*, life, *navyam* — praiseworthy by all the gods, devoted to the performance of rites. Then *kṛdhi* — make — me *sahasrasām* — endowed with gains reckoned in thousands — a *ṛṣi*, a seer of what is beyond the senses." *(Grammar, noted briefly:* tū *— lengthened in the Saṃhitā;* naḥ *— svarita after an udātta in the Saṃhitā;* indra*,* kauśika *— vocatives, lowered;* mandasānaḥ *— root* madi *with* asānac *(Uṇ. 2-86), final-udātta;* navyam *— root* ṇu stutau *with* yat*,* av *before* y *(Pā. 6-1-79), initial-udātta;* āyuḥ *— from* iṇ *with* usi *(Uṇ. 2-119), vṛddhi and* āy*, initial-udātta;* sū *— lengthened as a particle;* tira *— root* tṝ *with* śa *by Vedic exchange,* i *(Pā. 7-1-100), loss of* hi*;* kṛdhi *— śap dropped,* hi *→* dhi*;* ṛṣim *— root* ṛṣī gatau *with* in*, kit, initial-udātta.)*

### Page 440 — Rik 11: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **तु (tu)** — quickly | **नः (naḥ)** — our (to our side) | **आ (gaccha)** — come | **(हे) कौशिक ((he) kauśika)** — O Indra, son of Kuśika | *(you)* **मन्दसानः (mandasānaḥ)** — being glad | **सुतम् (sutam)** — the Soma-juice, pressed and prepared | **पिब (piba)** — drink | **नव्यम् (navyam)** — [which is] requested (that is, desired) | **आयुः (āyuḥ)** — life | **प्र सु तिर (pra su tira)** — increase specially (for me) | **सहस्रसाम् (sahasrasām)** — [one who is] winning thousands of gains | **ऋषिम् (ṛṣim)** — a seer | **कृधि (kṛdhi)** — make (me).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! Come quickly to us, and drink with delight this Soma-juice that we have pressed. Increase our life, and make me, an ordinary person, one who gains thousands of benefits.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Come quickly, Indra, son of Kusika, and drink the soma libation with delight; prolong the life which we merit and make me a Rishi abnndantly [sic] endowed with thousands of benefits.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Tu," "su," "kṛdhi"** — the final syllables of these words in this rik are lengthened for the convenience of the meter.

**"Ā"** — in this rik only the prefix *ā* occurs; with it the verb *gaccha* ("come") has to be supplied. Such usages are needed in the Ṛgveda.

**"Kauśika"** — here Indra is addressed as the son of Kuśika. In this connection the Bhāṣyakāra cites an account from the Anukramaṇikā:

> कुशिकस्त्वैषीरथिरिन्द्रतुल्यं पुत्रमिच्छन् ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्येन्द्र एव गाथी पुत्रो जज्ञे ॥ (ऋ. अनु. ३-१)
> *kuśikas tv aiṣīrathir indra-tulyaṃ putram icchan brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasyendra eva gāthī putro jajñe || (ṛ. anu. 3-1)*
> "Kuśika, the son of Iṣīratha, wishing a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity; Indra himself was born as his son, Gāthin."

Skandasvāmī, on this subject:

> अत्र चेतिहासमाचक्षते । इषीरथपुत्रः कुशिको नाम राजा पुत्रमिन्द्रतुल्यं कामयमानो ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्य गाथी नामेन्द्र एव स्वयं पुत्रो जात इति ॥
> *atra cetihāsam ācakṣate | iṣīrathaputraḥ kuśiko nāma rājā putram indra-tulyaṃ kāmayamāno brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasya gāthī nāmendra eva svayaṃ putro jāta iti ||*
> "Here they tell a legend: a king named Kuśika, son of Iṣīratha, desiring a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity; Indra himself was born to him as a son named Gāthin."

### Page 441 — Rik 11: Special Topics (continued)

**Veṅkaṭamādhava:**

> पुत्रमिन्द्रसमम् इच्छन् कुशिको ब्रह्मचर्यं चचार । तस्येन्द्रः स्वयमेव पुत्रो ऽभूत् । सास्य कौशिकता ॥
> *putram indra-samam icchan kuśiko brahmacaryaṃ cacāra | tasyendraḥ svayam eva putro 'bhūt | sāsya kauśikatā ||*
> "Desiring a son equal to Indra, Kuśika practised celibate austerity; Indra himself became his son. That is his Kauśika-hood."

The chief point is this: in ancient times a king named Iṣīratha had a son called Kuśika. He, desiring a son equal to Indra, practised celibate austerity. Then Indra himself was born as his son, under the name Gāthin. The sage Viśvāmitra was the son of King Gāthin; and since Madhucchandas, the seer who saw this rik, was born in the family of Viśvāmitra, he addresses Indra, born in his own family — that is, in the family of Kuśika — as "Kauśika."

**"Navyam"** — the Bhāṣyakāra says that the word *navya* is another form of the root *ṇu stutau*, and explains it as *sarvair devaiḥ stutyaṃ karmānuṣṭhānaparam* — "that is to be praised by all gods, devoted to the performance of rites," or, as the Kannada gloss gives it, "that is wanted by all, even the gods": that is, long life, as everyone naturally desires to live long. Or, as Skandasvāmī says, if the word *navyam* is given the sense "new" (*navam* — fresh), then the sense would be: a new vitality for the words *navyam āyuḥ* — or, to bring out the underlying idea, a still greater lifespan henceforth. In sum: "make us live long; increase our life — *prolong our life*" [the source's own English].

**"Sahasrasām"** — thousands of gains, benefits, or many kinds of desired things.

**"Ṛṣim"** — the root *ṛṣī gatau* ("to go") has the senses of motion and knowledge; so *ṛṣi* means one who knows, one endowed with wisdom, or — as the Bhāṣyakāra says — **अतीन्द्रियद्रष्टारम्** (*atīndriyadraṣṭāram*): a great person with the power to know things beyond the reach of the outer senses. Here "ṛṣi" means Madhucchandas, the seer who saw this mantra. When he prays to Indra, "give me long life and make me an excellent seer," he does not use a first-person verb but a third-person usage.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 441–443, noted briefly)*

**तु (*tu*)** — in the Saṃhitā lengthened by "ṛcitunughamakṣutaṅkutroruṣyāṇām" (Pā. 6-3-133); a *nipāta*, initial-udātta ("nipātā ādyudāttāḥ," Phiṭ-sūtra 80). *(The grammar continues on p. 442.)*

### Pages 442–443 — Rik 11 grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 442–443, noted briefly)*

**नः (*naḥ*)** — *nas* replaces *asmān* by "bahuvacanasya vasnasau" (Pā. 8-1-21); unaccented as a substitute; in the Saṃhitā it becomes *svarita* by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-66) after an udātta. **इन्द्र (*indra*)**, **कौशिक (*kauśika*)** — vocatives, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). **मन्दसानः (*mandasānaḥ*)** — *hṛṣyan* ("rejoicing"); root *madi stuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu*; by "ṛñjivṛdhimandisahibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. 2-244 [as printed]), with *asānac* carried over from "chandasy asānac chujyābhyām" (Uṇ. 2-243 [as printed]), the suffix *asānac*, *kit*, comes after *ṛji bharjane*, *vṛdhu vṛddhau*, *madi stuti…* and *ṣaha marṣaṇe*; the source remarks that the Bālamanoramā reads the roots there as *ṛji gatau* and *madī harṣe*, but *ṛji gatau* is not found in the Dhātupāṭha (only *ṛja gatau*), and *madī harṣe* is not *idit* and so takes no *num*; so "mandi" in the sūtra would not fit, and the reading may be due to a copyist's or proof-reader's slip; the suffix is *cit*, so final-udātta ("citaḥ," Pā. 6-1-163). **सुतम् (*sutam*)** — *kta*-ending; the suffix accent. **नव्यम् (*navyam*)** — root *ṇu stutau*; *ṇ* → *n* ("ṇo naḥ," Pā. 6-1-65); *yat* after a vowel-ending root ("aco yat," printed "3-1-96" [as printed], i.e. 3-1-97), *nu* + *ya*; since *ya* is an *ārdhadhātuka*, *guṇa* ("sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ"), *u* → *o*; then "vānto yi pratyaye" (Pā. 6-1-79): before a *y*-initial suffix *o* and *au* become *av* and *āv*, so *no* → *nav*; *navya*; "yato 'nāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-213) gives initial-udātta; accusative singular *navyam*. **आयुः (*āyuḥ*)** — by "eter ṇic ca" (Uṇ. 2-283 [?] as printed), with *usi* carried over from "janer usiḥ" (Uṇ. 2-286 [as printed]) and *nit* from "artipṛvapiyajitanidhanitapibhyo nit" (Uṇ. 2-284 [as printed]), the suffix *usi* comes after *iṇ gatau*, being both *ṇit* and *nit*; *i* + *us*: *vṛddhi* by "aco ñṇiti" (Pā. 7-2-115) — *i* → *ai*; then *ai* → *āy* ("eco 'yavāyāvaḥ," Pā. 6-1-78), *āyus*; *ru* and visarga, *āyuḥ*; initial-udātta, "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). **सु (*su*)** — in the Saṃhitā lengthened by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. 6-3-136). **तिर (*tira*)** — root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ* (*bhvādi*); *loṭ* second singular *sip*; *sip* → *hi* by "seryapicca" (Pā. 3-4-87); *śap* should arise but by Vedic inversion the vikaraṇa *śa* arises, which is *apit* and so *ṅit*-like; hence "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4) and no *guṇa* by "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5); "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-100): *i* in place of the *ṛ*, the final, by "alo 'ntyasya" (Pā. 1-1-52); then "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51): *tir*; *hi* is dropped after a stem ending in *a* ("ato heḥ," Pā. 6-4-105); *tira*. **कृधि (*kṛdhi*)** — root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, *loṭ*, *sip*, *hi*; the *śap* is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); *hi* → *dhi* by "śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi" (6-4-102). **सहस्रसाम् (*sahasrasām*)** — explained in the earlier mantra (Rik 10). **ऋषिम् (*ṛṣim*)** — root *ṛṣī gatau*; by "igupadhāt kit" (Uṇ. 4-559 [as printed]) with *in* carried from "sarvadhātubhya in" (Uṇ. 4-557 [as printed]), the suffix *in*, *kit*, after a root with *ik* in the penultimate position, so *ṛṣ* + *in*; the suffix is *kit*, so no *guṇa*; *nit*, so initial-udātta ("ñnityādir nityam," Pā. 6-1-197); the accusative singular *am* with *pūrvarūpa* gives *ṛṣim*.

**॥११॥**

> वृ॒द्धायु॒मनु॒ वृद्ध॑यो॒ जुष्टा॑ भवन्तु॒ जुष्ट॑यः ॥१२॥ [accent ?]

> *pari tvā girvaṇo gíra imā́ bhavantu viśvátaḥ |* [accent ?]

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> परि । त्वा । गिर्वणः । गिरः । इमाः । भवन्तु । विश्वतः ॥
> वृद्धऽआयुम् । अनु । वृद्धयः । जुष्टाः । भवन्तु । जुष्टयः ॥१२॥
>

> *vṛddha-āyum | anu | vṛddhayaḥ | juṣṭāḥ | bhavantu | juṣṭayaḥ ||12||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> प्रवर्ग्ये परि त्वेत्यभिष्टुयात् । स्पृष्ट्वोदकमिति खण्डे परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिरो ऽधि द्वयोरदधा उक्थ्यं वचः । आ. ४-६ । इति सूत्रितम् । तथा हविर्धानप्रवर्तने सेयं परिधानीया । हविर्धाने प्रवर्तयन्तीति खण्डे परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इति परिदध्यात् । आ. ४-९ । इति सूत्रितम् । तथा ब्राह्मणं च । परि त्वा गिर्वणो गिर इत्युत्तमया परिदधाति । ऐ. ब्रा. १-२९ । इति ॥
>
> *pravargye pari tvetyabhiṣṭuyāt | spṛṣṭvodakamiti khaṇḍe pari tvā girvaṇo giro 'dhi dvayoradadhā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ | ā. 4-6 | iti sūtritam | tathā havirdhānapravartane seyaṃ paridhānīyā | havirdhāne pravartayantīti khaṇḍe pari tvā girvaṇo gira iti paridadhyāt | ā. 4-9 | iti sūtritam | tathā brāhmaṇaṃ ca | pari tvā girvaṇo gira ityuttamayā paridadhāti | ai. brā. 1-29 | iti ||*
>
> हे गिर्वणो ऽस्मदीयस्तुतिभागिन्द्र विश्वतः सर्वेषु कर्मसु प्रयुज्यमाना इमा गिरो ऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतयस्त्वां परि भवन्तु । सर्वतः प्राप्नुवन्तु । कीदृश्यो गिरः । वृद्धायुमनु प्रवृद्धेनायुष्येणोपेतं त्वामनुसृत्य वृद्धयो वर्धमानाः । किंचैता गिरो जुष्टास्त्वया सेविताः सत्यो जुष्टयो ऽस्माकं प्रीतिहेतवो भवन्तु ॥ गिर्वणः । गीर्भिर्वन्यत इति गिर्वणाः । वन षण संभक्तौ । सर्वधातुभ्यो ऽसुन् । गिर उपधाया दीर्घाभावश्छान्दसः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । विश्वतः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । वृद्धायुम् । वृधु वृद्धौ । क्तप्रत्ययः । उदितो वा । पा. ७-२-५६ । इतीटः क्त्वाप्रत्यये विकल्पितत्वाद्यस्य विभाषा । पा. ७-२-१५ । इति निष्ठायामिडभावः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । इण् गतौ । छन्दसीणः । उ. १-२ । इत्युण् । णित्त्वाद्वृद्धिः । आयादेशश्च । वृद्धमायुर्यस्य । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वृद्धयः । वृधेः क्तिनि तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु च । पा. ७-२-९ । इतीडभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । जुष्टाः । श्वीदितो निष्ठायाम् । पा. ७-२-१४ । इतीडभावः । जुष्टार्पिते चेत्यनुवृत्तौ नित्यं मन्त्रे । पा. ६-१-२१० । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । जुष्टयः । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । क्तिन् । तितुत्रेतीडभावः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥ २० ॥
>
> *he girvaṇo 'smadīyastutibhāgindra viśvataḥ sarveṣu karmasu prayujyamānā imā giro 'smadīyāḥ stutayastvāṃ pari bhavantu | sarvataḥ prāpnuvantu | kīdṛśyo giraḥ | vṛddhāyumanu pravṛddhenāyuṣyeṇopetaṃ tvāmanusṛtya vṛddhayo vardhamānāḥ | kiṃcaitā giro juṣṭāstvayā sevitāḥ satyo juṣṭayo 'smākaṃ prītihetavo bhavantu || girvaṇaḥ | gīrbhirvanyata iti girvaṇāḥ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | gira upadhāyā dīrghābhāvaśchāndasaḥ | āmantritanighātaḥ | viśvataḥ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvam | vṛddhāyum | vṛdhu vṛddhau | ktapratyayaḥ | udito vā | pā. 7-2-56 | itīṭaḥ ktvāpratyaye vikalpitatvādyasya vibhāṣā | pā. 7-2-15 | iti niṣṭhāyāmiḍabhāvaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | iṇ gatau | chandasīṇaḥ | u. 1-2 | ityuṇ | ṇittvādvṛddhiḥ | āyādeśaśca | vṛddhamāyuryasya | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vṛddhayaḥ | vṛdheḥ ktini titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca | pā. 7-2-9 | itīḍabhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | juṣṭāḥ | śvīdito niṣṭhāyām | pā. 7-2-14 | itīḍabhāvaḥ | juṣṭārpite cetyanuvṛttau nityaṃ mantre | pā. 6-1-210 | ityādyudāttatvam | juṣṭayaḥ | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | ktin | titutretīḍabhāvaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ || 20 ||*

**Translation:** "In the *pravargya* one should praise with *pari tvā*: in the section beginning *spṛṣṭvodakam* it is laid down, '*pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ*, *adhi dvayor adadhā ukthyaṃ vacaḥ*' (Āśvalāyana 4-6). Likewise, in the moving forward of the *havirdhāna* carts this [ṛk] is the closing verse: in the section *havirdhāne pravartayanti* it is laid down, 'one should close with *pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ*' (Āśvalāyana 4-9). And the Brāhmaṇa too: 'he closes with the last [ṛk], *pari tvā girvaṇo giraḥ*' (Ai. Brā. 1-29). O *girvaṇaḥ* — O Indra, sharer in our praises — *imāḥ giraḥ*, these our praises, used *viśvataḥ*, in all rites, *tvāṃ pari bhavantu*: may they reach you on all sides. What kind of praises? *Vṛddhāyum anu* — following you, who are endowed with grown life; *vṛddhayaḥ* — growing. And further: may these praises, *juṣṭāḥ* — enjoyed by you — become *juṣṭayaḥ*, the causes of our delight." *(Grammar, noted briefly:* girvaṇaḥ *— "he who is served with praises", root* vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau *with* asun*, no lengthening of* gir *as a Vedic form, lowered as a vocative;* viśvataḥ *— the syllable before the suffix udātta;* vṛddhāyum *— vṛddha *from* vṛdhu *with* kta*, no* iṭ *(Pā. 7-2-56, 7-2-15);* āyu *from* iṇ *with* uṇ *(Uṇ. 1-2); a bahuvrīhi with the first-member accent;* vṛddhayaḥ *— ktin*, no* iṭ *(Pā. 7-2-9), initial-udātta;* juṣṭāḥ *— no* iṭ *(Pā. 7-2-14), initial-udātta by "nityaṃ mantre" (Pā. 6-1-210);* juṣṭayaḥ *— root* juṣī *with* ktin*, initial-udātta. The bhāṣya closes "॥ २० ॥", the twentieth varga.)*

### Page 445 — Rik 12: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) गिर्वणः ((he) girvaṇaḥ)** — O Indra, worthy of being praised by us | **विश्वतः (viśvataḥ)** — in all (that is, in all the rites in which we make use of them) | **इमाः गिरः (imāḥ giraḥ)** — these words in the form of praise | **त्वा (tvā)** — you | **परि भवन्तु (pari bhavantu)** — may they come from every side and join (you) | **वृद्धायुम् (vṛddhāyum)** — you who have long life | **अनु (anu)** — following | **वृद्धयः (vṛddhayaḥ)** — growing | **जुष्टाः (juṣṭāḥ)** — [the words] served (accepted) by you | **जुष्टयः (juṣṭayaḥ)** — [may they be] the means of giving us delight | **भवन्तु (bhavantu)** — may they be.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra, lover of praise! May these words of praise that we make come to you from every side and bring you delight. As these words give you delight, may your life-span (your strength) increase; and as these words of ours bring you delight, may they bring delight to us as well.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O deserver of praise, may these our praises be on all occasions around you (accepted by you); may they increase your power, O long-lived, and being agreeable to you, may they become our enjoyments.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The sense of this rik is very involved (difficult); the intention does not fit together properly, and what the seer means is not clearly known.

**"Girvaṇaḥ"** — **गीर्भिर्वन्यत इति गिर्वणाः । वन षण संभक्तौ । अस्मदीयस्तुतिभाक्** (*gīrbhir vanyata iti girvaṇāḥ | vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau | asmadīya-stuti-bhāk*) — "one who is served with praises; the root *vana*/*ṣaṇa* in the sense of sharing: one who partakes of our praise": that is, one who is worshipped with our words, who is praised, who is worthy of praise.

**"Viśvataḥ"** — in all places, or on all occasions.

**"Vṛddhāyum"** — **प्रवृद्धेनायुष्येणोपेतम्** (*pravṛddhenāyuṣyeṇopetam*) — "endowed with increased lifespan": endowed with a life that is great or growing, one who lives for a long time. Skandasvāmī explains this word as *vṛddhān śatrūn atigantāram* — "one who overcomes enemies that have grown great," one who subdues enemies.

**"Anu"** — *anusṛtya*, *prāpya* — "following," "reaching": that is, may the hymns we make reach you; may you hear them.

### Page 446 — Rik 12: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Vṛddhayaḥ"** — *vardhamānāḥ* — growing; much, specially, flourishing, abundant.

**"Juṣṭāḥ," "juṣṭayaḥ"** — the root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ* has the senses "to be fond of" and "to serve"; so these words mean "that which gives delight, that which is an object of delight."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 446–447, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)** — "gīrbhir vanyate iti girvaṇāḥ": root *gṝ śabde* (*kryādi*) with *kvip* ("kvip ca," Pā. 3-2-76); "ṛta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-100) gives *i* in place of *ṛ*, which, as an *alo 'ntyasya* substitute, comes at the end; root *vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau* with *asun* ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-638 [?] [as printed]); *gir* + *bhis* + *vanas* receive the technical name *prātipadika*, and by "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71) *bhis* is dropped; by *pratyaya-lakṣaṇa* *gir* counts as a *pada*; so "vor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-76): the penultimate *ik* of a stem ending in *r* or *v* is lengthened at the end of a *pada*, which would lengthen the *i* of *gir*; but "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (Paribhāṣā 35) makes this optional, so it does not arise; the vocative singular *su* is added to *girvaṇas*, the *su* dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisy apṛktaṃ hal" (Pā. 6-1-68); *ru* and visarga: *girvaṇaḥ*; a vocative, unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). **विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)** — from *tasil*, which is *l*-marked, so the vowel before it is udātta ("liti," Pā. 6-1-193). **वृद्धायुम् (*vṛddhāyum*)** — root *vṛdhu vṛddhau* with *kta*; *vṛdh* + *ta*; *vṛdh* is *udit*, so by "udito vā" (Pā. 7-2-56) the *iṭ* augment before *ktvā* is optional (the print then discusses whether *kta* too takes *iṭ*, citing "yasya vibhāṣā" (Pā. 7-2-15): a suffix beginning *kt*-/*ktavat* does not take *iṭ* after a root to which *iṭ* is optional); so the *iṭ* that "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-35) would give is barred; *vṛdh* + *ta* → by "jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-40) *t* → *dh* after a *jhaṣ*; then *dh* + *dh* → *ddh* by "jhalāṃ jaś jhaśi" (Pā. 8-4-53): *vṛddha*; the root *iṇ gatau*, with *uṇ* in the Veda ("chandasīṇaḥ," Uṇ. 1-2), *uṇ* being *ṇit*, so *vṛddhi* ("aco ñṇiti," Pā. 7-2-115) gives *ai* + *u*, then "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78) gives *āy* + *u* → *āyu*; *vṛddham āyur yasya saḥ*: *vṛddhāyuḥ*, a bahuvrīhi, with the first member's accent ("bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam," Pā. 6-2-1); accusative singular *vṛddhāyum*. **वृद्धयः (*vṛddhayaḥ*)** — *ktin* ("striyāṃ ktin," Pā. 3-3-94) after *vṛdh*; the *iṭ* augment does not arise by "ti, tu, tra, ta, tha, si, su, sara, ka, seṣu ca" (Pā. 7-2-9); *th* → *dh* and *j*-type changes as before: *vṛddhi*; initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-17 [as printed]); nominative plural *vṛddhayaḥ*. **जुष्टाः (*juṣṭāḥ*)** — root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*, *idit*; *kta*; "śvīditaḥ niṣṭhāyām" (Pā. 7-2-14): after *śvi* and *idit* roots, *niṣṭhā* does not take *iṭ*, so *kta* has no augment; the suffix accent would arise but is set aside by "nityaṃ mantre" (Pā. 6-1-210), and *juṣṭa* and *arpita* are, by the previous sūtra's carried-over words "juṣṭārpite ca chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-209), always initial-udātta in the mantra. **जुष्टयः (*juṣṭayaḥ*)** — root *juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*, *ktin*; the augment *iṭ* barred by "ti-tu-tra…." (Pā. 7-2-9); "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) turns *t* → *ṭ*: *juṣṭi*; initial-udātta by the *nit* accent; nominative plural *juṣṭayaḥ*.

**॥१२॥**

*iti daśamaṃ sūktaṃ samāptam |*
"Thus the tenth sūkta is completed."
