### Page 475 — Rik 7: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं मायिनं नानाविधकपटोपेतं शुष्णं भूतानां शोषणहेतुमेतन्नामकमसुरं मायाभिस्तत्प्रतिकूलैः कपटविशेषैः । यद्वा । तद्विधोपायगोचरप्रज्ञाभिः । अवातिरः । हिंसितवानसि । एतच्च यास्केनोक्तम् । इन्द्रः शुष्णं जघान । नि. ३-११ । इति । शुष्णं पिप्रुम् । ऋग्वे. १-१०३-८ । इत्यादिमन्त्रे चायमर्थो विस्पष्टः । मेधिरा मेधावन्तो ऽनुष्ठातारस्तस्य तादृशस्य ते तव महिमानं विदुः । जानन्ति । तेषां जानतामनुष्ठातॄणां श्रवांस्यन्नान्युत्तिर । वर्धय । केतः केतुरित्यादिष्वेकादशसु प्रज्ञानामसु माया वयुनमिति पठितम् । श्रवःशब्दं यास्को निर्वक्ति । श्रव इत्यन्ननाम श्रूयत इति सतः । नि. १०-३ । इति ॥ मायाभिः । माङ् माने । माच्छाससिसूभ्यो यः । उ. ४-१०९ । इति यप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मायिनम् । मायास्यास्तीति मायी । व्रीह्यादित्वादिनिप्रत्ययः । पा. ५-२-११६ । प्रत्ययस्वरः । शुष्णम् । शुष शोषणे । अस्मादन्तर्भावितण्यर्थान्निदित्यनुवृत्तौ तृषिशुषिरसिभ्यः कित् । उ. ३-१२ । इति नप्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अतिरः । तरतेर्लङि व्यत्ययेन शः । तस्य ङित्त्वेन गुणाभावादृत इद्धातोरितीत्त्वम् । रपरत्वम् । विदुष्टे तस्य । गतं मन्त्रे गतम् । मेधिराः । मिधृ मेधृ मेधाहिंसनयोः । औणादिक इरन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । श्रवांसि । नब्विषयत्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥
>
> *he indra tvaṃ māyinaṃ nānāvidhakapaṭopetaṃ śuṣṇaṃ bhūtānāṃ śoṣaṇahetumetannāmakamasuraṃ māyābhistatpratikūlaiḥ kapaṭaviśeṣaiḥ | yadvā | tadvidhopāyagocaraprajñābhiḥ | avātiraḥ | hiṃsitavānasi | etacca yāskenoktam | indraḥ śuṣṇaṃ jaghāna | ni. 3-11 | iti | śuṣṇaṃ piprum | ṛgve. 1-103-8 | ityādimantre cāyamartho vispaṣṭaḥ | medhirā medhāvanto 'nuṣṭhātārastasya tādṛśasya te tava mahimānaṃ viduḥ | jānanti | teṣāṃ jānatāmanuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ śravāṃsyannānyuttira | vardhaya | ketaḥ keturityādiṣvekādaśasu prajñānāmasu māyā vayunamiti paṭhitam | śravaḥśabdaṃ yāsko nirvakti | śrava ityannanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ | ni. 10-3 | iti || māyābhiḥ | māṅ māne | mācchāsasisūbhyo yaḥ | u. 4-109 | iti yapratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | māyinam | māyāsyāstīti māyī | vrīhyāditvādinipratyayaḥ | pā. 5-2-116 | pratyayasvaraḥ | śuṣṇam | śuṣa śoṣaṇe | asmādantarbhāvitaṇyarthānnidityanuvṛttau tṛṣiśuṣirasibhyaḥ kit | u. 3-12 | iti napratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | atiraḥ | taraterlaṅi vyatyayena śaḥ | tasya ṅittvena guṇābhāvādṛta iddhātoritīttvam | raparatvam | viduṣṭe tasya | gataṃ mantre gatam | medhirāḥ | midhṛ medhṛ medhāhiṃsanayoḥ | auṇādika iran | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | śravāṃsi | nabviṣayatvādādyudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra! You *avātiraḥ* — slew — *śuṣṇam*, the asura of that name, *māyin* — possessed of various kinds of trickery — and the cause of the drying up of beings, *māyābhiḥ* — with special devices of deceit opposed to his; or [alternatively] with *prajñā*s, insights into such means. This Yāska says: '*indraḥ śuṣṇaṃ jaghāna*' (Ni. 3-11); and this sense is clear in the mantra beginning *śuṣṇaṃ pipruṃ* (Ṛgveda 1-103-8). *Medhirāḥ* — the wise performers — *viduḥ te* — know your greatness, of such a one. For those who thus know, *uttira* — increase — *śravāṃsi*, foods. Among the eleven words for 'wisdom' beginning with *ketaḥ* and *ketuḥ*, *māyā* and *vayunam* are read. Yāska explains the word *śravas*: '*śravas* is a name for food; because it is heard (*śrūyate*)' (Ni. 10-3)." (Grammatical tail: *māyā* — *māṅ māne* with *ya* by "mācchā-sasi-sūbhyo yaḥ" (Uṇ. 4-109), suffix accent; *māyinam* — "māyā asya asti," *ini* as one of the *vrīhyādi* (Pā. 5-2-116), suffix accent; *śuṣṇam* — *śuṣa śoṣaṇe* with causative sense, *na* by "tṛṣi-śuṣi-rasibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. 3-12) with *nit* carried over, initial-udātta; *atiraḥ* — *laṅ* of *tṝ* with *śa* by exception, no *guṇa* because it is *ṅit*, so *i* by "ṛta id dhātoḥ", with *r*; *viduṣ ṭe tasya* — as in the previous mantra; *medhirāḥ* — *midhṛ medhṛ medhāhiṃsanayoḥ*, the Uṇādi *iran*, initial-udātta as *nit*; *śravāṃsi* initial-udātta as a *nab-viṣaya* word.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) इन्द्र ((he) indra)** — O Indra | **त्वम् (tvam)** — you | **मायिनम् (māyinam)** — endowed with many kinds of trickery | **शुष्णम् (śuṣṇam)** — the asura named Śuṣṇa who harms people | **मायाभिः (māyābhiḥ)** — by deceitful stratagems suited to the occasion, or by [your] intelligence and capacity | **अव अतिरः (ava atiraḥ)** — have destroyed | **मेधिराः (medhirāḥ)** — wise people | **विदुः (viduḥ)** — know | **तेषाम् (teṣām)** — to those | *(that is, to those who perform sacrifices and the like, being wise)* **श्रवांसि (śravāṃsi)** — foods (food and other nourishment) | **उत् तिर (ut tira)** — increase (give in abundance).

### Page 476 — Rik 7: overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra! The asura named Śuṣṇa was exceedingly deceitful. You killed that asura of deceitful nature by deceitful stratagems, or by your own intelligence and power. Wise people know this greatness of yours. Give them food and other nourishment in abundance.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Indra, you killed the wily Sushna by your stratagems; the wise men have known this your greatness; bestow upon them abundant food.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Māyābhiḥ," "māyinam"** — *māyā* means a special kind of deceit, a device, a means, power and capacity: *wile, stratagem, etc.* [the source's English]. A couple of riks that explain this sense of the word *māyā* are given below:

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-8; the "१" after तन्वं is printed so.)*

> रूपं रूपं मघवा बोभवीति मायाः कृण्वानस्तन्वं१ परि स्वाम् ॥
>
> *rūpaṃ rūpaṃ maghavā bobhavīti māyāḥ kṛṇvānastanvaṃ1 pari svām ||*

*("Maghavan becomes form after form, making māyās about his own body" — mine and tentative.)*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-18.)*

> इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश ॥
>
> *indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa ||*

*("Indra goes about, of many forms, by his māyās; for his ten hundred bay horses are yoked" — mine and tentative.)*

There are many such examples. Since the word *māyā* is read among the eleven words for "wisdom" beginning with *ketaḥ*, *ketuḥ* (Ni. 3-13), *māyā* also means *prajñā*, understanding, intelligence, a means, and so on. In considering this sense *prajñā*, the sage Yāska in the Nirukta, explaining the rik

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6.)*

> मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् ।
> माया मू तु यज्ञियानामेतामपो यत्तूर्णिश्चरति प्रजानन् ॥
>
> *mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūryo jāyate prātarudyan |*
> *māyā mū tu yajñiyānāmetāmapo yattūrṇiścarati prajānan ||*

says

> मूर्धा मूर्तमस्मिन्धीयते मूर्धा यः सर्वेषां भूतानां भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते प्रातरुद्यन्स एव प्रज्ञां त्वेतां मन्यन्ते यज्ञियानां देवानां यज्ञसंपादिनामपो यत्कर्म चरति प्रजानन्सर्वाणि स्थानान्यनुसंचरते त्वरमाणः
>
> *mūrdhā mūrtamasmindhīyate mūrdhā yaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūryo jāyate prātarudyansa eva prajñāṃ tvetāṃ manyante yajñiyānāṃ devānāṃ yajñasaṃpādināmapo yatkarma carati prajānansarvāṇi sthānānyanusaṃcarate tvaramāṇaḥ*

(Ni. "7-27" [?]) — thus plainly giving the word *māyā* the sense *prajñā*; and also —

### Page 477 — Rik 7: Special Topics (continued)

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-58-1.)*

> शुक्रं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्विषुरूपे अहनी द्यौरिवासि ।
> विश्वा हि माया अवसि स्वधावो भद्रा ते पूषन्निह रातिरस्तु ॥
>
> *śukraṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadviṣurūpe ahanī dyaurivāsi |*
> *viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣanniha rātirastu ||*

*("Bright is one [form] of yours, worshipful the other; you are like the sky, with the two days of different form; for you protect all māyās, O self-powered one; may your bounty be auspicious here, O Pūṣan" — mine and tentative.)*

in the explanation of this rik too —

> शुक्रं ते अन्यल्लोहितं ते अन्यद्यजतं ते अन्यद्यज्ञियं ते अन्यद्विषमरूपे ते अहनी कर्म द्यौरिव चासि सर्वाणि प्रज्ञानान्यवस्यन्नवन्भाजनवती ते पूषन्निह दत्तिरस्तु ॥
>
> *śukraṃ te anyallohitaṃ te anyadyajataṃ te anyadyajñiyaṃ te anyadviṣamarūpe te ahanī karma dyauriva cāsi sarvāṇi prajñānānyavasyannavanbhājanavatī te pūṣanniha dattirastu ||*

(Ni. "12-17" [?]) — he explained the word *māyā* as *prajñā*.

**"Śuṣṇam"** — the asura named Śuṣṇa. The word *śuṣṇa* also means strength (Ni. 3-9). There are many riks that tell of Indra's killing the asura Śuṣṇa:

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-103-8.)*

> शुष्णं पिप्रुं कुयवं वृत्रमिन्द्र यदावधीर्वि पुरः शम्बरस्य ॥
>
> *śuṣṇaṃ pipruṃ kuyavaṃ vṛtramindra yadāvadhīrvi puraḥ śambarasya ||*

*("When, O Indra, you slew Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava, Vṛtra, [you broke] apart the forts of Śambara" — mine and tentative.)*

In this rik it is said that when Indra destroyed the city of the asura Śambara he killed four asuras, Śuṣṇa, Pipru, Kuyava and Vṛtra.

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-11.)*

> उग्रो ययिं निरपः स्रोतसासृजद्वि शुष्णस्य दृंहिता ऐरयत्पुरः ॥
>
> *ugro yayiṃ nirapaḥ srotasāsṛjadvi śuṣṇasya dṛṃhitā airayatpuraḥ ||*

*("The mighty one let out the rushing waters with a stream; he shook apart the firm forts of Śuṣṇa" — mine and tentative.)*

In this rik it is said that Indra laid siege to the city of the asura Śuṣṇa. There are many riks suggesting such a sense. Besides this, the word *śuṣṇa* can be given the sense *śoṣayitṛ*, "one who dries up." In such contexts the sense can be given that Indra, by his power, strikes the cloud that does not pour rain and makes the earth parch, and so brings about rain. In considering this sense Yāska,

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-5.)*

> नियुद्व्वणक्षि [?] श्वसनस्य मूर्धनि शुष्णस्य चिद्व्रन्दिनो रोरुवद्वना ॥
>
> *niyudvvaṇakṣi [?] śvasanasya mūrdhani śuṣṇasya cidvrandino roruvadvanā ||*

in explaining this rik, explained the word *śuṣṇa* as *śoṣayituḥ*, "one who dries up": "शुष्णस्यादित्यस्य च शोषयितुः" (*śuṣṇasyādityasya ca śoṣayituḥ*) (Ni. 5-16); and also,

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-33-12.)*

> न्याविध्यदिलीबिशस्य दृळ्हा वि शृङ्गिणमभिनच्छुष्णमिन्द्रः ॥
>
> *nyāvidhyadilībiśasya dṛḷhā vi śṛṅgiṇamabhinacchuṣṇamindraḥ ||*

in this rik too, "निरविध्यदिलाबिलशयस्य दृढानि व्यभिनच्छृङ्गिणं शुष्णमिन्द्रः" (*niravidhyadilābilaśayasya dṛḍhāni vyabhinacchṛṅgiṇaṃ śuṣṇamindraḥ*): that is, he explained that Indra struck the cloud that stays over the mountain top and, not pouring rain, makes the earth dry up (Ni. "6-20" [?]).

### Page 478 — Rik 7: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Ava atiraḥ"** — *hiṃsitavān asi*: "you have struck, smitten, killed."

**"Viduḥ te"** — "they know you or yours": that is, they know your greatness, or your power and capacity.

**"Medhirāḥ"** — *medhāvantaḥ puruṣāḥ*: wise, discerning people and the like.

**"Śravāṃsi"** — foods, food and nourishment. In explaining the rik *āsasrāṇāsaḥ śavasā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-62-3 [?]) Yāska gives the word *śravas* the sense of food: "śrava ity annanāma śrūyata iti sataḥ" (Ni. 10-3).

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 478–479, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**मायाभिः (*māyābhiḥ*)** — root *māṅ māne*; "mācchāsasi(sū)bhyo yaḥ" (Uṇ. "4-549" [?]): after *māṅ māne*, *cho chedane*, *ṣasa svapne*, the suffix *ya*: *māya*, final-udātta by the suffix accent; for the feminine, *ṭāp* by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (Pā. 4-1-4), unaccented as *pit*; *savarṇa*-lengthening, and the single substitute udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5); then *bhis*, *ru* and visarga; *bhis* unaccented, made svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ". **मायिनम् (*māyinam*)** — "māyā asya asti": "vrīhyādibhyaś ca" (Pā. 5-2-116) gives *ini* and *ṭhan* in the possessive sense after the words of the *vrīhi* group: *ini*; the *ā* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148); accusative singular *am*: *māyinam*; the suffix accent. **शुष्णम् (*śuṣṇam*)** — root *śuṣa śoṣaṇe*, with the causative sense included; "tṛṣi-śuṣi-rasibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. "3-292" [?]): after *ñitṛṣā pipāsāyām*, *śuṣa śoṣaṇe*, *rasa śabde* the suffix *na*, *kit* and *nit*; *kit*, so no *laghūpadha-guṇa*; the *nit* accent; *ṇ* by "raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade" (Pā. 8-4-1): *śuṣṇa*. **अतिरः (*atiraḥ*)** — root *tṝ plavanataraṇayoḥ*, *bhvādi*; *laṅ*, second singular *sip*; *śap*, replaced by Vedic exception by *śa*: *tṝ* + *a* + *s*; "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4) makes *śa* *ṅit*, so no *guṇa*;

"ṛta id dhātoḥ" (printed "17-1-100" [sic]) gives *i*, with *r*; the augment *aṭ* by "luṅ-laṅ-lṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-71): *atiras*; *ru* and visarga. **विदुष्टे तस्य (*viduṣ ṭe tasya*)** — these three words were explained in the previous mantra; but there [*viduḥ*] stands at the beginning of the fourth pāda, here at the beginning of the third pāda — that is the only difference. **मेधिराः (*medhirāḥ*)** — root *midhṛ medhṛ medhāhiṃsanayoḥ*; after *midhṛ* the Uṇādi suffix *iran*; being *nit*, the *nit* accent. **श्रवांसि (*śravāṃsi*)** — initial-udātta by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya" (Phiṭ-sū. ### Page 479 (lower) — Rik 8: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(runs onto p. 480; the closing "॥२१॥" is printed so — the varga number.)*

> स्तोमाः स्तोतार ऋत्विज ओजसा बलेनेशानं जगतो नियामकमिन्द्रमभ्यनूषत । सर्वत्र स्तुतवन्तः । यस्येन्द्रस्य रातयो धनदानानि सहस्रं सहस्रसंख्योपेतानि सन्ति । उत वाथवा भूयसीः सहस्रसंख्याया अप्यधिकाः सन्ति । तमिन्द्रमिति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ इन्द्रम् । ऋज्रेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ईशानम् । लटः शानच् । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । धातोरनुदात्तेत्त्वात्तास्यनुदात्तेत्यादिना शानचो ऽनुदात्तत्वम् । ओजसा । नब्विषयत्वादाद्युदात्तः । स्तोमाः । अर्तिस्तुस्वित्यादिना मन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अनूषत । णु स्तुतौ । णो नः । लुङ् । व्यत्ययेन झः । तस्यादादेशः । पा. ७-१-५ । च्लेः सिच् । अस्य धातोः कुटादित्वेन सिचो ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । इडभावश्छान्दसः । दीर्घत्वं च । अडागमः । सहस्रम् । कर्दमादीनां च । फि. ३-१० । इति द्वितीयाक्षरमुदात्तम् । रातयः । मन्त्रे वृषेत्यादिना क्तिन्नुदात्तः । उत । प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । वा । चादिरनुदात्तः । सन्ति । प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति प्रतिषेधात् । स हि व्यवहिते ऽपि भवतीत्युक्तम् । भूयसीः । सहस्रादतिशयेन बह्व्यो भूयस्यः । अत्र विभक्तव्यस्य सहस्रस्य संनिधिबलादुपपदत्वप्रतीतेर्द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ । पा. ५-३-५७ । इति बहुशब्दादीयसुन् । बहोर्लोपो भू च बहोः । पा. ६-४-१५८ । इतीकारलोपः । प्रकृतेर्भू इत्यादेशश्च । ईयसुनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । उगितश्चेति ङीप् ॥२१॥
>
> *stomāḥ stotāra ṛtvija ojasā baleneśānaṃ jagato niyāmakamindramabhyanūṣata | sarvatra stutavantaḥ | yasyendrasya rātayo dhanadānāni sahasraṃ sahasrasaṃkhyopetāni santi | uta vāthavā bhūyasīḥ sahasrasaṃkhyāyā apyadhikāḥ santi | tamindramiti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || indram | ṛjrendretyādinā ran | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | īśānam | laṭaḥ śānac | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | dhātoranudāttettvāttāsyanudāttetyādinā śānaco 'nudāttatvam | ojasā | nabviṣayatvādādyudāttaḥ | stomāḥ | artistusvityādinā manpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | anūṣata | ṇu stutau | ṇo naḥ | luṅ | vyatyayena jhaḥ | tasyādādeśaḥ | pā. 7-1-5 | cleḥ sic | asya dhātoḥ kuṭāditvena sico ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | iḍabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | dīrghatvaṃ ca | aḍāgamaḥ | sahasram | kardamādīnāṃ ca | phi. 3-10 | iti dvitīyākṣaramudāttam | rātayaḥ | mantre vṛṣetyādinā ktinnudāttaḥ | uta | prātipadikasvaraḥ | vā | cādiranudāttaḥ | santi | pratyayādyudāttatvam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati yadvṛttānnityamiti pratiṣedhāt | sa hi vyavahite 'pi bhavatītyuktam | bhūyasīḥ | sahasrādatiśayena bahvyo bhūyasyaḥ | atra vibhaktavyasya sahasrasya saṃnidhibalādupapadatvapratīterdvivacanavibhajyopapade tarabīyasunau | pā. 5-3-57 | iti bahuśabdādīyasun | bahorlopo bhū ca bahoḥ | pā. 6-4-158 | itīkāralopaḥ | prakṛterbhū ityādeśaśca | īyasuno nittvādādyudāttatvam | ugitaśceti ṅīp ||21||*

**Translation:** "The *stomāḥ* — the praisers, the priests — with *ojas*, strength, *abhy anūṣata*: praised on all sides Indra, *īśānam*, the ruler who governs the world; *yasya* — of which Indra — the *rātayaḥ*, gifts of wealth, *sahasraṃ santi*, are a thousand in number; *uta vā* — or — *bhūyasīḥ*, are more even than a thousand. 'That Indra' is the connection with what precedes." (Grammatical tail: *indram* — *ran* by "ṛjrendra…", initial-udātta as *nit*; *īśānam* — *śānac* for *laṭ*, *śap* dropped, the *śānac* unaccented because the root is *anudātta*-marked ("tāsy anudātta…"); *ojasā* initial-udātta as a *nab-viṣaya* word; *stomāḥ* — *man* by "arti-stu-su…", initial-udātta; *anūṣata* — *ṇu stutau*, *n* by "ṇo naḥ", *luṅ*, *jha* by exception, *at* for it (Pā. 7-1-5), *sic* for *cli*, no *guṇa* because, the root being *kuṭādi*, *sic* is *ṅit*, the absence of *iṭ* and the lengthening Vedic, augment *aṭ*; *sahasram* — second syllable udātta by "kardamādīnāṃ ca" (Phi. 3-10); *rātayaḥ* — *ktin* udātta by "mantre vṛṣa…"; *uta* — the stem accent; *vā* unaccented as one of the *cādi*; *santi* — initial-udātta of the suffix, and not unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" because of the bar "yad-vṛttān nityam", which applies even with words between; *bhūyasīḥ* — "more than a thousand": since *sahasra*, the thing to be divided, is near, it is felt as an *upapada*, so *īyasun* after *bahu* by "dvivacana-vibhajyopapade tarab-īyasunau" (Pā. 5-3-57); "bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-158) drops the *ī* and gives *bhū* for the stem; initial-udātta as *nit*; *ṅīp* by "ugitaś ca".)

### Page 480 — Rik 8: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**यस्य (yasya)** — of which Indra | **रातयः (rātayaḥ)** — gifts of wealth | **सहस्रम् (sahasram)** — as many as thousands | **उत वा (uta vā)** — or | **भूयसीः (bhūyasīḥ)** — still more | **सन्ति (santi)** — are *(such)* | **ईशानम् (īśānam)** — who governs the world | **इन्द्रम् (indram)** — Indra | **स्तोमाः (stomāḥ)** — the priests who praise | **ओजसा (ojasā)** — with all the strength they have | **अभि अनूषत (abhi anūṣata)** — praise.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Indra gives to those who praise him wealth and the like to the number of a thousand, or even more. The priests and other people praise such an Indra using all their strength.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The reciters of Sacred hymns praise with all their might Indra, the ruler of the world whose bounties are counted by thousends [sic] or even more.

**Īśānam** — the lord, the master of the world: "Thr [sic] ruler of the world" [the source's English].

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Ojasā"** — *balena*: "with strength, with all the strength they have; with enthusiasm too," and so on.

**"Stomāḥ"** — for this word the Bhāṣyakāra gives the meaning *stotāra ṛtvijaḥ*, "priests who praise." When the word *stoma* is neuter it means "hymn"; when it is masculine, "those who praise."

**"Sahasram"** — a thousand in number; many.

**"Bhūyasīḥ"** — more than a thousand; more than can be counted; exceedingly, and so on.

### Page 481 — Rik 8 grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 481–482, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**इन्द्रम् (*indram*)** — the suffix *ran* by "ṛjrendrāgra…" (Uṇ. 2-186); initial-udātta as *nit*. **ईशानम् (*īśānam*)** — root *īśa aiśvarye*, *anudātta*-marked, hence ātmanepada; *laṭ* → *śānac* by "laṭaḥ śatṛ-śānacau…": *īś* + *āna*; *śap* dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); the *śānac*, a *sārvadhātuka* in place of a *lakāra*, unaccented by "tāsy anudātteṭ…" (Pā. 6-1-186). **ओजसा (*ojasā*)** — initial-udātta by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya" (Phiṭ-sū. "26"). **स्तोमाः (*stomāḥ*)** — *man* after *stu* by "arti-stu-su…" (Uṇ. "1-138" [?]); the *nit* accent, initial-udātta. **अनूषत (*anūṣata*)** — root *ṇu stutau*; *n* for *ṇ* by "ṇo naḥ" (Pā. 6-1-65); *luṅ*, *cli* by "cli luṅi" (Pā. 3-1-43), *sic* by "cleḥ sic" (3-1-44); the root is *parasmaipada*, so the third plural should properly be *jhi*, but here by exception the ātmanepada *jha* comes; *at* for *jh* by "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. 7-1-5): *nu* + *s* + *ata*; the root is in the *kuṭādi* list, so by "gāṅ-kuṭādibhyo 'ñṇin ṅit" (Pā. 1-2-1) *sic* is *ṅit* and there is no *guṇa*; by Vedic procedure no *iṭ*; the lengthening of the root vowel is also Vedic; augment *aṭ*: *anūṣata*. **सहस्रम् (*sahasram*)** — by "kardamādīnāṃ ca" (Phiṭ-sū. "59" [?]) the first or the second syllable is udātta: here the second. **रातयः (*rātayaḥ*)** — after *rā*, the udātta *ktin* by "mantre vṛṣeṣa-paca-mana-vida-bhū-vīrā udāttaḥ" (Pā. 3-3-96). **उत (*uta*)** — the stem accent. **वा (*vā*)** — unaccented by "cādayo 'nudāttāḥ" (Phiṭ-sū. 84). **सन्ति (*santi*)** — root *as bhuvi*; *laṭ*, *jhi*, *ant* for *jh*; *śap* dropped; *a* of the root dropped by "śnasor allopaḥ" (printed "vā. sū." [sic] 6-4-111): *santi*, with the accent of the *tiṅ* suffix. The bar "yad-vṛttān nityam" (Pā. 8-1-66), as was explained earlier, applies even when words stand between, because *pūjita* is taken again in the sūtra "pūjanāt pūjitam…"; so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" does not make it unaccented.

### Page 482 — Rik 8 grammar closes; close of Sūkta 11

**भूयसीः (*bhūyasīḥ*)** — "sahasrād api atiśayena bahvyaḥ." "dvivacana-vibhajyopapade tarab-īyasunau" (Pā. 5-3-57): when a word meaning two or a word for the thing to be divided is the *upapada*, *tarap* and *īyasun* come in their own sense after a *subanta* or *tiṅanta* that expresses superiority of one over the other and denotes the property that makes the division. By *upapada* is meant a word spoken nearby; "tatropapadaṃ saptamīstham" (Pā. 3-1-92) is not meant, since that applies only within the section on roots. The word expressing duality or the thing to be divided need be used only in the analytical phrase; in the *taddhita* formation its meaning is included, so it need not be used. The sense of the second half of the mantra is that Indra has wealth and grain to the number of a thousand, or wealth exceeding a thousand. With *sahasra*, the thing to be divided, as the *upapada*, this sūtra gives *īyasun* after *bahu*: *bahu* + *īyas*; "bahor lopo bhū ca bahoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-158): after *bahu*, the suffixes *iman*, *iṣṭhan*, *īyasun* lose [their initial] and *bahu* is replaced by *bhū*; by "ādeḥ parasya" (Pā. 1-1-54) the loss falls on the first letter of what follows, so the *ī* is dropped, and by the same sūtra *bhū* replaces the stem: *bhūyas*; *īyasun* is *nit*, so *bhūyas* is initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197); *bhūyas* is an *ugit* stem, so "ugitaś ca" (Pā. 4-1-6) gives *ṅīp* in the feminine; in *bhūyas* + *ṅīp*, the *ṅ* is *it* by "laśakv ataddhite" and the *p* by "halantyam" (Pā. 1-3-3), dropped by "tasya lopaḥ" (Pā. 1-3-9); *ṅīp* is *pit*, so unaccented by "anudāttau sup-pitau" (Pā. 3-1-4).

**॥८॥**

*(A printed ornament follows. The page carries no separate Sanskrit colophon and no Kannada closing line for this sūkta, unlike Sūkta 10. The next printed page, 483, opens the twelfth sūkta, "agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe," and follows below.)*

**End of Sūkta 11.**

### Page 483 — opening of Sūkta 12 (fourth anuvāka)

**॥ ಹನ್ನೆರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 12 — *"agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe"* ("The Twelfth Sūkta")**

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta)**

> चतुर्थानुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्राग्निं दूतमित्यादिकस्य द्वादशर्चस्य प्रथमस्य सूक्तस्य कण्वपुत्रो मेधातिथिर्ऋषिः । अपवादाभावादनुवर्तमानं प्राग्घिरण्यस्तूपादित्युक्तं गायत्रमेव छन्दः । अग्निदेवताकत्वं विस्पष्टम् । अत एवानुक्रम्यते । अग्निं द्वादश मेधातिथिः काण्व आग्नेयमग्निनेति पादो द्व्यग्निदैवतो निर्मथ्य आहवनीयश्चेति ॥ विनियोगस्तु । प्रातरनुवाक आग्नेये क्रतौ गायत्रे छन्दस्यग्निं दूतमिति सूक्तम् । अथैतस्या रात्रेर्विवासकाल इति खण्डे ऽग्निमीळे ऽग्निं दूतम् । आ. ४-१३ । इति सूत्रितम् ॥ तथा पृष्ठ्यषडहस्य द्वितीये ऽहनीदमेव सूक्तमाज्यशस्त्रम् । पृष्ठ्यस्याभिप्लवेनोक्ते अहनी इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । अग्निं दूतमिति द्वितीये । आ. ७-१० । इति ॥ दर्शपूर्णमासयोः सामिधेनीष्वग्निं दूतमित्येका नमः प्रवक्त्र इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । ईळेन्यो नमस्यस्तिरो ऽग्निं दूतं वृणीमहे ॥ आ. १-२ । इति ॥
>
> *caturthānuvāke ṣaṭ sūktāni | tatrāgniṃ dūtamityādikasya dvādaśarcasya prathamasya sūktasya kaṇvaputro medhātithirṛṣiḥ | apavādābhāvādanuvartamānaṃ prāgghiraṇyastūpādityuktaṃ gāyatrameva chandaḥ | agnidevatākatvaṃ vispaṣṭam | ata evānukramyate | agniṃ dvādaśa medhātithiḥ kāṇva āgneyamagnineti pādo dvyagnidaivato nirmathya āhavanīyaśceti || viniyogastu | prātaranuvāka āgneye kratau gāyatre chandasyagniṃ dūtamiti sūktam | athaitasyā rātrervivāsakāla iti khaṇḍe 'gnimīḷe 'gniṃ dūtam | ā. 4-13 | iti sūtritam || tathā pṛṣṭhyaṣaḍahasya dvitīye 'hanīdameva sūktamājyaśastram | pṛṣṭhyasyābhiplavenokte ahanī iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | agniṃ dūtamiti dvitīye | ā. 7-10 | iti || darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ sāmidhenīṣvagniṃ dūtamityekā namaḥ pravaktra iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | īḷenyo namasyastiro 'gniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe || ā. 1-2 | iti ||*

**Translation:** "In the fourth anuvāka there are six sūktas. Of these, of the first sūkta, of twelve riks, beginning *agniṃ dūtam*, the ṛṣi is Medhātithi, son of Kaṇva. Since there is no exception, the meter is the Gāyatrī that continues, as was said, 'up to Hiraṇyastūpa.' That Agni is the deity is clear. Therefore the Anukramaṇī says: '*agniṃ dvādaśa medhātithiḥ kāṇva āgneyam agnineti pādo dvyagnidaivato nirmathya āhavanīyaś ca*' — [the sūkta] *agnim*, twelve [riks], Medhātithi Kāṇva, to Agni; the pāda *agninā* has two Agnis as deity, the churned [fire] and the Āhavanīya. Its application: in the morning litany (*prātaranuvāka*), in the Āgneya rite, in the Gāyatrī meter, the sūkta *agniṃ dūtam*; laid down in the section *athaitasyā rātrer vivāsakāle*: '*agnim īḷe*, *agniṃ dūtam*' (Āś. 4-13). Likewise on the second day of the Pṛṣṭhya Ṣaḍaha this same sūkta is the *ājya-śastra*; laid down in the section *pṛṣṭhyasyābhiplavenokte ahanī*: '*agniṃ dūtam* on the second' (Āś. 7-10). In the Darśa and Pūrṇamāsa, among the *sāmidhenī*s, the single [rik] *agniṃ dūtam*; laid down in the section *namaḥ pravaktre*: '*īḷenyo namasyas tiro*, *agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe*' (Āś. 1-2)."

**॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥** The fourth anuvāka begins with the twelfth sūkta; this anuvāka has six sūktas. Of these six sūktas, of the first, the sūkta of twelve riks called *agniṃ dūtam*, the ṛṣi is Medhātithi, son of Kaṇva; the meter is Gāyatrī; the deity is Agni. This is said in the Anukramaṇikā in the section *agniṃ dvādaśa medhātithiḥ kāṇvaḥ*. The order of application: at the time of reciting the mantras of the *prātaranuvāka* of the Āgneya rite, when the riks in the Gāyatrī meter are recited, this sūkta *agniṃ dūtam* is to be recited; this is said in the Śrautasūtra of Āśvalāyana in the section *athaitasyā rātrer vivāsakāle* (Ā. 4-13). And on the second day of the Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha rite this sūkta is recited as the *ājya-śastra* mantras; this is said in Āśvalāyana's sūtra 7-10, in the section *pṛṣṭhyasyābhiplavenokte ahanī*, as "*agniṃ dūtam iti dvitīye*." And in the Darśapūrṇamāsa sacrifices, when the riks called *sāmidhenī* are recited, the rik *agniṃ dūtam* is to be recited, as is said in the section *namaḥ pravaktre*; this too is said in section 1-2 of Āśvalāyana's Śrautasūtra: "*īḷenyo namasyas tiro 'gniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe*."

**॥ Chandaḥ — Gāyatrī ॥**

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒ग्निं दू॒तं वृ॑णीमहे॒ होता॑रं वि॒श्ववे॑दसम् ।
> अ॒स्य य॒ज्ञस्य॑ सु॒क्रतु॑म् ॥१॥
>
> *agníṃ dūtáṃ vṛṇīmahe hótāraṃ viśvávedasam |*
> *asyá yajñásya sukrátum ||1||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्निम् । दूतम् । वृणीमहे । होतारम् । विश्वऽवेदसम् ॥
> अस्य । यज्ञस्य । सुऽक्रतुम् ॥१॥
>
> *agnim | dūtam | vṛṇīmahe | hotāram | viśva-vedasam ||*
> *asya | yajñasya | su-kratum ||1||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> अग्नेर्दूतत्वमेतन्मन्त्रव्याख्याने तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मणे समाम्नायते । अग्निर्देवानां दूत आसीदुशनाः काव्यो ऽसुराणाम् । तै. सं. २-५-८-५ । इति । तादृशं देवदूतमग्निमस्मिन्कर्मणि वृणीमहे । संभजामः । कीदृशम् । होतारं देवानामाह्वातारं विश्ववेदसं सर्वधनोपेतम् अस्य प्रवर्तमानस्य यज्ञस्य निष्पादकत्वेन सुक्रतुं शोभनकर्माणं शोभनप्रज्ञं वा ॥ मघमित्यादिष्वष्टाविंशतिसंख्याकेषु धननामसु वेदस्शब्दः पठितः ॥ होतारम् । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । तृन् । ताच्छील्यादिषु । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणे । परपूर्वत्वे गुणः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । विश्ववेदसम् । बहुव्रीहौ । विश्वं संज्ञायाम् । पा. ६-२-१०६ । इति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तः । अस्य । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । सुक्रतुम् । क्रत्वादयश्च । पा. ६-२-११८ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥
>
> *agner dūtatvam etan-mantra-vyākhyāne taittirīya-brāhmaṇe samāmnāyate | agnir devānāṃ dūta āsīd uśanāḥ kāvyo 'surāṇām | tai. saṃ. 2-5-8-5 | iti | tādṛśaṃ deva-dūtam agnim asmin karmaṇi vṛṇīmahe | saṃbhajāmaḥ | kīdṛśam | hotāraṃ devānām āhvātāraṃ viśvavedasaṃ sarva-dhanopetam asya pravartamānasya yajñasya niṣpādakatvena sukratuṃ śobhana-karmāṇaṃ śobhana-prajñaṃ vā || magham ity-ādiṣv aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyākeṣu dhana-nāmasu vedas-śabdaḥ paṭhitaḥ || hotāram | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | tṛn | tācchīlyādiṣu | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇe | parapūrvatve guṇaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttaḥ | viśvavedasam | bahuvrīhau | viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām | pā. 6-2-106 | iti pūrvapadāntodāttaḥ | asya | ūḍidam ity-ādinā vibhakter udāttatvam | sukratum | kratv-ādayaś ca | pā. 6-2-118 | ity-ādyudāttatvam ||*

**Translation:** "That Agni is a messenger is stated in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, in explanation of this mantra: 'Agni was the messenger of the gods; Uśanas Kāvya, of the asuras' (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-5-8-5). Such an Agni, messenger of the gods, we *vṛṇīmahe* — choose, serve — in this rite. What kind? *Hotāram* — the caller of the gods; *viśvavedasam* — endowed with all wealth; *sukratum* — as the accomplisher of this rite now in progress, of excellent action, or of excellent wisdom. Among the twenty-eight words for 'wealth' beginning with *magham*, *vedas* is read." *(Grammar noted briefly: that* hotṛ *is from* hveñ *with* tṛn *in the habitual sense, with* saṃprasāraṇa*, pūrvarūpa and* guṇa*, initial-udātta since* nit*; that* viśvavedasam *is a bahuvrīhi in which* viśva*, in a name, ends in udātta (Pā. 6-2-106); that the case-ending of* asya *is udātta by* ūḍ-idam…*; and that* sukratu *has initial accent by Pā. 6-2-118.)*

### Page 485 — Rik 1: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**दूतम् (dūtam)** — the messenger of the gods | **होतारम् (hotāram)** — one who invokes the gods for sacrifices and the like | **विश्ववेदसम् (viśvavedasam)** — endowed with all wealth | **अस्य यज्ञस्य (asya yajñasya)** — of this sacrifice | **सुक्रतुम् (sukratum)** — the performer of the rite, or one who knows well the procedure of this sacrifice | **अग्निम् (agnim)** — the deity named Agni | *(we)* **वृणीमहे (vṛṇīmahe)** — choose and invoke (call).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Agni is the messenger of the gods, and he brings them to the sacrificial rites that we perform. This Agni has abundant wealth, and is the chief performer in this sacrifice, or one who knows well the nature of the rite. Such an Agni we choose (we pray to).

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> We select (invoke) Agni, the messenger of Gods, their invoker, the possessor of riches, the perfector of this rite or the highly wise.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

From this 12th sūkta up to the 23rd sūkta, too, the ṛṣi is Medhātithi, son of Kaṇva. These sūktas are not, like the sūktas of the ṛṣi Madhucchandas explained so far, full of tangles; there is no need to supply special words; they are in a fairly easy style and can be understood by all. The style of language of some ṛṣis is very involved; the style of others is easy to understand. In the order stated earlier, at the beginning there are sūktas addressed to Agni, then sūktas addressed to Indra, and after that sūktas of other deities. The descendants of this ṛṣi are the seers of Sūktas 36–50 in this maṇḍala, of the sūktas of the 8th maṇḍala, and of the 2nd sūkta of the 9th maṇḍala. The rik *agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe* is read in these places: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-5-8-5 and 5-5-6-1 [?]; Tai. Brā. 3-5-2-3; Sāmaveda 1-3; Maitrāyaṇīya Saṃhitā 4-10-2.

### Page 486 — Rik 1: Special Topics (continued) and grammar begins

*(The* dūtam *note begins at the foot of p. 485.)*

**"Dūtam"** — in explaining the word *dūta*, the Bhāṣyakāra cites the Yajurveda sentence "*agnir devānāṃ dūta āsīd uśanāḥ kāvyo 'surāṇām*" (printed "Tai. Saṃ. 3-5-8-5"; the bhāṣya gives 2-5-8-5): that is, Agni was the messenger of the gods, and Uśanas, son of Kavi, the messenger of the asuras. And the Yajurveda śruti says "*parokṣaṃ vā anye devāḥ*" — the other gods (those other than Agni) are not visible to us directly. When we humans pour into Agni the oblations we offer, so that they reach the gods, Agni stands between humans and gods, and it is believed that he carries the oblations to the gods. Hence Agni is called the messenger of the gods, as is customary.

**"Vṛṇīmahe"** — "we choose; we select; *select, choose*" and so on [the source's own English]. Skandasvāmī explains it as "we pray."

**"Viśvavedasam"** — *sarvadhanopetam* — "endowed with all wealth"; the word *ratnadhātamam* in the first rik of the Ṛgveda, *agnim īḷe*, supports this sense. *Vedas* is read among the twenty-eight words for wealth beginning with *magham* (printed "2-3-9" [?]); so *vedas* is to be given the sense of wealth.

**"Sukratum"** — *śobhana-karmāṇam* or *śobhana-prajñam*: one who has good deeds or good wisdom; that is, one who performs the needed acts of sacrifice and brings the sacrificial rite to completion with all its limbs; one of excellent wisdom; one who knows well the nature of the rites of sacrifice and the like. The word *kratu* is read both among the twenty-six words for 'work' beginning with *apaḥ* (Ni. "3-1" [as printed]), and among the eleven words for 'wisdom' beginning with *ketaḥ* (Ni. 3-13), so *kratu* has two senses, work and wisdom.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 486–487, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**होतारम् (*hotāram*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *tṛn* by "tṛn" (Pā. 3-2-135) in the senses of habit, duty and doing it well: *hve* + *tṛ*; "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34) gives *samprasāraṇa*, *u* for the *v*; *pūrvarūpa* by "samprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. 6-1-108); *hu* + *tṛ*: "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) gives *guṇa* to an *ik*-final stem before these suffixes; by "tiṅ-śit sārvadhātukam" (Pā. 3-4-113) the *tiṅ* endings and *ś*-marked suffixes are *sārvadhātuka*, and by "ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-114) the other suffixes taught under "dhātoḥ" (Pā. 3-1-91) are *ārdhadhātuka*; *tṛn* is neither *tiṅ* nor *śit*, so it is *ārdhadhātuka*, and the *u* of *hu* takes *guṇa*: *hotṛ*; then the accusative singular *am*:

### Page 487 — Rik 1 grammar closes

"ṛto ṅi-sarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-110) gives *guṇa* of the *ṛ* with *r*: *hotar* + *am*; "ap-tṛn-tṛc…" (Pā. 6-4-11) lengthens the penultimate: *hotāram*; *hotṛ* initial-udātta by the *nit* accent. **विश्ववेदसम् (*viśvavedasam*)** — "viśvaṃ vedo yasya saḥ": a bahuvrīhi; "bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām" (Pā. 6-2-106) — *viśva* as the first member in a name-bahuvrīhi ends in udātta; without this sūtra *viśva* would be initial-udātta, being a *kvan* word, and "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1) would keep that; the sūtra overrides it, so the final syllable is udātta. **अस्य (*asya*)** — after *idam*, the genitive ending is udātta by "ūḍidam-padādy-appum-raidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-171). **सुक्रतुम् (*sukratum*)** — "kratvādayaś ca" (Pā. 6-2-118): words of the *kratu* class after *su* are initial-udātta, so the *kratu* in *sukratu* is initial-udātta.

**॥१॥**

### Page 487 (lower) — Sūkta 12, Rik 2

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒ग्निम॑ग्निं॒ हवी॑मभिः॒ सदा॑ हवन्त वि॒श्पति॑म् ।
> ह॒व्य॒वाहं॑ पुरुप्रि॒यम् ॥२॥
>
> *agním-agniṃ hávīmabhiḥ sádā havanta viśpátim |*
> *havyavā́haṃ purupriyám ||2||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्निम्ऽअग्निम् । हवीमऽभिः । सदा । हवन्त । विश्पतिम् ॥
> हव्यऽवाहम् । पुरुऽप्रियम् ॥२॥
>
> *agnim-agnim | havīma-bhiḥ | sadā | havanta | viśpatim ||*
> *havya-vāham | puru-priyam ||2||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(The bhāṣya runs onto p. 488.)*

> यद्यप्यग्निः स्वरूपेणैक एव तथापि प्रयोगभेदादाहवनीयादिस्थानभेदात्पावकादिविशेषणभेदाद्वा बहुविधत्वमभिप्रेत्याग्निमग्निमिति वीप्सा । तं हवीमभिराह्वानकरणैर्मन्त्रैः सदा हवन्ते । निरन्तरमनुष्ठातार आह्वयन्ति । कीदृशम् । विश्पतिं विशां प्रजानां होत्रादीनां पालकं हव्यवाहं यजमानसमर्पितस्य हविषो देवान्प्रति वोढारं अत एव पुरुप्रियं बहूनां प्रीत्यास्पदम् ॥ अग्निमग्निम् । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति वीप्सायां द्विर्भावः । तस्य परमाम्रेडितमित्युत्तरस्याम्रेडितसंज्ञायामनुदात्तं चेत्यनुदात्तम् । हवीमभिः । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । आह्वानकरणभूतेषु मन्त्रेषु स्वव्यापारस्वातन्त्र्यात्कर्तृत्वविवक्षयान्येभ्यो ऽपि दृश्यन्त इति कर्तरि मनिन् । तस्य छान्दस ईडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति धातोः संप्रसारणम् । परपूर्वत्वं गुणावादेशौ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सदा । सर्वैकान्येत्यादिना । पा. ५-३-१५ । सर्वशब्दाद्दाप्रत्ययः । सर्वस्य सो ऽन्यतरस्यां दि । पा. ५-३-६ । इति सभावः । व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वम् । हवन्त । ह्वेञो लट् । झस्यान्तादेशः । टेरेत्वाभावश्छान्दसः । शपि बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । विश्पतिम् । पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । हव्यवाहम् । वह प्रापणे । वहश्च । पा. ३-२-६४ । इति ण्विप्रत्ययः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । पुरुप्रियम् । पुरूणां प्रियम् । समासान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥
>
> *yadyapyagniḥ svarūpeṇaika eva tathāpi prayogabhedādāhavanīyādisthānabhedātpāvakādiviśeṣaṇabhedādvā bahuvidhatvamabhipretyāgnimagnimiti vīpsā | taṃ havīmabhirāhvānakaraṇairmantraiḥ sadā havante | nirantaramanuṣṭhātāra āhvayanti | kīdṛśam | viśpatiṃ viśāṃ prajānāṃ hotrādīnāṃ pālakaṃ havyavāhaṃ yajamānasamarpitasya haviṣo devānprati voḍhāraṃ ata eva purupriyaṃ bahūnāṃ prītyāspadam || agnimagnim | nityavīpsayoriti vīpsāyāṃ dvirbhāvaḥ | tasya paramāmreḍitamityuttarasyāmreḍitasaṃjñāyāmanudāttaṃ cetyanudāttam | havīmabhiḥ | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | āhvānakaraṇabhūteṣu mantreṣu svavyāpārasvātantryātkartṛtvavivakṣayānyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti kartari manin | tasya chāndasa īḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti dhātoḥ saṃprasāraṇam | parapūrvatvaṃ guṇāvādeśau | nittvādādyudāttatvam | sadā | sarvaikānyetyādinā | pā. 5-3-15 | sarvaśabdāddāpratyayaḥ | sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di | pā. 5-3-6 | iti sabhāvaḥ | vyatyayenādyudāttatvam | havanta | hveño laṭ | jhasyāntādeśaḥ | ṭeretvābhāvaśchāndasaḥ | śapi bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | viśpatim | patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvare prāpte parādiśchandasi bahulamityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | havyavāham | vaha prāpaṇe | vahaśca | pā. 3-2-64 | iti ṇvipratyayaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | purupriyam | purūṇāṃ priyam | samāsāntodāttatvam ||*

**Translation:** "Although Agni is one in his own nature, nevertheless, with a view to his manifoldness — by differences of use, by differences of place such as the *āhavanīya* [fire] and the rest, or by differences of epithets such as *pāvaka* [the purifier] — the repetition *agnim agnim* ('Agni, Agni') is used. Him, *havīmabhiḥ* — with mantras that serve as the means of invocation — the performers *sadā havante* — constantly call. What kind of Agni? *Viśpatim* — protector of the *viś*, the people: the hotṛ priests and others; *havyavāham* — the carrier, to the gods, of the oblation offered by the sacrificer; and therefore *purupriyam* — the dear one of many."

### Page 488 — Rik 2: grammatical tail of the bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

(Grammatical tail of the bhāṣya: *agnim agnim* — doubled in the sense of *vīpsā* by "nitya-vīpsayoḥ"; the second member is *āmreḍita* by "tasya param āmreḍitam" and unaccented by "anudāttaṃ ca"; *havīmabhiḥ* — *hveñ*, *manin* in the agent sense by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante", since the mantras that are instruments of calling are spoken of as independent agents; Vedic *ī* augment, *samprasāraṇa* by "bahulaṃ chandasi", *pūrvarūpa*, *guṇa* and *av*; initial-udātta as *nit*; *sadā* — *dā* after *sarva* (Pā. 5-3-15), *sa* for *sarva* by "sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di" (Pā. 5-3-6), initial-udātta by exception; *havanta* — *laṭ* of *hveñ*, *ant* for *jha*, no *e* for the *ṭi* (Vedic), *samprasāraṇa* before *śap*, unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ"; *viśpatim* — instead of the first-member accent of "patyāv aiśvarye", "parādiś chandasi bahulam" makes the second member initial-udātta; *havyavāham* — *ṇvi* by "vahaś ca" (Pā. 3-2-64), the *kṛt* second member keeping its accent; *purupriyam* — "purūṇāṃ priyam," the compound final-udātta.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**विश्पतिम् (viśpatim)** — the lord, the protector, of the people (the hotṛ priests and others) | **हव्यवाहम् (havyavāham)** — [the one] who carries to the gods the oblations offered by the sacrificer | **पुरुप्रियम् (purupriyam)** — dear to all | **अग्निमग्निम् (agnim-agnim)** — to Agni (who is seen in places such as the *āhavanīya*) | **हवीमभिः (havīmabhiḥ)** — with the mantras used for invocation | **सदा (sadā)** — always | **हवन्त (havanta)** — [the performers of sacrifices] invoke.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Although Agni is one, he appears separately in different places — the *āhavanīya*, the *gārhapatya* and others. He is the protector of all people, beginning with the sacrificer; he carries to the gods the oblations offered in the sacrifice; he is dear to all. The people who perform sacrifices always invoke such an Agni with mantras of invocation.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> They (offerers of oblations) constantly invoke Agni and Agni again, the lord of men, the bearer of offerings, the beloved of many.


### Page 489 — Rik 2: Special Topics and grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Agnim-agnim"** — "nityavīpsayor iti vīpsāyāṃ dvirbhāvaḥ": by pronouncing one word twice the sense "each one" is conveyed. Here it means each Agni: the *āhavanīya*, the *dakṣiṇāgni*, the *gārhapatya* and the others established in different places in the sacrifices.

**"Viśpatim"** — *viśāṃ prajānāṃ patim*: the lord, the master, of the subjects or people: "Ruler of men, progeny" [the source's English].

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 489–490, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**अग्निमग्निम् (*agnim-agnim*)** — "nitya-vīpsayoḥ" (Pā. 8-1-4): the word *nitya-vīpsayoḥ* names the two senses *nitya* and *vīpsā*; since there is an expectation of what comes in which sense — an expectation of the place and of what is enjoined — the sūtra "sarvasya dve" (Pā. 8-1-1) is in force as a heading, and the later sūtra "padasya" (Pā. 8-1-16) is connected too. *Dve* is a numeral, so it expects a counted thing, and since this is a grammar of words, "words" is understood. *Nitya* means *ābhīkṣṇya*, repetition; *vīpsā* means the wish to pervade; in verbal cognition only pervasion appears. When repetition or pervasion is to be shown, two words come in place of the whole word: so, with pervasion meant, two words *agnim* come in place of the one *agnim* — *agnim agnim*, "each Agni." Repetition is a property of an action, so the doubling in that sense comes with a *tiṅanta* and with a *kṛdanta* that is an indeclinable. By "tasya param āmreḍitam" (Pā. 8-1-2) the second form of the doubled word is named *āmreḍita*, and by "anudāttaṃ ca" (Pā. 8-1-3) it is unaccented. **हवीमभिः (*havīmabhiḥ*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *manin* in the agent sense by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. 3-2-75). Although the mantras are instruments in calling, by the maxim "vivakṣātaḥ kārakāṇi bhavanti" — as in *sthālī pacati*, where the pot gets the name of agent — their independence in their own activity is meant, so nothing bars *manin* in the agent sense: *hve* + *man*; the Vedic augment *ī*: *hve* + *īman*; "bahulaṃ chandasi"

### Page 490 — Rik 2 grammar closes

(Pā. 6-1-34) gives *samprasāraṇa*, *u* for the *e*-ending root's *v*, *pūrvarūpa*, *guṇa*, *av*: *havīman*; instrumental plural *bhis*; by "svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne" (Pā. 1-4-17) [*pada* status], loss of *n*, *ru* and visarga: *havīmabhiḥ*; initial-udātta by the *nit* accent. **सदा (*sadā*)** — "sarvaikānya-kiṃ-yat-tadaḥ kāle dā" (Pā. 5-3-15): after *sarva*, *eka*, *anya*, *kim*, *yad*, *tad* in the locative sense of time, *dā* in its own sense: *sarva* + *dā*; "sarvasya so 'nyatarasyāṃ di" (Pā. 5-3-6): before a *d*-initial suffix of the *prāgdiśīya* group, *sa* optionally replaces *sarva*: *sadā*; "sarvasmin kāle"; properly the suffix accent would make *sadā* final-udātta, but by exception it is initial-udātta. **हवन्त (*havanta*)** — root *hveñ*; *laṭ*, *jha*; *ant* for *jh* by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-3); the *e* that "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (printed "3-4-79" [?]) would give is absent as a Vedic form; *śap*: *hve* + *a* + *anta*; "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34) gives *samprasāraṇa*, then *pūrvarūpa*, *guṇa*, *av*: *havanta*; unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **विश्पतिम् (*viśpatim*)** — "patyāv aiśvarye" (Pā. 6-2-18) would give the first member's accent; setting it aside, "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (printed "pā. sada." [sic] 6-2-199) makes the second member *pati* initial-udātta. **हव्यवाहम् (*havyavāham*)** — "havyaṃ vahati iti havyavāhaḥ, tam"; root *vaha prāpaṇe*; "vahaś ca" (Pā. 3-2-64): in the Veda, with a *subanta* as *upapada*, *ṇvi* after *vah*: *havya* + *am* + *vah* + *ṇvi*; properly the non-surface analysis should be shown as *havya* + *as* *vah* + *ṇvi*; as a *kṛdanta* it is a *prātipadika*, the *sup* dropped; *ṇvi* lost part by part; *vṛddhi* of the penultimate: *havyavāha*, with the accent of the *kṛt* second member; accusative singular *am*: *havyavāham*. **पुरुप्रियम् (*purupriyam*)** — "purūṇāṃ priyas tam": a genitive tatpuruṣa; final-udātta by "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223).

**॥२॥**

### Page 491 — Sūkta 12, Rik 3

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्ने॑ दे॒वाँ इ॒हा व॑ह जज्ञा॒नो वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषे ।
> असि॒ होता॑ न॒ ईड्यः॑ ॥३॥
>
> *ágne devā́m̐ ihā́ vaha jajñānó vṛktábarhiṣe |*
> *asi hótā na ī́ḍyaḥ ||3||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्ने । देवान् । इह । आ । वह । जज्ञानः । वृक्तऽबर्हिषे ॥
> असि । होता । नः । ईड्यः ॥३॥
>
> *agne | devān | iha | ā | vaha | jajñānaḥ | vṛkta-barhiṣe ||*
> *asi | hotā | naḥ | īḍyaḥ ||3||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे अग्ने जज्ञानो ऽरण्योरुत्पन्नस्त्वं वृक्तबर्हिष आस्तरणार्थं छिन्नेन बर्हिषा युक्ताय तं यजमानमनुग्रहीतुमिह कर्मणि हविर्भुजो देवाना वह । सो ऽस्मदर्थं होता देवानामाह्वाता त्वमीड्यः स्तुत्यो ऽसि ॥ देवानित्यत्र संहितायां दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति रुत्वम् । आतो ऽटि नित्यमित्यनुनासिकभावः । जज्ञानः । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । लिटः कानच् । गमहनेत्युपधालोपः । द्विर्वचने ऽचि । पा. १-१-५९ । इति तस्य स्थानिवद्भावाद्द्विर्वचनम् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । वृक्तबर्हिषे । ओव्रश्चू छेदने । निष्ठेति क्तप्रत्ययः । यस्य विभाषेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । वृक्तं बर्हिर्यस्मै यजमानाय येन वा ऋत्विजा । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरः । असि । अस्तेः सिप् । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । तासस्त्योर्लोपः । पा. ७-४-५० । इति सकारस्य लोपः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । होता । ह्वयतेस्ताच्छील्यादिषु तृन् । बहुलं छन्दसीति संप्रसारणम् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । ईड्यः । ईड स्तुतौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । पा. ३-१-१२४ । तित्स्वरिते प्राप्त ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यतः । पा. ६-१-२१४ । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥
>
> *he agne jajñāno 'raṇyorutpannastvaṃ vṛktabarhiṣa āstaraṇārthaṃ chinnena barhiṣā yuktāya taṃ yajamānamanugrahītumiha karmaṇi havirbhujo devānā vaha | so 'smadarthaṃ hotā devānāmāhvātā tvamīḍyaḥ stutyo 'si || devānityatra saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti rutvam | āto 'ṭi nityamityanunāsikabhāvaḥ | jajñānaḥ | janī prādurbhāve | liṭaḥ kānac | gamahanetyupadhālopaḥ | dvirvacane 'ci | pā. 1-1-59 | iti tasya sthānivadbhāvāddvirvacanam | cittvādantodāttaḥ | vṛktabarhiṣe | ovraścū chedane | niṣṭheti ktapratyayaḥ | yasya vibhāṣetīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | vṛktaṃ barhiryasmai yajamānāya yena vā ṛtvijā | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraḥ | asi | asteḥ sip | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | tāsastyorlopaḥ | pā. 7-4-50 | iti sakārasya lopaḥ | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | hotā | hvayatestācchīlyādiṣu tṛn | bahulaṃ chandasīti saṃprasāraṇam | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | īḍyaḥ | īḍa stutau | ṛhalorṇyat | pā. 3-1-124 | titsvarite prāpta īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ | pā. 6-1-214 | ityādyudāttatvam ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni! *Jajñānaḥ* — born of the two *araṇis* — you, *vṛktabarhiṣe*, for [the sacrificer] who is equipped with *barhis* cut for strewing, in order to favour that sacrificer, bring here, to this rite, the gods who eat the oblation. You, *hotā*, the caller of the gods on our behalf, are *īḍyaḥ* — worthy of praise." (Grammatical tail: *devān* — in the Saṃhitā *ru* by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde", and nasalization by "āto 'ṭi nityam"; *jajñānaḥ* — *janī prādurbhāve*, *kānac* for *liṭ*, loss of the penultimate by "gama-hana…", doubling because by "dvirvacane 'ci" (Pā. 1-1-59) the lost vowel counts as present, final-udātta as *cit*; *vṛktabarhiṣe* — *ovraścū chedane* with *kta*, *iṭ* barred by "yasya vibhāṣā"; "for whom or by whom the *barhis* has been cut", a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; *asi* — *sip* after *as*, *śap* dropped, the *s* of the root dropped by "tāsastyor lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-50), not unaccented because it begins the pāda; *hotā* — *tṛn* after *hve*, *samprasāraṇa*, initial-udātta; *īḍyaḥ* — *īḍa stutau*, *ṇyat* by "ṛhalor ṇyat" (Pā. 3-1-124), where the *tit* svarita would arise "īḍa-vanda-vṛ-śaṃsa-duhāṃ ṇyataḥ" (Pā. 6-1-214) gives initial-udātta.)

### Page 491 (lower) — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne)** — O Agni | **जज्ञानः (jajñānaḥ)** — [you] born in the *araṇi* | **वृक्तबर्हिषे (vṛktabarhiṣe)** — for the sacrificer who has spread the cut sacred grass as seats [for the gods] | **इह (iha)** — in this rite (sacrifice) | **देवान् (devān)** — the gods | **आ वह (ā vaha)** — bring | **नः (naḥ)** — for us | **होता (hotā)** — [you] who bring the gods | **ईड्यः (īḍyaḥ)** — worthy of praise | **असि (asi)** — you are.

### Page 492 — Rik 3: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni! You are born (in the *araṇi*). Such as you are, to favour the sacrificer who has spread and made ready the cut *darbha* for the gods to come and sit on, bring the gods here. For, since you bring the gods, you are worthy of being praised by all of us.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Agni, when born, bring hither the gods for him who has prepared their seats with the clipped sacred grass; you are their invoker for us and are to be adored.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Jajñānaḥ"** — born, arisen: *born* [the source's English]. "Born Agni" means: in sacrifices people produce fire by rubbing together two pieces of wood called *araṇi*; hence the usage that Agni is born in the *araṇi*.

**"Vṛktabarhiṣe"** — this word has been explained earlier. *Barhis* is cut *darbha*. The sense is "for the sacrificer who has spread and made ready such *darbha* for the gods to come and sit on."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 492–494, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**देवान् (*devān*)** — in the Saṃhitā an *i* follows, so "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9): when the *n* and the *aṭ* letter are in the same pāda, the *n* after a long vowel is replaced by *ru*: *devār i*; "āto 'ṭi nityam" (printed "8-3-3"): before an *aṭ* letter, the long *ā* before the *ru* is always nasalized; then "bho-bhago-agho-apūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. 8-3-17) gives *y* for the *r*, and "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19) drops the *y*: *devām̐ iha*. **जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)** — root *janī prādurbhāve*; *liṭ*, replaced by *kānac* by "liṭaḥ kānaj vā" (Pā. 3-2-106); "gama-hana-jana-khana-ghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi"

### Page 493 — Rik 3 grammar (continued)

(Pā. 6-4-98): before a vowel-initial *kit* or *ṅit* suffix other than *aṅ*, the penultimate of *gam* etc. is dropped, so the *a* after *j* is dropped: *jn* + *āna*; "dvirvacane 'ci" (Pā. 1-1-59): when a vowel that causes doubling follows, a substitute for a vowel counts as that vowel for doubling, so the dropped *a* counts as present and "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-8) gives doubling: *jan jn āna*; "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-60) removes the *n* of the reduplicate; by *ścutva* the dental nasal *n* becomes the palatal nasal *ñ*: *jajñāna*; the suffix being *cit*, final-udātta. **वृक्तबर्हिषे (*vṛktabarhiṣe*)** — root *ovraścū chedane*, *ūdit*; "svarati-sūti-sūyati-dhūñ-ūdito vā" (Pā. 7-2-44): after *svṛ* etc. and *ūdit* roots the *iṭ* augment before a *val*-initial *ārdhadhātuka* is optional; so after *kta* by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. 3-2-102), "yasya vibhāṣā" (Pā. 7-2-15) bars *iṭ*: *vraśc* + *ta*; "oditaś ca" (Pā. 8-2-45): after an *o*-marked root the *t* of *kta* becomes *n*: *vraśc* + *na*; "grahi-jyā-vayi-vyadhi-vaṣṭi-vicati-vṛścati-pṛcchati-bhṛjjatīnāṃ ṅiti ca" (Pā. 6-1-16) gives *samprasāraṇa*, *ṛ* for the *r*, and *pūrvarūpa*: *vṛśc* + *na*; "skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca" (Pā. 8-2-29): the *s* or *k* at the start of a cluster at the end of a *pada* or before a *jhal* is dropped — so the *s* is dropped. In doing this, the *n* of the *niṣṭhā* substitute given by "oditaś ca" (8-2-45) is *asiddha* by "pūrvatrāsiddham", so the cluster counts as standing before a *jhal*. By the verse "nakārajāv anusvāra-pañcamau jhali dhātuṣu | sakārajaḥ śakāraś ce ṣāṭ ṭavargas tavargajaḥ" — in roots, an anusvāra or fifth-of-class before a *jhal* comes from *n*; *ś* before *c* comes from *s*; and *ṣ* with a *ṭ*-class letter comes from the *t*-class — the *ś* before *c* in *vraśc* is known to come from *s*: *vras* + *c*, with *ścutva* by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-40). When the cluster-initial loss is made, that *ś* from *ścutva* is *asiddha* by "pūrvatrāsiddham", so the cluster-initial *s* is found [and dropped]. With the cluster-initial loss, *vṛc* + *na*; "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā.

### Page 494 — Rik 3 grammar closes

8-2-30): before a *jhal* or at the end of a *pada* a palatal becomes a velar, so *c* → *k*; here too, in making the velar, the *n* is *asiddha* by "pūrvatrāsiddham". One may ask why, the *n* being *asiddha*, "vraśca-bhrasja-sṛja-mṛja-yaja-rāja-bhrāja-cchaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-36) does not make the *c* of *vraśc* *ṣ*; but by "niṣṭhādeśaḥ ṣatva-svara-pratyaya-iḍvidhiṣu siddho vācyaḥ" (printed "8-2-6 vā. 6") the *niṣṭhā* substitute counts as effective for rules of *ṣatva* and the like, so the *n* is not *asiddha* and no *ṣ* arises. This is made clear in the Mādhavīya Dhātuvṛtti and in the Siddhāntakaumudī. Since *nṛnamana* is read in the *kṣubhnādi* group to bar that *ṇatva*, the *ṛ* gives *ṇatva* by "aṭ-kupv-āṅ-num-vyavāye 'pi" (Pā. 8-4-2); so by the sūtra mentioned the *n* would become *ṇ*, and the form should be *vṛkṇaḥ*. Here it must be said that, by Vedic procedure, neither the *niṣṭhā-natva* given by "oditaś ca" nor the *ṣatva* given by "vraśca-bhrasja…" (Pā. 8-2-36) applies. So *vṛc* + *ta*, and with the velar the form *vṛkta* is obtained. *Vṛkta* is final-udātta by the suffix accent. As a bahuvrīhi, "vṛktaṃ barhiḥ yasmai yajamānāya" or "vṛktaṃ barhiḥ yena ṛtvijā", it takes the first member's accent by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1). **असि (*asi*)** — root *asa bhuvi*; *laṭ* → *sip*; the *śap* dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (2-4-72); "tāsastyor lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-50): before an *s*-initial suffix the final *s* of *tās* and *as* is dropped: *asi*; standing at the beginning of the pāda, it is not unaccented. **होता (*hotā*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *tṛn* by "tṛn" (Pā. 3-2-135) in the senses of habit etc.; *samprasāraṇa* by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34), *pūrvarūpa* by "samprasāraṇāc ca", *guṇa*; nominative singular *hotā*; initial-udātta by the *nit* accent. **ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*)** — root *īḍa stutau*; "ṛhalor ṇyat" (Pā. 3-1-124): after roots ending in *ṛ* or a consonant, *ṇyat*; the svarita that "tit svaritam" (Pā. 6-1-185) would give is set aside by "īḍa-vanda-vṛ-śaṃsa-duhāṃ ṇyataḥ" (Pā. 6-1-214), which gives initial-udātta.

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ताँ उ॑श॒तो वि बो॑धय॒ यद॑ग्ने॒ यासि॑ दू॒त्यम् ।
> दे॒वैरा स॑त्सि ब॒र्हिषि ॥४॥
>
> *tā́m̐ uśató ví bodhaya yád agne yā́si dūtyám |*
> *deváir ā́ satsi barhíṣi ||4||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तान् । उशतः । वि । बोधय । यत् । अग्ने । यासि । दूत्यम् ॥
> देवैः । आ । सत्सि । बर्हिषि ॥४॥
>
> *tān | uśataḥ | vi | bodhaya | yat | agne | yāsi | dūtyam ||*
> *devaiḥ | ā | satsi | barhiṣi ||4||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे अग्ने यद्यस्मात्कारणाद्दूत्यं यासि देवानां दूतकर्म प्राप्नोषि तस्मात्कारणादुशतो हविः कामयमानांस्तान्देवान् हविःस्वीकारार्थं वि बोधय । विबोध्य च बर्हिष्यस्मिन्कर्मणि तैर्देवैः सह आ सत्सि । आसीद । आगत्योपविश ॥ तान् । दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति संहितायां रुत्वम् । आतो ऽटि नित्यमित्यनुनासिकभावः । उशतः । वश कान्तौ । लटः शतृ । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना संप्रसारणम् । शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । यासि । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः । दूत्यम् । दूतस्य भागः कर्म वा दूत्यम् । दूतस्य भागकर्मणी । पा. ४-४-१२० । इति यत् । तस्य तित्स्वरितापवादत्वेन यतो ऽनाव इति प्राप्तमाद्युदात्तत्वं सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति निवर्तते । अतस्तित्स्वरितमित्येव भवति । शेषनिघातः । सत्सि । सीदसि । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । लटः सिपि शपो बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । न लुमताङ्गस्येति प्रत्ययलक्षणप्रतिषेधात् पाघ्रेत्यादिना । पा. ७-३-७८ । सीदादेशो न भवति । बर्हिषि । बृह बृहि वृद्धौ । बृंहेर्नलोपश्च । उ. २-११० । इतीसिप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः ॥
>
> *he agne yadyasmātkāraṇāddūtyaṃ yāsi devānāṃ dūtakarma prāpnoṣi tasmātkāraṇāduśato haviḥ kāmayamānāṃstāndevān haviḥsvīkārārthaṃ vi bodhaya | vibodhya ca barhiṣyasminkarmaṇi tairdevaiḥ saha ā satsi | āsīda | āgatyopaviśa || tān | dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti saṃhitāyāṃ rutvam | āto 'ṭi nityamityanunāsikabhāvaḥ | uśataḥ | vaśa kāntau | laṭaḥ śatṛ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | grahijyetyādinā saṃprasāraṇam | śaturanumo nadyajādī iti vibhakterudāttatvam | yāsi | yadvṛttānnityamiti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | dūtyam | dūtasya bhāgaḥ karma vā dūtyam | dūtasya bhāgakarmaṇī | pā. 4-4-120 | iti yat | tasya titsvaritāpavādatvena yato 'nāva iti prāptamādyudāttatvaṃ sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti nivartate | atastitsvaritamityeva bhavati | śeṣanighātaḥ | satsi | sīdasi | ṣadlṛ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu | laṭaḥ sipi śapo bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | na lumatāṅgasyeti pratyayalakṣaṇapratiṣedhāt pāghretyādinā | pā. 7-3-78 | sīdādeśo na bhavati | barhiṣi | bṛha bṛhi vṛddhau | bṛṃhernalopaśca | u. 2-110 | itīsipratyayaḥ | pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni! Because you *yāsi dūtyam* — attain the work of messenger of the gods — therefore *uśataḥ* — those gods who desire the oblation — *vi bodhaya*: awaken them, so as to make them accept the oblation; and having awakened them, *ā satsi* — sit down — with those gods on the *barhis* in this rite; come and be seated." (Grammatical tail: *tān* — *ru* in the Saṃhitā by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde", nasalization by "āto 'ṭi nityam"; *uśataḥ* — *vaśa kāntau*, *śatṛ*, *śap* dropped, *samprasāraṇa* by "grahi-jyā…", the case ending udātta by "śatur anumo nady-ajādī"; *yāsi* — not unaccented, by "yad-vṛttān nityam"; *dūtyam* — "the share or the work of a messenger", *yat* by "dūtasya bhāga-karmaṇī" (Pā. 4-4-120); the initial accent of "yato 'nāvaḥ", which would set aside the *tit* svarita, is withdrawn by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante", so "tit svaritam" holds, the rest unaccented; *satsi* — = *sīdasi*: *ṣadḷ*, the *śap* after *sip* dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi", and since "na lumatāṅgasya" bars *pratyaya-lakṣaṇa*, the *sīd* of "pā-ghrā…" (Pā. 7-3-78) does not come; *barhiṣi* — *bṛha bṛhi vṛddhau*, *isi* by "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. 2-110), the *i* udātta by the suffix accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne)** — O Agni | **यत् (yat)** — for which reason | **दूत्यम् (dūtyam)** — the state of being a messenger of the gods | **यासि (yāsi)** — you have attained | *(for that reason)* **उशतः (uśataḥ)** — [the gods] who desire the oblation | **तान् (tān)** — those gods | **वि बोधय (vi bodhaya)** — awaken (urge) | *(then)* **देवैः (devaiḥ)** — together with the gods | **बर्हिषि (barhiṣi)** — on the *darbha* grass spread out for seats | **आ सत्सि (ā satsi)** — sit down.

### Page 496 — Rik 4: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni! You are the gods' messenger. Therefore rouse those gods who desire the oblation (in the sacrifices), bring them here, and sit with them on the cut *darbha* made ready for seats.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Agni, as you go as messenger of Gods, awaken them desirous of oblations; sit down with them on the sacred grass.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Barhiṣi"** — "for seats": it is the custom to spread *darbha* cut with its tips so that the gods may sit. Vessels of ghee and the oblations, too, are placed on such spread *darbha*; this is held to be best and the custom.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 496–497, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**तान् (*tān*)** — by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9) the *n* becomes *ru* in the Saṃhitā; by "āto 'ṭi nityam" (printed "8-3-3") the long *ā* is nasalized; *y* by "bho-bhago…" (Pā. 8-3-17), and the *y* dropped by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19): *tām̐ uśataḥ*. **उशतः (*uśataḥ*)** — root *vaśa kāntau*; *laṭ* → *śatṛ* by "laṭaḥ śatṛ…" (Pā. 3-2-124); the *śap* dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-72); "grahi-jyā-vayi-vyadhi-vaṣṭi…" (Pā. 6-1-16) gives *samprasāraṇa*, *u* for the *v*, *pūrvarūpa* by "samprasāraṇāc ca": *uśat*, accusative plural; the case ending udātta by "śatur anumo nady-ajādī" (Pā. 6-1-173). **यासि (*yāsi*)** — root *yā prāpaṇe*; *laṭ*, second singular; "yad-vṛttān nityam" (Pā. 8-1-66): a *tiṅanta* after a word containing *yad* is not unaccented, so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" does not apply. **दूत्यम् (*dūtyam*)** — "dūtasya bhāvaḥ [sic] karma vā"; *bhāga* means a share, *karma* an act; in the sense of share it is masculine, in the sense of act neuter, accusative singular. "dūtasya bhāga-karmaṇī" (Pā. 4-4-120): after the genitive of *dūta*, *yat* in the senses of share and act;

### Page 497 — Rik 4 grammar closes

*yat* is *t*-marked, so by "tit svaritam" (Pā. 6-1-185) the svarita would come; setting it aside, "yato 'nāvaḥ" (printed "6-1-213") would give initial-udātta; that is optional by the paribhāṣā "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (printed "Paribhā. 35" [?]), so it does not apply, and the svarita stands; the remaining *dū* is unaccented by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158). **सत्सि (*satsi*)** — meaning *sīdasi*; root *ṣadḷ viśaraṇa-gaty-avasādaneṣu*; *laṭ* → second singular *sip*: *sad* + *si*; the *śap* dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); "na lumatāṅgasya" (Pā. 1-1-63) bars *pratyaya-lakṣaṇa*, so the *sīda* of "pā-ghrā-dhmā…" (Pā. 7-3-78) does not come; *car* by "khari ca" (Pā. 8-4-55); wholly unaccented. **बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)** — root *bṛha bṛhi vṛddhau*; "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. "2-266" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-110): after *bṛṃh* the suffix *isi*, with loss of the *n*; the *n* is that of the *num* augment, *bṛhi* being *idit*, by "idito num dhātoḥ" (printed "7-1-58"); *bṛh* + *is*: *laghūpadha-guṇa* with *r*: *barhis*; the *i* udātta by the suffix accent; locative singular *barhiṣi*.

### Page 498 — Rik 5: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

*(The bhāṣya and its long grammatical tail fill p. 498.)*

> हे घृताहवन घृतेनाहूयमान दीदिवो दीप्यमानाग्ने त्वं रक्षस्विनो रक्षोयुक्तान्रिषतो हिंसकाञ्छत्रून्प्रत्यस्माकं प्रतिकूलान्दह स्म । सर्वथा भस्मीकुरु ॥ घृतेनाहूयते ऽस्मिन्निति करणाधिकरणयोश्चेत्यधिकरणे ल्युट् । अत्र जुहोतेरविवक्षितकर्मत्वेनाकर्मकत्वाद्घृतस्य करणत्वमेव न तु कर्मत्वम् । अतो नैषा तृतीया च होश्छन्दसि । पा. २-३-३ । इति कर्मणि तृतीया । किंतु कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया । पा. २-३-१८ । इति करणवाचिन्येव । अतः कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलम् । पा. २-१-३२ । इति समासः । तत्र पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरापवादे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरे प्राप्ते प्रातिपदिकावस्थायामेव कृते सति पश्चाद्विभक्त्युत्पन्नायामामन्त्रितस्य चेत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । दीदिवः । दीव्यतेर्लिटः क्वसुः । तस्य वस्वेकाजाद्घसामिति नियमादिडभावः । द्विर्वचनम् । हलादिः शेषः । उत्तरवकारस्य लोपो व्योर्वलीति लोपः । क्वसुः कित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । तुजादीनां दीर्घो ऽभ्यासस्य । पा. ६-१-७ । इति दीर्घत्वमभ्यासस्य । संबुद्धावुगिदचामिति नुम् । संयोगान्तस्य लोपः । पा. ८-२-२३ । इति सकारलोपे नकारस्य मतुवसो रु संबुद्धौ छन्दसीति रुत्वम् । विसर्गः । पदात्परत्वादामन्त्रितनिघातः । ननु पूर्वामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वात्तत्पादादित्वेन न निघातोपपत्तिः । न च नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनम् । पा. ८-१-७३ । इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधः । उभयोरग्निपदविशेषणत्वेन विशेषवचनत्वात् । अत एव परस्परमनन्वयेनासामर्थ्यात्समर्थः पदविधिः । पा. २-१-१ । इति च नियमात्पूर्वस्य न पराङ्गवद्भावो येनैकपद्येन निघातः स्यात् । अत एवेडे रन्ते ऽदिते सरस्वतीत्यादौ । तै. सं. ७-१-६-८ । पृथक्पृथगाद्युदात्तत्वमिति । उच्यते । अत्र दीदिव इति नाग्निपदस्य विशेषणं किंतु घृताहवनपदस्यैव द्योतनार्थम् । घृताहवन इति विशेष्यत्वेन विवक्षितत्वात् । विशिष्टस्य तु पश्चादग्निविशेषणता । तत्र दीदिवः पदं प्रति घृताहवनपदस्य विशेष्यत्वान्नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरण इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधान्निघातोपपत्तिः । अत एव परस्परविशेषणविशेष्यभावेन सामर्थ्यात्सुबामन्त्रित इति पराङ्गवद्भावे शेषनिघातेनापि स्वरोपपत्तिरिति । इडे रन्त इत्यादौ तु नैवं परस्परान्वय इति वैषम्यम् । रिषतः । रुष रिष हिंसार्था इति भौवादिकस्य लटः शत्रादेशे शपि छान्दसो गुणाभावः । तौदादिकस्य वा रुश रिश हिंसायामित्यस्य छान्दसं षत्वम् । विकरणस्य शस्य ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । रक्षस्विनः । रक्षःशब्दादस्मायामेधास्रजो विनिः । पा. ५-२-१२१ । इति मत्वर्थीयो विनिः । तस्य प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥

**Translation:** "O *ghṛtāhavana* — O Agni, called with ghee; *dīdivaḥ* — blazing! You, *prati daha sma*: burn on every side — turn into ashes completely — the enemies who are *rakṣasvinaḥ*, accompanied by rākṣasas, *riṣataḥ*, injurious, hostile to us." (Grammatical tail: *ghṛtāhavana* — "in whom one is called with ghee": *lyuṭ* in the locative sense by "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca"; since *juhoti* is here intransitive, its object not being meant, the ghee is an instrument, not an object, so not the object-sense third case of "tṛtīyā ca hoś chandasi" (Pā. 2-3-3) but the instrumental of "kartṛ-karaṇayos tṛtīyā" (Pā. 2-3-18); compound by "kartṛ-karaṇe kṛtā bahulam" (Pā. 2-1-32); the *kṛt* second-member accent, which sets aside the first-member accent, is made at the stem stage, and after the ending the vocative is initial-udātta by "āmantritasya ca"; *dīdivaḥ* — *kvasu* for *liṭ* of *div*, no *iṭ* by the restriction "vasv-ekāj-ād-ghasām", doubling, "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ", the second *v* dropped by "lopo vyor vali", no *guṇa* as *kit*, the reduplicate lengthened by "tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-7), *num* in the vocative, the *s* dropped (Pā. 8-2-23), *ru* for the *n* by "matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi", visarga; unaccented as a vocative after a word. Objection: the first vocative being treated as absent, *dīdivaḥ* would begin the pāda and could not be unaccented; and the bar "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) does not apply, since both are specific qualifiers of *agni*; for the same reason, lacking mutual connection, "samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ" (Pā. 2-1-1) prevents the first from being treated as part of the next, as in "iḍe rante 'dite sarasvati" (T.S. 7-1-6-8), where each is initial-udātta. Answer: here *dīdiva* qualifies not *agni* but *ghṛtāhavana*, which is meant as the qualified term, and the whole then qualifies *agni*; so the bar of 8-1-73 applies and the loss of accent is in order, and by the qualifier-qualified relation "subāmantrite…" also works; in *iḍe rante* there is no such mutual connection — hence the difference. *riṣataḥ* — *śatṛ* after *ruṣa riṣa hiṃsārthāḥ* (*bhvādi*), the absence of *guṇa* with *śap* Vedic; or from *ruśa riśa hiṃsāyām* (*tudādi*) with Vedic *ṣ*, no *guṇa* because *śa* is *ṅit*; *rakṣasvinaḥ* — *vini* by "as-māyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121), initial-udātta of the suffix.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**घृताहवन (ghṛtāhavana)** — [you] called by offering ghee | **दीदिवः (dīdivaḥ)** — shining | **(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne)** — O Agni | **त्वम् (tvam)** — you | **रक्षस्विनः (rakṣasvinaḥ)** — accompanied by *rākṣasas* | **रिषतः (riṣataḥ)** — who do harm | **प्रति (prati)** — to us | **विरोधिनः (virodhinaḥ)** — the enemies | **दह स्म (daha sma)** — burn them to ashes.

### Page 499 — Rik 5: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar begins

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni! When we call you, we make offerings with ghee. Therefore you shine blazing. As such, burn to ashes those enemies of ours who are accompanied by rākṣasas and who do us harm.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Resplendent Agni, invoked by oblations of clarified butter burn down our adversaries defended by evil spirits (Rakshas).

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Ghṛtāhavana," "dīdivaḥ"** — to call Agni by pouring ghee into him is the custom in sacrifices; and since Agni, when ghee is offered, blazes brightly, the word *dīdivaḥ* is used here.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 499–502, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**घृताहवन (*ghṛtāhavana*)** — with the analysis "ghṛtena hūyate asmin", "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca" (printed "pā. sū. sū." [sic] 3-3-117): after a root, *lyuṭ* in the senses of instrument and locus; so *lyuṭ* after *hu dānādanayoḥ*; *ana* by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. 7-1-1), *guṇa*, *av*: *havana*. Although the root is transitive, its object is not meant, so it is intransitive; hence the ghee is an instrument in the action of *hu*, not an object; not being an object, the third case of "tṛtīyā ca hoś chandasi" (Pā. 2-3-3) — in the Veda the third, and by *ca* the second, case after the object of the action of *hu* — does not come; "kartṛ-karaṇayos tṛtīyā" (Pā. 2-3-18) gives the third case in the instrumental sense: *ghṛtena*. This is compounded with the *kṛdanta* *havana* by "kartṛ-karaṇe kṛtā bahulam" (printed "Pā. 2-1-3" at a line end, the last digit not printed; the bhāṣya gives 2-1-32): a third-case *subanta* in the sense of agent or instrument is compounded with a connected *kṛdanta*: *ghṛtahavana* [sic]. Now "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2) would give the first member's accent, but setting it aside "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139)

### Page 500 — Rik 5 grammar (continued)

gives the accent of the *kṛt* second member at the stem stage itself. Then, on adding the vocative singular, "eṅ-hrasvāt saṃbuddheḥ" (Pā. 6-1-69) drops the consonant of the vocative ending after a stem ending in *eṅ* or a short vowel; *ghṛtahavana* [sic] becomes a vocative, initial-udātta by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198). **दीदिवः (*dīdivaḥ*)** — root *divu krīḍā-vijigīṣā-vyavahāra-dyuti-moda-mada-svapna-kānti-gatiṣu*; *liṭ*, replaced by *kvasu* by "kvasuś ca" (Pā. 3-2-107): *div* + *vas*; "vasv-ekāj-ād-ghasām" (Pā. 7-2-67): only after roots that are monosyllabic after doubling, roots in *ā*, and *ghasḷ* does *vas* take *iṭ*; after other roots it does not, so here none; doubling by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-8): *div div* + *vas*; "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (printed "(Pā. sū.) 7-4-60") removes the *v* of the reduplicate; "tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-7): *tujādi* is an *ākṛtigaṇa*, and the reduplicate of its roots is lengthened in the Veda: *dīdiv* + *vas*; "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. 6-1-66) drops *v* or *y* before a *val* letter, so the *v* of the second *div*: *dīdivas*; *kvasu* is *kit*, so "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) gives no *guṇa*. Then the vocative singular *su*; "ugid-acāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-70) gives *num* before a *sarvanāmasthāna* to *ugit* non-root stems and to *añc* that has lost its *n*: *dīdivans* + *su*; *su* dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-68); "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-23) drops the *s*: *dīdivan*; "matuvaso ru saṃbuddhau chandasi" (Pā. 8-3-1) gives *ru* for the final of a *matup*- or *vasu*-stem before the vocative in the Veda; visarga by "kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ" (Pā. 8-3-15): *dīdivaḥ*. It stands after the word *ghṛtāhavana*, so "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19) makes it wholly unaccented. But here *ghṛtāhavana* and *dīdivaḥ* are both vocatives, and "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. 8-1-72) treats the earlier vocative as absent; then the second vocative does not stand after a word, so how could the eighth-chapter loss of accent apply? [For] "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) — *sāmānyavacana* means the word for the qualified —

### Page 501 — Rik 5 grammar (continued)

when a vocative in apposition expressing a qualifier follows, the vocative that expresses the qualified is not treated as absent; so the bar would apply, and with the "absent" treatment not arising, the word would follow another word and the eighth-chapter loss of accent would be in order — but this cannot be said, because here both vocatives *ghṛtāhavana* and *dīdivaḥ* qualify *agne*: *agne* is the general term and both are specific terms, so the bar does not apply. In the same way both vocatives are connected with *agne*, not with each other; lacking mutual connection, they lack *sāmarthya*, the capacity of conveying a joint sense. The treatment of a *subanta* before a vocative as part of the following vocative for accent, given by "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. 2-1-2), is a rule about words, and by the paribhāṣā "samarthaḥ padavidhiḥ" (Pā. 2-1-1) it applies only where there is *sāmarthya*; here neither has it, so the *parāṅgavat* treatment does not arise either, and one cannot say that, treating *ghṛtāhavana dīdiva* as one word, the sixth-chapter "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198) makes *ghṛ* udātta and "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158) the rest unaccented. Hence, just as in the mantra "iḍe rante 'dite sarasvati" (Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-6-8), where there is no mutual connection, each vocative is initial-udātta by the sixth-chapter sūtra, so here too each should be separately initial-udātta — how then is the eighth-chapter loss of accent justified? So one may object. The answer: here *dīdivaḥ* is not a qualifier of *agne* but of *ghṛtāhavana*; *ghṛtāhavana* is meant as the qualified term, and then the qualified-plus-qualifier *dīdivaḥ ghṛtāhavana* becomes a qualifier of *agne*. With reference to *dīdivaḥ*, *ghṛtāhavana* is the qualified, hence the general term; so "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) bars the "absent" treatment, the word follows another word, and the eighth-chapter loss of accent is in order. In this way *dīdivaḥ* and *ghṛtāhavana* are mutually connected and have *sāmarthya*, so "subāmantrite parāṅgavat svare" (Pā. 2-1-2) gives the *parāṅgavat* treatment too; with it, *ghṛtāhavana dīdivaḥ* count as one word, so the sixth-chapter "āmantritasya ca" makes *ghṛ* udātta and "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158) the rest unaccented; in this way too *dīdivaḥ* is wholly unaccented. In "iḍe rante 'dite sarasvati" (Tai. Saṃ. 7-1-6-8) there is no such mutual connection, so the full loss of accent does not arise there, and each vocative by the sixth-chapter sūtra

### Page 502 — Rik 5 grammar closes

is initial-udātta. Thus between *ghṛtāhavana dīdivaḥ* and *iḍe rante* there is the difference of the presence and absence of mutual connection. **रिषतः (*riṣataḥ*)** — root *ruṣa riṣa hiṃsārthāḥ*, in the *bhvādi* (first) class; *laṭ*, replaced by *śatṛ* by "laṭaḥ śatṛ-śānacau…" (Pā. 3-2-124); the vikaraṇa *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68); with it the *laghūpadha-guṇa* of "puganta-laghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. 7-3-86) would arise, but by Vedic procedure there is no *guṇa*: *riṣ* + *a* + *at*; *pararūpa* of the two *a*'s by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97): *riṣat*. Or the root *ruśa riśa hiṃsāyām*, in the *tudādi* class: with *śatṛ* for *laṭ*, the vikaraṇa *śa* by "tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-77); it is *apit*, so *ṅit* by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. 1-2-4), and "kṅiti ca" (Pā. 1-1-5) bars the *laghūpadha-guṇa*; the *ṣ* here comes by Vedic procedure; *pararūpa*: *riṣat*; either way the accusative plural is *riṣataḥ*. **रक्षस्विनः (*rakṣasvinaḥ*)** — *rakṣas* ends in *as*, so "as-māyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121) gives *vini* in the possessive sense after words in *as* and after *māyā*, *medhā*, *sraj*: *rakṣasvin*; accusative plural *śas*: *rakṣasvinaḥ*, initial-udātta by the suffix accent.

**॥५॥**
