pūrvasyāvidyamānavattvena padātparatvābhāvātpādāditvācca | parasparasāmānādhikaraṇye 'pi hotarityasya viśeṣaṇatve samānamevāvidyamānavattvam | ata evāvidyamānavattvātsāmarthye 'pi na parāṅgavadbhāva iti naikasvaryasiddhiḥ | ato hotariti viśeṣyam | ataḥ punātīti pāvaka ityavayavaprasiddhisvīkāreṇa viśeṣaṇatvāddhotariti viśeṣyam | tacca sāmānyavacanamiti nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇa ityavidyamānavattvapratiṣedhātpadātparatvādapādāditvācca dvitīyāmantritasyāṣṭamikanighātena vā parāṅgavadbhāve sati śeṣanighātena vā sarvānudāttatvasiddhiḥ | yakṣi | yajerloṭaḥ sipi bahulaṃ chandasīti śapo luk | vraścādinā ṣatvam | ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si | pā. 8-2-41 | iti katvam | serhirādeśaśchāndasatvānna bhavati | sipaḥ pittvenānudāttatvāddhātusvara eva śiṣyate | na ca tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | pūrvasya pāvaketyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvena padādaparatvāt | ata eva tasyāvyavadhāyakatvena hotarityapekṣya nighātaḥ syāditi cenna | yakṣipadāpekṣayā hotarityasyāpi pūrvatvenāvidyamānavattvāt | nanu nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇa iti tasya niṣiddhamavidyamānavattvam | na ca pāvakapadasyāvidyamānavattvena samānādhikaraṇaparatvābhāvaḥ | yakṣipadasyaiva hi kāryaṃ prati pāvakapadaṃ pūrvatvādavidyamānavatsyāt | hotaḥpadakāryamavidyamānavattvapratiṣedhaṃ prati tu paratvādvidyamānavadeveti bhavatyeva hotarityasyāvidyamānavattvapratiṣedhaḥ | atastasya vidyamānavattvāttadapekṣayā yakṣītyasya nighātaḥ prāpnotyeva | satyam | atra yakṣītyasya caśabdaparatvāccādiṣu ca | 8-1-58 | iti nighātapratiṣedho bhaviṣyatītyadoṣaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni! You, who bear the name *Susamiddha*, bring the gods, to favour him, for our sacrificer who is *haviṣmat* — possessed of the oblation. O *pāvaka*, purifier! O *hotar*, accomplisher of the *homa*! *Yakṣi ca* — and sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: *susamiddhaḥ* — *sam*, as a qualifier of the action, is a *gati*, giving a *prādi* compound; *su*, meaning "good", is compounded with *samiddha* as a karmadhāraya by "viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam" (Pā. 2-1-57); *su* is udātta by the stem accent, and "karmadhāraye 'niṣṭhā" (Pā. 6-2-46) keeps the first member's accent; were *su* a qualifier of the action, it would be a *gati*, the udātta of *sam* by "gatir anantaraḥ" would stand as the accent of the *kṛt* second member, and *su* would be unaccented. *devām̐ agne* — *ru* and nasalization as before. *haviṣmate* — *matup*; *bha* status by "tasau matvarthe" (Pā. 1-4-19) bars *pada* status, so no *ru*. The vocatives *hotar* and *pāvaka*, each connected separately with the verb, lack mutual capacity, so they are not treated as one word; nor is the second unaccented by the eighth-chapter rule, since by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" the first counts as absent and the second would begin the pāda. Even if they are in apposition, if *hotar* is the qualifier the "absent" treatment is the same. So *hotar* is the qualified term, and *pāvaka* — "he purifies" — the qualifier; the qualified is the general term, so "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe" bars the "absent" treatment, the second vocative follows a word and does not begin the pāda, and it becomes wholly unaccented either by the eighth-chapter rule or, with the *parāṅgavat* treatment, by the rule for the remainder. *yakṣi* — *loṭ* of *yaj*, *śap* dropped after *sip* by "bahulaṃ chandasi", *ṣ* by "vraśca…", *k* by "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si" (Pā. 8-2-41), no *hi* for *si* (Vedic); *sip* unaccented as *pit*, so the root accent stands. Objection: "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" does not apply, since the vocative *pāvaka* before it counts as absent, so *yakṣi* does not follow a word — nor does it follow *hotar*, which also counts as absent with respect to *yakṣi*. But "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe" has barred the "absent" treatment of *hotar*; with respect to *yakṣi* only *pāvaka* counts as absent, while for the bar on *hotar* it counts as present; so *hotar* is present and *yakṣi* would be unaccented after it. True; but since *yakṣi* is followed by *ca*, "cādiṣu ca" (8-1-58) bars the loss of accent — so there is no fault.)

### Page 527 (lower) — Rik 1: word-meanings

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne)** — O Agni | **सुसमिद्धः (susamiddhaḥ)** — [you, named] thoroughly kindled (well lit) | **नः (naḥ)** — to our | **हविष्मते (haviṣmate)** — sacrificer who is endowed with the oblation | *(for the purpose of favouring)* **देवान् (devān)** — the gods | **आ वह (ā vaha)** — bring here | **(हे) पावक ((he) pāvaka)** — O purifier | **(हे) होतः ((he) hotaḥ)** — O Agni, accomplisher of the *homa* | **यक्षि च (yakṣi ca)** — and accomplish the sacrifice.

### Page 528 — Rik 1: overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni! They call you *Susamiddha*, because you are well kindled and blaze brightly. Such as you are, bring the gods here to favour our sacrificer, who has prepared the oblation, and bring this sacrifice to completion.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Being well lighted, O Agni, invoker and purifier, bring hither the gods to the offerer of our oblations and perform the sacrifice.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

This is an **Āpri-sūkta**. We have given a short account of the Āpri-sūktas on pages 73–74. On this subject the great sage Yāska says in his Nirukta:

> अथात आप्रियः । आप्रियः कस्मादाप्नोतेः प्रीणातेर्वा । आप्रीभिराप्रीणातीति च ब्राह्मणम् ॥
>
> *athāta āpriyaḥ | āpriyaḥ kasmādāpnoteḥ prīṇātervā | āprībhirāprīṇātīti ca brāhmaṇam ||*

That is, *āpriya* means "being pleased": because the gods are pleased by these sūktas, they came to be called *āprī-sūktas*; and he cites the Brāhmaṇa sentence *āprībhir āprīṇāti ca*.

**"Susamiddhaḥ"** — the deity of this rik is Agni, called by the name *samiddha*. Here *su* = well; *sam* = fully; *iddhaḥ* = kindled: that is the sense of the parts: that is, well kindled, blazing up and burning brightly — "the thoroughly kindled" [the source's English]. When the animal offering is made, since Agni must be burning well, it may be the custom to address Agni in this way. Although the first five riks of this Āpri-sūkta have deities of different names, they are all called by Agni's names. On this, Yāska

> इध्मः । तासामिध्मः प्रथमागामी भवति । इध्मः समिन्धनात् । यज्ञेध्म इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥
>
> *idhmaḥ | tāsāmidhmaḥ prathamāgāmī bhavati | idhmaḥ samindhanāt | yajñedhma iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ||*

says. That is, among these five names of Agni, *samiddha* is the first; for the *idhma* (firewood, *fuel*) is the first means of kindling Agni; Yāska says that Kātthakya takes the word as the *idhma* — the *samidh* sticks used in the sacrifice — and Śākapūṇi as Agni (Ni. 8-4).

### Page 529 — Rik 1: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Hotaḥ"** — *homaniṣpādakaḥ*: the chief vessel-bearer in the *homa*, the carrier [of the oblation], or the one who invokes the gods.

**"Pāvaka"** — *śodhaka*: the purifier, the one who makes holy; or the one who shines brightly.

**"Yakṣi"** — "perform the sacrifice." The reason the poet prays Agni to "sacrifice" is that without Agni there is no sacrifice. Therefore, having called the gods to the sacrificial ground, making [Agni] pour the oblation into the fire so that it reaches the gods, and acting as the chief vessel-bearer so that the sacrifice is completed with all its limbs — in this sense the seer prays Agni, "perform the sacrifice."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 529–532, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**सुसमिद्धः (*susamiddhaḥ*)** — root *ñi indhī dīptau*, *rudhādi*; after it *kta*; by "anidatāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti" (Pā. 6-4-24), before a *kit* or *ṅit* suffix the penultimate *n* of a consonant-ending stem that is not *idit* is dropped: *idh* + *ta*; "jhaṣas tathor dho 'dhaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-40) gives *dh* for the *t*, and *jaśtva*: *iddha*. *Sam*, qualifying the action, has the name *gati*, and is compounded with *iddhaḥ* by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. 2-2-18). *Su* here is a *prātipadika* meaning "good", not a *gati*; it is compounded with *samiddha* as a karmadhāraya by "viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam" (Pā. 2-1-57). *Su* is final-udātta by the stem accent; by "karmadhāraye 'niṣṭhā" (printed "6-2 46"), in a karmadhāraya with a *kta*-ending second member, a first member that is not a *niṣṭhā* keeps its own accent, so the udātta of *su* stands, the other vowels unaccented by the rule for the remainder; the *sa* after *su* is svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-66), and the following vowels are *pracaya* by "svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām" (Pā. 1-2-39). If, like *sam*, *su* too were taken as qualifying the action, it would be a *gati* and give a *prādi* compound; by "gatir anantaraḥ" (Pā. 6-2-49), before a *kta*-ending in the object sense an immediately preceding *gati* keeps its accent, so *sam* would be udātta; even after compounding, by "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) the accent of the *kṛt* second member would have to stand, and *su* would be unaccented by the rule for the remainder. So *su* is not taken as qualifying the action but as a *prātipadika* meaning "good", and the desired initial udātta of *susamiddha* is obtained.

### Page 530 — Rik 1 grammar (continued)

*Su* does not qualify the action. Even granting it is a *prātipadika* meaning "good", the first-member accent of "karmadhāraye 'niṣṭhā" does not arise here: that sūtra applies only where the compound is the one specifically prescribed with *kta*-endings by "śreṇyādayaḥ kṛtādibhiḥ" (printed "2-1-59"). That is why in "mahān vrīhy-aparāhṇa-gṛṣṭīṣvāsa-jābāla-bhāra-bhārata-hailihila-raurava-pravṛddheṣu" (Pā. 6-2-38) — *mahat* keeps its own accent before these ten words, *vrīhi* and the rest — the mention of *pravṛddha* has a purpose; otherwise in *mahāpravṛddha* "karmadhāraye 'niṣṭhā" (6-2-46) would already give the first-member accent, and the mention of *pravṛddha* would be useless. This point is clear in the Mahābhāṣya on the sūtra *mahān vrīhi*; the lines there are:

> किमर्थं महतः प्रवृद्धशब्द उत्तरपदे पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वमुच्यते ? न कर्मधारये ऽनिष्ठेत्येव सिद्धम् ? न सिध्यति । किं कारणम् ? । श्रेण्यादिसमास इत्येवं तत् । किं पुनः कारणं श्रेण्यादिसमास इत्येवं तत् ? इह मा भूत् महानिलनिष्को [?] दक्षिणा दीयत इति ।
>
> *kimarthaṃ mahataḥ pravṛddhaśabda uttarapade pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvamucyate ? na karmadhāraye 'niṣṭhetyeva siddham ? na sidhyati | kiṃ kāraṇam ? | śreṇyādisamāsa ityevaṃ tat | kiṃ punaḥ kāraṇaṃ śreṇyādisamāsa ityevaṃ tat ? iha mā bhūt mahānilaniṣko [?] dakṣiṇā dīyata iti |*

In the Kaiyaṭa, taking up the words *śreṇyādisamāsa iti*, the explanation is:

> लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तपरिभाषया क्तान्तेन प्रतिपदोक्तो यः कर्मधारयस्तस्य ग्रहणमित्यर्थः
>
> *lakṣaṇapratipadoktaparibhāṣayā ktāntena pratipadokto yaḥ karmadhārayastasya grahaṇamityarthaḥ*

So, just as in *mahāpravṛddha*, formed by "san-mahat-paramottamotkṛṣṭāḥ pūjyamānaiḥ" (Pā. 2-1-61), so in *susamiddhaḥ*, compounded by "viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyeṇa bahulam" (printed "2-1-52" [?]), "karmadhāraye 'niṣṭhā" (Pā. 6-2-46) does not apply. The root *indhī* means "to shine", so it is intransitive, and the *kta* after it can only be in the sense of the state, not of the object; therefore, on the view that *sam* qualifies the action, deriving the udātta of *sam* by "gatir anantaraḥ" (Pā. 6-2-49) is not right. Even granting that derivation on the strength of the upasarga, it is proper to derive the udātta of *sam* in the second compound by the same rule; since the special accent of *thātha*… stays alert, the accent of the *kṛt* second member does not apply. The *dāsībhārādi* group (printed "6-2-42") is an *ākṛtigaṇa*; it is proper to include *susamiddha* in it and so derive the first-member accent. **देवाँ अग्ने (*devām̐ agne*)** — *ru* and nasalization as before. **हविष्मते (*haviṣmate*)** — "haviḥ asya asti": *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94); in *havis* + *mate*, "tasau matvarthe" (Pā. 1-4-19) gives the name *bha* to stems ending in *t* or *s* before a possessive suffix, and this *bha* bars the name *pada*; so the *ru* of "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. 8-2-66) does not come.

### Page 531 — Rik 1 grammar (continued)

**होतः पावक (*hotaḥ pāvaka*)** — both words are vocatives. If each is said to connect separately with the action alone, they have no mutual connection and so no *sāmarthya*, hence no *parāṅgavat* treatment; so one cannot say that, by that treatment, the sixth-chapter sūtra makes the *o* udātta and the rest unaccented by the rule for the remainder, giving a single accent. By "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. 8-1-72) the first vocative counts as absent, so the second does not follow a word and also begins the pāda; so "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19) cannot make it wholly unaccented. Now consider them as mutually connected. If *hotaḥ* is taken as the qualifier, the first counts as absent just as before; and because of that, even with *sāmarthya* from the mutual connection there is no *parāṅgavat* treatment; so in this case too the single unaccented form is not obtained. Therefore, accepting the familiar sense of the parts, "punāti iti pāvakaḥ", *pāvaka* must be taken as the qualifier and *hotaḥ* as the qualified. *Hotaḥ*, being the qualified, is the general term; so "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) bars the "absent" treatment. Thus the second vocative follows a word and is not at the beginning of the pāda, so the eighth-chapter loss of accent applies. Or, with the *parāṅgavat* treatment by "subāmantrite…" (printed "2-1-2"), the sixth-chapter "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 6-1-198) makes the *o* udātta and "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158), the rule for the remainder, makes all the other vowels unaccented. **यक्षि (*yakṣi*)** — root *yaja deva-pūjā-saṅgatikaraṇa-dāneṣu*; *loṭ*, second singular *sip*; being Vedic, the *hi* of "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. 3-4-87) does not replace *si*; the vikaraṇa *śap* is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73); in *yaj* + *si*, "vraśca-bhrasja-sṛja-mṛja-yaja-rāja-bhrāja-cchaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-36) gives *ṣ* for the *j*; "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si" (Pā. 8-2-41): before *s*, *ṣ* and *ḍh* become *k*; *ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59): *yakṣi*. *Sip*, being *pit*, is unaccented by "anudāttau sup-pitau" (Pā. 3-1-4); hence the root accent stands. Before *yakṣi* stands *pāvaka*, a vocative; by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. 8-1-72) it counts as absent, so *yakṣi* does not follow a word that is not a *tiṅanta*, and "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" does not make it wholly unaccented. For *yakṣi*,

### Page 532 — Rik 1 grammar closes

since *pāvaka* counts as absent, it cannot intervene; so one may say that, coming after the word *hotaḥ*, it should be wholly unaccented. But with respect to *yakṣi*, *hotaḥ* too is an earlier word, so by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" it too counts as absent; hence even with *hotaḥ* as the condition, the full loss of accent does not come. But in deriving the accent of *hotaḥ* and *pāvaka*, *hotaḥ* was said to be the qualified and *pāvaka*, by the familiar sense of its parts, the qualifier; so by "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. 8-1-73) the "absent" treatment of *hotaḥ* is barred. One cannot say that the following *pāvaka*, counting as absent, gives no following appositive vocative and so no occasion for the bar: for *pāvaka* counts as absent only when an operation is made on *yakṣi*, for which it is an earlier word; when the bar on *hotaḥ*'s "absent" treatment is being made, *pāvaka* is later than *hotaḥ*, not earlier, so it does not then count as absent. So an appositive vocative does follow, the bar of "nāmantrite…" applies, and *hotaḥ* does not count as absent. Thus *yakṣi* follows the word *hotaḥ*, and "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" should make it wholly unaccented — that is true. But here *yakṣi* is followed by the word *ca*; so "cādiṣu ca" (Pā. 8-1-58) — a *tiṅanta* is not unaccented before the five words *ca*, *vā*, *ha*, *aha*, *eva* — bars "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28); so *yakṣi* is not wholly unaccented, and, as said before, the root accent alone stands.

**॥१॥**

### Page 533 — Rik 2: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे कवे मेधाविन्नग्ने तनूनपादेतन्नामकस्त्वमद्यास्मिन्दिने नो ऽस्मदीयं मधुमन्तं रसवन्तं यज्ञं हविर्वीतये भक्षणार्थं देवेषु कृणुहि । कुरु । प्रापयेत्यर्थः ॥ मधुमन्तम् । फलिपाटिनमिमनिजनां गुक्पटिनाकिधतश्च । उ. १-१९ । इति मन्यतेरुप्रत्ययो धकारश्चान्तादेशः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेः प्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तो मधुशब्दः । तनूनपात् । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । अद्य । सद्यःपरुदित्यादिनास्मिन्काल इत्यर्थे द्यप्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । तद्धितश्चासर्वविभक्तिरित्यव्ययत्वादव्ययादाप्सुप इत्युपरि सप्तम्या लुक् । संहितायामन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घत्वम् । कृणुहि । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । इदितो नुम् धातोरिति नुम् । लोटः सेर्हिरादेशः । धिन्विकृण्व्योरच्चेति शपो ऽपवादो विकरण उप्रत्ययः । तत्संनियोगेन वकारस्याकारः । तस्यातो लोप इति लोपः । तस्य स्थानिवद्भावाल्लघूपधगुणो न भवति । उतश्च प्रत्ययादसंयोगपूर्वात् । पा. ६-४-१०६ । इति हेर्लुग्न भवत्युतश्च प्रत्ययाच्छन्दो वा वचनम् । पा. ६-४-१०६-१ । इति वचनात् । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । वीतये । मन्त्रे वृषेषपचमनविदभूवीरा उदात्त इति क्तिन्नुदात्तः ॥
>
> *he kave medhāvinnagne tanūnapādetannāmakastvamadyāsmindine no 'smadīyaṃ madhumantaṃ rasavantaṃ yajñaṃ havirvītaye bhakṣaṇārthaṃ deveṣu kṛṇuhi | kuru | prāpayetyarthaḥ || madhumantam | phalipāṭinamimanijanāṃ gukpaṭinākidhataśca | u. 1-19 | iti manyaterupratyayo dhakāraścāntādeśaḥ | nidityanuvṛtteḥ pratyayasya nittvādādyudātto madhuśabdaḥ | tanūnapāt | āmantritanighātaḥ | adya | sadyaḥparudityādināsminkāla ityarthe dyapratyayānto nipātitaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | taddhitaścāsarvavibhaktirityavyayatvādavyayādāpsupa ityupari saptamyā luk | saṃhitāyāmanyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti dīrghatvam | kṛṇuhi | kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca | idito num dhātoriti num | loṭaḥ serhirādeśaḥ | dhinvikṛṇvyoracceti śapo 'pavādo vikaraṇa upratyayaḥ | tatsaṃniyogena vakārasyākāraḥ | tasyāto lopa iti lopaḥ | tasya sthānivadbhāvāllaghūpadhaguṇo na bhavati | utaśca pratyayādasaṃyogapūrvāt | pā. 6-4-106 | iti herlugna bhavatyutaśca pratyayācchando vā vacanam | pā. 6-4-106-1 | iti vacanāt | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | vītaye | mantre vṛṣeṣapacamanavidabhūvīrā udātta iti ktinnudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O *kave* — wise Agni — you who bear the name *Tanūnapāt*, *adya* — on this day — *deveṣu kṛṇuhi*, make among the gods — that is, cause to reach them — our *madhumantam*, flavourful, *yajñam*, oblation, *vītaye*, for their eating." (Grammatical tail: *madhumantam* — the suffix *u* after *man* by "phali-pāṭi-nami-mani-janāṃ guk-paṭi-nāki-dhataś ca" (Uṇ. 1-19), with *dh* for the final; since *nit* is carried over, *madhu* is initial-udātta; *tanūnapāt* — unaccented as a vocative; *adya* — formed irregularly with *dya* in the sense "at this time" by "sadyaḥ-parut…", final-udātta by the suffix accent; an indeclinable by "taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ", so the locative after it is dropped by "avyayād āp-supaḥ"; lengthened in the Saṃhitā by "anyeṣām api dṛśyate"; *kṛṇuhi* — *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*, *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ", *hi* for *si* of *loṭ*, the vikaraṇa *u* instead of *śap* by "dhinvi-kṛṇvyor a ca", *a* for the *v* along with it, dropped by "ato lopaḥ", and since that loss counts as present there is no penultimate *guṇa*; the loss of *hi* by "utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt" (Pā. 6-4-106) does not take place, by the vārttika "utaś ca pratyayāc chando vā vacanam" (Pā. 6-4-106-1); unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ"; *vītaye* — *ktin* udātta by "mantre vṛṣeṣa…".)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) कवे ((he) kave)** — O wise Agni | **तनूनपात् (tanūnapāt)** — you named Tanūnapāt | **अद्य (adya)** — this day, now | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **मधुमन्तम् (madhumantam)** — tasty like honey | **यज्ञम् (yajñam)** — that is, the oblation offered in the sacrifice | **वीतये (vītaye)** — for the gods to eat | **देवेषु (deveṣu)** — among the gods | **कृणुहि (kṛṇuhi)** — make (that is, offer).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, you are wise, and you are also called Tanūnapāt. Such as you are, today offer to the gods, for their eating, the sacrifice we are performing (or the oblation belonging to the sacrifice).

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Wise Agni, also called Tanunapat present, this day our well-flavoured sacrifice to the gods that they may feast.

### Page 534 — Rik 2: Special Topics

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**"Madhumantam"** — *rasavantam*: tasty, sweet like honey: *well-flavoured, rich in honey* [the source's English]. The author of the *Vedārthayatna* takes *madhu* as Soma and explains "the oblation joined with Soma-juice." In support of this sense he gives as an example the rik

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-11.)*

> अश्विना पिबतं मधु दीद्यग्नी शुचिव्रता ।
>
> *aśvinā pibataṃ madhu dīdyagnī śucivratā |*

*("O Aśvins, of bright fires and pure vows, drink the honey" — mine and tentative.)*

In explaining this rik Sāyaṇa plainly says *madhu-mādhuryopetaṃ somam*, "the sweet Soma-juice." Besides this, in explaining the rik

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-73-2.)*

> मधोर्धाराभिर्जनयन्तो अर्कमित्प्रियामिन्द्रस्य तन्वमवीवृधन् ।
>
> *madhordhārābhirjanayanto arkamitpriyāmindrasya tanvamavīvṛdhan |*

*("Producing the hymn with streams of honey, they have increased the dear body of Indra" — mine and tentative.)*

the Bhāṣyakāra gives the word *madhoḥ* the sense *madakarasya somasya*, "of the Soma-juice that causes exhilaration." There are many riks in the Ṛgveda that give *madhu* the sense of Soma-juice; so the word *madhumantam* can be given the sense "accompanied by Soma-juice."

**"Tanūnapāt"** — this word too is another name of Agni. Some explain it as "one born from himself." In support of this sense they cite the rik *agninā agniḥ samidhyate* — "fire is kindled by (another) fire"; and since in the Nirukta the word *napāt* is read among the fifteen words for offspring beginning with *tuk*, *tokam* (Ni. 2-2), *napāt* means a son: *tanū* = from one's own body, *napāt* = one born. And the great sage Yāska, explaining the word *tanūnapāt* in the Daivatakāṇḍa of his Nirukta, says:

> तनूनपात् । तनूनपादाज्यमिति कात्थक्यः । नपादित्यनन्तरायाः प्रजाया नामधेयं निर्णततमा भवति । गौरत्र तनूरुच्यते । तता अस्यां भोगाः तस्याः पयो जायते पयस आज्यं जायते ॥
> अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । आपो ऽत्र तन्व उच्यन्ते । तता अन्तरिक्षे ताभ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायन्त ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्य एष जायते ॥
>
> *tanūnapāt | tanūnapādājyamiti kātthakyaḥ | napādityanantarāyāḥ prajāyā nāmadheyaṃ nirṇatatamā bhavati | gauratra tanūrucyate | tatā asyāṃ bhogāḥ tasyāḥ payo jāyate payasa ājyaṃ jāyate ||*
> *agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | āpo 'tra tanva ucyante | tatā antarikṣe tābhya oṣadhivanaspatayo jāyanta oṣadhivanaspatibhya eṣa jāyate ||*

(Ni. 8-5)

### Page 535 — Rik 2: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

The idea is this: Kātthakya says *tanūnapāt* means *ājya* (melted ghee). In support he says *tanūḥ* = *gauḥ*, the cow, and *napāt* = *prajā*, "born": so "from the cow" (*tanū*) "born" (*napāt*) is milk, and what comes from milk is ghee or *ājya*; thus he supports the sense *ājya* for *tanūnapāt*. As an example of this sense he gives the rik

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-2.)*

> तनूनपात्पथ ऋतस्य यानान्मध्वा समञ्जन्त्स्वदया सुजिह्व ।
> मन्मानि धीभिरुत यज्ञमृन्धन्देवत्रा च कृणुह्यध्वरं नः ॥
>
> *tanūnapātpatha ṛtasya yānānmadhvā samañjantsvadayā sujihva |*
> *manmāni dhībhiruta yajñamṛndhandevatrā ca kṛṇuhyadhvaraṃ naḥ ||*

*("O Tanūnapāt, anointing the paths of order with honey, make them sweet, O fair-tongued; prospering our thoughts and our sacrifice with insights, make our rite go to the gods" — mine and tentative.)*

Since this rik too is in an Āpri-sūkta, there is room for doubt whether the sense *ājya* fits the word *tanūnapāt* in it. According to Śākapūṇi's view, *tanūnapāt* is Agni: here *tanū* means water. Water falls as rain and from it plants and trees are produced; since Agni is born from a tree (the piece of wood called *araṇi*), Agni is called *tanūnapāt*.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 535–537, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**मधुमन्तम् (*madhumantam*)** — "phali-pāṭi-nami-mani-janāṃ guk-paṭi-nāki-dhataś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "1-18"): after *phala niṣpattau*, *paṭa gatau* in its *ṇic* form, *ṇama prahvatve śabde*, *mana jñāne* and *janī prādurbhāve* the suffix *u*, which is *nit*; *phal* takes the augment *guk*, and the others, in order, the substitutes *paṭ*, *nāki*, *dh*, *t*: that is the sense of the sūtra. By the maxim "ekāpi ṣaṣṭhī viṣayabhedād bhidyate" — one genitive gives different senses by difference of topic — the genitive connected with *phali* is a genitive of the part for the augment *guk*, while in the other four, where the substitutes *paṭ* etc. are prescribed, it is a genitive of the place; and in the case of the substitutes *dh* and *t* it denotes a substitute for the final of *man* and *jan*. So with *u* after *man*: *man* + *u*, *dh* for the *n*: *madhu*. The suffix being *nit*, *madhu* is initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197); *nit* is carried over from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. sū. 1-9) into *phali-pāṭi*…. **तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*)** — it is a vocative; so the eighth-chapter "āmantritasya ca" (printed "Pā. sū. 1-19" [sic]; the sūtra is 8-1-19) makes it wholly unaccented. **अद्य (*adya*)** — analysed "asmin kāle"; formed irregularly by "sadyaḥ-parut-parāry-aiṣamaḥ-paredyavy-adya…" (Pā. 5-3-22). "idamo 'š dyaś ca": that is, after *idam* in the locative the suffix *dya*, ending in *a*, comes,

### Page 536 — Rik 2 grammar (continued)

and *aś* replaces *idam*: that is the sense of the Bhāṣya sentence. So with *dya* after the locative of *idam*: *idam* + *ṅi* + *dya*; as a *taddhita*-ending it gets the name *prātipadika*; "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (printed "24-71" [sic]; the sūtra is 2-4-71) drops the *ṅi*; *aś* replaces *idam*, and being *śit* it replaces the whole: *adya*, final-udātta by the suffix accent. "taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 1-1-38): in *asarvavibhaktiḥ* a bahuvrīhi must be made; there the plural analysis "sarvā vibhaktayo yasmāt na bhavanti saḥ" is not possible. For in the Mahābhāṣya on this very sūtra, breaking up the arrangement of "dvy-ekayor dvivacanaikavacane" (Pā. 1-4-22) and "bahuṣu bahuvacanam" (printed "1-4-21"), the sūtras are rearranged as *ekavacanam*, *dvayor dvivacanam*, *bahuṣu bahuvacanam*, and it is established that the singular comes as the general rule, and the dual and plural set it aside where duality and plurality appear. Here *ekavacanam* yields the sense that the singular comes after stems ending in *ṅī*, *āp* and the *prātipadika*; by this general rule, where duality and plurality do not appear, the singular comes; so whether there is singularity or not, the singular comes. Since in duality and plurality the dual and plural come merely by being prescribed, where duality etc. do not appear the singular arises; so *ekavacanam*, being otherwise useless, teaches that the singular comes even where no sense of object etc. is present. So, after indeclinables, which have no connection with gender and number, the singular, operating without restriction, comes in every case. That is why the use of the *pratyāhāra* in *avyayād āp-supaḥ* is meaningful. In this way all case endings come after an indeclinable. So the plural analysis "sarvā vibhaktayo yasmān na bhavanti" cannot be made; the result is: "sarvā vacanatrayātmikā vibhaktir yasmān notpadyate kintu ekavacanāny evotpadyante sa taddhitāntaḥ avyayasaṃjñako bhavati" — a *taddhita*-ending after which not all case endings in the three numbers arise, but only the singular, takes the name *avyaya*: this is the settled sense of the sūtra. In *adya*, once this sūtra gives the name *avyaya*, the locative singular after it is dropped by "avyayād āp-supaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-82); in the Saṃhitā "anyeṣām api dṛśyate" (printed "7-3-137" [sic], with the same first digit as "7-1-58" below; the sūtra is 6-3-137) lengthens it. **कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)** — root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*; *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58): *kṛnv*; *loṭ*, second singular *sip*, replaced by *hi*; in place of the vikaraṇa *śap* the vikaraṇa *u* by "dhinvi-kṛṇvyor a ca"

### Page 537 — Rik 2 grammar closes

(Pā. 3-1-80): after *dhinv* and *kṛṇv*, where *śap* would come, the suffix *u*, and *a* as the substitute for their final; so the *v* becomes *a*: *kṛna* + *u* + *hi*; "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-48) drops the *a*; that loss counts as present, so there is no *laghūpadha-guṇa*. Here "utaś ca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt" (Pā. 6-4-106) would drop the *hi*; but by "utaś ca pratyayāc chando vā vacanam" (Pā. 6-4-106-1) the loss of *hi* prescribed by that sūtra is optional in the Veda, so it is not dropped. By "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam" the *n* becomes *ṇ*: *kṛṇuhi*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). **वीतये (*vītaye*)** — by "mantre vṛṣeṣa-paca-mana-vida-bhū-vīrā udāttaḥ" (Pā. 3-3-96) the suffix *ktin* is udātta.

**॥२॥**

> मधु॑जिह्वं हवि॒ष्कृत॑म् ॥३॥ [accent ?]
>
> *narāśáṃsam ihá priyam asmín yajñá úpa hvaye |* [accent ?]

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> नराशंसम् । इह । प्रियम् । अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । उप । ह्वये ॥
> मधुऽजिह्वम् । हविःऽकृतम् ॥३॥
>
> *narāśaṃsam | iha | priyam | asmin | yajñe | upa | hvaye ||*
> *madhu-jihvam | haviḥ-kṛtam ||3||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> इह देवयजनदेशे ऽस्मिन्प्रवर्तमाने यज्ञे नराशंसनामकमग्निमुप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । कीदृशम् । प्रियं देवानां प्रीतिहेतुं मधुजिह्वं मधुरभाषिजिह्वोपेतं माधुर्यरसास्वादकजिह्वोपेतं वा हविष्कृतं हविषो निष्पादकम् ॥ नरशब्दो नॄ नये इत्यस्मादबन्तः । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । शंसन्त्यस्मिन्निति शंसः । हलश्च । पा. ३-३-१२१ । इत्यधिकरणे घञ् । नराणां शंस इति समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्त उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपत् । पा. ६-२-१४० । इति पूर्वोत्तरपदे प्रकृतिस्वरे भवतः । अत एव वनस्पत्यादिषु पाठान्नरशब्दस्य दीर्घत्वम् । इह । इदमो ह इति ह-प्रत्ययः । इदम इशितीशादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । प्रियम् । प्रीणातीति प्रियः । इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः क इति कः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अस्मिन् । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । ह्वये । निघातः । मधुजिह्वम् । मधुशब्दस्याद्युदात्तत्वमुक्तम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरेण स एव शिष्यते । हविष्कृतम् । हविः करोतीति हविष्कृत् । क्विपि ह्रस्वस्य तुक् । नित्यं समासे ऽनुत्तरपदस्थस्येति षत्वम् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥
>
> *iha devayajanadeśe 'sminpravartamāne yajñe narāśaṃsanāmakamagnimupa hvaye | āhvayāmi | kīdṛśam | priyaṃ devānāṃ prītihetuṃ madhujihvaṃ madhurabhāṣijihvopetaṃ mādhuryarasāsvādakajihvopetaṃ vā haviṣkṛtaṃ haviṣo niṣpādakam || naraśabdo nṝ naye ityasmādabantaḥ | pratyayasya pittvāddhātusvara eva śiṣyate | śaṃsantyasminniti śaṃsaḥ | halaśca | pā. 3-3-121 | ityadhikaraṇe ghañ | narāṇāṃ śaṃsa iti samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpta ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat | pā. 6-2-140 | iti pūrvottarapade prakṛtisvare bhavataḥ | ata eva vanaspatyādiṣu pāṭhānnaraśabdasya dīrghatvam | iha | idamo ha iti ha-pratyayaḥ | idama iśitīśādeśaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | priyam | prīṇātīti priyaḥ | igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ ka iti kaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | asmin | ūḍidamityādinā vibhakterudāttatvam | hvaye | nighātaḥ | madhujihvam | madhuśabdasyādyudāttatvamuktam | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvareṇa sa eva śiṣyate | haviṣkṛtam | haviḥ karotīti haviṣkṛt | kvipi hrasvasya tuk | nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasyeti ṣatvam | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||*

**Translation:** "Here, in this sacrifice now in progress, at the place of worship of the gods, *upa hvaye* — I invoke — the fire named *Narāśaṃsa*. What is he like? *Priyam* — the cause of delight to the gods; *madhujihvam* — having a tongue that speaks sweetly, or a tongue that tastes the flavour of sweetness; *haviṣkṛtam* — the accomplisher of the oblation." (Grammatical tail: *nara* — from *nṝ naye* with *ap*; the suffix being *pit*, the root accent alone remains; *śaṃsa* — "they recite in it", *ghañ* in the locative sense by "halaś ca" (Pā. 3-3-121); in the compound "narāṇāṃ śaṃsaḥ", where the *kṛt* second-member accent would come, "ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat" (Pā. 6-2-140) gives both members their own accents at once, and from its reading in the *vanaspatyādi* group *nara* is lengthened; *iha* — *ha* by "idamo haḥ", *iś* for *idam* by "idama iś", suffix accent; *priyam* — "he pleases", *ka* by "igupadha-jñā-prī-kiraḥ kaḥ", suffix accent; *asmin* — the case ending udātta by "ūḍ-idam…"; *hvaye* — unaccented; *madhujihvam* — *madhu* initial-udātta as said, and in the bahuvrīhi that accent alone remains; *haviṣkṛtam* — "he makes the oblation", *tuk* for the short vowel before *kvip*, *ṣ* by "nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya", the *kṛt* second-member accent.)

### Page 538 — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics begin

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**इह (iha)** — at this sacrificial ground | **अस्मिन् यज्ञे (asmin yajñe)** — in this sacrifice that we perform | **प्रियम् (priyam)** — dear to the gods | **मधुजिह्वम् (madhujihvam)** — who has a tongue that speaks sweetly, or that tastes sweet juice | **हविष्कृतम् (haviṣkṛtam)** — who makes (cooks) the oblation | **नराशंसम् (narāśaṃsam)** — Agni, called by the name Narāśaṃsa | **उप ह्वये (upa hvaye)** — I invoke.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni called *Narāśaṃsa*! You are dear to the gods; you speak sweetly, or you taste the sweet oblation; you cook the oblation and make it ready. Such a Narāśaṃsa I now call in this sacrifice that we perform.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> I invoke here at this sacrifice Narasamsa, the beloved one, the sweet-tongoned [sic], preparer of sacrifcial [sic] food.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The deity of this rik is Narāśaṃsa — that is, Agni, called by that name. Yāska's explanation of the word runs as follows:

> (१) नराशंसः । नराशंसो यज्ञ इति कात्थक्यः । नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसन्ति ॥
>
> *(1) narāśaṃsaḥ | narāśaṃso yajña iti kātthakyaḥ | narā asminnāsīnāḥ śaṃsanti ||*

### Page 539 — Rik 3: Special Topics (continued)

> (२) अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः । नर्यैः प्रशस्यो भवति ॥
>
> *(2) agniriti śākapūṇiḥ | naryaiḥ praśasyo bhavati ||*



Two different senses of the word *narāśaṃsa* are thus given: (1) *narāśaṃsa* means the sacrifice: because in this sacrifice *narāḥ*, men, sitting down, *śaṃsanti*, praise (Agni or the gods), this rite is called *yajña* — this is Kātthakya's view; (2) because he is praised by men, Agni is called *narāśaṃsa* — this is Śākapūṇi's view. The second explanation is the fitting one here. **Skandasvāmī** says: *naraiḥ praśasyata iti narāśaṃso 'gniḥ taṃ narāśaṃsam* — "he who is praised by men is *narāśaṃsa*, Agni; that Narāśaṃsa [I invoke]."

**"Priyam"** — the Bhāṣyakāra explains *devānāṃ priyam*, "dear to the gods"; Skandasvāmī explains *manuṣyāṇāṃ priyam*, "dear to men." Both senses are fitting.

### Page 540 — Rik 3: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Madhujihvam"** — *madhura-bhāṣi-jihvopetam*, "having a tongue that speaks sweetly", and *mādhurya-rasāsvādaka-jihvopetam*, "having a tongue that tastes the sweet flavour (of the oblation, the *ājya* and the other *homa* substances)": so the Bhāṣyakāra explains. **Skandasvāmī** says *madhujihvaḥ* =

> नित्यमुत्सृष्टानां हविषां भक्षयिता । अथवा जिह्वेति वाङ्नाम मध्वी जिह्वा यस्य स मधुजिह्वः । होतृत्वाद्ध्यग्नेर्देवतानां स्तावकत्वादस्ति मधुवाक्त्वम् । सुभगवचनमित्यर्थः ॥
>
> *nityamutsṛṣṭānāṃ haviṣāṃ bhakṣayitā | athavā jihveti vāṅnāma madhvī jihvā yasya sa madhujihvaḥ | hotṛtvāddhyagnerdevatānāṃ stāvakatvādasti madhuvāktvam | subhagavacanamityarthaḥ ||*

— one who always eats the tasty or sweet oblation; *jihvā* means speech, words; so *madhujihvaḥ* is one who speaks good words, words that give delight to the ear. Since Agni, when calling the gods, speaks sweet words addressed to them, he is called *madhujihva*: Skandasvāmī thus states, in another way, the same two senses the Bhāṣyakāra gave. Senses such as "Honey-tongoned, sweet-longoned" [sic] [the source's English] may be given.

**"Haviṣkṛtam"** — *haviṣo niṣpādakam*: "the maker of the oblation, one who prepares the oblation": when the oblation is made, it must be placed on Agni and cooked; hence Agni is said to make the oblation. [The source's English: "Preparer of sacrifical [sic] food."]

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 540–541, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**नराशंसम् (*narāśaṃsam*)** — root *nṝ* [?] *naye*; by "ṛdorap" (printed "vā. sū." [sic] 3-3-57), after roots ending in *ṝ* or *u*, *ap* comes both in the sense of the state and for a *kāraka* other than the agent; so *ap* after *nṝ*: *nṝ* + *a*, *guṇa*

### Page 541 — Rik 3 grammar closes

with *r*: *nara*. The suffix being *pit*, it is unaccented; the *a* after the *n* stays udātta by the root accent. "śaṃsanti asmin iti śaṃsaḥ": "halaś ca" (Pā. 3-3-121) — after a consonant-ending root, *ghañ* — gives *ghañ* after *śaṃs* in the locative sense; *śaṃsa* is initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). On compounding "narāṇāṃ śaṃsaḥ", "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) would give the *kṛt* second-member accent; setting it aside, "thātha-ghañ-ktāj-abitra-kāṇām" (Pā. 6-2-144) would make the second member final-udātta; setting that aside, since *narāśaṃsa* is read in the *vanaspatyādi* group, "ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat" (Pā. 6-2-140) — in the words of this group the first and second members both keep their own accents at once — gives both members their own accent together. Because in this *vanaspatyādi* group *nara* is read lengthened as *narāśaṃsa*, *nara* is lengthened; the author of the Kaumudī too explains the lengthening in this way as irregular formation. Some derive the lengthening of the first member from "anyeṣām api dṛśyate" (Pā. 6-3-137). **इह (*iha*)** — "idamo haḥ" (Pā. 5-3-11): after a locative of *idam* the suffix *ha*: *idam* + *ṅi* + *ha*; *luk* of *ṅi*; *iś* for *idam* by "idama iś" (Pā. 5-3-3): *iha*; the suffix accent. **प्रियम् (*priyam*)** — "prīṇāti iti priyaḥ": "igupadha-jñā-prī-kiraḥ kaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-135): after roots with *ik* as penultimate and after *jñā avabodhane*, *prīñ tarpaṇe* and *kṝ vikṣepe*, the suffix *ka*; so *ka* after *prīñ tarpaṇe*; being *kit*, no *guṇa*; *iyaṅ* by "aci śnu-dhātu-bhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅ-uvaṅau" (Pā. 6-4-77): *priya*; the suffix accent. *Asmin*: by "ūḍ-idam-padādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ" (printed "6-1-71" [sic]; the sūtra is 6-1-171) the case ending is udātta. **ह्वये (*hvaye*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; being *ñit*, it is *ubhayapadin*; ātmanepada *laṭ*, first singular *iṭ*; "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. 3-4-79) gives *e* for it; *pararūpa* with the *śap* of "kartari śap": *hvaye*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ". **मधुजिह्वम् (*madhujihvam*)** — *madhu* was said in the previous mantra to be initial-udātta; "madhu jihvā yasya saḥ", a bahuvrīhi; by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1) the first-member accent stands. **हविष्कृतम् (*haviṣkṛtam*)** — "haviḥ karoti"; after *ḍukṛñ* with *havis* as *upapada*, "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76) gives *kvip*; as a *kṛdanta* it is a *prātipadika*; the *sup* dropped, the *kvip* lost; before *havis* + *kṛ*, "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk" (Pā. 6-1-71) gives *tuk* to a stem ending in a short vowel before a *p*-marked *kṛt*; by the paribhāṣā "ādyantau ṭakitau" it is added at the end: *havis* + *kṛt*; *ru* and visarga for the *s*; "nityaṃ samāse 'nuttarapadasthasya" (Pā. 8-3-45) turns the visarga into *ṣ*: *haviṣkṛt*. By "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (printed "6-2 139") the *kṛt* second member keeps its accent, final-udātta; the *kṛt* is final-udātta by the root accent; after it *am*, unaccented as a *sup*, then svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ".

**॥३॥**

### Page 541 (lower) — Sūkta 13, Rik 4

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्ने॑ सु॒खत॑मे॒ रथे॑ दे॒वाँ ई॑ळि॒त आ व॑ह ।
> असि॒ होता॒ मनु॑र्हितः ॥४॥
>
> *ágne sukhátame ráthe devā́m̐ īḷitá ā́ vaha |*
> *asi hótā mánur hitaḥ ||4||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्ने । सुखऽतमे । रथे । देवान् । ईळितः । आ । वह ॥
> असि । होता । मनुःऽहितः ॥४॥
>
> *agne | sukha-tame | rathe | devān | īḷitaḥ | ā | vaha ||*
> *asi | hotā | manuḥ-hitaḥ ||4||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(runs onto p. 542)*

> इट्शब्दाभिधेय हे अग्ने ईळितो ऽस्माभिः स्तुतः सन्सुखतमे ऽतिशयेन सुखहेतौ कस्मिंश्चिद्रथे देवान्स्थापयित्वा कर्मभूमावा वह । इट्शब्दाभिधेयत्वमत्र सूचयितुमीळित इति विशेषणम् । मनुर्हितो मनुना मन्त्रेण मनुष्येण वा यजमानादिरूपेण हितो ऽत्र स्थापितस्त्वं होता देवानामाह्वातासि ॥ सुखतमे । सुखमस्मिन्नस्तीति मतुप् । तस्य गुणवचनेभ्यो मतुपो लुग्वक्तव्यः । पा. ५-२-९४-३ । इति लुक् । अतिशयेन सुखः सुखतमः । तमपो ऽनुदात्तत्वात्प्रातिपदिकस्वरः । रथे । रमु क्रीडायाम् । रमन्ते ऽस्मिन्निति रथः । हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन् । उ. २-२ । इति क्थन् । एकाच उपदेशे ऽनुदात्तात् । पा. ७-२-१० । इतीट्प्रतिषेधः । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिना । पा. ६-४-३७ । मकारलोपः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । ईळितः । ईड स्तुतौ । निष्ठेति क्तः । इडागमः । तस्यागमा अनुदात्ता इत्यनुदात्तः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । देवानिति नकारस्य संहितायां दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति रुत्वम् । आतो ऽटि नित्यमित्याकारस्यानुनासिकभावः । भोभगो इत्यादिना रोर्यत्वम् । तस्य लोपः शाकल्यस्येति लोपः । तस्यासिद्धत्वादाद्गुणो न भवति । आ । निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तः । असि । अस भुवि । लटः सिप् । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । तासस्त्योर्लोप इति सकारस्य लोपः । होता । ताच्छील्ये तृन् । सौ ऋदुशनसित्यादिना । पा. ७-१-९४ । अनङ् । ङित्त्वादन्तादेशः । अप्तृन्नित्यादिना । पा. ६-४-११ । उपधादीर्घः । हल्ङ्यादिलोपनलोपौ । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । मनुर्हितः । मन्यत इति मनुः । मन ज्ञाने । शॄस्वृस्निहित्रप्यसिवसिहनिक्लिदिबन्धिमनिभ्यश्च । उ. १-१० । इत्युप्रत्ययः । तत्र निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । हितः । दधातेर्निष्ठेति कर्मणि क्तः । दधातेर्हिः । पा. ७-४-४२ । इति हिरादेशः । मनुना हित इति समासे तृतीयायाः स्थाने सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना स्वित्यादेशः [?] । तस्य रुत्वम् । लुगभावश्छान्दसः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥
>
> *iṭśabdābhidheya he agne īḷito 'smābhiḥ stutaḥ sansukhatame 'tiśayena sukhahetau kasmiṃścidrathe devānsthāpayitvā karmabhūmāvā vaha | iṭśabdābhidheyatvamatra sūcayitumīḷita iti viśeṣaṇam | manurhito manunā mantreṇa manuṣyeṇa vā yajamānādirūpeṇa hito 'tra sthāpitastvaṃ hotā devānāmāhvātāsi || sukhatame | sukhamasminnastīti matup | tasya guṇavacanebhyo matupo lugvaktavyaḥ | pā. 5-2-94-3 | iti luk | atiśayena sukhaḥ sukhatamaḥ | tamapo 'nudāttatvātprātipadikasvaraḥ | rathe | ramu krīḍāyām | ramante 'sminniti rathaḥ | hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan | u. 2-2 | iti kthan | ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt | pā. 7-2-10 | itīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | anudāttopadeśetyādinā | pā. 6-4-37 | makāralopaḥ | nittvādādyudāttatvam | īḷitaḥ | īḍa stutau | niṣṭheti ktaḥ | iḍāgamaḥ | tasyāgamā anudāttā ityanudāttaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | devāniti nakārasya saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti rutvam | āto 'ṭi nityamityākārasyānunāsikabhāvaḥ | bhobhago ityādinā roryatvam | tasya lopaḥ śākalyasyeti lopaḥ | tasyāsiddhatvādādguṇo na bhavati | ā | nipātatvādādyudāttaḥ | asi | asa bhuvi | laṭaḥ sip | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | tāsastyorlopa iti sakārasya lopaḥ | hotā | tācchīlye tṛn | sau ṛduśanasityādinā | pā. 7-1-94 | anaṅ | ṅittvādantādeśaḥ | aptṛnnityādinā | pā. 6-4-11 | upadhādīrghaḥ | halṅyādilopanalopau | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | manurhitaḥ | manyata iti manuḥ | mana jñāne | śṝsvṛsnihitrapyasivasihaniklidibandhimanibhyaśca | u. 1-10 | ityupratyayaḥ | tatra nidityanuvṛtternittvādādyudāttaḥ | hitaḥ | dadhāterniṣṭheti karmaṇi ktaḥ | dadhāterhiḥ | pā. 7-4-42 | iti hirādeśaḥ | manunā hita iti samāse tṛtīyāyāḥ sthāne supāṃ sulugityādinā svityādeśaḥ [?] | tasya rutvam | lugabhāvaśchāndasaḥ | tṛtīyā karmaṇīti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni, denoted by the word *Iṭ*! Being *īḷitaḥ* — praised by us — *ā vaha*: having seated the gods in some *sukhatame* chariot, the greatest cause of ease, bring them to the place of the rite. The epithet *īḷitaḥ* is used here to indicate that [you] are denoted by the word *Iṭ*. *Manurhitaḥ* — placed here by *manu*, the mantra, or by man in the form of the sacrificer and the rest — you are *hotā*, the invoker of the gods." (Grammatical tail, partly on p. 542: *sukhatame* — *matup* "there is happiness in it", dropped by the vārttika "guṇavacanebhyo matupo lug vaktavyaḥ" (Pā. 5-2-94-3); "exceedingly *sukha*": *sukhatama*; *tamap* being unaccented, the stem accent stands; *rathe* — *ramu krīḍāyām*, "they delight in it", *kthan* by "hani-kuṣi-nī-rami-kāśibhyaḥ kthan" (Uṇ. 2-2), *iṭ* barred by "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" (Pā. 7-2-10), the *m* dropped by "anudāttopadeśa…" (Pā. 6-4-37), initial-udātta as *nit*; *īḷitaḥ* — *īḍa stutau*, *kta*, the augment *iṭ* unaccented as an augment, the suffix accent; *devān* — in the Saṃhitā *ru* by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde", nasalization of the *ā* by "āto 'ṭi nityam", *y* by "bho-bhago…", dropped by "lopaḥ śākalyasya", and since that loss is *asiddha* there is no *guṇa*; *ā* — initial-udātta as a particle; *asi* — *sip* after *asa bhuvi*, *śap* dropped, the *s* dropped by "tāsastyor lopaḥ"; *hotā* — *tṛn* in the habitual sense, *anaṅ* by "ṛd-uśanas…" (Pā. 7-1-94), replacing the final as *ṅit*, lengthening of the penultimate by "ap-tṛn…" (Pā. 6-4-11), loss of *su* and of *n*, initial-udātta as *nit*; *manurhitaḥ* — *manu* "he thinks", from *mana jñāne* with *u* by "śṝ-svṛ-snihi-trapy-asi-vasi-hani-kliḍi-bandhi-manibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. 1-10), initial-udātta as *nit* is carried over; *hita* — *kta* after *dhā* in the object sense, *hi* by "dadhāter hiḥ" (Pā. 7-4-42); in the compound "placed by Manu", the substitute *su* [?] for the third case by "supāṃ suluk…", with *ru* — the absence of *luk* being Vedic; the first member's accent by "tṛtīyā karmaṇi".)

### Page 542 — Rik 4: word-meanings, overall sense, English

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne)** — O Agni, called by the name *Iṭ* | **ईळितः (īḷitaḥ)** — praised by us | **देवान् (devān)** — the gods | **सुखतमे (sukhatame)** — [in a chariot] that gives the greatest comfort | **रथे (rathe)** — in a chariot | *(having seated them)* **आ वह (ā vaha)** — bring | *(for)* **मनुर्हितः (manurhitaḥ)** — [you are] placed by the mantra, or by men — the sacrificer and the rest | **होता (hotā)** — the invoker of the gods | **असि (asi)** — you are.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, they call you *Iṭ* (*Iḷa*), because you are praised by us (men). Such as you are, seat the gods in a chariot that gives comfort and bring them here; for the sacrificer has placed you as the *hotṛ*, to invoke the gods.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Agni (called Ila) being praised (by men) conduct the gods hither in an easy-moving chariot; for you are the invoker instituted by men.

### Page 543 — Rik 4: Special Topics and grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

Yāska's explanation:

> ईळः । ईळ ईट्टेः स्तुतिकर्मण इन्धतेर्वा ॥
>
> *īḷaḥ | īḷa īṭṭeḥ stutikarmaṇa indhatervā ||*

— *īḷaḥ*, or the word *īḷita*, is formed from the root *īḍa stutau*, "to praise"; since he is praised, Agni is called *Īḷa*.

**"Sukhatame"** — *sukham asminn asti* — "that in which there is comfort"; *atiśayena sukhaḥ sukhatamaḥ*: *atiśayena sukhahetau (kasmiṃścid rathe)*: a chariot that gives great comfort, that does not jolt when moving, in which soft seats and the like have been laid ready for sitting, and which is comfortable for travelling — an *easy-moving chariot* [the source's English].

**"Rathe"** — *ramu krīḍāyām; ramante 'smin iti rathaḥ*: "since people sit in it and travel with delight, it is called *ratha*."

**"Īḷitaḥ"** — *īḍa stutau*: praised; *praised, adored etc.* [the source's English].

**"Hotā"** — *devānām āhvātā*: one who calls the gods to the sacrificial ground.

**"Manurhitaḥ"** — *manunā mantreṇa, yajamānādi-rūpeṇa manuṣyeṇa vā sthāpitaḥ* — "established by Manu, i.e., by a mantra, or by a man in the form of the sacrificer and others"; that is, placed with a mantra, or appointed by the sacrificer who is a man (*prārthita*, requested; *niyamita*, appointed). **Skandasvāmī** gives the senses *prajāpatinā nihitaḥ*, "placed by Prajāpati (Brahmā)", and *manuṣyeṣu nihitaḥ upakāraka ity arthaḥ*, "placed (by the gods) among men" — that is, placed on earth among men to help them, one who does men good. The Western scholar **Oldenberg** explains this word as "Instituted by Manus," not by men [the source's English].

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 543–546, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**सुखतमे (*sukhatame*)** — analysed "sukham asmin asti"; after the quality-word *sukha*, "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94) gives *matup*; "guṇavacanebhyo matupo lug iṣṭaḥ" (printed "Pā. sū. 5-2-94 vā. 3") drops it; then after the quality-word *sukha*, in the sense of excess, "atiśāyane tamab-iṣṭhanau" (Pā. 5-3-55) gives *tamap*: *sukhatama*; *matup* [sic, for *tamap*], being *pit*, is unaccented; the stem accent alone stands.

### Page 544 — Rik 4 grammar (continued)

**रथे (*rathe*)** — analysed "ramante asmin"; root *ramu krīḍāyām*; after it "hani-kuṣi-nī-rami-kāśibhyaḥ kthan" (Uṇ. sū. "2-159" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 2-2): after *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*, *kuṣa niṣkarṣe*, *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*, *ramu krīḍāyām*, *kāśṛ dīptau* the suffix *kthan*: *ram* + *tha*; before this *ārdhadhātuka* *tha*, "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-35) would give *iṭ*. *Ram* is counted in the *kārikā* listing the *anudātta* roots — "lip lup vap śap svap sṛpi yabh rabh labh gam nam yamo ramiḥ" — so it is *anudātta* in the *upadeśa* and monosyllabic; therefore "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" (Pā. 7-2-10) bars *iṭ* before a *val*-initial *ārdhadhātuka*. Then "anudāttopadeśa-vanati-tanoty-ādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti" (printed "6-4-32" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 6-4-37): before a *jhal*-initial *kit* or *ṅit* suffix, the final nasal of *anudātta*-*upadeśa* roots and others, and the final of *van*, is dropped: the *m* is dropped: *ratha*. The suffix being *nit*, *ratha* is initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (printed "6-7-193" [?] [sic]; the sūtra is 6-1-197). **ईळितः (*īḷitaḥ*)** — root *īḍa stutau*; after it *kta* by "niṣṭhā" (printed "3-2-10" [sic]; the sūtra is 3-2-102); *iṭ* by "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-35); by the tradition "ajmadhyastha-ḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ", or by "dvayoś cāsya svarayoḥ" (printed "Prā. śā."), *ḷ* for the *ḍ*; the *i* that came by the augment is unaccented by "āgamā anudāttāḥ"; the suffix accent stands. **देवान् (*devān*)** — in the Saṃhitā "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. 8-3-9) gives *ru* for the *n*; "āto 'ṭi nityam" (printed "8-3-3") nasalizes the *ā*; "bho-bhago-agho-apūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. 8-3-17) gives *y* for the *ru*; the loss of *y* by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19) is *asiddha*, so "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-87) gives no *guṇa*. **आ (*ā*)** — a *nipāta*, so initial-udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ". **असि (*asi*)** — root *asa bhuvi*; after it *laṭ*, replaced by the second singular *sip*; the *śap* of "kartari śap" (Pā. 3-1-68) is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ…" (Pā. 2-4-72); "tāsastyor lopaḥ" (Pā. 7-4-50): before an *s*-initial suffix the final of *tās* and of *as* is dropped, so the *s* of *as*

### Page 545 — Rik 4 grammar (continued)

is dropped: *asi*. Standing at the beginning of the pāda, it is not made wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28). *Sip*, being *pit*, is unaccented; the root accent stands. **होता (*hotā*)** — root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; after it, under the heading "ā kves tacchīla-taddharma-tatsādhukāriṣu" (Pā. 3-2-134), *tṛn* by "tṛn" (Pā. 3-2-135); *samprasāraṇa* by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 6-1-34); *pūrvarūpa* by "samprasāraṇāc ca" (printed "6-8-108" [sic]; the sūtra is 6-1-108); *guṇa* of the *u* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84): *hotṛ*; then the nominative singular *su*; "ṛd-uśanas-purudaṃso-'nehasāṃ ca" (Pā. 7-1-94): before *su* other than the vocative, stems ending in *ṛ* and *uśanas*, *purudaṃsas*, *anehas* take the substitute *anaṅ*; although it has more than one letter, being *ṅit* it replaces the final by "ṅic ca" (Pā. 1-1-53): *hotan* + *s*; "ap-tṛn-tṛc-svasṛ-naptṛ-neṣṭṛ-tvaṣṭṛ-kṣattṛ-hotṛ-potṛ-praśāstṝṇām" (Pā. 6-4-11) lengthens the penultimate before a *sarvanāmasthāna* other than the vocative: *hotān* + *s*; *su* dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-68), *n* dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7): *hotā*; ending in an *n*-marked suffix, it is initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). **मनुर्हितः (*manurhitaḥ*)** — "manyate iti manuḥ": root *mana jñāne*; "śṝ-svṛ-snihi-trapy-asi-vasi-hani-kliḍi-bandhi-manibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "1-10"): after *śṝ hiṃsāyām*, *svṛ śabdopatāpayoḥ*, *ṣṇiha upatāpe*, *trapūṣ lajjāyām*, *asu kṣepaṇe*, *vasa nivāse*, *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*, *klidū ārdrībhāve*, *bandha bandhane*, *mana jñāne* the suffix *u*, which is *nit* — this sense follows from carrying over *nit* from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. sū. 1-9); so by this sūtra *u*, and the *nit* accent makes it initial-udātta: *manu*. *Hitaḥ*: root *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *kta* in the object sense by "niṣṭhā" (printed "3-2-102"); "dadhāter hiḥ" (Pā. 7-4-42): before a *t*-initial *kit* suffix, *hi* replaces *dhā*: *hita*. Then "manunā hitaḥ",

### Page 546 — Rik 4 grammar closes

a third-case tatpuruṣa: *manu* + *ṭā* + *hita* + *su*; for the instrumental *ṭā*, "supāṃ su-luk…" (printed "7-1-39") gives the substitute *su*: *manu* + *s* + *hita*; *ru* by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. 8-2-66): *manur hita*. By *sthānivadbhāva* the *ru* is still a *sup*, so "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71) would drop it; but in the Veda, by "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (printed "Paribhā. 35"), every rule is optional, so the *luk* does not come here. "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223) would give the final udātta; setting it aside, "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. 6-2-2) would give the first-member accent; setting that aside, "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) the accent of the *kṛt* second member; setting that aside too, "thātha-ghañ-ktāj-abitra-kāṇām" (printed "6-2-1-144" [sic]) the final udātta of a *kta*-ending after a *kāraka*; and setting that aside, "tṛtīyā karmaṇi" (Pā. 6-2-48) — before a *kta*-ending in the object sense, a third-case first member keeps its accent — gives the first-member accent. That is, in *manurhita* the *a* after the *m* alone is udātta; the other vowels are unaccented by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. 6-1-158); then the second vowel, the *u*, becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (Pā. 8-4-66), and the rest become *pracaya* by "svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām" (Pā. 1-2-39).

**॥४॥**

### Page 546 (lower) — Sūkta 13, Rik 5

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> स्तृ॒णी॒त ब॒र्हिरा॑नु॒षग्घृ॒तपृ॑ष्ठं मनीषिणः ।
> य॒त्रा॒मृत॑स्य॒ चक्ष॑णम् ॥५॥
>
> *stṛṇītá barhír ānuṣág ghṛtápṛṣṭhaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ |*
> *yatrāmṛ́tasya cákṣaṇam ||5||*

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. The bar under the first syllable of line 2 is not clearly printed; the conjunct of* मृ *in* यत्रामृतस्य *is printed in an unusual form, here read as* मृ*.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> स्तृणीत । बर्हिः । आनुषक् । घृतऽपृष्ठम् । मनीषिणः ॥
> यत्र । अमृतस्य । चक्षणम् ॥५॥
>
> *stṛṇīta | barhiḥ | ānuṣak | ghṛta-pṛṣṭham | manīṣiṇaḥ ||*
> *yatra | amṛtasya | cakṣaṇam ||5||*

> हे मनीषिणो बुद्धिमन्त ऋत्विजो बर्हिर्दर्भं स्तृणीत । वेदेरुपर्याच्छादयत । अत्रापि बर्हिर्नामको ऽग्निः सूच्यते । कीदृशं बर्हिरास्तरणीयम् । आनुषगनुक्रमेण सक्तं परस्परं संबद्धं घृतपृष्ठम् । घृतपूर्णानां स्रुचां बर्हिष्यासादितत्वाद्घृतं पृष्ठ उपरिभागे यस्य बर्हिषस्तद्घृतपृष्ठम् । यत्र यस्मिन्बर्हिष्यमृतस्यामृतसमानस्य घृतस्य चक्षणं दर्शनं भवति । यद्वा । मरणरहितस्य देवस्य बर्हिर्नामकस्याग्नेर्दर्शनं भवति । तद्बर्हिः स्तृणीतेति पूर्वत्रान्वयः ॥ स्तृणीत । स्तृञ् आच्छादने । लोण्मध्यमपुरुषस्य बहुवचनम् । लोटो लङ्वत् । पा. ३-४-८५ । तस्थस्थमिपाम् । पा. ३-४-१०१ । इति थस्य तादेशः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । ई हल्यघोः । पा. ६-४-११३ । इतीत्त्वम् । ऋवर्णाच्चेति वक्तव्यम् । का. ८-४-१-१ । इति णत्वम् । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः । पा. ७-३-८० । इति धातोर्ह्रस्वत्वम् । सतिशिष्टस्वरबलीयस्त्वमन्यत्र विकरणेभ्यः । अतस्तिङ एव प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तत्वम् । बर्हिः । बृंहेर्नलोपश्च । उ. २-११० । इतीसिप्रत्ययनलोपौ । प्रत्ययस्वरः । आनुषक् । आ समन्तादनुषजतीत्यानुषक् । षञ्ज सङ्गे । धात्वादेः षः सः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । अनिदिताम् । पा. ६-४-२४ । इति लोपः । आङन्वोरुपसर्गयोः प्राक्प्रयोगः । गतिसमासः । उपसर्गात्सुनोतीत्यादिना षत्वम् । घृतपृष्ठम् । घृ क्षरणदीप्त्योः । निष्ठेति क्तः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । घृतयुक्तं पृष्ठमस्येति बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । मनीषिणः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । अमृतस्य । न विद्यते मृतं मरणमस्मिन्नित्यमृतम् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं बाधित्वा नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः । पा. ६-२-११६ । इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । चक्षणम् । चक्षिङ् व्यक्तायां वाचि । वागभिव्यक्तिवाची धातुरिहाभिव्यक्तिमात्रं लक्षयति । ल्युट् च । पा. ३-३-११५ । इति भावे ल्युट् । योरनादेशः । तस्यार्धधातुकत्वाच्चक्षिङः ख्याञ् । पा. २-४-५४ । इति ख्याञादेशे प्राप्ते ऽसनयोश्च । पा. २-४-५४-१० । इति प्रतिषेधः ॥
>
> *he manīṣiṇo buddhimanta ṛtvijo barhirdarbhaṃ stṛṇīta | vederuparyācchādayata | atrāpi barhirnāmako 'gniḥ sūcyate | kīdṛśaṃ barhirāstaraṇīyam | ānuṣaganukrameṇa saktaṃ parasparaṃ saṃbaddhaṃ ghṛtapṛṣṭham | ghṛtapūrṇānāṃ srucāṃ barhiṣyāsāditatvādghṛtaṃ pṛṣṭha uparibhāge yasya barhiṣastadghṛtapṛṣṭham | yatra yasminbarhiṣyamṛtasyāmṛtasamānasya ghṛtasya cakṣaṇaṃ darśanaṃ bhavati | yadvā | maraṇarahitasya devasya barhirnāmakasyāgnerdarśanaṃ bhavati | tadbarhiḥ stṛṇīteti pūrvatrānvayaḥ || stṛṇīta | stṛñ ācchādane | loṇmadhyamapuruṣasya bahuvacanam | loṭo laṅvat | pā. 3-4-85 | tasthasthamipām | pā. 3-4-101 | iti thasya tādeśaḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | ī halyaghoḥ | pā. 6-4-113 | itīttvam | ṛvarṇācceti vaktavyam | kā. 8-4-1-1 | iti ṇatvam | pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ | pā. 7-3-80 | iti dhātorhrasvatvam | satiśiṣṭasvarabalīyastvamanyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ | atastiṅa eva pratyayasvareṇodāttatvam | barhiḥ | bṛṃhernalopaśca | u. 2-110 | itīsipratyayanalopau | pratyayasvaraḥ | ānuṣak | ā samantādanuṣajatītyānuṣak | ṣañja saṅge | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | kvipceti kvip | aniditām | pā. 6-4-24 | iti lopaḥ | āṅanvorupasargayoḥ prākprayogaḥ | gatisamāsaḥ | upasargātsunotītyādinā ṣatvam | ghṛtapṛṣṭham | ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ | niṣṭheti ktaḥ | pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | ghṛtayuktaṃ pṛṣṭhamasyeti bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | manīṣiṇaḥ | āmantritanighātaḥ | amṛtasya | na vidyate mṛtaṃ maraṇamasminnityamṛtam | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ bādhitvā nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatve prāpte naño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ | pā. 6-2-116 | ityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | cakṣaṇam | cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci | vāgabhivyaktivācī dhāturihābhivyaktimātraṃ lakṣayati | lyuṭ ca | pā. 3-3-115 | iti bhāve lyuṭ | yoranādeśaḥ | tasyārdhadhātukatvāccakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ | pā. 2-4-54 | iti khyāñādeśe prāpte 'sanayośca | pā. 2-4-54-10 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O *manīṣiṇaḥ*, wise priests! *Barhiḥ stṛṇīta* — spread the *darbha*; cover [the top of] the altar with it. Here too the fire named *Barhis* is indicated. What kind of *barhis*, the one to be strewn? *Ānuṣak* — attached in order, connected with one another; *ghṛtapṛṣṭham* — since the ladles full of ghee are set down on the *barhis*, the *barhis* whose *pṛṣṭha*, upper part, has ghee. *Yatra* — on which *barhis* — there is *cakṣaṇam*, the sight, *amṛtasya*, of the ghee, which is like ambrosia; or, the sight of the deathless god, the Agni named *Barhis*: spread that *barhis* — this is the connection with what precedes." (Grammatical tail: *stṛṇīta* — *stṛñ ācchādane*, *loṭ* second plural, treated like *laṅ* by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. 3-4-85), *ta* for *tha* by "tas-thas-tha-mipām…" (Pā. 3-4-101), *śnā* of the *kryādi*, *ī* by "ī haly aghoḥ" (Pā. 6-4-113), *ṇ* by the vārttika "ṛvarṇāc ca" (Kā. 8-4-1-1), the root shortened by "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-3-80); by "sati śiṣṭa-svara-balīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ" the *tiṅ* alone is udātta by the suffix accent; *barhiḥ* — *isi* with loss of *n* by "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. 2-110), suffix accent; *ānuṣak* — "it clings all around": *ṣañja saṅge*, *s* for *ṣ*, *kvip*, the *n* dropped (Pā. 6-4-24), the upasargas *āṅ* and *anu* placed before, a *gati* compound, *ṣ* by "upasargāt sunoti…"; *ghṛtapṛṣṭham* — *ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ* with *kta*, suffix accent; "whose back is joined with ghee", a bahuvrīhi with the first member's accent; *manīṣiṇaḥ* — unaccented as a vocative; *amṛtasya* — "in which there is no death"; instead of the first-member accent, and of the final udātta of "nañ-subhyām", "nañ jara-mara-mitra-mṛtāḥ" (Pā. 6-2-116) makes the second member initial-udātta; *cakṣaṇam* — *cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*, a root meaning manifestation of speech, here indicating mere manifestation; *lyuṭ* in the sense of the state by "lyuṭ ca" (Pā. 3-3-115), *ana* for *yu*; the *khyāñ* of "cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ" (Pā. 2-4-54) that would come before an *ārdhadhātuka* is barred by "asanayoś ca" (Pā. 2-4-54-10).)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

*(O)* **मनीषिणः (manīṣiṇaḥ)** — wise priests | **आनुषक् (ānuṣak)** — in sequence, one touching the next (so that they lie close together) | **घृतपृष्ठम् (ghṛtapṛṣṭham)** — sprinkled with ghee (or water) on the upper part | **यत्र (yatra)** — on which *barhis* | **अमृतस्य (amṛtasya)** — [of] the ghee equal to ambrosia, or of the deathless god [Agni] named *Barhis* | **चक्षणम् (cakṣaṇam)** — sight | **बर्हिः (barhiḥ)** — the *kuśa* grass with its ends cut | **स्तृणीत (stṛṇīta)** — spread (over the altar).

### Page 548 — Rik 5: overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O wise priests! Spread the *darbha* on the altar as a seat, for the fire called *Barhis* to come and sit. When spreading it, lay it close together so that it is soft. It must be moistened with ghee or water and be soft. The ghee on it, or the fire called *Barhis*, must be visible to all. Spread the *darbha* called *kuśa* well on the altar in this way.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Strew, learned priests, in due order, the sacrificial grass the back (or surface) of which is sprinkled with clarified butter (or water), that we may see the immortal ones thereon.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The sense of this rik is somewhat involved. Yāska explains the word *barhiḥ* as *barhiḥ paribarhaṇāt*:

> बर्हिः प्रसिद्धमेव कुशमयं यज्ञाङ्गम् । परिबर्हणात्परिच्छेदनाल्लूनं हि तद्भवति ।
>
> *barhiḥ prasiddhameva kuśamayaṃ yajñāṅgam | paribarhaṇātparicchedanāllūnaṃ hi tadbhavati |*

That is, *barhis* is the *kuśa* grass with its tip cut off, used in the sacrifice; *paribarhaṇa* means cutting; since its tip has been cut, such *darbha* is called *barhiḥ*. Or *barhiḥ* is from

> प्रवृज्यते = प्रच्छिद्यते लूयते अथवा प्रवृज्यते = प्रस्तीर्यते ॥
>
> *pravṛjyate = pracchidyate lūyate athavā pravṛjyate = prastīryate ||*

— because it is cut, or because it is spread, it may be said to be called *barhiḥ*. In support of this sense Yāska cites the rik

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-4.)*

> प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वस्तोरस्या वृज्यते अग्रे अह्नाम् ।
> व्यु प्रथते वितरं वरीयो देवेभ्यो अदितये स्योनम् ॥
>
> *prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vastorasyā vṛjyate agre ahnām |*
> *vyu prathate vitaraṃ varīyo devebhyo aditaye syonam ||*

*("The barhis is cut, eastward-pointing, at the dawn of days, by the direction of this earth, for its covering; it spreads wide, wider and broader, pleasant for the gods and for Aditi" — mine and tentative.)*

and by way of explanation:

> प्राचीनं बर्हिः प्रदिशा पृथिव्या वसनायास्याः प्रवृज्यते अग्रे अह्नां बर्हिः पूर्वाह्णे तद्विप्रथते वितरं विकीर्णतरमिति वा विस्तीर्णतरमिति वा वरीयो वरतरमुरुतरं वा देवेभ्यश्चादितये च स्योनम् । स्योनमिति सुखनाम स्यतेरवस्यन्त्येतत्सेवितव्यं भवतीति वा ॥
>
> *prācīnaṃ barhiḥ pradiśā pṛthivyā vasanāyāsyāḥ pravṛjyate agre ahnāṃ barhiḥ pūrvāhṇe tadviprathate vitaraṃ vikīrṇataramiti vā vistīrṇataramiti vā varīyo varataramurutaraṃ vā devebhyaścāditaye ca syonam | syonamiti sukhanāma syateravasyantyetatsevitavyaṃ bhavatīti vā ||*

### Page 549 — Rik 5: Special Topics (continued)

he says. From this explanation the word *barhiḥ* means cut *darbha* spread well and widely. Such cut *darbha* is spread and made ready in the sacrifice for two reasons: one, to set the *ājya*-vessel (the ghee vessel) and the *sruk* in front of Agni; two, as a seat for the invoked gods to come and sit on. Performing rites seated on a *darbha* seat is counted best. So the practice is to spread the cut *darbha* called *barhiḥ* on one part of the sacrificial altar and make a seat ready for the gods to sit on. The five spoken of so far — *samiddha*, *tanūnapāt*, *narāśaṃsa*, *iḷa*, *barhiḥ* — are all thought of as different forms of Agni, and with these names they offer *homa* in the animal sacrifice.

**"Ānuṣak"** — *anukrameṇa saktaṃ parasparaṃ saṃbaddham*: so that the *darbha* blades touch one another, connected with each other — that is, close together, not sparse. If a few blades are laid sparsely, it will not be soft; the idea is that the seat is soft when the *darbha* is laid much and close together.

**"Ghṛtapṛṣṭham"** — *ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ*; *ghṛtayuktaṃ pṛṣṭham asya*: smeared with ghee, or moistened, or sprinkled with water. The word *ghṛta* also means water (Ni. 1-12). The practice is to sprinkle water so that the dry *darbha* becomes soft.

**"Amṛtasya"** — *na vidyate mṛtaṃ maraṇam asminn ity amṛtam*: free from death, that is, the god Agni; or, as the Bhāṣyakāra says, ghee, which is like ambrosia.

**"Cakṣaṇam"** — *cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*: becoming manifest, appearing. What the right sense of the words *amṛtasya cakṣaṇam* is, is not clear; the seer's intention too cannot be properly known. Although we have given the meaning current in tradition for these words, the main intention in the seer's mind is not clear.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 549–551, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**स्तृणीत (*stṛṇīta*)** — *stṝñ ācchādane*, a root of the *kryādi* class; after it the *loṭ* *parasmaipada* second plural *tha*: *stṝ* + *tha*; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. 3-4-85) the operations of *laṅ* apply to *loṭ*, so "tas-thas-tha-mipāṃ tān-tan-tāmaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-101) — for *tas*, *thas*, *tha*, *mip* in place of a *ṅit* *lakāra*, the four substitutes *tām*, *tam*, *ta*, *am* in order — gives *ta* for *tha*. "kryādibhyaḥ śnā" (Pā. 3-1-81): before a *sārvadhātuka* in the agent sense,

### Page 550 — Rik 5 grammar (continued)

after the roots of the *kryādi* group, the vikaraṇa *śnā* in its own sense: *stṝ* + *nā* + *ta*. "ī haly aghoḥ" (printed "6-4-11" [sic]; the sūtra is 6-4-113): before a consonant-initial *kit* or *ṅit* *sārvadhātuka*, the *ā* of *śnā* and of a reduplicated root not named *ghu* becomes *ī*: *stṝ* + *nī* + *ta*; "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. 7-3-80) shortens the root's *ṝ*; "ṛvarṇāc ceti vaktavyam" (printed "8-4-1-1") gives *ṇ* for the *n*: *stṛṇīta*. Standing at the beginning of the pāda, it is not made wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ". Although the accent of the suffix *śnā* is "*sati śiṣṭa*", that is, it comes last, being a vikaraṇa it does not prevail, according to the statement "sati-śiṣṭa-svara-balīyastvam anyatra vikaraṇebhyaḥ"; so the *tiṅ* suffix *ta* alone is udātta by the suffix accent. **बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)** — *bṛhi vṛddhau*, a root that is *idit*; so *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (printed "7-1-58"); after it "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "2--266" [sic]; the bhāṣya gives 2-110): after *bṛhi* both the suffix *isi* and the loss of *n*: *bṛh* + *is*; *laghūpadha-guṇa* with *r*: *barhis*; the suffix accent; accusative singular *barhiḥ*. **आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*)** — "ā samantāt anuṣajati iti ānuṣak": root *ṣañja saṅge*; *s* for *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 6-1-64); *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76), which is lost entirely; "anidatāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti" (Pā. 6-4-24) drops the *n*; the upasargas *āṅ* and *anu* are used before it in order: *ā* + *anu* + *saj*, a *gati* compound by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. 2-2-18); *savarṇa*-lengthening of *ā anu*; *ṣ* for the *s* by "upasargāt sunoti-suvati…" (Pā. 8-3-65); then the accusative singular *am*, dropped by "svamor napuṃsakāt" (Pā. 7-1-23) after a neuter stem; *k*-series by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30): *g* for the voiced palatal *j*; *jaś* by "jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte" (Pā. 8-2-39); *car* by "vāvasāne" (Pā. 8-4-56): *k* for *g*: *ānuṣak*. **घृतपृष्ठम् (*ghṛtapṛṣṭham*)** — root *ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ*; *kta* by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. 3-2-102); *ghṛta* is final-udātta by the suffix accent; "ghṛtayuktaṃ pṛṣṭham asya", a bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. 6-2-1). **मनीषिणः (*manīṣiṇaḥ*)** — a vocative, hence unaccented by the eighth-chapter rule.

### Page 551 — Rik 5 grammar closes

**अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)** — analysed "na vidyate mṛtaṃ maraṇam asmin". *Amṛta* being a bahuvrīhi, the first-member accent would come; setting it aside, "nañ-subhyām" (Pā. 6-2-172) — in a bahuvrīhi the second member after *nañ* or *su* is final-udātta — would give the final udātta; setting that aside too, "nañ jara-mara-mitra-mṛtāḥ" (Pā. 6-2-116) — in a bahuvrīhi, after *nañ*, the words *jara*, *mara*, *mitra*, *mṛta* are initial-udātta — makes the second member initial-udātta. **चक्षणम् (*cakṣaṇam*)** — *cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*, a root which can denote the manifestation of speech; here by implication it conveys only manifestation. After it, by "lyuṭ ca" (Pā. 3-3-115) — after a root, in the neuter, in the sense of the state, the suffixes *lyuṭ* and *kta* — *lyuṭ* comes; the *l* and *ṭ* are *it* and dropped; *ana* for *yu* by "yuvor anākau" (printed "2-1-1" [sic]; the sūtra is 7-1-1): *cakṣ* + *ana*; *ana* is an *ārdhadhātuka*, so by "cakṣiṅaḥ khyāñ" (Pā. 2-4-54) — before an *ārdhadhātuka* *cakṣiṅ* is replaced by *khyāñ* — the substitute *khyāñ* would arise; but "asanayoś ca" (printed "Pā. sū. 2-4-54 vā. 10") — before the suffixes *as* and *ana*, *cakṣiṅ* does not take *khyāñ* — bars it, so *khyāñ* does not come. Here the Kaiyaṭa, by "anudāttetaś ca halādeḥ" (Pā. 3-2-149), gives the suffix *yuc* and derives *vicakṣaṇaḥ*; on that view *vicakṣaṇa* is final-udātta. On the *lyuṭ* view "liti" makes [the *ca*] udātta; the other two *a*'s are unaccented by the rule for the remainder; then by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" the second *a* is svarita, and by "svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām" the third *a* is *pracaya*. It is to get this accent that *lyuṭ* is described here.

**॥५॥**
