### Page 552 — Rik 6: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> द्वारो यज्ञशालाद्वाराणि वि श्रयन्ताम् । कपाटोद्घाटनेन विव्रियन्ताम् । कीदृश्यः । ऋतावृध ऋतस्य सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य वा वर्धयित्र्यो देवीर्द्योतमाना असश्चतो ऽसक्ताः । उद्घाटनेन प्रवेष्टृपुरुषसङ्गरहिताः । यद्वा । असश्चतः प्रवेष्टृपुरुषरहितान्यज्ञगृहांस्तत्पुरुषप्रवेशाय द्वाराभिमानिन्य एतत्संज्ञिका अग्निविशेषमूर्तयो वि श्रयन्ताम् । विशेषेण सेवन्ताम् । द्वारसेवया तत्र पुरुषप्रवेशेन वा किं प्रयोजनमिति तदुच्यते । अद्यास्मिन्दिने नूनमवश्यं यष्टवे यष्टुम् । चकाराद्दिनान्तरेष्वपीति द्रष्टव्यम् ॥ ऋतावृधः । ऋतं वर्धयन्तीत्यर्थे वृधेरन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्क्विप्चेति क्विप् । उपपदसमासः । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घत्वम् । वृधिर्धातुस्वरेणोदात्तः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । देवीः । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वम् । देवशब्दात्पचाद्यजन्तात्पुंयोगादाख्यायाम् । पा. ४-१-४८ । इति ङीष् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । विभक्त्या सहैकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । असश्चतः । ग्लुञ्चु षस्ज गतौ । जकारस्य व्यत्ययेन चकारः । लटः शत्रादेशः । द्वाराभावे न विद्यन्ते सश्चन्तो गच्छन्तो येषु प्राग्वंशादिषु तानसश्चतः । अद्य । सद्यःपरुदित्यादिना द्यप्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । तद्धितश्चासर्वविभक्तिरित्यव्ययसंज्ञकत्वात्परस्या विभक्तेर्लुक् । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । संहितायामन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घत्वम् । नूनम् । एवमादीनामन्त इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वम् । यष्टवे । यजेस्तुमर्थे सेसेनित्यादिना । पा. ३-४-९ । तवेन्प्रत्ययः । व्रश्चादिना षत्वम् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥
>
> *dvāro yajñaśālādvārāṇi vi śrayantām | kapāṭodghāṭanena vivriyantām | kīdṛśyaḥ | ṛtāvṛdha ṛtasya satyasya yajñasya vā vardhayitryo devīrdyotamānā asaścato 'saktāḥ | udghāṭanena praveṣṭṛpuruṣasaṅgarahitāḥ | yadvā | asaścataḥ praveṣṭṛpuruṣarahitānyajñagṛhāṃstatpuruṣapraveśāya dvārābhimāninya etatsaṃjñikā agniviśeṣamūrtayo vi śrayantām | viśeṣeṇa sevantām | dvārasevayā tatra puruṣapraveśena vā kiṃ prayojanamiti taducyate | adyāsmindine nūnamavaśyaṃ yaṣṭave yaṣṭum | cakārāddināntareṣvapīti draṣṭavyam || ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | ṛtaṃ vardhayantītyarthe vṛdherantarbhāvitaṇyarthātkvipceti kvip | upapadasamāsaḥ | anyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti pūrvapadasya dīrghatvam | vṛdhirdhātusvareṇodāttaḥ | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena sa eva śiṣyate | devīḥ | vā chandasīti pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvam | devaśabdātpacādyajantātpuṃyogādākhyāyām | pā. 4-1-48 | iti ṅīṣ | pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | vibhaktyā sahaikādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttaḥ | asaścataḥ | gluñcu ṣasja gatau | jakārasya vyatyayena cakāraḥ | laṭaḥ śatrādeśaḥ | dvārābhāve na vidyante saścanto gacchanto yeṣu prāgvaṃśādiṣu tānasaścataḥ | adya | sadyaḥparudityādinā dyapratyayānto nipātitaḥ | taddhitaścāsarvavibhaktirityavyayasaṃjñakatvātparasyā vibhakterluk | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāmanyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti dīrghatvam | nūnam | evamādīnāmanta ityantodāttatvam | yaṣṭave | yajestumarthe sesenityādinā | pā. 3-4-9 | tavenpratyayaḥ | vraścādinā ṣatvam | nittvādādyudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "May the *dvāraḥ* — the doors of the sacrificial hall — *vi śrayantām*: be opened by the opening of their leaves. What kind? *Ṛtāvṛdhaḥ* — increasers of *ṛta*, truth or the sacrifice; *devīḥ* — shining; *asaścataḥ* — unattached: by being opened, free of contact with the persons who enter. Or else: may the special forms of Agni, presiding over the doors and called by this name, *vi śrayantām* — specially serve — the sacrificial houses hitherto without persons entering, for those persons to enter. What is the purpose of serving the doors or of persons entering there? That is told: *adya*, on this day, *nūnam*, without fail, *yaṣṭave*, to sacrifice; from the word *ca*, on other days too, it is to be understood." (Grammatical tail: *ṛtāvṛdhaḥ* — "they increase *ṛta*": *kvip* after *vṛdh* with the causative sense included, by "kvip ca"; an *upapada* compound; the first member lengthened by "anyeṣām api dṛśyate"; *vṛdh* udātta by the root accent, which alone remains in the compound as the *kṛt* second member's accent; *devīḥ* — *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening by "vā chandasi"; *ṅīṣ* after *deva*, an *ac*-ending of the *pacādi*, by "puṃyogād ākhyāyām" (Pā. 4-1-48); udātta by the suffix accent, and the single substitute with the case ending udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ"; *asaścataḥ* — from *gluñcu ṣasja gatau*, *c* for the *j* by exception, *śatṛ* for *laṭ*: "those in which there are no goers, as the *prāgvaṃśa* and other [halls] in the absence of doors"; *adya* — formed irregularly with *dya* by "sadyaḥ-parut…", an indeclinable by "taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ", so the ending after it is dropped, final-udātta, lengthened in the Saṃhitā; *nūnam* — final-udātta by "evamādīnām antaḥ"; *yaṣṭave* — *taven* in the sense of *tumun* by "se-sen…" (Pā. 3-4-9), *ṣ* by "vraśca…", initial-udātta as *nit*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अद्य (adya)** — today (now itself) | **नूनम् (nūnam)** — certainly | **यष्टवे च (yaṣṭave ca)** — in order that [we] may perform the sacrifice | **ऋतावृधः (ṛtāvṛdhaḥ)** — helping the sacrifice to go forward | **देवीः (devīḥ)** — shining (making light) | **असश्चतः (asaścataḥ)** — free of contact, that is, entered by no one until now | **द्वारः (dvāraḥ)** — the doors (gates) of the sacrificial hall | **वि श्रयन्ताम् (vi śrayantām)** — be opened.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The doors of the sacrificial hall make it well lit and help the sacrifice go forward. Until now (that is, today) no one has entered this sacrificial hall. May such doors of the sacrificial hall be opened now, without delay, for the sacrifice we perform.

### Page 553 — Rik 6: English, Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Let the divine doors, the promoters of the sacred rite, hitherto unentered be set open; for certainly to-day the sacrifice is to be performed.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

When entering the sacrificial hall the sacrificer and the priests pray to the doors of the hall. Although all the riks of this sūkta are addressed to Agni, in this rik *devīr dvāraḥ* — "the divine doors" — the door-deities (that is, the deities who preside over the doors) are prayed to. Yāska's explanation:

> द्वारः । द्वारो जवतेर्वा द्रवतेर्वा वारयतेर्वा ॥
> अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥
>
> *dvāraḥ | dvāro javatervā dravatervā vārayatervā ||*
> *agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ||*


*Dvāra* is that by which one enters, goes inside, or that which stops one going inside; so it is called *dvāra*. Śākapūṇi's view is that *dvāra* is Agni: since Agni is the form in which the *homa* is made, the doors of the *homa*-chamber are also called "special forms of Agni." *The doors of the chamber in which the oblation is offered, said to be personifications of Agni* [the source's English].

**"Viśrayantām"** — *kapāṭodghāṭanena vivriyantām | vivṛtā bhavantu*: let the doors be opened well.

**"Ṛtāvṛdhaḥ"** — *ṛtaṃ (yajñaṃ) vardhayantīti ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*: helpful for the sacrifice to go forward — that is, by [letting one] enter the sacrificial hall, they help to carry out the *homa* and the other acts to be done in the sacrifice.

**"Devīḥ"** — *dyotamānāḥ*: "shining, making light well": when the door is opened, light naturally fills the room. Whether the word *devīḥ* is understood as an adjective of *dvāraḥ*, or both words are taken in the sense "the deities presiding over the doors," either use is possible; for in the Anukramaṇikā the deity of this rik is named *devīr dvāraḥ*.

### Page 554 — Rik 6: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

**"Asaścataḥ"** — *dvārābhāve saścanto gacchanto yeṣu | na saścataḥ asaścataḥ*: free of entry, entered by no one, or which stop those who would enter — such senses may be given.

**"Adyā"** — "now, today; this time at which we are performing this sacrifice." The final vowel is lengthened in the Saṃhitā for the convenience of the meter.

**"Nūnam"** — "necessarily, certainly, without fail" [the source's English: *certainly, without fail*].

**"Ca"** — this word has no special sense here; looking at it one way, there is no need of it in this rik. The Bhāṣyakāra gives the sense *dinānteṣv api* — "on other days too."

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 554–555, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)** — in the sense "ṛtaṃ vardhayanti", after the root *vṛdh* with the causative sense included, *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. 3-2-76); "upapadam atiṅ" (Pā. 2-2-19): an *upapada* that is a *subanta* is always compounded with the connected word — so a compound; "anyeṣām api dṛśyate" (Pā. 6-3-137) lengthens the first member. *Vṛdh* is udātta by the root accent; once compounded, "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) gives the accent of the *kṛt* second member, and that same accent stands. Nominative plural. **देवीः (*devīḥ*)** — the word *deva* is formed from *divu krīḍādau* with the suffix *ac* by "nandi-grahi-pacādibhyo lyu-ṇiny-acaḥ" (printed "vā. sū." [sic] 3-1-134); so it is final-udātta by "citaḥ". After it "puṃyogād ākhyāyām" (Pā. 4-1-48): a word well known in the masculine, when used by implication in the feminine through connection with a man, takes *ṅīṣ* (the connection with a man being that of marriage, or of being begotten) — so when *devasya strī* is meant, *ṅīṣ* comes: *deva* + *ī*; "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148) drops the *a*; the *ī* is udātta by the suffix accent. Then the nominative plural *jas*; the *pūrvasavarṇa*-lengthening of "prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-102) is barred by "dīrghāj jasi ca" (Pā. 6-1-105); yet by "vā chandasi" (printed "3-4-88" [sic]; the sūtra is 6-1-106) the *pūrvasavarṇa*-lengthening comes as a single substitute, and that single substitute is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5).

### Page 555 — Rik 6 grammar closes

**असश्चतः (*asaścataḥ*)** — root *gluñcu ṣasja gatau*; *c* for the *j* by exception; *s* for the *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 6-1-64); then *laṭ*, replaced by *śatṛ* by "laṭaḥ śatṛ…" (Pā. 3-2-124); the vikaraṇa *śap*: *sasc* + *a* + *at*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe": *sascat*. "dvārābhāvena na vidyante saścantaḥ gacchantaḥ yeṣu prāgvaṃśādiṣu, tān" — so the analysis; with the accusative plural *śas*: *asaścataḥ*. **अद्य (*adya*)** — formed irregularly, as ending in the suffix *dya*, by the sūtra "sadyaḥ parut…" (Pā. 5-3-22). Since it has the name *avyaya* by "taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 1-1-38), the locative singular *ṅi* after it is dropped by "avyayād āp-supaḥ" (Pā. 2-4-82). It is final-udātta by the suffix accent; in the Saṃhitā it is lengthened by "anyeṣām api dṛśyate" (Pā. 6-3-137). **नूनम् (*nūnam*)** — final-udātta by "evādīnām antaḥ" (printed "pā. sū. 82"). **यष्टवे (*yaṣṭave*)** — root *yaja devapūjādau*; after it "tumarthe se-sen-ase-asen-kse-kasen-adhyai-adhyain-kadhyai-kadhyain-śadhyai-śadhyain-tavai-taveṅ-tavenaḥ" (Pā. 3-4-9) gives *taven* in the sense of *tumun*: *yaj* + *tave*; "vraśca-bhrasja-sṛja-mṛja-yaja-rāja-bhrāja-cchaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-36) gives *ṣ* for the *j*; *ṣṭutva* by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) gives *ṭ* for the *t*: *yaṣṭave*; the suffix being *nit*, it is initial-udātta by the *nit* accent.

**॥६॥**

### Page 555 (lower) — Sūkta 13, Rik 7

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented. Line 1: the bars are crowded under नक्तो and सास्मि — [accent ?].)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> न॒क्तो॒षासा॑ सु॒पेश॑सा॒स्मिन्य॒ज्ञ उप॑ ह्वये । [accent ?]
> इ॒दं नो॑ ब॒र्हिरा॒स॑दे ॥७॥
>
> *naktoṣā́sā supéśasāsmín yajñá úpa hvaye |* [accent ?]
> *idáṃ no barhír āsade ||7||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> नक्तोषसा । सुऽपेशसा । अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । उप । ह्वये ॥
> इदम् । नः । बर्हिः । आऽसदे ॥७॥
>
> *naktoṣasā | su-peśasā | asmin | yajñe | upa | hvaye ||*
> *idam | naḥ | barhiḥ | ā-sade ||7||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(runs onto p. 556)*

> नक्तशब्द उषःशब्दश्च लोके कालविशेषवाचिनौ । इह तु तत्कालाभिमानि वह्निमूर्तिद्वये प्रयुज्येते । नक्तोषासा नक्तोषो नामिके वह्निमूर्ती अस्मिन्प्रवर्तमाने यज्ञकर्मण्युप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । किमर्थम् । नो ऽस्मदीयमिदं वेद्यामास्तीर्णं बर्हिर्दर्भमासदे । आसत्तुम् । प्राप्तुम् । कीदृशौ । सुपेशसा शोभनरूपयुक्ते ॥ नक्तं चोषाश्च नक्तोषसा । द्वितीयाद्विवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । मलोप उपधादीर्घश्छान्दसौ । देवताद्वन्द्वे च । पा. ६-२-१४१ । इति पूर्वोत्तरपदयोर्युगपत्प्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सुपेशसा । शोभनं पेशो रूपं ययोस्ते । पूर्ववदाकारः । पेशःशब्दो नब्विषयत्वादाद्युदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वस्यापवादत्वेनाद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसि । पा. ६-२-११९ । इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अस्मिन् । ऊडिदमित्यादिना विभक्तिरुदात्ता । आसदे । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । धात्वादेः षः सः । आङ्पूर्वादस्मात्संपदादिभ्यो भावे क्विप् । पा. ३-३-१०८-९ । प्रादिसमासः । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् ॥
>
> *naktaśabda uṣaḥśabdaśca loke kālaviśeṣavācinau | iha tu tatkālābhimāni vahnimūrtidvaye prayujyete | naktoṣāsā naktoṣo nāmike vahnimūrtī asminpravartamāne yajñakarmaṇyupa hvaye | āhvayāmi | kimartham | no 'smadīyamidaṃ vedyāmāstīrṇaṃ barhirdarbhamāsade | āsattum | prāptum | kīdṛśau | supeśasā śobhanarūpayukte || naktaṃ coṣāśca naktoṣasā | dvitīyādvivacanasya supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | malopa upadhādīrghaśchāndasau | devatādvandve ca | pā. 6-2-141 | iti pūrvottarapadayoryugapatprakṛtisvaratvam | supeśasā | śobhanaṃ peśo rūpaṃ yayoste | pūrvavadākāraḥ | peśaḥśabdo nabviṣayatvādādyudāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvasyāpavādatvenādyudāttaṃ dvyacchandasi | pā. 6-2-119 | ityuttarapadādyudāttatvam | asmin | ūḍidamityādinā vibhaktirudāttā | āsade | ṣadlṛ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu | dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ | āṅpūrvādasmātsaṃpadādibhyo bhāve kvip | pā. 3-3-108-9 | prādisamāsaḥ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ||*

**Translation:** "The words *nakta* and *uṣas* in ordinary use denote particular times; here, however, they are used of the pair of fire-forms presiding over those times. *Naktoṣāsā* — the two fire-forms named Night and Dawn — I *upa hvaye*, call, in this sacrificial rite now in progress. For what? *Naḥ idaṃ barhiḥ āsade* — to sit on, to reach, this our *darbha* spread on the altar. What are they like? *Supeśasā* — endowed with beautiful form." (Grammatical tail: *naktoṣasā* — "night and dawn": *ā* for the accusative dual ending by "supāṃ suluk…"; the loss of *m* and the lengthening of the penultimate are Vedic; by "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. 6-2-141) both members keep their own accents at once; *supeśasā* — "whose *peśas*, form, is beautiful", *ā* as before; *peśas* initial-udātta as a *nab-viṣaya* word; in the bahuvrīhi, setting aside the second member's final udātta of "nañ-subhyām", "ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi" (Pā. 6-2-119) makes the second member initial-udātta; *asmin* — the case ending udātta by "ūḍ-idam…"; *āsade* — *ṣadḷ*, *s* for *ṣ*, *kvip* in the sense of the state after *sad* with *āṅ*, by "sampadādibhyaḥ" (Pā. 3-3-108-9), a *prādi* compound, the *kṛt* second-member accent.)

### Page 556 — Rik 7: word-meanings, overall sense, English

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**नः (naḥ)** — our | **इदम् (idam)** — this, spread on the altar | **बर्हिः (barhiḥ)** — the *darbha* grass prepared as a seat | **आसदे (āsade)** — in order that they may come and sit [on] it (that is, to sit on the *darbha* that we have spread) | **सुपेशसा (supeśasā)** — endowed with beautiful forms | **नक्तोषासा (naktoṣāsā)** — the deities of night and dawn (or the presiding deities of those times) | **अस्मिन् यज्ञे (asmin yajñe)** — in this sacrifice now proceeding | **उप ह्वये (upa hvaye)** — I invoke.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

In the sacrifice we are performing we have spread *darbha* on the altar and made a seat ready. To come and sit on this seat, I now call in the sacrifice in progress the deities who shine with excellent forms (the deities called *Naktoṣāsā*, presiding over night and the morning time).

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> I invoke here at this sacrifice Night and Dawn, the beautifully adorned goddesses, that they may sit down on this our sacrificial grass.

### Page 557 — Rik 7: Special Topics

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

In this rik the presiding deities of night and of the morning time, called *Naktoṣāsā*, are invoked. Yāska's explanation of the word *naktoṣasā* is as follows:

> उषासानक्ता । उषासानक्तोषाश्च नक्ता चोषा व्याख्याता । नक्तेति रात्रिनामानक्ति भूतान्यवश्यायेनापि वा नक्ताव्यक्तवर्णा ॥
>
> *uṣāsānaktā | uṣāsānaktoṣāśca naktā coṣā vyākhyātā | nakteti rātrināmānakti bhūtānyavaśyāyenāpi vā naktāvyaktavarṇā ||*

Although read in two ways, *naktoṣāsā* and *uṣāsānaktā*, the sense is one. We have given the explanation of the word *uṣas* earlier. *Naktā* is a name of night; for *naktā* means *avyaktavarṇā*, "of indistinct colour": because of the darkness things are indistinct, not clearly seen; so the night, joined with darkness, is called *naktā*, and in this night-time living beings are unable to do their work.

> अनक्ति क्लेदयति भूतानि अवश्यायेन इति । अपि वा नक्ता अव्यक्तवर्णा । यथा अहः सर्वमभिव्यक्तरूपं भवति न तथा रात्रिः ॥
>
> *anakti kledayati bhūtāni avaśyāyena iti | api vā naktā avyaktavarṇā | yathā ahaḥ sarvamabhivyaktarūpaṃ bhavati na tathā rātriḥ ||*

The darkness gives living beings trouble, leaving no room for their activities to go on properly; so the night joined with such darkness is called *naktā*; or, since nothing is clearly seen and all is indistinct, it is called *naktā*. By day the forms of all things are seen clearly; at night they are not seen so. Therefore he explained that the night-time is called *naktā* (Ni. 8-11).

He says that he has already explained the word *uṣas*; that explanation runs: "*vibhāvarī*, *sūnarī* and the other sixteen words are names of dawn" (printed "2-19"), and

> उषाः कस्मादुच्छतीति सत्या रात्रेरपरः कालः ॥
>
> *uṣāḥ kasmāducchatīti satyā rātreraparaḥ kālaḥ ||*

Because it removes the darkness of night it is called *uṣas*; that is, the latter time of the night, its last part. In support of this sense he gives an example:

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-1.)*

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागाच्चित्रः प्रकेतो अजनिष्ट विभ्वा ।
> यथा प्रसूता सवितुः सवायँ एवा रात्र्युषसे योनिमारैक् ॥
>
> *idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgāccitraḥ praketo ajaniṣṭa vibhvā |*
> *yathā prasūtā savituḥ savāya~ evā rātryuṣase yonimāraik ||*

*("This best light of lights has come; the bright sign is born, far-reaching. As [Night] was set in motion for Savitṛ's impulse, so has Night given up her womb to Dawn" — mine and tentative.)*

The Nirukta of this rik:

### Page 558 — Rik 7: Special Topics (continued)

> इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरागमत् । चित्रं प्रकेतनं प्रज्ञाततममजनिष्ट विभूततमं यथा प्रसूता सवितुः प्रसवाय रात्रिरादित्यस्य । एवं रात्र्युषसे योनिमरिचत्स्थानम् । स्त्रीयोनिरभियुत एनां गर्भः ॥
>
> *idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāgamat | citraṃ praketanaṃ prajñātatamamajaniṣṭa vibhūtatamaṃ yathā prasūtā savituḥ prasavāya rātrirādityasya | evaṃ rātryuṣase yonimaricatsthānam | strīyonirabhiyuta enāṃ garbhaḥ ||*

The best and exceedingly bright light of the sun is rising. The dawn-time, which comes before the sun's light, appears ahead of the light like its banner (*niketana*, its flag). For, just as the sun's light, shining all day, becomes at the time of setting the *yoni* — the cause — for night, so night at the end of its own time becomes the *yoni*, the cause, for the dawn-time. *Yoni* means a place of birth. The chief idea is that at the end of the day night, and at the end of night dawn, keep coming round in a cycle of change. So *uṣas* means the brightness, the light, that spreads through all the quarters and appears before sunrise, after the night has passed.

The Bhāṣyakāra's (Sāyaṇa's) explanation: "*naktaśabda uṣaḥśabdaś ca loke kālaviśeṣavācinau | iha tu tatkālābhimānivahnimūrtidvaye prayujyete | naktoṣāsā naktoṣonāmike vahnimūrtī*" — that is, the two words *nakta* (night) and *uṣas* (the morning time) have, in ordinary usage, the sense of denoting particular times, night and the morning time; here, that is, in this rik or in the Ṛgveda, these words convey the sense of the presiding deities of night and of the morning time. Hence the words *naktoṣāsā* or *uṣāsānaktā* are used in the sense of two forms (*mūrti*) of Agni that are the presiding deities of night and of the morning time. The word *supeśasā* (having a fine form or shape) used in this rik supports this sense: since night and the morning time are divisions of time, they have neither form nor shape; on the view that they are the presiding deities of those times, a form can be ascribed to those deities. Since the rik makes such a statement, it must be understood that here the presiding deities of those times are meant. The *ṣa* in the word *naktoṣasā* is lengthened for the convenience of the metre.

**"Supeśasā"** — since the word *peśas* is read among the sixteen words for form, *nirṇik*, *vavriḥ* and the rest, *peśas* means form; so *supeśasā* = *śobhanarūpayukte*, endowed with beautiful form, lovely.

**"Āsade"** — *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*: "for reaching", that is, for coming and sitting.

### Page 559 — Rik 7 grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar page, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**नक्तोषसा (*naktoṣasā*)** — "naktaṃ ca uṣaś ca naktoṣasā": a dvandva; after it the accusative dual *auṭ*; "supāṃ su-luk…" (printed "7-1-39") gives the substitute *ā*; the loss of the *m* of *naktam* and the lengthening of the penultimate *a* of *uṣas* both come as Vedic forms; "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. 6-2-141): in a dvandva of words for deities, the first and second members both keep their own accent at once — so both members keep their own accent. **सुपेशसा (*supeśasā*)** — "śobhanaṃ peśaḥ yayoḥ te"; as before, *ā* for the accusative dual; *peśas* is neuter, so initial-udātta by "nab-viṣayasyānisantasya" (Phi. sū. "2-26"). In the bahuvrīhi, "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" would give the first member's accent; setting it aside, "nañ-subhyām" (Pā. 6-2-172) would make the second member final-udātta; setting that aside too, "ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi" (Pā. 6-2-119) — in a bahuvrīhi, a second member that is initial-udātta and of two syllables stays initial-udātta after *su* — so *peśas* is initial-udātta. **अस्मिन् (*asmin*)** — the case ending udātta by "ūḍ-idam-padādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ" (printed "pā. mā." [sic] 6-1-171). **आसदे (*āsade*)** — *ṣadḷ viśaraṇa-gaty-avasādaneṣu*; *s* for *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. 6-1-64); by "sampadādibhyaḥ kvip" (printed "Pā. sū. 3-3-108 vā. 9") *kvip* in the sense of the state after *sad* preceded by *āṅ*; *sad* is udātta by the root accent; with *āṅ*, a *prādi* compound by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. 2-2-18); in *āsad*, by "gati-kārakopapadāt kṛt" (printed "6-2-9139" [sic]) that same accent stands as the *kṛt* second member's; then the dative singular *ṅe*, unaccented as a *sup*, made svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya" (Pā. 8-4-66).

### Page 560 — Rik 8: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> तच्छब्दो ऽत्र सर्वनामत्वात्प्रसिद्धार्थवाची । ता तौ याज्ञिकानां प्रसिद्धौ द्वावग्नी उप ह्वये । आह्वयामि । नो ऽस्मदीयमिमं यज्ञं यक्षताम् । तावुभौ यजतामनुतिष्ठताम् । कीदृशौ । सुजिह्वौ शोभनजिह्वोपेतौ । प्रियवचनौ शोभनज्वालौ वेत्यर्थः । होतारौ होमनिष्पादकौ दैव्या दैव्यौ देवसंबन्धिनौ । अत एवेमावग्नी दैव्यहोतृनामकौ । कवी मेधाविनौ ॥ ता तौ । द्वितीयाद्विवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । सुजिह्वौ । शोभना जिह्वा ययोस्तौ । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् । पूर्वपद एकादेशस्वरः । संहितायामावादेशः । वस्य लोपः शाकल्यस्येति लोपः । होतारा । जुहोतेस्तृन् । द्विवचने ऋतो ङि । पा. ७-३-११० । इति गुणः । अप्तृन्नित्युपधादीर्घः । पूर्ववदाकारः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । दैव्या । देवानामिमौ । देवाद्यञञौ । पा. ४-१-८५-३ । इति यञ् । यस्येति चेत्यकारलोपः । ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यमित्याद्युदात्तः । पूर्ववदाकारः । यक्षताम् । यजताम् । लोटि शपि परतः सिब्बहुलं लेटीति बहुलग्रहणात्सिप् । कुत्वचर्त्वषत्वानि ॥
>
> *tacchabdo 'tra sarvanāmatvātprasiddhārthavācī | tā tau yājñikānāṃ prasiddhau dvāvagnī upa hvaye | āhvayāmi | no 'smadīyamimaṃ yajñaṃ yakṣatām | tāvubhau yajatāmanutiṣṭhatām | kīdṛśau | sujihvau śobhanajihvopetau | priyavacanau śobhanajvālau vetyarthaḥ | hotārau homaniṣpādakau daivyā daivyau devasaṃbandhinau | ata evemāvagnī daivyahotṛnāmakau | kavī medhāvinau || tā tau | dvitīyādvivacanasya supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ | ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttaḥ | sujihvau | śobhanā jihvā yayostau | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvam | pūrvapada ekādeśasvaraḥ | saṃhitāyāmāvādeśaḥ | vasya lopaḥ śākalyasyeti lopaḥ | hotārā | juhotestṛn | dvivacane ṛto ṅi | pā. 7-3-110 | iti guṇaḥ | aptṛnnityupadhādīrghaḥ | pūrvavadākāraḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | daivyā | devānāmimau | devādyañañau | pā. 4-1-85-3 | iti yañ | yasyeti cetyakāralopaḥ | ñnityādirnityamityādyudāttaḥ | pūrvavadākāraḥ | yakṣatām | yajatām | loṭi śapi parataḥ sibbahulaṃ leṭīti bahulagrahaṇātsip | kutvacartvaṣatvāni ||*

**Translation:** "The word *tad* here, being a pronoun, denotes what is well known. *Tā* — those two fires well known to the sacrificers — I *upa hvaye*, call. May they both *yakṣatām*, perform, *imaṃ yajñam*, this our sacrifice. What kind? *Sujihvā* — endowed with good tongues, that is, of pleasant speech or of fine flames; *hotārā* — accomplishers of the *homa*; *daivyā* — belonging to the gods; hence these two fires bear the name *Daivya-hotṛ*; *kavī* — wise." (Grammatical tail: *tā* = *tau*, *ā* for the accusative dual by "supāṃ suluk…", udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ"; *sujihvau* — "whose tongue is fine", the second member final-udātta by "nañ-subhyām", the single-substitute accent in the first member [?]; in the Saṃhitā *āv*, and the *v* dropped by "lopaḥ śākalyasya"; *hotārā* — *tṛn* after *hu*, *guṇa* in the dual by "ṛto ṅi…" (Pā. 7-3-110), lengthening of the penultimate by "ap-tṛn…", *ā* as before, initial-udātta as *nit*; *daivyā* — "these two belong to the gods", *yañ* by "devād yañ-añau" (Pā. 4-1-85-3), the *a* dropped by "yasyeti ca", initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam", *ā* as before; *yakṣatām* = *yajatām*: with *śap* following in *loṭ*, *sip* by the word *bahula* in "sib bahulaṃ leṭi"; *k*, *car* and *ṣ*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**सुजिह्वा (sujihvā)** — having excellent tongues, that is, speaking pleasant words or having fine flames | **कवी (kavī)** — wise | **ता (tā)** — those, well known in the rites of sacrifice | **दैव्या (daivyā)** — belonging to the gods | **होतारा (hotārā)** — accomplishers of the *homa* | *(the two fire-forms called Daivya-hotārā)* **उप ह्वये (upa hvaye)** — I invoke (near me) | **नः (naḥ)** — our (i.e., that we perform) | **इमं यज्ञम् (imaṃ yajñam)** — this sacrifice | **यक्षताम् (yakṣatām)** — may they perform.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The two deities called *Daivyā Hotārā* (special forms of Agni) speak pleasant words (or are joined with brightly blazing flames), are very wise, and are expert in the *hotṛ* work. I call such divine deities named *Daivyā Hotārā*; may they come here, take the place of the *hotṛ*, and carry out the sacrificial rite we are performing.

### Page 561 — Rik 8: English, Special Topics

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> I invoke those Daivya and Hotara, those two divine hotries [sic] who are good-tongued and wise. May they perform this our sacrifice.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

On the words *daivyā hotārā*, Yāska's explanation:

> दैव्या होतारा दैव्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः ॥
>
> *daivyā hotārā daivyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ ||*

That is, the word points to Agni himself. Since Agni calls the gods, Agni stands in the middle between gods and men; in this matter he gives an example:

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. "10-110-7" [?]; the last digit is unclear.)*

> दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै ।
> प्रचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता ॥
>
> *daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai |*
> *pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśantā ||*

*("The two divine invokers, the first, fair-spoken, measuring out the sacrifice for man to worship, urging on, the two doers at the gatherings, pointing out the eastern light by direction" — mine and tentative.)*

Durgācārya's commentary on it:

> यावेतौ दैव्यौ होतारौ । देवेषु भवौ दैव्यौ देवावेव दैव्यौ । स्वार्थ एव तद्धितः । मनुष्यहोतारावपेक्ष्य । दैव्या होतारौ होतृमैत्रावरुणौ इति विशेषणम् । होतारा होतारावाह्वातारौ देवानां वाय्वग्नी । प्रथमा प्रथमौ मुख्यौ मनुष्यहोतारावपेक्ष्य । सुवाचा सुवाचौ प्रशस्तवाचौ सुस्तुतौ । मिमाना यज्ञं यज्ञनिर्मातारौ नित्यम् । मनुषः मनुष्यस्य यजध्यै यजनाय । प्रचोदयन्ता प्रचोदयमानौ । विदथेषु यज्ञेषु । कारू कर्तारौ । इत्यादि
>
> *yāvetau daivyau hotārau | deveṣu bhavau daivyau devāveva daivyau | svārtha eva taddhitaḥ | manuṣyahotārāvapekṣya | daivyā hotārau hotṛmaitrāvaruṇau iti viśeṣaṇam | hotārā hotārāvāhvātārau devānāṃ vāyvagnī | prathamā prathamau mukhyau manuṣyahotārāvapekṣya | suvācā suvācau praśastavācau sustutau | mimānā yajñaṃ yajñanirmātārau nityam | manuṣaḥ manuṣyasya yajadhyai yajanāya | pracodayantā pracodayamānau | vidatheṣu yajñeṣu | kārū kartārau | ityādi*

The chief idea: for the gods, Agni and Vāyu are known as the *hotṛs*; for men, the priests Hotṛ and Maitrāvaruṇa are known as the *hotṛs*. Since Agni, or Agni and Vāyu, stand between the gods and men and make a connection between them, Agni is called "the middle one". The name of these deities, *daivyā hotārā*, apart from the Āpri-sūktas, is read only in the two riks

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-10.)*

> त्वष्टारं वायुमृभवो य ओहते दैव्या होतारा उषसं स्वस्तये ॥
>
> *tvaṣṭāraṃ vāyumṛbhavo ya ohate daivyā hotārā uṣasaṃ svastaye ||*

### Page 562 — Rik 8: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-66-13.)*

> दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा पुरोहित ऋतस्य पन्थामन्वेमि साधुया ॥
>
> *daivyā hotārā prathamā purohita ṛtasya panthāmanvemi sādhuyā ||*

In the rik Ṛ. Saṃ. "7-2-7" [?] they are also called *jātavedasā*, and in the rik Ṛ. Saṃ. "10-70-7" [?] *purohitau* (the repeated digit is the same glyph in both, read as 7). And since the words in the riks just cited — *mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai*, *yajñeṣu mānuṣeṣu kārū*, and *pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū* — say that these deities carry out or urge on the sacrifices men perform, calling them *purohitas* is natural. Among the gods the *hotṛs* are Agni and Vāyu; among men the Hotṛ and his helper-priest, the Maitrāvaruṇa, are called the *hotṛs*. This Maitrāvaruṇa, by the *praiṣa* mantras, directs the other priests to do their several tasks. In the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-, the rest of the number left blank in the print) it is said: "मैत्रावरुणो हि पुरस्तादृत्विग्भ्यो वाचं विभजति" (*maitrāvaruṇo hi purastādṛtvigbhyo vācaṃ vibhajati*).

**"Sujihvā"** — *sujihvau — śobhanā jihvā yayos tau sujihvau | śobhanajihvopetau, priyavacanau, śobhanajvālau vā*: having excellent tongues, speaking pleasant words, or, if said of Agni, having excellent flames.

**"Yakṣatām"** — *yajatām*: may they sacrifice, that is, carry the sacrifice through.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 562–563, noted briefly; numbers checked against the print)*

**ता (*tā*)** — meaning *tau*. After *tad*, the accusative dual *auṭ*; for it "supāṃ suluk…" (printed "7-1-39") gives *ā*; "tyadādīnām aḥ" (printed "7-2-102") gives *a* for the *d*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (printed "6-1-96" [sic]; the sūtra is 6-1-97); *savarṇa*-lengthening; by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-5) the *ā* formed by the single substitute is udātta. **सुजिह्वा (*sujihvā*)** — "śobhanā jihvā yayoḥ tau"; *jihvā* is formed irregularly with *van* by "śeva-yahva-jihvā-grīvā-pvāmīvāḥ" (printed "Pā. sū. 1-152" [sic, an Uṇādi sūtra]): "lihanti anayā iti jihvā"; root *liha āsvādane*, with *van*, *j* for the *l*, and the absence of *guṇa* also irregular; *jihvā* is initial-udātta by the *nit* accent. In the bahuvrīhi, instead of the first-member accent, "nañ-subhyām" (Pā. 6-2-172) makes the second member *jihvā* final-udātta. Then the accusative dual *auṭ*: *sujihva* + *au*; the *vṛddhi* of "vṛddhir eci" (Pā. 6-1-88) would arise but "prathama-

### Page 563 — Rik 8 grammar closes

yoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-102) would give the *pūrvasavarṇa*-lengthening instead; that is barred by "nādici" (Pā. 6-1-104) — no *pūrvasavarṇa*-lengthening after *a* before an *ic* vowel — so "vṛddhir eci" makes the *vṛddhi* as the single substitute: *sujihvau*. By "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" the *au* formed by the *vṛddhi* single substitute is udātta. Since the word *upa* follows *sujihvau*, in the Saṃhitā "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78) gives *āv* for the *au*: *sujihvāv* + *upa*; "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. 8-3-19) drops the *v*; when *guṇa* by "ād guṇaḥ" is to be made, this loss is *asiddha* by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. 8-2-1), so the *v* intervenes and there is no *guṇa*. **होतारा (*hotārā*)** — *hu dānādanayoḥ*, a root of the *juhotyādi* class; after it *tṛn*; *laghūpadha-guṇa*; the nominative dual *au*: *hotṛ* + *au*; "ṛto ṅi-sarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (printed "7-3-110") gives *guṇa* with *r*; "ap-tṛn-tṛc-svasṛ…" (Pā. 6-4-11) lengthens the penultimate: *hotārau*; "supāṃ suluk" gives *ā* for the *au*: *hotārā*; *hotṛ*, ending in an *n*-marked suffix, is initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). **दैव्या (*daivyā*)** — after *div*, the suffix *ac* by "nandigrahi…" (Pā. 3-1-134); *laghūpadha-guṇa*; *deva* final-udātta by the *cit* accent. "devād yañ-añau" (printed "Pā. sū. 4-1-85 vā. 3"): after *deva*, in the senses of the *prāgdīvyatīya* section, the suffixes *yañ* and *añ*; with "devasya imau" meant, *yañ*; "taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ" (Pā. 7-2-117) gives *vṛddhi* of the first vowel, *ai* for the *e*; "yasyeti ca" (Pā. 6-4-148) drops the *a* before the suffix; *daivya* initial-udātta by "ñnity ādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197); then *au*, replaced by *ā* as before, *savarṇa*-lengthening: *daivyā*. **यक्षताम् (*yakṣatām*)** — *yaja devapūjādau*; after it *loṭ*, third dual *tas*; by "loṭo laṅvat" the treatment of *laṅ*, so *tām* for it by "tas-thas-tha-mipāṃ tān-tan-tāmaḥ"; the vikaraṇa *śap*: *yaj* + *a* + *tām*; since the sūtra "sib bahulaṃ leṭi" (Pā. 3-1-34) contains the word *bahula*, *sip* comes before the vikaraṇa *śap*: *yaj* + *s* + *a* + *tām*; *k*-series by "coḥ kuḥ": *g* for the *j*; *car* by "khari ca" (printed "8-4-55"): *k* for *g*; *ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśa-pratyayayoḥ" (printed "8-3-5?" [?]): *yakṣatām*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ".

### Page 564 — Sūkta 13, Rik 9

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इळा॒ सर॑स्वती म॒ही ति॒स्रो दे॒वीर्म॑यो॒भुवः॑ ।
> ब॒र्हिः सी॑दन्त्व॒स्रिधः॑ ॥९॥
>
> *iḷā sárasvatī mahī́ tisró devī́r mayobhúvaḥ |*
> *barhíḥ sīdantv asrídhaḥ ||9||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इळा । सरस्वती । मही । तिस्रः । देवीः । मयःऽभुवः ॥
> बर्हिः । सीदन्तु । अस्रिधः ॥९॥
>
> *iḷā | sarasvatī | mahī | tisraḥ | devīḥ | mayaḥ-bhuvaḥ ||*
> *barhiḥ | sīdantu | asridhaḥ ||9||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> अत्र महीशब्दो महत्त्वगुणयुक्तां भारतीमाचष्टे ऽन्येष्वाप्रीसूक्तेषु सदृशेष्विळा सरस्वती भारतीत्याम्नातत्वात् । इळादिशब्दाभिधेया वह्निमूर्तयस्तिस्रो देवीर्दीप्यमाना बर्हिर्वेद्यामास्तीर्णं सीदन्तु । प्राप्नुवन्तु । कीदृश्यः । मयोभुवः सुखोत्पादिका अस्रिधः शोषेण क्षयेण वा रहिताः ॥ इळा । ईड स्तुतौ । छान्दसं ह्रस्वत्वं । क्विप् । धातुस्वरः । टापं चापि हलन्तानां यथा वाचा दिशा निशेति टाप् । सरस्वती । सरोऽसुनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । तदस्यास्तीति मतुप् । आदुपधत्वाद्वत्वं । तसौ मत्वर्थ इति भत्वेन पदत्वस्य बाधितत्वाद्रुत्वाद्यभावः । उगितश्चेति ङीप् । मतुब्ङीपौ पित्त्वादनुदात्तौ । मही । महतीशब्दे तकारलोपश्छान्दसः । यस्येति चेत्यकारलोपः । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण ङीप उदात्तत्वं । तिस्रः । त्रिशब्दाज्जसि त्रिचतुरोः स्त्रियां तिसृचतसृ । पा. ७-२-९९ । इति तिस्रादेशः । अचि र ऋतः । पा. ७-२-१०० । इति रेफादेशः । तिसृभ्यो जसः । पा. ६-१-१६६ । इति जस उदात्तत्वं । देवीः । देवानां पत्न्यो देव्यः पुंयोगादाख्यायामिति ङीष् । यस्येति चेत्यकार लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेण ङीष उदात्तत्वं । जसि दीर्घाज्जसि च । पा. ६-१-१०४ [?] । इति निषिद्धं दीर्घत्वं । वा छन्दसीति पक्षेऽभ्यनुज्ञायते । मयोभुवः । मीञ् हिंसायां । हिनस्ति दुःखमिति सुखं मयः । तद्भावयन्तीति मयोभुवः । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थाद्भुवः क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । बर्हिः । बृंहेर्नलोपश्चेति इसिप्रत्ययः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । सीदन्तु । षद्लृ विशरणादौ । पाघ्रेत्यादिना सीदादेशः । अस्रिधः । स्रिधेर्हिंसार्थस्य शोषणार्थस्य वा सम्पदादिभ्यो भावे क्विपि नञा बहुव्रीहिः । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरं बाधित्वा नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं ॥
>
> *atra mahīśabdo mahattvaguṇayuktāṃ bhāratīmācaṣṭe 'nyeṣvāprīsūkteṣu sadṛśeṣviḷā sarasvatī bhāratītyāmnātatvāt | iḷādiśabdābhidheyā vahnimūrtayastisro devīrdīpyamānā barhirvedyāmāstīrṇaṃ sīdantu | prāpnuvantu | kīdṛśyaḥ | mayobhuvaḥ sukhotpādikā asridhaḥ śoṣeṇa kṣayeṇa vā rahitāḥ || iḷā | īḍa stutau | chāndasaṃ hrasvatvaṃ | kvip | dhātusvaraḥ | ṭāpaṃ cāpi halantānāṃ yathā vācā diśā niśeti ṭāp | sarasvatī | saro 'sunanto nittvādādyudāttaḥ | tadasyāstīti matup | ādupadhatvādvatvaṃ | tasau matvartha iti bhatvena padatvasya bādhitatvādrutvādyabhāvaḥ | ugitaśceti ṅīp | matubṅīpau pittvādanudāttau | mahī | mahatīśabde takāralopaśchāndasaḥ | yasyeti cetyakāralopaḥ | udāttanivṛttisvareṇa ṅīpa udāttatvaṃ | tisraḥ | triśabdājjasi tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ | pā. 7-2-99 | iti tisrādeśaḥ | aci ra ṛtaḥ | pā. 7-2-100 | iti rephādeśaḥ | tisṛbhyo jasaḥ | pā. 6-1-166 | iti jasa udāttatvaṃ | devīḥ | devānāṃ patnyo devyaḥ puṃyogādākhyāyāmiti ṅīṣ | yasyeti cetyakāra lopaḥ | pratyayasvareṇa ṅīṣa udāttatvaṃ | jasi dīrghājjasi ca | pā. 6-1-104 [?] | iti niṣiddhaṃ dīrghatvaṃ | vā chandasīti pakṣe 'bhyanujñāyate | mayobhuvaḥ | mīñ hiṃsāyāṃ | hinasti duḥkhamiti sukhaṃ mayaḥ | tadbhāvayantīti mayobhuvaḥ | antarbhāvitaṇyarthādbhuvaḥ kvip | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | barhiḥ | bṛṃhernalopaśceti isipratyayaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | sīdantu | ṣadlṛ viśaraṇādau | pāghretyādinā sīdādeśaḥ | asridhaḥ | sridherhiṃsārthasya śoṣaṇārthasya vā sampadādibhyo bhāve kvipi nañā bahuvrīhiḥ | pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaraṃ bādhitvā nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "Here the word *mahī* denotes *Bhāratī*, endowed with the quality of greatness, since in other Āprī-sūktas, which are similar, *Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Bhāratī* are recited. The three shining goddesses, forms of Fire denoted by the words *Iḷā* and the rest, *sīdantu*: may sit, may reach, the *barhis* spread on the altar. What are they like? *Mayobhuvaḥ*: producing happiness; *asridhaḥ*: free of drying up or of decay." (Grammatical tail: *iḷā* from *īḍ* 'to praise', the shortening Vedic, *kvip*, *ṭāp* as in *vācā, diśā, niśā*; *sarasvatī* from *saras* (*asun*) with *matup* and *ṅīp*; *mahī* with the Vedic loss of the *t* of *mahatī*; *tisraḥ* with *tisṛ* (Pā. 7-2-99) and *r* (Pā. 7-2-100), the case ending udātta by Pā. 6-1-166; *devīḥ* with *ṅīṣ*, the lengthening barred by "6-1-104" [?] but allowed optionally in the Veda; *mayobhuvaḥ* 'causing happiness to be', from *bhū* with *kvip*; *barhiḥ* with the suffix *isi*; *sīdantu* with *sīd* for *sad*; *asridhaḥ*, a bahuvrīhi with *nañ*, final udātta.)

### Page 565 — Rik 9: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**मयोभुवः (mayobhuvaḥ)** — giving happiness | **अस्रिधः (asridhaḥ)** — not cruel, or doing no harm | **इळा (iḷā)** — the goddess named *Iḷā* | **सरस्वती (sarasvatī)** — the goddess *Sarasvatī* | **मही (mahī)** — the goddess [named *Bhāratī*] endowed with the quality of greatness | **तिस्रः देवीः (tisraḥ devīḥ)** — these three goddesses, forms of Agni, shining, called by the words *Iḷā* and the rest | **बर्हिः (barhiḥ)** — the *darbha* spread on the altar as a seat | **सीदन्तु (sīdantu)** — may they sit (that is, may they come and sit on the *darbha*).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

May the three goddesses *Iḷā*, *Sarasvatī* and *Bhāratī* (*Mahī*) — who are forms of Agni, shine brilliantly, give happiness to all, and harm none — come to the *darbha* spread on the sacrificial altar as a seat and sit upon it.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> May Ila, Saraswati, Mahi (Bharati), the three comfort-giving and unhurting goddesses sit on the sacrificial grass.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

On *tisro devīḥ* Yāska says only

> तिस्रो देवीः । तिस्रो देवीस्तिस्रो देव्यः ॥
>
> *tisro devīḥ | tisro devīstisro devyaḥ ||*

and in the Ṛk he gives as an example,

> आ नो यज्ञं भारती तूयमेत्विळा मनुष्वदिह चेतयन्ती ।
> तिस्रो देवीर्बर्हिरेदं स्योनं सरस्वती स्वपसः सदन्तु ॥
>
> *ā no yajñaṃ bhāratī tūyametviḷā manuṣvadiha cetayantī |*
> *tisro devīrbarhiredaṃ syonaṃ sarasvatī svapasaḥ sadantu ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-8.)* *("May Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice, and Iḷā, awakening [us] here like Manu; may the three goddesses, Sarasvatī and the skilful ones, sit on this pleasant barhis" — mine and tentative.)*

he explains:

> ऐतु नो यज्ञं भारती क्षिप्रम् । भरत आदित्यस्तस्य भा इळा च मनुष्वदिह चेतयमाना तिस्रो देव्यो बर्हिरिदं सुखं सरस्वती च सकर्माण [?] आसीदन्तु ॥
>
> *aitu no yajñaṃ bhāratī kṣipram | bharata ādityastasya bhā iḷā ca manuṣvadiha cetayamānā tisro devyo barhiridaṃ sukhaṃ sarasvatī ca sakarmāṇa [?] āsīdantu ||*

That is:

### Page 566 — Rik 9: Special Topics (continued)

**Bhāratī**: *Bharata* is one of the twelve Ādityas; the lustre of the Āditya is called *bhā*. So *bhāratī* is the light of the sun, or the fire that is in the orb of the sun in the form of light.

**Iḷā**: *iḷā* is the earth. *Manuṣvat cetayantī*: having the power of urging, as men do; that is, since she gives food and other nourishment and wealth to the men on the earth, *Iḷā* is a particular form of the Agni that is in the earth-region.

**Sarasvatī**: since she is the presiding deity of the lightning in the atmosphere, *Sarasvatī* is said to be the form of Agni that is in the atmosphere.

So it is the custom to call the three goddesses *Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Bhāratī* the three forms of the fire in heaven, atmosphere and earth. (See pages "74–75" [?].)

**Mahī**:

> महीशब्दो महत्त्वगुणयुक्तां भारतीमाचष्टे ऽन्येष्वाप्रीसूक्तेषु सदृशेष्विळा सरस्वती भारतीत्याम्नातत्वात् ॥
>
> *mahīśabdo mahattvaguṇayuktāṃ bhāratīmācaṣṭe 'nyeṣvāprīsūkteṣu sadṛśeṣviḷā sarasvatī bhāratītyāmnātatvāt ||*

That is, the word *mahī* in this Ṛk means *Bhāratī*, endowed with the quality of greatness. For in the Āprī-sūktas, in the Ṛks that speak of *tisro devīḥ*, the names of the three goddesses *Iḷā, Sarasvatī, Bhāratī* are stated plainly. In this Ṛk only the two names *Iḷā* and *Sarasvatī* are given, and in the place of the other *mahī* is said, so there is no doubt that the word *mahī* points to the name *Bhāratī*. Some Western scholars think that the word *mahī* denotes a separate deity named *Mahī*. That is not right. The word *mahī* may have been used in place of the word *bhāratī* for the sake of the metre.

**Barhiḥ sīdantu**: *वेद्यामास्तीर्णं प्राप्नुवन्तु* (*vedyāmāstīrṇaṃ prāpnuvantu*, "may they reach what is spread on the altar"): may they reach the *darbha* spread as a seat, that is, may they sit on the seat of *darbha*: that is the sense.

**Iḷā, sarasvatī, mahī**:

> ईड स्तुतौ । सर अस्यास्तीति । मही महती, तकारलोपश्छान्दसः ॥
>
> *īḍa stutau | sara asyāstīti | mahī mahatī, takāralopaśchāndasaḥ ||*

Since she is praised she is *iḍā*; since she has *saras* (water) she is *sarasvatī*; and since the *t* of the word *mahatī* has dropped for the sake of the metre, she is *mahī*, endowed with greatness (*Bhāratī*): this is the derivation of the parts of these words.

### Page 567 — Rik 9: Special Topics (end) and grammar

**Devīḥ**:

> देवानां पत्न्यो देव्यः । ताः । अथवा देवीः दीप्यमानाः ॥
>
> *devānāṃ patnyo devyaḥ | tāḥ | athavā devīḥ dīpyamānāḥ ||*

Since they are the wives of the gods, or since they shine, these deities are called *devīḥ*.

**Mayobhuvaḥ**:

> मीञ् हिंसायाम् । हिनस्ति दुःखमिति सुखं मयः । तद्भावयन्तीति मयोभुवः ।
>
> *mīñ hiṃsāyām | hinasti duḥkhamiti sukhaṃ mayaḥ | tadbhāvayantīti mayobhuvaḥ |*

The root *mīñ* means to harm; to make sorrow. What is free of sorrow is happiness. Since they make happiness, the form *mayobhuvaḥ* is derived.

**Asridhaḥ**:

> स्रिधेर्हिंसार्थस्य शोषणार्थस्य वा भावे क्विप् । शोषेण क्षयेण वा रहिताः ॥
>
> *sridherhiṃsārthasya śoṣaṇārthasya vā bhāve kvip | śoṣeṇa kṣayeṇa vā rahitāḥ ||*

The root *sridh* means to harm, to dry up. *Asridhaḥ* means those who are not cruel, free of drying up, free of decay.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 567–569, noted briefly)*

**इळा (*iḷā*)**: root *īḍa stutau*, the *ī* shortened in the Veda; *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76), dropped; final udātta by "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162); *ḍ* → *ḷ* by "dvayoś cāsya svarayoḥ" (Prātiśākhya); the verse "vaṣṭi bhāgurir allopam avāpyor upasargayoḥ | āpaṃ caiva halantānāṃ yathā vācā niśā diśā" (Kau. "2-4-82" [?]): Bhāguri drops the *a* of *ava* and *api* (*vagāhaḥ*, *pidhānam*) and adds *āp* after consonant stems, so *iḷ* + *ṭāp* gives *iḷā*. **सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*)**: *sṛ* + *asun* by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-628" [?]), *guṇa*, *raparatva*: *saras*, initial udātta (*nit*); *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. sū. 5-2-94); *m* → *v* by "mādupadhāyāś ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-9); *bha* by "tasau matvarthe" (Pā. sū. 1-4-19), so "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66) does not apply; *ṅīp* by "ugitaś ca" (Pā. sū. "6-3-45" [?]); *matup* and *ṅīp* both unaccented.

### Page 568 — Rik 9: grammar (continued)

**मही (*mahī*)**: the *t* of *mahatī* dropped in the Veda, the *a* after *h* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148); the *ī* udātta by "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-161). **तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)**: *tri* + *jas*; *tisṛ* by "tricaturoḥ striyāṃ tisṛcatasṛ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-99); the *guṇa* of "ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-110 [as printed]) is set aside by "aci ra ṛtaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-100), giving *r*; *ru*, visarga; *jas* unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau", *tisṛ* final udātta like *tri* (*sthānivadbhāva*); the svarita of "udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya" is overridden by "tisṛbhyo jasaḥ" (Pā. sū. "7-1-166" [?]), making *jas* udātta. **देवीः (*devīḥ*)**: *deva* (*ac*-ending); *ṅīṣ* by "puṃyogād ākhyāyām" (Pā. sū. 4-1-48); *a* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (6-4-148); *ṅīṣ* udātta; the *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening of "prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-102) is barred by "dīrghāj jasi ca" (Pā. sū. "6-?-104" [?]) but allowed optionally by "vā chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-106); *ru*, visarga. **मयोभुवः (*mayobhuvaḥ*)**: *mīñ hiṃsāyām* (*kryādi*), "mināti hinasti duḥkham" (that which drives sorrow away); *asun* by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-628" [?]), *guṇa*, *ay*: *mayas* "happiness"; "mayaḥ bhāvayanti": *bhū* with the inner causative + *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); *uvaṅ* by "aci śnu…" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77); *ru*, *u*, *guṇa*; final udātta of the *kṛt* member by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139).

### Page 569 — Rik 9: grammar (end)

**बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)**: *bṛhi vṛddhau*, *idit*, so *num*; *isi* and loss of *n* by "bṛṃher nalopaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "2-266" [?]); *laghūpadha-guṇa*; final udātta by the suffix accent. **सीदन्तु (*sīdantu*)**: *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*, *ṣ* → *s* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ"; *loṭ* 3rd plural *jhi*, *jh* → *ant* by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-3); *u* by "eruḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-86); *śap*; *sīda* by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78); wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ". **अस्रिधः (*asridhaḥ*)**: *sridh* (harm or drying up) + *kvip* by "sampadādibhyaḥ kvip" (Pā. sū. vā. "0-3-108-9" [?]); "na vidyate sridh yāsāṃ tāḥ": bahuvrīhi; the first-member accent of "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) is overridden by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172), final udātta on the second member.

**॥९॥**

### Page 569 — Sūkta 13, Rik 10

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इ॒ह त्वष्टा॑रमग्रि॒यं वि॒श्वरू॑प॒मुप॑ ह्वये ।
> अ॒स्माक॑मस्तु॒ केव॑लः ॥१०॥
>
> *ihá tváṣṭāram agriyáṃ viśvárūpam úpa hvaye |*
> *asmā́kam astu kévalaḥ ||10||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इह । त्वष्टारम् । अग्रियम् । विश्वऽरूपम् । उप । ह्वये ॥
> अस्माकम् । अस्तु । केवलः ॥१०॥
>
> *iha | tvaṣṭāram | agriyam | viśva-rūpam | upa | hvaye ||*
> *asmākam | astu | kevalaḥ ||10||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> पत्नीसंयाजे त्वष्टुः पुरोनुवाक्येह त्वष्टारमग्रियमिति । शं युवाकाय संप्रेषित इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । सं ते पयांसि समु यन्तु वाजा इह त्वष्टारमग्रियम् । आ. १-१० ॥ इति ॥
>
> *patnīsaṃyāje tvaṣṭuḥ puronuvākyeha tvaṣṭāramagriyamiti | śaṃ yuvākāya saṃpreṣita iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | saṃ te payāṃsi samu yantu vājā iha tvaṣṭāramagriyam | ā. 1-10 || iti ||*

### Page 570 — Rik 10: bhāṣya (continued), word-meanings, overall sense, English

> त्वष्टारं त्वष्टृनामकमग्निमिह कर्मण्युपह्वये । कीदृशम् । अग्रियं श्रेष्ठं विश्वरूपं बहुविधरूपोपेतं । सो ऽस्माकं केवलो ऽसाधारणो ऽस्तु । इतरयजमानेभ्यो ऽप्यधिकमनुग्रहं करोत्वित्यर्थः ॥ त्वष्टारं । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । तृन् । स्वरतिसूतिसूयतिधूञूदितो वा । पा. ७-२-४४ । इतीडभावपक्षे स्कोः संयोगाद्योरन्ते च । पा. ८-२-२९ । इति ककारलोपः । ष्टुत्वं । द्वितीयैकवचने ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोरिति गुणे ऽप्तृन्नित्यादिनोपधाया दीर्घः । तृनो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । अग्रियं । अग्रादित्यनुवृत्तौ घच्छौ च । पा. ४-४-११७ [?] । इति घच् । आयनेयीनीत्यादिना । पा. ७-१-२ । घकारस्य इयादेशः । यस्येति लोपः । आयनादिषूपदेशिवद्वचनं स्वरसिद्ध्यर्थं । पा. ७-१-२-१ । इत्युपदेशिवद्भावात्प्रत्ययाद्युदात्तत्वा[?]द्घचश्चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वं । विश्वरूपं । विश्वानि रूपाणि त्वष्टृत्पन्नत्वेन यस्य । त्वष्टा वै पशूनां मिथुनानां रूपकृत् । तै. सं. ६-१-८-५ [?] । इति श्रुतेः । विश्वशब्दस्याद्युदात्तत्वात्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वे प्राप्ते बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायां । पा. ६-२-१०६ । इति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । अस्माकं । असु क्षेपणे । युष्यसिभ्यां मदिक् । उ. १-१३८ [?] । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । षष्ठीबहुवचनमाम् । अत्र परमपि योऽचि । पा. ७-२-८९ । इति यत्वं बाधित्वा नित्यत्वात्प्रतिपदविधित्वाच्च साम आकमादेशे कृते । पा. ७-१-३३ । अनादेश इति निषेधेन । पा. ७-२-८६ । यत्वाभावाच्छेषे लोप इति दकारलोपे ऽकारान्तत्वेन पश्चात्प्राप्तस्यापि सुटः । पा. ७-१-५२ । साम इति निर्देशे स्थानिन्यन्तर्भावेन निवृत्तिः । एवमर्थ एव हि साम इति ससुट्कनिर्देशः । केवलः । वृषादेराकृतिगणत्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥
>
> *tvaṣṭāraṃ tvaṣṭṛnāmakamagnimiha karmaṇyupahvaye | kīdṛśam | agriyaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ viśvarūpaṃ bahuvidharūpopetaṃ | so 'smākaṃ kevalo 'sādhāraṇo 'stu | itarayajamānebhyo 'pyadhikamanugrahaṃ karotvityarthaḥ || tvaṣṭāraṃ | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | tṛn | svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā | pā. 7-2-44 | itīḍabhāvapakṣe skoḥ saṃyogādyorante ca | pā. 8-2-29 | iti kakāralopaḥ | ṣṭutvaṃ | dvitīyaikavacane ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoriti guṇe 'ptṛnnityādinopadhāyā dīrghaḥ | tṛno nittvādādyudāttatvaṃ | agriyaṃ | agrādityanuvṛttau ghacchau ca | pā. 4-4-117 [?] | iti ghac | āyaneyīnītyādinā | pā. 7-1-2 | ghakārasya iyādeśaḥ | yasyeti lopaḥ | āyanādiṣūpadeśivadvacanaṃ svarasiddhyarthaṃ | pā. 7-1-2-1 | ityupadeśivadbhāvātpratyayādyudāttatvā[?]dghacaścittvādantodāttatvaṃ | viśvarūpaṃ | viśvāni rūpāṇi tvaṣṭṛtpannatvena yasya | tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt | tai. saṃ. 6-1-8-5 [?] | iti śruteḥ | viśvaśabdasyādyudāttatvātpūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratve prāpte bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyāṃ | pā. 6-2-106 | iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvaṃ | asmākaṃ | asu kṣepaṇe | yuṣyasibhyāṃ madik | u. 1-138 [?] | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | ṣaṣṭhībahuvacanamām | atra paramapi yo 'ci | pā. 7-2-89 | iti yatvaṃ bādhitvā nityatvātpratipadavidhitvācca sāma ākamādeśe kṛte | pā. 7-1-33 | anādeśa iti niṣedhena | pā. 7-2-86 | yatvābhāvāccheṣe lopa iti dakāralope 'kārāntatvena paścātprāptasyāpi suṭaḥ | pā. 7-1-52 | sāma iti nirdeśe sthāninyantarbhāvena nivṛttiḥ | evamartha eva hi sāma iti sasuṭkanirdeśaḥ | kevalaḥ | vṛṣāderākṛtigaṇatvādādyudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "In the *patnīsaṃyāja*, *iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam* is Tvaṣṭṛ's *puronuvākyā*. It is laid down in the section '*śaṃ yuvākāya saṃpreṣite*': '*saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā*, *iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam*' (Āśv. 1-10). I invoke here, in this rite, *tvaṣṭāram*, the fire named Tvaṣṭṛ. What kind? *Agriyam*: the best; *viśvarūpam*: endowed with forms of many kinds. May he be *asmākaṃ kevalaḥ*, ours alone: that is, may he show us more favour than he shows other sacrificers." (Grammatical tail: *tvaṣṭāram* from *tvakṣū* with *tṛn*, *iṭ* optional by Pā. 7-2-44, *k* dropped by Pā. 8-2-29, *ṣṭutva*, *guṇa*, lengthening of the penultimate, initial udātta because *tṛn* is *nit*; *agriyam* with *gha* (Pā. "4-4-117" [?]), *iya* for *gh* (Pā. 7-1-2), treated as in *upadeśa* by the vārttika 7-1-2-1, final udātta because *ghac* is *cit*; *viśvarūpam*, a bahuvrīhi, the first member final-udātta by Pā. 6-2-106, the sense supported by T.S. "6-1-8-5" [?]; *asmākam* from *as* with *madik* (Uṇ. "1-138" [?]), *ākam* for *sām* by Pā. 7-1-33 overriding *yatva* (7-2-89, 7-2-86), *suṭ* (7-1-52) excluded by the form *sāma* with *suṭ* in the sūtra; *kevalaḥ*, initial udātta as of the *vṛṣādi* class.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अग्रियम् (agriyam)** — the foremost | **विश्वरूपम् (viśvarūpam)** — having forms of many kinds | **त्वष्टारम् (tvaṣṭāram)** — the deity named Tvaṣṭṛ (a special form of Agni) | **इह (iha)** — in this sacrifice | **उप ह्वये (upa hvaye)** — I invoke | *(that Tvaṣṭṛ)* **अस्माकम् (asmākam)** — to us (in our regard) | **केवलः (kevalaḥ)** — [being] uniquely, very attached | **अस्तु (astu)** — may he be.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The deity named Tvaṣṭṛ is the foremost among the gods. He has many kinds of forms (shapes), and is the maker of things. I call such a deity to this sacrifice. May he be exceedingly kind to us.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> I invoke Twashtir, the foremost and the multi.form [sic] here. May he be soley [sic] ours.

### Page 571 — Rik 10: Special Topics

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

The application of this mantra: in the *homa* called *patnīsaṃyāja* in the sacrifice, the Ṛk *iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam* is used as the *puronuvākyā* mantra. In the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section *śaṃ yuvākāya saṃpreṣite*, it is said that the Ṛks *saṃ te payāṃsi sam u yantu vājā* and *iha tvaṣṭāram agriyam* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-13-10) are to be used as *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* mantras (Āśv. sū. 1-10). Yāska's explanation:

> त्वष्टा । त्वष्टा तूर्णमश्नुत इति नैरुक्ताः । त्विषेर्वा स्याद्दीप्तिकर्मणस्त्वक्षतेर्वा स्यात्करोतिकर्मणः ॥ माध्यमिकस्त्वष्टेत्याहुर्मध्यमे च स्थाने समाम्नातः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥
>
> *tvaṣṭā | tvaṣṭā tūrṇamaśnuta iti nairuktāḥ | tviṣervā syāddīptikarmaṇastvakṣatervā syātkarotikarmaṇaḥ || mādhyamikastvaṣṭetyāhurmadhyame ca sthāne samāmnātaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ||*

*(Ni. 8-14.)*

That is, the etymologists say the word *tvaṣṭā* means one who pervades quickly; or one who shines; or one who makes things (crafts? [the source's own question mark]); some say he is *mādhyamika*, that is, one who is between heaven and earth; Śākapūṇi says he is Agni.

Some also say that Tvaṣṭṛ, like Viśvakarman, is the craftsman of the gods. For in the Ṛk Yāska gives as an example,

> य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।
> तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥
>
> *ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhuvanāni viśvā |*
> *tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-9.)* *("He who adorned with forms these two, heaven and earth, the begetters, and all the worlds: that god Tvaṣṭṛ, O hotṛ, urged on today, best at sacrificing, knowing, worship here" — mine and tentative.)*

it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of heaven and earth and the cause of the form, beauty, intelligence, growth and so on suited to each of the beings in all the worlds. Besides this, Śruti (Yajurveda) sentences such as

> त्वष्टा वै पशूनां मिथुनानां रूपकृत्
>
> *tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt*

*(T.S. "6-1-8-5" [?]; "Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of the forms of paired animals"),*

> त्वष्टा रूपाणामधिपतिः
>
> *tvaṣṭā rūpāṇāmadhipatiḥ*

*(T.S. "3-3-", the rest not printed; "Tvaṣṭṛ is the lord of forms"),*

> त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति
>
> *tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti*

*("Tvaṣṭṛ shapes forms")* set out Tvaṣṭṛ's skill in making things. And

> मह्यं त्वष्टा वज्रमतक्षदायसं मयि देवासो ऽवृजन्नपि क्रतुम् ॥
>
> *mahyaṃ tvaṣṭā vajramatakṣadāyasaṃ mayi devāso 'vṛjannapi kratum ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-48-3.)* *("For me Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the iron thunderbolt; in me the gods placed resolve" — mine and tentative.)*

Indra says, "Tvaṣṭṛ made me the thunderbolt-weapon of steel." Many mantras of the Ṛgveda say that he made the sacrificial materials the gods need and many other things.

### Page 572 — Rik 10: Special Topics (end) and grammar

Tvaṣṭṛ is well known as one of the twelve Ādityas. That is why Yāska explained the sense as "the shining one".

**Agriyam**: *śreṣṭham*, *pradhānam*: the best, the chief.

**Viśvarūpam**:

> विश्वानि रूपाणि त्वष्टृत्पन्नत्वेन यस्य ॥
>
> *viśvāni rūpāṇi tvaṣṭṛtpannatvena yasya ||*

Since he is the cause and maker of many forms, he is called *viśvarūpa*.

**Asmākam astu kevalaḥ**: the third quarter of this Ṛk, *asmākam astu kevalaḥ*, is found also in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-10, where it refers to Indra. Its sense is "may he be our chief benefactor".

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 572–575, noted briefly)*

**त्वष्टारम् (*tvaṣṭāram*)**: *takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe*; *tvakṣū* + *tṛn*; the root is *ūdit*, so by "svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā" (Pā. sū. 7-2-44) *iṭ* is optional; without *iṭ*, *tvakṣ* + *tṛ*: by "skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-29) the *s* or *k* at the start of a conjunct at the end of a *pada* or before a *jhal* drops, so *k* drops: *tvaṣ* + *tṛ*; "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-41) gives *ṭ*: *tvaṣṭṛ*; accusative singular *am*; *guṇa* by "ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-110), *r* by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-51); penultimate lengthened by "ap tṛn tṛc…" (Pā. sū. 6-4-11): *tvaṣṭāram*; *tṛn* is *nit*, so initial udātta. **अग्रियम् (*agriyam*)**: "ghacchau ca" (Pā. sū. "4-4-117" [?]) with *agrāt* carried on from "agrād yat" (Pā. sū. 4-4-116): after *agra* in the locative, in the sense *bhavaḥ*, *ghac* and *cha*; *agra* + *gha*; by "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ phaḍhakhachaghāṃ pratyayādīnām" (Pā. sū. 7-1-2) *gh* → *iy*: *agra* + *iy* + *a*; *a* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148): *agriya*. The question of its accent follows:

### Page 573 — Rik 10: grammar (continued)

These replacements fall on *ph* and the other consonants that begin suffixes; here *gh* becomes *iy*. Being taught under the *aṅga* heading, they depend on both stem and suffix, so they are *bahiraṅga*; "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3) does not depend on the stem, so it is *antaraṅga*, and the initial udātta comes before the *āyan*-type replacements. "pratyayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-1), "paraś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-2) and "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3) all govern suffix rules, so the initial udātta is tied to the introduction of the suffix: first the accent of *ghac*, then *iy* for *gh*. *Gh* is a consonant and has no accent; the replacement too comes in, by *āntaratamya*, without accent. The Bhāṣyakāra says this:

> अक्रियमाणे ह्युपदेशिवद्भावे प्रत्ययसंज्ञासन्नियोगेनाद्युदात्तत्वे कृते ऽन्तर्यत आदेशा अस्वरकाणामस्वरकाः स्युः
>
> *akriyamāṇe hyupadeśivadbhāve pratyayasaṃjñāsanniyogenādyudāttatve kṛte 'ntaryata ādeśā asvarakāṇāmasvarakāḥ syuḥ*

*(7-1-2 MB.)* Though without accent when they come in, a sound cannot be uttered without accent, so by "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" the replacements must be unaccented. *Asvarakāṇām asvarakāḥ syuḥ* can also be explained another way: uttering an anudātta causes slackness of the limbs, softness of tone and wideness of the throat; the same happens in uttering a consonant; but since consonants are not fit for it they take no anudātta. So consonants have the property of the anudātta, not of the udātta; *svara* in *asvarakāṇām* is taken as udātta: for consonants without udātta, replacements without the desired udātta, that is, anudātta replacements, come in. So the *iy* for *gh* here would have to be anudātta. Hence the Vārttikakāra says "āyanādiṣūpadeśivadvacanaṃ svarasiddhyartham" (Pā. sū. 7-1-2-1): for the sake of the accent the *āyan*-type replacement must be said to come in at the time the suffix is taught. Then, if *iya* comes in when the suffix arises, in *agra* + *iya* the suffix-initial udātta is overridden by the *cit* marker, "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163), and *iya* is final udātta. Otherwise, if the replacements, being *bahiraṅga*, did not come first, the *cit* marker in "ghacchau ca" would be useless: with *agra* + *gha* the suffix-initial udātta would come, and after the udātta *a* the anudātta *iy* would come, so *iya* would be final udātta anyway, and the *cit* marker would be pointless. *Vyarthaṃ sat kiṃcid arthaṃ jñāpayati*: a useless

### Page 574 — Rik 10: grammar (continued)

word, so as to have a purpose, makes something known, here a statement: that in the state of *upadeśa* the *āyan*-type replacements already come in. The Uddyotakāra explains it:

> प्रत्ययसम्बन्ध्यादेशानामुत्पत्तिसन्नियोगशिष्टकार्यादपि पूर्वं प्रवृत्तिर्ज्ञाप्यते इति भाष्यार्थः
>
> *pratyayasambandhyādeśānāmutpattisanniyogaśiṣṭakāryādapi pūrvaṃ pravṛttirjñāpyate iti bhāṣyārthaḥ*

That is, it is made known by the *cit* marker that the *āyan*-type replacements tied to the suffix come in even before the initial udātta tied to the arising of the suffix. Now, if there were no *cit* marker, then with *agra* + *gha*, *iya* would come in before the initial udātta, and with *agra* + *iya* the initial udātta would make the *i* udātta, whereas in the Śruti the *a* is udātta. So the *cit* marker serves the final udātta, and the *upadeśivad* statement is not needed. The Vārttikakāra himself says this in "na vā kvacic citkaraṇāt" (Pā. sū. 7-1-2-2). Thus *agriya* is final udātta.

**विश्वरूपम् (*viśvarūpam*)**: "viśvāni rūpāṇi tvaṣṭuḥ utpannatvena yasya saḥ viśvarūpaḥ", a bahuvrīhi; the Śruti "tvaṣṭā vai paśūnāṃ mithunānāṃ rūpakṛt" (Tai. Śru. Saṃ. "6-1-8-5" [?]) shows the sense "produced by Tvaṣṭṛ"; *viśva* is *viś* + *kvan*, initial udātta (*nit*); the first-member accent of "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) is overridden by "bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-106): in a bahuvrīhi that is a name, the first member *viśva* is final udātta.

**अस्माकम् (*asmākam*)**: *asu kṣepaṇe*; "yuṣyasibhyāṃ madik" (Uṇ. sū. "1-136" [?]): *madik* after *yuṣ* and *as*: *asmad*, final udātta by the suffix accent; genitive plural *ām*: *asmad* + *ām*. "yo 'ci" (Pā. sū. 7-2-89) gives *y* for *yuṣmad*/*asmad* before a vowel-initial ending without a replacement; "sāma ākam" (Pā. sū. 7-1-33) gives *ākam* for *sām* after them; "yo 'ci" is the later rule, so by the paribhāṣā "vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam" (Pā. sū. 1-4-2) *yatva* would apply; but "sāma ākam" (Pā. sū. 7-1-33) is *nitya*: *ākam* comes whether or not *yatva* is made; so *ākam* applies in both cases. Since

### Page 575 — Rik 10: grammar (end)

it is *nitya*, even though *yatva* had the prior claim, once *ākam* has come "yo 'ci" does not apply, for it applies before an ending that has no replacement, and after *ākam* the ending has one; so the *nitya* rule, applicable whether or not the other applies, is not blocked by "yo 'ci". So by "paranityāntaraṅgāpavādānām uttarottaraṃ balīyaḥ" (paribhāṣā "38" [?]) the *nitya* *ākam* overrides the later *yatva*; being *pratipadokta*, *ākam* is also stronger than *yatva*. Here with *asmad* + *ām* there is no *sām*: the *ām* would get the augment *suṭ* by "āmi sarvanāmnaḥ suṭ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-52) after a pronoun ending in *a*, giving *sām*. Since *yatva* comes before *ākam*, "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-90) does not apply, so the stem does not end in *a*, and stating *sām* with *suṭ* in the sūtra may seem useless. But if the sūtra had been made "āma ākam" without *suṭ*, then after *ākam*, by *sthānivadbhāva*, *ākam* would count as *ām*, and where "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-90) drops the final *d*, *suṭ* would have to come; to prevent that *suṭ* the sūtra states it with *suṭ*. Stated with *suṭ*, *suṭ* too counts as the original, so the *suṭ* that would come later is excluded, and the statement with *suṭ* has its use. On the view that "śeṣe lopaḥ" drops the *ṭi*, the statement with *suṭ* is not needed.

**केवलः (*kevalaḥ*)**: *vṛṣādi* is an *ākṛtigaṇa*, so by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-203) it is final udātta [as printed; the bhāṣya on p. 570 says initial udātta].

**॥१०॥**

### Page 575 — Sūkta 13, Rik 11

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अव॑ सृजा वनस्पते॒ देव॑ दे॒वेभ्यो॑ ह॒विः ।
> प्र दा॒तुर॑स्तु॒ चेत॑नम् ॥११॥
>
> *áva sṛjā vanaspate déva devébhyo havíḥ |*
> *pra dātúr astu cétanam ||11||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अव । सृज । वनस्पते । देव । देवेभ्यः । हविः ॥
> प्र । दातुः । अस्तु । चेतनम् ॥११॥
>
> *ava | sṛja | vanaspate | deva | devebhyaḥ | haviḥ ||*
> *pra | dātuḥ | astu | cetanam ||11||*

### Page 576 — Rik 11: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे वनस्पते एतन्नामकाग्ने देव हविर्भुग्भ्यो देवेभ्यो ऽस्मदीयं हविरव सृज । समर्पयेत्यर्थः । प्र दातुर्यजमानस्य चेतनं परलोकविषयं विज्ञानं त्वत्प्रसादादस्तु ॥ वनस्पते । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । देव । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । हविः । इसः प्रत्ययस्वरः । दातुः । ददातेस्तृच् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तः । जसि ऋत उत् । पा. ६-१-१११ । इत्युत्वं । एकादेशो रपरत्वं च । रात्सस्य । पा. ८-२-२४ । इति सलोपः । एकादेशस्वरेणोकार उदात्तः । चेतनं । चिती संज्ञाने । करणे ल्युट् । योरनादेशः । लघूपधगुणः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं ॥
>
> *he vanaspate etannāmakāgne deva havirbhugbhyo devebhyo 'smadīyaṃ havirava sṛja | samarpayetyarthaḥ | pra dāturyajamānasya cetanaṃ paralokaviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ tvatprasādādastu || vanaspate | āmantritanighātaḥ | deva | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | ṣāṣṭhikamāmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | haviḥ | isaḥ pratyayasvaraḥ | dātuḥ | dadātestṛc | cita ityantodāttaḥ | jasi ṛta ut | pā. 6-1-111 | ityutvaṃ | ekādeśo raparatvaṃ ca | rātsasya | pā. 8-2-24 | iti salopaḥ | ekādeśasvareṇokāra udāttaḥ | cetanaṃ | citī saṃjñāne | karaṇe lyuṭ | yoranādeśaḥ | laghūpadhaguṇaḥ | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "O *vanaspate*, Agni of this name, O god, *ava sṛja*: release, that is, deliver, our oblation to the gods who eat oblations. By your favour may there be for the giver, the sacrificer, *cetanam*: knowledge concerning the other world." (Grammatical tail: *vanaspate* lowered as a vocative; *deva* not lowered at the head of a pāda, initial udātta by the *ṣāṣṭhika* rule; *haviḥ* with the accent of the suffix *is*; *dātuḥ* from *dā* with *tṛc*, final udātta (*cit*), *ut* by Pā. 6-1-111, *s* dropped by "rātsasya" (Pā. 8-2-24), the *u* udātta; *cetanam* from *citī saṃjñāne* with *lyuṭ* in the instrumental sense, *guṇa*, udātta before the suffix by "liti".)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**देव (deva)** — shining | **वनस्पते (vanaspate)** — O Agni, named *Vanaspati* | **देवेभ्यः (devebhyaḥ)** — to the gods | **हविः (haviḥ)** — the oblation that we have prepared | **अव सृज (ava sṛja)** — convey, offer | **दातुः (dātuḥ)** — to the sacrificer who gives the oblation to the gods | **चेतनम् (cetanam)** — excellent knowledge (concerning the other world) | **अस्तु (astu)** — [by your favour] may there be.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Vanaspati, or Agni named Vanaspati, deliver to the gods the oblation we give, and by your favour may excellent knowledge come to the sacrificer who gives the oblation.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Present, divine Vanaspati, our oblation to the gods, and may trne [sic] knowledge be the reward of the giver.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Vanaspate**: Yāska's explanation of the word *vanaspati*:

> वनस्पत इत्येनमाहैष हि वनानां पाता वा पालयिता वा । वनं वनोतेः ॥
>
> *vanaspata ityenamāhaiṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā vā pālayitā vā | vanaṃ vanoteḥ ||*

*(Ni. 8-3.)*

> तत्को वनस्पतिः । यूप इति कात्थक्यः । अग्निरिति शाकपूणिः ॥
>
> *tatko vanaspatiḥ | yūpa iti kātthakyaḥ | agniriti śākapūṇiḥ ||*

*(Ni. 8-18.)*

### Page 577 — Rik 11: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

That is, Agni himself is called *vanaspati*. For Agni is the protector or guardian of the woods: though Agni is present within the tree he does not burn it, so he is called its guardian. Or, since it serves for wood and other means of the sacrifice, it is called *vana*. *Vanaspati* means king of trees, a large tree. Which deity is *vanaspati*? Kātthakya's view is that it is the wooden post set up to tie the animal at the sacrifice; Śākapūṇi's view is that *vanaspati* is Agni.

To support Kātthakya's view Yāska gives a Ṛk as an example:

> अञ्जन्ति त्वामध्वरे देवयन्तो वनस्पते मधुना दैव्येन ॥
>
> *añjanti tvāmadhvare devayanto vanaspate madhunā daivyena ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8-1.)* That is, "O Vanaspati (sacrificial post), at the sacrifice the priests and sacrificer anoint you with ghee purified by mantras": the post to which the animal is tied is addressed. And in the 3rd, 6th and 11th Ṛks of the same sūkta *vanaspati* is addressed as the sacrificial post; besides, it is well known that the post is the deity of that sūkta. In the eleventh Ṛk of that sūkta,

> वनस्पते शतवल्शो वि रोह सहस्रवल्शा वि वयं रुहेम
>
> *vanaspate śatavalśo vi roha sahasravalśā vi vayaṃ ruhema*

that is, "O Vanaspati, grow with hundreds and thousands of shoots (in places)", which fits the tree *vanaspati*. In the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. "10-70-10" [?],

> वनस्पते रशनया नियूय
>
> *vanaspate raśanayā niyūya*

"O Vanaspati, having tied the animal with the rope", confirms the sense "sacrificial post" for the word *vanaspati*. So *vanaspati* means the sacrificial post; "Agni" is an indirect sense.

**Dātuḥ**: *हविःप्रदातुः यजमानस्य* (*haviḥpradātuḥ yajamānasya*): of the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

**Cetanam**: *परलोकविषयं विज्ञानं* (*paralokaviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ*): the Bhāṣyakāra says it is knowledge concerning the other world. *Cetana* means knowledge, understanding, discrimination. Veṅkaṭamādhava says

> दातुर्यजमानस्य प्रज्ञापनं देवेषु त्वया निवेदितस्य
>
> *dāturyajamānasya prajñāpanaṃ deveṣu tvayā niveditasya*

that is, "you must make the gods aware concerning the sacrificer".

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 577–578, noted briefly)*

**वनस्पते (*vanaspate*)**: wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19). **देव (*deva*)**: it stands at the head of the second pāda, so the prohibition "apādādau" (Pā. sū. 8-1-18) stops the lowering, and the sixth-adhyāya rule "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198) gives initial udātta.

### Page 578 — Rik 11: grammar (end)

**हविः (*haviḥ*)**: *hu dānādanayoḥ*; *isi* by "arciśucihu…" (Uṇ. sū. "2-266" [?]); *guṇa*. The *paryudāsa* "anisantasya": the verse

> प्रसज्यप्रतिषेधो ऽयं क्रियया सह यत्र नञ् । पर्युदासस्तु विज्ञेयो यत्रोत्तरपदेन नञ् ॥
>
> *prasajyapratiṣedho 'yaṃ kriyayā saha yatra nañ | paryudāsastu vijñeyo yatrottarapadena nañ ||*

explains that where *nañ* is construed with the verb it is a *prasajya-pratiṣedha*, where with the following member (*n'is*, *anis*) a *paryudāsa*. A *prasajya-pratiṣedha* always brings three faults (supplying a fitting verb, a compound of an unconnected word, splitting the sentence), so it is taken only where a *paryudāsa* cannot be; here the *paryudāsa* is taken. So "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" (Phi. sū.) means: the beginning of a neuter stem other than one ending in *is* is udātta. *Havis* ends in *is*, so this rule gives no initial udātta; the suffix accent stands, and *haviḥ* is final udātta. **दातुः (*dātuḥ*)**: *ḍudāñ dāne*; *tṛc* by "ṇvultṛcau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-133); *cit*, so final udātta by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163); genitive singular "jas" [as printed, for *ṅas*]; "ṛta ut" (Pā. sū. 6-1-111): *u* as single replacement for *ṛ* + *a*; *r* after it by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-51): *dātur* + *s*; "rātsasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-24) drops the final member of a conjunct after *r*, here the *s*. Though "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-23) could drop the *s*, this sūtra is needed as a restriction: after *r* only *s* is dropped, so in *ūrk* the *k* is not dropped. Visarga: *dātuḥ*; the *u* udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-5). **चेतनम् (*cetanam*)**: *citī saṃjñāne*; *lyuṭ* in the instrumental sense by "karaṇādhikaraṇayoś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-117); *ana* for *yu* by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1); *laghūpadha-guṇa* by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86): *cetana*; the *e* before the suffix udātta by "liti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-193).

**॥११॥**
