### Page 579 — Sūkta 13, Rik 12 (the last)

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> स्वाहा॑ य॒ज्ञं कृ॑णोत॒नेन्द्रा॑य॒ यज्व॑नो गृ॒हे ।
> तत्र॑ दे॒वाँ उप॑ ह्वये ॥१२॥
>
> *svā́hā yajñáṃ kṛṇotanéndrāya yájvano gṛhé |*
> *tátra devā́m̐ úpa hvaye ||12||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> स्वाहा । यज्ञम् । कृणोतन । इन्द्राय । यज्वनः । गृहे ॥
> तत्र । देवान् । उप । ह्वये ॥१२॥
>
> *svāhā | yajñam | kṛṇotana | indrāya | yajvanaḥ | gṛhe ||*
> *tatra | devān | upa | hvaye ||12||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> स्वाहाशब्दो हविष्प्रदानवाची सन् एतन्नामकमग्निविशेषं लक्षयति । तदग्निसम्पादितं यज्ञमिन्द्रायेन्द्रतुष्ट्यर्थं यज्वनो यजमानस्य गृहे ऋत्विजः कृणोतन । कुरुत । तत्र यज्ञे देवानुप ह्वये ॥ कृणोतन । कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च । इदित्त्वान्नुम् । लोण्मध्यमबहुवचनस्य तस्थस्थमिपामिति तादेशः । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च । पा. ७-१-४५ । इति तनबादेशः । शपि प्राप्ते धिन्विकृण्व्योरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः । तत्सन्नियोगेन वकारस्य चाकारः । तस्यातो लोप इति लोपः । तस्याचः परस्मिन्निति स्थानिवद्भावादृकारस्य लघूपधगुणो न भवति । तनपः पित्त्वेनाङित्त्वादुकारस्य गुणः । इन्द्राय । ऋज्रेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । यज्वनः । यज देवपूजासङ्गतिकरणदानेषु । सुयजोर्ङ्वनिप् । पा. ३-२-१०३ । जसि भसंज्ञायामल्लोपे प्राप्ते न संयोगाद्वमन्तात् । पा. ६-४-१३७ । इति निषेधः । वनिपः पित्त्वेन धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । गृहे । ग्रह उपादाने । गेहे कः । पा. ३-१-१४४ । इति कप्रत्ययः । ग्रहिज्येत्यादिना । पा. ६-१-१६ । सम्प्रसारणं । परपूर्वत्वं । प्रत्ययस्वरः । तत्र । त्रल् । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वं । देवाँ उपेत्यत्र संहितायां दीर्घादटीति नकारस्य रुत्वं । आतोऽटि नित्यमित्याकारस्यानुनासिकादेशः । भोभगो इति यत्वं । तस्य लोपः शाकल्यस्येति लोपः ॥ २४ ॥
>
> *svāhāśabdo haviṣpradānavācī san etannāmakamagniviśeṣaṃ lakṣayati | tadagnisampāditaṃ yajñamindrāyendratuṣṭyarthaṃ yajvano yajamānasya gṛhe ṛtvijaḥ kṛṇotana | kuruta | tatra yajñe devānupa hvaye || kṛṇotana | kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca | idittvānnum | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanasya tasthasthamipāmiti tādeśaḥ | taptanaptanathanāśca | pā. 7-1-45 | iti tanabādeśaḥ | śapi prāpte dhinvikṛṇvyoraccetyupratyayaḥ | tatsanniyogena vakārasya cākāraḥ | tasyāto lopa iti lopaḥ | tasyācaḥ parasminniti sthānivadbhāvādṛkārasya laghūpadhaguṇo na bhavati | tanapaḥ pittvenāṅittvādukārasya guṇaḥ | indrāya | ṛjrendretyādinā ran | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | yajvanaḥ | yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu | suyajorṅvanip | pā. 3-2-103 | jasi bhasaṃjñāyāmallope prāpte na saṃyogādvamantāt | pā. 6-4-137 | iti niṣedhaḥ | vanipaḥ pittvena dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | gṛhe | graha upādāne | gehe kaḥ | pā. 3-1-144 | iti kapratyayaḥ | grahijyetyādinā | pā. 6-1-16 | samprasāraṇaṃ | parapūrvatvaṃ | pratyayasvaraḥ | tatra | tral | litīti pratyayātpūrvasyodāttatvaṃ | devā~ upetyatra saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghādaṭīti nakārasya rutvaṃ | āto 'ṭi nityamityākārasyānunāsikādeśaḥ | bhobhago iti yatvaṃ | tasya lopaḥ śākalyasyeti lopaḥ || 24 ||*

**Translation:** "The word *svāhā*, which denotes the giving of an oblation, indicates the particular fire of that name. O priests, *kṛṇotana*, perform, in the house of the *yajvan*, the sacrificer, the sacrifice brought about by that fire, for Indra, for Indra's satisfaction. In that sacrifice I invoke the gods." (Grammatical tail: *kṛṇotana* from *kṛvi* with *num*, *ta* for *tha* and *tana* for it (Pā. 7-1-45), the suffix *u* in place of *śap* with *a* for the *v*, then loss of that *a*, no *guṇa* of the *ṛ* by *sthānivadbhāva*, *guṇa* of the *u* since *tanap* is *pit*; *indrāya* with *ran*, initial udātta; *yajvanaḥ* with *ṅvanip* (Pā. 3-2-103), the loss of *a* barred by Pā. 6-4-137 ("jasi" as printed for *ṅasi*), the root accent; *gṛhe* from *grah* with *ka* (Pā. 3-1-144) and *saṃprasāraṇa* (Pā. 6-1-16); *tatra* with *tral*, udātta before the *l*-marked suffix; *devām̐ upa*: *ru* for the *n*, nasal *ā*, *y*, then its loss. The closing "24" is the varga number.)

### Page 580 — Rik 12: word-meanings (begun on p. 579), overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

*(O priests!)* **इन्द्राय (indrāya)** — for Indra's satisfaction | **यज्वनः (yajvanaḥ)** — of the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice | **गृहे (gṛhe)** — in the house (the sacrificial hall) | **स्वाहा (svāhā)** — [performed] by the utterance *svāhā* (or *svāhā*, the fire named Svāhā, accomplishing it) | **यज्ञम् (yajñam)** — the sacrifice | **कृणोतन (kṛṇotana)** — perform | **तत्र (tatra)** — to that sacrificial ground | **देवान् (devān)** — the gods | **उप ह्वये (upa hvaye)** — I invoke.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O priests, the *adhvaryu* and the others! In the sacrificer's house, perform the sacrifice for Indra's satisfaction with the cry *svāhā*; or perform it, offering the oblations belonging to the fire named *Svāhā*. For that I call the gods there.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Perform the sacrifice to Indra conveyed through swaha in the house of the sacrificer. I invoke the gods thither.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Svāhā**: Yāska's explanation:

> स्वाहाकृतयः । स्वाहाकृतयः स्वाहेत्येतत् सु आहेति वा । स्वा वागाहेति वा । स्वं प्राहेति वा । स्वाहुतं हविर्जुहोतीति वा ॥
>
> *svāhākṛtayaḥ | svāhākṛtayaḥ svāhetyetat su āheti vā | svā vāgāheti vā | svaṃ prāheti vā | svāhutaṃ havirjuhotīti vā ||*

*(No Nirukta number is printed.)* The word *svāhā* has four different senses of its parts:

(1) *su āheti vā*: *su* = well, *āha* = says: since it is uttered well, or clearly, it is called *svāhā*.

(2) *svā vāg āheti vā*: *svā* = one's own, *vāk* = speech. There is the Śruti (Brāhmaṇa) sentence

> तं स्वा वागभ्यवदज्जुहुधीति तत्स्वाहाकारस्य जन्म
>
> *taṃ svā vāgabhyavadajjuhudhīti tatsvāhākārasya janma*

("his own speech said to him, 'offer!'; that is the birth of the *svāhākāra*" — mine and tentative). That is, since the one who makes the *homa* himself adds the word *svāhā* at the end of the Ṛk, the Vedic mantra, it is called *svāhā*.

(3) *svaṃ prāheti vā*: here *svam* = his own oblation; *āha*: he says that he offers it in the fire. So it is called *svāhā*.

(4) *svāhutaṃ havir juhotīti vā*: since he offers the oblation he has offered by uttering the word *svāhā*, that is, since he gives the oblation into the fire, it is called *svāhā*.

For the sense of the *svāhākāra* Yāska gives this Ṛk as an example:

### Page 581 — Rik 12: Special Topics (continued) and grammar

> सद्यो जातो व्यमिमीत यज्ञमग्निर्देवानामभवत्पुरोगाः ।
> अस्य होतुः प्रदिश्यृतस्य वाचि स्वाहाकृतं हविरदन्तु देवाः ॥
>
> *sadyo jāto vyamimīta yajñamagnirdevānāmabhavatpurogāḥ |*
> *asya hotuḥ pradiśyṛtasya vāci svāhākṛtaṃ haviradantu devāḥ ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-11.)* *("Born at once, Agni measured out the sacrifice and became the leader of the gods; at the word of this hotṛ, in the direction of order, let the gods eat the oblation made with svāhā" — mine and tentative.)*

Its chief sense: Agni, just born (that is, now established at the sacrifice), sits before the gods, carries out the duty of the *hotṛ*, that is, the work of calling the gods, and brings the sacrifice to completion. May the gods eat the oblation that such a *hotṛ*, being in the eastern quarter, offers with the word *svāhā*. So *svāhā* is the name of the word uttered at the end of the mantra when the oblation is offered, for the gods' pleasure, into the fire set up in due form for the sacrifice.

In some Āprī-sūktas the plural *svāhākṛtayaḥ* is used: since the word *svāhā* is added also to the eleven *prayāja* mantras used in offering to the eleven deities of the sūkta, the plural *svāhākṛtayaḥ* is used.

In the Purāṇas and other works the word *svāhā* is used in another sense. The Mahābhārata says that the daughter of Bṛhaspati, the son of the sage Aṅgiras, is Svāhā; the Purāṇas say that the goddess Svāhā is the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati and the wife of Agni.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 581–583, noted briefly)*

**कृणोतन (*kṛṇotana*)**: *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*, *idit*, so *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ": *kṛnv*; *loṭ* 2nd plural *tha*; with *laṅvadbhāva* by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85), *ta* for *tha* by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. "śū." [sic] 3-4-101); "taptanaptanathanāś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-1-45) gives four replacements of that *t* in the *loṭ* 2nd person (*tap*, *tanap*, *tana*, *thana*), here *tanap*: *kṛnv* + *tana*; *śap* by "kartari śap" would come, but "dhinvikṛṇvyor a ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-80) gives *a* for the last letter of *dhinv*, *kṛṇv* and, in the place of *śap*, the suffix *u*: *kṛna* + *u* + *tana*; "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-48) drops the *a* of what ends in *a* at the time the *ārdhadhātuka* suffix is taught,

### Page 582 — Rik 12: grammar (continued)

so the *a* of *kṛna* drops; for this loss "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-57) gives *sthānivadbhāva*, so the *ṛ* gets no *laghūpadha-guṇa*. *Tanap* is *pit*, so by the exclusion *apit* in "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) it does not become *ṅit*, and "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) does not bar the *guṇa*; by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84) the *u* takes *guṇa*, *o*; *ṇ* for *n* by "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vaktavyam" (Pā. sū. 8-4-1-1): *kṛṇotana*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ". **इन्द्राय (*indrāya*)**: *idi paramaiśvarye*, *num*; *ran* by "ṛjrendrāgra…" (Uṇ. sū. 2-186); the suffix is *nit*, so by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) *indra* is initial udātta. **यज्वनः (*yajvanaḥ*)**: *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; "suyajor ṅvanip" (Pā. sū. 3-2-103): after *ṣuñ abhiṣave* and *yaja devapūjādau*, *ṅvanip* in the past sense; *van* remains; *yajvan* + *as* (genitive singular, "jas" [as printed, for *ṅas*]); *bha* by "yaci bham" (Pā. sū. 1-4-18); so "allopo 'naḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-134) would drop the *a* of an *an* that is part of the stem before a vowel- or *y*-initial ending other than the *sarvanāmasthāna*, but "na saṃyogād vamantāt" (Pā. sū. 6-4-137) bars the loss of the *a* of *an* after a conjunct ending in *v* or *m*, so after *jv* it does not drop. **गृहे (*gṛhe*)**: *ka* by "gehe kaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-144); the *k* is *it* by "laśakvataddhite" (Pā. sū. 1-3-8) and drops by "tasya lopaḥ"; "grahijyāvayivyadhivaṣṭivicativṛścatipṛcchatibhṛjjatīnāṃ ṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-16) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*, *ṛ* for the *r*; by "igyaṇaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-45) *i, u, ṛ, ḷ* in place of *y, v, r, l* are called *saṃprasāraṇa*; "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108) gives *pūrvarūpa* of *ṛ* and *a*: *gṛha*, locative singular *gṛhe*; the accent of the suffix *ka*. **तत्र (*tatra*)**: "saptamyās tral" (Pā. sū. 5-3-10): *tral* after *tad* in the locative; ending in a *taddhita*, it is a *prātipadika* by "kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca", the ending dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ", and by "prāg diśo vibhaktiḥ" *tral* is called *vibhakti*; so before it "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102) gives

### Page 583 — Rik 12: grammar (end); close of Sūkta 13

*a* for the *d*: *ta* + *a* + *tra*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97): *tatra*; by "liti" (6-1-193) the syllable before *tral* is udātta. **देवाँ उप (*devām̐ upa*)**: *deva* from *div* with *ac* by the *pacādi* rule (Pā. sū. 3-1-134) and *laghūpadha-guṇa* (Pā. sū. 7-3-86); accusative plural *śas*: *deva* + *as*; *pūrvasavarṇa-dīrgha* by "prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-102): *devās*; "tasmāc chaso naḥ puṃsi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-103): *n* for the *s* of *śas*: *devān*; in the Saṃhitā, before *upa*, "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. sū. 8-3-9) gives *ru* for the *n*: *devār* + *upa*; "āto 'ṭi nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-3-3) nasalises the *ā* before the *r*; "bhobhagoaghoapūrvasya yo 'śi" (Pā. sū. 8-3-17) gives *y* for the *ru*: *devāy* + *upa*; "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. sū. 8-3-19) drops the *y*: *devā* + *upa*; "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87) would give *o*, but by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. sū. 8-2-1) the loss of *y* is treated as not done for the *guṇa*, so the *y* counts as standing after the *a*, no vowel follows it, and there is no *guṇa*.

> ऐभिरग्न इत्यादिकस्य द्वादशर्चस्य तृतीयसूक्तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । तच्च सूक्तं बहुदेवताकम् । अत एवानुक्रम्यते । ऐभिर्वैश्वदेवमिति ॥ विनियोगस्तु । व्यूढद्वादशाहस्य प्रथमे छन्दोमे तृतीयसवने वैश्वदेवशस्त्र ऐभिरग्ने दुवो गिर इति सूक्तम् ॥ तथा च सूत्रितम् । अथ छन्दोमाः समुद्रादूर्मिरित्युपक्रम्यैभिरग्ने दुवो गिर इति वैश्वदेवम् । आ. ८-९१ [?] । इति ॥
>
> *aibhiragna ityādikasya dvādaśarcasya tṛtīyasūktasya ṛṣicchandasī pūrvavat | tacca sūktaṃ bahudevatākam | ata evānukramyate | aibhirvaiśvadevamiti || viniyogastu | vyūḍhadvādaśāhasya prathame chandome tṛtīyasavane vaiśvadevaśastra aibhiragne duvo gira iti sūktam || tathā ca sūtritam | atha chandomāḥ samudrādūrmirityupakramyaibhiragne duvo gira iti vaiśvadevam | ā. 8-91 [?] | iti ||*

**Translation:** "The sūkta of twelve Ṛks beginning *aibhir agne*, the third sūkta [of the anuvāka]: its ṛṣi and metre are as before. That sūkta has many deities; that is why the Anukramaṇikā says only *aibhir vaiśvadevam*. Its application: in the first *chandoma* day of the *vyūḍha-dvādaśāha*, at the third pressing, in the *vaiśvadeva-śastra*, the sūkta *aibhir agne duvo giraḥ*. So it is laid down in the Sūtra: 'Now the *chandomas*: beginning with *samudrād ūrmiḥ*, … *aibhir agne duvo giraḥ* is the Vaiśvadeva' (Āśv. "8-91" [?] as printed in the Sanskrit; the Kannada below gives 8-9)."

**॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥** In the fourth anuvāka, the third sūkta, *aibhir agne*, has twelve Ṛks. Its ṛṣi and metre are as in the preceding sūkta. Since it has many deities the sūkta is *bahudevatāka*; so the Anukramaṇikā calls it a sūkta to the Viśvedevas. Application: in the first *chandoma* of the *vyūḍha-dvādaśāha* sacrifice, at the third pressing,

### Page 584 — Sūkta 14, Rik 1

when the *vaiśvadeva-śastra* mantras are recited, the sūkta *aibhir agne duvo giraḥ* is to be recited. In the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, *atha chandomāḥ samudrād ūrmir ity upakramyaibhir agne duvo gira iti vaiśvadevam*: that is, the mantras beginning with *samudrād ūrmiḥ* and going on to *aibhir agne duvo giraḥ* are called *chandoma* mantras. (Ā. sū. 8-9.)

**Translation:** "O Agni, together with these, *viśvebhir devebhiḥ*, all the gods honoured at this sacrifice, *somapītaye*, for the sacrifice that has the drinking of soma, come towards *duvaḥ*, our service, and *giraḥ*, our praises. *Yāhi*: come. *Yakṣi ca*: and having come, sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: *ebhiḥ*: *idam* refers back to the gods named before, so in *anvādeśa* it takes the unaccented *aś* (Pā. 2-4-32), replacing the whole word since it is *śit*; *ais* for *bhis* is barred by Pā. 7-1-11; the ending stays unaccented, since the rule *ūḍidam…* applies only after a final-udātta stem; *duvaḥ* initial udātta by *nabviṣayasyānisantasya*; *viśvebhiḥ*: *viśva* from *viś* with *kvan*, initial udātta (*nit*), no *ais* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*, *e* by Pā. 7-3-103; *somapītaye*: *soma* with *man*, initial udātta; *somapīti* "the sacrifice in which there is the drinking of soma", dative of purpose; *devebhiḥ* likewise; *yakṣi*: *yaj*, *loṭ*, *sip*, *śap* dropped, *ṣ* and then *k* (*ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si*), *hi* for *si* not made, being Vedic; the root accent, *sip* being unaccented.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(Kannada)*

**(हे) अग्ने ((he) agne)** — O Agni | **एभिः (ebhiḥ)** — these [gods], honoured at this our sacrifice (Kannada *saṃbhāvitarāda*) | **विश्वेभिः (viśvebhiḥ)** — all | **देवेभिः (devebhiḥ)** — with the gods | **दुवः (duvaḥ)** — the service (*śuśrūṣā*) that we render | **गिरः (giraḥ)** — words in the form of hymns of praise | **सोमपीतये (somapītaye)** — for the drinking of soma | **प्रति आ याहि (prati ā yāhi)** — come so as to receive | **यक्षि च (yakṣi ca)** — and bring the sacrifice to completion.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, come with all the gods, to receive the service we render in this our sacrifice and the hymns of praise, and to drink the soma. After you have come, bring this sacrificial act to completion in all its parts.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Come, Agni with all those gods to receive our adoration and praises and for drinking soma; and also perform the sacrifice.

### Page 586 — Rik 1: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 586–588, noted briefly)*

**एभिः (*ebhiḥ*)**: *idam* + *bhis*; *idam* refers to the deities mentioned before, so there is *anvādeśa*; hence by "idamo 'nvādeśe 'śanudāttas tṛtīyādau" (Pā. sū. 2-4-32) the unaccented replacement *aś* comes for *idam*; being *śit*, it replaces the whole word by "anekāl śit sarvasya": *a* + *bhis*; "ato bhisa ais" (Pā. sū. 7-1-9) would give *ais*, but "nedamadasor akoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-11) bars *ais* after *idam* and *adas* without the *k* (of *aka*); so no *ais*. "bahuvacane jhaly et" (Pā. sū. 7-3-103) gives *e* to the *a*-final stem before a *jhal*-initial plural ending: *e* + *bhis*, *ru*, visarga: *ebhiḥ*. "ūḍidampadādyappumraidyubhyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-171): here, by "sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-168), *ekācaḥ*, and by "antodāttād uttarapadād anyatarasyām anityasamāse" (Pā. sū. 6-1-169), *antodāttāt*, are carried on, so the sūtra means: a non-*sarvanāmasthāna* ending after *idam* and the rest, when they have one vowel and are final-udātta, is udātta. Here *aś* is an unaccented replacement, and *e* is not final-udātta even though by *sthānivadbhāva* it counts as *idam*; so this sūtra gives the ending no udātta, and by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4) *bhis* stays unaccented.

**दुवः (*duvaḥ*)**: initial udātta by "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" (Phi. sū. 26). **विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*)**: *viśa praveśane* + *kvan* by "aśūpruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan" (Uṇ. sū. 149 [as printed]); the suffix is *nit*, so initial udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197); before *bhis*, "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 7-1-10) makes *ais* optional in the Veda, so no *ais*; *e* by "bahuvacane jhaly et" (Pā. sū. 7-3-103): *viśve* + *bhis*, *ru*, visarga: *viśvebhiḥ*.

**सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)**: *soma* from *ṣu* with *man* by "artistusuhusṛdhṛkṣikṣubhāyāvāpadiyakṣinībhyo man" (Uṇ. sū. 1-136), initial udātta (*nit*); "somasya pītir yasmin yāge saḥ", for him: *somapītaye*, a bahuvrīhi. By "caturthīvidhāne tādarthye upasaṃkhyānam" (Pā. sū. 2-3-13-1), and "tasmā idaṃ tadartham; arthena nityasamāsaḥ viśeṣyaliṅgatā ca", the compound; *tadarthasya bhāvaḥ tādarthyam*: by "guṇavacanabrāhmaṇādibhyaḥ ṣyañ" (Pā. sū. 5-1-124)

### Page 587 — Rik 1: grammar (end)

in the *bhāva* sense. *Tad* means the effect; the cause is for the sake of the effect, is it not? So the word *tadartha* denotes a cause that serves an effect. In cases like *brāhmaṇāya dadhi* ("curds for the brāhmaṇa") the fourth case needs a particular effect meant by the word for the effect: brāhmaṇas are not produced from curds, so the fourth case could not come here; but if a particular effect is meant, the brāhmaṇa as qualified by eating is the effect, and curds, being the cause of the qualifying eating, may be the cause of the brāhmaṇa so qualified; thus the fourth case is justified here. By "samāsakṛttaddhiteṣu bhāvapratyayena sambandhābhidhānam" (the abstract suffix after a compound, a *kṛdanta* or a *taddhitānta* expresses the relation), the *ṣyañ* after the compound *tadartha* expresses the relation; so *tādarthya* means the relation of a cause serving an effect, and the vārttika means that when a relation of effect and cause is shown, the fourth case comes after the stem that denotes the effect. Here the sacrifice that has the drinking of soma comes about from Agni's coming, so *somapīti* denotes the effect, and the fourth case follows it. The Bhāṣya gives *yūpāya dāru* ("wood for the sacrificial post") as an example of this statement: *dāru* is wood; since the post comes from the wood, the post is the effect, and so the fourth case comes after it. *Kuṇḍalāya hiraṇyam* ("gold for an earring") is another example the Bhāṣya gives.

**देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)**: *deva* ends in *a*; *ais* for the *bhis* after it would come by "ato bhisa ais" (Pā. sū. 7-1-9), but by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 7-1-10) it does not; then, *bhis* being a *jhal*-initial plural ending, "bahuvacane jhaly et" gives *e* for the *a*; *ru*, visarga: *devebhiḥ*. **याहि (*yāhi*)**: wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

**यक्षि (*yakṣi*)**: *yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadāneṣu*; *loṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*: *yaj* + *si*; the *śap* that comes by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68) is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73); *ṣ* for the *j* by "vraścabhrasjasṛjamṛjayajarājabhrājacchaśāṃ ṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-36): *yaṣ* + *si*; "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si" (Pā. sū. 8-2-41): before *s*, *k* for *ṣ* and *ḍh*: *yak* + *si*; "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87) would give *hi* for *si*, but in the Veda it does not come here. *Sip* is *pit*, so it is unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" [as printed]. *ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ": *yakṣi*. Since it follows the *tiṅanta* *yāhi*, "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not make it wholly unaccented.

**॥१॥**

### Page 588 — Sūkta 14, Rik 2

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आ त्वा॒ कण्वा॑ अहूषत गृ॒णन्ति॑ विप्र ते॒ धियः॑ ।
> दे॒वेभि॑रग्न॒ आ ग॑हि ॥२॥
>
> *ā tvā káṇvā ahūṣata gṛṇánti vipra te dhíyaḥ |*
> *devébhir agna ā́ gahi ||2||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आ । त्वा । कण्वाः । अहूषत । गृणन्ति । विप्र । ते । धियः ॥
> देवेभिः । अग्ने । आ । गहि ॥२॥
>
> *ā | tvā | kaṇvāḥ | ahūṣata | gṛṇanti | vipra | te | dhiyaḥ ||*
> *devebhiḥ | agne | ā | gahi ||2||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे विप्र मेधाविन्नग्ने कण्वा मेधाविन ऋत्विजस्त्वा यज्ञनिष्पादकं त्वामाहूषत । आह्वयन्ति । तथा ते धियस्त्वदीयानि कर्माणि गृणन्ति । कथयन्ति । ततो हे अग्ने देवेभिर्देवैः सहा गहि । आगच्छ । विप्र इत्यादिषु चतुर्विंशतिसंख्याकेषु मेधाविनामसु कण्व ऋभुरिति पठितम् ॥ त्वा । त्वामौ द्वितीयाया इति त्वादेशः । सर्वानुदात्तः । कण्वाः । कण शब्दार्थः । अशिप्रुषिलटिकणिखटीत्यादिना क्वन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । अहूषत । ह्वेञ् स्पर्धायां शब्दे च । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने लुङ् । ञित्त्वादात्मनेपदम् । झ आत्मनेपदेष्वनत इत्यदादेशः । च्लेः सिच् । एकाच इतीट्प्रतिषेधः । पा. ७-२-१० । बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणं परपूर्वत्वं । हलः । पा. ६-४-२ । इति दीर्घत्वं । आदेशप्रत्यययोरिति षत्वं । छान्दसत्वादूकारस्य न गुणः । अडागमः । गृणन्ति । गॄ शब्दे । लट् । झि । झोऽन्तः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति धातोर्ह्रस्वत्वं । श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः । पा. ६-४-११२ । इत्याकारलोपः । ऋवर्णाच्चेति वक्तव्यम् । का. ८-४-१-१ । इति णत्वं । तिङः स्वर एव शिष्यते । विप्र । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । ते । अनुदात्तमित्यनुवृत्तौ तेमयावेकवचनस्य । पा. ८-१-२२ । इति षष्ठ्यास्ते इत्यादेशः । देवेभिः । छान्दस ऐसभावः । गहि । गम्लृ सृप्लृ गतौ । लोटः सिप् । सेर्ह्यपिच्च । कर्तरि शप् । तस्य बहुलं छन्दसीति लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिना मकारलोपः । तस्यासिद्धवदत्राभादित्यसिद्धत्वादतो हेरिति हेर्लुग्न भवति ॥
>
> *he vipra medhāvinnagne kaṇvā medhāvina ṛtvijastvā yajñaniṣpādakaṃ tvāmāhūṣata | āhvayanti | tathā te dhiyastvadīyāni karmāṇi gṛṇanti | kathayanti | tato he agne devebhirdevaiḥ sahā gahi | āgaccha | vipra ityādiṣu caturviṃśatisaṃkhyākeṣu medhāvināmasu kaṇva ṛbhuriti paṭhitam || tvā | tvāmau dvitīyāyā iti tvādeśaḥ | sarvānudāttaḥ | kaṇvāḥ | kaṇa śabdārthaḥ | aśipruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭītyādinā kvan | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | ahūṣata | hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti vartamāne luṅ | ñittvādātmanepadam | jha ātmanepadeṣvanata ityadādeśaḥ | cleḥ sic | ekāca itīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | pā. 7-2-10 | bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇaṃ parapūrvatvaṃ | halaḥ | pā. 6-4-2 | iti dīrghatvaṃ | ādeśapratyayayoriti ṣatvaṃ | chāndasatvādūkārasya na guṇaḥ | aḍāgamaḥ | gṛṇanti | gṝ śabde | laṭ | jhi | jho 'ntaḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | pvādīnāṃ hrasva iti dhātorhrasvatvaṃ | śnābhyastayorātaḥ | pā. 6-4-112 | ityākāralopaḥ | ṛvarṇācceti vaktavyam | kā. 8-4-1-1 | iti ṇatvaṃ | tiṅaḥ svara eva śiṣyate | vipra | āmantritanighātaḥ | te | anudāttamityanuvṛttau temayāvekavacanasya | pā. 8-1-22 | iti ṣaṣṭhyāste ityādeśaḥ | devebhiḥ | chāndasa aisabhāvaḥ | gahi | gamlṛ sṛplṛ gatau | loṭaḥ sip | serhyapicca | kartari śap | tasya bahulaṃ chandasīti luk | anudāttopadeśetyādinā makāralopaḥ | tasyāsiddhavadatrābhādityasiddhatvādato heriti herlugna bhavati ||*

**Translation:** "O *vipra*, wise Agni, the *kaṇvāḥ*, the wise priests, *āhūṣata*, call you, the accomplisher of the sacrifice; and they *gṛṇanti*, declare, *te dhiyaḥ*, your deeds. So, O Agni, come with the gods. *Kaṇva* and *ṛbhu* are read among the twenty-four names for the wise beginning with *vipra*." (Grammatical tail: *tvā* by "tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ", wholly unaccented; *kaṇvāḥ* from *kaṇa* 'to sound' with *kvan*, initial udātta; *ahūṣata* from *hveñ*, *luṅ* in the present sense, *ātmanepada* (the root is *ñit*), *at* for *jh*, *sic*, no *iṭ* (Pā. 7-2-10), *saṃprasāraṇa* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*, lengthening by "halaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-2), *ṣ*, no *guṇa* of the *ū* (Vedic), the augment *a*; *gṛṇanti* from *gṝ* with *śnā*, the root shortened, the *ā* of *śnā* dropped (Pā. 6-4-112), *ṇ* (Kā. 8-4-1-1); *vipra* lowered as a vocative; *te* for *tava* by Pā. 8-1-22; *devebhiḥ* without *ais*; *gahi*: *gam*, *sip*, *hi*, *śap* dropped, *m* dropped, and that loss being treated as not done, *hi* is not dropped by "ato heḥ".)

### Page 589 — Rik 2: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**(हे) विप्र ((he) vipra)** — O wise Agni | **कण्वाः (kaṇvāḥ)** — the priests, who are wise (descendants of the ṛṣi Kaṇva) | **त्वा (tvā)** — you | **आ अहूषत (ā ahūṣata)** — call (with prayer) | *(likewise)* **ते (te)** — your | **धियः (dhiyaḥ)** — deeds | **गृणन्ति (gṛṇanti)** — praise | *(therefore)* **अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **देवेभिः (devebhiḥ)** — with the gods | **आ गहि (ā gahi)** — be pleased to come.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O wise Agni, the wise priests (or the descendants of the ṛṣi Kaṇva) pray to you and call you to the sacrifice to praise your qualities, and they praise your excellent deeds. So come to our sacrifice with all the gods.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The Kanwas invoke you, wise Agni, and extrol [sic] your deeds; come Agni with the gods,

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Kaṇvāḥ**: since the word *kaṇva* is read among the twenty-four names for the wise beginning with *vipra* (Ni. 3-19), *kaṇva* means wise, intelligent. Though the Bhāṣyakāra gives this general sense, since the ṛṣi of this Ṛk is of the Kaṇva line, it seems fitting to take *kaṇvāḥ* here as the sacrificers, priests and others born in the Kaṇva line.

**Dhiyaḥ**: since the word *dhīḥ* is read among the twenty-six words for action beginning with *apaḥ* (Ni. 3-2), *dhiyaḥ* means actions, deeds.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 589–592, noted briefly)*

**आ (*ā*)**: initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ". **त्वा (*tvā*)**: "tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-1-23 [as printed, for 8-1-23]): for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* in the accusative singular, after a word and not at the beginning of a pāda, the unaccented replacements *tvā* and *mā*; so the unaccented *tvā* for *tvām*.

### Page 590 — Rik 2: grammar (continued)

**कण्वाः (*kaṇvāḥ*)**: *kaṇa śabdārthe*; *kvan* by "aśūpruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan" (Uṇ. sū. "1-1-49" [as printed]). There are three roots *kaṇa*: *kaṇa bhāṣārthaḥ*, *kaṇa gatau*, *kaṇa nimīlane*; the commentators on the Tattvabodhinī and others take the *curādi* root *kaṇa nimīlane* here, but the Vedabhāṣyakāra holds that *kvan* may come after all three. The suffix is *nit*, so *kaṇvāḥ* is initial udātta.

**अहूषत (*ahūṣata*)**: *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; by "chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-6) these *lakāras* come in any time (past, future, present) when a relation of the root's sense is shown, so *luṅ* comes after *hveñ* in the present; *hve* + *l*; the *ñ* is *it*, so the root is *ñit*, and by "svaritañitaḥ kartrabhiprāye kriyāphale" (Pā. sū. 1-3-72) the *ātmanepada* comes when the fruit of the action goes to the agent; 3rd plural *jha*: *hve* + *jha*; *cli* by "cli luṅi" (Pā. sū. 3-1-43), *sic* for it by "cleḥ sic" (Pā. sū. 3-1-44): *hve* + *s* + *jha*. *Sic* is *ārdhadhātuka*, so "ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-35) would give *iṭ*; but *hve*, ending in a vowel, is not in the kārikā "ūdṛdantaiḥ…", so it is unaccented in *upadeśa*, and being one-syllabled there, "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" (Pā. sū. 7-2-10) bars the *iṭ*. With "hvaḥ samprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-32) carried on, "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-34) gives *saṃprasāraṇa*, *u* for the *v*: *hu* + *e* + *s* + *jha*; "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108) gives *pūrvarūpa* of *u* and *e*: *hu* + *s* + *jha*; "halaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-2): the final of a stem ending in a *saṃprasāraṇa* after a consonant is lengthened: *hū* + *s* + *jha* (this sense of "halaḥ" is given to bar lengthening in *utaḥ*, *nirutam*, *vidhyati*). "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5): *at* for the *jh*: *hūs* + *ata*; the augment *a* by "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍ udāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-71): *ahūs* + *ata*; *ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59): *ahūṣata*. Though *guṇa* of the *ū* would come by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84) because of *sic*, by the paribhāṣā

> सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्ते
>
> *sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyante*

*(Paribhāṣā 35)* it is optional in the Veda and does not come here. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ".

**गृणन्ति (*gṛṇanti*)**: *gṝ śabde*; "vartamāne laṭ" (Pā. sū. 3-2-123): *vartamāne* qualifies the sense of the stem; the suffix only marks it: *laṭ* after a root denoting a present action.

### Page 591 — Rik 2: grammar (continued)

The Bhāṣya has "bhūtabhaviṣyatoḥ pratidvandvī vartamānakālaḥ" (the present is the counterpart of past and future); some define the present as "atītānāgatabhinnakālatvaṃ vartamānakālatvam", the time other than past and future; others as "prārabdhāparisamāptakriyāśrayatvaṃ kālagataṃ vartamānatvam", the time that holds an action begun and not finished. By this sūtra *laṭ* after *gṝ*: *gṝ* + *l*; *parasmaipada* 3rd plural *jhi*; *ant* for *jh* by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-3): *gṝ* + *anti*; *śnā* by "kryādibhyaḥ śnā" (Pā. sū. 3-1-81): *gṝ* + *nā* + *anti*; the root shortened by "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-80): *gṛ* + *nā* + *anti*; "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-112): before a *kit* or *ṅit* suffix the *ā* of *śnā* and of a reduplicated stem drops; *śnā* is *ṅit* by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4): *gṛ* + *n* + *anti*; *ṇ* for *n* by "ṛvarṇāc ceti vaktavyam" (Pā. sū. 8-4-1 vā. 1): *gṛṇanti*. It follows the *tiṅanta* *ahūṣata*, so "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not make it wholly unaccented; *tiṅ* being a suffix, "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3) gives the initial udātta, so the *a* of *anti* is udātta.

**विप्र (*vipra*)**: a vocative; so by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. "1-19" [as printed, for 8-1-19]) wholly unaccented.

**ते (*te*)**: with "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (Pā. sū. 8-1-18) and "padāt" (Pā. sū. "8-11-7" [as printed, for 8-1-17]) carried on, "te mayāv ekavacanasya" (Pā. sū. 8-1-22) gives *te* and *me* for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* in the genitive singular, after a word and not at the beginning of a pāda, unaccented; so *te* for *tava*, unaccented.

**देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)**: no *ais* by "bahulaṃ chandasi".

**गहि (*gahi*)**: *gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau*; *loṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*: *gam* + *si*; *hi* for *si* by "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87), which by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) is *ṅit*; the *śap* of "kartari śap" is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73); "anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti" (Pā. sū. 6-4-37) drops the *m*. "asiddhavad atrābhāt" (Pā. sū. 6-4-22) is said to govern the rules up to the end of this pāda; so when "ato heḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-105) would drop the *hi*,

### Page 592 — Rik 2: grammar (end)

the loss of *m* by "anudāttopadeśa…" counts as not done, so *hi* does not stand after a stem ending in *a*, and is not dropped.

**॥२॥**

### Page 592 (lower) — Sūkta 14, Rik 3

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इ॒न्द्र॒वा॒यू बृह॒स्पतिं॑ मि॒त्राग्निं पू॒षणं॒ भग॑म् ।
> आ॒दि॒त्यान्मारु॑तं ग॒णम् ॥३॥
>
> *indravāyū́ bṛhaspátiṃ mitrā́gniṃ pūṣáṇaṃ bhágam |*
> *ādityā́n mā́rutaṃ gaṇám ||3||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> इन्द्रवायू इति । बृहस्पतिम् । मित्रा । अग्निम् । पूषणम् । भगम् ॥
> आदित्यान् । मारुतम् । गणम् ॥३॥
>
> *indravāyū iti | bṛhaspatim | mitrā | agnim | pūṣaṇam | bhagam ||*
> *ādityān | mārutam | gaṇam ||3||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> इन्द्रादिदेवान्मारुतं मरुतां वायूनां सम्बन्धिनं गणं च हे अग्ने यक्षीति पदद्वयमनुवर्तते ॥ इन्द्रश्च वायुश्चेन्द्रवायू । देवताद्वन्द्वे च । पा. ६-३-२६ । इति प्राप्तस्यानङ उभयत्र वायोः प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः । पा. ६-३-२६-१ । इति प्रतिषेधः । देवताद्वन्द्वे च । पा. ६-२-१४१ । इति प्राप्तस्योभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरस्य नोत्तरपदेऽनुदात्तादौ । पा. ६-२-१४२ । इति निषेधः । समासान्तोदात्तत्वमेव । बृहस्पतिं । तद्बृहतोः करपत्योश्चोरदेवतयोः सुट् तलोपश्च वक्तव्यः । म. ६-१-१५८ । इति तलोपः सुडागमश्च । बृहच्छब्दमाद्युदात्तं केचिद्वर्णयन्तीति वामनः । पा रक्षणे । पातीति पतिः । पातेर्डतिः । उ. ४-५८ । प्रत्ययस्वरेणाद्युदात्तः । समास उभे वनस्पत्यादिषु युगपत् । पा. ६-२-१४० । इत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । मित्रा । द्वितीयायाः सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराजादेशः । आदित्यान् । अदितेरपत्यान्यादित्याः । दित्यदित्यादित्यपत्युत्तरपदाण्ण्यः । पा. ४-१-८५ । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मारुतं । मरुतां विकारः । अनुदात्तादेश्च । पा. ४-३-१४० । इत्यञ् । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥
>
> *indrādidevānmārutaṃ marutāṃ vāyūnāṃ sambandhinaṃ gaṇaṃ ca he agne yakṣīti padadvayamanuvartate || indraśca vāyuścendravāyū | devatādvandve ca | pā. 6-3-26 | iti prāptasyānaṅa ubhayatra vāyoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ | pā. 6-3-26-1 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ | devatādvandve ca | pā. 6-2-141 | iti prāptasyobhayapadaprakṛtisvarasya nottarapade 'nudāttādau | pā. 6-2-142 | iti niṣedhaḥ | samāsāntodāttatvameva | bṛhaspatiṃ | tadbṛhatoḥ karapatyoścoradevatayoḥ suṭ talopaśca vaktavyaḥ | ma. 6-1-158 | iti talopaḥ suḍāgamaśca | bṛhacchabdamādyudāttaṃ kecidvarṇayantīti vāmanaḥ | pā rakṣaṇe | pātīti patiḥ | pāterḍatiḥ | u. 4-58 | pratyayasvareṇādyudāttaḥ | samāsa ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat | pā. 6-2-140 | ityubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | mitrā | dvitīyāyāḥ supāṃ sulugityādinā vibhakterājādeśaḥ | ādityān | aditerapatyānyādityāḥ | dityadityādityapatyuttarapadāṇṇyaḥ | pā. 4-1-85 | pratyayasvaraḥ | mārutaṃ | marutāṃ vikāraḥ | anudāttādeśca | pā. 4-3-140 | ityañ | ñittvādādyudāttaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "The two words *he agne yakṣi* ('O Agni, sacrifice') are carried on: [sacrifice to] Indra and the other gods, and to *mārutaṃ gaṇam*, the host belonging to the Maruts, the winds." (Grammatical tail: *indravāyū*, "Indra and Vāyu": the *ānaṅ* of Pā. 6-3-26 is barred for *vāyu* by its vārttika (6-3-26-1); the double accent of Pā. 6-2-141 is barred by Pā. 6-2-142, so the compound is final-udātta; *bṛhaspatim*: loss of *t* and the augment *s* by the statement on *tad*/*bṛhat* before *kara*/*pati* in the sense of thief/deity (MB. "6-1-158" as printed); Vāmana says some take *bṛhat* as initial-udātta; *pati* from *pā* 'to protect' with *ḍati* (Uṇ. 4-58), initial udātta; both members keep their accents by Pā. 6-2-140; *mitrā*, *ā* for the accusative ending by *supāṃ suluk…*; *ādityān*, "the sons of Aditi", *ṇya* by Pā. 4-1-85, the suffix accent; *mārutam*, "a product of the Maruts", *añ* by Pā. 4-3-140, initial udātta.)

### Page 593 — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

*(O Agni)* **इन्द्रवायू (indravāyū)** — Indra and Vāyu | **बृहस्पतिम् (bṛhaspatim)** — Bṛhaspati | **मित्रा (mitrā)** — Mitra | **अग्निम् (agnim)** — Agni | **पूषणम् (pūṣaṇam)** — Pūṣan | **भगम् (bhagam)** — Bhaga | **आदित्यान् (ādityān)** — the Ādityas | **मारुतं गणम् (mārutaṃ gaṇam)** — the hosts of the Maruts, having them in view | *(yakṣi — sacrifice)*.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, sacrifice with these in view: Indra, Vāyu, Bṛhaspati, Mitra, Agni, Pūṣan, Bhaga, the Ādityas (or the gods) and the hosts of the Maruts.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Sacrifice to Indra, Vayu, Brihaspati, Mitra, Agni, Pushan, Bhaga, the Adityas. [sic] and the hosts of Maruts.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

Since this Ṛk has no verb, the Bhāṣyakāra says the words *agne yakṣi*, "O Agni, sacrifice", are to be supplied. But Agni is in this group too, so it does not seem fitting to address Agni and say "sacrifice to Agni". For this reason the author of the Vedārthayatna supplies the two words *ahaṃ hvaye*, "I invoke", that is, "I invoke the deities Indra, Vāyu and the rest".

**Indravāyū**: *indraś ca vāyuś ca indravāyū*, a *devatā-dvandva*: the two deities Indra and Vāyu are named by a single word in the dual.

**Mitrā**: here the word has the sense of the accusative singular.

**Ādityān**: *aditer apatyāny ādityāḥ*: the children of Aditi, the mother of the gods, are called Ādityas; it means the gods, or the twelve Ādityas.

**Mārutam**: the last syllable of the genitive plural *mārutām* is shortened to suit the metre.

### Page 594 — Rik 3: Special Topics (end) and grammar

**Mārutaṃ gaṇam**: the host of the Marut deities. The Purāṇas and other works say there are seven Maruts (the seven Marut hosts). In the Ṛgveda too the word *marut* is generally used in the plural. *Mārutaṃ gaṇam* means the group, the host of the Marut deities.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 594–596, noted briefly)*

**इन्द्रवायू (*indravāyū*)**: *indraś ca vāyuś ca*, a dvandva. By "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-26), in a dvandva of words denoting deities, the first member before the second takes the replacement *ānaṅ*; *indra* and *vāyu* denote deities, so *ānaṅ* would come for *indra* before *vāyu*; but by the vārttika "ubhayatra vāyoḥ pratiṣedho vaktavyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-26-1), whether *vāyu* is the first or the second member, *ānaṅ* is barred in that dvandva. By "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-2-141) both members of a deity dvandva keep their own accents at once: *indra* ends in the suffix *ran* and is initial udātta; *vāyu* ends in *uṇ* and is final udātta by the suffix accent. But "nottarapade 'nudāttādāv apṛthivīrudrapūṣamanthiṣu" (Pā. sū. 6-2-142) bars that accent when the second member, other than *pṛthivī* and the rest, begins with an unaccented syllable; so the double accent does not come; by "samāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-223) the compound is final udātta, and the other syllables are unaccented by the *śeṣanighāta*.

**बृहस्पतिम् (*bṛhaspatim*)**: *bṛhatī* means speech; *bṛhatyāḥ patiḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*. For *bṛhatī* before *pati*, by "kukkuṭyādīnām aṇḍādiṣu" (Pā. sū. 6-3-42-1 vā.) the *puṃvadbhāva* comes (feminines like *kukkuṭī* before *aṇḍa* and the like), and the *ṅīp* goes: *bṛhat* + *pati*. Then "tadbṛhatoḥ karapatyoś coradevatayoḥ suṭ talopaś ca" ("ga. sū. 6-1-158" [as printed]): for *tad* and *bṛhat* before *kara* and *pati*, the *d*/*t* drops and *kara*/*pati* take the augment *suṭ*; *suṭ* is *ṭit*, so by "ādyantau ṭakitau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-46) it comes at the beginning of *pati*: *bṛhaspati*. The Mahābhāṣyakāra has rejected the reading "kukkuṭyādīnām aṇḍādiṣu"

### Page 595 — Rik 3: grammar (continued)

on that view the analysis is *bṛhataḥ vāksamūhasya patiḥ*. The analysis *bṛhatyāḥ patiḥ* follows the Chandoga-brāhmaṇa *vāg vai bṛhatī, tasyā eṣa patiḥ*. Vāmana holds that some say *bṛhat* is initial udātta; so *bṛhat* is initial udātta. *Pā rakṣaṇe*: *pātīti patiḥ* (the protector); "pāter ḍatiḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 4-58): the suffix *ḍati* after *pā*: *pā* + *ati*; since the suffix is *ḍit*, the *ā* (the *ṭi*) of *pā* drops: *p* + *ati* = *pati*. By the suffix accent "ādyudāttaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-3) it is initial udātta; when the two are compounded, "ubhe vanaspatyādiṣu yugapat" (Pā. sū. 6-2-140) keeps the own accent of both members. The *a* of *bṛhat* takes the *anudāttatara* accent by "udāttasvaritaparasya sannataraḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-2-40).

**मित्रा (*mitrā*)**: *mitra* is final udātta by the stem accent; accusative singular *am*; "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39) gives *āc* for it: *mitra* + *ā*, lengthening of like vowels; the single replacement is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-5).

**आदित्यान् (*ādityān*)**: *aditeḥ apatyāni pumāṃsaḥ ādityāḥ*. "dityadityādityapatyuttarapadāṇ ṇyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-1-85): in the senses beginning with *apatya* set out in the Aṣṭādhyāyī from this sūtra to "tena dīvyati khanati jayati jitam" (Pā. sū. 4-4-2), the suffix *ṇya* comes after *diti*, *aditi*, *āditya* and words with *pati* as the second member; so *ṇya* after the genitive of *aditi*: *aditi* + *jas* [as printed, for *ṅas*] + *ya*; ending in a *taddhita*, it is a *prātipadika*, the ending is dropped: *aditi* + *ya*; the *i* drops by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148); initial *vṛddhi* by "taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-117): *āditya*. It is final udātta by the suffix accent; accusative plural *śas*, *pūrvasavarṇa-dīrgha*, *n* for the *s* by "tasmāc chaso naḥ puṃsi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-103); the single replacement is udātta: *ādityān*.

**मारुतम् (*mārutam*)**: "mṛgror utiḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 1-94): after *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge* and *gṝ nigaraṇe* the suffix *uti*: *mṛ* + *uti*, *guṇa* and *raparatva*; the *u* is udātta by the suffix accent and the *a* unaccented by the *śeṣanighāta*, so *marut* begins with an unaccented syllable. *Marutāṃ vikāraḥ*: by "anudāttādeś ca" (Pā. sū. 4-1-84 [as printed, for 4-3-140]), after the genitive of a word beginning with an unaccented syllable, in the senses of product and part,

### Page 596 — Rik 3: grammar (end)

the suffix *añ*: *marut* + *a*, initial *vṛddhi*: *māruta*. The suffix is *ñit*, so by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) *māruta* is initial udātta.

**॥३॥**

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्रादिदेवा वो युष्मदर्थमिन्दवः सोमाः प्र भ्रियन्ते । प्रकर्षेण सम्पाद्यन्ते । कीदृशाः । मत्सरास्तृप्तिकराः । मत्सरः सोमो मन्दतेस्तृप्तिकर्मणः । नि. २-५ । इति यास्कः । मादयिष्णवो हर्षहेतवो द्रप्सा बिन्दुरूपा मध्वो मधुराश्चमूषदश्चमूषु चमसादिपात्रेष्ववस्थिताः ॥ प्र । व्यवहिताश्च । पा. १-४-८२ । इति व्यवहितप्रयोगः । भ्रियन्ते । भृञो यकि रिङ् शयग्लिङ्क्षु । पा. ७-४-२८ । इति रिङादेशः । हृञो वा । हृग्रहोर्भश्छन्दसीति हकारस्य भकारः । इन्दवः । उन्दी क्लेदने । उन्दन्ति पात्राणीति । नित्यनुवृत्तावुन्देरिच्चादेः । उ. १-१२ । इत्युप्रत्यय आदेरिकारश्च । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । मत्सराः । मद तृप्तियोगे । चिदित्यनुवृत्तौ कृधूमदिभ्यः कित् । उ. ३-७३ । इति सरप्रत्ययः । तितुत्रतथसिसुसरकसेषु चेतीट्प्रतिषेधः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । मादयिष्णवः । मदी हर्षग्लपनयोः । मदेर्ण्यन्ताच्छन्दसि । पा. ३-२-१३८ । इतीष्णुच् । णेरनिटीति णिलोपे प्राप्तेऽयामन्ताल्वाय्येत्न्विष्णुषु । पा. ६-४-५५ । इत्ययादेशः । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तः । मध्वः । मधुशब्द आद्युदात्त उक्तः । मधुशब्दस्य व्यत्ययेन पुंलिङ्गत्वं । संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनि-

### Page 597 — Rik 4: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

> -त्य इति जसि च । पा. ७-३-१०९ । इति गुणो न भवति । चमूषदः । चमु छमु जमु झमु अदने । चम्यते भक्ष्यते येषु चमसेषु ते चम्वः । कृषिचमीत्यादिना । उ. १-८२ । ऊः । तत्र सीदन्तीति चमूषदः । सत्सूद्विषेत्यादिना । पा. ३-२-६१ । क्विप् । सुषामादेराकृतिगणत्वात्षत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥
>
> *-tya iti jasi ca | pā. 7-3-109 | iti guṇo na bhavati | camūṣadaḥ | camu chamu jamu jhamu adane | camyate bhakṣyate yeṣu camaseṣu te camvaḥ | kṛṣicamītyādinā | u. 1-82 | ūḥ | tatra sīdantīti camūṣadaḥ | satsūdviṣetyādinā | pā. 3-2-61 | kvip | suṣāmāderākṛtigaṇatvātṣatvaṃ | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra and the other gods, for you the *indavaḥ*, the soma juices, *pra bhriyante*, are well prepared. Of what kind? *Matsarāḥ*, causing satisfaction ('*matsara* is soma, from *mand*, a root of satisfaction', Yāska, Ni. 2-5); *mādayiṣṇavaḥ*, causes of delight; *drapsāḥ*, in the form of drops; *madhvaḥ*, sweet; *camūṣadaḥ*, resting in the *camūs*, the vessels such as the *camasa*." (Grammatical tail: *pra* separated from its verb by Pā. 1-4-82; *bhriyante*, *riṅ* by Pā. 7-4-28, or from *hṛ* with *bh* for *h* in the Veda; *indavaḥ* from *und* with *u* and *i* for the initial (Uṇ. 1-12), initial udātta; *matsarāḥ* from *mad* with *sara* (Uṇ. 3-73), no *iṭ*, final udātta (*cit*); *mādayiṣṇavaḥ* with *iṣṇuc* (Pā. 3-2-138), *ay* for the *ṇi* (Pā. 6-4-55), final udātta; *madhvaḥ*, *madhu* masculine by *vyatyaya*, no *guṇa* before *jas* (Pā. 7-3-109) by the paribhāṣā *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*; *camūṣadaḥ*, *camū* (Uṇ. 1-82) + *sad* with *kvip* (Pā. 3-2-61), *ṣ* by the *suṣāmādi* class, the accent of the *kṛt* second member.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

*(O Indra and the other deities)* **वः (vaḥ)** — for you | **मत्सराः (matsarāḥ)** — giving satisfaction | **मादयिष्णवः (mādayiṣṇavaḥ)** — giving delight | **द्रप्साः (drapsāḥ)** — in the form of drops | **मध्वः (madhvaḥ)** — sweet | **चमूषदः (camūṣadaḥ)** — that are in the *camasa* vessels | **इन्दवः (indavaḥ)** — the soma juices | **प्र भ्रियन्ते (pra bhriyante)** — are being well prepared.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra and the other gods, for you the soma juices, sweet, giving you delight and satisfaction, in the form of drops, are being gathered, or prepared.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> For you (gods) are poured out these (soma) jnices [sic], satisfying, exhilarat-ing› [sic] sweet, falling in drops or standing in the cup.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Matsarāḥ**:

> सोमो मन्दतेस्तृप्तिकर्मणः
>
> *somo mandatestṛptikarmaṇaḥ*

*(Ni. 2-5.)* Since it causes delight, the soma juice is called *matsara*.

**Mādayiṣṇavaḥ**: the word is formed from the root *madī harṣaglapanayoḥ*, and means "causing delight".

**Drapsāḥ**: *bindurūpāḥ*, in the form of drops: when the soma creeper is crushed and pressed, the juice trickles and falls drop by drop, so it is called drop-like.

**Camūṣadaḥ**:

> चम्यते भक्ष्यते येषु चमसेषु ते चम्वः
>
> *camyate bhakṣyate yeṣu camaseṣu te camvaḥ*

("the *camasas* in which it is eaten are the *camūs*"): that are in the sacrificial vessel called *camasa*. The vessel for eating or drinking is called *camasa*; that is the derivation of the word. The soma juice in such a vessel.

### Page 598 — Rik 4: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 598–599, noted briefly)*

**प्र (*pra*)**: by "vyavahitāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-82) the *upasargas* may be used separated from the verb in the Veda, so it is used separated here.

**भ्रियन्ते (*bhriyante*)**: *bhṛ bharaṇe* or *ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *laṭ* in the passive; by "bhāvakarmaṇoḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-3-13) the *ātmanepada* for a *lakāra* in the impersonal or passive sense; 3rd plural *jha*: *bhṛ* + *jha*; "sārvadhātuke yak" (Pā. sū. 3-1-67) gives *yak* before a *sārvadhātuka* in those senses: *bhṛ* + *ya* + *jha*; *e* for the *ṭi* by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); *ant* for *jh* by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-3): *bhṛ* + *ya* + *ante*; "riṅ śayagliṅkṣu" (Pā. sū. 7-4-28): before *śa*, *yak* and a *y*-initial *ārdhadhātuka liṅ*, *riṅ* for a short *ṛ*: *bhriyante*; *yak* is *kit*, so no *guṇa*. Or from *hṛñ haraṇe* in the passive, *hriyante* as above, and *bh* for *h* by "hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi" (Pā. sū. 8-2-32-1): *bhriyante*.

**इन्दवः (*indavaḥ*)**: *undī kledane*; *undanti pātrāṇi* (they wet the vessels): *indavaḥ*. "under ic cādeḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 1-12): the suffix *u* after *und*, *nit*, and *i* for the initial *u*: *indu*; initial udātta (*nit*).

**मत्सराः (*matsarāḥ*)**: *mada tṛptiyoge* (*curādi*); "kṛdhūmadibhyaḥ kit" (Uṇ. sū. "3-73" [?]; *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, *dhūñ kampane*, *mada tṛptiyoge*): the suffix *sara*, *kit* and *cit*. Though *ārdhadhātuka*, it takes no *iṭ* by "titutratathasisusarakaseṣu ca" (Pā. sū. 7-2-9); final udātta by "citaḥ".

**मादयिष्णवः (*mādayiṣṇavaḥ*)**: *madī harṣaglapanayoḥ*; *ṇic* by "hetumati ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-26); "ṇeś chandasi" (Pā. sū. 3-2-138 [as printed]) gives *iṣṇuc* in the Veda after a *ṇic*-ending root in the senses of habit and the like: *mad* + *i* + *iṣṇu*; "ṇer aniṭi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-51) would drop the *ṇi*, but "ayāmantālvāyyetnviṣṇuṣu" (Pā. sū. 6-4-55)

### Page 599 — Rik 4: grammar (end)

gives *ay* for *ṇi* before *ām*, *anta*, *ālu*, *āyya*, *itnu*, *iṣṇu*: *mad* + *ay* + *iṣṇu*; *vṛddhi* of the penultimate; nominative plural *mādayiṣṇavaḥ*; final udātta by the *cit* accent.

**मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)**: in Sūkta 13, Ṛk 2 the word *madhu* was said to be initial udātta. *Madhu* is neuter, but here masculine by *vyatyaya*. Before *jas*, "jasi ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-109) would give *guṇa* to an *ik*-final stem; but it comes naming the technical term *guṇa*, so by "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" (paribhāṣā 93) it is optional, and does not come here.

**चमूषदः (*camūṣadaḥ*)**: *camu chamu jamu jhamu adane*; "kṛṣicamitanidhanisarjikharjibhya ūḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "1-81" [?]; *kṛṣa vilekhane*, *camu adane*, *tanu vistāre*, *dhana dhānye*, *sarja sarjane*, *kharja vyathane*) gives *ū* after *cam*: *camū*; *camyate bhakṣyate yeṣu camaseṣu te* (the vessels in which it is eaten); *camvaḥ camūṣu sīdantīti camūṣadaḥ*. "satsūdviṣadruhaduhayujavidabhidacchidajinīrājām upasarge 'pi kvip" (Pā. sū. 3-2-61): after *ṣadḷ viśaraṇādau*, *ṣūṅ prāṇigarbhavimocane*, *dviṣa aprītau*, *druha jighāṃsāyām*, *duha prapūraṇe*, *yujir yoge*, *yuja samādhau*, *vida jñāne*, *vida vicāraṇe*, *vida sattāyām*, *chidir dvaidhīkaraṇe*, *bhidir vidāraṇe*, *ji jaye*, *ṇīñ prāpaṇe*, *rājṛ dīptau*, with or without an *upasarga*, when there is a suitable *upapada*, *kvip* comes; so *kvip* after *sad* with the *upapada* *camū*: *camūsad*; by "suṣāmādiṣu ca" (Pā. sū. 8-3-98) the *s* of words in the *suṣāmādi* class becomes *ṣ*; that class is an *ākṛtigaṇa*, and this word belongs to it. By "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) the *kṛt* second member keeps its accent, final udātta by the root accent; *jas* after it is unaccented and becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya".

**॥४॥**

> ईळ॑ते॒ त्वाम॑व॒स्यवः॒ कण्वा॑सो वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः ।
> ह॒विष्म॑न्तो अ॒रं॒कृतः॑ ॥५॥ [accent ?]

> *ī́ḷate tvā́m avasyávaḥ káṇvāso vṛktábarhiṣaḥ |*

### Page 600 — Rik 5: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ईळते । त्वाम् । अवस्यवः । कण्वासः । वृक्तऽबर्हिषः ॥
> हविष्मन्तः । अरम्ऽकृतः ॥५॥
>
> *īḷate | tvām | avasyavaḥ | kaṇvāsaḥ | vṛkta 'barhiṣaḥ ||*
> *haviṣmantaḥ | aram 'kṛtaḥ ||5||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वामीळते । ऋत्विजः स्तुवन्ति । कीदृशाः । अवस्यवः । अवनं रक्षणं तद्धेतून्देवानिच्छन्तः । कण्वासो मेधाविनो वृक्तबर्हिष आस्तरणार्थं छिन्नदर्भा हविष्मन्तो हविर्युक्ता अरंकृतो ऽलंकर्तारः ॥ ईळते । ईड स्तुतौ । अनुदात्तेत्त्वाल्लटो झः । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । झस्यादादेशः । टेरेत्वं । तास्यनुदात्तेदित्यादिना लसार्वधातुकस्यानुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । अवस्यवः । अवन्तीत्यवा देवाः । तानतिशयेनेच्छन्ति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । क्यचि च । पा. ७-४-३३ । इतीत्वं न भवति । न छन्दस्यपुत्रस्य । पा. ७-४-३५ । इति निषेधात् । सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यो लालसायां सुग्वक्तव्यः । म. ७-१-५१-२ । इति सुक् । क्याच्छन्दसीत्युप्रत्ययः । अतो लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तत्वं । कण्वासः । कण शब्दार्थः । कणन्ति ध्वनन्ति स्तोत्रादिपाठेनेति कण्वा ऋत्विजः । अशिप्रुषीत्यादिना क्वन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । आज्जसेरसुक् । पा. ७-१-५० । इत्यसुक् । वृक्तबर्हिषः । वृक्तमुक्तं । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । हविष्मन्तः । हविरेषामस्तीति हविष्मन्तः । तसौ मत्वर्थ इति भत्वेनापदत्वान्न रुत्वं । अरंकृतः । अलंकुर्वन्तीत्यरंकृतः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । ह्रस्वस्य तुक् । कपिलकादीनां संज्ञाछन्दसोर्वा लो रत्वमापद्यते । पा. ८-२-१८-३ । इति लकारस्य रेफादेशः ॥
>
> *he agne tvāmīḷate | ṛtvijaḥ stuvanti | kīdṛśāḥ | avasyavaḥ | avanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ taddhetūndevānicchantaḥ | kaṇvāso medhāvino vṛktabarhiṣa āstaraṇārthaṃ chinnadarbhā haviṣmanto haviryuktā araṃkṛto 'laṃkartāraḥ || īḷate | īḍa stutau | anudāttettvāllaṭo jhaḥ | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | jhasyādādeśaḥ | ṭeretvaṃ | tāsyanudāttedityādinā lasārvadhātukasyānudāttatvāddhātusvara eva śiṣyate | avasyavaḥ | avantītyavā devāḥ | tānatiśayenecchanti | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | kyaci ca | pā. 7-4-33 | itītvaṃ na bhavati | na chandasyaputrasya | pā. 7-4-35 | iti niṣedhāt | sarvaprātipadikebhyo lālasāyāṃ sugvaktavyaḥ | ma. 7-1-51-2 | iti suk | kyācchandasītyupratyayaḥ | ato lopaḥ | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttatvaṃ | kaṇvāsaḥ | kaṇa śabdārthaḥ | kaṇanti dhvananti stotrādipāṭheneti kaṇvā ṛtvijaḥ | aśipruṣītyādinā kvan | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | ājjaserasuk | pā. 7-1-50 | ityasuk | vṛktabarhiṣaḥ | vṛktamuktaṃ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | haviṣmantaḥ | havireṣāmastīti haviṣmantaḥ | tasau matvartha iti bhatvenāpadatvānna rutvaṃ | araṃkṛtaḥ | alaṃkurvantītyaraṃkṛtaḥ | kvipceti kvip | hrasvasya tuk | kapilakādīnāṃ saṃjñāchandasorvā lo ratvamāpadyate | pā. 8-2-18-3 | iti lakārasya rephādeśaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni, the priests *īḷate*, praise, you. What are they like? *Avasyavaḥ*: desiring the gods, who are the cause of *avana*, protection; *kaṇvāsaḥ*, wise; *vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*, having cut the *darbha* for spreading; *haviṣmantaḥ*, having the oblation; *araṅkṛtaḥ*, adorners." (Grammatical tail: *īḷate* from *īḍ*, *ātmanepada* (*anudātta*-marked root), *śap* dropped, *at* for *jh*, *e* for the *ṭi*, the root accent; *avasyavaḥ*: *avāḥ* are the gods, who protect, "they desire them greatly": *kyac*, no *ī* (Pā. 7-4-33 barred by Pā. 7-4-35), the augment *s* by the vārttika on *lālasā* (MB 7-1-51-2), *u* by *kyāc chandasi*, the *a* dropped, final udātta; *kaṇvāsaḥ* from *kaṇ* with *kvan*, initial udātta, *asuk* by Pā. 7-1-50; *vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*, a bahuvrīhi, first-member accent; *haviṣmantaḥ*, no *ru* (*bha* status); *araṅkṛtaḥ* with *kvip*, *tuk*, and *r* for the *l* of *alam* by the vārttika on *kapilakādi* (Pā. 8-2-18-3).)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

*(O Agni)* **अवस्यवः (avasyavaḥ)** — seeking the help of the gods who protect | **वृक्तबर्हिषः (vṛkta-barhiṣaḥ)** — having *darbha* made ready (for the seat) | **हविष्मन्तः (haviṣmantaḥ)** — holding the oblation | **अरंकृतः (araṅkṛtaḥ)** — offering ornaments | **कण्वासः (kaṇvāsaḥ)** — the priests, who are wise, or of the line of the ṛṣi Kaṇva | **त्वाम् (tvām)** — you | **ईळते (īḷate)** — praise.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, the priests seek the help of the gods for the protection of their sacrifice. They are skilled at praising. It is you who call the gods, so they now praise you. They have made the *darbha* ready for your seat. They offer the oblation and ornaments. Be gracious and come.

### Page 601 — Rik 5: English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Agni, the Kanvas (or the wise priests) desirous of your favour, having spread the sacrificial grass and carrying the oblations and ornaments are praising you.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Avasyavaḥ**:

> अवनं रक्षणं तद्धेतून् देवानिच्छन्तः । अवन्तीत्यवा देवाः ॥
>
> *avanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ taddhetūn devānicchantaḥ | avantītyavā devāḥ ||*

Since they protect men, the gods are called *avāḥ*; those who look to those gods are called *avasyavaḥ*.

**Kaṇvāsaḥ**: the plural of the word *kaṇva*; *kaṇvāsaḥ* is the old form of *kaṇvāḥ*.

> कणन्ति ध्वनन्ति स्तोत्रादिपाठेनेति कण्वा ऋत्विजो मेधाविनः ॥
>
> *kaṇanti dhvananti stotrādipāṭheneti kaṇvā ṛtvijo medhāvinaḥ ||*

Since they recite hymns and the like aloud, the priests are called *kaṇvāḥ*. The Bhāṣyakāra gives the word the sense *medhāvinaḥ*, the wise. Besides the sense that comes from the derivation of its parts, another sense can be given: since the ṛṣi of this Ṛk is of the Kaṇva line, it is fitting to say that, speaking of the priests, sacrificers and others of his line, he used the word *kaṇvāsaḥ* with the sense "we of the line of the ṛṣi Kaṇva" in mind.

**Vṛktabarhiṣaḥ**: we have given the explanation of this word on page "25" [?].

**Araṅkṛtaḥ**: for the explanation of this word see Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 1, page "677" [?].

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 601–603, noted briefly)*

**ईळते (*īḷate*)**: *īḍa stutau*, *anudāttet*, so the *ātmanepada* by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. sū. 1-3-12); 3rd plural *jha*; the *śap* of "kartari śap" is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72); *at* for the *jh* by "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5); *e* for the *ṭi* by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); *ḷ* for the *ḍ* of *īḍate* by "dvayoś cāsya svarayoḥ"; by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam ahnviṅoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186) the *sārvadhātuka* *ate* standing for the *lakāra* is unaccented, and the root accent remains.

**अवस्यवः (*avasyavaḥ*)**: *avanti rakṣanti ity avāḥ = devāḥ*; *ava rakṣaṇe* with *ac*; *avān atiśayena icchanti*. "supa ātmanaḥ kyac" (Pā. sū. 3-1-8) gives *kyac*.

### Page 602 — Rik 5: grammar (continued)

"na chandasy aputrasya" (Pā. sū. 7-4-35) bars in the Veda the *ī* and the lengthening before *kyac* for *a*-final words other than *putra*; so neither "kyaci ca" (Pā. sū. 7-4-33, *ī* for *a* before *kyac*) nor, by the same bar, the lengthening of "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. "7-4-2?" [?]) comes. "sarvaprātipadikebhyo lālasāyāṃ sug vaktavyaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-51 vā. 2): when eagerness is shown, all stems before *kyac* take the augment *suk*: *avas* + *ya*; "kyāc chandasi" (Pā. sū. 3-2-170): *kya* covers *kyac*, *kyaṅ* and *kyaṣ* alike; after a *kya*-ending root the suffix *u* comes in the Veda in the senses of habit and the like, so the Kāśikākāra holds; some hold that by the force of the explanation the word *kya* also takes in the *kaṇḍvādi* *yak*. With *u*: *avasya* + *u*; "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-48) drops the *a*: *avasyu*; final udātta by the suffix accent; nominative plural *avasyavaḥ*.

**कण्वासः (*kaṇvāsaḥ*)**: *kaṇa śabdārthaḥ*; *kaṇanti dhvananti stotrādipāṭhena* (they make sound by reciting hymns and the like) *iti kaṇvāḥ ṛtvijaḥ*. "aśūpruṣilaṭikaṇikhaṭiviśibhyaḥ kvan" (Uṇ. sū. 1-149) gives *kvan* after *kaṇ*; then *jas*, and "ājjaser asuk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-50) gives the augment *as*: *kaṇvāsaḥ*.

**वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)**: the formation of *vṛkta* is set out in Sū. "12" [?] Ṛk 3; *vṛkta* is final udātta by the suffix accent. *Vṛktāni barhīṃṣi yeṣāṃ te*: a bahuvrīhi; by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the first member keeps its accent.

**हविष्मन्तः (*haviṣmantaḥ*)**: *haviḥ eṣām asti iti*; *matup* after *havis* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. sū. 5-2-94); *ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59); *jas*; *num* by "ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-70); *havis* is *bha* by "tasau matvarthe" (Pā. sū. 1-4-19), which bars the *pada* status, so the *s* does not become *ru*.

**अरंकृतः (*araṅkṛtaḥ*)**: *alaṃkurvanti ity araṅkṛtaḥ*; with the *subanta* *alam* as *upapada*, *kvip* after *kṛñ* by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76),

### Page 603 — Rik 5: grammar (end)

and the *kvip* drops. By *pratyayalakṣaṇa* the *kvip* still counts as following, so "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk" (Pā. sū. 6-1-71) gives the augment *tuk*, which, being *kit*, comes at the end by "ādyantau ṭakitau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-46). "kapilakādīnāṃ saṃjñāchandasor vā lo ratvam āpadyate" (Pā. sū. ma. 8-2-18): in names and in the Veda the *l* of words in the *kapilakādi* class becomes *r* optionally, so the *l* of *alam* becomes *r*; *kapilakādi* is an *ākṛtigaṇa*, and *alam* belongs to it. The Mahābhāṣya here has

> वालमूललघ्वलमङ्गुलीनां वा लो रत्वमापद्यते
>
> *vālamūlalaghvalamaṅgulīnāṃ vā lo ratvamāpadyate*

*(MB 8-2-18-2)*: the *l* of *vāla*, *mūla*, *laghu*, *alam*, *aṅguli* becomes *r* optionally; examples: *aśvavāraḥ*/*aśvavālaḥ*, *mūradevaḥ*/*mūladevaḥ*, *laghusyadaḥ*/*raghusyadaḥ*, *alambhaktāya*/*arambhaktāya*, *svaṅguliḥ*/*svaṅguriḥ*; and then the statement *saṃjñāchandasor vā kapilakādīnām*, with the examples *kapirakaḥ*/*kapilakaḥ*, *tilvilikam*/*tirvirikam*, *kalmaṣam*/*karmaṣam*, *romāṇi*/*lomāni*, *pāṃsulam*/*pāṃsuram*, *karma*/*kalma*, *śukraḥ*/*śuklaḥ*. The Kaiyaṭakāra says *kapilakādiṣu vāraśyalaḥ*: for the *r* of the *kapilakādi* words *l* comes optionally. On this the Uddyota has

> पूर्ववाक्येन लस्य रत्वं प्रोक्तम् अनेन रस्य लो वेत्यर्थः
>
> *pūrvavākyena lasya ratvaṃ proktam anena rasya lo vetyarthaḥ*

that is, by the earlier statement *vāla-mūla…* the *r* for the *l* is laid down optionally, and by this statement the *l* for the *r* optionally. So, following the reading of Kaiyaṭa and the Uddyotakāra, it is fitting to say that here the *r* for the *l* comes by *vālamūla…*.

**॥५॥**

### Page 604 — Rik 6: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वा त्वां ये ऽश्वा रथेन वहन्ति । कीदृशाः । घृतपृष्ठाः । पुष्टाङ्गत्वेन दीप्तपृष्ठा मनोयुजो मनःसंकल्पमात्रेण रथे युज्यमाना वह्नयो वोढारः । तैरश्वैः सोमपीतये सोमपानयागार्थं देवाना वहेति शेषः ॥ घृतपृष्ठाः । घृ क्षरणदीप्त्योः । घृतं दीप्तं पृष्ठं येषां ते घृतपृष्ठाः । घृतशब्दः प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । मनसा युञ्जत इति मनोयुजः । ऋत्विग्दधृगित्यादिना क्विन् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । त्वा । त्वामौ द्वितीयाया इत्यनुदात्तस्त्वादेशः । वहन्ति । शप्तिपोरनुदात्तत्वाद्धातुस्वरः । यद्वृत्तयोगान्निघाताभावः । वह्नयः । निरित्यनुवृत्तौ वहिश्रिश्रुयुद्रुग्लाहात्वरिभ्यो नित् । उ. ४-५१ । इति निप्रत्ययः । तस्य नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । सोमपीतये । उक्तं । सकारे परतो नकारस्य संहितायां नश्च । पा. ८-३-३० । इति धुडागमः । खरि च । पा. ८-४-५५ । इति चर्त्वं । चयो द्वितीयाः शरि पौष्करसादेः । पा. ८-४-४८-३ । इति द्वितीयस्थकारः ॥ २६ ॥
>
> *he agne tvā tvāṃ ye 'śvā rathena vahanti | kīdṛśāḥ | ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ | puṣṭāṅgatvena dīptapṛṣṭhā manoyujo manaḥsaṃkalpamātreṇa rathe yujyamānā vahnayo voḍhāraḥ | tairaśvaiḥ somapītaye somapānayāgārthaṃ devānā vaheti śeṣaḥ || ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ | ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ | ghṛtaṃ dīptaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ yeṣāṃ te ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ | ghṛtaśabdaḥ pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | manasā yuñjata iti manoyujaḥ | ṛtvigdadhṛgityādinā kvin | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | tvā | tvāmau dvitīyāyā ityanudāttastvādeśaḥ | vahanti | śaptiporanudāttatvāddhātusvaraḥ | yadvṛttayogānnighātābhāvaḥ | vahnayaḥ | nirityanuvṛttau vahiśriśruyudruglāhātvaribhyo nit | u. 4-51 | iti nipratyayaḥ | tasya nittvādādyudāttatvaṃ | somapītaye | uktaṃ | sakāre parato nakārasya saṃhitāyāṃ naśca | pā. 8-3-30 | iti dhuḍāgamaḥ | khari ca | pā. 8-4-55 | iti cartvaṃ | cayo dvitīyāḥ śari pauṣkarasādeḥ | pā. 8-4-48-3 | iti dvitīyasthakāraḥ || 26 ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni, the horses that draw you by chariot: what are they like? *Ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ*, with shining backs, being well fed; *manoyujaḥ*, yoked to the chariot by a mere resolve of the mind; *vahnayaḥ*, bearers: with those horses bring the gods for the *somapīti*, the sacrifice with the drinking of soma; 'bring' is understood." (Grammatical tail: *ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ*, "whose back is *ghṛta*, shining", from *ghṛ* 'to shine', *ghṛta* final udātta, a bahuvrīhi with the first-member accent; *manoyujaḥ*, "yoked by the mind", *kvin*, the accent of the *kṛt* second member; *tvā* unaccented; *vahanti*, the root accent, not lowered because of the relative *ye*; *vahnayaḥ* with *ni* (Uṇ. 4-51), initial udātta; *somapītaye* as before; in the Saṃhitā the augment *dh* (Pā. 8-3-30), *t* by *khari ca* (Pā. 8-4-55), *th* by the vārttika of Pauṣkarasādi (8-4-48-3). The closing "26" is the varga number.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

*(O Agni)* **घृतपृष्ठाः (ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ)** — whose backs, being well fed, are smooth like ghee | **मनोयुजः (manoyujaḥ)** — that join (the chariot) by a mere resolve | **वह्नयः (vahnayaḥ)** — able to draw | **ये (ye)** — the horses that | **त्वा (tvā)** — you | **वहन्ति (vahanti)** — draw along | *(by those horses)* **सोमपीतये (somapītaye)** — for drinking soma | **देवान् (devān)** — the gods | **आ (वह) (ā (vaha))** — bring.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, the backs of the horses that seat you in the chariot and bring you to the place of sacrifice shine, being well fed. They can join the chariot by a mere resolve; they are able to draw it. On them bring the gods for the drinking of soma.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> By means of horses which have backs as soft and smooth as clarified butter which harnessing themselves promptly according to your wish, carry you and the gods hither to drink soma-juice.

### Page 605 — Rik 6: Special Topics and grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ**: we explained this word in the fifth Ṛk of the preceding sūkta (page 549). Here the word qualifies *vahnayaḥ*, so the sense differs a little: with backs soft or smooth as ghee, "backs as smooth as clarifed [sic] butter".

**Vahnayaḥ**:

> वोढारः अश्वा इत्यर्थः
>
> *voḍhāraḥ aśvā ityarthaḥ*

Since they draw the chariot, the horses are called *vahnayaḥ*.

**Manoyujaḥ**: yoked to the chariot by a mere resolve of Agni's mind;

> मनसा युञ्जते इति मनोयुजः
>
> *manasā yuñjate iti manoyujaḥ*

is the derivation.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 605–607, noted briefly)*

**घृतपृष्ठाः (*ghṛtapṛṣṭhāḥ*)**: final udātta by the suffix accent; the initial udātta that its exception "nabviṣayasyānisantasya" (Phi. sū. 26) would give is overridden by "ghṛtādīnāṃ ca" (Phi. sū. 21), so *ghṛta* is final udātta. *Ghṛ kṣaraṇadīptyoḥ*; *ghṛtaṃ = dīptaṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ yeṣāṃ te*, a bahuvrīhi; the first member keeps its accent by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1).

**मनोयुजः (*manoyujaḥ*)**: *manasā yuñjate iti*; by "ṛtvigdadhṛksragdiguṣṇigañcuyujikruñcāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-59) *kvin* after *yuj* with *manas* as *upapada*; *yuj* is final udātta by the root accent; after compounding, by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) the *kṛt* second member keeps its accent. The Kaumudīkāra and others hold that *kvin* comes after *yuj* without an *upapada* (*nirupapadād yujeḥ kvin*); but, as the Vedabhāṣyakāra holds, the *kvin* is derived here after *yuj* with an *upapada*.

**त्वा (*tvā*)**: for *tvām*, the accusative singular of *yuṣmad*, the unaccented *tvā* by "tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-23).

**वहन्ति (*vahanti*)**: *vaha prāpaṇe*, *laṭ*, *jhi*, *ant* by "jho 'ntaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-3); *śap*, *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe"; *śap* is *pit*, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4); *anti*, a *sārvadhātuka* for a *lakāra*, follows the *śap* of *adupadeśa*, so it is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186); the root

### Page 606 — Rik 6: grammar (continued)

accent remains. In *ye tvā vahanti vahnayaḥ*, *vahanti* follows the word with *yat*; so by "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66), a *tiṅanta* after a word containing *yat* is not made unaccented, and "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not apply. Here there is the vārttika "kāṣṭhādibhya iti vaktavyam" on "pūjanāt pūjitam anudāttam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-67): what is praised after *kāṣṭha* and other words of praise is unaccented. Even if the sūtra had been framed "pūjanād anudāttam", "the praised" would be got from *pūjita* as a correlate and from proximity; so the mention of *pūjita* would be useless, and it makes known that *atra prakaraṇe pañcamīnirdeśe 'pi nānantaryam āśrīyate* — in this section, though there is a fifth-case statement, immediate sequence is not required. With the fifth case *pūjanāt* alone, the sense of immediate sequence would not be got. With *pūjita* stated, in *kamalāni kamalāni*, by repetition, the sense "excellent lotus" arises, and the two words, *pūjita* in the sūtra and *pūjita* got by proximity, convey "excellent, praised"; here the excellence takes the form of immediate sequence. So the mention of *pūjita* has its use for getting immediate sequence. Without this made-known statement, since *pūjanāt* is in the fifth case, immediate sequence would follow by "tasmād ity uttarasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-67), and the mention of *pūjita* would be useless. So it must be granted that in this section, though there is a fifth-case statement, immediate sequence is not required. In *ye tvā vahanti* the word *tvā* intervenes, yet the bar of "yadvṛttān nityam" applies. So it is not wholly unaccented.

**वह्नयः (*vahnayaḥ*)**: "vahiśriśruyudruglāhātvaribhyo nit" (Uṇ. sū. "4-51" [?]), with *niḥ* carried on from "vījyājvaribhyo niḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 4-48): after *vaha prāpaṇe*, *śriñ sevāyām*, *śru śravaṇe*, *yu miśraṇe*, *dru gatau*, *glai mlai harṣakṣaye*, *ohāk tyāge*, *ñitvarā sambhrame*, the suffix *ni*, and it is *nit*; so *ni* after *vah*, and being *nit*, *vahni* is initial udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197).

**सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)**: its formation was given in the first Ṛk of this sūkta. In *devān somapītaye*, in the Saṃhitā, *s* follows the *n*; so "naś ca" (Pā. sū. 8-3-30) gives the augment *dhuṭ* to the *s* after a word ending in *n*; being *ṭit*, it comes at the beginning of the *s*: *devān* + *dh* + *soma*. "khari ca" (Pā. sū. 8-4-55): before a *khar* letter, *car* letters replace the *jhal* letters; the *s* is a *khar*, so the *jhal* *dh* gets a *car*. Of the *car* letters *c, ṭ, t, k, p, ś, ṣ, s*, by "sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-50) the dental

### Page 607 — Rik 6: grammar (end)

*t*, of the same place, comes: *devān* + *t* + *soma*. "cayo dvitīyāḥ śari pauṣkarasādeḥ" (Pā. sū. vā. 8-4-48-3): Pauṣkarasādi is the name of a teacher; in his view, before *śar* letters the *cay* letters take the second letter of their class; so the *t* before the *śar* *s* becomes *th*, the second of the dental class: *devān* + *th* + *soma*. By this derivation the mantra should read *devānthsomapītaye*.

**॥६॥**

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> तान् । यजत्रान् । ऋतऽवृधः । अग्ने । पत्नीऽवतः । कृधि ॥

>
> *tān | yajatrān | ṛta 'vṛdhaḥ | agne | patnī 'vataḥ | kṛdhi ||*
> *madhvaḥ | su 'jihva | pāyaya ||7||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे अग्ने तानिन्द्रादीन्देवान्यजत्रान्यजनीयान् ऋतावृधः सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य वा वर्धकान् पत्नीवतः पत्नीयुक्तान्कृधि । कुरु । हे सुजिह्व । शोभनजिह्वोपेत मध्वो मधुरस्य सोमस्य भागं देवान्पायय ॥ यजत्रान् । अमिनक्षियजिबन्धिपतिभ्योऽत्रन् । उ. ३-१०५ । इति यजेरत्रन्प्रत्ययः । ऋतावृधः । वृधु वृद्धौ । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्क्विप्चेति क्विप् । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घत्वं । वृधेर्धातुस्वरः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अग्ने । पादादित्वान्नामन्त्रितनिघातः । षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं । पत्नीवतः । पत्युर्नो यज्ञसंयोगे । पा. ४-१-३३ । इति ङीप् । इकारस्य च नकारः । ता एषां सन्तीति मतुप् । छन्दसीर इति वत्वं । पतिशब्दो डतिप्रत्ययान्तत्वादाद्युदात्तः । ङीम्मतुपोरनुदात्तत्वात्स एव शिष्यते । कृधि । कृञो लोटः सिः । सेर्ह्यपिच्चेति हिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणलुक् । श्रुशृणुपॄकृवृभ्यश्छन्दसि । पा. ६-४-१०२ । इति हेर्धिरादेशः । ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । मध्वः । उक्तं । सुजिह्व । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । पायय । पा पाने । पिबन्तं प्रयुङ्क्त इति हेतुमति चेति णिच् । शाछासाह्वाव्यावेपां युक् । पा. ७-३-३७ । इति युक् । पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वं । अत एवाव्यवधायकत्वान्मध्व इत्यपेक्ष्य तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥
>
> *he agne tānindrādīndevānyajatrānyajanīyān ṛtāvṛdhaḥ satyasya yajñasya vā vardhakān patnīvataḥ patnīyuktānkṛdhi | kuru | he sujihva | śobhanajihvopeta madhvo madhurasya somasya bhāgaṃ devānpāyaya || yajatrān | aminakṣiyajibandhipatibhyo 'tran | u. 3-105 | iti yajeratranpratyayaḥ | ṛtāvṛdhaḥ | vṛdhu vṛddhau | antarbhāvitaṇyarthātkvipceti kvip | anyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti pūrvapadasya dīrghatvaṃ | vṛdherdhātusvaraḥ | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | agne | pādāditvānnāmantritanighātaḥ | ṣāṣṭhikamādyudāttatvaṃ | patnīvataḥ | patyurno yajñasaṃyoge | pā. 4-1-33 | iti ṅīp | ikārasya ca nakāraḥ | tā eṣāṃ santīti matup | chandasīra iti vatvaṃ | patiśabdo ḍatipratyayāntatvādādyudāttaḥ | ṅīmmatuporanudāttatvātsa eva śiṣyate | kṛdhi | kṛño loṭaḥ siḥ | serhyapicceti hiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇaluk | śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaśchandasi | pā. 6-4-102 | iti herdhirādeśaḥ | ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | madhvaḥ | uktaṃ | sujihva | āmantritanighātaḥ | pāyaya | pā pāne | pibantaṃ prayuṅkta iti hetumati ceti ṇic | śāchāsāhvāvyāvepāṃ yuk | pā. 7-3-37 | iti yuk | pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvaṃ | ata evāvyavadhāyakatvānmadhva ityapekṣya tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni, make those gods, Indra and the rest, *yajatrāḥ*, worthy of worship, *ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*, who make the truth or the sacrifice grow, *patnīvataḥ*, accompanied by their wives: *kṛdhi*, do so. O *sujihva*, you of the fine tongue, make the gods drink their share of the *madhvaḥ*, the sweet soma." (Grammatical tail: *yajatrān* with *atran* (Uṇ. 3-105); *ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*, *vṛdh* with the inner causative and *kvip*, the first member lengthened, the accent of the *kṛt* second member; *agne*, at the head of the pāda, not lowered, initial udātta; *patnīvataḥ*, *ṅīp* and *n* by Pā. 4-1-33, *matup* with *v*, *pati* initial udātta (*ḍati*); *kṛdhi*, *hi*, the *vikaraṇa* dropped, *dhi* by Pā. 6-4-102, no *guṇa*; *sujihva* lowered as a vocative; *pāyaya* from *pā* with *ṇic* and *yuk* (Pā. 7-3-37); the vocative before it counts as absent, so it is lowered after *madhvaḥ* by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*.)

### Page 608 — Rik 7: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **यजत्रान् (yajatrān)** — worthy of worship | **पत्नीवतः (patnīvataḥ)** — joined with their wives | **तान् (tān)** — those gods, Indra and the rest | **ऋतावृधः (ṛtāvṛdhaḥ)** — as makers of the sacrifice (the truth) to grow | **कृधि (kṛdhi)** — make | **सुजिह्व (sujihva)** — O Agni of the shining tongue | **मध्वः (madhvaḥ)** — the sweet soma juice | **पायय (pāyaya)** — make (them) drink.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, Indra and the other gods are worthy of worship. Bring them with their wives and help so that our sacrifice prospers. O Agni, whose tongue can taste sweetness, make Indra and the other gods too drink the sweet soma juice.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O sweet tongued Agni, put those adorable gods with their wives here and make them drink of the sweet Soma

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Yajatrān**: *yajanīyān*, worthy of worship.

**Patnīvataḥ**: accompanied by their wives.

**Ṛtāvṛdhaḥ**: *ṛtasya satyasya vā yajñasya vardhakān*: those who make the sacrificial act grow, who make it go on without obstacle.

**Madhvaḥ**: means "of the soma juice". If the word *bhāgam* is supplied, it means "the share of the soma juice".

### Page 609 — Rik 7: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 609–611, noted briefly)*

**यजत्रान् (*yajatrān*)**: "aminakṣiyajivadhipatibhyo 'tran" (Uṇ. sū. "3-385" [?]; *ama gatyādiṣu*, *nakṣa gatau*, *yaja devapūjādau*, *vadha hiṃsāyām*, *patḷ gatau*): the suffix *atran* after *yaj*; *nit*, so *yajatra* is initial udātta by the *nit* accent; accusative plural *yajatrān*. In the Saṃhitā, before the *ṛ*, "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. sū. 8-3-9) gives *ru* for the *n*, and "āto 'ṭi nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-3-3) a nasal *ā*.

**ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)**: in the sense *ṛtaṃ vardhayanti*, *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76) after *vṛdh* with the inner *ṇic* and *ṛta* as *upapada*; the ending dropped; by "anyeṣām api dṛśyate" (Pā. sū. 6-3-137) the first member *ṛta* is lengthened; accusative plural. In *ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*, "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162) gives final udātta; after compounding, the accent of the *kṛt* second member remains.

**अग्ने (*agne*)**: it is at the head of the pāda, so the eighth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19) does not lower it; the sixth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198) makes it initial udātta.

**पत्नीवतः (*patnīvataḥ*)**: "patyur no yajñasaṃyoge" (Pā. sū. 4-1-33): in the feminine, when connection with a sacrifice is shown, *n* replaces the last letter of *pati*: *patn*; ending in *n*, it takes *ṅīp* by "ṛnnebhyo ṅīp" (Pā. sū. 4-1-5): *patnī*. In the Vedābhyāsa the sūtra is explained to mean that *ṅīp* comes after *pati* in the feminine and *n* for the *i*; on that view, from the difference of what is enjoined, faults such as splitting the sentence arise, so other grammarians do not accept it. In Śrutis such as *svargakāmo yajeta* the masculine *svargakāmaḥ* is used, so performing the sacrifice and enjoying its fruit belong to the man. How then does a woman have a connection with the sacrifice? And without such connection, how would the *n* of *yajñasaṃyoge* fit? Because in the sacrifice the authority belongs to husband and wife together: a man who is a widower has no authority to perform it. Under this sūtra the Kaiyaṭa shows: *patnyā śiṣṭa dampatyoḥ sahādhikārād yajñe 'dhikārāt kartṛtvāt tatphalasambandhād yajñasaṃyogaḥ*. In the Pūrvamīmāṃsā too, in the sixth adhyāya, first pāda, in the *adhikaraṇa* *liṅgaviśeṣanirdeśāt puṃyuktam aitiśāyanaḥ* and in the *adhikaraṇa* *svavato 'stu vacanād aikakarmyaṃ syāt*, the joint authority of husband and wife is established. *Patiśabdo 'yam aiśvarya-*

### Page 610 — Rik 7: grammar (continued)

*vācī*: in the Mahābhāṣya the word *pati* in this sūtra is shown to mean "lordship". Then *yajñasaṃyoge* is a locative absolute: when there is a connection with the sacrifice, the word *pati*, meaning the lordship that arises, by proximity, from that sacrifice, takes *n* in the feminine: that is the sense of the sūtra. Analysed *patnyaḥ eṣāṃ santi*, *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. sū. 5-2-94); *v* for the *m* by "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-15): *patnīvat*. By "pāter ḍatiḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 4-57 [as printed; p. 595 prints 4-58]) *pati* ends in the suffix *ḍati*, so it is initial udātta by the suffix accent; *ṅīp* and *matup* are both *pit*, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4); the initial udātta remains; accusative plural *patnīvataḥ*.

**कृधि (*kṛdhi*)**: *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *loṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*; *hi* for *si* by "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87); the *u* *vikaraṇa* of "tanādikṛñbhya uḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-79) is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. "9-4-73" [as printed, for 2-4-73]); "śruśṛṇupṝkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-4-102) gives *dhi* for the *hi* after these; by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) the suffix is *ṅit*, and "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) bars the *guṇa*: *kṛdhi*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ".

**मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)**: in Sū. 13 Ṛk 2 *madhu* was shown to be initial udātta. It is neuter, but here masculine by *vyatyaya*. Genitive singular "jas" [as printed, for *ṅas*]. By "śeṣo ghy asakhi" (Pā. sū. 1-4-7) short *i*/*u*-final words other than *sakhi* that are not *nadī* are called *ghi*; so "gher ṅiti" (Pā. sū. 7-3-111) would give *guṇa* before a *ṅit* ending; but by "saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ" (paribhāṣā) the *guṇa* does not come. *Yaṇ*, *ru*, visarga: *madhvaḥ*.

**सुजिह्व (*sujihva*)**: lowered as a vocative.

**पायय (*pāyaya*)**: *pā pāne*; in the sense *pibantaṃ prayuṅkte* (one who urges the one drinking), *ṇic* by "hetumati ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-26); "śāchāsāhvāvyāvepāṃ yuk" (Pā. sū. "7-3-37" [?]; *śo tanūkaraṇe*, *cho chedane*, *ṣo 'ntakarmaṇi*, *hveñ spardhāyām*, *vyeñ saṃvaraṇe*, *veñ tantusantāne*, *pā pāne*): before *ṇi* these roots take the augment *yuk*: *pāy* + *i*. There are two roots, *pā rakṣaṇe* (*adādi*, with *luk* of the *vikaraṇa*) and *pā pāne* (*bhvādi*, without it); by "lugvikaraṇālugvikaraṇayor alugvikaraṇasya" (paribhāṣā "83" [?]), when both are possible,

### Page 611 — Rik 7: grammar (end)

the one without *luk* is taken, so the *bhvādi* root is meant. After *pāyi*, *loṭ*, *sip*, the *vikaraṇa* *śap*, *guṇa*, *ay*, *hi* for *si* and its *luk*: *pāyaya*. For the vocative *sujihva* before it, "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. sū. 8-1-72) makes it count as absent; so it does not intervene, and with reference to *madhvaḥ* "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) makes *pāyaya* wholly unaccented.

**॥७॥**

> ये यज॑त्रा॒ य ई॒ड्या॒स्ते ते॑ पिबन्तु जि॒ह्वया॑ । [accent ?]
