*(Line 1: bars stand under ई/ड्या and under स्ते of ईड्यास्ते, the stroke over the second ते; the exact syllables under the two bars are not certain.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ये । यजत्राः । ये । ईड्याः । ते । ते । पिबन्तु । जिह्वया ॥
> मधोः । अग्ने । वषट्ऽकृति ॥८॥
>
> *ye | yajatrāḥ | ye | īḍyāḥ | te | te | pibantu | jihvayā ||*
> *madhoḥ | agne | vaṣaṭ 'kṛti ||8||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> ये देवा यजत्रा यष्टव्याः । तथा ये देवा ईड्याः स्तुत्याः । ते सर्वेऽपि वषट्कृति वषट्कारकाले वषट्कारयुक्ते यागे वा हे अग्ने ते त्वदीयया जिह्वया मधोर्मधुरस्य सोमस्य भागं पिबन्तु ॥ यजत्राः । गतं । ईड्याः । ईड स्तुतौ । ऋहलोर्ण्यत् । तित्स्वरिते प्राप्त ईडवन्दवृशंसदुहां ण्यत इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । द्वितीयस्य तेशब्दस्य युष्मदादेशस्य सर्वानुदात्तत्वं । मधोः । उप्रत्ययस्य नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वमुक्तं । अग्ने । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । वषट्कृति । करोतेः सम्पदादिभ्यो भावे क्विप् । वषडित्यस्य करणं यस्मिन्याग इति बहुव्रीहिः । वषडित्यस्य निपातत्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥
>
> *ye devā yajatrā yaṣṭavyāḥ | tathā ye devā īḍyāḥ stutyāḥ | te sarve 'pi vaṣaṭkṛti vaṣaṭkārakāle vaṣaṭkārayukte yāge vā he agne te tvadīyayā jihvayā madhormadhurasya somasya bhāgaṃ pibantu || yajatrāḥ | gataṃ | īḍyāḥ | īḍa stutau | ṛhalorṇyat | titsvarite prāpta īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyata ityādyudāttatvaṃ | dvitīyasya teśabdasya yuṣmadādeśasya sarvānudāttatvaṃ | madhoḥ | upratyayasya nittvādādyudāttatvamuktaṃ | agne | āmantritanighātaḥ | vaṣaṭkṛti | karoteḥ sampadādibhyo bhāve kvip | vaṣaḍityasya karaṇaṃ yasminyāga iti bahuvrīhiḥ | vaṣaḍityasya nipātatvādādyudāttatvaṃ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "The gods who are *yajatrāḥ*, to be worshipped, and the gods who are *īḍyāḥ*, to be praised: may they all, *vaṣaṭkṛti*, at the time of the *vaṣaṭ* call or in the rite that has the *vaṣaṭ* call, O Agni, drink with *te jihvayā*, your tongue, the share of the *madhoḥ*, the sweet soma." (Grammatical tail: *yajatrāḥ* gone through; *īḍyāḥ* from *īḍ* with *ṇyat*, initial udātta by *īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ* instead of the svarita of a *tit* suffix; the second *te*, the *yuṣmad* replacement, wholly unaccented; *madhoḥ* initial udātta as said; *agne* lowered; *vaṣaṭkṛti*, *kvip* in the action sense, a bahuvrīhi "the rite in which *vaṣaṭ* is made", *vaṣaṭ* initial udātta as a *nipāta*, the first-member accent.)

### Page 612 — Rik 8: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **ये (ye)** — the deities who | **यजत्राः (yajatrāḥ)** — worthy of a share in the sacrifice | *(and likewise)* **ये (ye)** — the deities who | **ईड्याः (īḍyāḥ)** — worthy of praise | **ते (te)** — all of them | **वषट्कृति (vaṣaṭkṛti)** — at the time of the *vaṣaṭkāra* of the sacrifice (at the time of offering the oblation) | **ते (te)** — your | **जिह्वया (jihvayā)** — with the tongue (by the offering into Agni) | **मधोः (madhoḥ)** — the share of the sweet soma juice | **पिबन्तु (pibantu)** — may they drink.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, may all the deities who are worthy of a share in the sacrifice and those who are worthy of praise, together, at the time of offering the oblation preceded by the *vaṣaṭkāra*, drink the share of the sweet soma juice through your mouth, that is, by the offering into Agni.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Agni, those gods that deserve to be sacrificed and those that deserve to be praised, may they drink of the sweet soma with your tongue as soon as (the word) Vashat is pronounced

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Yajatrāḥ**: *yajanīyāḥ*: worthy of worship, worthy of a share in the sacrifice.

**Īḍyāḥ**: worthy of praise, worthy of commendation.

**Vaṣaṭkṛti**: at the time of the *vaṣaṭkāra*, or in a rite that has the *vaṣaṭkāra*. When the *homa* is made with certain mantras in the sacrifice, at the end of the mantra the word *vauṣaṭ* is added and uttered as the *svāhākāra* is; that is called *vaṣaṭkṛti* or *vaṣaṭkāra*.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 612–613, noted briefly)*

**यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*)**: explained in the preceding mantra.

The *t* of *ṇyat* is *it*, so "tit svaritam" (Pā. sū. "6-1-185" [?]) would make it svarita; but, overriding it, "īḍavandavṛśaṃsaduhāṃ ṇyataḥ" (Pā. sū.

### Page 613 — Rik 8: grammar (end)

6-1-214): the first syllable of these roots before *ṇyat* is udātta; so *īḍya* is initial udātta.

**ते (*te*)**: *tad* + *jas*. "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102): before a case ending the final of the *tyadādi* words becomes *a*: *ta* + *a*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97); "jasaḥ śī" (Pā. sū. 7-1-17) gives *śī* for *jas* after an *a*-final pronoun; it is not *anekāl*, but by "anekālśit sarvasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-55) it replaces the whole; *guṇa* by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87): *te*. By "phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ" (Phi. sū. 1) *tad* is final udātta; *pararūpa* and *guṇa* are single replacements, udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ".

**ते (*te*)**: this is the replacement for *tava*, the genitive singular of *yuṣmad*; so it is wholly unaccented.

**मधोः (*madhoḥ*)**: the suffix *u* is *nit* by extension, so *madhu* is initial udātta, as set out in Sū. 13, Ṛk 2; here masculine by *vyatyaya*. Genitive singular "jas" [as printed, for *ṅas*]; by "śeṣo ghy asakhi" it is *ghi*, so by "gher ṅiti" *guṇa*, *o* for the *u*; "ṅasiṅasoś ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-110): after *e* and *o*, the *a* of *ṅasi* and *ṅas* gives *pūrvarūpa*; *ru*, visarga.

**अग्ने (*agne*)**: lowered as a vocative by the eighth-adhyāya sūtra.

**वषट्कृति (*vaṣaṭkṛti*)**: "sampadādibhyaḥ kvip" (Pā. sū. 3-3-108-9): *kvip* after *kṛñ* in the action sense; *kvip* is *pit*, a *kṛt*, so before it *kṛ* takes the augment *tuk* by "hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk": *kṛt*. *Vaṣaṭ kṛt yasmin saḥ*, the rite in which there is the making of *vaṣaṭ*: by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" the first member keeps its accent; *vaṣaṭ* is a *nipāta*, so initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Phi. sū. 80). Locative singular *vaṣaṭkṛti*.

**॥८॥**

### Page 614 — Rik 9: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> आकीम् । सूर्यस्य । रोचनात् । विश्वान् । देवान् । उषःऽबुधः ॥
> विप्रः । होता । इह । वक्षति ॥९॥
>
> *ākīm | sūryasya | rocanāt | viśvān | devān | uṣaḥ 'budhaḥ ||*
> *vipraḥ | hotā | iha | vakṣati ||9||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> विप्रो मेधावी होता होमनिष्पादको ऽग्निरुषर्बुध उषःकाले यागगमनाय प्रबुध्यमानान्विश्वान्देवान्सूर्यस्य सम्बन्धिनो रोचनात्स्वर्गलोकादिह कर्मण्याकीं वक्षति । आवहतु ॥ आकीं । निपात आद्युदात्तः । सूर्यस्य । सूर्यशब्दो राजसूयसूर्येत्यादिना । पा. ३-१-११४ । क्यप्प्रत्ययान्तो निपातितः । क्यपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरेणाद्युदात्तः । रोचनात् । रोचमानात् । रुच दीप्तौ । अनुदात्तेतश्च हलादेः । पा. ३-२-१४९ । इति कर्तरि युच् । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । विश्वान् । विशेः क्वनन्तो नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । उषर्बुधः । उषसि बुध्यन्त इत्युषर्बुधः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । धातुस्वरेणोकार उदात्तः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । विप्रः । ऋज्रेन्द्रेत्यादिना रन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । होता । ह्वयतेस्ताच्छील्ये तृन् । बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणं । परपूर्वत्वं । गुणः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । इह । इदमो ह इति हप्रत्ययः । इदम इशिति इश् । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । वक्षति । वहेः प्रार्थनायां लिङर्थे लेट् । तस्य तिप् । कर्तरि शप् । शपि परतः सिब्बहुलं लेटीति सिप् । ढत्वकत्वषत्वानि । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः ॥
>
> *vipro medhāvī hotā homaniṣpādako 'gniruṣarbudha uṣaḥkāle yāgagamanāya prabudhyamānānviśvāndevānsūryasya sambandhino rocanātsvargalokādiha karmaṇyākīṃ vakṣati | āvahatu || ākīṃ | nipāta ādyudāttaḥ | sūryasya | sūryaśabdo rājasūyasūryetyādinā | pā. 3-1-114 | kyappratyayānto nipātitaḥ | kyapaḥ pittvāddhātusvareṇādyudāttaḥ | rocanāt | rocamānāt | ruca dīptau | anudāttetaśca halādeḥ | pā. 3-2-149 | iti kartari yuc | cita ityantodāttatvaṃ | viśvān | viśeḥ kvananto nittvādādyudāttaḥ | uṣarbudhaḥ | uṣasi budhyanta ityuṣarbudhaḥ | kvipceti kvip | dhātusvareṇokāra udāttaḥ | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | vipraḥ | ṛjrendretyādinā ran | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | hotā | hvayatestācchīlye tṛn | bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇaṃ | parapūrvatvaṃ | guṇaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | iha | idamo ha iti hapratyayaḥ | idama iśiti iś | śittvātsarvādeśaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | vakṣati | vaheḥ prārthanāyāṃ liṅarthe leṭ | tasya tip | kartari śap | śapi parataḥ sibbahulaṃ leṭīti sip | ḍhatvakatvaṣatvāni | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "May the *vipra*, the wise *hotā*, Agni who accomplishes the *homa*, *ākīṃ vakṣati*, bring here to this rite, from the *rocana* of the Sun, the heaven-world, all the gods, *uṣarbudhaḥ*, who awake at dawn to go to the sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: *ākīm*, a *nipāta*, initial udātta; *sūryasya*, *sūrya* made with *kyap* by *nipātana* (Pā. 3-1-114), the root accent (*kyap* is *pit*), initial udātta; *rocanāt*, "shining", *yuc* by Pā. 3-2-149, final udātta (*cit*); *viśvān* with *kvan*, initial udātta; *uṣarbudhaḥ*, "awaking at dawn", *kvip*, the *u* udātta by the root accent, the *kṛt* second-member accent; *vipraḥ* with *ran*, initial udātta; *hotā* from *hve* with *tṛn* and *saṃprasāraṇa*, initial udātta; *iha*, *ha* after *idam*, *i* for it; *vakṣati*, *leṭ* in the sense of prayer, *sip*, *ḍh*, *k*, *ṣ*, lowered by *tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**विप्रः (vipraḥ)** — wise | **होता (hotā)** — Agni, who accomplishes the *homa* | **उषर्बुधः (uṣarbudhaḥ)** — woken at dawn itself for going to the sacrifice | **विश्वान् देवान् (viśvān devān)** — all the gods | **सूर्यस्य (sūryasya)** — of the Sun | **रोचनात् (rocanāt)** — from the divine sphere, or from heaven | **इह (iha)** — to this rite (the sacrifice) | **आकीं वक्षति (ākīṃ vakṣati)** — may he bring.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

Agni is wise, the accomplisher of the *homa*. He wakes all the gods at dawn to come for the sacrifice. May he bring them all from the bright heaven-world belonging to the Sun to this sacrificial rite.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Let the wise invoker of the gods bring hither, from the region of solar light the Visve Devas (all the gods) that awake with the dawn.

*(The left edge of the English is cut in this scan; the words are as in the earlier reading.)*

### Page 615 — Rik 9: Special Topics and grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Ākīm**: since Yāska says that the nine words *hikam*, *nukam*, *sukam*, *ahikam*, *ākīm* and the rest are the *sarvapadasamāmnāya* (Ni. 3-13), the word *ākīm* has the sense of *sarvapada*. It is used as an *upasarga*; so here *ākīṃ vakṣati* means *ā vakṣati*.

**Uṣarbudhaḥ**:

> उषःकाले यागगमनाय प्रबुध्यमानान् । उषसि बुध्यन्त इत्युषर्बुधः ॥
>
> *uṣaḥkāle yāgagamanāya prabudhyamānān | uṣasi budhyanta ityuṣarbudhaḥ ||*

Woken at dawn.

**Hotā**: here *hotā* means Agni, who calls the deities.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 615–616, noted briefly)*

**आकीम् (*ākīm*)**: a *nipāta*, so initial udātta.

**सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)**: by "rājasūyasūryamṛṣodyarucyakupyakṛṣṭapacyāvyathyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-114) these seven words are made by *nipātana* ending in *kyap*; so *sūrya* ends in *kyap*. If taken as *sarati ākāśe* (it goes in the sky), *kyap* after *sṛ gatau* with *u* for the *ṛ* by *nipātana*, *r* after it by "uraṇ raparaḥ": *sur* + *ya*; lengthening by "hali ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-77) of *i, u, ṛ, ḷ* in the penultimate of *r*/*v*-final roots before a consonant. Or, taken as *suvati karmaṇi lokaṃ prerayati* (he urges people to work), *kyap* after the *tudādi* *ṣū preraṇe* with the augment *ruṭ* by *nipātana*: *sūrya*. *Kyap* is *pit*, so unaccented; the root accent makes *sūrya* initial udātta.

**रोचनात् (*rocanāt*)**: *ruca dīptau*, *anudāttet*. "anudāttetaś ca halādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-2-149): after an intransitive *anudāttet* root beginning with a consonant, *yuc* in the agent sense; *ana* for *yu* by "yuvor anākau" (Pā. sū. 7-1-1); *laghūpadha-guṇa*: *rocana*; final udātta by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163).

**विश्वान् (*viśvān*)**: *viśa praveśane* + *kvan* by "aśūpruṣi…" (Uṇ. sū. 1-149); *nit*, so initial udātta.

**उषर्बुधः (*uṣarbudhaḥ*)**: *uṣasi budhyante iti*; *kvip* by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76) after *budha avagamane* with *uṣas* as *upapada*; the *u* is udātta by the root accent; after compounding, the *kṛt* second member keeps its accent by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt".

### Page 616 — Rik 9: grammar (end)

**विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)**: "ṛjrendrāgravipra…" (Uṇ. sū. 2-186): when *ran* comes after *ḍuvap bījasantāne*, *i* is put by *nipātana* for the *a* of the penultimate; initial udātta by the *nit* accent.

**होता (*hotā*)**: *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *tṛn* by "tṛn" (Pā. sū. 3-2-135) in the sense of habit; with "hvaḥ samprasāraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-32) carried on, *saṃprasāraṇa* by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-34); *pūrvarūpa* by "saṃprasāraṇāc ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-108); *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84): *hotṛ*; initial udātta (*nit*).

**इह (*iha*)**: "idamo haḥ" (Pā. sū. 5-3-11): after the locative of *idam* the suffix *ha*: *idam* + *ṅi* + *ha*; ending in a *taddhita*, a *prātipadika* by "kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-2-46); the *ṅi* dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71); "idam iś" (Pā. sū. 5-3-3) gives *iś* for *idam* before the *prāgdiśīya* suffixes; being *śit*, it replaces the whole by "anekālśit sarvasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-55): *iha*; the suffix accent.

**वक्षति (*vakṣati*)**: *vaha prāpaṇe*. "liṅarthe leṭ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-7): *leṭ* in the sense of prayer; *tip*: *vah* + *ti*; *śap* by "kartari śap"; "sib bahulaṃ leṭi" (Pā. sū. 3-1-34): *sip* after the root before *śap*: *vah* + *s* + *a* + *ti*; "ho ḍhaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-31) gives *ḍh* for the *h* at the end of a word or before a *jhal*; "ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si" (Pā. sū. 8-2-41) *k* for *ṣ*/*ḍh* before *s*; "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59) *ṣ* for the *s*: *vakṣati*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ".

**॥९॥**

### Page 617 — Rik 10: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> विश्वेभिः । सोम्यम् । मधु । अग्ने । इन्द्रेण । वायुना ॥
> पिब । मित्रस्य । धामऽभिः ॥१०॥
>
> *viśvebhiḥ | somyam | madhu | agne | indreṇa | vāyunā ||*
> *piba | mitrasya | dhāma 'bhiḥ ||10||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे अग्ने त्वं विश्वेभिः सर्वैः पूषभगादिभिर्देवैरिन्द्रेण वायुना मित्रस्य सम्बन्धिभिर्धामभिस्तेजोभिर्मूर्तिविशेषरूपैश्च सह सोम्यं सोमसम्बन्धि मधु मधुरं भागं पिब ॥ विश्वेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसादेशाभावः । सोम्यं । सोममर्हति य इत्यनुवृत्तौ मये च । पा. ४-४-१३८ । इति यप्रत्ययः सोमस्य विकार इत्यर्थे । यस्येति चेत्यकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । मधु । फलिपाटिनमिमनीत्यादिना । उ. १-१९ । उप्रत्ययः । नित्यनुवृत्तेर्नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । वायुना । कृवापाजीत्यादिना उण् । आतो युक् चिण्कृतोः । पा. ७-३-३३ । इति युक् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । पिब । पा पाने । लोटः सेर्हिरादेशः । शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना पिबादेशः । अतो हेरिति हेर्लुक् । शपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । द्व्यचो ऽतस्तिङ इति संहितायां दीर्घः । धामभिः । धाञ् । आतो मनिन्निति मनिन् । नित्स्वरः ॥
>
> *he agne tvaṃ viśvebhiḥ sarvaiḥ pūṣabhagādibhirdevairindreṇa vāyunā mitrasya sambandhibhirdhāmabhistejobhirmūrtiviśeṣarūpaiśca saha somyaṃ somasambandhi madhu madhuraṃ bhāgaṃ piba || viśvebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisādeśābhāvaḥ | somyaṃ | somamarhati ya ityanuvṛttau maye ca | pā. 4-4-138 | iti yapratyayaḥ somasya vikāra ityarthe | yasyeti cetyakāralopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | madhu | phalipāṭinamimanītyādinā | u. 1-19 | upratyayaḥ | nityanuvṛtternittvādādyudāttaḥ | vāyunā | kṛvāpājītyādinā uṇ | āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ | pā. 7-3-33 | iti yuk | pratyayasvaraḥ | piba | pā pāne | loṭaḥ serhirādeśaḥ | śapi pāghretyādinā pibādeśaḥ | ato heriti herluk | śapaḥ pittvāddhātusvaraḥ | pādāditvānna nighātaḥ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghaḥ | dhāmabhiḥ | dhāñ | āto maninniti manin | nitsvaraḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni, together with *viśvebhiḥ*, all the gods, Pūṣan, Bhaga and the rest, with Indra, with Vāyu, and with the *dhāmans* belonging to Mitra, his radiances and particular forms, drink the *somya madhu*, the sweet share belonging to the soma." (Grammatical tail: *viśvebhiḥ* without *ais*; *somyam* with *ya* by Pā. 4-4-138 in the sense "product of soma", the *a* dropped, the suffix accent; *madhu* with *u* (Uṇ. 1-19), initial udātta; *vāyunā* with *uṇ* and *yuk* (Pā. 7-3-33); *piba*, *pib* for *pā*, *hi* dropped, the root accent, not lowered at the head of the pāda, lengthened in the Saṃhitā by *dvyaco 'tas tiṅaḥ*; *dhāmabhiḥ*, *dhā* with *manin*, the *nit* accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **विश्वेभिः (viśvebhiḥ)** — with all the gods, Pūṣan, Bhaga and the rest | **इन्द्रेण (indreṇa)** — with Indra | **वायुना (vāyunā)** — with Vāyu | **मित्रस्य धामभिः (mitrasya dhāmabhiḥ)** — with Mitra's particular forms and radiances, together | **सोम्यं मधु (somyaṃ madhu)** — the sweet soma juice | **पिब (piba)** — drink.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, drink the sweet soma juice together with Indra, with Vāyu, with all the other gods, Pūṣan, Bhaga and the rest, and with the particular forms of Mitra, which are in the form of radiance.

### Page 618 — Rik 10: English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Agni, drink this sweet soma juice with the Visve devas, Indra, Vayu, and the various forms of Mitra.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

This Ṛk is used in the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice as the *yājyā* mantra of the recitation of the *praüga-śastra*. In the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section *stotram agre śastrāt*, it is said that the Ṛk *viśvebhiḥ somyaṃ madhu* is to be used as the *yājyā* mantra (Ā. 5-10).

**Piba**: in the Saṃhitā the final syllable is long, to suit the metre.

**Mitrasya dhāmabhiḥ**:

> मित्रस्य सम्बन्धिभिर्धामभिस्तेजोमूर्तिविशेषरूपैश्च
>
> *mitrasya sambandhibhirdhāmabhistejomūrtiviśeṣarūpaiśca*

with Mitra's forms of radiance, "with various forms of Mitra". *Dhāmabhiḥ* means with radiances or forms of radiance, "Rays". Which the radiant forms of Mitra are here is not clear.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 618–619, noted briefly)*

**विश्वेभिः (*viśvebhiḥ*)**: by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 7-1-10) the *ais* that "ato bhisa ais" (Pā. sū. 7-1-9) would give for *bhis* does not come.

**सोम्यम् (*somyam*)**: with *somam* and *yaḥ* carried on from "somam arhati yaḥ" (Pā. sū. 4-4-137), "maye ca" (Pā. sū. 4-4-138): after *soma* in the fitting case, in the senses of *mayaṭ* (come from, product, part, statement of plenty), the suffix *ya*. In the sense "come from" the fitting case is the fifth; in product and part the sixth; in the statement of plenty the first. Here, meant as *somasya vikāraḥ*, *ya* after the genitive in the sense of product; ending in a *taddhita*, a *prātipadika*; the ending dropped: *soma* + *ya*; the *a* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148); the suffix accent; accusative singular *somyam*.

**मधु (*madhu*)**: the suffix *u* by "phalipāṭinamimani…" (Uṇ. sū. "1-18" [as printed; the bhāṣya gives 1-19]); *nit* is carried on, so the suffix is *nit*, and the *nit* accent comes. **वायुना (*vāyunā*)**: *uṇ* after *vā* by "kṛvāpāji…" (Uṇ. sū. 1-1); "āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ"

### Page 619 — Rik 10: grammar (end)

(Pā. sū. 7-3-33): before *ciṇ* and a *kṛt* suffix with *ñ*/*ṇ*, an *ā*-final root takes the augment *yuk*; *yuk*, being *kit*, comes at the end; the suffix accent.

**पिब (*piba*)**: *pā pāne*, *loṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*; *hi* for *si* by "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87); the *vikaraṇa* *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68); *pib* for *pā* by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78); *hi* dropped by "ato heḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-105); *śap* is *pit*, so the root accent remains. At the head of the pāda, "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) does not lower it. "dvyaco 'tas tiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-135): in the mantra the final *a* of a two-vowel *tiṅanta* is lengthened, so in the Saṃhitā the *a* of *piba* becomes long.

**धामभिः (*dhāmabhiḥ*)**: *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; "āto manin kvanib vanipaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-74) gives the suffix *manin*; being *nit*, *dhāman* is initial udātta by the *nit* accent.

**॥१०॥**

> -र्निष्ठेति क्तप्रत्ययः । दधातेर्हिरिति हिरादेशः । मनुषा हितो मनुर्हितः । कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलमिति समासः । कृत्स्वरापवादेन तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । सीदसि । षद्लृ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु । लटः सिप् । शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना सीदादेशः । निघातः । सेममित्यत्र संहितायां सो ऽचि लोपे चेत्पादपूरणं । पा. ६-१-१३४ । इति सोर्लोपे गुणः । अध्वरं । न विद्यते ध्वरो हिंसा यस्मिन्सो ऽध्वरः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । नो अध्वरमित्यत्र संहितायामेङः पदान्तादति । पा. ६-१-१०९ । इति पूर्वरूपं प्राप्तं प्रकृत्यान्तःपादमव्यपर इति प्रकृतिभावान्निवर्तते ॥
>
> *-rniṣṭheti ktapratyayaḥ | dadhāterhiriti hirādeśaḥ | manuṣā hito manurhitaḥ | kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulamiti samāsaḥ | kṛtsvarāpavādena tṛtīyā karmaṇīti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | sīdasi | ṣadlṛ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu | laṭaḥ sip | śapi pāghretyādinā sīdādeśaḥ | nighātaḥ | semamityatra saṃhitāyāṃ so 'ci lope cetpādapūraṇaṃ | pā. 6-1-134 | iti sorlope guṇaḥ | adhvaraṃ | na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasminso 'dhvaraḥ | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | no adhvaramityatra saṃhitāyāmeṅaḥ padāntādati | pā. 6-1-109 | iti pūrvarūpaṃ prāptaṃ prakṛtyāntaḥpādamavyapara iti prakṛtibhāvānnivartate ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni, you who are *manurhitaḥ*, set up by man in the form of the *hotṛ* and others, the accomplisher of the *homa*, who *sīdasi*, sit, at the sacrifices: such as you are, *yaja*, accomplish, this our *adhvara*, sacrifice." (Grammatical tail: *manuḥ*, "who thinks", with *us* (Uṇ. "2-122" [?]), initial udātta; *hitaḥ*, *kta* after *dhā* with *hi* for it; *manurhitaḥ*, "set up by man", compounded by *kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam*, the first-member accent by *tṛtīyā karmaṇi*, an exception to the *kṛt* accent; *sīdasi*, *sīd* for *sad*, lowered; *sa imam* → *semam* in the Saṃhitā by Pā. 6-1-134, the loss of *su* to fill the pāda, then *guṇa*; *adhvaram*, "in which there is no harm", final udātta by *nañsubhyām*; *no adhvaram*: the *pūrvarūpa* of Pā. 6-1-109 is barred by *prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni, (who) | **त्वम् (tvam)** — you | **मनुर्हितः (manurhitaḥ)** — appointed by men as *hotṛ* and the rest | **होता (hotā)** — as the accomplisher of the *homa* | **यज्ञेषु (yajñeṣu)** — at the times of our sacrifices | **सीदसि (sīdasi)** — sit (with us) | **सः (saḥ)** — such as you | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **इमम् अध्वरम् (imam adhvaram)** — this sacrifice | **यज (yaja)** — accomplish.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, you bring the gods to the sacrifice and stay with us at the times of the sacrifices that we men perform. Such as you are, accomplish our sacrifice.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Agni, appointed by man as the invoker of the gods you are present at the sacrifice. Therefore perform this our sacrifice.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Manurhitaḥ**:

> मन्यते इति मनुः । मनुषा होत्रादिरूपेण मनुष्येण हितः सम्पादितः ॥
>
> *manyate iti manuḥ | manuṣā hotrādirūpeṇa manuṣyeṇa hitaḥ sampāditaḥ ||*

Since the human sacrificer has appointed him to take part in the sacrificial rite, or since he bears the chief role in the sacrifice, he is the one placed in the fire-pit.

### Page 621 — Rik 11: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 621–622, noted briefly)*

**मनुर्हितः (*manurhitaḥ*)**: *manyate iti manuḥ*; *mana jñāne* (*divādi*). With *nit* (Uṇ. sū. "2-2-64" [?]) carried on, "bahulam anyatrāpi" (Uṇ. sū. "2-128" [?]): after other roots too *us* comes variously, and it is *nit*; so *us* after *man*: *manuḥ*; initial udātta (*nit*). **हितः (*hitaḥ*)**: *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ* + *kta* in the passive by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. sū. 3-2-102); *hi* for *dhā* by "dadhāter hiḥ" (7-4-42). *Manuṣā hitaḥ*: by "kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam" (Pā. sū. 2-1-32) a word in the third case denoting the agent or instrument is compounded with a fitting *kṛdanta*. "samāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-223) would give final udātta; overriding it, "tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…" (Pā. sū. 6-2-2) the first-member accent; overriding that, "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) the *kṛt* second-member accent; overriding that, "thāthaghañktājabitrakāṇām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-144) final udātta; and overriding that too, "tṛtīyā karmaṇi" (Pā. sū. 6-2-48) the first-member accent. In the Vedabhāṣya, after *kṛtsvarāpavādena*, one must add *thāthādisūtreṇāntodātte prāpte tadapavādena*. So the Śekharakāra says plainly under "tṛtīyā karmaṇi":

> अयमपि थाथादिस्वरापवादः
>
> *ayamapi thāthādisvarāpavādaḥ*

that is, this too is an exception to the accent laid down by *thāthaghañ…*.

**सीदसि (*sīdasi*)**: *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; *laṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*; *s* for *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ"; *śap* by "kartari śap"; *sīd* for *sad* by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78): *sīdasi*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ".

**सेमम् (*semam*)**: with *sas* + *imam*, "so 'ci lope cet pādapūraṇam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-134): if the loss fills the pāda, the *su* of *sas* drops before a vowel; so the *s* drops. If it did not drop, with *sas* + *imam*, *ru* by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66), *y* for the *ru* by "bhobhago…" (Pā. sū. 8-3-17): *say* + *imam*; *y* dropped by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. sū. 8-3-19): *sa* + *imam*; then, when the *guṇa* of "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-) is to be made, the loss of *y* by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" would be treated as not done by "pūrvatrāsi-

### Page 622 — Rik 11: grammar (end)

ddham" (Pā. sū. 8-2-1); so, from the point of view of the rule giving *guṇa*, it is *say imam*; the *a* is not followed by *i*, so no *guṇa*, and it would have to stay *sa imam*. Then in *semaṃ no adhvaraṃ yaja* it would have to be *sa imaṃ no adhvaraṃ yaja*: the pāda would have nine syllables, one more than the eight that fill it, so the pāda would not be filled. When the *s* drops by "so 'ci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-134), "pūrvatrāsiddham" does not apply, so *guṇa* comes: *semam*. In *semaṃ no adhvaraṃ yaja* there are eight syllables, so the pāda is filled.

**अध्वरम् (*adhvaram*)**: *na vidyate dhvaraḥ hiṃsā yasmin saḥ adhvaraḥ*: that in which there is no harm. Being a bahuvrīhi, the first-member accent would come; overriding it, "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172) makes the second member final udātta. With *nas* + *adhvaram*, *ru* for the *s* by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66); *u* for the *ru* by "ato ror aplutād aplute" (Pā. sū. 6-1-113): *na* + *u* + *adhvaram*; *guṇa* by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87): *no* + *adhvaram*. In the Saṃhitā "eṅaḥ padāntād ati" (Pā. sū. 6-1-109) would give *pūrvarūpa* when a short *a* follows a word-final *e*/*o*; but "prakṛtyāntaḥpādam avyapare" (Pā. sū. 6-1-115) keeps the natural form for *e*/*o* inside a Ṛk-pāda before a short *a* not followed by *v* or *y*. So there is no *pūrvarūpa*; it stays *no adhvaram*.

**॥११॥**

### Page 623 — Rik 12: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे देवाग्ने रोहितो रोहिच्छब्दाभिधेयास्त्वदीया वडवा रथे युक्ष्व । योजय । हिशब्दः पादपूरणार्थः । कीदृशीः । अरुषीर्गतिमतीर्हरितो हर्तुं रथारूढान्पुरुषान्नेतुं समर्थाः । ताभिर्वडवाभिरिहास्मिन्कर्मणि देवाना वह ॥ युक्ष्व । युजिर् योगे । लोट् । स्वरितेत्त्वादात्मनेपदं । थासः से । सवाभ्यां वामौ । रुधादिभ्यः श्नम् । तस्य बाहुलकाल्लुक् । कुत्वषत्वे । प्रत्ययस्वरेणान्तोदात्तः । संहितायां द्व्यचो ऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः । अरुषीः । ऋ गतौ । ऋच्छन्ति गच्छन्तीत्यरुष्यो वडवाः । ऋहनिभ्यामुषन् । उ. ४-७३ । धातोर्गुणो रपरत्वं । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तो ऽरुषशब्दः । तस्मात्स्त्रियां छान्दसो ङीप् । शसि प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः । पा. ६-१-१०२ । इति दीर्घः । रथे । रमेरौणादिकः क्थन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । हरितः । हृसृरुहियुषिभ्य इतिः । उ. १-९७ । इति हरतेरितिप्रत्ययः । इकारः प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । रोहितः । रुहेरपि तेनैव सूत्रेणेतिः । इकारः प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तः । ताभिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेः प्राप्तमुदात्तत्वं सावर्वर्णेति निषिध्यते । देवानित्यत्र पूर्ववद्रुत्वानुनासिकौ ॥ २७ ॥
>
> *he devāgne rohito rohicchabdābhidheyāstvadīyā vaḍavā rathe yukṣva | yojaya | hiśabdaḥ pādapūraṇārthaḥ | kīdṛśīḥ | aruṣīrgatimatīrharito hartuṃ rathārūḍhānpuruṣānnetuṃ samarthāḥ | tābhirvaḍavābhirihāsminkarmaṇi devānā vaha || yukṣva | yujir yoge | loṭ | svaritettvādātmanepadaṃ | thāsaḥ se | savābhyāṃ vāmau | rudhādibhyaḥ śnam | tasya bāhulakālluk | kutvaṣatve | pratyayasvareṇāntodāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ | aruṣīḥ | ṛ gatau | ṛcchanti gacchantītyaruṣyo vaḍavāḥ | ṛhanibhyāmuṣan | u. 4-73 | dhātorguṇo raparatvaṃ | nittvādādyudātto 'ruṣaśabdaḥ | tasmātstriyāṃ chāndaso ṅīp | śasi prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ | pā. 6-1-102 | iti dīrghaḥ | rathe | ramerauṇādikaḥ kthanpratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | haritaḥ | hṛsṛruhiyuṣibhya itiḥ | u. 1-97 | iti harateritipratyayaḥ | ikāraḥ pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | rohitaḥ | ruherapi tenaiva sūtreṇetiḥ | ikāraḥ pratyayasvareṇodāttaḥ | tābhiḥ | sāvekāca iti vibhakteḥ prāptamudāttatvaṃ sāvarvarṇeti niṣidhyate | devānityatra pūrvavadrutvānunāsikau || 27 ||*

**Translation:** "O god Agni, *yukṣva*, yoke, to the chariot your mares called by the word *rohit*. The word *hi* is to fill the pāda. What are they like? *Aruṣīḥ*, swift-moving; *haritaḥ*, able to carry, to take along, the men mounted on the chariot. With those mares bring the gods here to this rite." (Grammatical tail: *yukṣva*, *yuj* with *loṭ*, *ātmanepada* (*svaritet*), *se* for *thās*, *v* for the *e*, the *śnam* dropped, *k* and *ṣ*, final udātta by the suffix accent, lengthened in the Saṃhitā; *aruṣīḥ*, "the mares that go", *uṣan* after *ṛ* (Uṇ. 4-73), *guṇa*, *aruṣa* initial udātta, Vedic *ṅīp*, lengthening by Pā. 6-1-102; *rathe* with *kthan*, initial udātta; *haritaḥ* and *rohitaḥ* with *iti* (Uṇ. 1-97), the *i* udātta; *tābhiḥ*, the udātta of *sāv ekācaḥ* barred by *sāv avarṇa…*; *devān* as before. The closing "27" is the varga number.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**देव (deva)** — O shining Agni | **अरुषीः (aruṣīḥ)** — able to run swiftly | **हरितः (haritaḥ)** — able to draw | **रोहितः (rohitaḥ)** — your mares named *Rohit* | **रथे (rathe)** — to the chariot | **युक्ष्व (yukṣva)** — join (yoke to the pole) | **ताभिः (tābhiḥ)** — with the help of those mares | **इह (iha)** — for this our sacrificial rite | **देवान् (devān)** — the gods | **आ वह (ā vaha)** — bring.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, you are divine. Your mares called *Rohit* are strong; they can run swiftly; they can draw those seated without effort. Yoke those mares to your chariot and with their help bring the gods for this our sacrificial rite.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Agni, harness your twany [sic] red mares to your chariot and by means of them bring the gods hither.

### Page 624 — Rik 12: Special Topics and grammar

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Yukṣva**: the final syllable is long in the Saṃhitā to suit the metre.

**Aruṣīḥ**:

> ऋ गतौ । ऋच्छन्ति गच्छन्तीत्यरुष्यो वडवाः ॥
>
> *ṛ gatau | ṛcchanti gacchantītyaruṣyo vaḍavāḥ ||*

The root *ṛ* has the sense of going. Since horses are endowed with motion, they are called *aruṣyaḥ*; *aruṣīḥ* is the accusative plural.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 624–626, noted briefly)*

**युक्ष्व (*yukṣva*)**: *yujir yoge*; *loṭ*; the root is *svaritet*, so the *ātmanepada*; 2nd singular *thās*; *se* for it by "thāsas se" (Pā. sū. 3-4-80); *v* for the *e* by "savābhyāṃ vāmau" (Pā. sū. 3-4-91); the *vikaraṇa* *śnam* by "rudhādibhyaḥ śnam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-78), dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. sū. 2-4-73); *yuj* + *sva*: *g* for *j* by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-30); *k* by "khari ca" (Pā. sū. 8-4-55); *ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59): *yukṣva*. At the head of the pāda and not after a word, so "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) does not make it wholly unaccented; the suffix accent makes it final udātta. In the Saṃhitā "dvyaco 'tas tiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-135) lengthens the *a*.

**अरुषीः (*aruṣīḥ*)**: the root *ṛ gatau*. It is read in the *bhvādi* class as *ṛ gatiprāpaṇayoḥ*: *laṭ*, 3rd plural *jhi*, *ant* for *jh* by "jho 'ntaḥ", *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. "4-1-68" [as printed, for 3-1-68]): *ṛ* + *a* + *anti*; *ṛcch* for *ṛ* by "pāghrādhmā…": *ṛcchanti*. Another root *ṛ* is read in the *juhotyādi* class as *ṛ sṛ gatau*: *laṭ*, *jhi*, *śap*, then the loss of *śap* by "juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ" (2-4-75), reduplication by "ślau": *ṛ* + *ṛ* + *jhi*; "urat" (Pā. sū. 7-4-66): *a* for the *ṛ* of the reduplicate, with *r*; *i* for the *a* by "artipiparttyoś ca"; *ir* + *ṛ* + *jhi*; the *r* removed by "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ"; *jhi* is *ṅit* by "sārvadhātukam apit", so the second *ṛ* takes no *guṇa*; *iy* for the *i* by "abhyāsasyāsavarṇe": *iy* + *ṛ* + *jhi*; "adabhyastāt" (Pā. sū. 7-1-4): *at* for the *jh* after a reduplicated stem; *yaṇ* by "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77), *r* for the *ṛ*:

### Page 625 — Rik 12: grammar (continued)

*iyrati*. So from the root *ṛ* the form *ranti* does not arise. Here the analysis *iyrati* or *ṛcchanti gacchanti iti aruṣyaḥ vaḍavāḥ* is fitting. "ṛhanibhyām uṣan" (Uṇ. sū. "4-473" [?]; *ṛ gatau*, *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*): after these roots the suffix *uṣan*; so *uṣan* after *ṛ*; *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ", with *r* after it: *aruṣa*. In the Uṇādi text now available the reading is long, *ṛhanibhyām ūṣan*; on that reading the shortening of the *ū* here is Vedic. *Aruṣa* is initial udātta by the *nit* accent. After it, Vedic *ṅīp*; the *a* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148): *aruṣī*; accusative plural *śas*; *pūrvasavarṇa-dīrgha* by "prathamayoḥ pūrvasavarṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-102); *ru*, visarga: *aruṣīḥ*.

**रथे (*rathe*)**: *ramu krīḍāyām*; *ramante asminn iti rathaḥ*. "hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan" (Uṇ. sū. "2-159" [?]) gives the suffix *kthan*; "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" ("7-2-10") bars the *iṭ*; the *m* dropped by "anudāttopadeśa…" (Pā. sū. 6-4-37); initial udātta by the *nit* accent.

**हरितः (*haritaḥ*)**: "hṛsṛruhiyuṣibhya itiḥ" (Uṇ. sū. "1-96" [?]; *hṛñ haraṇe*, *sṛ gatau*, *ruha bījajanmani*, *yuṣ*, a *sautra* root): the suffix *iti*; *iti* after *hṛ*: *hṛ* + *it*; *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ", with *r*: *harit*; the *i* udātta by the suffix accent; accusative plural.

**रोहितः (*rohitaḥ*)**: *ruha bījajanmani*; *iti* after *ruh* too by "hṛsṛ…" (Uṇ. sū. "1-97" [?]); the *i* udātta by the suffix accent; *laghūpadha-guṇa* by "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-86), *o* for the *u*; accusative plural *rohitaḥ*.

**ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)**: *tad* + *bhis*; *a* for the *d* by "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102); *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97); *ṭāp* by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (Pā. sū. 4-1-4), lengthening: *tābhiḥ*. The udātta that "sāv ekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-168) would give the ending is barred by "na go-śvan-sāv-avarṇa…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-182); so by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4) the ending is unaccented.

**देवाँ इह (*devām̐ iha*)**: with *devān* + *iha*, in the Saṃhitā, *ru* for the *n* by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. sū. "8-4-9" [as printed, for 8-3-9]); the *ā* nasalised by "āto 'ṭi nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-3-3);

### Page 626 — Rik 12: grammar (end); close of Sūkta 14

*y* for the *ru* by "bhobhago…"; the *y* dropped by "lopaḥ śākalyasya" (Pā. sū. 8-3-19); since by "pūrvatrāsiddham" the loss of *y* is treated as not done, no *guṇa* by "ād guṇaḥ": *devām̐ iha*.

**॥१२॥**

*(The sūkta ends here; the print has no separate colophon for Sūkta 14. The bhāṣya closes with the varga number "27", agreeing with the heading's "26, 27".)*

## ॥ ಹದಿನೈದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು ॥ — Sūkta 15 — *"indra somaṃ piba"* ("The Fifteenth Sūkta")

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥ (introductory note on the application of the sūkta; printed p. 626, lower half; re-read from the print)**

> इन्द्र सोममित्यादिकस्य द्वादशर्चस्य चतुर्थस्य सूक्तस्य ऋषिच्छन्दसी पूर्ववत् । यद्यप्येतत्सूक्तं कृत्स्नमृतुदेवताकं तथापि प्रत्यृचमिन्द्रादिदेवतान्तराणि मिलितानि । तथा चानुक्रम्यते । इन्द्र सोममृतव्यं तत्रैन्द्री मारुती त्वाष्ट्र्याग्नेय्यैन्द्री मैत्रावरुणी चतस्रो द्रविणोदस आश्विनाग्नेय्य ऋतुदेवताः सर्वत्रेति ॥ विनियोगस्तु स्मार्तो द्रष्टव्यः ॥
>
> *indra somam ity-ādikasya dvādaśarcasya caturthasya sūktasya ṛṣi-chandasī pūrvavat | yady apy etat sūktaṃ kṛtsnam ṛtu-devatākaṃ tathāpi pratyṛcam indrādi-devatāntarāṇi militāni | tathā cānukramyate | indra somam ṛtavyaṃ tatraindrī mārutī tvāṣṭryāgneyyaindrī maitrāvaruṇī catasro draviṇodasa āśvināgneyya ṛtu-devatāḥ sarvatreti || viniyogas tu smārto draṣṭavyaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "The twelve-rik sūkta beginning *indra somam* is the fourth sūkta [of this anuvāka]; its ṛṣi and meter are as before [Medhātithi Kāṇva; Gāyatrī]. Although this whole sūkta has the Ṛtus (Seasons) for its deity, in each rik other deities, Indra and the rest, are joined with them. So the Anukramaṇikā says: '*indra somam ṛtavyam* ("*indra somam* is to the Ṛtus"): there [the deities are] *aindrī* (Indra), *mārutī* (the Maruts), *tvāṣṭrī* (Tvaṣṭṛ), *āgneyī* (Agni), *aindrī* (Indra), *maitrāvaruṇī* (Mitra and Varuṇa), the four to the Draviṇodases, *āśvinī* (the Aśvins), *āgneyī* (Agni): the Ṛtus are the deities throughout.' Its application (*viniyoga*) is to be seen from the *smārta* usage."

**॥ Anuvāda (Kannada rendering) ॥** The twelve-rik sūkta *indra somaṃ piba*, the fourth sūkta of the fourth anuvāka. Its ṛṣi and meter are as in the preceding sūkta. Although all the riks of this sūkta have the Ṛtus as deities, in each rik the deities Indra and others are joined with the Ṛtu. In the Anukramaṇikā: "*indra somam ṛtavyam tatraindrī, mārutī, tvāṣṭrī, āgneyī, aindrī, maitrāvaruṇī*, four [riks] to the *draviṇodas*, *āśvinī*, *āgneyī*; the Ṛtus are the deities in all" — that is, the whole sūkta is in praise of the Ṛtu-deities. With that Ṛtu, the deities Indra, the Maruts, Tvaṣṭṛ, Agni, Indra, Mitrāvaruṇau [belong] one to each rik; the next four riks have the deity Draviṇodāḥ, and of the remaining two riks the deities are in order the Aśvinau and Agni. The application is to be understood from the *smārta* usage.

### Page 628 — Rik 1: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

> -दिना मन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पिब । पिबा मित्रस्य । ऋग्वे. १-१४-१० । इत्यत्रोक्तं । अस्य त्वा विशन्त्वित्युत्तरवाक्यगताख्यातार्थेन सह समुच्चयार्थश्चशब्दो लुप्तः । अतश्चादिलोपे विभाषेतीयं प्रथमा तिङ्विभक्तिर्न निहन्यते । विशन्त्विति चलोपसाम्ये ऽपि द्वितीयत्वान्निहन्यत एव । संहितायामाद्गुण इति प्राप्तस्य गुणस्य ऋत्यकः । पा. ६-१-१२८ । इति शाकल्यमते प्रकृतिभावादभावः । इन्दवः । प्र वो भ्रियन्त । ऋग्वे. १-१४-४ [?] । इत्यत्रोक्तं । मत्सरासः । तत्रैवोक्तं । आज्जसेरसुगित्यसुक् । तदोकसः । तदेवौकः स्थानं येषां ते तथोक्ताः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥

> *-dinā man | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | piba | pibā mitrasya | ṛgve. 1-14-10 | ityatroktaṃ | asya tvā viśantvityuttaravākyagatākhyātārthena saha samuccayārthaścaśabdo luptaḥ | ataścādilope vibhāṣetīyaṃ prathamā tiṅvibhaktirna nihanyate | viśantviti calopasāmye 'pi dvitīyatvānnihanyata eva | saṃhitāyāmādguṇa iti prāptasya guṇasya ṛtyakaḥ | pā. 6-1-128 | iti śākalyamate prakṛtibhāvādabhāvaḥ | indavaḥ | pra vo bhriyanta | ṛgve. 1-14-4 [?] | ityatroktaṃ | matsarāsaḥ | tatraivoktaṃ | ājjaserasugityasuk | tadokasaḥ | tadevaukaḥ sthānaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra, drink the soma together with the Ṛtu. May the *indavaḥ*, the soma juices being drunk, *ā viśantu*, enter you. What are they like? *Matsarāsaḥ*, causing satisfaction; *tadokasaḥ*, having that as their dwelling: the sense is that they always stay in your belly." (Grammatical tail: *indra*, initial udātta by the *ṣāṣṭhika* rule; *somam* with *man*, initial udātta; *piba*, as said at Ṛ. 1-14-10; the word *ca* joining it with the verb of the next clause, *tvā viśantu*, is dropped, so by *cādilope vibhāṣā* this first *tiṅ* form is not lowered, while *viśantu*, being the second, is; in the Saṃhitā the *guṇa* of *ād guṇaḥ* does not come, by Śākalya's view in Pā. 6-1-128 (*ṛty akaḥ*); *indavaḥ* and *matsarāsaḥ* as said at Ṛ. "1-14-4" [?], *asuk* by *ājjaser asuk*; *tadokasaḥ*, "whose dwelling is that", a bahuvrīhi with the first-member accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**इन्द्र (indra)** — O Indra | **ऋतुना सह (ṛtunā saha)** — together with the Ṛtu deity | **सोमम् (somam)** — the soma juice | **पिब (piba)** — drink | **मत्सरासः (matsarāsaḥ)** — giving satisfaction | **इन्दवः (indavaḥ)** — the soma juices | **तदोकसः (tadokasaḥ)** — having your belly as their very dwelling | **त्वाम् (tvām)** — you (your belly) | **आ विशन्तु (ā viśantu)** — may they enter.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra, drink the soma juice with the Ṛtu deity. It gives you satisfaction. And may it enter your belly so as to stay in your belly always as its home.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Indra, drink with the Ritu (season) the Soma juice; let the satisfying drops enter your stomach and stay there (as if that were their home).

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Tadokasaḥ**:

> तन्निवासाः । सर्वदा त्वदुदरस्थायिन इत्यर्थः । तदेवौकः स्थानं येषां ते तदोकसः ॥
>
> *tannivāsāḥ | sarvadā tvadudarasthāyina ityarthaḥ | tadevaukaḥ sthānaṃ yeṣāṃ te tadokasaḥ ||*

That is, your belly, which is that very dwelling, is always the dwelling of the soma juice. "May the soma juice always be in your belly" means "may you always be drinking soma".

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 628–629, noted briefly)*

**इन्द्र (*indra*)**: initial udātta by the sixth-adhyāya sūtra "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198).

### Page 629 — Rik 1: grammar (end)

**सोमम् (*somam*)**: the suffix *man* by "artistusu…" (Uṇ. sū. "1-1-36" [as printed]); being *nit*, initial udātta by the *nit* accent.

**पिब (*piba*)**: explained at *pibā mitrasya* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-10). Here the word *ca*, which would join it with the verb (*tiṅanta*) of the following clause *ā tvā viśantu*, is dropped, that is, not used. So by "cādilope vibhāṣā" (Pā. sū. 8-1-63): when *ca*, *vā*, *ha*, *aha*, *eva* are dropped, the first *tiṅanta* is not unaccented. The śāstra does not enjoin a dropping of *ca*, *vā* and the rest; so "dropping" here means not using them: since the sense of *ca* is understood from the meaning and context, *ca* and the rest are not used. *Ca* means conjunction; *aha* means "only". When the two *tiṅantas* have the same agent, *ca* is dropped; when the agents differ, *aha* is dropped. This rule holds only when *eva*, meaning restriction, is used, not everywhere. Where they are so left unused, the *tiṅanta* is not lowered. In *viśantu* too the dropping of *ca* is alike, but it is not the first *tiṅanta*, so it is lowered. *Piba* + *ṛtunā*: in the Saṃhitā *guṇa* would come by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87); but "ṛty akaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-128): in Śākalya's view the *a*, *i*, *u*, *ṛ* at the end of a word before a short *ṛ* is short (natural form); so the *a* of *piba* stays short. By the force of this rule of shortness the *guṇa* does not come; the commentators explain it as natural form with this result in mind.

**इन्दवः (*indavaḥ*)**: its formation is set out at the mantra *pra vo bhriyanta indavaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-4). Here the augment *asuk* comes by "ājjaser asuk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-50) [for *matsarāsaḥ*].

**तदोकसः (*tadokasaḥ*)**: *tat okaḥ sthānaṃ yeṣāṃ te tadokasaḥ*: the soma juices whose dwelling is Indra's belly itself. Being a bahuvrīhi compound, by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the first-member accent comes.

**॥१॥**

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

>
> *marutaḥ | pibata | ṛtunā | potrāt | yajñam | punītana ||*
> *yūyam | hi | stha | su 'dānavaḥ ||2||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे मरुत ऋतुना सह पोत्रात्पोतृनामकस्य ऋत्विजः पात्रात्सोमं पिबत । ततो ऽस्मदीयं यज्ञं पुनीतन । शोधयत । हे सुदानवः शोभनदातारो मरुतः । हि यस्माद्यूयं स्थ युष्माकं शोधयितृत्वं प्रसिद्धं । तस्माच्छोधयतेत्यर्थः ॥ पिबत । अत्र तिङो ऽदुपदेशाच्छपः परत्वाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वं । धातुस्वरः । पूर्वामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वेन पदादपरत्वान्निघाताभावः । पूर्ववत्प्रकृतिभावः । पोत्रात् । पोतुः सम्बन्धि पात्रं पोत्रं । तस्येदमित्यण् । तद्धितेष्वचामादेः । पा. ७-२-११७ । इति प्राप्ता वृद्धिः सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्त इति न भवति । नन्वेवमन्त्यस्य ऋकारस्याचो ञ्णिति । पा. ७-२-११५ । इति वृद्धिः प्राप्नोति । त्वाष्ट्रो जागत इत्यत्र हि विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यं । पा. १-४-२ । इति परयादिवृद्ध्यान्त्योपधलक्षणा वृद्धिर्बाध्यत इत्युक्तं । इह तु परस्या आदिवृद्धेश्छान्दसत्वेन निवृत्तत्वादन्त्यवृद्धिः प्राप्नोत्येवेति । एवं तर्ह्यत्राप्यादिवृद्धिरौकारः क्रियतां । तस्य तु छान्दस ओकारो भविष्यति । पुनीतन । पूञ् पवने । लोट् । लोटो लङ्वत् । पा. ३-४-८५ । इति लङ्वद्भावात्तस्य तस्थस्थमिपामिति तादेशः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । ई हल्यघोरितीकारः । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तनादेशः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वः । प्रत्ययद्वयस्यापि सार्वधातुकमपिदिति ङित्त्वात्तत्पूर्वयोरिकोर्गुणाभावः । यूयं । युष्मदः परस्य जसो ङे प्रथमयोरम् । पा. ७-१-२८ । इत्यमादेशः । न विभक्तौ तुस्माः । पा. १-३-४ । इति मकारस्येत्संज्ञाप्रतिषेधः । यूयवयौ जसि । पा. ७-२-९३ । इति मपर्यन्तस्य यूयादेशः । शेषे लोपः । अत्र यूयादेशात्प्रा-
>
> *he maruta ṛtunā saha potrātpotṛnāmakasya ṛtvijaḥ pātrātsomaṃ pibata | tato 'smadīyaṃ yajñaṃ punītana | śodhayata | he sudānavaḥ śobhanadātāro marutaḥ | hi yasmādyūyaṃ stha yuṣmākaṃ śodhayitṛtvaṃ prasiddhaṃ | tasmācchodhayatetyarthaḥ || pibata | atra tiṅo 'dupadeśācchapaḥ paratvāllasārvadhātukānudāttatvaṃ | dhātusvaraḥ | pūrvāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvena padādaparatvānnighātābhāvaḥ | pūrvavatprakṛtibhāvaḥ | potrāt | potuḥ sambandhi pātraṃ potraṃ | tasyedamityaṇ | taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ | pā. 7-2-117 | iti prāptā vṛddhiḥ sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyanta iti na bhavati | nanvevamantyasya ṛkārasyāco ñṇiti | pā. 7-2-115 | iti vṛddhiḥ prāpnoti | tvāṣṭro jāgata ityatra hi vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryaṃ | pā. 1-4-2 | iti parayādivṛddhyāntyopadhalakṣaṇā vṛddhirbādhyata ityuktaṃ | iha tu parasyā ādivṛddheśchāndasatvena nivṛttatvādantyavṛddhiḥ prāpnotyeveti | evaṃ tarhyatrāpyādivṛddhiraukāraḥ kriyatāṃ | tasya tu chāndasa okāro bhaviṣyati | punītana | pūñ pavane | loṭ | loṭo laṅvat | pā. 3-4-85 | iti laṅvadbhāvāttasya tasthasthamipāmiti tādeśaḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | ī halyaghoritīkāraḥ | taptanaptanathanāśceti tanādeśaḥ | pvādīnāṃ hrasva iti hrasvaḥ | pratyayadvayasyāpi sārvadhātukamapiditi ṅittvāttatpūrvayorikorguṇābhāvaḥ | yūyaṃ | yuṣmadaḥ parasya jaso ṅe prathamayoram | pā. 7-1-28 | ityamādeśaḥ | na vibhaktau tusmāḥ | pā. 1-3-4 | iti makārasyetsaṃjñāpratiṣedhaḥ | yūyavayau jasi | pā. 7-2-93 | iti maparyantasya yūyādeśaḥ | śeṣe lopaḥ | atra yūyādeśātprā-*

### Page 631 — Rik 2: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

> -गेवान्तरङ्गत्वात्प्रातिपदिकस्यान्तोदात्तत्वं । शेषनिघातः । ततो यूयादेशः स्थाने ऽन्तरतमः । पा. १-१-५० । इति सर्वानुदात्तः । तत्र शेषे लोपो ऽन्त्यलोप इति पक्षे पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घत्वं बाधित्वा यो ऽयममि पूर्वः । पा. ६-१-१०७ । इति प्रातिपदिकान्तेनोदात्तेन सहानुदात्तस्य सुप एकादेशः स एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । टिलोपपक्षे तूदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । स्थ । अस भुवि । लटो मध्यमबहुवचनं थ । अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः शप इति शपो लुक् । श्नसोरल्लोप इत्यकारलोपः । व्यत्ययेन षत्वं । हि चेति निषेधात्तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति । संहिता-
>
> *-gevāntaraṅgatvātprātipadikasyāntodāttatvaṃ | śeṣanighātaḥ | tato yūyādeśaḥ sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ | pā. 1-1-50 | iti sarvānudāttaḥ | tatra śeṣe lopo 'ntyalopa iti pakṣe pūrvasavarṇadīrghatvaṃ bādhitvā yo 'yamami pūrvaḥ | pā. 6-1-107 | iti prātipadikāntenodāttena sahānudāttasya supa ekādeśaḥ sa ekādeśa udāttenodātta ityudāttaḥ | ṭilopapakṣe tūdāttanivṛttisvareṇa vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | stha | asa bhuvi | laṭo madhyamabahuvacanaṃ tha | adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapa iti śapo luk | śnasorallopa ityakāralopaḥ | vyatyayena ṣatvaṃ | hi ceti niṣedhāttiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati | saṃhitā-*

> -यामन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति दीर्घत्वं । अत्र हे सुदानवो यूयं हि स्थेति विवक्षितं । सुदानवः । दाभाभ्यां नुः । उ. ३-३२ । सोः प्रादिसमासः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । अत्र यूयमित्युद्दिश्य सुदानवः स्थेति न विधीयते येनानामन्त्रितत्वान्निघातो न स्यात् । किन्तु सुदानव इति सिद्धवद्दातृत्वेन सम्बोध्य तेषु तेषु मारुतसूक्तेषु मरुतां प्रसिद्धात्प्रभावातिशयाद्यूयं स्थेति युष्मच्छब्देन प्रतिनिर्दिश्य पुनीतनेति प्रार्थने पवने तेषां हेतुत्वं हिशब्देनोच्यते ॥
>
> *-yāmanyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti dīrghatvaṃ | atra he sudānavo yūyaṃ hi stheti vivakṣitaṃ | sudānavaḥ | dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ | u. 3-32 | soḥ prādisamāsaḥ | āmantritanighātaḥ | atra yūyamityuddiśya sudānavaḥ stheti na vidhīyate yenānāmantritatvānnighāto na syāt | kintu sudānava iti siddhavaddātṛtvena sambodhya teṣu teṣu mārutasūkteṣu marutāṃ prasiddhātprabhāvātiśayādyūyaṃ stheti yuṣmacchabdena pratinirdiśya punītaneti prārthane pavane teṣāṃ hetutvaṃ hiśabdenocyate ||*

**Translation:** "O Maruts, together with the Ṛtu, drink the soma from the vessel of the priest called Potṛ. Then *punītana*, purify, our sacrifice. O *sudānavaḥ*, good givers, Maruts: for *hi*, since, you are (such); your power to purify is well known; so purify: that is the sense." (Grammatical tail: *pibata*: the ending unaccented after the *śap* of *adupadeśa*, the root accent; not lowered, since the vocative before it counts as absent and it is not after a word; natural form as before; *potrāt*, "the Potṛ's vessel", *aṇ*; the initial *vṛddhi* (Pā. 7-2-117) is optional in the Veda and does not come; then the final *vṛddhi* of Pā. 7-2-115 would come (in *tvāṣṭro jāgataḥ* it is overridden by the later initial *vṛddhi*, Pā. 1-4-2, but here that later rule is withdrawn as Vedic); "then let the initial *vṛddhi* *au* be made here too, and it will become a Vedic *o*"; *punītana*: *pū* with *loṭ*, *ta*, *śnā*, *ī*, *tana*, shortening, no *guṇa* (*ṅit*); *yūyam*: *am* for *jas* (Pā. 7-1-28), its *m* not *it* (Pā. 1-3-4), *yūya* for the part up to *m* (Pā. 7-2-93), *śeṣe lopaḥ*; the stem accent comes first as *antaraṅga*, then the unaccented *yūya* by Pā. 1-1-50; *am* by Pā. 6-1-107, udātta as a single replacement; on the *ṭi*-loss view the ending is udātta by the *udāttanivṛtti* accent; *stha*: *as*, *tha*, *śap* dropped, the *a* dropped, *ṣ* by *vyatyaya*, not lowered because of *hi*, lengthened in the Saṃhitā; *sudānavaḥ* with *nu* (Uṇ. 3-32), a *prādi* compound, lowered as a vocative: the sense intended is "O good givers, you are (such)", not a predication "you are good givers", else it would not be a vocative and would not be lowered; *hi* gives the reason, the Maruts' well-known power praised in the Māruta sūktas.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**मरुतः (marutaḥ)** — O Maruts | **ऋतुना (ṛtunā)** — together with the Ṛtu deity | **पोत्रात् (potrāt)** — from the vessel of the priest called Potṛ | **पिबत (pibata)** — drink (the soma juice); (then) | **यज्ञम् (yajñam)** — our sacrifice | **पुनीतन (punītana)** — make pure | **सुदानवः (sudānavaḥ)** — Marut deities who give well what is desired | **यूयम् (yūyam)** — you | **हि स्थ (hi stha)** — are you not known in the mantras as such?

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Maruts, first drink the soma juice of our sacrifice from the vessel of the priest called Potṛ together with the Ṛtu deity, and then make our sacrifice pure. O Maruts, who give what is desired, are you not the ones famed in the mantras as so mighty?

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> O Maruts, drink with Ritu from the Potri's sacrificial cup; consecrate the sacrifice, for you are great givers.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Potrāt**: one of the sixteen priests who take part in the sacrifice is called Potṛ. He ordinarily works together with the priest called Neṣṭṛ. Here, for the words *potrāt pibata*, the Bhāṣyakāra explains

> पोतुः सम्बन्धिपात्रात् सोमं पिबत
>
> *potuḥ sambandhipātrāt somaṃ pibata*

"drink the soma juice in the Potṛ's vessel".

**Sudānavaḥ**:

> शोभनदातारः । अथवा सुष्ठु दातारः
>
> *śobhanadātāraḥ | athavā suṣṭhu dātāraḥ*

those who give good things, or who give well (abundantly).

### Page 632 — Rik 2: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 632–635, noted briefly)*

**पिबत (*pibata*)**: *pā pāne*; *loṭ*, 2nd plural *tha*. "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85): the operations of *laṅ* come for *loṭ*, so the *laṅvadbhāva* is an *atideśa*:

> अतिदेशः = तद्धर्माभाववति तद्धर्मबोधकत्वम्
>
> *atideśaḥ = taddharmābhāvavati taddharmabodhakatvam*

that is, ascribing a property to what lacks it: *loṭ* does not have the form of *laṅ*, so the *laṅ* operations could not come, but they come by this sūtra. *Ta* for *tha* by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. "3-4-100" [as printed, for 3-4-101]); *śap*; *pib* for *pā* by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78): *pibata*. *Śap* is *pit*, so unaccented; the *ta*, a *sārvadhātuka* for a *lakāra*, follows the *a*-final *śap*, so it is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186); the root accent remains. The vocative *marutaḥ* before it is treated as absent by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. sū. "8-1-2" [as printed, for 8-1-72]); so *pibata* does not follow a word and is at the head of the pāda, and "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not make it wholly unaccented.

**पोत्रात् (*potrāt*)**: *potuḥ idam* (the vessel belonging to the Potṛ). "tasyedam" (Pā. sū. 4-3-120): after the genitive of a fitting *prātipadika*, the suffix *aṇ* in the sense "this belongs to it". Of the two fitting words *potuḥ* and *idam*, the first named in the sūtra is *tasya*; so after the genitive *potuḥ*, *aṇ* in the sense *idam*: *potṛ* + *as* + *a*; a *prātipadika* by "kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-2-46); the ending dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71): *potṛ* + *a*. "taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-117) would give *vṛddhi* to the first vowel; but by

> सर्वे विधयश्छन्दसि विकल्प्यन्ते
>
> *sarve vidhayaśchandasi vikalpyante*

*(paribhāṣā 35)* this *vṛddhi* is optional and does not come. Without it, "aco ñṇiti" (Pā. sū. 7-2-115) would give *vṛddhi* to the final *ṛ* of *potṛ*: for the *su* after *go*, "goto ṇit" (Pā. sū. 7-1-90) gives *ṇit*; *su* is not a *taddhita*, so no initial *vṛddhi*, and "aco ñṇiti" has scope there; after *pac*, *ṇvul* gives *aka*: *pac* + *aka*

### Page 633 — Rik 2: grammar (continued)

here neither initial nor final *vṛddhi* applies; "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116) gives the penultimate *vṛddhi*: *pācaka*; so the penultimate *vṛddhi* has scope there. *Sauśrutaḥ*, *suśrutaḥ apatyaṃ pumān*: "tasyāpatyam" (Pā. sū. 4-1-92) *aṇ*: *suśrut* + *a*; the stem does not end in a vowel, so no final *vṛddhi* by "aco ñṇiti" (Pā. sū. 7-2-115); the penultimate is not *a*, so no penultimate *vṛddhi*; where final and penultimate *vṛddhi* do not come, the initial *vṛddhi* has scope. So each of the three has its own field. In *tvaṣṭuḥ apatyaṃ pumān tvāṣṭraḥ*, with *aṇ* after *tvaṣṭṛ* in the sense of *apatya*, both final and initial *vṛddhi* apply; in *jagat* + *a*, both penultimate and initial *vṛddhi*. When so, "vipratiṣedhe paraṃ kāryam" (Pā. sū. 1-4-2): when rules that have scope elsewhere apply to one case at one time, that is *vipratiṣedha*, and the later rule wins; so in both places the later initial *vṛddhi* overrides the final and penultimate *vṛddhi*. Once the initial *vṛddhi* has come, by

> सकृद्गतौ विप्रतिषेधेन यद्बाधितं तद्बाधितमेव
>
> *sakṛdgatau vipratiṣedhena yadbādhitaṃ tadbādhitameva*

*(paribhāṣā 40)* the final and penultimate *vṛddhi* do not come again. Since Puṣkarasad is read in the *anuśatikādi* class for *vṛddhi* of both members, here

> पुनःप्रसङ्गविज्ञानात्सिद्धम्
>
> *punaḥprasaṅgavijñānātsiddham*

*(paribhāṣā 39)* does not apply: on the view that relies on this paribhāṣā, with *puṣkarasad* + *i*, if both initial and penultimate *vṛddhi* came, the form *pauṣkarasādi* would be got, and the reading of *puṣkarasad* in *anuśatikādi* for *vṛddhi* of both members by "anuśatikādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 7-3-20) would be useless. So here the *sakṛdgati* applies, not the *punaḥprasaṅga*. Thus the initial *vṛddhi* overrides the final and penultimate *vṛddhi*. The Kaumudī states this point as

> आदिवृद्धिरन्त्योपधावृद्धी बाधते
>
> *ādivṛddhirantyopadhāvṛddhī bādhate*

Here the overriding initial *vṛddhi* does not come, being optional in the Veda, so the final *vṛddhi* is not overridden, and one may say the final *vṛddhi* should come. On that view, let the initial *vṛddhi* come here too: in *pautra* the *au* becomes *o* as a Vedic form, they say. Then, being overridden by the initial *vṛddhi*, the final *vṛddhi* does not come.

**पुनीतन (*punītana*)**: *pūñ pavane* (*kryādi*); *loṭ*, *parasmaipada* 2nd plural *tha*: *pū* + *tha*; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the *laṅvadbhāva*, so *ta* for *tha* by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101); *tana* for *ta* by "taptanaptanathanāś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-1-45): *pū* + *tana*; the *vikaraṇa* *śnā* by "kryādibhyaḥ śnā" (Pā. sū. 3-1-81): *pū* + *nā* + *tana*. "ī halyaghoḥ"

### Page 634 — Rik 2: grammar (continued)

(Pā. sū. 6-4-113): before a consonant-initial *sārvadhātuka* that is *kit* or *ṅit*, *ī* for the *ā* of *śnā* and of reduplicated stems: *pū* + *nī* + *tana*; *pū* shortened by "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-80): *punītana*. Both *nī* and *tana* are *apit* *sārvadhātukas*, so *ṅit* by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4); "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) bars *guṇa*; so neither the *ī* before *tana* nor the *u* before *nī* takes *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84).

**यूयम् (*yūyam*)**: "yuṣyasibhyāṃ madik" (Uṇ. sū. 1-136): *yuṣ* is a *sautra* root; after it the suffix *madik*: *yuṣmad*, final udātta by the suffix accent. On the view

> उणादयो ऽव्युत्पन्नानि प्रातिपदिकानि
>
> *uṇādayo 'vyutpannāni prātipadikāni*

*(paribhāṣā 22)*, that words formed by Uṇādi sūtras are underived stems without division into base and suffix, it is final udātta by "phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ" (Phi. sū. 1). *Yuṣmad* + *jas*; "ṅe prathamayor am" (Pā. sū. "7-1-25" [?]): *am* for the first and second case endings after *yuṣmad* and *asmad*: *yuṣmad* + *am*. The *m* of *am* would be *it* by "hal antyam" (Pā. sū. 1-3-3), but "na vibhaktau tusmāḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-3-4) bars it for dentals, *s* and *m* in an ending. "yūyavayau jasi" (Pā. sū. 7-2-93): before *jas*, *yūya* and *vaya* for the part up to *m* of *yuṣmad* and *asmad*: *yūya* + *ad* + *am*. *Śeṣe lopaḥ* comes with reference to an ending that is not the cause of *ātva* or *yatva*; so, its cause being outside, it is *bahiraṅga*; the *pararūpa* of "ato guṇe", whose cause is inside, is *antaraṅga*. So by

> असिद्धं बहिरङ्गमन्तरङ्गे
>
> *asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgamantaraṅge*

*(paribhāṣā 50)* *śeṣe lopaḥ* counts as not done, and the *pararūpa* comes first; though *śeṣe lopaḥ* is later, it does not come first. With *pararūpa*: *yuṣmad* + *am*. Then "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-90) comes. Here, before the *bahiraṅga* *yūya* replacement, being *antaraṅga*, the suffix accent or the stem accent comes first. By "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-158) the *śeṣanighāta* makes *yuṣma* unaccented; then by the paribhāṣā "sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-50) the wholly unaccented *yūya* comes in place of the unaccented *yuṣma*. The *pararūpa*, a single replacement, of *yūya* + *ad* is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-5). "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-90): before an ending other than the causes of *ātva* and *yatva*, the final of *yuṣmad*/*asmad* drops: that is the sense of the sūtra;

### Page 635 — Rik 2: grammar (end)

on the view that the final drops, the *d* drops: *yūya* + *am*. "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107) gives *pūrvarūpa* as the single replacement; the *a* so arising is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-5). Taking "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-90) with *śeṣa* as a locative in the sense of place, the sense is: before such an ending, the *ad* after the *m*-portion drops; then in *yūyad* + *am* the *ad* drops. On this view the udātta *ad* drops with reference to the unaccented *am*; so by the *udāttanivṛtti* accent "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-161) the ending becomes udātta. On both views *yūyam* is final udātta.

**स्थ (*stha*)**: *asa bhuvi*; *laṭ*, *parasmaipada* 2nd plural *tha*; the *vikaraṇa* *śap* of "kartari śap" is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ"; *as* + *tha*; "śnasor allopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-111): the *a* of *śnam* and of *as* drops before a *kit* or *ṅit* *sārvadhātuka*: *stha*. By *vyatyaya* *ṣ* for the *s*; *ṭh* by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-4-41): *ṣṭha*. By "hi ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-34) a *tiṅanta* joined with *hi* is not unaccented; here there is the use of *hi*, so the bar applies, and "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not lower it. In the Saṃhitā it is lengthened by "anyeṣām api dṛśyate".

**सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*)**: "dābhābhyāṃ nuḥ" (Uṇ. sū. 3-32; *ḍudāñ dāne*, *bhā dīptau*): after these the suffix *nu*: *dānu*. With *su*, a compound by "kugatiprādayaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-2-18); vocative plural; it is a vocative, so wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19). Here *sudānavaḥ* is not taken as a nominative plural with *yūyaṃ sudānavaḥ stha*, predicating "you are well-known givers" of the Maruts meant by *yūyam*; for then *sudānavaḥ* would not be a vocative, and its vocative lowering would not fit. So *sudānavaḥ* is a vocative plural, and the intended sense is *he sudānavaḥ yūyaṃ hi stha*: "O Maruts, well-known givers, you are endowed with the great power set out in the several Māruta sūktas": addressing the Maruts by their established generosity as *sudānavaḥ*, and pointing back by *yūyam* to the great powers famed in those sūktas, when one prays *punītana*, "purify", the word *hi* conveys that those great powers, gathered under the word *yuṣmad*, are the reason for the purifying.

**॥२॥**

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अ॒भि य॒ज्ञं गृ॑णीहि नो॒ ग्नावो॒ नेष्टः॒ पिब॑ ऋ॒तुना॑ ।
> त्वं हि र॑त्न॒धा असि॑ ॥३॥
>
> *abhí yajñáṃ gṛṇīhi no gnā́vo néṣṭaḥ píba ṛtúnā |*
> *tvaṃ hí ratnadhā́ ási ||3||*

### Page 636 — Rik 3: Pada and bhāṣya

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अभि । यज्ञम् । गृणीहि । नः । ग्नावः । नेष्टरिति । पिब । ऋतुना ॥
> त्वम् । हि । रत्नऽधाः । असि ॥३॥
>
> *abhi | yajñam | gṛṇīhi | naḥ | gnāvaḥ | neṣṭariti | piba | ṛtunā ||*
> *tvam | hi | ratna 'dhāḥ | asi ||3||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> ग्नाशब्दः स्त्रीवाची । तथा च यास्क आह । मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां मेना मानयन्त्येना ग्ना गच्छन्त्येनाः । नि. ३-२१ । इति । ग्ना अस्य सन्तीति ग्नावान् । नेष्टृशब्दो ऽत्र त्वष्टारं देवमाह । कस्मिंश्चिद्देवसत्रे नेष्टृत्वेन त्वष्टुर्वर्तितत्वात् । हे ग्नावः पत्नीयुक्त नेष्टस्त्वष्टः नो ऽस्मदीयं यज्ञमभि गृणीहि । अभितो देवानां समीपे स्तुहि । ऋतुना सह त्वं सोमं पिब । हि यस्मात्त्वं रत्नधा असि रत्नानां दाता भवसि तस्मात्सोमं पातुमर्हसीत्यर्थः ॥ अभि । उपसर्गाश्चाभिवर्जं । फि. ४-१३ । इति पर्युदासादभेरन्तोदात्तत्वं । गृणीहि । गॄ शब्दे । लोटि सिपो हिः । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । हेर्ङित्त्वादी हल्यघोरितीत्वं । श्नाप्रत्ययस्य ङित्त्वाद्गुणाभावः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । ग्ना अस्य सन्तीति मतुप् । व्यत्ययेन वत्वं । सम्बुद्धौ मतुवसो रुरिति रुत्वं । विसर्गः । पादादित्वेनामन्त्रितनिघाताभावात्षाष्ठिकमामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । ग्नाव इत्यस्य विशेषणतया विशेषवचनत्वान्नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरण इति निषेधाभावादविद्यमानवत्त्वेनोत्तरस्य नेष्टृशब्दस्य षाष्ठिकमाद्युदात्तत्वं । पिब । शपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । पूर्वयोरामन्त्रितयोरविद्यमानवत्त्वेन निघाताभावः । रत्नानि दधातीति रत्नधाः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । धातुस्वरः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । असि । सिपः पित्त्वाद्धातुस्वरः । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातो न भवति हि चेति प्रतिषेधात् ॥
>
> *gnāśabdaḥ strīvācī | tathā ca yāska āha | menā gnā iti strīṇāṃ menā mānayantyenā gnā gacchantyenāḥ | ni. 3-21 | iti | gnā asya santīti gnāvān | neṣṭṛśabdo 'tra tvaṣṭāraṃ devamāha | kasmiṃściddevasatre neṣṭṛtvena tvaṣṭurvartitatvāt | he gnāvaḥ patnīyukta neṣṭastvaṣṭaḥ no 'smadīyaṃ yajñamabhi gṛṇīhi | abhito devānāṃ samīpe stuhi | ṛtunā saha tvaṃ somaṃ piba | hi yasmāttvaṃ ratnadhā asi ratnānāṃ dātā bhavasi tasmātsomaṃ pātumarhasītyarthaḥ || abhi | upasargāścābhivarjaṃ | phi. 4-13 | iti paryudāsādabherantodāttatvaṃ | gṛṇīhi | gṝ śabde | loṭi sipo hiḥ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | herṅittvādī halyaghoritītvaṃ | śnāpratyayasya ṅittvādguṇābhāvaḥ | pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | gnā asya santīti matup | vyatyayena vatvaṃ | sambuddhau matuvaso ruriti rutvaṃ | visargaḥ | pādāditvenāmantritanighātābhāvātṣāṣṭhikamāmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | gnāva ityasya viśeṣaṇatayā viśeṣavacanatvānnāmantrite samānādhikaraṇa iti niṣedhābhāvādavidyamānavattvenottarasya neṣṭṛśabdasya ṣāṣṭhikamādyudāttatvaṃ | piba | śapaḥ pittvāddhātusvaraḥ | pūrvayorāmantritayoravidyamānavattvena nighātābhāvaḥ | ratnāni dadhātīti ratnadhāḥ | kvipceti kvip | dhātusvaraḥ | samāse kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvena sa eva śiṣyate | asi | sipaḥ pittvāddhātusvaraḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighāto na bhavati hi ceti pratiṣedhāt ||*

**Translation:** "The word *gnā* denotes woman; so Yāska says, '*menā*, *gnā*: names of women; *menā* because they honour them, *gnā* because they go to them' (Ni. 3-21). '*Gnāḥ* are his' gives *gnāvān*. The word *neṣṭṛ* here means the god Tvaṣṭṛ, since at a certain *sattra* of the gods Tvaṣṭṛ acted as Neṣṭṛ. O *gnāvaḥ*, you who have your wife with you, O *neṣṭaḥ*, Tvaṣṭṛ, *abhi gṛṇīhi*, praise our sacrifice round about, near the gods. Drink the soma with the Ṛtu. *Hi*, since, you are *ratnadhāḥ*, a giver of jewels, so you are worthy to drink the soma: that is the sense." (Grammatical tail: *abhi*, final udātta, being excluded by *upasargāś cābhivarjam* (Phi. 4-13); *gṛṇīhi*: *gṝ*, *hi*, *śnā*, *ī*, no *guṇa*, shortening, lowered; *gnāvaḥ*: *matup*, *v* by *vyatyaya*, *ru* in the vocative, initial udātta by the *ṣāṣṭhika* rule at the head of the pāda; as an adjective of *neṣṭaḥ* it is a *viśeṣavacana*, so *nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe* does not bar its being treated as absent, and *neṣṭaḥ* is initial udātta; *piba*, the root accent, not lowered, the two vocatives before it counting as absent; *ratnadhāḥ*, *kvip*, the *kṛt* second-member accent; *asi*, the root accent, not lowered because of *hi*.)

### Page 637 — Rik 3: word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**ग्नावः (gnāvaḥ)** — accompanied by your wife | **नेष्टः (neṣṭaḥ)** — O Tvaṣṭṛ | **नः (naḥ)** — our | **यज्ञम् (yajñam)** — sacrifice | **अभि गृणीहि (abhi gṛṇīhi)** — praise everywhere (near the gods) | **ऋतुना (ṛtunā)** — with the Ṛtu deity | **पिब (piba)** — drink the soma juice | **हि (hi)** — for | **त्वम् (tvam)** — you | **रत्नधाः (ratnadhāḥ)** — giving the wealth of jewels and the like, the fruit of the sacrifice | **असि (asi)** — are.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Tvaṣṭṛ, you are famed as the giver of the wealth of jewels and the like that is the fruit of the sacrifice. Such as you are, come with your wife and drink our soma juice with the Ṛtu deity; and go to the gods and praise our sacrifice.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Neshtri, (Twashtri) commend our sacrifice to the gods; drink with Ritu, for you are a giver of riches.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Gnāvaḥ**: the word *gnā* denotes woman; Yāska says

> ग्ना गच्छन्त्येनाः
>
> *gnā gacchantyenāḥ*

*(Ni. 3-21.)*

> ग्ना अस्य सन्तीति ग्नावान् तस्य सम्बुद्धिः
>
> *gnā asya santīti gnāvān tasya sambuddhiḥ*

"one who is with a woman is called *gnāvān*"; this vocative singular *gnāvaḥ* qualifies the word *neṣṭaḥ*.

**Neṣṭaḥ**: since it is well known that at some sacrifices Tvaṣṭṛ took the part of the priest called Neṣṭṛ, it is customary to address Tvaṣṭṛ by the word *neṣṭṛ*. So the Bhāṣyakāra's intention is that here the word *neṣṭṛ* must be given the sense "the god Tvaṣṭṛ".

**Ratnadhāḥ**:

> रत्नानां दाता
>
> *ratnānāṃ dātā*

giver of jewels (excellent things). In the Ṛgveda the root *dhā* is commonly used in place of the root *dā*.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 637–639, noted briefly)*

**अभि (*abhi*)**: since "upasargāś cābhivarjam" (Phi. sū. 81) makes an exclusion, *abhi* is not initial udātta; it is final udātta by "phiṣo 'nta udāttaḥ".

### Page 638 — Rik 3: grammar (continued)

Many accept the reading of the word *abhi* in the *evādi* class; so by "evādīnām antaḥ" (Phi. sū. 82) *abhi* is final udātta. In the mantra *mā no martā abhi druhan* (Ṛ. Saṃ. "6-5-10" [?]) and in *ehi stomām̐ abhi* (Ṛ. Saṃ. "10-5-4" [?]) too the Vedabhāṣyakāra derives the final udātta by *evādīnām antaḥ*.

**गृणीहि (*gṛṇīhi*)**: *gṝ śabde* (*kryādi*); *loṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*; *hi* by "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. "4-4-87" [as printed, for 3-4-87]): *gṝ* + *hi*; the *vikaraṇa* *śnā* by "kryādibhyaḥ śnā": *gṝ* + *nā* + *hi*; *hi* is *ṅit* by "sārvadhātukam apit"; so by "ī halyaghoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-113) *ī* for the *ā* of *śnā*: *gṝ* + *nī* + *hi*; *hi* being *ṅit*, the *ī* before it takes no *guṇa*; *śnā* being *ṅit* by "sārvadhātukam apit", the *ṝ* before it takes no *guṇa*. *Gṝ* shortened by "pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-80): *gṛṇīhi*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

**ग्नावः (*gnāvaḥ*)**: with the analysis *gnāḥ striyaḥ asya santi*, *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup"; *v* for the *m* by *vyatyaya*: *gnāvat*; vocative singular *su*; *num* by "ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-70): *gnāvant* + *s*; *su* dropped by "hal-ṅyābbhyo dīrghāt…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-68); *t* dropped by "saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-23): *gnāvan*; *ru* for the *n* by "matuvaso ru sambuddhau chandasi" (Pā. sū. 8-3-1); visarga by "sasajuṣo ruḥ": *gnāvaḥ*. With *gnāvar* + *neṣṭaḥ*, in the Saṃhitā "haśi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-114) gives *u* for a *ru* after a non-*pluta* short *a* before a *haś* letter. But the *u* is an operation of the *sapāda-saptādhyāyī*; when it is made, by "pūrvatrāsiddham" (Pā. sū. 8-2-1) the loss of the final of the conjunct is treated as not done; so the *t* stands after it, no *haś* follows, and how can the *u* come? Though the *u* is a rule of the *sapāda-saptādhyāyī*, by the vārttika "saṃyogāntalopo ror uttve" (Pā. sū. 8-2-6 vā.) the loss of the final of the conjunct counts as done when the *u* for the *ru* is made; so it is not treated as not done, and the *u* comes: *gnāva* + *u* + *neṣṭaḥ*, *guṇa*: *gnāvo neṣṭaḥ*. *Gnāvaḥ* is at the head of the second pāda; so "apādādau" (Pā. sū. 8-1-18) bars the lowering by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19), and the sixth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198) makes it initial udātta. *Gnāvaḥ* qualifies *neṣṭaḥ*, so it is a *viśeṣavacana*, not a *sāmānyavacana*; so "nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-73) does not bar its being treated as absent.

### Page 639 — Rik 3: grammar (end)

So by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. sū. 8-1-72) the earlier vocative *gnāvaḥ* is treated as absent. So the vocative *neṣṭaḥ* also counts as at the head of the pāda, and the eighth-adhyāya lowering does not come; by the *ṣāṣṭhika* sūtra it is initial udātta.

**पिब (*piba*)**: *śap* is *pit*, so the root accent remains. The two vocatives before it are treated as absent, so *piba* is not wholly unaccented.

**रत्नधाः (*ratnadhāḥ*)**: *ratnāni dadhāti iti*; *kvip* after *ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ* by "kvip ca"; the root accent. After compounding, the *kṛt* second-member accent comes by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt", and that accent remains.

**असि (*asi*)**: *asa bhuvi*, *laṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*; the *vikaraṇa* *śap* is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ"; the *s* dropped by "tāsastyor lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. "7-4-50" [as printed]): *asi*. *Sip* is *pit*, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau"; the root accent remains. The use of *hi* brings the bar of "hi ca"; so "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" does not make it wholly unaccented. The *i* of *sip* becomes svarita by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ".

**॥३॥**

### Page 639 (lower) — Sūkta 15, Rik 4

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्ने॑ दे॒वाँ इ॒हा व॑ह सा॒दया॒ योनि॑षु त्रि॒षु । [accent ?]
> परि॑ भूष॒ पिब॑ ऋ॒तुना॑ ॥४॥
>
> *ágne devā́m̐ ihā́ vaha sādáyā yóniṣu triṣú |* [accent ?]
> *pári bhūṣa píba ṛtúnā ||4||*

*(Line 1: the bars under सादया are read under सा and या; not certain.)*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अग्ने । देवान् । इह । आ । वह । सादय । योनिषु । त्रिषु ॥
> परि । भूष । पिब । ऋतुना ॥४॥
>
> *agne | devān | iha | ā | vaha | sādaya | yoniṣu | triṣu ||*
> *pari | bhūṣa | piba | ṛtunā ||4||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे अग्ने देवानिहास्मिन्कर्मण्या वह । ततो योनिषु स्थानेषु त्रिषु सवनेषु सादय । देवानुपवेशय । ततस्तान्परि भूष । अलंकुरु । ऋतुना सह त्वं सोमं
>
> *he agne devānihāsminkarmaṇyā vaha | tato yoniṣu sthāneṣu triṣu savaneṣu sādaya | devānupaveśaya | tatastānpari bhūṣa | alaṃkuru | ṛtunā saha tvaṃ somaṃ*

### Page 640 — Rik 4: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

> पिब ॥ अग्ने देवानित्ययं पादो गतः । योनिषु । यु मिश्रणे । वहिश्रीत्यादिना । उ. ४-५१ । निप्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । त्रिषु । षट्त्रिचतुर्भ्यो हलादिः । पा. ६-१-१७९ । इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । भूष अलंकारे । तिङ्ङतिङ इति निघातः । पिब ऋतुनेति गतौ ॥
>
> *piba || agne devānityayaṃ pādo gataḥ | yoniṣu | yu miśraṇe | vahiśrītyādinā | u. 4-51 | nipratyayaḥ | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | triṣu | ṣaṭtricaturbhyo halādiḥ | pā. 6-1-179 | iti vibhakterudāttatvaṃ | bhūṣa alaṃkāre | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | piba ṛtuneti gatau ||*

**Translation:** "O Agni, bring the gods here to this rite. Then seat them, place the gods, in the *yonis*, the places, the three pressings. Then *pari bhūṣa*, adorn, them. Drink the soma with the Ṛtu." (Grammatical tail: the pāda *agne devān…* has been gone through; *yoniṣu* from *yu* 'to mix' with *ni* (Uṇ. 4-51), initial udātta; *triṣu*, the ending udātta by Pā. 6-1-179; *bhūṣa*, 'to adorn', lowered; *piba ṛtunā* gone through.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**अग्ने (agne)** — O Agni | **देवान् (devān)** — the gods | **इह (iha)** — for this sacrificial rite | **आ वह (ā vaha)** — bring | **त्रिषु योनिषु (triṣu yoniṣu)** — in the three (separate) places (in the pressings) | **सादय (sādaya)** — seat | **परि भूष (pari bhūṣa)** — adorn | **ऋतुना (ṛtunā)** — with the Ṛtu deity | **पिब (piba)** — drink (the soma juice).

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, bring the gods to our sacrifice. Seat them in three separate places, in the three pressings: the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing. Make fitting adornments. You too drink the soma juice with the Ṛtu deity.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Agni, bring the gods hither, seat them in three places (or in the three savanas), decorate them and drink with Ritu.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Sādaya**: the final syllable of this word is long in the Saṃhitā to suit the metre.

**Yoniṣu triṣu**:

> त्रिषु स्थानेषु
>
> *triṣu sthāneṣu*

that is, the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing. A pressing (*savana*) is the act of pressing out the soma juice. Since this act is done in the sacrifice at three times, morning, midday and evening, with the recitation of mantras, these acts are called in order the morning pressing, the midday pressing and the third pressing.

**Pari bhūṣa**: *alaṃkuru*: the Bhāṣyakāra gives the sense "adorn". Though *bhūṣa* means "adorn", there is room to doubt what need there could be here to adorn the gods.

### Page 641 — Rik 4: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar page 641, noted briefly)*

**अग्ने देवाँ इहा वह**: the derivation of this pāda is set out in the 3rd and 10th Ṛks of Sūkta 12.

**सादया (*sādayā*)**: *ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; *ṇic*; *s* for *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ"; the penultimate *vṛddhi* by "ata upadhāyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-116): *sādi*. Then *loṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*; *hi* by "ser hy apic ca" (Pā. sū. 3-4-87); the *vikaraṇa* *śap*, *guṇa*, *ay*: *sādaya* + *hi*; *hi* dropped by "ato heḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-105). The *a* that has come in place of the *ṇic* is udātta by the suffix accent; *śap* is *pit*, so unaccented. As in *sajasvānaḥ*, it is lengthened here too.

**योनिषु (*yoniṣu*)**: *yu miśraṇe*; "vahiśriśruyudruglātvaribhyo nit" (Uṇ. sū. "4-491" [?]): after these roots the suffix *ni*, and it is *nit*; so *ni* after *yu*: *yu* + *ni*; *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84), *o* for the *u*; locative plural *yoniṣu*. The suffix *ni* is *nit*, so the *nit* accent makes it initial udātta.

**त्रिषु (*triṣu*)**: "ṣaṭtricaturbhyo halādiḥ" (Pā. sū. "9-1-179" [as printed, for 6-1-179]); with "ṣṇāntā ṣaṭ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-24) the numerals ending in *ṣ* and *n* are called *ṣaṭ*; after such a *ṣaṭ* word, after *tri* and after *catur*, a consonant-initial ending is udātta; so the ending is udātta.

**भूष (*bhūṣa*)**: *bhūṣa alaṃkāre* (*bhvādi*); *loṭ*, 2nd singular *sip*, *hi*, the *vikaraṇa* *śap*; *hi* dropped by "ato heḥ": *bhūṣa*; wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ".

**पिब ऋतुना**: these two words are explained at *indra somaṃ piba ṛtunā* (Ṛ. Saṃ. Sū. 15, Ṛk 1).

**॥४॥**

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

> ब्राह्म॑णादिन्द्र॒ राध॑सः॒ पिबा॒ सोम॑मृ॒तूँरनु॑ ।
> तवे॑द्धि स॒ख्यम॑स्तृतम् ॥५॥ [accent ?]
>
> *brā́hmaṇād indra rā́dhasaḥ píbā sómam ṛtū́m̐r ánu |*
