*(Line 2: the stroke over वे and over म of सख्यम, the bar under स; the foot of the line is cut in the scan.)*

### Page 642 — Rik 5: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> ब्राह्मणात् । इन्द्र । राधसः । पिब । सोमम् । ऋतून् । अनु ॥
> तव । इत् । हि । सख्यम् । अस्तृतम् ॥५॥
>
> *brāhmaṇāt | indra | rādhasaḥ | piba | somam | ṛtūn | anu ||*
> *tava | it | hi | sakhyam | astṛtam ||5||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे इन्द्र ब्राह्मणाद्ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिसम्बद्धाद्राधसो धनभूतात्पात्रात्सोमं पिब । किं कृत्वा । ऋतूननु ऋतुदेवाननुसृत्य । ऋतवो ऽपि पिबन्त्वित्यर्थः । हि यस्मात्तवेत्तवैव सख्यमस्तृतमृतूनामविच्छिन्नं तस्मादृतुभिः सह पानं युक्तं ॥ ब्राह्मणात् । ब्रह्मशब्देनात्र ब्रह्मवर्गे द्वितीयो ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी कथ्यते । स च पुंलिङ्गे शेषनिघातेनानुदात्तादिः । तस्य सम्बन्ध्युत्तप्तश्चमसः । स च तस्यैवावयवहन्नियत इत्यवयवविवक्षायामनुदात्तादेरञ् । पा. ४-३-१४० । तेन ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तश्चमसपरो ऽत्र ब्राह्मणशब्दः । राधसः । सर्वधातुभ्यो ऽसुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । पिब । पादादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । द्व्यचो ऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घत्वं । ऋतूँरनुत्यत्र दीर्घादटि समानपाद इति नकारस्य रुत्वं । अत्रानुनासिकः पूर्वस्य तु वा । पा. ८-३-२ । इत्यूकारस्यानुनासिकत्वं । तव । युष्मदस्मद्भ्यां ङसो ऽश् । पा. ७-१-२७ । शित्त्वात्सर्वादेशः तवममौ ङसीति तवादेशः । युष्मदस्मदोर्ङसीत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । सख्यं । सख्युः कर्म सख्यं । सख्युर्यः । यस्येति लोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अस्तृतं । स्तृणातेर्हिंसार्थस्य क्तः । नञ्समासः । अव्ययपूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥
>
> *he indra brāhmaṇādbrāhmaṇācchaṃsisambaddhādrādhaso dhanabhūtātpātrātsomaṃ piba | kiṃ kṛtvā | ṛtūnanu ṛtudevānanusṛtya | ṛtavo 'pi pibantvityarthaḥ | hi yasmāttavettavaiva sakhyamastṛtamṛtūnāmavicchinnaṃ tasmādṛtubhiḥ saha pānaṃ yuktaṃ || brāhmaṇāt | brahmaśabdenātra brahmavarge dvitīyo brāhmaṇācchaṃsī kathyate | sa ca puṃliṅge śeṣanighātenānudāttādiḥ | tasya sambandhyuttaptaścamasaḥ | sa ca tasyaivāvayavahanniyata ityavayavavivakṣāyāmanudāttāderañ | pā. 4-3-140 | tena ñittvādādyudāttaścamasaparo 'tra brāhmaṇaśabdaḥ | rādhasaḥ | sarvadhātubhyo 'sun | nittvādādyudāttaḥ | piba | pādāditvādādyudāttatvaṃ | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghatvaṃ | ṛtū~ranutyatra dīrghādaṭi samānapāda iti nakārasya rutvaṃ | atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā | pā. 8-3-2 | ityūkārasyānunāsikatvaṃ | tava | yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś | pā. 7-1-27 | śittvātsarvādeśaḥ tavamamau ṅasīti tavādeśaḥ | yuṣmadasmadorṅasītyādyudāttatvaṃ | sakhyaṃ | sakhyuḥ karma sakhyaṃ | sakhyuryaḥ | yasyeti lopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ | astṛtaṃ | stṛṇāterhiṃsārthasya ktaḥ | nañsamāsaḥ | avyayapūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "O Indra, drink the soma from the *rādhas*, the vessel that is wealth, belonging to the *brāhmaṇa*, the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin. Having done what? *Ṛtūn anu*, following the Ṛtu gods: let the Ṛtus too drink, is the sense. *Hi*, since, *tava it*, yours alone, the friendship with the Ṛtus is *astṛtam*, unbroken, so drinking with the Ṛtus is fitting." (Grammatical tail: *brāhmaṇāt*: the word *brahman* here means the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, second in the Brahman group; masculine, initial unaccented by the *śeṣanighāta*; his raised *camasa*, a fixed part of him, so *añ* in the sense of part (Pā. 4-3-140), initial udātta, *brāhmaṇa* meaning that *camasa*; *rādhasaḥ* with *asun*, initial udātta; *piba*, initial udātta at the head of the pāda, lengthened in the Saṃhitā; *ṛtūm̐r anu*: *ru* for the *n*, the *ū* nasalised (Pā. 8-3-2); *tava*: *aś* for *ṅas* (Pā. 7-1-27), *tava* for the part up to *m*, initial udātta; *sakhyam*, "the act of a friend", *ya*, the suffix accent; *astṛtam*, *kta* after *stṛ* 'to harm', a *nañ* compound with the first-member accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**इन्द्र (indra)** — O Indra | **हि (hi)** — for the reason that | **तव इत् (tava it)** — yours alone | **सख्यम् (sakhyam)** — friendship | **अस्तृतम् (astṛtam)** — is unbroken (with the Ṛtu deities); (for that reason) | **ब्राह्मणात् (brāhmaṇāt)** — of the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin | **राधसः (rādhasaḥ)** — from the costly *camasa* vessel | **सोमम् (somam)** — the soma juice | **पिब (piba)** — drink.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Indra, it is well known in the world that the friendship of you and the Ṛtu deities is everlasting. So, from the costly *camasa* vessel of the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, you too drink the soma juice with the Ṛtu deities.

### Page 643 — Rik 5: English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Drink the soma juice, Indra, from the cups of priest called Brahmanachamsi, after Ritu for whom your friendship is uninterrupted (everlasting).

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Brāhmaṇāt**: the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.

**Rādhasaḥ**: *धनभूतात् पात्रात्* (*dhanabhūtāt pātrāt*, "from the vessel that is wealth"): the word *rādhas* means only wealth. It does not mean "vessel", but the Commentator has supplied that sense. Or one may give the word *rādhasaḥ* the sense "from the priceless, precious vessel", "costly vessel".

**Astṛtam**: unbroken, uninterrupted, "uninteruptedr" [sic]: not stopping after some time, everlasting, and so on.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 643–646, noted briefly)*

**ब्राह्मणात् (*brāhmaṇāt*)**: in a sacrifice whose base is soma, the four Brahman, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Āgnīdhra and Potṛ belong to the Brahman group. The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, second in this group, is denoted here by the word *brahman*. The word *brahman* is formed from the root *bṛhi vṛddhau* with the suffix *manin*, by "bṛṃher am nalopaś ca" in the old order, or by "bṛṃher no 'c ca" in the order of the Uṇādi sūtras now available. By "brahman puṃsi ca" (Liṅga sū. 140) it is neuter and masculine. In the neuter it is initial udātta by "ñnityādir nityam"; in the masculine final udātta by "uñchādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-160), the words of this class being final udātta; on this view, by the *śeṣanighāta* "anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-158), the word *brahman* begins with an unaccented syllable. Those of the Brahman group, and some others, chiefly the sacrificer, have a drinking of soma. The vessel for drinking soma is called *camasa*. It must be square; their handles are of various kinds:

> चतुरश्रो ब्रह्मचमसो होतुस्तु परिमण्डलः ।
> पृथुस्तु यजमानस्य त्र्यश्रिरुद्गातुरिष्यते ॥१॥
>
> *caturaśro brahmacamaso hotustu parimaṇḍalaḥ |*
> *pṛthustu yajamānasya tryaśrirudgāturiṣyate ||1||*

### Page 644 — Rik 5: grammar (continued)

> प्रशास्तुरवतप्तः स्यादुत्तप्तो ब्रह्मशंसिनः ।
> पोतुरग्रे विशाखी स्यान्नेष्टुस्तु विगृहीतकः ॥२॥
>
> *praśāsturavataptaḥ syāduttapto brahmaśaṃsinaḥ |*
> *poturagre viśākhī syānneṣṭustu vigṛhītakaḥ ||2||*

> अच्छावाकस्य राष्णावानाग्नीध्रस्य मयूखगः ।
> सव्यावृतः सदस्यः स्यादेतच्चमसलक्षणम् ॥३॥
>
> *acchāvākasya rāṣṇāvānāgnīdhrasya mayūkhagaḥ |*
> *savyāvṛtaḥ sadasyaḥ syādetaccamasalakṣaṇam ||3||*

> दण्डानामेष आकारश्चमसाश्चतुरश्रगाः ।
> होतुर्ब्रह्मण उद्गातुर्यष्टुः शास्तुश्च शंसिनः ॥४॥
>
> *daṇḍānāmeṣa ākāraścamasāścaturaśragāḥ |*
> *hoturbrahmaṇa udgāturyaṣṭuḥ śāstuśca śaṃsinaḥ ||4||*

> पोतृनेष्ट्रच्छावाकानामाग्नीध्रस्येति च क्रमः ॥
>
> *potṛneṣṭracchāvākānāmāgnīdhrasyeti ca kramaḥ ||*

*("The Brahman's camasa is square, the Hotṛ's round; the sacrificer's broad; the Udgātṛ's is wanted three-cornered. The Praśāstṛ's is with the handle bent down, the Brahmaśaṃsin's with it raised; the Potṛ's forked at the tip; the Neṣṭṛ's with the handle set apart. The Acchāvāka's is rāṣṇāvān, the Āgnīdhra's mayūkhaga; the Sadasya's turned to the left: this is the mark of the camasas. This is the shape of the handles; the camasas are square in form; the order is: of the Hotṛ, Brahman, Udgātṛ, sacrificer, Praśāstṛ, Śaṃsin, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, Acchāvāka and Āgnīdhra" — mine and tentative; *rāṣṇāvān* and *mayūkhaga* are left untranslated.)*

The ancients gave this description in the Agniṣṭoma procedure, in the section on setting down the soma vessels at the morning pressing. From this it is settled that the handle of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's soma vessel is *uttapta*, that is, carved so as to stand raised. The *camasa* with the raised handle is fixed to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin as a part is to the whole. So it may be meant as a part. So meant, "anudāttāder añ" (Pā. sū. 4-3-140): after the genitive of a stem beginning with an unaccented syllable, in the senses of part, product and group, the suffix *añ*; so *añ* comes with the analysis *brahmaṇaḥ avayavaḥ* (a part of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin). So the word *brāhmaṇa* here means the *camasa* vessel with the carved raised handle, fixed to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin as a part to the whole. The suffix *añ* is *ñit*, so by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) it is initial udātta.

**राधसः (*rādhasaḥ*)**: by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. sū. "4-628" [?]) the suffix *asun* after the root *rādh*; initial udātta by the *nit* accent.

**पिब (*piba*)**: this is set out at *pibā mitrasya* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-10). It is at the head of the pāda, so the eighth-adhyāya lowering does not come. Lengthened by "dvyaco 'tas tiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-3-135).

**ऋतूँरनु (*ṛtūm̐r anu*)**: with *ṛtūn* + *anu*, by "dīrghād aṭi samānapāde" (Pā. sū. "8-4-9" [as printed, for 8-3-9]) *ru* for the *n*: *ṛtūr* + *anu*. "atrānunāsikaḥ pūrvasya tu vā" (Pā. sū. 8-3-2): in the *ru* section, in place of what precedes what is enjoined, a nasal comes optionally; so the *ū* becomes a nasal *ū*: *ṛtūm̐ anu* [as printed].

### Page 645 — Rik 5: grammar (continued)

**तव (*tava*)**: *yuṣmad* + genitive singular "jas" [as printed, for *ṅas*]; "yuṣmadasmadbhyāṃ ṅaso 'ś" (Pā. sū. 7-1-27): *aś* for the *ṅas* after *yuṣmad* and *asmad*; being *śit*, it replaces the whole by "anekālśit sarvasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-55): *yuṣmad* + *a*. "tavamamau ṅasi" (Pā. sū. "7-2-96" [as printed]): before *ṅas*, *tava* and *mama* for the part up to *m* of *yuṣmad* and *asmad*: *tava* + *ad* + *a*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe"; *ṭi* dropped by "śeṣe lopaḥ". "yuṣmadasmador ṅasi" (Pā. sū. 6-1-211): before *ṅas* the first syllable of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* is udātta. Though the ending would be udātta by the *udāttanivṛtti* accent "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-161) where *śeṣe lopaḥ* (Pā. sū. 7-2-90) drops the *ṭi*, and by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-5) where it drops the final, overriding that the first syllable of *yuṣmad* is udātta; the other letters are unaccented by the *śeṣānudātta* accent.

**सख्यम् (*sakhyam*)**: *sakhyuḥ karma*. "sakhyur yaḥ" (Pā. sū. 5-1-126): after the fitting genitive of *sakhi*, in the senses of state and act, the suffix *ya*; so *ya* after *sakhi* in the sense of act; *sakhi* + *ya*; the *i* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-148); the suffix accent.

**अस्तृतम् (*astṛtam*)**: *stṛñ ācchādane* (*svādi*). Roots have many senses, so here *stṛ* is in the sense of harming. *Kta* after it: *stṛ* + *ta*; "ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt" (Pā. sū. 7-2-10) bars the *iṭ*, or "ṛtaś ca saṃyogādeḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-43): after a root ending in *ṛ* that begins with a conjunct, *iṭ* is optional for *liṅ* and *sic* before an *ātmanepada* ending; since the *iṭ* is enjoined as optional, by "yasya vibhāṣā" the suffix *kta* takes no *iṭ*. *Na stṛtam astṛtam*: a *nañ* compound. By "tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyāsaptamyupamānāvyayadvitīyākṛtyāḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-2-2) the first member, an *avyaya*, keeps its accent; the first member is a *nipāta*, so initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Phi. sū. 80). *Stṝñ ācchādane* is a *kryādi* root, with *laṭ* *stṛṇāti*. If the suffix *kta* is put after it: *stṝ* + *ta*; "liṅsicor ātmanepadeṣu" (Pā. sū. 7-2-42): after *vṛṅ*, *vṛñ* and roots ending in long *ṝ*, *iṭ* is optional for *liṅ* and *sic* before an *ātmanepada* ending; since it is enjoined as optional, by "yasya vibhāṣā" (Pā. sū. 7-2-15) the suffix *kta* takes no *iṭ*. By "ralvādibhyaś ca" (Pā. sū. 8-2-44) the *t* of the suffix *kta*

### Page 646 — Rik 5: grammar (end)

becomes *n*: *stṝ* + *na*; "ṝta id dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-100) gives *i* for the *ṝ*, with *r* after it by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-1-51); lengthening by "hali ca" (Pā. sū. "8-2-77" [?]): *stīr* + *na*; *ṇ* for the *n* by "raṣābhyāṃ no ṇaḥ samānapade" (Pā. sū. 8-4-1): *stīrṇa*. So in *astṛtam* it is fitting to take the *svādi* root.

**॥५॥**

### Page 646 (lower) — Sūkta 15, Rik 6

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> यु॒वं दक्षं॑ धृतव्रत॒ मित्रा॑वरुण दू॒ळभ॑म् ।
> ऋ॒तुना॑ य॒ज्ञमा॑शाथे ॥६॥
>
> *yuváṃ dákṣaṃ dhṛtavrata mítrāvaruṇa dūḷábham |*
> *ṛtúnā yajñám āśāthe ||6||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> युवम् । दक्षम् । धृतऽव्रता । मित्रावरुणा । दुःऽदभम् ॥
> ऋतुना । यज्ञम् । आशाथे इति ॥६॥
>
> *yuvam | dakṣam | dhṛta 'vratā | mitrāvaruṇā | duḥ 'dabham ||*
> *ṛtunā | yajñam | āśāthe iti ||6||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे धृतव्रता स्वीकृतकर्माणौ मित्रावरुणा हे मित्रनामकवरुणनामकौ देवौ युवमुभौ युवामृतुना सहास्मदीयं यज्ञमाशाथे । व्याप्नुथः । कीदृशं यज्ञं । दक्षं प्रवृद्धं दूळभं दुर्दहं शत्रुभिर्दग्धुं विनाशयितुमशक्यमित्यर्थः ॥ युवं । प्रथमाद्विवचनस्य ङे प्रथमयोरमित्यमादेशः । युवावौ द्विवचने । पा. ७-२-९२ । इति मपर्यन्तस्य युवादेशः । शेषे लोप इति टिलोपो ऽन्त्यलोपो वा । अमि पूर्वत्वं । भाषायामेव ह्यात्वं । टिलोपपक्ष उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेणामुदात्तत्वं । अन्त्यलोपपक्ष एकादेश उदात्तः । दक्षं । दक्ष वृद्धौ । दक्षन्त्यनेनेति करणे घञ् । एवं हि पुंलिङ्गत्वनियमः । अन्यस्यानियम इति नपुंसकत्वं । धृतव्रता मित्रावरुणा । धृतानि व्रतानि याभ्यां तौ धृतव्रतौ । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च मित्रावरुणौ । उभयत्र सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । मित्रशब्दस्य देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्यानङादेशः । प्रथमस्यामन्त्रितनिघातः । द्वितीयस्य पादादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । संहितायां
>
> *he dhṛtavratā svīkṛtakarmāṇau mitrāvaruṇā he mitranāmakavaruṇanāmakau devau yuvamubhau yuvāmṛtunā sahāsmadīyaṃ yajñamāśāthe | vyāpnuthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ yajñaṃ | dakṣaṃ pravṛddhaṃ dūḷabhaṃ durdahaṃ śatrubhirdagdhuṃ vināśayitumaśakyamityarthaḥ || yuvaṃ | prathamādvivacanasya ṅe prathamayoramityamādeśaḥ | yuvāvau dvivacane | pā. 7-2-92 | iti maparyantasya yuvādeśaḥ | śeṣe lopa iti ṭilopo 'ntyalopo vā | ami pūrvatvaṃ | bhāṣāyāmeva hyātvaṃ | ṭilopapakṣa udāttanivṛttisvareṇāmudāttatvaṃ | antyalopapakṣa ekādeśa udāttaḥ | dakṣaṃ | dakṣa vṛddhau | dakṣantyaneneti karaṇe ghañ | evaṃ hi puṃliṅgatvaniyamaḥ | anyasyāniyama iti napuṃsakatvaṃ | dhṛtavratā mitrāvaruṇā | dhṛtāni vratāni yābhyāṃ tau dhṛtavratau | mitraśca varuṇaśca mitrāvaruṇau | ubhayatra supāṃ sulugityādinā vibhakterākāraḥ | mitraśabdasya devatādvandve cetyānaṅādeśaḥ | prathamasyāmantritanighātaḥ | dvitīyasya pādāditvādādyudāttatvaṃ | saṃhitāyāṃ*

### Page 647 — Rik 6: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

> छान्दसं ह्रस्वत्वं । दूळभं । दह भस्मीकरणे । दुःखेन दह्यत इति दुर्दहं । ईषद्दुःसुष्वित्यादिना । पा. ३-३-१२६ । दुर्युपपदे दहेः खल् । व्यत्ययो बहुलमित्युकारस्योकारो रेफस्य लोपो दकारस्य डकारो हकारस्य च भकारः । लितीति प्रत्ययात्पूर्वमुदात्तत्वं । कृदुत्तरपदत्वेन स एव शिष्यते । आशाथे । अशू व्याप्तौ । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने लिट् । मध्यमद्विवचनमाथां । टेरेत्वं । अत आदेः । पा. ७-४-७० । इत्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घः । अश्नोतेश्च । पा. ७-४-७२ । इति प्राप्तो नुडागमो ऽनित्यमागमशासनमिति निवर्तते ॥ २८ ॥
>
> *chāndasaṃ hrasvatvaṃ | dūḷabhaṃ | daha bhasmīkaraṇe | duḥkhena dahyata iti durdahaṃ | īṣadduḥsuṣvityādinā | pā. 3-3-126 | duryupapade daheḥ khal | vyatyayo bahulamityukārasyokāro rephasya lopo dakārasya ḍakāro hakārasya ca bhakāraḥ | litīti pratyayātpūrvamudāttatvaṃ | kṛduttarapadatvena sa eva śiṣyate | āśāthe | aśū vyāptau | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti vartamāne liṭ | madhyamadvivacanamāthāṃ | ṭeretvaṃ | ata ādeḥ | pā. 7-4-70 | ityabhyāsasya dīrghaḥ | aśnoteśca | pā. 7-4-72 | iti prāpto nuḍāgamo 'nityamāgamaśāsanamiti nivartate || 28 ||*

**Translation:** "O *dhṛtavratā*, you two who have taken up the rites, O *mitrāvaruṇā*, gods named Mitra and Varuṇa, *yuvam*, both of you, *āśāthe*, pervade, our sacrifice with the Ṛtu. What kind of sacrifice? *Dakṣam*, grown great; *dūḷabham*, hard to burn, that is, that cannot be burnt, destroyed, by enemies." (Grammatical tail: *yuvam*: *am* for the nominative dual, *yuva* for the part up to *m* (Pā. 7-2-92), *śeṣe lopaḥ*, *pūrvarūpa*; the *ā* is only in the spoken language; on the *ṭi*-loss view *am* is udātta by the *udāttanivṛtti* accent, on the final-loss view the single replacement; *dakṣam*: *dakṣ* 'to grow', *ghañ* in the instrumental sense, neuter, the masculine rule not binding here; *dhṛtavratā mitrāvaruṇā*: "by whom rites are held", a dvandva, *ā* for the endings by *supāṃ suluk…*, *ānaṅ* for *mitra*; the first vocative lowered, the second initial udātta at the head of the pāda; shortened in the Saṃhitā as Vedic; *dūḷabham*: "hard to burn", *khal* after *dah* with *dur* (Pā. 3-3-126), by *vyatyayo bahulam* *ū* for *u*, loss of *r*, *ḍ* for *d* and *bh* for *h*; udātta before the *l*-marked suffix; *āśāthe*: *aś* 'to pervade', *liṭ* in the present, *āthām*, *e*, the reduplicate lengthened (Pā. 7-4-70), the *nuṭ* of Pā. 7-4-72 withdrawn as the augment-rule is not binding. The closing "28" is the varga number.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**धृतव्रता (dhṛtavratā)** — who accept the sacrificial rite we perform | **मित्रावरुणा (mitrāvaruṇā)** — O Mitra and Varuṇa | **युवम् (yuvam)** — you two | **ऋतुना (ṛtunā)** — with the Ṛtu deity | **दक्षम् (dakṣam)** — grown great | **दूळभम् (dūḷabham)** — that cannot be burnt (destroyed) (by enemies) | **यज्ञम् आशाथे (yajñam āśāthe)** — pervade the sacrifice: you are gracious to our sacrifice.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Mitra and Varuṇa, you accept our sacrificial rite. By your favour our sacrifice is growing, and since you help us, enemies cannot obstruct it. Kindly come to our sacrifice with the Ṛtu deity.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Mitra and Varuna, propitious to pious acts, be present with Ritu at our sacrifiee [sic], efficacious and undisturbed by foes.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Dhṛtavratā**:

> धृतकर्माणौ । अथवा स्वीकृतकर्माणौ
>
> *dhṛtakarmāṇau | athavā svīkṛtakarmāṇau*

that is, "who accept the sacrificial rite we perform". The final syllables of the words *dhṛtavratā* and *mitrāvaruṇā* are short in the Saṃhitā to suit the metre. This word *dhṛtavratā* is read also in the Ṛk

> इन्द्रावरुणा सुतपाविमं सुतं सोमं पिबतं मद्यं धृतव्रता ॥
>
> *indrāvaruṇā sutapāvimaṃ sutaṃ somaṃ pibataṃ madyaṃ dhṛtavratā ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-68-10.)*

### Page 648 — Rik 6: Special Topics (end) and grammar

There the word refers to Indra and Varuṇa. Besides this, the words *dhṛtavrataḥ*, *dhṛtavratāḥ*, *dhṛtavratāya*, *dhṛtavrate* are read in many Ṛks.

**Dūḷabham**: *duḥdabham*:

> दुर्दभं शत्रुभिर्दग्धुं विनाशयितुमशक्यं ॥
>
> *durdabhaṃ śatrubhirdagdhuṃ vināśayitumaśakyaṃ ||*

that is, "that cannot be burnt by enemies". The word *dūḷabhe*, which points to the same sense, is read also in Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-8 and 7-46-4 [?]; the word *dūḷabhaḥ* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-2-2, 4-9-2 and 4-9-8; and the word *dūḷabhāsaḥ* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-56-8 [?] and 7-60-6.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 648–650, noted briefly)*

**युवम् (*yuvam*)**: *yuṣmad* + nominative dual *au*. "yuvāvau dvivacane" (Pā. sū. 7-2-92): before an ending, for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* conveying duality, *yuva* and *āva* for the part up to *m*; so *yuva* for *yuṣma*, *pararūpa*: *yuvad* + *au*. "ṅe prathamayor am" (Pā. sū. 7-1-28): *am* also for the first and second case endings after *yuṣmad*/*asmad*, so *am* for *au*: *yuvad* + *am*. "prathamāyāś ca dvivacane bhāṣāyām" (Pā. sū. 7-2-88): before the first-case dual, *ā* as the final replacement of *yuṣmad*/*asmad* in the spoken language; so this *ā* does not come in the Veda. By "śeṣe lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-90) the *ṭi* drops, or the final letter. On the final-loss view *pūrvarūpa* by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-107): *yuvam*. On the *ṭi*-loss view the *a* of *am* is udātta by the *udāttanivṛtti* accent "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-161); on the final-loss view the single replacement of *ami pūrvaḥ* is udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ" (Pā. sū. "6-2-5" [as printed, for 8-2-5]). So on both views *yuvam* is final udātta.

**दक्षम् (*dakṣam*)**: *dakṣa vṛddhau*; *dakṣanti anena iti dakṣam*. "halaś ca" (Pā. sū. 3-3-121): after consonant-final roots, in the senses of instrument and locus, in the masculine, when a name is meant, the suffix *ghañ*; so *ghañ* after *dakṣ* in the instrumental sense. With *ghañ*, by rule it should be masculine, *dakṣaḥ*; but by *anyasyāniyamaḥ* it is neuter.

**धृतव्रता मित्रावरुणा (*dhṛtavratā mitrāvaruṇā*)**: *dhṛtāni vratāni yābhyāṃ tau* (Mitra and Varuṇa, by whom the rite is accepted): *dhṛtavratau*. *Mitraś ca varuṇaś ca mitrāvaruṇau*, a dvandva compound. In both, for the vocative-nominative dual ending *au*, by "supāṃ suluk…"

### Page 649 — Rik 6: grammar (continued)

(Pā. sū. 7-1-39) and so on, the replacement *ā* comes. For the word *mitra*, by "devatādvandve ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-26) the replacement *ānaṅ* comes; being *ṅit*, by "ṅic ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-53) a *ṅit* replacement, though of several letters, comes for the final letter; so *ān* for the final *a* of *mitra*; the *n* dropped by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-7): *mitrāvaruṇā*. In *dhṛtavratā* the vocative lowering comes by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19). *Mitrāvaruṇā* is at the head of the pāda, so it does not get the vocative lowering; by the sixth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" it is initial udātta. In *dhṛtavratā* and *mitrāvaruṇā* the shortening in the Saṃhitā is Vedic.

**दूळभम् (*dūḷabham*)**: *daha bhasmīkaraṇe*; *duḥkhena dahyate iti durdaham*. "īṣadduḥsuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal" (Pā. sū. 3-3-126): after a root following *īṣat*, *dus* (in the sense of difficulty) and *su* (in the sense of ease), in the senses of action and object, the suffix *khal*; so *khal* after *dah* with *dur* before it; the *l* and *kh* are *it* and go: *dur* + *dah* + *a*. "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85): here the Bhāṣyakāra divides the sūtra in two. *Vyatyayaḥ*, the first part: in the Veda the *vikaraṇa* suffixes such as *sya* are interchanged. *Bahulam*, the second part: in the Veda all rules apply variously. The Vārttikakāra has summed up this sense of *bahula*:

> सुप्तिङुपग्रहलिङ्गनराणां कालहलच्स्वरकर्तृयङां च ।
> व्यत्ययमिच्छति शास्त्रकृदेषां सो ऽपि च सिध्यति बाहुलकेन ॥
>
> *suptiṅupagrahaliṅganarāṇāṃ kālahalacsvarakartṛyaṅāṃ ca |*
> *vyatyayamicchati śāstrakṛdeṣāṃ so 'pi ca sidhyati bāhulakena ||*

*(Pā. sū. 3-1-85 vā. 1.)* By this, in *dur* + *dah* + *a*, *ū* for the *u*, loss of the *r*, *ḍ* for the *d* and *bh* for the *h* all come: *dūḍabha*. By "ajmadhyasya ḍakārasya ḷakāraṃ bahvṛcā jaguḥ" the *ḍ* becomes *ḷ*: *dūḷabham*. By "liti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-193) the *a* of *ḷa* before the suffix is udātta. When compounded with *dur*, by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) the *kṛt* second-member accent comes, and that accent remains.

**आशाथे (*āśāthe*)**: *aśū vyāptau*; by "chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-6) *liṭ* in the present sense. "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-8): reduplication: *aś* + *aś* + *liṭ*; for *liṭ*, the 2nd dual *āthām*; "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79): *e* for the *ām*: *aś* + *aś* + *āthe*. "halādiḥ śeṣaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-60), whether by the division of the rule or by reliance on the class, removes the *ś* of the reduplicate. "ata ādeḥ" (Pā. sū. "7--70" [as printed, for 7-4-70])

### Page 650 — Rik 6: grammar (end)

lengthens the initial *a* of the reduplicate: *ā* + *aś* + *athe*. "aśnoteś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-4-72): after the lengthened *a* of the reduplicate, the root *aś* takes the augment *nuṭ*; though the *nuṭ* would come, by "anityam āgamaśāsanam" (paribhāṣā 96 [?]) it is not binding and does not come. *Savarṇa-dīrgha* by "akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-101): *āśāthe*. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ".

> य॒ज्ञेषु॑ दे॒वमी॑ळते ॥७॥

> द्रविणःऽदाः । द्रविणसः । ग्रावऽहस्तासः । अध्वरे ॥
> यज्ञेषु । देवम् । ईळते ॥७॥
>
> *draviṇaḥ 'dāḥ | draviṇasaḥ | grāva 'hastāsaḥ | adhvare ||*
> *yajñeṣu | devam | īḷate ||7||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> अध्वरे ऽग्निष्टोमे प्रकृतिरूपे यज्ञेषु विकृतिरूपेषूक्थ्यादिषु च देवमग्निमीळते । ऋत्विजः स्तुवन्ति । कीदृशा ऋत्विजः । द्रविणसो धनार्थिनो ग्रावहस्तासो ऽभिषवसाधनपाषाणधारिणः । कीदृशं देवं । द्रविणोदा धनप्रदं । यद्वा । धनप्रदो ऽग्निः सोमं पिबत्विति शेषः । तमेतं मन्त्रं यास्क एवं निराह । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते यदेनदभिद्रवन्ति बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवन्ति तस्य दाता द्रविणोदास्तस्यैषा भवति । द्रविणोदा द्रविणस इत्यादि । नि. ८-१ । सो ऽयं यास्कोक्तो निर्वचनप्रपञ्चस्तस्मिन्नेव ग्रन्थे ऽवगन्तव्यः ॥ द्रविणोदाः । द्रुदक्षिभ्यामिनन् । उ. २-५० [?] । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तो द्रविणशब्दः । तद्ददातीति द्रविणोदाः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । पूर्वपदस्य सकारोपजनश्छान्दसः । रुत्वोत्वे । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । देवविशेषणत्वेनैकवाक्यतापक्षे द्वितीयायाः स्वादेशः । अथवा द्रविणमात्मन इच्छन्ति द्रविणस्यन्ति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । सर्वप्रातिपदिकेभ्यो
>
> *adhvare 'gniṣṭome prakṛtirūpe yajñeṣu vikṛtirūpeṣūkthyādiṣu ca devamagnimīḷate | ṛtvijaḥ stuvanti | kīdṛśā ṛtvijaḥ | draviṇaso dhanārthino grāvahastāso 'bhiṣavasādhanapāṣāṇadhāriṇaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ devaṃ | draviṇodā dhanapradaṃ | yadvā | dhanaprado 'gniḥ somaṃ pibatviti śeṣaḥ | tametaṃ mantraṃ yāska evaṃ nirāha | draviṇodāḥ kasmāddhanaṃ draviṇamucyate yadenadabhidravanti balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yadenenābhidravanti tasya dātā draviṇodāstasyaiṣā bhavati | draviṇodā draviṇasa ityādi | ni. 8-1 | so 'yaṃ yāskokto nirvacanaprapañcastasminneva granthe 'vagantavyaḥ || draviṇodāḥ | drudakṣibhyāminan | u. 2-50 [?] | nittvādādyudātto draviṇaśabdaḥ | taddadātīti draviṇodāḥ | kvipceti kvip | pūrvapadasya sakāropajanaśchāndasaḥ | rutvotve | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | devaviśeṣaṇatvenaikavākyatāpakṣe dvitīyāyāḥ svādeśaḥ | athavā draviṇamātmana icchanti draviṇasyanti | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | sarvaprātipadikebhyo*

### Page 651 — Rik 7: bhāṣya (end), word-meanings, overall sense, English

> लालसायां सुग्वक्तव्यः । म. ७-१-५१-२ । इति क्यचि परतः सुगागमः । द्रविणस्यतेः सम्पदादित्वाद्भावे क्विप् । अतो लोपः । क्वौ लुप्तं न स्थानिवद्भवति । म. १-१-५८-२ । इति तस्य स्थानिवत्त्वप्रतिषेधाद्यलोपः । एवं द्रविणस्शब्दो धनेच्छावचनः । द्रविणेच्छां दस्यति यथेष्टधनप्रदानेनोपक्षपयतीत्यर्थे दसु उपक्षये इत्यस्मादन्तर्भावितण्यर्थात्क्विप्चेति क्विप् । एवं द्रविणोदःशब्दः सकारान्तो भवति । तथा द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्तीति नैरुक्तो व्यवहार उपपद्यते । नि. ८-२ । अतो द्रविणोदस्शब्दो भिन्नवाक्यत्वे स्वार्थे प्रथमा । एकवाक्यत्वे तु व्यत्ययेन द्वितीयार्थो भवति । द्रविणस इत्यत्रापि वाक्यभेदपक्षे द्रविणसः सोमस्येत्यर्थे सकारोपजनश्छान्दसः । आद्युदात्तत्वं तु नियमेन स्थितं । ऋत्विग्विशेषणत्वेनैकवाक्यत्वपक्षे तु क्यजन्तात्क्विप् । अतो लोपादि पूर्ववत् । अत्र तु पक्षे क्यचश्चित्त्वेनान्तोदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते व्यत्ययेनाद्युदात्तत्वं । ग्रावयुक्ता हस्ता येषां ते ग्रावहस्तासः । आज्जसेरसुक् । ग्रावशब्दो वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अध्वरे । न विद्यते ध्वरो हिंसा यस्मिन् । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । ईळते । अनुदात्तेत्त्वादात्मनेपदं । अदिप्रभृतिभ्य इति शपो लुक् । झस्यादादेशः ॥
>
> *lālasāyāṃ sugvaktavyaḥ | ma. 7-1-51-2 | iti kyaci parataḥ sugāgamaḥ | draviṇasyateḥ sampadāditvādbhāve kvip | ato lopaḥ | kvau luptaṃ na sthānivadbhavati | ma. 1-1-58-2 | iti tasya sthānivattvapratiṣedhādyalopaḥ | evaṃ draviṇasśabdo dhanecchāvacanaḥ | draviṇecchāṃ dasyati yatheṣṭadhanapradānenopakṣapayatītyarthe dasu upakṣaye ityasmādantarbhāvitaṇyarthātkvipceti kvip | evaṃ draviṇodaḥśabdaḥ sakārānto bhavati | tathā draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavantīti nairukto vyavahāra upapadyate | ni. 8-2 | ato draviṇodasśabdo bhinnavākyatve svārthe prathamā | ekavākyatve tu vyatyayena dvitīyārtho bhavati | draviṇasa ityatrāpi vākyabhedapakṣe draviṇasaḥ somasyetyarthe sakāropajanaśchāndasaḥ | ādyudāttatvaṃ tu niyamena sthitaṃ | ṛtvigviśeṣaṇatvenaikavākyatvapakṣe tu kyajantātkvip | ato lopādi pūrvavat | atra tu pakṣe kyacaścittvenāntodāttatve prāpte vyatyayenādyudāttatvaṃ | grāvayuktā hastā yeṣāṃ te grāvahastāsaḥ | ājjaserasuk | grāvaśabdo vṛṣāditvādādyudāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | adhvare | na vidyate dhvaro hiṃsā yasmin | nañsubhyāmityuttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | īḷate | anudāttettvādātmanepadaṃ | adiprabhṛtibhya iti śapo luk | jhasyādādeśaḥ ||*

**Translation:** "At the *adhvara*, the Agniṣṭoma in its model form, and at the *yajñas*, the modified forms such as the Ukthya, the priests *īḷate*, praise, the god Agni. What are the priests like? *Draviṇasaḥ*, seeking wealth; *grāvahastāsaḥ*, holding the stones that are the means of pressing. What is the god like? *Draviṇodāḥ*, the giver of wealth. Or: 'may Agni, the giver of wealth, drink the soma' is to be supplied. Yāska explains this mantra so: '*Draviṇodāḥ*: why? Wealth is called *draviṇa* because they run towards it; or strength is *draviṇa*, because by it they run towards (the foe); its giver is *draviṇodāḥ*; this Ṛk is about him: *draviṇodā draviṇasaḥ*…' (Ni. 8-1). That etymological account of Yāska is to be learnt from that very work." (Grammatical tail: *draviṇa* with *inan* (Uṇ. "2-50" [?]), initial udātta; *draviṇodāḥ*, "who gives it", *kvip*, the Vedic insertion of *s* in the first member, *ru* and *u*, the accent of the *kṛt* second member; taken with *devam* as one sentence, the accusative is replaced by the nominative; or *draviṇasyanti* "they desire wealth for themselves", *kyac* with the augment *s* (MB 7-1-51-2), *kvip* in the action sense, the *a* and then the *y* dropped (the *kvip* loss not *sthānivat*, MB 1-1-58-2), so *draviṇas* means desire for wealth; *draviṇodas*, "who removes that desire by giving wealth", from *das* 'to waste' with the inner causative and *kvip*, ending in *s*, which fits Yāska's *draviṇodasaḥ pravādāḥ* (Ni. 8-2); in separate sentences a nominative in its own sense, in one sentence by *vyatyaya* in the accusative sense; *draviṇasaḥ*, on the separate-sentence view "of the soma" with a Vedic *s*, initial udātta as a rule; as an epithet of the priests, *kvip* after the *kyac* form, final udātta (*cit*) overridden by *vyatyaya* to initial udātta; *grāvahastāsaḥ*, a bahuvrīhi with *asuk*, *grāvan* initial udātta as of the *vṛṣādi* class; *adhvare* final udātta by *nañsubhyām*; *īḷate*, *ātmanepada*, *śap* dropped, *at* for *jh*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**द्रविणसः (draviṇasaḥ)** — the priests who seek wealth | **ग्रावहस्तासः (grāvahastāsaḥ)** — holding in their hands the stones (the means of pressing the soma juice) | **द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ)** — the giver of wealth (or the one named Draviṇodas) | **देवम् (devam)** — Agni, the god | **अध्वरे (adhvare)** — at the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice in its model form | **यज्ञेषु (yajñeṣu)** — and at the sacrifices such as the Ukthya in their modified forms | **ईळते (īḷate)** — praise.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

The priests who seek wealth, holding in their hands the stones that are the means of pressing the soma juice, at the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, the model, and at the Ukthya and other sacrifices, the modifications, invoke and praise Agni called Draviṇodas so that he drinks the soma juice.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> The priests desirous of wealth, with the soma-pressing stones in their hands praise the divine (Agni) Dravinodas who is the giver of riches, in the Soma and other sacrifices.

### Page 652 — Rik 7: Special Topics

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Draviṇodāḥ**: Yāska has written a full explanation of this word:

> द्रविणोदाः । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते । यदेनदभिद्रवन्ति । बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवन्ति । तस्य दाता द्रविणोदाः ॥
>
> *draviṇodāḥ | draviṇodāḥ kasmāddhanaṃ draviṇamucyate | yadenadabhidravanti | balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yadenenābhidravanti | tasya dātā draviṇodāḥ ||*

*(Ni. 8-1.)* Here the word *draviṇodāḥ* is derived as *draviṇaṃ dadāti iti draviṇodāḥ*. The word *draviṇa* has two senses, wealth and strength; so *draviṇodāḥ* means the giver of wealth or of strength. This is the sense of the parts of the word. Besides, Yāska gives the etymological explanation of this Ṛk thus:

> द्रविणोदा यस्त्वं । द्रविणस इति द्रविणसादिन इति वा द्रविणसानिन इति वा द्रविणसस्तस्मात्पिबत्विति वा । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते । याचन्ति स्तुवन्ति वर्धयन्ति पूजयन्तीति वा ॥
>
> *draviṇodā yastvaṃ | draviṇasa iti draviṇasādina iti vā draviṇasānina iti vā draviṇasastasmātpibatviti vā | yajñeṣu devamīḷate | yācanti stuvanti vardhayanti pūjayantīti vā ||*

That is, the priests who look for wealth, oblations and the like pray to you, called Draviṇodas, to drink the soma at the sacrifices: this is the chief sense. Though *draviṇodāḥ* here is a nominative singular, how does it qualify the accusative singular *devam*? Words must be supplied so that the sense is *draviṇodā yaḥ devaḥ taṃ devam*, "the god who is the giver of wealth: that god". *Draviṇasaḥ*: since they pray to the god for wealth or oblations for the worship of the gods, *draviṇasaḥ* means the priests. And *īḷate* may be given many senses: they beg, they praise, they extol, they worship.

> तत्को द्रविणोदा इन्द्र इति क्रौष्टुकिः । स बलधनयोर्दातृतमस्तस्य च सर्वा बलकृतिः ॥
>
> *tatko draviṇodā indra iti krauṣṭukiḥ | sa baladhanayordātṛtamastasya ca sarvā balakṛtiḥ ||*

### Page 653 — Rik 7: Special Topics (continued)

So much for the sense of the parts of the word *draviṇodāḥ*. But who is the deity *draviṇodāḥ*? Indra is the one called *draviṇodāḥ*, for it is Indra who gives most the strength and wealth that the word *draviṇa* points to; so Indra himself should be called *draviṇodāḥ*: this is Krauṣṭuki's view.

> अथाप्यग्निं द्रविणोदसमाहैष पुनरेतस्माज्जायते । यो अश्मनोरन्तरग्निं जजान इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥
>
> *athāpyagniṃ draviṇodasamāhaiṣa punaretasmājjāyate | yo aśmanorantaragniṃ jajāna ityapi nigamo bhavati ||*

And they give this word another sense: Indra created heaven and earth, and created Agni too between them; so the word *draviṇodāḥ* may also be said to mean Agni; to support this sense they give the Ṛk "*aśmanor antar agniṃ jajāna*" as an example.

> अथाप्यृतुयाजेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्ति । तेषां पुनः पात्रस्यैन्द्रपानमिति भवति ॥ अथाप्येनं सोमपानेन स्तौति । अथाप्याह द्रविणोदाः पिबतु द्रविणोदस इति ॥
>
> *athāpyṛtuyājeṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti | teṣāṃ punaḥ pātrasyaindrapānamiti bhavati || athāpyenaṃ somapānena stauti | athāpyāha draviṇodāḥ pibatu draviṇodasa iti ||*

Since it is said that at the sacrifices made with the Ṛtus in view Indra drinks the soma from the vessel in the priests' hands, and since Indra is praised with mantras about drinking soma, there is the custom of calling the priests *draviṇodasaḥ*: all this is Krauṣṭuki's view.

> अयमेवाग्निर्द्रविणोदा इति शाकपूणिः । आग्नेयेष्वेव हि सूक्तेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवन्ति ॥
>
> *ayamevāgnirdraviṇodā iti śākapūṇiḥ | āgneyeṣveva hi sūkteṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti ||*

That Agni himself is *draviṇodāḥ* is Śākapūṇi's view; for in the sūktas about Agni, when the priests praise Agni, they use the word *draviṇodāḥ* as an epithet of Agni.

> यथो एतत्स बलधनयोर्दातृतम इति सर्वासु देवतास्वैश्वर्यं विद्यते । यथो एतदोजसो जातमुतमन्य एनमिति चाहेत्ययमप्यग्निरोजसा बलेन मथ्यमानो जायते तस्मादेनमाह सहसस्पुत्रं सहसः सूनुं सहसो यहुं ॥
>
> *yatho etatsa baladhanayordātṛtama iti sarvāsu devatāsvaiśvaryaṃ vidyate | yatho etadojaso jātamutamanya enamiti cāhetyayamapyagnirojasā balena mathyamāno jāyate tasmādenamāha sahasasputraṃ sahasaḥ sūnuṃ sahaso yahuṃ ||*

In all deities there is lordship; so Agni too gives strength and wealth. Since he gives strength and wealth, Agni too can be called *draviṇodāḥ*. Besides, it is clear that the word *draviṇa* means strength. Since in kindling Agni one churns using strength, there is the notion that Agni is born of strength. That is why they praise Agni with the words *sahasas putram* (the son of strength), *sahasaḥ sūnum*, *sahaso yahum*:

> द्र्वन्नः सर्पिरासुतिः प्रत्नो होता वरेण्यः ।
> सहसस्पुत्रो अद्भुतः ॥
>
> *drvannaḥ sarpirāsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ |*
> *sahasasputro adbhutaḥ ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. "2-7-6" [?]; the print reads द्र्वन्नः for the first word.)* *("Eating wood, receiving ghee as his libation, the ancient Hotṛ, choice-worthy, the son of strength, the wonderful" — mine and tentative.)*

### Page 654 — Rik 7: Special Topics (end) and grammar

> त्वं ह यद्यविष्ठ्य सहसः सूनवाहुतः ।
> ऋतावा यज्ञियो भुवः ॥
>
> *tvaṃ ha yadyaviṣṭhya sahasaḥ sūnavāhutaḥ |*
> *ṛtāvā yajñiyo bhuvaḥ ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. "8-23-3" [?]; the middle digits are small.)* *("When you, youngest, son of strength, are offered to, you become true to order and worthy of worship" — mine and tentative.)*

> अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो ।
> अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥
>
> *agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho |*
> *asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ||*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-79-4.)* *("O Agni, lord of strength rich in cattle, son of strength, give us great fame, O Jātavedas" — mine and tentative.)*

In these Ṛks the words *sahasas putra*, *sahasaḥ sūnu* and *sahaso yahu* are used in turn in praising Agni. So, though other deities too give strength and wealth, it is Agni above all who is set forth by the word *draviṇodāḥ*.

**Grāvahastāsaḥ**: those who hold stones in their hands to crush the soma creeper.

**Adhvare, yajñeṣu**: though the words *adhvara* and *yajña* generally denote the same thing, sacrifice, here the Bhāṣyakāra, fearing the fault of repetition, gives *adhvara* the sense of the Agniṣṭoma in its model form and *yajña* the sense of the particular sacrifices such as the Ukthya in their modified forms. The model (*prakṛti*) is the basic sacrificial rite that contains the procedures common to all sacrifices. The modification (*vikṛti*) is a sacrificial rite carried out with some changes here and there as the occasion requires; that is, in a modified sacrifice all the acts are as in the model sacrifice, with a slight difference in only one or two matters. We have explained the model and modified sacrifices earlier.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 654–656, noted briefly)*

**द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*)**: "drudakṣibhyām inan" (Uṇ. sū. "2-50" [?]; *dru gatau*, *dakṣa vṛddhau*): after these roots the suffix *inan*; with *inan* after *dru*: *dru* + *ina*; *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84), *o* for the *u*; *av* for the *o* by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-78): *dravina*; *ṇ* for the *n* by "aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi" (Pā. sū. 8-4-2): *draviṇa*. *Draviṇaṃ dadāti iti draviṇodāḥ*: with the *subanta* *draviṇam* as *upapada*, *kvip* after *dā* by "kvip ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-76); *kvip* drops; a *prātipadika* by "kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-2-46); the *am* dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71); the first member, as a Vedic form,

### Page 655 — Rik 7: grammar (continued)

takes the augment *suk*, joining an *s*: *draviṇas* + *dā*; *ru* for the *s* by "sasajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-2-66): *draviṇar* + *dā*; *u* for the *ru* by "haśi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-114): *draviṇa* + *u* + *dā*; *guṇa* by "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-87): *draviṇodā*. *Dā* is final udātta by the root accent of "dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-162); after compounding, the *kṛt* second-member accent comes by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. sū. 6-2-139) and remains. *Draviṇodāḥ* qualifies the accusative singular *devam*; so if one sentence is meant, for the accusative *am* after *draviṇodā* the replacement *su* comes by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. sū. 7-1-39): *draviṇodās*, *ru*, visarga: *draviṇodāḥ*. Or, with the analysis *draviṇam ātmanaḥ icchanti*, it becomes *draviṇasyanti*: in this case *kyac* by "supa ātmanaḥ kyac" after *draviṇam* in the sense "they desire for themselves"; the *kyac*-form is called a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-1-32); the *sup* inside the root is dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-71); by "sarvaprātipadikebhyo lālasāyāṃ sug vaktavyaḥ" (Pā. sū. Ma. Bhā. 7-1-51-2) (*lālasā* is *atiśayenābhyavajihīrṣā*, as the Kaiyaṭa explains; *utkaṭecchā*, eager desire, says the Tattvabodhinī), when eager desire is shown before *kyac* all stems take the augment *suk*: *draviṇasya*. After it, by "sampadādibhyaḥ kvip" (Pā. sū. vārtti. 3-3-108-9) *kvip* in the action sense: *draviṇasya* + *v*; "ato lopaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-4-48): the *a* of what ends in *a* at the time the *ārdhadhātuka* suffix is taught drops; so the *a* before the suffix drops: *draviṇasy* + *v*. In this *a*-loss view, when the *y* is to be dropped, "acaḥ parasmin pūrvavidhau" (Pā. sū. 1-1-57) would give *sthānivadbhāva*, but by "kvau luptaṃ na sthānivad bhavati" (Pā. Ma. 1-1-58-2) what is dropped with reference to the *kvip* suffix is not *sthānivat*; so *sthānivadbhāva* is barred. "lopo vyor vali" (Pā. sū. 6-1-66): before a *val* letter *v* and *y* drop; so the *y* drops. "ver apṛktasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-67): *apṛkta* is a suffix of a single letter; the *apṛkta* *v* drops. Though the loss of the *apṛkta* *v*, having no outside cause, is *antaraṅga*, and the loss before *val*, having an outside cause, is *bahiraṅga*, so that by "asiddhaṃ bahiraṅgam antaraṅge" (paribhāṣā 50) the *val*-loss would count as not done when the *apṛkta* loss is made, and then, once the *apṛkta* loss came first, the bar of *sthānivadbhāva* in the *al*-rule would make the *val*-loss not come: yet by "ver apṛktalopād vali lopo balīyān", the *val*-loss comes first, then the *apṛkta* loss: *draviṇas*. This means desire for wealth. *Draviṇecchāṃ dasyati*: one who, by giving

### Page 656 — Rik 7: grammar (end)

wealth as desired, removes the desire for wealth: with this sense meant, *kvip* by "kvip ca" after the root *dasu upakṣaye* with the inner causative; the *kvip* drops. In this way the word *draviṇodas* ends in *s*. By this derivation Yāska's usage *draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavanti* (Ni. 8-2) fits. So if *draviṇodāḥ* is taken as not qualifying *devam*, two sentences arise; on this view the nominative singular *su* comes in its own sense, giving *draviṇodāḥ*; on the one-sentence view the nominative must be taken in the sense of the accusative by *vyatyaya*.

**द्रविणसः (*draviṇasaḥ*)**: here too, on the separate-sentence view, *draviṇasaḥ* means "of the soma juice"; in this sense, by a Vedic process, the augment *s* comes, giving *draviṇasaḥ*. By "ñnityādir nityam" it is initial udātta as a rule. On the view that *draviṇasaḥ* qualifies the priests and there is one sentence, as said before, *kvip* after the *kyac* form, and by "ato lopaḥ" and the other rules the loss of *a* and the other operations come as before. On this view the *kyac* suffix is *cit*, so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) final udātta would come, but by *vyatyaya* it is initial udātta. On the one-sentence view the construction is *adhvare yajñeṣu ca draviṇaso grāvahastāso ṛtvijaḥ draviṇodā devam īḷate*. On the separate-sentence view the constructions are *draviṇasaḥ grāvahastāsaḥ ṛtvijaḥ adhvare yajñeṣu ca devam īḷate, draviṇodāḥ agniḥ somaṃ pibatu*, and *grāvahastāsaḥ ṛtvijaḥ adhvare yajñeṣu ca devam īḷate, draviṇodāḥ agniḥ draviṇasaḥ somasya pātā bhavatu*.

**ग्रावहस्तासः (*grāvahastāsaḥ*)**: *grāvayuktāḥ hastāḥ yeṣāṃ te grāvahastāsaḥ*, a bahuvrīhi compound. After *grāvahasta*, *jas*; by "ājjaser asuk" (Pā. sū. 7-1-50) *jas* takes the augment *asuk*. The word *grāvan* belongs to the *vṛṣādi* class, so it is initial udātta by "vṛṣādīnāṃ ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-203); even after compounding, by "bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam" (Pā. sū. 6-2-1) the first-member accent comes.

**अध्वरे (*adhvare*)**: *na vidyate dhvaraḥ hiṃsā yasmin saḥ adhvaraḥ*; overriding the first-member accent, by "nañsubhyām" (Pā. sū. 6-2-172) the second member is final udātta.

**ईळते (*īḷate*)**: *īḍa stutau*; the root is *anudāttet*, so by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (Pā. sū. 1-3-12) the *ātmanepada*. *Laṭ*, 3rd plural *jha*. The *vikaraṇa* *śap* is dropped by "adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-72). By "ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-5) *at* for the *jh*. By "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79) *e* for the *ṭi*: *īḍate*; *ḷ* for the *ḍ* by "ajmadhyasya ḍakārasya…".

**॥७॥**

### Page 657 — Sūkta 15, Rik 8

*(Saṃhitā accents as printed; Pada unaccented.)*

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> द्र॒वि॒णो॒दा द॑दातु नो॒ वसू॑नि॒ यानि॑ शृण्वि॒रे ।
> दे॒वेषु॒ ता व॑नामहे ॥८॥
>
> *draviṇodā́ dadātu no vásūni yā́ni śṛṇviré |*
> *devéṣu tā́ vanāmahe ||8||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> द्रविणःऽदाः । ददातु । नः । वसूनि । यानि । शृण्विरे ॥
> देवेषु । ता । वनामहे ॥८॥
>
> *draviṇaḥ 'dāḥ | dadātu | naḥ | vasūni | yāni | śṛṇvire ||*
> *deveṣu | tā | vanāmahe ||8||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> द्रविणोदा देवो नो ऽस्मभ्यं वसूनि धनानि ददातु । यानि धनानि शृण्विरे हविरुपयुक्तत्वेन श्रूयन्ते । ता तानि च सर्वाणि धनानि देवेषु निमित्तभूतेषु वनामहे । सम्भजामः । धनैर्देवान्यष्टुं तानि स्वीकुर्म इत्यर्थः ॥ द्रविणोदाः । गतं । वसूनि । शृस्वृस्निहीत्यादिना । उ. १-११ । उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेराद्युदात्तः । शृण्विरे । श्रु श्रवणे । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने लिट् । झ इरेच् । पा. ३-४-८१ । छन्दस्युभयथेति सार्वधातुकत्वे व्यत्ययेन श्नुः । तत्सन्नियोगेन शृभावश्च । उवङि प्राप्ते हुश्नुवोः सार्वधातुके । पा. ६-४-८७ । इति यणादेशः । चित इत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । यद्वृत्तान्नित्यमिति निघातप्रतिषेधः । ता । शेश्छन्दसि बहुलमिति शेर्लोपः । नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य । पा. ८-२-७ । इति नलोपः । वनामहे । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥
>
> *draviṇodā devo no 'smabhyaṃ vasūni dhanāni dadātu | yāni dhanāni śṛṇvire havirupayuktatvena śrūyante | tā tāni ca sarvāṇi dhanāni deveṣu nimittabhūteṣu vanāmahe | sambhajāmaḥ | dhanairdevānyaṣṭuṃ tāni svīkurma ityarthaḥ || draviṇodāḥ | gataṃ | vasūni | śṛsvṛsnihītyādinā | u. 1-11 | upratyayaḥ | nidityanuvṛtterādyudāttaḥ | śṛṇvire | śru śravaṇe | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti vartamāne liṭ | jha irec | pā. 3-4-81 | chandasyubhayatheti sārvadhātukatve vyatyayena śnuḥ | tatsanniyogena śṛbhāvaśca | uvaṅi prāpte huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke | pā. 6-4-87 | iti yaṇādeśaḥ | cita ityantodāttatvaṃ | yadvṛttānnityamiti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | tā | śeśchandasi bahulamiti śerlopaḥ | nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya | pā. 8-2-7 | iti nalopaḥ | vanāmahe | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | vyatyayenātmanepadaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "May the god Draviṇodas give us *vasūni*, riches. The riches that *śṛṇvire*, are heard of, as fit for oblations: *tā*, all those riches, *devesu*, for the sake of the gods, *vanāmahe*, we accept; that is, we take them in order to worship the gods with riches." (Grammatical tail: *draviṇodāḥ* gone through; *vasūni* with *u* (Uṇ. 1-11), initial udātta (*nit* carried on); *śṛṇvire*: *śru*, *liṭ* in the present, *irec* for *jha* (Pā. 3-4-81), by *chandasy ubhayathā* *sārvadhātuka* status and so by *vyatyaya* *śnu* with *śṛ* for *śru*, *yaṇ* for the *uvaṅ* by Pā. 6-4-87, final udātta (*cit*), not lowered because of the relative *yāni*; *tā*: the *śi* dropped by *śeś chandasi bahulam*, the *n* dropped (Pā. 8-2-7); *vanāmahe*, *van* 'to share', *ātmanepada* by *vyatyaya*.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ)** — the god who gives wealth (Agni) | **यानि (yāni)** — the riches which | **शृण्विरे (śṛṇvire)** — are well known as fit for oblations | **ता वसूनि (tā vasūni)** — those riches | **नः (naḥ)** — to us | **ददातु (dadātu)** — may he give | **ता (tā)** — all those riches | **देवेषु (devesu)** — for the sake of the gods | **वनामहे (vanāmahe)** — we take.

### Page 658 — Rik 8: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

We look for wealth for the works of the gods, such as sacrifices. May Agni, the giver of wealth, graciously grant us all the wealth known to be for these works.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> May Dravinodas give us riches that may be heard of; we ask them towards the service of the gods.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Yāni śṛṇvire**: all such things, of whatever kinds of wealth and lordship we have heard there are. Since it is said here *devesu tā vanāmahe*, those things must be fit to be offered to the gods; so the Bhāṣyakāra says they are things fit for offering oblations.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 658–659, noted briefly)*

**द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*)**: explained in the previous mantra.

**वसूनि (*vasūni*)**: by "śṛsvṛsnihitrapyasivasihanikledibandhimanibhyaś ca" (Uṇ. sū. "1-10" [?]; the bhāṣya gives 1-11) the suffix *u* after *vasa nivāse*. In this sūtra *nit* is carried on from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. sū. 1-9); so the suffix *u* is *nit*, and by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-197) initial udātta comes.

**शृण्विरे (*śṛṇvire*)**: *śru śravaṇe*; by "chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-6) *liṭ* in the present sense; 3rd plural *jha*; by "liṭas tajhayor eśirec" (Pā. sū. 3-4-81) *irec* for the *jha*. By "chandasy ubhayathā" (Pā. sū. 3-4-117) it also has *sārvadhātuka* status; so by "śruvaḥ śṛ ca" (Pā. sū. 3-1-74) *śṛ* comes for *śru*, together with the suffix *śnu*: *śṛ* + *nu* + *ire*. Now "iko yaṇ aci" (Pā. sū. 6-1-77) would give *yaṇ*; overriding it, "aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-77) would give *uvaṅ*; overriding that too, "huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke" (Pā. sū. 6-4-87): before a vowel-initial *sārvadhātuka* suffix, the *u* of *hu* and of a stem ending in *śnu* with several vowels,

### Page 659 — Rik 8: grammar (end)

not preceded by a conjunct, takes *yaṇ*; so *yaṇ*. By "ṛvarṇān nasya ṇatvaṃ vācyam" (Pā. sū. 8-4-1 vā. 1) *ṇ* for the *n*: *śṛṇvire*. The suffix *irec* is *cit*, so by "citaḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-163) it is final udātta. By "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66) the full lowering is barred, so "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28) does not make it wholly unaccented.

**ता (*tā*)**: *tad* in the neuter, with *śas* after it; *a* for the *d* by "tyadādīnām aḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-2-102); *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. sū. 6-1-97). "jaśśasoḥ śiḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-20): for *jas* and *śas* after a neuter stem, the replacement *śi*; so *śi* for *śas*. By "śi sarvanāmasthānam" (Pā. sū. 1-1-42) *śi* is a *sarvanāmasthāna*. "napuṃsakasya jhalacaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-1-72): a neuter stem ending in a *jhal* or a vowel takes the augment *num* before a *sarvanāmasthāna*; so *num*: *tan* + *i*; by "sarvanāmasthāne cāsambuddhau" (Pā. sū. 6-4-8) the penultimate is lengthened: *tān* + *i*. By "śeś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. sū. 6-1-70) the *śi* drops; by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. sū. 8-2-7) the *n* drops: *tā*. It means *tāni*.

**वनामहे (*vanāmahe*)**: *vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau*. In "vyatyayo bahulam" (Pā. sū. 3-1-85), in the kārikā *suptiṅupagraha…*, *upagraha* is explained as *parasmaipada* and *ātmanepada*; so there is interchange between *parasmaipada* and *ātmanepada*. The word *vyatyaya* is made from the root *iṇ gatau* with the two *upasargas* *vi* and *ati*, with *ac* in the action sense; it means "going beyond". So it is settled that where there is a cause for *parasmaipada*, going beyond it the *ātmanepada* comes, and where there is a cause for *ātmanepada*, going beyond it the *parasmaipada* comes, in some places. Though the root *van* is *parasmaipadin*, going beyond that, the *ātmanepada* comes by "vyatyayo bahulam" (3-1-85). Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

**॥८॥**

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> द्र॒वि॒णो॒दाः पि॑पीषति जु॒होत॒ प्र च॑ तिष्ठत ।
> ने॒ष्ट्रादृ॒तुभि॑रिष्यत ॥९॥ [accent ?]
>
> *draviṇodā́ḥ pipīṣati juhóta prá ca tiṣṭhata |*

### Page 660 — Rik 9: Pada, bhāṣya, word-meanings

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> द्रविणःऽदाः । पिपीषति । जुहोत । प्र । च । तिष्ठत ॥
> नेष्ट्रात् । ऋतुऽभिः । इष्यत ॥९॥
>
> *draviṇaḥ 'dāḥ | pipīṣati | juhota | pra | ca | tiṣṭhata ||*
> *neṣṭrāt | ṛtu 'bhiḥ | iṣyata ||9||*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> *draviṇodā deva ṛtubhiḥ saha neṣṭrānneṣṭṛsambandhipātrātpipīṣati | somaṃ pātumicchati | tato he ṛtvija iṣyata | homasthāne gacchata | gatvā ca juhota | homaṃ kuruta | hutvā pra tiṣṭhata ca | homasthānātsthānāntaraṃ prati prasthānamapi kuruta || draviṇodāḥ | gataṃ | pipīṣati | pā pāne | pātumicchatīti san | chāndasa īkāraḥ | tiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | juhota | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanaṃ | tasya laṅvadbhāvāttādeśaḥ | tasya taptanaptanathanāśceti tabādeśaḥ | tasya pittvādguṇaḥ | abhyastānāmādirityanuvṛttāvanudātte ca | pā. 6-1-190 | ityādyudāttatve prāpte bhīhrībhṛhumadajanadhanadaridrājāgarāṃ pratyayātpūrvaṃ piti | pā. 6-1-192 | iti hokāra udāttaḥ | tiṣṭhata | ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanasya thasya laṅvadbhāvāttādeśaḥ | śapi pāghretyādinā tiṣṭhādeśaḥ | samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ | pā. 1-3-22 | ityātmanepadaṃ na bhavati | tatrānuvṛttasya nirdiṣṭagrahaṇasyānantaryārthatvāt | atra caśabdena vyavadhānātte prāgdhātoḥ | pā. 1-4-80 | ityupasargatvena prākprayoktavyasyāpi praśabdasya vyavahitāśceti chandasi vyavahitaprayogaḥ | atra caśabdo juhoteti pūrveṇa saha samuccayārthaḥ | na punariṣyatetyuttareṇa | tenāprathamatvāccavāyoge prathamā | pā. 8-1-59 | iti niṣedhābhāvāttiṅṅatiṅa iti nighātaḥ | neṣṭrāt | potrādyajñaṃ punītana | ṛgve. 1-15-2 | ityatra potraśabdena yaduktaṃ tadatra draṣṭavyaṃ | iṣyata | iṣa gatau | loṇmadhyamabahuvacanaṃ ||*

**Translation:** "The god Draviṇodas, with the Ṛtus, *pipīṣati*, wishes to drink the soma, from the *neṣṭra*, the vessel belonging to the Neṣṭṛ. So, O priests, *iṣyata*, go to the place of the *homa*; having gone, *juhota*, make the *homa*; having made it, *pra tiṣṭhata ca*, also set out from the place of the *homa* to another place." (Grammatical tail: *draviṇodāḥ* gone through; *pipīṣati*, *san* after *pā* 'to drink' in the sense of wishing, the *ī* Vedic, lowered; *juhota*: *loṭ* 2nd plural, *ta* by *laṅvadbhāva*, *tap* for it, *guṇa* (*pit*); the initial udātta of Pā. 6-1-190 is overridden by Pā. 6-1-192, so the *o* is udātta; *tiṣṭhata*: *tiṣṭha* for *sthā*; the *ātmanepada* of Pā. 1-3-22 does not come, the immediate sequence being required there and *ca* intervening; *pra*, which as an *upasarga* should come before the root (Pā. 1-4-80), is used separated in the Veda; *ca* joins *juhota* with what precedes, not with *iṣyata*; so, *tiṣṭhata* not being the first, the bar of Pā. 8-1-59 does not apply and it is lowered; *neṣṭrāt* as said for *potra* at Ṛ. 1-15-2; *iṣyata*, *iṣ* 'to go', *loṭ* 2nd plural.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ)** — Agni, the giver of wealth | **ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ)** — with the Ṛtu deities | **नेष्ट्रात् (neṣṭrāt)** — from the Neṣṭṛ's vessel | **पिपीषति (pipīṣati)** — wishes to drink (the soma juice); (so, O priests) | **इष्यत (iṣyata)** — go (to the place of sacrifice) | **जुहोत (juhota)** — make the *homa*; (then) | **प्र तिष्ठत च (pra tiṣṭhata ca)** — leave the place of the *homa* and go back to your own places.

### Page 661 — Rik 9: overall sense, English, Special Topics, grammar

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O priests, Agni, the giver of wealth and the self of the gods, looks to drink the soma juice from the Neṣṭṛ's vessel. So all of you come to the place of sacrifice, make the *homa*, and then go out.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Dravinodas desires to drink with the Ritu's from the cup of Neshtri; hasten, priests, present the oblation and depart.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Pipīṣati**:

> पा पाने । पातुमिच्छति ॥
>
> *pā pāne | pātumicchati ||*

he looks to drink.

**Neṣṭrāt**: the soma juice from the vessel in the hand of the priest called Neṣṭṛ.

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 661–663, noted briefly)*

**द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*)**: explained in the seventh mantra.

**पिपीषति (*pipīṣati*)**: the root *pā pāne*; analysed *pātum icchati*. "dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samānakartṛkād icchāyāṃ vā" (Pā. sū. 3-1-7): the root *iṣu icchāyām*; after a root expressing an activity that has the same agent as this *iṣ* and is the object of the *iṣ*, the suffix *san* comes in the sense of wishing: that is the sense of the sūtra. Here the one who wishes is Agni; Agni is the agent of *iṣ*; the same Agni is the agent in the activity favourable to contact with the throat, which is the sense of *pā*; so the activity of *pā* has the same agent as the wishing, and this activity is the object of *iṣ*. So *san* comes after *pā*, denoting such an activity, in the sense of wishing: *pā* + *sa*; reduplication by "sanyaṅoḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-9): *pā* + *pā* + *sa*; the reduplicate shortened by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-59); *i* for the *a* of the reduplicate by "sanyataḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-79): *pipāsati*. Now the *ā* becomes *ī* as a Vedic form. *Ṣ* for the *s* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-3-59): *pipīṣati*. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" ("8-12-28" [as printed, for 8-1-28]).

**जुहोत (*juhota*)**: *hu dānādanayoḥ* (*juhotyādi*); *loṭ*, 2nd plural *tha*; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the *laṅvadbhāva*; so

### Page 662 — Rik 9: grammar (continued)

by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) *ta* for *tha*; *tap* for it by "taptanaptanathanāś ca" (Pā. sū. 7-1-45); the *vikaraṇa* *śap* by "kartari śap", dropped (*ślu*) by "juhotyādibhyaḥ śluḥ" (Pā. sū. 2-4-75); reduplication of the root by "ślau" (Pā. sū. 6-1-10): *hu* + *hu* + *ta*; by "kuhoś cuḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-62), for the *h*, closed, with great breath, a *jh* of that kind; by "abhyāse carc ca" (Pā. sū. 8-4-54) *j* for the *jh*: *ju* + *hu* + *ta*. *Tap* is *pit*, so by "sārvadhātukam apit" (Pā. sū. 1-2-4) it is not *ṅit*; so "kṅiti ca" (Pā. sū. 1-1-5) does not bar *guṇa*; *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-3-84): *juhota*. The *sārvadhātuka* *ta* standing for the *lakāra* is *pit*, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4). With "abhyastānām ādiḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-189) carried on in "anudātte ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-190), *na vidyate udāttaḥ yasmin saḥ anudāttaḥ, tasmin anudātte*: before an unaccented *sārvadhātuka* in the place of a *lakāra*, the first syllable of a reduplicated stem is udātta; so the initial udātta would come; but overriding it, "bhīhrībhṛhumadajanadhanadaridrājāgarāṃ pratyayāt pūrvaṃ piti" (Pā. sū. 6-1-192): *ñibhī bhaye*, *hrī lajjāyām*, *ḍubhṛñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*, *hu dānādanayoḥ*, *madī harṣe* (a *divādi* root, but by a Vedic process *śap* gets *ślu*), *jana janane*, *dhana dhānye*, *daridrā durgatau*, *jāgṛ nidrākṣaye*. *Daridrā* and *jāgṛ* are reduplicated by "jakṣityādayaḥ ṣaṭ" (Pā. sū. "6-1-6" [?]), by which *jakṣ* and the six roots after it are called reduplicated; the others are reduplicated by "ubhe abhyastam" (Pā. sū. "6-1-5" [?]). Before a *pit* *sārvadhātuka* in the place of a *lakāra*, in the roots *bhī* and the rest that are reduplicated, the syllable before the suffix is udātta; so the *o* before the suffix *ta* is udātta.

**तिष्ठत (*tiṣṭhata*)**: the root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *s* for the *ṣ* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ" (Pā. sū. 6-1-64); with the *ṣṭutva* gone, the *ṭh* reverts: *sthā*. *Loṭ*, 2nd plural *tha*: *sthā* + *tha*; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the *laṅvadbhāva*; by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) *ta* for *tha*; by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68) *śap*: *sthā* + *a* + *ta*; by "pāghrādhmā…" (Pā. sū. 7-3-78) *tiṣṭha* for *sthā*: *tiṣṭhata*. "samavapravibhyaḥ sthaḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-3-22): after the *upasargas* *sam*, *ava*, *pra*, *vi*, the root *sthā* takes the *ātmanepada* in the place of the *lakāra*; but here, though there is an *upasarga*, the *ātmanepada* does not come, since *samavapravibhyaḥ* is a fifth-case statement. So by "tasmād ity uttarasya" (Pā. sū. 1-1-67), the paribhāṣā

### Page 663 — Rik 9: grammar (end)

means: the operation enjoined in a rule that names a fifth-case form comes for what immediately follows. By this paribhāṣā, the *ātmanepada* is enjoined when *sthā* immediately follows *sam* and the other *upasargas*. Here, in *pra ca tiṣṭhata*, *ca* intervenes between them; so the *ātmanepada* does not come. *Pra* is an *upasarga*; so by "te prāg dhātoḥ" (Pā. sū. 1-4-80) the *gati* and *upasarga* words must be used immediately before the root, and *pra* ought to be used immediately before the root. But by "vyavahitāś ca" (Pā. sū. 1-4-82) in the Veda the *gati* and *upasarga* words may be used separated too; so here *pra* is used separated. Here *ca* conveys the joining with the earlier action: *juhota*, *pratiṣṭhata ca*, "make the *homa*, and having made it go to another place". It does not convey joining with *iṣyata* as *pratiṣṭhata iṣyata ca*. So, with reference to the action joined by *ca*, *tiṣṭhata* is not the first *tiṅanta*. So "cavāyoge prathamā" (Pā. sū. 8-1-59): when joined with *ca* or *vā*, the first *tiṅanta* is not unaccented; this bar does not apply, and by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" it is wholly unaccented.

**नेष्ट्रात् (*neṣṭrāt*)**: the derivation must be given here as for the word *potra* in the mantra *potrād yajñaṃ punītana* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-2).

**इष्यत (*iṣyata*)**: *iṣa gatau* (*divādi*), *loṭ*, 2nd plural *tha*; by "loṭo laṅvat" (Pā. sū. 3-4-85) the *laṅvadbhāva*; by "tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ" (Pā. sū. 3-4-101) *ta* for *tha*; by "divādibhyaḥ śyan" the *vikaraṇa* *śyan*: *iṣyata*. Wholly unaccented by "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" (Pā. sū. 8-1-28).

**॥९॥**

### Page 664 — Rik 10: bhāṣya, word-meanings, overall sense, English, Special Topics

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥**

> हे द्रविणोदो देव यद्यस्मात्कारणादृतुभिः सह त्वां यजामहे । अधेत्ययं निपातस्तच्छब्दार्थः । तस्मात्कारणान्नो ऽस्मभ्यं ददिर्धनस्य दाता भव स्म । अवश्यं भव । तुरीयं चतुर्णां पूरणं ॥ तुरीयं । चतुरश्छयतावाद्यक्षरलोपश्च । पा. ५-२-५१-१ । इति छप्रत्ययः । तस्य प्रत्ययस्वरेणोदात्तात्प्रागेवायनेयीनीत्यादिना । पा. ७-१-२ । ईयादेशः । आयनादिषूपदेशिवद्वचनं स्वरसिद्ध्यर्थं । पा. ७-१-२-१ । इति वचनात्कृत आदेशे प्रत्ययस्वरेणेकार उदात्तः । द्रविणोदः । उक्तं । पादादित्वादामन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वं । यजामहे । अत्र शपः पित्त्वेन तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव । पूर्वस्यामन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानवत्त्वाद्यद्वृत्तयोगाद्वा न निघातः । व्यवहितयोगे ऽपि हि स निषेध इत्युक्तं । अध । छान्दसो धकारः । स्म । चादिरनुदात्तः । संहितायां निपातस्य चेति दीर्घः । ददिः । डुदाञ् दाने । आदृगमहनजनः किकिनौ लिट् च । पा. ३-२-१७१ । इति किप्रत्ययः । लिड्वद्भावाद्द्विर्वचनादि । आतो लोप इटि च । पा. ६-४-६४ । इत्याकारलोपः । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥
>
> *he draviṇodo deva yadyasmātkāraṇādṛtubhiḥ saha tvāṃ yajāmahe | adhetyayaṃ nipātastacchabdārthaḥ | tasmātkāraṇānno 'smabhyaṃ dadirdhanasya dātā bhava sma | avaśyaṃ bhava | turīyaṃ caturṇāṃ pūraṇaṃ || turīyaṃ | caturaśchayatāvādyakṣaralopaśca | pā. 5-2-51-1 | iti chapratyayaḥ | tasya pratyayasvareṇodāttātprāgevāyaneyīnītyādinā | pā. 7-1-2 | īyādeśaḥ | āyanādiṣūpadeśivadvacanaṃ svarasiddhyarthaṃ | pā. 7-1-2-1 | iti vacanātkṛta ādeśe pratyayasvareṇekāra udāttaḥ | draviṇodaḥ | uktaṃ | pādāditvādāmantritādyudāttatvaṃ | yajāmahe | atra śapaḥ pittvena tiṅaśca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvara eva | pūrvasyāmantritasyāvidyamānavattvādyadvṛttayogādvā na nighātaḥ | vyavahitayoge 'pi hi sa niṣedha ityuktaṃ | adha | chāndaso dhakāraḥ | sma | cādiranudāttaḥ | saṃhitāyāṃ nipātasya ceti dīrghaḥ | dadiḥ | ḍudāñ dāne | ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca | pā. 3-2-171 | iti kipratyayaḥ | liḍvadbhāvāddvirvacanādi | āto lopa iṭi ca | pā. 6-4-64 | ityākāralopaḥ | pratyayasvaraḥ ||*

**Translation:** "O god Draviṇodas, *yat*, since, we worship you with the Ṛtus, *adha*, a particle in the sense of *tad*, for that reason be *dadiḥ*, the giver of wealth, *naḥ*, to us: *bhava sma*, be so without fail. *Turīyam*: the filler of four, the fourth." (Grammatical tail: *turīyam* with *cha* and the loss of the first syllable by the vārttika 5-2-51-1, the replacement *īya* (Pā. 7-1-2) made first, before the suffix accent, by the vārttika 7-1-2-1, so the *ī* is udātta; *draviṇodaḥ* as said, initial udātta at the head of the pāda; *yajāmahe*, the root accent, not lowered, the earlier vocative counting as absent, or because of the relative *yat*, for the bar holds even when *yat* is not adjacent; *adha*, the *dh* Vedic; *sma*, unaccented as of the *cādi* class, lengthened in the Saṃhitā by *nipātasya ca*; *dadiḥ*, *ki* after *dā* (Pā. 3-2-171), reduplication as in *liṭ*, the *ā* dropped (Pā. 6-4-64), the suffix accent.)

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥**

**द्रविणोदः (draviṇodaḥ)** — O Agni, giver of wealth | **यत् (yat)** — for the reason that | **ऋतुभिः (ṛtubhiḥ)** — with the Ṛtu deities | **तुरीयम् (turīyam)** — for the fourth time | **त्वा (tvā)** — you | **यजामहे (yajāmahe)** — we worship | **अध (adha)** — so | **नः (naḥ)** — to us | **ददिः (dadiḥ)** — as the giver of wealth | **भव स्म (bhava sma)** — be, without fail.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Agni, seeking wealth, we worship you, the fourth, with the Ṛtu deities. So surely accept our worship and become the giver of wealth.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Dravinodas, Since we adore you for the fourth time along with the Ritus; therefore be a giver (of riches) to us.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥**

**Turīyam**: for the fourth time. In this sūkta there are four Ṛks praising Agni called Draviṇodas (the Ṛks from 7 to 10); among them this is the fourth. So here *turīyam* means "for the fourth time", or "we praise with the fourth Ṛk".

### Page 665 — Rik 10: grammar

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā ॥** *(grammar pages 665–666, noted briefly)*

**तुरीयम् (*turīyam*)**: analysed *caturṇāṃ pūraṇam*. "caturaś chayatāv ādyakṣaralopaś ca" (Pā. sū. "5-2-51" [as printed; the bhāṣya gives 5-2-51-1]): in the sense of filling, after *catur* the suffixes *cha* and *yat* come alternately, and the first syllable also drops; so the suffix *cha* after *catur*: *catur* + *cha*; by this vārttika itself the first *akṣara* drops. *Akṣara* should not be explained as the first consonant with its vowel, nor as the first vowel with its consonant. If it is so explained, by the maxim "naṭabhāryāvad vyañjanāni bhavanti" it would mean the first vowel with the consonants before and after it, and then in *catur* the *cat* would have to drop. So *ādyakṣara* means the first consonant with its vowel. Thus *ca* drops: *tur* + *cha*. "āyanādiṣūpadeśivadvacanaṃ svarasiddhyartham" (Pā. Ma. "2-1-2-1" [as printed, for 7-1-2-1]): before the initial udātta comes by "ādyudāttaś ca", by "āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ…" (Pā. sū. "2-1-2" [as printed, for 7-1-2]) *īya* replaces the suffix *cha*; after this replacement, by the suffix accent the *ī* of *īya* becomes udātta.

**द्रविणोदः (*draviṇodaḥ*)**: its formation is set out in the 7th mantra. Here *draviṇodaḥ* is a vocative singular, so it is a vocative. Being at the head of the pāda, it is not made unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 8-1-19); by the sixth-adhyāya "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-1-198) it is initial udātta.

**यजामहे (*yajāmahe*)**: *yaja devapūjādau*, *laṭ*, *ātmanepada* 1st plural *mahiṅ*; *śap* by "kartari śap" (Pā. sū. 3-1-68): *yaj* + *a* + *mahi*; *e* for the *ṭi* by "ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere" (Pā. sū. 3-4-79); lengthening by "ato dīrgho yañi" (Pā. sū. 7-3-101): *yajāmahe*. Here *śap* is *pit*, so unaccented by "anudāttau suppitau" (Pā. sū. 3-1-4). The *sārvadhātuka* *mahe* in place of the *lakāra* follows the *śap* of *adupadeśa*, so it is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttet…" (Pā. sū. 6-1-186). So the root accent remains. The earlier vocative *draviṇodaḥ* is treated as absent by "āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat" (Pā. sū. "8-1-27" [as printed, for 8-1-72]); so *yajāmahe* counts as at the head of the pāda, and "tiṅṅatiṅaḥ" ("8-8-28" [as printed]) does not make it wholly unaccented. Or the bar comes by "yadvṛttān nityam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-66). Since *pūjita* is mentioned again in "pūjanāt pūjitam" (Pā. sū. 8-1-67), it is made known that "in this section, though there is a fifth-case statement, immediate sequence is not required", as was set out before. So, though *yat* is not adjacent, there is no obstacle to the bar of *yadvṛttān nityam*.

### Page 666 — Rik 10: grammar (end)

**अध (*adha*)**: *atha* is a *nipāta*; the *th* becomes *dh* as a Vedic form. Initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Phi. sū. 80).

**स्म (*sma*)**: unaccented by "cādayo 'nudāttāḥ" (Phi. sū. 84). In the Saṃhitā lengthened by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. sū. 6-3-136).

**ददिः (*dadiḥ*)**: the root *ḍudāñ dāne*. "ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca" (Pā. sū. 3-2-171): after roots ending in *ā* and in *ṛ*, and after *gam* and the others, the suffixes *ki* and *kin* come, and they behave as *liṭ*; so the suffix *ki* after the *ā*-final root *dā*. Since it behaves as *liṭ*, reduplication by "liṭi dhātor anabhyāsasya" (Pā. sū. 6-1-8); shortening by "hrasvaḥ" (Pā. sū. 7-4-59): *da* + *dā* + *i*; by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pā. sū. 6-4-64) the *ā* drops: *dadi*. By the suffix accent it is final udātta.

**॥१०॥**

---

### Pages 666–670 — Sūkta 15, Rik 11

**॥ Saṃhitā-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अश्विना पिबतं मधु दीद्यग्नी शुचिव्रता ।
> ऋतुना यज्ञवाहसा ॥११॥
>
> *aśvinā pibataṃ madhu dīdyagnī śucivratā |*
> *ṛtunā yajñavāhasā ||11||*

**॥ Pada-pāṭhaḥ ॥**

> अश्विना । पिबतम् । मधु । दीद्यग्नी इति दीदिऽअग्नी । शुचिऽव्रता ॥
> ऋतुना । यज्ञऽवाहसा ॥११॥
>
> *aśvinā | pibatam | madhu | dīdyagnī iti dīdi-agnī | śuci-vratā ||*
> *ṛtunā | yajña-vāhasā ||11||*

*(Accent-marks printed in the source; not reproduced.)*

**॥ Sāyaṇa-bhāṣyam ॥** *(pp. 666–667; compressed; [?] marks doubtful readings)*

> हे अश्विनौ मधु माधुर्योपेतं सोमं पिबतम् । कीदृशौ । दीद्यग्नी द्योतमानाहवनीयाद्यग्नियुक्तौ शुचिव्रता शुद्धकर्माणौ ऋतुना ऋतुदेवतया सह यज्ञवाहसा यज्ञस्य निर्वाहकौ ॥ अश्विना । सम्बोधनद्विवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तः । पिबतम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । तिङश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । मधु । फलिपाटीत्यादिना । उ. [१-१८]। उप्रत्ययः । निदित्यनुवृत्तेर्णित्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । दीद्यग्नी । दिवु क्रीडादौ । आन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते इति विच् । वेरपृक्तलोपाद्वलि लोपो बलीयान् इति प्रथमवकारस्य लोपः । पा. [६-१-६६, ६७] । प्रथमं प्रत्ययलोपे हि वर्णाश्रयविधौ प्रत्ययलक्षणं नास्ति … इति निषेधाद्वलिलोपो न स्यात् । छान्दसं द्विर्वचनम् । तुजादित्वादभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् । यज्ञलुगन्तताद्वा संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्य इत्यभ्यासस्य गुणाभावः । दीदिरग्निर्ययोस्तौ दीद्यग्नी । आमन्त्रिताद्युदात्तत्वम् । पादादित्वान्न निघातः । शुचिव्रता । शुचि व्रतं ययोस्तौ । सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः । दीद्यग्नीशब्दस्य सामान्यवचनत्वेन नामन्त्रित इत्यविद्यमानवत्त्वप्रतिषेधाद्… । पूर्वस्य पराङ्गवद्भावात् … । यज्ञवाहसा । वह प्रापणे । यज्ञं वहत इति यज्ञवाहसौ । वहिहाधाङ्भ्यश्छन्दसि । उ. [४-२२०]। इत्यसुन् । तत्र हि गतिकारकोपपदात्कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं चेति वचनाल्लोपपदानामपि भवति । उ. [४-२१६]। इत्युक्तम् । जिदित्यनुवृत्तेरुपधावृद्धिः । सुपां सुलुगित्यादिना विभक्तेराकारः । आमन्त्रितनिघातः । आसामर्थ्यात्पूर्वस्य न पराङ्गवद्भावः ॥११॥
>
> *he aśvinau madhu mādhuryopetaṃ somaṃ pibatam | kīdṛśau | dīdyagnī dyotamānāhavanīyādy-agni-yuktau śucivratā śuddha-karmāṇau ṛtunā ṛtu-devatayā saha yajñavāhasā yajñasya nirvāhakau || aśvinā | sambodhana-dvivacanasya supāṃ sulug ity ākāraḥ | āmantritādyudāttaḥ | pibatam | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | tiṅaś ca lasārvadhātuka-svareṇa dhātu-svara eva śiṣyate | madhu | phali-pāṭī-ty-ādinā | u. [1-18] | u-pratyayaḥ | nid ity anuvṛtter ṇittvād ādyudāttaḥ | dīdyagnī | divu krīḍādau | ānyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante iti vic | ver apṛkta-lopād vali lopo balīyān iti prathama-vakārasya lopaḥ | pā. [6-1-66, 67] | prathamaṃ pratyaya-lope hi varṇāśraya-vidhau pratyaya-lakṣaṇaṃ nāsti … iti niṣedhād vali-lopo na syāt | chāndasaṃ dvirvacanam | tujādittvād abhyāsasya dīrghatvam | yaja-luganta-tvād vā saṃjñā-pūrvako vidhir anitya ity abhyāsasya guṇābhāvaḥ | dīdir agnir yayos tau dīdyagnī | āmantritādyudāttatvam | pādāditvān na nighātaḥ | śucivratā | śuci vrataṃ yayos tau | supāṃ sulug ity ākāraḥ | dīdyagnī-śabdasya sāmānya-vacanatvena nāmantrita ity avidyamānavatva-pratiṣedhād … | pūrvasya parāṅgavad-bhāvāt … | yajñavāhasā | vaha prāpaṇe | yajñaṃ vahata iti yajñavāhasau | vahi-hā-dhāṅbhyaś chandasi | u. [4-220] | ity asun | tatra hi gati-kārakopapadāt kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svaratvaṃ ceti vacanāl lopa-padānām api bhavati | u. [4-216] | ity uktam | jid ity anuvṛtter upadhā-vṛddhiḥ | supāṃ sulug ity-ādinā vibhakter ākāraḥ | āmantrita-nighātaḥ | āsāmarthyāt pūrvasya na parāṅgavad-bhāvaḥ ||11||*

**Translation:** "O Aśvins! Drink the sweet (*madhu*, sweet-tasting) soma. Of what sort are you? *Dīdyagnī* — joined with the shining *āhavanīya* and other fires; *śucivratā* — of pure works; *yajñavāhasā* — together with the Ṛtu, the carriers (completers) of the sacrifice." The rest is grammar, noted briefly: *aśvinā* (the dual vocative with *ā* by P. 7-1-39 *supāṃ sulug…*; first-syllable accent of the vocative); *pibatam* (*śap* *pit*, unaccented; the root accent remains); *madhu* (the Uṇādi *u* suffix, first-syllable accent); *dīdyagnī* (*div* "to play" with *vic*, doubling of the verb stem in the Veda; the first *v* dropped; the compound "those whose fire is shining"; the vocative at the start of a *pāda* is not unaccented); *śucivratā* ("those whose vow is pure"; the *ā* ending for the dual vocative); *yajñavāhasā* (*vah* "to carry", Uṇ. 4-220 *vahi-hā-dhāṅbhyaś chandasi* with *asun*; the lengthening of the penultimate by *ñit*-ness; the accent of the compound that of the final member; the vocative unaccented as not first in the *pāda*). *(Grammar, noted briefly; P. 6-1-66 and 6-1-67 as read agree with the standard numbering.)*

**Grammar pages (pp. 668 lower half–670), noted briefly.** The Kannada treats: *aśvinā* (P. 7-1-39 *supāṃ sulug…*, *ā* for the dual vocative; accent by P. 6-1-198 *āmantritasya ca*; P. 8-1-18/19 does not apply, since it stands at the head of the *pāda*); *pibatam* (*pā*; *loṭ* 2nd dual *thas*; *loṭo laṅvat* P. 3-4-85; *tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ* P. 3-4-101: *thas* → *tam*; *śap* P. 3-1-68; *pāghrādhmā…* P. 7-3-78: *piba*; *ato guṇe* P. 6-1-97 *pararūpa*: *pibatam*, with a note on the alternative view that *piba* is an *ādyudātta nipātana* in the sūtra — Vārttika *pibāv ānipātanāt* — and the debate over the accent of *pibā-*; *pugantalaghūpadhasya ca* P. 7-3-86 not applying; *dhātoḥ* P. 6-1-162 ending-accent; the rule *aṅgavṛtte punar vṛttāv avidhiḥ* (paribhāṣā) so the guṇa does not apply after *piba*-substitution; "the accent of the root alone remains, so the Vedabhāṣya says"; *śap* *pit* unaccented, the suffix *tam* a *lasārvadhātuka* unaccented by *tāsyanudāttenṇiḍ-adupadeśāt* P. 6-1-186 [as read]); *madhu* ("*madhumantam*", see Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-?-? in the earlier part, where the process is explained; here *man* "to know" with the Uṇādi *u* — *phali-pāṭi-…* Uṇ. 1-18 [?], *nit* so first-syllable accent); *dīdyagnī* (*div* "to play", with the suffixes *manin, kvanip, vanip, vic* which are added after the root *div* in the Veda, by P. 3-2-75 *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante*; *div* + *vic* with *ver apṛktasya* P. 6-1-67 dropping *vi*'s *v*, and *lopo vyor vali* P. 6-1-66 dropping the *v* of *div*: the rule that [the dropping of the first *v* by the *ver apṛktasya* rule takes precedence], argued in detail by the paribhāṣā "*varṇāśraye nāsti pratyayalakṣaṇam*"; the Vedic doubling *didiv* with *tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya* P. 6-1-7 lengthening *dīdi*; or alternatively from *div* with *yaṅ* P. 3-1-22 *dhātor ekāco halādeḥ kriyāsamabhihāre yaṅ* and its *luk* P. 2-4-74 [*yaṅo vā*], then *sanyaṅoḥ* P. 6-1-9, *halādiḥ śeṣaḥ* P. 7-4-60, and *guṇo yaṅluk-ṛnoḥ* P. 7-4-82 whose guṇa is barred by the paribhāṣā *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*; *dīrgho 'kitaḥ* P. 7-4-83 lengthening the reduplicative; "*dīdiḥ agniḥ yayoḥ tau* — a bahuvrīhi; the vocative accent on the first syllable; not unaccented by P. 8-1-19 as it begins the *pāda*"); *śucivratā* (*śuci vrataṃ yayoḥ tau*; the dual vocative *ā* by P. 7-1-39; the grammarian's discussion of whether *dīdyagnī* and *śucivratā*, both vocatives, are connected by sense with *aśvinā*, by P. 8-1-73 *nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam* [as read] and P. 8-1-72 *āmantritaṃ pūrvam avidyamānavat* and P. 8-1-74 [?] *supāmantrite parāṅgavat svare* — the Kannada concludes that *dīdyagnī* and *śucivratā* are adjectives of *aśvinā* and *aśvinā* is the general term, so P. 8-1-73's bar applies and P. 8-1-72 does not make *dīdyagnī* ... unaccented; the whole is treated as one word, so *śucivratā* has the first-syllable accent only and the others are all-unaccented by *anudāttaṃ padam ekavarjam* P. 6-1-158, with *svarita* from *udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ* P. 8-4-66 and the *pracaya* of *svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām* P. 1-2-39); *yajñavāhasā* (*yajñaṃ vahataḥ*; *vah*; Uṇ. 4-220 *vahi-hā-dhāṅbhyaś chandasi* *asun*; the compound accent by Uṇ. 4-216; P. 7-2-116 *ata upadhāyāḥ* for the *ā*; *ñit*; the vocative dual ending *au* → *ā* by P. 7-1-39; accent by P. 8-1-72: the preceding word *ṛtunā* does not become *parāṅgavat*, since P. 8-1-74 *supāmantrite parāṅgavat svare* does not apply here, as the two words have no mutual connexion; the wholly unaccented *yajñavāhasā* by P. 8-1-19). ॥11॥ *(A long, crowded grammatical argument about the accent of the cluster* aśvinā … dīdyagnī śucivratā … ṛtunā yajñavāhasā*; I have given its outline only, with numerals as read from small print; pointers only.)*

**॥ Prati-padārthaḥ ॥** *(p. 667)*

**दीद्यग्नी (dīdyagnī)** — those shining with the *āhavanīya* and other fires | **शुचिव्रता (śucivratā)** — whose works are pure | **ऋतुना (ṛtunā)** — together with the Ṛtu-deity | **यज्ञवाहसा (yajña-vāhasā)** — the carriers of the sacrifice | **अश्विना (aśvinā)** — O Aśvin-deities | **मधु (madhu)** — the sweet soma-juice | **पिबतम् (pibatam)** — drink.

**॥ Bhāvārthaḥ ॥**

O Aśvins! You are ever shining with the *āhavanīya* and other fires; together with the Ṛtu-deity you carry through the sacrifice. Be pleased to drink the sweet soma-juice.

**॥ English Translation ॥** *(as printed in the source)*

> Aswins, performers of pious acts, accepters of the sacrifice with the Ritus, and accompanied by brilliant Agni, drink the sweet draught.

**॥ Viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu (Special Topics) ॥** *(p. 668)*

**दीद्यग्नी (dīdyagnī)** — *divu krīḍādau*; *dīdir agnir yayos tau*: "shining" — because the offerings for the Aśvin deities are made in the *āhavanīya* and other fires, they are said to be possessed of shining fire.

**शुचिव्रता (śucivratā)** — *śuci vrataṃ yayos tau*: "having pure works", that is, the works done by them are pure.

**यज्ञवाहसा (yajña-vāhasā)** — *vaha prāpaṇe*: *yajñaṃ vahata iti yajñavāhasau*: *yajñasya nirvāhakau*: "those who carry the sacrifice through" — who make it proceed without obstacle.

### Pages 671–676 — Sūkta 15, Rik 12 (last rik of the sūkta)

[७-४-३७] । इत्यात्वविधानादीत्वनिषेधे प्राप्तस्य दीर्घस्यैष निषेध इत्युक्तम् । शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् । अत्र क्यचि [?] … अन्तोदात्तत्वम् । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेणोभयोः … एकादेश उदात्तेनोदात्त इत्युदात्तः । तस्मादन्तोदात्तत्वात्परस्या विभक्तेः शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी इत्युदात्तत्वम् ॥१२॥
